q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q15) Which is different in the following: Lion, Wolf, Leopard, Lamb, Tiger?
f: Lion, wolf, leopard and tiger are carnivorous predators, while a lamb is a gentle animal that eats plants.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q16) Which one of the following is different: Mile, Kanal, Marla, Acre?
f: Kanal, marla and acre are units of land area, while a mile is a unit of length.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q17) Hand is to Touch as Nose is to?
f: The hand is the organ of touch, and the nose is the organ of smell.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q18) Which one of the following is different from others: Shirts, Boots, Coats, Trousers, Necktie?
f: Shirts, coats, trousers and necktie are clothes worn on the body, while boots are footwear.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q19) Easy is to Light as Rough is to:
f: Easy and light both mean not hard or heavy to deal with, and rough is closest to hard (a rough surface feels hard and coarse). The paper's answer key gives Hard.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q20) Which of the following is different from others: Plate, Dish, Knife, Spoon, Sugar?
f: Plate, dish, knife and spoon are utensils, while sugar is a food item.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q21) One third of one half is equal to?
f: One third of one half is 1/3 x 1/2 = 1/6.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q22) Hot is to Burn as Cold is to?
f: Excessive heat makes things burn, and excessive cold makes things freeze.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q23) Which number will come next: 6, 11, 12, 11, 18, ?
f: Take alternate terms: 6, 12, 18 goes up by 6, and the other terms stay at 11, 11, so the next is 11.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q24) Which is different from others: Whisper, Shout, Sing, Tell?
f: Whisper, shout and tell are ways of speaking words, while singing involves music and a tune.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q25) Which one is different from others: Selfish, Dishonest, Foolish, Ugly?
f: Selfish, dishonest and foolish describe character or behaviour, while ugly describes physical appearance.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q26) Bird is to Cage as Prisoner is to?
f: A bird is kept in a cage, and a prisoner is kept in jail.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q27) Which is different from other: Radius, Diagonal, Diameter, Circumference?
f: Radius, diameter and circumference are all parts of a circle, but a diagonal belongs to polygons such as squares and rectangles.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q28) Which number is out of order: Four, Eight, Ten, Seven, Twelve?
f: Four, eight, ten and twelve are even numbers, while seven is odd.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q29) What comes next: 62, 31, 34, 17, 20, ?
f: The series alternates between halving and adding 3: 62/2 = 31, +3 = 34, /2 = 17, +3 = 20, so the next step is 20/2 = 10.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q30) Which one of the following is different: Cow, Goat, Sheep, Horse, Buffalo?
f: Cow, goat, sheep and buffalo are milk-giving farm animals, while a horse is not kept for milk.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q31) Which number will come next: 1, 4, 10, 22, ?
f: The differences are 3, 6, 12, which double each time, so the next difference is 24: 22 + 24 = 46.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q32) Which is different in the following: Speech, Lecture, Oration, Sermon, Gossip?
f: Speech, lecture, oration and sermon are formal talks given to an audience, while gossip is casual talk about other people.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q33) If A is to E then C is to?
f: A to E is a jump of 4 letters (A=1, E=5), so C (3) plus 4 gives G (7).

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q34) Which one is different in the following: Petrol, Oil, Water, Spirit?
f: Petrol, oil and spirit are flammable liquids, while water does not burn.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q35) Write the number that comes next: 5, 3, 6, 4, 7, ?
(Forces Academy Test 1 · Q36) Nib is to Pen as Blade is to?
f: A nib is the writing part of a pen, and a blade is the cutting part of a knife.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q37) Which number comes next: 3, 8, 14, 21, ?
f: The differences are 5, 6, 7, so the next difference is 8: 21 + 8 = 29.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q38) Which letters will come next: BY, CX, DW, EV, ?
f: The first letters go forward B, C, D, E, F and the second letters go backward Y, X, W, V, U, so the next pair is FU.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q39) A cake is cut so that one piece, which is half of the cake, is twice as large as one of the other pieces. How many pieces are there?
f: One piece is 1/2 of the cake, and each other piece is half of that, 1/4. The remaining 1/2 makes two pieces of 1/4, so there are 3 pieces in all.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q40) Which is different in the following: Violin, Piano, String, Cutter, Banjo?
f: Violin, piano, string and banjo are all connected with music, while a cutter is a cutting tool.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q41) Which number comes next in the following: 5, 9, 8, 12, 11, ?
f: The pattern is +4, -1, +4, -1, so after 11 comes 11 + 4 = 15.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q42) December is to October as June is to?
f: December is two months after October in reverse, so go two months back: June gives April.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q43) Which number will come next: 20, 15, 18, 13, 16, ?
f: The pattern is -5, +3, -5, +3, so 16 - 5 = 11.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q45) Which number comes next in the following: 2, 4, 5, 10, 11, 22, ?
f: The pattern is multiply by 2, then add 1: 2x2=4, 4+1=5, 5x2=10, 10+1=11, 11x2=22, 22+1=23.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q46) Laugh is to Cry, so Weep is to?
f: Cry is the opposite of laugh, and the opposite of weep is smile.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q47) Add all even numbers and divide it by its middle number: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.
f: The even numbers are 4, 6 and 8, which add up to 18. The middle number is 6, so 18 / 6 = 3.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q48) Which number comes next: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
f: The differences are 4, 6, 8, 10, so the next difference is 12: 30 + 12 = 42.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q49) Tobacco is to Pipe as Coal is to:
f: Tobacco is burned in a pipe, and coal is burned in an oven.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q50) Which number comes next in the following: 3/4, 6/8, 12/16, 24/32, ?
f: Each fraction doubles both numerator and denominator: 24 x 2 = 48 and 32 x 2 = 64.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q51) If 2200 hours is 10 o'clock in the evening then write the answer as 4, and if not then write 5.
f: 2200 hours in the 24-hour clock is 22 - 12 = 10 in the evening, so the statement is true and the answer is 4.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q52) The next number in the series is: 120, 108, 97, 87, 78, ?
f: The differences are -12, -11, -10, -9, so the next is -8: 78 - 8 = 70.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q53) Finger is to Hand as Toe is to?
f: A finger is a part of the hand, and a toe is a part of the foot.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q55) What will be the next letter: A, E, I, M, ?
f: Each letter is 4 places after the previous one: A(1), E(5), I(9), M(13), then Q(17).

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q56) If L comes before P then write 5, otherwise write 4.
f: In the alphabet L is the 12th letter and P is the 16th, so L comes before P and the answer is 5.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q54) Which is different in the following: Ounce, Pound, Ton, Maund?
f: Ounce, pound and ton belong to the same Western (imperial) system, while the maund is a traditional South Asian unit.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q57) List is to Last as Fist is to?
f: List becomes Last by changing the vowel I to A, so Fist becomes Fast.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q58) What letter comes next in the following series: A, C, F, J, ?
f: The letters are at positions 1, 3, 6, 10, whose gaps are 2, 3, 4, so the next gap is 5: 10 + 5 = 15, which is O.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q59) Triangle is to Prism as Circle is to?
f: A prism is the three-dimensional solid built from a triangle, and a sphere is the solid form of a circle.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q60) Which word does not belong to this list: Less, Depart, Abate, Decrease?
f: Less, abate and decrease all mean to reduce, while depart means to leave.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q61) Tomorrow is to Yesterday as Thursday is to?
f: Yesterday is two days before tomorrow, so the matching day is two days before Thursday, which is Tuesday.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q62) If 6 and 5 make 10 then write A, otherwise write B.
f: 6 + 5 = 11, not 10, so the condition fails and the answer is B.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q63) If W precedes X then write the answer as 5, otherwise 6.
f: In the alphabet W comes right before X, so W precedes X and the answer is 5.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q64) Which number comes next: 6, 12, 9, 16, 12, ?
f: Alternate terms form two series: 6, 9, 12 (adding 3) and 12, 16, 20 (adding 4). The next term is 20.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q65) A watch reads half past nine. The minute hand points toward North. In which direction does the hour hand point?
f: At half past nine the minute hand points to 6 and the hour hand lies between 9 and 10. If the minute hand (6) points North, the clock is turned half a turn, so the 9-10 position (about 3) points East.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q66) What will be the next number in the series: 5, 8, 9, 16, 13, ?
f: Odd-position terms go 5, 9, 13 (adding 4) and even-position terms go 8, 16, 24 (adding 8). The next term is 24.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q67) Bright is to Dim as Clear is to?
f: Dim is the opposite of bright, and vague is the opposite of clear.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q68) P is to L as N is to?
f: P is the 16th letter and L is the 12th, which is 4 places back. N is the 14th, and 4 places back is J (10).

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q69) What will be the next number: 11, 21, 40, 77, 150, ?
f: The differences are 10, 19, 37, 73, and each difference is double the previous minus 1. The next difference is 145, so 150 + 145 = 295.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q71) Write the fifth last letter of the alphabet.
f: Counting from the end: Z (1st last), Y, X, W, V (5th last), so the answer is V.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q72) Write the 4th letter before W, as counted from the end of the alphabet.
f: Going back from W: V, U, T, S, so the 4th letter before W is S.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q75) If three oranges cost Rs. 9, how much will it cost to buy four and a half dozen?
f: Four and a half dozen is 54 oranges. One orange costs 9 / 3 = Rs. 3, so 54 x 3 = Rs. 162.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q74) Write the next letter in the series: A, C, D, H, K, ?
f: The letter positions are 1, 3, 4, 8, 11, with gaps +2, +1, +4, +3, so the gaps are +2, +1, +4, +3, +6, and the next letter is 11 + 6 = 17, which is Q.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q77) Write the next number: 10, 30, 50, 80, ?
f: The differences are 20, 20, 30, 30, so the next difference is 30 (then 40, 40): 80 + 30 = 110.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q78) NECESSARY CUSTOM TO TRADE ROAD DEVELOPMENT. If one word is omitted from the above, the others could be arranged as one sentence. Write the second letter of the word to be omitted.
f: Without the word CUSTOM the rest forms the sentence 'Road development necessary to trade'. CUSTOM has U as its second letter.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q80) How much distance will you cover in 3 and a half minutes if you are moving at the speed of 120 km/h?
f: 120 km/h is 2 km per minute, so in 3.5 minutes you cover 2 x 3.5 = 7 km.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q1) SICK is to SACK as LICK is to:
f: SICK changes its vowel I to A to make SACK, so LICK becomes LACK.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q2) What letter comes next in the following series: B, D, G, K, P, ?
f: The gaps are +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next gap is +6: P (16) + 6 = 22, which is V.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q3) What number comes next in the following series: 34, 24, 16, 10, 6, ?
f: The differences are -10, -8, -6, -4, so the next is -2: 6 - 2 = 4.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q4) If 4 is more than 9 write 2 as your answer, otherwise write 3.
f: 4 is not more than 9, so the condition fails and the answer is 3.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q5) Students go to school because:
o: They want to be away from home.
They want to tease the teacher.
f: The main purpose of school is to gain knowledge; the other choices are minor or silly reasons.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q6) What number comes next in the following series: 18, 13, 9, 6, ?
f: The differences are -5, -4, -3, so the next is -2: 6 - 2 = 4.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q7) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Car, train, aircraft and ship are machines with engines, while a cart is pulled by an animal or by hand.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q8) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: February, December, June and September are months, while Monday is a day of the week.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q9) What number comes next in the following series: 49, 36, 25, 16, ?
f: These are squares in reverse: 7 squared, 6 squared, 5 squared, 4 squared, so next is 3 squared = 9.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q10) NORTH is to SOUTH as EAST is to:
f: South is the direct opposite of north, and west is the direct opposite of east.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q11) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Brother, uncle, son and grandfather are male relatives, while a sister is female.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q12) Girls wear glasses because:
f: The usual real reason for wearing glasses is weak eyesight.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q13) In a group of 50 players, 30% play hockey and 80% play cricket. Are there any who play both hockey and cricket?
o: One cannot say without further detail
f: 30% of 50 is 15 and 80% of 50 is 40. Since 15 + 40 = 55 is more than 50, at least 5 players must play both.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q14) What number comes next in the following series: 40, 30, 35, 25, 30, 20, ?
(Forces Academy Test 2 · Q15) Engine is to Car as Cell is to:
f: An engine powers a car, and a cell (battery) powers a torch.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q16) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Tennis, hockey, cricket and football are outdoor games, while billiard is an indoor game.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q17) If 7 and 6 make 19, write 5 as your answer, otherwise write 3.
f: 7 + 6 = 13, which is not 19, so the condition fails and the answer is 3.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q18) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Huge, great, fat and big all describe large size, while small is the opposite.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q19) What number comes next in the following series: 62, 32, 30, 16, 14, 8, 6, ?
f: Terms alternate between halving plus 1 and subtracting 2: 62 to 32, 32 to 30, 30 to 16, 16 to 14, 14 to 8, 8 to 6, then 6 halved plus 1 is 4.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q20) If Arza is older than Munir and Munir is younger than Javaid, then Arza is:
f: Munir is below both Arza and Javaid, but nothing links Arza and Javaid directly, so their order cannot be known.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q21) If Asif is 12 years old and all boys over 10 are hockey players, then:
o: It is not sure that Asif is hockey player.
Asif is likely to become hockey player.
f: Asif is 12, which is over 10, and the rule says all boys over 10 are hockey players, so he is one.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q22) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Mango, lemon and orange are fruits, while tomato is generally treated as a vegetable in cooking.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q23) Women go to market because:
o: They have plenty of spare time.
They don't want to stay at home.
f: The practical purpose of going to a market is to buy things.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q24) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Two, four, twenty and fifty are even numbers, while five is odd.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q25) What number comes next in the following series: 27, 20, 14, 9, 5, ?
f: The differences are -7, -6, -5, -4, so the next is -3: 5 - 3 = 2.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q26) What letter comes next in the following series: J, H, F, D, ?
f: Each letter is 2 places before the previous one: J, H, F, D, then B.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q27) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Yard, foot, mile and kilometer are units of measuring length, while length itself is the quantity being measured.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q28) Forests are useful because:
o: They help in building the economy.
f: Forests supply timber and other resources, so their main usefulness is to the economy.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q29) NEAR is to FAR as CLOSE is to:
f: Far is the opposite of near, and open is the opposite of close (shut).

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q30) What is the area of a square which is 8 feet long?
f: The area of a square is side times side: 8 x 8 = 64 square feet.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q31) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Cup, mug, glass and jug are containers, while a drink is what goes inside them.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q32) If 5 is subtracted from 30, what would be the square root of the remaining?
f: 30 - 5 = 25 and the square root of 25 is 5.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q33) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Sword, knife, fork and axe are sharp tools or weapons, while a cup is a container with no sharp edge.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q1) Which of the following is different from the rest?
f: Unearth, discover, find and locate all mean to come across something that already exists. Invention means to create something new.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q2) What number comes next in the following series? 2413, 2420, 2434, 2462, 2518, ?
f: The differences are 7, 14, 28, 56, doubling each time, so the next difference is 112: 2518 + 112 = 2630.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q3) Which one is different from the rest? Cow, Hen, Duck, Bull, Mare
f: Cow, hen and mare are female animals, while bull is the only male.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q4) If Shoe is to Foot then Helmet is to ____.
f: A shoe is worn on the foot and a helmet is worn on the head.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q5) What number comes next in the following series? 3, 10, 4, 17, 5, ?
f: Alternate terms form two series: 3, 4, 5 (plus 1) and 10, 17, 24 (plus 7). The next term belongs to the second series: 24.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q6) Which one is different from the rest? QS, EH, IL, MP, AD
f: In EH, IL, MP and AD the second letter is 3 places after the first. In QS the gap is only 2.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q7) If the second of the following numbers is added to the shortest number and divided by the third number, what will the answer be? 2, 14, 4
f: Second number 14 plus shortest number 2 is 16. Dividing by the third number 4 gives 4.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q8) What is the next number in the following series? 4, 8, 24, 96, ?
f: Each term is multiplied by 2, 3, 4 and then 5: 96 x 5 = 480.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q9) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Town, city, village and township are all human settlements on earth. Heaven is not.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q10) March is to 31/3 and June is to ____.
f: March has 31 days and is the 3rd month. June has 30 days and is the 6th month, so 30/6.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q11) Which one of the following is different from the rest? Infant, Adult, Child, Newborn, Baby
f: Infant, child, newborn and baby all describe young ones. Adult is a fully grown person.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q12) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Separation, split, divide and gap all involve parting. Union means joining together.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q13) What number comes next in the following series? 63, 3, 44, 0, 91, ?
f: Each pair is the first digit minus the second digit: 6 - 3 = 3, 4 - 4 = 0, so for 91: 9 - 1 = 8.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q14) What letter comes next in the following series? E, J, N, Q, ?
f: The steps are +5, +4, +3, so the next step is +2: Q + 2 = S.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q15) Which one is different from the rest?
f: Kabul, Delhi and Dhaka are national capitals. Karachi is not the capital of Pakistan.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q16) My mother is your brother's sister. What am I to you?
f: Your brother's sister is your sister, so my mother is your sister and I am your nephew.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q17) Kamal is older than Jamal, Jamal is older than Hussain, Hussain is older than Waqar. Who is the oldest?
f: The order is Kamal, Jamal, Hussain, Waqar from oldest to youngest.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q18) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: High, great, fat and big all suggest large size. Small is the opposite.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q19) What will come next in the following series? 2, 4, 8, 14, ?
f: The differences are 2, 4, 6, so the next difference is 8: 14 + 8 = 22.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q20) What will come next in the following series? 34, 24, 16, 10, 6, ?
f: The differences are 10, 8, 6, 4, so the next difference is 2: 6 - 2 = 4.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q22) Which one is different from the rest?
f: Relationship, kinship and friendship are all human bonds. Spaceship is a vehicle.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q23) Akmal and Jamal are brothers, Anjum and Ajmal are their sons. What is the relation between Anjum and Ajmal?
f: Anjum and Ajmal are sons of two brothers, so they are cousins.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q24) Which one is different from the rest? Oxygen, Sulphur, Silver, Zinc, Protenium
f: Oxygen is a gas at room temperature, while sulphur, silver and zinc are solids (the printed Protenium is not a standard element name). The answer key also gives Oxygen.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q25) A grandfather is always ____ than his daughter.
f: A grandfather is older than his daughter, which means he has lived longer and is more experienced. Taller, wiser and heavier are not always true.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q27) If 18:00 o'clock is to 6 o'clock, then 14:00 o'clock is to ____ o'clock.
f: 18:00 on the 24-hour clock is 6 on a 12-hour clock (18 - 12). Likewise 14:00 is 2 o'clock.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q28) Which one is different from the rest?
f: Confuse, puzzle, disturb and tense relate to being troubled or perplexed. Advancing means moving forward.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q29) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Dagger, sword and knife are cutting weapons. A fork is an eating tool without a blade.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q30) Which one is different from the rest? AC, DG, HK, LO
f: In DG, HK and LO the second letter is 3 places after the first. In AC it is only 2 places.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q1) Which comes next in the following series? A, B, C, D, E, ?
f: These are consecutive letters of the alphabet, so after E comes F.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q2) Which number comes next in the following series? 64, 32, 16, 8, ?
f: Each term is half of the one before: 8 / 2 = 4.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q3) Add the smallest and the largest numbers and divide the total by the third number. The numbers are 3, 6, 15.
f: Smallest 3 plus largest 15 is 18. The third number is 6, and 18 / 6 = 3.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q4) STONE is to HARD as COTTON WOOL is to:
f: A stone is characterised by being hard, and cotton wool by being soft.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q5) DEAL is to 7345 as LEAD is to:
f: D=7, E=3, A=4, L=5. LEAD is L, E, A, D = 5, 3, 4, 7, which gives 5347.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q6) Tree is to branches as river is to:
f: Branches spread out from a tree, and canals are channels taken off a river. This matches the answer key (a delta could also be argued).

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q8) Which letter comes next in the following series? A, C, E, G, I, ?
f: Every second letter is taken, so after I comes K.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q9) Which number comes next? 55, 50, 40, 25, ?
f: The differences are -5, -10, -15, so the next is -20: 25 - 20 = 5.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q10) What is the total cost of two pencils at Rs.2 each and one dozen sharpeners at Rs.3 each?
f: Pencils cost 2 x 2 = 4. A dozen sharpeners cost 12 x 3 = 36. The total is 40.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q11) If Akram is older than Kamal and Hamid is younger than Kamal but Amjad is older than Hamid, who is the youngest?
f: Hamid is younger than Kamal and Amjad, and Kamal is younger than Akram, so Hamid is the youngest.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q12) Write the letter that is as far from the beginning of the alphabet as D is from the beginning of the word PROUDLY.
f: In PROUDLY, D is the 5th letter (P, R, O, U, D). The 5th letter of the alphabet is E.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q13) Which letter comes next in the following series? A, D, G, J, M, ?
f: The letters go up by 3 each time, so after M comes P.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q14) Magazines are useful because:
o: They are helpful in finding jobs
f: The main purpose of a magazine is to inform readers by publishing news and information.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q15) If apples are selling at Rs.40 per kg, how much can you buy for Rs.1200?
(Forces Academy Test 4 · Q16) Sweet is to sour as cold is to:
f: Sweet and sour are opposites, and the opposite of cold is hot.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q17) Which one of the following is different from others?
f: Salmon, crab, shark and whale are all specific sea animals, while Fish is the general category name. This follows the answer key (whale is also not a true fish).

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q18) Which letter comes next in the following series? B, F, I, M, P, ?
f: The steps are +4, +3, +4, +3, so the next step is +4: P + 4 = T.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q19) A bakery sells a mixture of 2 parts cream and 3 parts milk. How many litres of cream will it take to make 15 litres of the mixture?
f: The mixture has 5 parts in total, so one part is 3 litres. Cream is 2 parts: 2 x 3 = 6 litres.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q20) Kund, Mora and Mokoma are three cities. Mora is 120 km in the west of Kund and Mokoma is 320 km in the North of Mora. Then Kund is in the ____ of Mokoma.
f: Mokoma is directly north of Mora, and Kund is east of Mora. So Kund is to the south and east of Mokoma, which is South East.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q21) Which letter comes next in the following series? A, B, D, G, K, ?
f: The steps are +1, +2, +3, +4, so the next step is +5: K + 5 = P.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q22) How many packs of envelopes can be bought for Rs.3 at the rate of 50 paisa each?
f: Rs.3 is 300 paisa, and 300 / 50 = 6 packs.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q23) In a college, out of 200 students 45% study Physics and 65% study Maths. Are there any students who neither study Physics nor Maths?
f: Physics has 90 students and Maths 130, a total of 220, so at least 20 study both. If exactly 20 study both there are none who study neither, but if more study both there are some. The answer cannot be fixed (the paper key says Yes).

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q24) Which number comes next? 30, 25, 19, 12, ?
f: The differences are 5, 6, 7, so the next difference is 8: 12 - 8 = 4.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q25) ADVANCE is to FORWARD as INCREASE is to:
f: Advance and forward are synonyms, and the synonym of increase is raise.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q26) Which one of the following is different from the others?
f: Brazil, Canada, Chile and Argentina are countries. New York is a city.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q27) Which number comes next? 3, 7, 12, 18, ?
f: The differences are 4, 5, 6, so the next difference is 7: 18 + 7 = 25.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q28) All animals have tails. Some birds have tails. X has a tail, therefore it is a bird:
f: Having a tail does not prove it is a bird, since every animal has a tail. So the conclusion is uncertain.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q29) A car is travelling at the speed of 120 km per hour. How many minutes will it take to travel 24 km?
f: 120 km per hour is 2 km per minute, so 24 km takes 24 / 2 = 12 minutes.

q: (Forces Academy Test 4 · Q30) CROWD is 92174 as WORD is to:
(Forces Academy Test 5 · Q1) Which letter comes next in the following series? A, H, N, S, W, ?
f: The letter positions are 1, 8, 14, 19, 23 with gaps 7, 6, 5, 4. The next gap is 3: 23 + 3 = 26, which is Z.

q: (Forces Academy Test 5 · Q2) Which number comes next? 486, 162, 54, 18, ?
f: Each term is divided by 3: 18 / 3 = 6.

q: (Forces Academy Test 5 · Q3) If apples are sold at Rs.26 per kg, how much can be bought for Rs.156?
(Forces Academy Test 5 · Q4) SHELLS is to 251442 as LESS is to:
(Forces Academy Test 5 · Q5) Easy means the opposite of:
f: The opposite of easy is difficult.

q: (Forces Academy Test 5 · Q6) Which one of the following is different from the others?
f: Red, blue, green and yellow are specific colors. Color is the general category.

q: (Forces Academy Test 5 · Q7) SMEAR is to 31247 as REAMS is to:
(Forces Academy Test 5 · Q8) Which letter comes next in the following series? B, D, J, L, R, ?
f: The steps alternate +2 and +6: B to D (+2), D to J (+6), J to L (+2), L to R (+6), so R + 2 = T.

q: (Forces Academy Test 5 · Q9) Which number comes next? 36, 20, 12, 8, ?
f: The differences are -16, -8, -4, so the next difference is -2: 8 - 2 = 6.

q: (Forces Academy Test 5 · Q10) Ten boxes of oranges weigh 120 kg. Each box when empty weighs 3 kg. What is the actual weight of oranges?
f: The ten empty boxes weigh 10 x 3 = 30 kg. The oranges weigh 120 - 30 = 90 kg.

q: (Forces Academy Test 5 · Q11) If Imran is older than Waseem and Kaleem is younger than Imran, which of the following statements is true?
o: Waseem and Kaleem are of equal age
f: Imran is older than both Waseem and Kaleem, so he is the oldest. The relative ages of Waseem and Kaleem are not known.

q: (Forces Academy Test 5 · Q12) How many letters in the word GENERAL are also found in the word REGULAR?
f: The letters G, E, R, A and L of GENERAL appear in REGULAR, while N does not. That gives 5 letters.

q: (Forces Academy Test 5 · Q13) Which letter comes next in the following series? A, F, K, P, U, ?
f: The letters go up by 5 each time, so U + 5 = Z.

q: (Forces Academy Test 5 · Q14) Which letter in the word PRODUCTION lies as far from the beginning of the word as it is from the beginning of the alphabet?
f: D is the 4th letter in PRODUCTION (P, R, O, D) and also the 4th letter of the alphabet.

q: (Forces Academy Test 5 · Q15) If one shirt can be made with 2 1/3 metres of cloth, how many shirts can be made from 14 metres of cloth?
f: 2 1/3 is 7/3. Then 14 divided by 7/3 is 14 x 3/7 = 6.

f: MNO, XYZ, EFG and BCD are three consecutive letters of the alphabet. STW skips a letter (S, T, then W).

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q2) Which one of the following is different? A. EVU, B. RHI, C. OLK, D. SHG, E. HSR
f: EVU, OLK, SHG and HSR all end with two letters in backward alphabetical order (V U, L K, H G, S R). RHI ends with H I, which goes forward.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q3) Which one of the following is different? A. PQO, B. KJL, C. UTV, D. SRT, E. FEG
f: KJL, UTV, SRT and FEG each go one step back then two steps forward (-1, +2). PQO goes forward then back (+1, -2), so it is the odd one.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q4) Which one of the following is different? A. LLMN, B. UUVW, C. CCDE, D. GGHI, E. RRRS
f: The others repeat the first letter twice and then follow with the next two consecutive letters. RRRS repeats its first letter three times.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q5) Which one of the following is different? A. Boy, B. Girl, C. Woman, D. Lady, E. Female
f: Girl, woman, lady and female all refer to the female sex. A boy is male.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q6) Which one of the following is different? A. Picture, B. Painting, C. Photography, D. Poster
f: Picture, painting and poster are finished visual items. Photography is the art or process of taking photographs, not an item.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q7) Which one of the following is different? A. Tobacco, B. Pipe, C. Cigarette, D. Cigar
f: Tobacco, cigarette and cigar are all made of tobacco. A pipe is only a device in which tobacco is smoked.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q8) Which one of the following is different? A. Stationary, B. Eraser, C. Pen, D. Paper
f: Eraser, pen and paper are all items of stationery. The word given, stationary, means not moving and is a different word.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q9) Which one of the following is different? A. Feathers, B. Hair, C. Grass, D. Wool
f: Feathers, hair and wool grow on the bodies of animals or birds. Grass is a plant.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q10) Which one of the following is different? A. Circle, B. Square, C. Triangle, D. Hexagon
f: Square, triangle and hexagon are polygons with straight sides and corners. A circle has a curved boundary and no corners.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q11) Which one of the following is different? A. Leprosy, B. Typhoid, C. Vomiting, D. Asthma
f: Leprosy, typhoid and asthma are diseases. Vomiting is a symptom, not a disease in itself.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q12) Which one of the following is different? A. Silver, B. Mercury, C. Gold, D. Iron
f: Silver, gold and iron are solid metals at room temperature. Mercury is a liquid metal.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q13) Which one of the following is different? A. Live, B. Die, C. Exist, D. Be
f: Live, exist and be all mean to have life or being. Die means the opposite, to stop living.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q14) Which one of the following is different? A. Hard, B. Stiff, C. Unbending, D. Flexible
f: Hard, stiff and unbending describe something rigid. Flexible means able to bend easily.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q15) Which one of the following is different? A. Sports, B. Teem, C. Game, D. Team
f: Sports, game and team all belong to the field of games and play. Teem (to be full of) is unrelated.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q16) Which one of the following is different? A. August, B. September, C. October, D. November
f: September, October and November all end in the letters ber. August does not.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q17) All the rivers have? A. Towns, B. Bridge, C. Banks, D. Fish
f: Every river, without exception, has banks on its sides. Not every river has towns, bridges or fish.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q18) ABD is to CBA as QRT is to?
f: ABD to CBA: first letter +2 (A to C), middle letter unchanged (B), last letter -3 (D to A). Apply this to QRT: Q+2 = S, R stays R, T-3 = Q, giving SRQ.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q19) What number comes next in the series: 13, 8, 5, 3, 2, ?
f: Each term is the sum of the next two terms (13 = 8 + 5, 8 = 5 + 3, 5 = 3 + 2, 3 = 2 + 1), so the next number is 1.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q20) What is the smallest even number (counting zero as an even whole number)?
f: Zero is divisible by 2 with no remainder, so it is an even number, and it is the smallest non-negative even number.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q21) What do you find once in a year and twice in a week?
f: The word YEAR contains the letter E once and the word WEEK contains it twice.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q22) Train is to track as bus is to?
f: A train runs on a track and a bus runs on a road. Both pairs show a vehicle and the path it travels on.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q23) If 8 men out of 10 are bald, how many out of 1000 are not bald?
f: 2 out of every 10 are not bald, which is 20 percent. 20 percent of 1000 is 200.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q24) What comes next in the series: 1, 2, 6, 12, 36, ?  (multiplying by 2, then 3, alternately)
f: The multipliers alternate x2, x3, x2, x3: 1x2 = 2, 2x3 = 6, 6x2 = 12, 12x3 = 36, so next is 36x2 = 72.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q25) Arrival is the opposite of? A. Reach, B. Departure, C. Away
f: Arrival means coming to a place and departure means leaving it, so they are opposites.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q26) 6 is to F as 11 is to? A. K, B. L, C. M
f: F is the 6th letter of the alphabet, so the pair is number to its letter. The 11th letter is K.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q27) Aslam is four times as old as Ashraf. If the sum of their ages is 60 years, how old is Ashraf? A. 48 yrs, B. 12 yrs, C. 72 yrs
f: Let Ashraf be x, so Aslam is 4x and x + 4x = 60, which gives 5x = 60 and x = 12.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q28) If 1/8 of a number is 6, what is the number? A. 14, B. 48, C. 42
f: The number is 6 x 8 = 48.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q29) Which one of the following is a prime number? A. 7, B. 8, C. 16, D. 12
f: 7 has only two factors, 1 and 7. The others are even numbers greater than 2, so they have more factors.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q30) 32% of 25 is? A. 16, B. 8, C. 4
f: 32 percent of 25 is 32/100 x 25 = 8.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q1) What number comes next in the following series? 11, 17, 23, ?
f: Each term increases by 6: 11, 17, 23, so next is 29.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q2) What number comes next in the following series? 23, 19, 15, 11, ?
f: Each term decreases by 4, so next is 11 - 4 = 7.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q3) What number comes next in the following series? 6/11, 5/10, 4/9, 3/8, ?
f: The numerator falls by 1 each time and the denominator falls by 1 each time, so after 3/8 comes 2/7.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q4) What number comes next in the following series? 1/3, 5, 1/7, 9, 1/11, ?
f: Alternate terms form two series: the fractions 1/3, 1/7, 1/11 and the whole numbers 5, 9, and the next is 13 (add 4).

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q5) What number comes next in the following series? 8, 4, 16, 8, 64, ?
f: The pattern is divide by 2, multiply by 4, divide by 2, multiply by 8, divide by 2: 8/2 = 4, 4x4 = 16, 16/2 = 8, 8x8 = 64, 64/2 = 32.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q6) What number comes next in the following series? 3, 5, 3/5, 7, 11, ?
f: The terms come in groups of three: the first two numbers and then their fraction (3, 5, 3/5), then (7, 11, 7/11).

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q7) What number comes next in the following series? 2/31, 3/52, 4/73, ?
f: The numerators go up by 1 (2, 3, 4, 5) and the denominators go up by 21 (31, 52, 73, 94), so next is 5/94.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q8) What number comes next in the following series? 93, 2, 73, 1, 63, 3, 33, 2, ?
f: Subtract ten times the number that follows: 93 - 20 = 73, 73 - 10 = 63, 63 - 30 = 33, 33 - 20 = 13.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q9) What number comes next in the following series? 1/2, A/B, 3, C, 4/5, D/E, ?
f: The pattern is number pair, letter pair, number, letter, so the terms run 1/2, A/B, 3, C, 4/5, D/E, 6, F and the next is 6.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q10) What number comes next in the following series? 34/65, 23/54, 67/98, 45/?
f: In every fraction the denominator is the numerator plus 31 (34+31 = 65, 23+31 = 54, 67+31 = 98), so 45+31 = 76.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q12) What number comes next in the following series? 2, 1, 3, 4, 7, ?
f: Each term is the sum of the two before it: 2+1 = 3, 1+3 = 4, 3+4 = 7, so next is 4+7 = 11.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q13) Which one of the following is different? A. Young, B. Lovely, C. Beautiful, D. Handsome, E. Pretty
f: Lovely, beautiful, handsome and pretty all describe good looks. Young describes age.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q14) Which one of the following is different? A. Month, B. Season, C. Year, D. Day, E. Week
f: Month, year, day and week are fixed units of time measured by the calendar. A season is a part of the year with a particular climate and has no fixed number of days.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q15) Which one of the following is different? A. GHI, B. JKL, C. NOP, D. QST, E. UVW
f: The others are three consecutive letters of the alphabet. QST skips R.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q16) Which one of the following is different? A. Green, B. Red, C. Dark, D. Yellow, E. Brown
f: Green, red, yellow and brown are colours. Dark describes shade, not a particular colour.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q17) Which one of the following is different? A. Camel, B. Ox, C. Horse, D. Donkey, E. Mule
f: Camel, ox, horse and donkey are natural animal species. A mule is a hybrid, the offspring of a male donkey and a female horse.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q18) Which one of the following is different? A. Hand, B. Arm, C. Body, D. Wrist, E. Fingers
f: Hand, arm, wrist and fingers are all parts of the arm. Body is the whole that contains them.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q19) Which one of the following is different? A. Hot, B. Steam, C. Water, D. Ice, E. Vapour
f: Steam, water, ice and vapour are forms of water. Hot is only a quality.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q20) Which one of the following is different? A. Square, B. Line, C. Triangle, D. Circle, E. Rectangle
f: Square, triangle, circle and rectangle are closed shapes enclosing an area. A line does not enclose any area.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q21) Which one of the following is different? A. Little, B. Rare, C. Less, D. Inferior, E. Few
f: Little, rare, less and few all refer to small quantity or amount. Inferior refers to lower quality.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q22) Which one of the following is different? A. RUS, B. FHG, C. MON, D. QSR, E. TVU
f: FHG, MON, QSR and TVU all follow the pattern +2, -1 between letters (F+2 = H, H-1 = G, and so on). RUS goes +3, -2.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q23) Which one of the following is different? A. ABCACB, B. NOPNPO, C. RSTSTR, D. GHIGIH, E. KLMKML
f: In the others, three consecutive letters are followed by the same three with the last two swapped (ABC ACB, NOP NPO, GHI GIH, KLM KML). RSTSTR repeats the letters as S T R, which is a rotation instead.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q24) Which one of the following is different? A. TSUS, B. NMOM, C. DCEC, D. HGJG, E. RQSQ
f: TSUS, NMOM, DCEC and RQSQ all follow -1, +2, -2 between letters. HGJG goes -1, +3, -3, so it is different.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q25) Which one of the following is different? A. Play, B. Cricket, C. Swimming, D. Football, E. Child
f: Play, cricket, swimming and football are all sports or games. Child is a person.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q26) Which one of the following is different? A. Two, B. Double, C. Pair, D. Three, E. Couple
f: Two, double, pair and couple all mean 2. Three is a different number.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q27) Which one of the following is different? A. STVU, B. HIJK, C. IJKL, D. OPQR, E. EFGH
f: The others are four consecutive letters of the alphabet. STVU has the order S, T, V, U, which is not consecutive.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q28) Which one of the following is different? A. Kingdom, B. State, C. Province, D. Citizen, E. Country
f: Kingdom, state, province and country are territories or political regions. A citizen is a person who lives in one.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q29) Which one of the following is different? A. Run, B. Flow, C. Swim, D. Fast, E. Move
f: Run, flow, swim and move are verbs of motion. Fast is an adjective or adverb describing speed.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q30) Which one of the following is different? A. DBC, B. MLK, C. ONM, D. CBA, E. ZYX
f: MLK, ONM, CBA and ZYX are each three consecutive letters in backward order. DBC is not in a consecutive order.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q1) We read newspaper because: A. It is a good hobby, B. These give us knowledge, C. One learns how to read, D. These are motivating, E. These help us to get job
o: These help us to get job
f: The main purpose of a newspaper is to inform, so the best reason is that it gives knowledge.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q2) Which statement is correct? A. A son is always better educated than his father, B. A son is always more healthier than his father, C. A son is always younger than his father, D. A son is always less tall than his father, E. A son is always wiser than his father
o: A son is always better educated than his father
A son is always more healthier than his father
A son is always younger than his father
A son is always less tall than his father
A son is always wiser than his father
f: A father is by definition born before his son, so the son is always younger. The other statements may be true sometimes but not always.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q3) If clock A goes faster than clock B and clock C keeps time with clock A, then: A. C is slower than B, B. B keeps time with C, C. C is faster than B, D. B may be faster or slower than C, E. B and C keeps time with A
o: B may be faster or slower than C
B and C keeps time with A
f: C keeps the same time as A, and A is faster than B, so C is faster than B.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q4) 2 is to 5 as K is to?
f: The step from 2 to 5 is +3. Moving 3 letters on from K (L, M, N) gives N.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q5) Parents give education to their children because: A. Children want it, B. It is a custom, C. It gives them better chances in life, D. It makes them obedient, E. It gives employment to teachers
o: It gives them better chances in life
f: The real purpose of education is to improve a child's opportunities and future.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q6) TIME is to EMIT as 4375 is to?
f: EMIT is TIME written backwards, so reverse 4375 to get 5734.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q7) Which one of the following is different? A. South-West, B. North-East, C. North-West, D. East-West, E. South-East
f: South-West, North-East, North-West and South-East are the four intermediate (diagonal) directions. East-West is a pair of opposite cardinal directions, not a single direction.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q8) Which statement is correct? A. Two is equal to the difference between three and four, B. Two is less than the difference between three and four, C. Two is greater than the difference between three and four, D. Two may be less than or greater than the difference between three and four, E. None of the statement is correct
o: Two is equal to the difference between three and four
Two is less than the difference between three and four
Two is greater than the difference between three and four
Two may be less than or greater than the difference between three and four
None of the statement is correct
f: The difference between three and four is 1, and 2 is greater than 1.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q9) Which one of the following is different from the rest? A. House, B. Mountain, C. River, D. Forest, E. Sea
f: Mountain, river, forest and sea are natural features. A house is man-made.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q10) STUN is to NUTS as POTS is to?
f: NUTS is STUN written backwards, so POTS reversed is STOP.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q11) About the word FLOWER which one of the following statement is true? A. O comes after L and E, B. E comes before R and W, C. L comes after E and before F, D. W is in the middle of R and L, E. None of the statement is correct
o: O comes after L and E
E comes before R and W
L comes after E and before F
W is in the middle of R and L
None of the statement is correct
f: In F-L-O-W-E-R, L is 2nd and R is 6th, and W is 4th, so W lies between L and R. The other statements fail, for example E is after O and W.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q12) EF is to DG as JK is to?
f: E-1 = D and F+1 = G. Apply the same to JK: J-1 = I and K+1 = L.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q13) If a man goes 10 yards due north, then 10 yards due east, then 10 yards due south, then 10 yards due west, then: A. he is South of his starting place, B. he is north of his starting place, C. he has back to his starting place, D. he is south east of his starting place, E. he is west of his starting place
o: he is South of his starting place
he is north of his starting place
he has back to his starting place
he is south east of his starting place
he is west of his starting place
f: North and south cancel out, and east and west cancel out, so he ends where he began.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q14) What number when taken away from 12 gives 3 less than one-third of 27?
f: One-third of 27 is 9, and 3 less than 9 is 6. So 12 - x = 6, giving x = 6.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q15) Even is to Uneven as Violent is to: A. Aggressive, B. Friendly, C. Responsible, D. Sadest, E. Unkind
f: Even and uneven are opposites, so we need the opposite of violent, and friendly (gentle) is the best match. Aggressive and unkind are similar to violent.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q16) Bird is to Cage as Prisoner is to: A. Chains, B. Court, C. Freedom, D. Cell, E. Police
f: A bird is kept in a cage and a prisoner is kept in a cell.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q17) If A is as tall as D, C is shorter than A, B is taller than D, then: A. A is taller than B, B. C is as tall as D, C. B may be taller or shorter than C, D. C is shorter than D, E. B is shorter than A
o: C is as tall as D
B may be taller or shorter than C
f: A and D are equal in height and C is shorter than A, so C is shorter than D. Also B is taller than D, so B is taller than A as well.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q18) 1/3 is to 9 as 1/2 is to:
f: 1/3 becomes 9, which is the square of its reciprocal (3 squared). The reciprocal of 1/2 is 2, and 2 squared is 4.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q19) SPHERE is to CIRCLE as CUBE is to: A. Cuboid, B. Angle, C. Square, D. Point, E. None
f: A sphere is the three-dimensional form of a circle, so the matching two-dimensional form of a cube is a square.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q20) If L is to 1, T is to 2, E is to 3, R is to 4, add up the digits for the word LETTER, divide the total by 5 and give the result as your answer.
f: LETTER = L1 + E3 + T2 + T2 + E3 + R4 = 15, and 15 divided by 5 = 3.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q21) (2/4) is to (1:2) as (18/24) is to?
f: 2/4 is reduced to its simplest ratio 1:2, so 18/24 in simplest form is 3:4.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q22) Which of the following words has P but not A, has E but not D, has C but not L, has O but not I? A. Possible, B. Police, C. Pagoda, D. Pocket, E. Please
f: POCKET has P, E, C and O, and has no A, D, L or I. Possible has no C, police has I, pagoda has A and D, and please has A.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q23) What number when added to 14 gives 12 less than 30?
f: 12 less than 30 is 18, so 14 + x = 18 and x = 4.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q24) People smoke because: A. They get pleasure from it, B. They want to show off, C. It is a fashion these days, D. It makes them social, E. It is good for health
o: It is a fashion these days
f: The most common reason smokers give is the pleasure or relief they feel, driven by nicotine. Smoking is not good for health.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q25) Three men A, B, C are standing in a row so that A and C are standing to the left of B, and B and A are standing to the right of C. Who is standing in the middle? (the paper prints A and B in the first part, which is a typing slip for A and C)
f: A and C are left of B, so B is last. B and A are right of C, so C is first. That leaves A in the middle: C, A, B.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q26) Which would be the middle letter if the letters of the word SUBORDINATE are arranged in an alphabetical order?
f: The 11 letters in order are A, B, D, E, I, N, O, R, S, T, U. The 6th (middle) letter is N.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q27) Nazar is 2/3 times younger than his elder brother. His brother Rab Nawaz is 21 years old, what is the age of Nazar?
f: Nazar's age is 2/3 of 21 = 14 years.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q28) People buy cars: A. To sell them at profit, B. So that they reach places quickly
o: So that they reach places quickly
f: The usual purpose of buying a car is transport, to reach places quickly and comfortably.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q29) 63 is to 9 as 71 is to?
f: 63 gives 9 as the sum of its digits (6 + 3 = 9). So 71 gives 7 + 1 = 8.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q30) FOUR is to ELEVEN as THREE is to?
f: FOUR means 4 and ELEVEN means 11, which is 7 more. THREE means 3, and 3 + 7 = 10, which is TEN.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q31) COMPARE is to 7324615 as OPERA is to?

(Forces Academy Test 17 · Q32) If A is greater than B and B is less than C; then: A. A is equal to C, B. C is greater than A, C. A is greater than C, D. One cannot say whether A is equal to, greater than or less than C
o: One cannot say whether A is equal to, greater than or less than C
f: Both A and C are greater than B, but nothing links A and C directly, so their order cannot be decided.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q33) If the following are arranged in order of size, what would come in the middle? A. Book, B. Word, C. Chapter, D. Sentence, E. Paragraph
f: In increasing order: word, sentence, paragraph, chapter, book. The middle one is paragraph.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q34) Which one of the following is different from the rest? A. KOOL, B. LOOM, C. NOOS, D. MOON, E. WOOX
f: In KOOL, LOOM, MOON and WOOX the first and last letters are consecutive in the alphabet (K L, L M, M N, W X). In NOOS, N and S are not consecutive.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q35) You should not tell lies because: A. People will not trust you, B. You will always be found out, C. It is bad to do so, D. Truth is bitter, E. You will be punished
o: You will always be found out
It is bad to do so
f: The basic reason not to lie is moral: it is wrong. The other reasons are consequences that may or may not follow.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q36) What letter group comes next in the following series? JKLMNOPQ, JKLOPQ, JKPQ, ?
f: Each step removes the middle letters: JKLMNOPQ, JKLOPQ, JKPQ, then JQ.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q37) If B and C are at equal distances from A, B is south-west of A and A is south-east of C, then: A. C is north of B, B. B is south east of C, C. A is north west of B, D. C is south west of A
o: B is south east of C
A is north west of B
C is south west of A
f: Put A at the centre: B is south-west and C is north-west (since A is south-east of C) at the same distance. So C lies directly north of B.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q38) Which one of the following is different? A. Teacher, B. Patient, C. Lawyer, D. Doctor, E. Medicine
f: Teacher, patient, lawyer and doctor are all people. Medicine is a thing.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q39) Which one of the following is different? A. Lion, B. Wolf, C. Cat, D. Goat, E. Tiger
f: Lion, wolf, cat and tiger are meat-eating (carnivorous) animals. A goat eats plants.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q40) GREEN is to GRASS, CLEAR is to: A. Crystal, B. Light, C. Dark, D. Close, E. Tone
f: Green is the typical colour of grass, and clear is the typical quality of crystal.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q1) Re-arrange the letters ARTGN and find the middle letter.
f: ARTGN rearranges to GRANT, whose middle (third) letter is A.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q2) Which country is this, re-arranged: MERYGAN?
f: The letters of MERYGAN can be rearranged to form GERMANY.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q3) What is the last letter if DASAL is re-arranged?
f: DASAL rearranges to SALAD, so the last letter is D.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q5) If the 7th of the month falls 2 days preceding Sunday, then what is the day which follows the 21st of the same month?
f: Two days before Sunday is Friday, so the 7th is a Friday. The 14th and 21st are also Fridays, so the day following the 21st is Saturday.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q6) How many letters are there after K and before T in the following series: AABKMXJTTC?
f: Between K and the first T come M, X and J, which is 3 letters.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q7) If three days later the day after tomorrow is Friday, then what was yesterday?
f: The day after tomorrow is today + 2, and three days later is today + 5. If that is Friday, today is Sunday, so yesterday was Saturday.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q8) If 25th December is Sunday then 25th January will be?
f: There are 31 days from 25 December to 25 January and 31 = 4 x 7 + 3, so it is three days after Sunday, which is Wednesday.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q9) If 3 days after tomorrow is Wednesday, then what will be the day before yesterday?
f: Three days after tomorrow is today + 4. If that is Wednesday, today is Saturday, so the day before yesterday is Thursday.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q10) If 15th of February in a leap year is Sunday, then what will be the 15th of the next month?
f: February has 29 days in a leap year, so 15 March is 29 days later. 29 = 4 x 7 + 1, so it is one day after Sunday, which is Monday.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q11) Arrange BROTHER in alphabetical order and then indicate the letter left of the middle letter.
f: In alphabetical order it is B, E, H, O, R, R, T. The middle (4th) letter is O and the letter to its left is H.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q12) Which letter is next to the middle letter between H and P?
f: From H to P the letters are H, I, J, K, L, M, N, O, P (9 letters). The middle one is L, and the letter next to it is M.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q13) It takes two minutes to boil an egg. How many minutes to boil 5 eggs together?
f: The eggs boil at the same time in the same pot, so 5 eggs together also take 2 minutes.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q14) Amjad is taller than Asif, Akram is taller than Amjad. Who is the shortest?
f: Akram is taller than Amjad, who is taller than Asif, so Asif is the shortest.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q15) If Ali is brother of the son of Salman's son, what relation is Ali to Salman?
f: Salman's son has a son, and Ali is that boy's brother, so Ali is also a son of Salman's son. That makes him Salman's grandson.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q16) X and Y are brothers, B is A's brother but A is the mother of X, what is B to Y?
f: A is the mother of X and Y, and B is her brother, so B is the maternal uncle of Y.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q17) A husband and his wife have five married sons who have two children each. How many total family members are there?
f: Husband and wife are 2, five sons make 7, their five wives make 12, and 5 x 2 = 10 grandchildren make 22.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q18) Today is Maria's birthday, one year after today she will be twice as old as she was 10 years ago. How old is she now?
f: Let her age now be x. Then x + 1 = 2(x - 10), so x + 1 = 2x - 20 and x = 21.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q19) A man walked 1 km towards south and then turned right and walked another 1 km, in which direction is he?
f: Facing south, his right hand points west, so after turning right he walks west.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q20) Time on Ali's watch is quarter to three. If the hour hand is pointing towards east, then where is the minute hand pointing?
f: At quarter to three the hour hand is almost at 3 and points east, while the minute hand is at 9, exactly opposite, so it points west.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q21) A man walked 10 m towards east and then 5 m to North and then 10 m towards West, how far is he from the starting point?
f: The east and west moves cancel, so only the 5 m north remains. He is 5 m from the start.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q22) If London is to Thames then Lahore is to ____?
f: The River Thames flows through London and the River Ravi flows by Lahore.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q23) If K-2 is mountain then Gobi is ____?
f: K-2 is a mountain and the Gobi is a desert in Asia, mainly in Mongolia and northern China.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q24) Which one is different? Camel, Donkey, Bull, Mare
f: Camel, donkey and bull are general or male animal names, while a mare is specifically a female horse.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q25) If a = 3, b = 4 and c = 5 then a squared + b squared + 2abc = ?
(Forces Academy Test 20 · Q26) Smile: Glad then Sadness: ____?
f: Glad is a word that goes with smile, so a word that goes with sadness is gloomy.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q27) What comes next: 7/49, 6/36, ____, 4/16?
f: Each fraction is a number over its own square (7/49, 6/36, 4/16), so the missing one is 5/25.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q28) What is 30% of 30?
f: 30 percent of 30 is 0.30 x 30 = 9.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q29) If straight: Curve then decent: ____?
f: Straight and curve are opposites, so the opposite of decent is indecent (rude).

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q30) Which is different: Triangle, Rectangle, Square, Circle?
f: Triangle, rectangle and square are polygons with straight sides. A circle is a curved shape with no sides.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q47) In which city is Pakistan's largest nuclear power plant (K-2 and K-3, 1100 MW each) located?

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 29) In which year was the first Martial Law imposed in Pakistan?

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q32) In which year was the famous Urdu autobiography 'Shahab Nama' by Qudratullah Shahab published?

f: The Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Abdullah bin Huzafah Sahmi (RA) with his letter inviting Khusro Parvez to Islam.

f: The Indian Councils Act of 1909, known as the Minto-Morley Reforms, gave Muslims separate electorates.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 7) Who was the first Chief Martial Law Administrator of Pakistan?

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 18) On which date did President Yahya Khan dismantle One Unit (West Pakistan)?

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 19) On which date was Mangla Dam inaugurated?

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 55) What is the officially accepted height of Mount Everest, as announced by China and Nepal in 2020?
