q: Who is the President of Turkey?
f: Recep Tayyip Erdogan has been President of Turkey since 2014 and was re-elected in 2023.

q: Who was the brother of Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA)?
f: Walid bin Walid (RA) was the brother of Khalid bin Waleed (RA) and accepted Islam before him.

q: Who wrote the Punjabi qissa (folk romance) Sohni Mahiwal?
f: The best-known Punjabi version of Sohni Mahiwal is attributed to Fazal Shah (Sayyid Fazal Shah). Waris Shah is known for Heer Ranjha.

q: A car travels at 60 km/h and a train at twice that speed (120 km/h). How far does the train travel in 30 minutes?
f: 30 minutes is half an hour, so distance = 120 x 0.5 = 60 km.

q: Which sea lies between Greece and Italy?
f: The Ionian Sea lies between southern Italy and western Greece.

q: What is one third of 90?
f: 90 divided by 3 is 30.

q: Which country is the second largest in the world by area?
f: Russia is the largest country and Canada, with about 9.98 million square km, is second.

q: According to the 1962 constitution, how was the President of Pakistan elected?
o: By an Electoral College of Basic Democrats
By the Governors of the provinces
f: The 1962 constitution introduced indirect election of the President by an Electoral College made up of the elected Basic Democrats.

q: Against whom was the Battle of Khyber fought?
f: The Battle of Khyber (7 AH) was fought by the Muslims against the Jewish tribes living in the fortresses of Khyber.

q: Al Jazeera TV channel belongs to which country?
f: Al Jazeera is an Arabic news channel founded in 1996 and funded by the Qatari state, based in Doha.

q: Hazrat Ayesha (RA) was the daughter of whom?
f: Hazrat Ayesha (RA), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA).

q: Hazrat Hafsa (RA) was the daughter of whom?
f: Hazrat Hafsa (RA), a wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of Hazrat Umar bin Khattab (RA).

q: How many Khulafa-e-Rashideen (rightly guided caliphs) are there?
f: They are Hazrat Abu Bakr, Hazrat Umar, Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Ali (RA).

q: How many sons did Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) have?
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) had two sons who were prophets: Hazrat Ismail (AS) and Hazrat Ishaq (AS).

q: In which Ghazwa were the blessed teeth of the Prophet (PBUH) martyred?
f: The Prophet's (PBUH) front tooth was broken and he was wounded in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH.

q: In which Hijri year was the Treaty of Hudaibiya signed?
f: The Treaty of Hudaibiya was signed between the Prophet (PBUH) and the Quraysh in Dhul Qadah 6 AH (628 CE).

q: In which province is Khanpur Dam located?
f: Khanpur Dam is on the Haro River near Khanpur in Haripur district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: In which year did Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) migrate from Makkah to Madina?
f: The Hijrah took place in 622 AD, the 13th year of prophethood.

q: In which year did Pakistan join the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)?
f: Pakistan was a founding member of the OIC, which was formed in 1969.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam die?
f: Quaid-e-Azam died on 11 September 1948 in Karachi.

q: Kaleemullah is the title of which prophet?
f: Kaleemullah means the one who spoke with Allah, the title of Hazrat Musa (A.S).

q: Which organism causes malaria?
f: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites, spread to humans by the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.

q: What is the area of Punjab (Pakistan) in square kilometres?
f: Punjab covers about 205,344 square kilometres.

q: What is the capital of Chile?
f: Santiago is the capital of Chile.

q: What is the meaning of the word alter?
f: To alter means to change something or make it different.

q: What is the currency of Cuba?
f: Cuba uses the Cuban peso (CUP).

q: On what date did the War of Independence of the Subcontinent begin?
f: The 1857 War of Independence began at Meerut on 10 May 1857.

q: On what date did the Chauri Chaura incident happen?
f: A mob burned a police station at Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh on 4 February 1922.

q: Which is the highest plateau in the world?
f: The Tibetan Plateau averages over 4,500 m above sea level and is called the Roof of the World.

q: What is the maximum length of a cricket bat under the laws of cricket?
f: The Laws of Cricket limit a bat to 38 inches (96.52 cm) in length.

q: What is the length of the coastline of Pakistan?
f: Pakistan's Arabian Sea coastline is officially about 1,046 km.

q: What is the national tree of Pakistan?
f: The Deodar (Himalayan cedar) is the national tree of Pakistan.

q: What is the relation of Hazrat Ishaq (AS) with Hazrat Ismail (AS)?
f: Both were sons of Prophet Ibrahim (AS), so they were brothers (half-brothers, by different mothers).

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Abdul Muttalib with the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: Abdul Muttalib was the father of Abdullah, the Prophet's father, so he was the paternal grandfather. He looked after the Prophet after the death of his mother Hazrat Amina.

q: What is the range of the Pakistani surface-to-surface missile Ababeel?
f: Ababeel is a medium-range ballistic missile with a range of 2,200 km, as announced by ISPR after its first test.

q: Which word is a synonym of evident?
f: Evident means clearly seen or understood, which is obvious.

q: Which word is a synonym of prevalent?
f: Prevalent means common or existing widely at a given time, which is widespread.

q: What is the total number of seats of the Provincial Assembly of Punjab?
f: The Punjab Assembly has 371 seats: 297 general, 66 reserved for women and 8 for non-Muslims.

q: Where does the Bay of Pigs invasion of 1961 belong, that is, which country was invaded?
f: The Bay of Pigs (Bahia de Cochinos) is on the southern coast of Cuba. In April 1961 CIA-backed Cuban exiles landed there to overthrow Fidel Castro and failed.

q: In which year did Pakistan win the ICC Champions Trophy?
f: Pakistan beat India by 180 runs in the final at The Oval in London on 18 June 2017 under captain Sarfraz Ahmed.

q: In which year did Swat merge fully into Pakistan?
f: Swat acceded to Pakistan in 1947 but remained a princely state. It was merged fully on 28 July 1969, when the state was abolished.

q: In which year was the first constitution of Pakistan enforced?
f: The first constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956 and made Pakistan an Islamic Republic. It was abrogated by Ayub Khan's martial law in October 1958.

q: In which province is Manchar Lake located?
f: Manchar Lake is in Dadu district of Sindh, west of the Indus.

q: In which city is the Shah Jahan Mosque of Pakistan located?
f: The Shah Jahan Mosque was built in Thatta, Sindh, in the 17th century.

q: Which country was the first foreign buyer of the JF-17 Thunder fighter jet?
f: Myanmar was the first export customer of the JF-17, signing its deal around 2015 and receiving aircraft from 2018.

q: Which is the month of Allah (Shahrullah) in the Islamic calendar?
f: Ramadan is commonly called the month of Allah in Pakistani textbooks, because fasting is observed in it.

q: Which is the outermost planet of the solar system?
f: Neptune is the eighth and farthest planet from the Sun since Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

q: Which is the smallest continent?
f: Australia (Oceania) has an area of about 7.7 million square km, the smallest of the continents.

q: Which prophet was swallowed by a fish and stayed in its belly?
f: Hazrat Younus (A.S) was swallowed by a large fish and prayed to Allah from within its belly.

q: Who was the first man to embrace Islam?
f: Among adult free men, Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was the first to accept Islam.

q: Who inaugurated the State Bank of Pakistan?
f: Quaid-e-Azam inaugurated the State Bank of Pakistan in Karachi on 1 July 1948.

q: Who is the Chief Minister of Sindh?
f: Syed Murad Ali Shah of the Pakistan Peoples Party has been Chief Minister of Sindh since 2016 and won a third consecutive term in 2024.

q: Who is the national poet of Pakistan?
f: Allama Muhammad Iqbal is the national poet of Pakistan, called Shair-e-Mashriq.

q: Who was the first Pakistani to climb Mount Everest?
f: Nazir Sabir reached the summit of Mount Everest in 1999 as the first Pakistani to do so.

q: Who wrote the book Das Kapital?
f: Das Kapital, a critique of capitalism, was written by the German thinker Karl Marx. The first volume appeared in 1867.

q: Who wrote The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam?
f: Allama Iqbal wrote this book, which is based on his lectures delivered in 1928-29.

q: My brother's sister is your mother. What am I to you (taking me as male)?
f: My brother's sister is my sister, so your mother is my sister. I am therefore your mother's brother, that is your maternal uncle.

q: What is 1/3 of 1/10 of 120?
Who was the commander of the Muslim army in the Ghazwa (Battle) of Tabuk?
f: The Ghazwa of Tabuk (9 AH) was a campaign in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) himself led the Muslim army of about 30,000. A Ghazwa is by definition a battle in which the Prophet personally took part.

q: Which is the largest freshwater lake of Pakistan?
f: Manchar Lake in Sindh is generally regarded as Pakistan's largest freshwater lake.

q: In which year was the Lucknow Pact signed?
f: The Lucknow Pact was signed in December 1916. It was an agreement in which the Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.

q: Out of 1500 students, 1300 are present. What is the percentage of present students?
f: Percentage present = 1300 / 1500 x 100 = 86.67%.

q: What is one tenth of 90?
f: 90 divided by 10 is 9.

q: Abdul Qadir was a famous player of which sport?
f: Abdul Qadir was a Pakistani leg-spin bowler famous for his googly and wrist-spin.

q: The Khilafat Movement started after which event?
f: The Khilafat Movement began in 1919 after the defeat of the Ottoman Empire in World War I, which threatened the Caliphate.

q: Asadullah (Lion of Allah) is the title of which Sahabi?
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) was given the title Asadullah for his bravery. Hazrat Hamza is also called Asadullah.

q: Bolan Pass connects Quetta with which place?
f: The Bolan Pass is a natural route in Balochistan linking Quetta with the plains of Sibi and Dadhar.

q: From which institution did Quaid-e-Azam obtain his law degree?
f: Muhammad Ali Jinnah studied at Lincoln's Inn in London and was called to the bar in 1896.

q: How many faraiz (obligatory acts) of ghusl are there (Hanafi fiqh)?
f: The three faraiz of ghusl are rinsing the mouth, rinsing the nose and washing the whole body.

q: How many Makki surahs are there in the Quran?
f: Commonly 86 surahs are counted as Makki (revealed before the Hijrah) and 28 as Madani.

q: How many seats of the National Assembly of Pakistan are reserved for women?
f: Article 51 of the Constitution reserves 60 seats for women, filled by proportional representation.

q: In which city of India is Jallianwala Bagh located?
f: Jallianwala Bagh is a public garden in Amritsar, Punjab, India. British troops under General Dyer fired on a crowd there on 13 April 1919.

q: In which country were the Olympic Games postponed from 2020 and held in 2021 hosted?
f: The Tokyo Olympics, scheduled for 2020, were postponed because of Covid-19 and held in Japan in July-August 2021.

q: In which Hijri year did the tragedy of Karbala take place?
f: The martyrdom of Hazrat Hussain (RA) at Karbala took place on 10 Muharram 61 AH (680 CE).

q: In which Hijri year was Makkah conquered?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) conquered Makkah peacefully in Ramadan 8 AH (630 CE).

q: In which language did Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai write poetry?
f: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai (1689-1752) is the great Sufi poet of the Sindhi language.

q: In which Islamic month is Eid ul Azha celebrated?
f: Eid ul Azha is celebrated on 10 Dhul Hijjah, the twelfth month of the Islamic calendar, to remember the sacrifice of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).

q: In which Islamic month was the Quran first revealed?
f: The Quran began to be revealed in the month of Ramadan, on Laylat ul Qadr, in the cave of Hira.

q: In which province is Keenjhar Lake located?
f: Keenjhar Lake is near Thatta in Sindh.

q: In which year did India carry out its first nuclear test?
f: India conducted its first nuclear test (Smiling Buddha) at Pokhran in May 1974.

q: In which Hijri year was the Battle of Khyber (Khaybar) fought?
f: The Battle of Khaybar was fought in 7 AH (628 AD) against the Jewish fortresses of Khaybar.

q: Riyadh is the capital of which country?
f: Riyadh is the capital and largest city of Saudi Arabia.

q: Safiullah is the title of which prophet?
f: Safiullah means the chosen one of Allah and is the title of Hazrat Adam (A.S).

q: Tirana is the capital of which country?
f: Tirana is the capital and largest city of Albania in the Balkans.

q: Tripoli is the capital of which country?
f: Tripoli is the capital of Libya on the Mediterranean coast of North Africa.

q: Turkey is surrounded by the Aegean Sea, the Black Sea and which other sea?
f: Turkey has the Black Sea to the north, the Aegean to the west and the Mediterranean to the south.

q: How many faraiz (obligatory acts) does Hajj have according to the Hanafi school?
f: The three faraiz are Ihram, standing at Arafat (Wuquf) and Tawaf-e-Ziyarat.

q: What does PEMRA stand for?
o: Pakistan Education and Media Regulatory Authority
f: PEMRA is the Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority, which regulates TV and radio broadcasting.

q: What does POF stand for?
f: POF stands for Pakistan Ordnance Factories, which make arms and ammunition.

q: What is observed on 8 March every year?
f: 8 March is International Women's Day, celebrating women's achievements and rights.

q: What is Pakistan's rank in the world by population (2026)?
f: Pakistan is the fifth most populous country, after India, China, the United States and Indonesia.

q: What is sin X divided by cos X equal to?
f: By definition, tan X equals sin X over cos X.

q: What is the product of the three cube roots of unity?
f: The cube roots of unity are 1, w and w squared, and w cubed equals 1. Their product is 1 x w x w squared = w cubed = 1.

q: What is the currency of Turkey?
f: Turkey uses the Turkish lira.

q: When did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah present his Fourteen Points?
f: Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points at Delhi in March 1929, answering the Nehru Report.

q: Which is the hottest city of Pakistan?
f: Jacobabad in Sindh regularly records the highest temperatures in Pakistan, often over 50 degrees Celsius.

q: What is the integration of 1 with respect to x?
f: The derivative of x is 1, so the integral of 1 dx is x + C.

q: Which is the largest airport of Pakistan by area?
f: Islamabad International Airport opened in 2018 and is the largest in Pakistan by area (about 19 square km).

q: What is the largest city of Punjab by population?
f: Lahore is the capital of Punjab and its largest city.

q: What is the second pillar of Islam?
f: The five pillars in order are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj. So Salah is the second.

q: The Treaty of Versailles, which ended World War I with Germany, was signed in which year?
f: The treaty was signed on 28 June 1919 at the Palace of Versailles in France.

q: What was the relation of Abu Talib with the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Abu Talib was the son of Abdul Muttalib and a brother of the Prophet's father Abdullah. He raised the Prophet after the death of Abdul Muttalib.

q: What was the old (previous) name of Makkah mentioned in the Holy Quran?
f: The Holy Quran (Surah Al-Imran, verse 96) calls the place of the first house of worship Bakkah, which is an old name of Makkah. It was also known as Umm al-Qura.

q: In which year did Pakistan win the ICC T20 World Cup?
f: Pakistan beat Sri Lanka in the final at Lord's in 2009 under captain Younis Khan. It is their only T20 World Cup title.

q: In which year did the Hijrat (migration) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) to Madina take place, marking the start of the Hijri calendar?
f: The Prophet migrated from Makkah to Madina in 622 AD, which is 1 AH. The Hijri calendar was introduced in the time of Hazrat Umar (RA) and counts from this event.

q: Between which two parties was the Lucknow Pact signed?
o: Muslim League and the British Government
Muslim League and the Khaksar movement
f: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was an agreement between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League. Both parties agreed to a joint demand for self-government.

q: In which city was the OIC established at the first Islamic summit in 1969?
f: The first Islamic summit, which created the OIC, was held at Rabat in Morocco in 1969. Jeddah is the permanent headquarters of the OIC, not the place of its founding.

q: In which country is Mina, the valley where pilgrims stay during Hajj?
f: Mina is a valley a few kilometres east of Makkah in Saudi Arabia.

q: In which province is Ranikot (Rani Fort) located?
f: Ranikot Fort lies in the Kirthar foothills near Sann in Jamshoro district, Sindh.

q: Where is the Pakistan Navy headquarters?
f: Naval Headquarters of the Pakistan Navy is in Islamabad.

q: Where is the shrine of Baba Fariduddin Ganj Shakar?
f: Baba Farid Ganj Shakar is buried in Pakpattan, Punjab.

q: Which country hosted the first Football World Cup in 1930?
f: The first FIFA World Cup was held in 1930 in Uruguay, which also won it.

q: Which is the biggest province of Pakistan by area?
f: Balochistan covers about 347,000 square km, roughly 44 percent of Pakistan.

q: Which SAARC country has the highest literacy rate?
f: The Maldives has a literacy rate of about 98 to 99 percent, the highest among SAARC countries, with Sri Lanka close behind.

q: Which Sahabi served the Holy Prophet (PBUH) for ten years?
f: Anas bin Malik (R.A) was given to the Prophet as a servant at Madina as a boy and served him for about ten years.

q: Who designed the flag of Pakistan?
f: The national flag was designed by Syed Amir-ud-Din Kedwaii on the basis of the Muslim League flag. The Constituent Assembly adopted it on 11 August 1947.

q: Who gave the name Pakistan?
f: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali coined the name Pakistan in 1933 in the pamphlet Now or Never.

q: Who is the President of Iran?
f: Masoud Pezeshkian won the 2024 snap election and took office in July 2024.

q: Who is the youngest recipient of the Nishan-e-Haider?
f: Pilot Officer Rashid Minhas was only 20 when he died in 1971 stopping a traitor pilot, and got the award.

q: Who led the Quit India Movement of 1942?
f: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942 with the call Do or Die.

q: Who rebuilt the Holy Kaaba with his son?
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) rebuilt the Kaaba with his son Hazrat Ismail (AS).

q: Who was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army?
f: General Sir Frank Messervy was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army from August 1947 to February 1948.

q: Who was the world's first woman Prime Minister?
f: Sirimavo Bandaranaike of Sri Lanka became the world's first woman Prime Minister in 1960.

q: Who was the President of the first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?
f: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was elected President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 August 1947.

q: Which team won the cricket World Cup in 1999?
f: Australia beat Pakistan by eight wickets in the 1999 final at Lord's.

q: A man going towards north turns left after some time, then turns right. In which direction is he now facing?
f: Facing north, a left turn makes him face west. A right turn from west makes him face north again.

q: What is one third of 10% of 120?
f: 10% of 120 is 12, and one third of 12 is 4.

q: What is the derivative of a constant?
f: A constant does not change as x changes, so its rate of change is zero.

q: Which one is different from the others: monkey, panda, baboon, chimpanzee?
f: Monkey, baboon and chimpanzee are primates, while the panda is a bear.

q: What was the official name of Pakistan under the 1956 Constitution?
f: The 1956 Constitution declared the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, ending its dominion status.

q: Under the 1956 Constitution, the President of Pakistan was elected by:
o: An electoral college of members of the National and Provincial Assemblies
f: The 1956 Constitution provided for the President to be elected by the members of the National Assembly and the Provincial Assemblies.

q: In whose house in Madinah did the camel of the Prophet (PBUH) stop after the Hijrat?
f: The Prophet's camel Qaswa knelt near the house of Hazrat Abu Ayyub Ansari (Khalid bin Zayd), and he stayed there until his own quarters and mosque were built.

q: In which battle was the tooth of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) broken?
f: The Prophet's lower front tooth was broken and he was wounded on the face during the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH, after the archers left their post.

q: In which year did the United Nations come into being?
f: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945 after ratification by the main founding members.

q: With which wife of the Prophet (PBUH) was the compiled copy of the Quran kept after Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) had it collected?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) had the Quran compiled in book form; it passed to Hazrat Umar (RA) and then was kept with his daughter Hazrat Hafsa (RA), the Prophet's wife. Hazrat Usman (RA) later borrowed it to prepare copies.

q: Which cricketer broke Shahid Afridi's record of the fastest century in ODIs (37 balls, 1996)?
f: New Zealand's Corey Anderson scored a century off 36 balls against the West Indies in January 2014 and broke Afridi's 17-year-old record.

q: A train is moving at 90 km/h. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes?
f: 12 minutes = 12/60 = 1/5 hour. Distance = 90 x 1/5 = 18 km.

q: In which city is the Wazir Khan Mosque located?
f: The Wazir Khan Mosque stands in the walled city of Lahore. It was built in 1634-35 in the Mughal era.

q: On which river is the Diamer Bhasha Dam being built?
f: The Diamer Bhasha Dam is being built on the Indus River in Gilgit-Baltistan, near Chilas.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Ali (RA) with Hazrat Abdul Muttalib?
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib, and Abu Talib was a son of Abdul Muttalib. So Hazrat Ali was his grandson.

q: Which pass connects Pakistan with China?
f: The Khunjerab Pass in the Karakoram links Gilgit-Baltistan with Xinjiang in China.

q: With the help of which country was Pakistan Steel Mills built?
f: Pakistan Steel Mills at Karachi was set up with Soviet technical and financial assistance in the 1970s.

q: In which district is Khanpur Dam located?
f: Khanpur Dam is built on the Haro River near Khanpur town in Haripur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: In which year was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) born?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) was born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant, taken as 570 AD in Pakistani textbooks.

q: After how many years of independence did Pakistan get its first constitution?
f: Pakistan became independent in 1947 and its first constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956, nearly 9 years later.

q: At what age (approximately) did the last revelation descend upon Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: Revelation began when the Prophet (PBUH) was 40 and continued for about 23 years, so the last revelation came at about age 63.

q: Boris Johnson served as Prime Minister (2019-2022) of which country?
f: Boris Johnson led the Conservative Party and was Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from July 2019 to September 2022.

q: For what purpose was the Khilafat Movement started?
f: Indian Muslims started it to save the Ottoman Caliph and the Ottoman Empire after World War I.

q: Harappa, a major city of the Indus Valley Civilization, was situated on the bank of which river?
f: Harappa lies in Sahiwal district of Punjab beside the (now partly dried) bed of the River Ravi.

q: Approximately how many disbelievers (Quraish) were killed in the Battle of Badr?
f: About 70 Quraish fighters were killed and about 70 were taken prisoner at Badr.

q: How many faraiz (obligatory acts) of wudu are there (Hanafi fiqh)?
f: The four faraiz are washing the face, washing the arms up to and including the elbows, wiping a quarter of the head, and washing the feet up to the ankles.

q: How many rukus are there in the Holy Quran (Pakistani edition)?
f: Pakistani printed copies of the Quran are divided into 540 rukus, marked by the letter Ain in the margin.

q: In which battle did Allah help the Muslims with angels?
f: The Quran (Surah Al-Imran and Al-Anfal) says Allah sent angels to help the Muslims at Badr.

q: Near which city in Punjab are the ruins of the Indus Valley site of Harappa?
f: The ruins of Harappa lie near the town of Harappa in Sahiwal district of Punjab, Pakistan. The site was first excavated in the 1920s.

q: Near which city is the Rohtas Fort located?
f: Rohtas Fort is near Dina in Jhelum district, Punjab. Sher Shah Suri built it in the 16th century.

q: In which direction of Pakistan is India located?
f: India lies along the eastern border of Pakistan.

q: In which months does the monsoon season occur in Pakistan?
f: The monsoon rains reach Pakistan in July and last until about September.

q: In which mountain range is K2, the second highest peak in the world, located?
f: K2 (8,611 m) lies on the Pakistan-China border in the Karakoram range.

q: Which is the last surah of the Holy Quran?
f: Surah An-Nas is number 114 and is the last surah in the order of the Quran.

q: In which year did Pakistan co-host the ICC Cricket World Cup together with India and Sri Lanka?
f: The 1996 World Cup was jointly hosted by Pakistan, India and Sri Lanka.

q: In which year was NATO founded?
f: NATO was founded by the North Atlantic Treaty signed in Washington in April 1949.

q: In which year was Sindh separated from the Bombay Presidency?
f: Sindh became a separate province on 1 April 1936 under the Government of India Act 1935.

q: Israel is the title of which prophet?
f: Israel was the title of Hazrat Yaqub (A.S). The Children of Israel are his descendants.

q: Jihad is a word of which language?
f: Jihad is an Arabic word meaning striving or struggle.

q: Lira is the currency of which country?
f: The Turkish lira is the official currency of Turkey.

q: On which side of Asia is Pakistan located?
f: Pakistan lies in South Asia (the Indian subcontinent).

q: The first five ayats revealed to the Prophet (PBUH) were from which surah?
f: The first five ayats revealed in the cave of Hira belong to Surah Al-Alaq, beginning with Iqra.

q: The Lowari Pass connects Chitral with which place?
f: The Lowari Pass links Chitral with Dir, and so with the rest of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: The rate of change is called what?
f: In calculus the derivative measures the rate of change of a quantity with respect to another.

q: The Shimla Agreement of 1972 was signed between Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and whom?
f: After the 1971 war, Bhutto and the Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi signed the agreement at Shimla on 2 July 1972.

q: What does Ahl-e-Bait mean?
f: Ahl means people or family and Bait means house, so Ahl-e-Bait is 'people of the house'.

q: What does LOC stand for in the context of Kashmir?
f: LOC stands for Line of Control, the military control line dividing Indian- and Pakistan-administered Kashmir.

q: What does Saifullah mean?
f: Saif means sword and Allah is God, so Saifullah means Sword of Allah.

q: What does WAPDA stand for?
f: WAPDA stands for Water and Power Development Authority.

q: What does yellow journalism mean?
f: Yellow journalism is journalism that exaggerates or sensationalises news to attract readers rather than reporting facts carefully.

q: K2, the second highest mountain in the world, is also known as what?
f: K2 is also known as Mount Godwin-Austen, after the British surveyor Henry Godwin-Austen, and as Chogori.

q: What is the capital of Armenia?
f: Yerevan is the capital and largest city of Armenia.

q: What is the capital of Libya?
f: Tripoli is the capital and largest city of Libya.

q: What is the capital of Punjab (Pakistan)?
f: Lahore is the provincial capital of Punjab.

q: What is the closest meaning of selfless?
f: A selfless person thinks of others before himself, which is what altruistic means.

q: What is the currency of Saudi Arabia?
f: Saudi Arabia uses the Saudi riyal.

q: On what date is Youm-e-Takbeer observed in Pakistan?
f: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests at Chagai on 28 May 1998, observed yearly as Youm-e-Takbeer.

q: Which is the fastest bird in the world (in a dive)?
f: The peregrine falcon reaches over 320 km/h in its hunting dive, making it the fastest animal on Earth.

q: Which surah contains the first verses of the Quran to be revealed?
f: The first five verses revealed to the Prophet (SAW) in the Cave of Hira were from Surah Al-Alaq, beginning with Iqra.

q: What is the full form of OPEC?
o: Organization of Producing and Exporting Countries
Organization of Power and Energy Countries
f: OPEC stands for Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, a group of oil producing nations.

q: What is the highest civil award of Pakistan?
f: Nishan-e-Pakistan is the highest civil award given by the state of Pakistan.

q: What is the highest military award of Pakistan?
f: Nishan-e-Haider is the highest gallantry award of Pakistan, given for extraordinary bravery in battle.

q: What is the highest military award of the Netherlands?
f: The Military William Order is the oldest and highest honour of the Netherlands.

q: Where is the hottest recorded air temperature in the world, 56.7 degrees Celsius (1913)?
f: The official record of 56.7 degrees Celsius (134 F) was measured at Furnace Creek in Death Valley, California, in July 1913.

q: What is the largest city of Balochistan by population?
f: Quetta is the provincial capital and the most populous city of Balochistan.

q: What is the largest ocean in the world?
f: The Pacific Ocean covers about 165 million square km, roughly a third of the Earth.

q: What is the approximate length of the Amazon River according to common textbooks?
f: Most textbooks give the Amazon length as about 6,400 km.

q: Which is the longest river of Europe?
f: The Volga in Russia is about 3,530 km long and is the longest river in Europe.

q: What is the meaning of Ijtihad?
o: To exert effort to reach a legal ruling
f: Ijtihad means to strive or exert one's utmost effort, in Islamic law to derive a ruling from the Quran and Sunnah.

q: What is the meaning of Jihad?
f: Jihad comes from an Arabic root meaning to strive or struggle in the way of Allah.

q: Who was the mother of Hazrat Ismail (AS)?
f: Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Hajra.

q: What is the national game of Pakistan?
f: Field hockey is commonly given as the national game of Pakistan.

q: What is the national language of Pakistan?
f: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan under the Constitution.

q: In the usual order of the oceans by size, what is the number of the Indian Ocean?
f: By size the order is Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic, so the Indian Ocean is third.

q: What was the old name of Madina?
f: Madina was known as Yathrib before the Prophet (PBUH) migrated there in 622 CE.

q: What is the land between two rivers called?
f: A doab is the strip of land between two converging rivers.

q: The Quaid-e-Azam Residency, where Quaid-e-Azam spent his last days, is located in which place?
f: The Quaid-e-Azam Residency is in Ziarat, Balochistan. The Quaid stayed there in 1948 during his final illness.

q: What is the normal term of office of the Secretary General of the United Nations?
f: The Secretary General is appointed by the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council for a five-year term, which can be renewed.

q: What is the total number of Ghazwat (battles in which the Prophet (PBUH) took part personally)?
f: Most Pakistani textbooks give 27 Ghazwat. Sources differ, as some list 26 or 29.

q: What is the total number of surahs in the Holy Quran?
f: The Quran has 114 surahs.

q: Which was the first battle fought by the Muslims?
f: The Battle of Badr, fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH, was the first major battle between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.

q: Which city was the first capital of Pakistan?
f: Karachi served as the capital from 1947 when Pakistan was created. The capital was shifted to Rawalpindi in 1959 and then to Islamabad in the 1960s.

q: What was the profession of Mother Teresa?
f: Mother Teresa was a Roman Catholic nun who founded the Missionaries of Charity in Kolkata in 1950 to serve the poor and the sick.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Ismail (AS) with Hazrat Ibrahim (AS)?
f: Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Hajra. He was the elder of Ibrahim's two sons.

q: When did Namaz (salah) become farz (obligatory) for Muslims?
f: The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the night of Miraj, roughly five years before the Hijrat. Before this, the Muslims offered some prayers without a fixed five-time rule.

q: In which year was Basic Democracy introduced in Pakistan by Ayub Khan?
f: President Ayub Khan introduced the Basic Democracies system through an order in October 1959. It had a five-tier structure with 80,000 Basic Democrats who elected the president.

q: In which year were the first general elections held under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan?
f: The 1973 Constitution came into force on 14 August 1973 and the first general elections under it were held in March 1977.

q: Where and when was the All-India Muslim League founded?
f: The Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 in Dhaka during the Muhammadan Educational Conference, at the house of Nawab Salimullah Khan.

q: Where does the Karakoram Highway (KKH) start in Pakistan?
f: In Pakistan the Karakoram Highway is commonly described as starting at Hassan Abdal and running north through Abbottabad, Gilgit and Sost to the Khunjerab Pass.

q: Where is Lake Victoria located?
f: Lake Victoria is shared by Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania in East Africa.

q: In which city is Nishtar Hospital located?
f: Nishtar Hospital is a large teaching hospital in Multan, Punjab.

q: Where is the Bay of Biscay located?
o: Atlantic Ocean, off the coasts of France and Spain
f: The Bay of Biscay is a gulf of the north-east Atlantic Ocean, bordered by the west coast of France and the north coast of Spain.

q: Which agreement was signed after the 1971 war between Pakistan and India?
f: The Shimla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi.

q: Which body regulates the distribution of Indus river system water among the provinces of Pakistan?
f: The Indus River System Authority (IRSA) was set up in 1992 to apportion water among the provinces under the Water Apportionment Accord.

q: Which city of Pakistan is called the Manchester of Pakistan?
f: Faisalabad is the centre of Pakistan's textile industry, like Manchester in England.

q: Which country is known as the land of a thousand lakes?
f: Finland has roughly 188,000 lakes, giving it this nickname.

q: Which city is known as the city of mosques?
f: Dhaka, capital of Bangladesh, is known as the City of Mosques because of its thousands of mosques.

q: Which is the correct spelling?
f: The correct word has a double c and a double m: accommodation.

q: Which is the second most populous country of the world?
f: India overtook China in 2023 to become the most populous country, so China is now second.

q: Which is the world's third longest river?
f: By length the Nile and Amazon are first and second, and the Yangtze in China is third at about 6,300 km.

q: Which mountain range is mainly associated with Afghanistan?
f: The Hindu Kush range runs through central and northeastern Afghanistan into Pakistan.

q: Which is the highest mountain range of Pakistan?
f: The Karakoram range contains K2 (8,611 m), the highest peak in Pakistan.

q: Which organization was formed by Turkey, Pakistan and Iran in 1964?
f: Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) was formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey.

q: Which of the following is a permanent member of the UN Security Council?
f: The five permanent members are the USA, UK, France, Russia and China.

q: Who gave the idea of SAARC?
o: J. R. Jayewardene of Sri Lanka
f: President Ziaur Rahman of Bangladesh proposed regional cooperation in South Asia in 1980, leading to SAARC.

q: Which company is responsible for inventing the iPhone, launched in 2007 under its co-founder Steve Jobs?
f: Apple Inc. launched the first iPhone in 2007, with Steve Jobs presenting it.

q: Who is the Secretary General of the United Nations?
f: Antonio Guterres has held the post since 2017 and his term ends on 31 December 2026.

q: Who suggested the name of the United Nations (UNO)?
f: US President Franklin D. Roosevelt suggested the name United Nations, first used in the Declaration of 1 January 1942.

q: Who was the ruler of Pakistan after Yahya Khan?
f: Yahya Khan handed over power in December 1971 after the fall of Dhaka, and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto became President and Chief Martial Law Administrator.

q: Who was the first Mughal emperor of India?
f: Babur founded the Mughal Empire after defeating Ibrahim Lodhi at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.

q: Who was the first woman martyred in Islam?
f: Hazrat Sumayyah bint Khayyat (RA) was killed by Abu Jahl for refusing to give up Islam.

q: Who was the first person in space?
f: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth aboard Vostok 1 on 12 April 1961.

q: Who was the second caliph (Khalifa) of Islam?
f: Hazrat Umar bin Khattab (RA) became the second caliph in 13 AH after being nominated by Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA). He ruled for about ten years.

q: Who accompanied the Prophet (PBUH) during the migration to Madinah?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) travelled with the Prophet (PBUH) and they hid in the cave of Thawr.

q: Who wrote Shah Jo Risalo?
f: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai composed the Sindhi poetry collection Shah Jo Risalo.

q: With which surah does the Holy Quran begin?
f: The Quran opens with Surah Al-Fatihah, which has seven verses.

q: Ali walks towards north, then turns left, and after some time turns left again. In which direction does he face now?
f: North then left is west. A second left from west is south.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day is the 15th day of that month?
f: From the 2nd to the 15th is 13 days, and 13 divided by 7 leaves remainder 6. Moving 6 day(s) forward from Monday gives Sunday.

q: If the vector (cross) product of two non-zero vectors is zero, how are the two vectors related?
f: The magnitude of the cross product is |A||B| sin(theta). It is zero only when sin(theta) = 0, so the vectors are parallel (or anti-parallel).

q: In a class of 30 students, 2/3 are boys. How many girls are there?
Out of 500 students, 360 are present. What is the percentage of present students?
f: Percentage present = 360 / 500 x 100 = 72%.

q: What is 60% of 90?
What is a quarter of 120?
f: 120 divided by 4 is 30.

q: Which letter comes next: A, C, F, J, O, ?
f: The gaps between letters are +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next gap is +6. O is the 15th letter and the 21st is U.

q: Your mother is my brother's sister. What is the relation between you and me?
f: My brother's sister is my own sister, so your mother is my sister. Therefore I am your maternal uncle.

q: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, which three rivers were allotted to Pakistan?
f: The 1960 Indus Waters Treaty gave the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab to Pakistan.

q: Babusar Pass connects the Kaghan Valley with which town?
f: Babusar Pass links Kaghan Valley in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to Chilas in Gilgit-Baltistan.

q: The ELISA test is used to diagnose which disease?
f: ELISA detects antibodies or antigens in blood and is the standard screening test for HIV infection. Candidates who said tuberculosis were wrong.

q: Mahatma Gandhi was a famous leader of which country?
f: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi led the Indian independence movement and the Indian National Congress.

q: How many Madani surahs does the Holy Quran contain, according to the common Pakistani textbook count?
f: Of the 114 surahs, 86 are Makki and 28 are Madani. Madani surahs were revealed after the Hijrat.

q: In which year were the first Commonwealth Games (then called the British Empire Games) held?
f: The first British Empire Games were held in Hamilton, Canada, in 1930. They were later renamed the Commonwealth Games.

q: Mohenjo-daro is located near which city of Sindh?
f: Mohenjo-daro, a city of the Indus Valley Civilisation, lies in Larkana District on the right bank of the Indus.

q: What are both houses of the Parliament of Pakistan (Senate and National Assembly) together called?
f: Under the 1973 Constitution the Parliament, called Majlis-e-Shoora, consists of the President, the Senate and the National Assembly.

q: How many Muslims took part in the Battle of Badr?
f: The Muslim army at Badr numbered about 313 men, against roughly 1000 Quraish soldiers.

q: In which province of Pakistan are the Chagai Hills located?
f: The Chagai Hills lie in Chagai district in the northwest of Balochistan, near the Afghan and Iranian borders.

q: The 1996 Cricket World Cup was co-hosted by Pakistan along with which two countries?
f: The 1996 World Cup was jointly hosted by Pakistan, India and Sri Lanka. Sri Lanka won the title by beating Australia in the final at Lahore.

q: Which country is the world's largest exporter of arms?
f: According to SIPRI, the United States is the largest arms exporter and supplies around 40 percent of global arms exports.

q: Which game is played on a court enclosed by four walls?
f: Squash is played in a closed court with four walls, and the ball may be hit off any wall except for out-of-play lines.

q: Which prophet is mentioned most often by name in the Quran?
f: Hazrat Musa (AS) is named about 136 times in the Quran, more than any other prophet.

q: Which prophet was given a great kingdom, including rule over the jinn and the winds?
f: Allah gave Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) a unique kingdom, with jinn, birds and winds under his command.

q: Who said that the life of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is the practical form of the Quran?
f: When asked about the Prophet's character, Hazrat Ayesha replied that his character was the Quran.

q: Who headed the committee that compiled the Holy Quran in one book during the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA), on the advice of Hazrat Umar (RA) after the Battle of Yamama, assigned Hazrat Zaid bin Sabit (RA), the Prophet's scribe of revelation, to collect the Quran. He had memorised the Quran and written much of it down in the Prophet's lifetime.

q: Which Sahabi is known by the title Zun-Noorain (Possessor of Two Lights)?
f: Hazrat Usman (RA) married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (SAW), one after the other, so he was called Zun-Noorain.

q: Zun-Noorain (Zunnurain), meaning 'possessor of two lights', is the title of which Companion of the Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Hazrat Usman (R.A) married two daughters of the Prophet (PBUH), Hazrat Ruqayyah and later Hazrat Umm Kulthum (R.A), one after the other. For this reason he is called Zun-Noorain.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, how many houses does the Parliament of Pakistan have?
f: The Parliament consists of the National Assembly (lower house) and the Senate (upper house), plus the President.

q: In which city is the Badshahi Mosque located?
f: The Badshahi Mosque stands in Lahore opposite the Lahore Fort.

q: Which is the world's largest uranium producing country?
f: Kazakhstan has been the top uranium producer since 2009 and supplied about 39 percent of world mine output in 2024.

q: 340 out of 500: what is the percentage?
If today is Monday, what day will it be the day after tomorrow?
f: Tomorrow is Tuesday, so the day after tomorrow is Wednesday.

q: On which date was the Battle of Uhud fought?
f: The Battle of Uhud was fought on 7 Shawwal 3 AH (March 625 CE) near Mount Uhud, close to Madina.

q: If A and B are disjoint sets, what is A intersection B?
f: Disjoint sets have no common element, so their intersection is the empty set.

q: What is a Ruku in the Holy Quran?
o: A section of verses marked in the text
f: A ruku in the Quran is a group of verses forming a section, marked with the letter ain in the margin.

q: Which is the world's largest silver producing country?
f: Mexico leads the world in mined silver, at about 173 million ounces in 2025, ahead of Peru and China.

q: What is 1/3 of 120?
What is a quarter of one tenth of 90?
f: One tenth of 90 is 9, and a quarter of 9 is 9 / 4 = 2.25.

q: What is an angle less than 90 degrees called?
f: An angle smaller than 90 degrees is called an acute angle.

q: What is one third of 120?
f: One third of 120 is 120 / 3 = 40.

q: A diagonal matrix is always what type of matrix?
f: A diagonal matrix has non-zero entries only on the main diagonal, and a main diagonal exists only for a square matrix. So every diagonal matrix is a square matrix.

q: Abdul Sattar Edhi is associated with which city of Pakistan?
f: Edhi made Karachi the base of his welfare work, and the Edhi Foundation is headquartered there.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, who resolves a dispute between the National Assembly and the Senate?
f: Under Article 70, a bill on which the two houses disagree is settled by a joint sitting of both houses, decided by a majority of the total members present.

q: According to the Islamic calendar, in which month did Pakistan become independent?
f: Pakistan came into being on 14 August 1947, which was 27 Ramazan 1366 AH, a Friday and the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) according to common belief.

q: Against whom did Shahid Afridi score his record 37-ball century in 1996?
f: Afridi hit the then fastest ODI century off 37 balls against Sri Lanka at Nairobi in October 1996.

q: Against whom was the Battle of Tabuk fought?
f: In 9 AH the Prophet (PBUH) led an army to Tabuk to face the Byzantine force, but no fighting took place.

q: By whom was the Objectives Resolution passed?
f: It was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan and passed by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan on 12 March 1949.

q: By whose hand was Hazrat Hamza martyred in the Battle of Uhud?
f: Wahshi bin Harb, a slave of Jubayr bin Mutim, killed Hazrat Hamza with a spear on the order of Hind.

q: The Coastal Highway connects Gwadar with which city?
f: The Makran Coastal Highway (N-10) runs along the Arabian Sea coast from Karachi to Gwadar.

q: The Danube is the second longest river of which continent?
f: The Danube, about 2,850 km long, is the second longest river in Europe after the Volga.

q: Desert Fox is the title of whom?
f: Field Marshal Erwin Rommel earned the name Desert Fox for his skilled command of the German Afrika Korps in North Africa.

q: Diphtheria is a disease of which part of the body?
f: Diphtheria is a bacterial infection that mainly affects the throat and upper airways.

q: Fill in the blank: He wasted his time ___ TV.
f: After the expression waste time, the gerund (-ing form) is used, so watching is correct.

q: Fill in the blank: The Pacific is ___ than the Arctic Ocean.
f: The sentence compares two things and uses than, so the comparative deeper is needed.

q: For the Khilafat Movement, Muslims of India migrated towards which country?
f: During the Hijrat Movement of 1920, thousands of Muslims left India for Afghanistan as a protest against British rule.

q: From which city did the Urdu-Hindi controversy start in 1867?
f: In 1867 Hindus of Banaras demanded that Hindi in Devanagari script replace Urdu in government offices, starting the controversy.

q: The Gulf of Siam, now known as the Gulf of Thailand, mainly lies in which country?
f: The Gulf of Siam is the old name of the Gulf of Thailand, which borders Thailand mainly, as well as Cambodia, Vietnam and Malaysia.

q: Hafeez Kardar was a player of which sport?
f: Abdul Hafeez Kardar was a Pakistani cricketer and the first captain of Pakistan in Test cricket.

q: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) belonged to which tribe?
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) belonged to the Quraish tribe, to its clan Banu Hashim.

q: How many ayats (verses) does Surah Al-Fatiha, the first surah of the Quran, have?
f: Surah Al-Fatiha has seven ayats, which is why it is also called Sab'a al-Mathani (the seven oft-repeated verses).

q: How many ayats were revealed in the first revelation (Surah Al-Alaq) to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: The first revelation in the Cave of Hira consisted of the first five ayats of Surah Al-Alaq, beginning with Iqra.

q: How many continents are there in the world?
f: The seven continents are Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia (Oceania).

q: How many Hajj did the Holy Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) perform after his migration to Madina?
f: He performed only one Hajj, in 10 AH, known as Hajjat-ul-Wada (the Farewell Pilgrimage).

q: How many Muslims were in the army at the Battle of Uhad (Uhud) in the end?
f: About 1000 set out, but Abdullah bin Ubayy withdrew with about 300 men, leaving about 700 Muslims.

q: How many players are there in a football team on the field?
f: A football team fields eleven players including the goalkeeper.

q: How many ayats are there in total in Surah Al-Baqarah?
f: Surah Al-Baqarah, the longest surah, has 286 ayats.

q: For how many years did the Holy Prophet (SAW) live in Madina after the Hijrah?
f: He migrated to Madina in 622 AD (1 AH) and passed away there in 632 AD (11 AH), about ten years later.

q: In how many fields is the Nobel Prize awarded today?
f: The Nobel Prizes are given in Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, Peace and Economics, which is six fields.

q: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, which rivers were allotted to India?
f: The 1960 treaty gave the three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas and Sutlej) to India and the western rivers to Pakistan.

q: In which city is the historic Bala Hisar Fort located?
f: Bala Hisar Fort stands in Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It overlooks the old city.

q: In which city is the Arfa Karim Tower located?
f: The Arfa Karim Tower is in Lahore, Punjab, near Gulberg. It is named after the young computer prodigy Arfa Karim.

q: In which city was the All India Muslim League founded in 1906?
f: The All India Muslim League was founded in Dhaka in December 1906 at the Muslim Educational Conference, hosted by Nawab Salimullah Khan.

q: In which country does the Orange River mainly flow?
f: The Orange River is the longest river in South Africa and flows westward to the Atlantic Ocean. It rises in the mountains of Lesotho.

q: In which country is the volcano Mount Etna located?
f: Mount Etna is on the island of Sicily, Italy. It is one of the most active volcanoes in the world.

q: In which country were the 2016 Olympic Games held?
f: The 2016 Summer Olympics were held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

q: In which direction of Pakistan is Iran located?
f: Iran lies to the west of Pakistan, bordering Balochistan.

q: In which Chinese city did the Covid-19 outbreak first appear in December 2019?
f: The first cases of Covid-19 were reported in Wuhan, the capital of Hubei province, China, in December 2019.

q: In which game is the agricultural shot played?
f: The agricultural shot is a cricket stroke in which the batsman swings the bat across the line in a cow-corner heave, like a farmer swinging a scythe.

q: In which Ghazwa did angels come to help the Muslims?
f: The Quran says that angels helped the Muslims in the Battle of Badr in 2 AH.

q: In which Hijri year was the Battle of Badr fought?
f: The Battle of Badr was fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH (624 CE).

q: In which province is the Kharan Desert located?
f: The Kharan Desert lies in Kharan district of Balochistan.

q: In which quadrant does the point (-2, -3) lie?
f: Both the x-coordinate (-2) and the y-coordinate (-3) are negative, which is the third quadrant.

q: In which surah is Ayat-ul-Kursi found?
f: Ayat-ul-Kursi is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah.

q: In which war was Major Aziz Bhatti martyred?
f: Major Aziz Bhatti was martyred on 12 September 1965 defending the BRB canal sector near Lahore.

q: In which year did the Khilafat delegation led by Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar go to England?
f: The delegation went to England in 1920 to plead the case of the Ottoman Caliphate before Prime Minister Lloyd George.

q: In which year did the Quit India Movement start?
f: Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942.

q: The Olympic Games were cancelled in which year of World War 1?
f: The 1916 Berlin Olympics were cancelled because of the war; the games are held every four years, so 1914 was not an Olympic year.

q: In which year were the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms enacted as the Government of India Act?
f: The Government of India Act 1919 implemented the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, which introduced dyarchy in the provinces.

q: In which year was the first Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences awarded?
f: The economics prize was first awarded in 1969 to Ragnar Frisch and Jan Tinbergen.

q: In which year was the Kargil war fought?
f: The Kargil conflict between India and Pakistan took place from May to July 1999.

q: In which year was the partition of Bengal annulled?
f: The partition of Bengal, made in 1905, was annulled in 1911 after Hindu agitation.

q: Into how many equal parts does a diameter divide a circle?
f: A diameter passes through the centre and splits the circle into two equal semicircles.

q: Is the sun a star or a planet?
f: The sun is a star because it produces its own light and heat by nuclear fusion. Planets only reflect light.

q: Which of the following is a city of Libya?
f: Tripoli is the capital and largest city of Libya. Casablanca is in Morocco, Tunis in Tunisia and Cairo in Egypt.

q: On what date was CPEC formed?
f: Candidates and many Pakistani sources give 22 May 2013, when Pakistan and China signed the agreement on the economic corridor during Chinese Premier Li Keqiang's visit.

q: On what date was the OIC established?
f: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation was established at the Rabat summit on 25 September 1969.

q: On which date is Defence Day observed in Pakistan?
f: Defence Day is observed on 6 September to commemorate the defence of Pakistan in the 1965 war.

q: Ruble is the currency of which country?
f: The ruble is the currency of Russia.

q: Saifullah (Sword of Allah) was the title of whom?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) gave the title Saifullah to the great general Khalid bin Waleed (R.A).

q: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai was a famous poet of which province?
f: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai was the great Sufi poet of Sindh. His collection is called Shah Jo Risalo.

q: Sultan Bahu and Bulleh Shah are poets of which language?
f: Both Sufi poets wrote in Punjabi.

q: Swine flu is caused by what?
f: Swine flu is caused by influenza viruses, mainly the H1N1 strain.

q: The diameter of a circle is equal to how many radii of the circle?
f: The diameter is a line through the centre, which is made of two radii. So diameter = 2 x radius.

q: The Hindu Kush mountain range connects Pakistan with which country?
f: The Hindu Kush extends from central Afghanistan into northern Pakistan.

q: The Thomas Cup is associated with which sport?
f: The Thomas Cup is the men's world team championship of badminton, contested between national teams.

q: The year 1995 was the golden jubilee (50th anniversary) of which international organisation?
f: The United Nations was founded in 1945, so 1995 marked its 50 years.

q: Which Sahabi was married to two daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), earning the title Dhun-Nurayn?
f: Hazrat Uthman (RA) married Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA) and, after her death, Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA).

q: Waris Shah is a famous poet of which language?
f: Waris Shah (1722-1798) wrote the Punjabi romantic epic Heer Ranjha.

q: Warsak Dam, near Peshawar, was completed during the government of which ruler?
f: Warsak Dam was completed in 1960 under Field Marshal Ayub Khan's government.

q: How many faraiz does wuzu (ablution) have according to the Hanafi school?
f: The four faraiz are washing the face, washing the arms up to the elbows, wiping a quarter of the head (masah) and washing the feet up to the ankles.

q: What does the word ayat mean?
f: Ayat is the plural of ayah, meaning a sign, and it is used for the verses of the Quran.

q: What does the word Jihad mean?
f: Jihad comes from the Arabic root j-h-d meaning to strive or exert effort.

q: What does OIC stand for?
f: OIC stands for Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, the collective voice of the Muslim world.

q: What does Saif mean in Arabic?
f: Saif is the Arabic word for sword.

q: What does zakat mean literally?
f: Zakat literally means purification and growth, as giving it purifies wealth and the soul.

q: What is a scalar matrix?
o: A diagonal matrix with all diagonal elements equal
A matrix with all elements zero
A matrix with one row only
A matrix whose rows and columns are interchanged
f: A scalar matrix is a square diagonal matrix in which all the main diagonal elements are the same and all other elements are zero.

q: Which word is a synonym of cleverness?
f: Cleverness means mental sharpness, so intelligence is the closest in meaning.

q: Which word is a synonym of constant?
f: Constant means continuing without change, so steady is the closest in meaning.

q: Which word is a synonym of elation?
f: Elation means great joy or high spirits, so delight is a synonym.

q: Which word is a synonym of idleness?
f: Idleness is the state of doing no work, which is laziness.

q: What is Astola?
o: An island off the Balochistan coast
f: Astola, also called Haft Talar, is an island in the Arabian Sea off the coast of Balochistan.

q: What was the Lucknow Pact of 1916?

q: Solve for x: 2x - 5 = x + 7
f: Move x to the left and 5 to the right: 2x - x = 7 + 5, so x = 12.

q: If y = 9x - 5 and x = 1, what is the value of y?
f: Substitute x = 1: y = 9 x 1 - 5 = 9 - 5 = 4.

q: The age of Ali is 6 years and Sara is three times as old as Ali. What will Ali's age be after 6 years?
f: Ali is 6 now, so after 6 years he will be 6 + 6 = 12. Sara's age does not matter for this question.

q: Water is to ice as milk is to what?
f: Ice is the solid form obtained from water, and cheese is the solid product obtained from milk.

q: What is 80% of 80?
What is a triangle with all sides equal called?
f: An equilateral triangle has three equal sides and three equal angles of 60 degrees each.

q: What is the derivative of x with respect to x?
f: By the power rule, d(x^1)/dx = 1 x x^0 = 1.

q: What is the formula for the area of a triangle?
f: The area of a triangle is half the area of the parallelogram with the same base and height.

q: What is the geometric mean of 3 and 12?
f: Geometric mean = square root of (3 x 12) = square root of 36 = 6.

q: What is the perimeter of a square of side 4 cm?
f: A square has four equal sides, so the perimeter is 4 x 4 = 16 cm.

q: What is the real part of -i(2i - 3)?
f: -i(2i - 3) = -2i squared + 3i = 2 + 3i, since i squared = -1. The real part is 2.

q: Which word is formed by the alphabet positions 18, 5, 19, 20?
f: Positions 18, 5, 19, 20 are R, E, S, T.

q: When Ali was 3, his sister's age was four times his age. How old is Ali's sister when Ali is 12?
f: When Ali was 3 his sister was 12, so she is 9 years older. When Ali is 12 she is 12 + 9 = 21.

q: Which number comes next: 2, 6, 14, 30, 62, ?
f: Each term is double the previous plus 2: 62 x 2 + 2 = 126.

q: After how many years did East Pakistan (Bangladesh) separate from West Pakistan?
f: Pakistan was created in 1947 and Bangladesh emerged in December 1971, which is 24 years later.

q: After which battle did the disbelievers become unable to attack Madinah (and Makkah-based enemies could no longer launch attacks)?
f: After the failed siege in the Battle of Khandaq the Holy Prophet (PBUH) said the Quraysh would no longer attack the Muslims, and the Muslims would march against them.

q: Against which country did Sachin Tendulkar score his 100th international century?
f: Tendulkar scored his 100th international century, 114 runs, against Bangladesh in the Asia Cup at Mirpur on 16 March 2012.

q: Pakistan won the 2017 ICC Champions Trophy final against which team?
f: Pakistan beat India by 180 runs in the final at The Oval, London, on 18 June 2017.

q: Along which parallel of latitude does the border between Canada and the United States largely run (west of the Great Lakes)?
f: The land border from the Pacific coast to Lake of the Woods follows the 49th parallel north, set by the Treaty of 1818 and later agreements.

q: Who elects the Prime Minister of Pakistan?
f: Under the 1973 Constitution the Prime Minister is elected by the members of the National Assembly, then appointed by the President.

q: How many books are included in the Sihah Sittah (Sahih Sitta), the six authentic collections of hadith?
f: Sihah Sittah literally means the six correct books. The six collections are Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasai and Ibn Majah.

q: How many manzils (stages) is the Holy Quran divided into?
f: The Quran is divided into seven manzils so that it can be recited in one week. Each manzil is read on one day of the week.

q: How many masarif (heads of expenditure) of zakat are mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah?
f: Surah At-Tawbah (9:60) names eight categories of zakat recipients: the poor, the needy, zakat collectors, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, slaves, debtors, the cause of Allah and the wayfarer.

q: How many Nishan-e-Haider awards have been given so far, according to the commonly cited count?
f: The commonly cited current count is 11 recipients, all awarded posthumously. Older sources say 10, and the status of the eleventh name is sometimes disputed.

q: In which surah is the longest verse of the Holy Quran?
f: The longest verse is Ayat ad-Dayn (verse 282) about written contracts of debt, in Surah Al-Baqarah.

q: How old was the Holy Prophet Muhammad (SAW) when his mother, Hazrat Amina, passed away?
f: Hazrat Amina died at Abwa while returning from Madina when the Prophet (SAW) was about six years old.

q: From which city did the Holy Prophet (SAW) migrate in 622 AD?
f: In 622 AD the Prophet (SAW) migrated from Makkah to Madina (then called Yathrib), which is called the Hijrat.

q: In which district of Balochistan is the Chamalang coal mine located?
f: The Chamalang coalfield lies in north-central Balochistan, mostly in Loralai district and extending towards Kohlu and Barkhan.

q: In which district of Pakistan is the Chashma nuclear power plant located?
f: The Chashma Nuclear Power Complex stands near Chashma barrage on the Indus in Mianwali district, Punjab.

q: For which achievement did Malala Yousafzai receive the Nobel Prize in 2014?
f: She received the Nobel Peace Prize for her struggle for the right of children and girls to education.

q: In which Islamic month did the tragedy of Karbala take place?
f: Imam Hussain (RA) was martyred at Karbala on 10 Muharram 61 AH, the day of Ashura.

q: In which Islamic month was the Ghazwa (Battle) of Badr fought?
f: The Battle of Badr took place on 17 Ramadan 2 AH.

q: In which province of Pakistan is Ghotki located?
f: Ghotki is a city and district in northern Sindh, on the border with Punjab.

q: In which year did Pakistan become a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)?
f: Pakistan (with India) was admitted as a full member at the SCO summit in Astana, Kazakhstan, in June 2017.

q: In which year was the M.A.O. School at Aligarh raised to the status of a College?
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the school in 1875, and it became Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in 1877.

q: In which year was the war of independence (the Mutiny) fought in the subcontinent?
f: The War of Independence broke out at Meerut in May 1857 against East India Company rule.

q: In which year were the modern Olympic Games first held?
f: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896. Baron Pierre de Coubertin revived the Games.

q: On which prophet was the Torah (Taurat) revealed?
f: The Torah was revealed on Hazrat Musa (AS) for the Bani Israil.

q: Rooh Ullah (Ruhullah) is the title of which prophet?
f: Hazrat Isa (AS) is called Ruhullah, the Spirit of Allah, because he was born by Allah's command without a father.

q: The first 5 verses revealed to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) belong to which surah?
f: The first five ayats revealed in the Cave of Hira begin with Iqra bismi rabbika and are from Surah Al-Alaq.

q: The OIC is an organization of which countries?
f: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation is the collective voice of Muslim countries of the world.

q: The Secretary-General of the United Nations, Antonio Guterres, belongs to which country?
f: Antonio Guterres, the ninth UN Secretary-General, is a former Prime Minister of Portugal.

q: The Silk Road connects Pakistan with which country?
f: The Karakoram Highway follows part of the ancient Silk Road and links Pakistan to China through the Khunjerab Pass.

q: Under the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty, which rivers were allotted to Pakistan?
f: The treaty gave the three western rivers, Indus, Jhelum and Chenab, to Pakistan and the three eastern rivers, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, to India.

q: What does the Arabic word Badr (Badar) mean?
f: Badr means the full moon in Arabic. The Battle of Badr in 2 AH was fought at a place of that name near Madina.

q: What is 28 May, the day Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests in 1998, known as?
f: On 28 May 1998 Pakistan carried out nuclear tests at Chagai, and the day is observed as Youm-e-Takbeer. Takbeer means proclaiming the greatness of God.

q: What does the word Pakistan mean?
f: Pakistan is a Persian and Urdu word made of pak (pure) and stan (land), so it means land of the pure. It is not related to truth.

q: What does wuzu (wudu) mean?
f: Wuzu is the ritual ablution in which the face, arms, head and feet are washed or wiped before prayer. It is a condition for offering Salah.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word voyage?
f: A voyage is a long journey, especially by sea or in space. Journey is the closest meaning.

q: Another name for the Manila Pact of 1954 is:
f: The Manila Pact created the South East Asia Treaty Organization (SEATO), signed in Manila in September 1954.

q: What does SAFTA stand for?
f: SAFTA stands for South Asian Free Trade Area. It is a trade arrangement among the member states of SAARC to reduce customs duties.

q: What is Sahih Muslim?
f: Sahih Muslim is a collection of authentic Hadith compiled by Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj.

q: Which name is given to the Battle of Khandaq (the Trench) in the Quran?
f: The Battle of Khandaq (5 AH) is also called Ahzab (the Confederates), after the allied tribes who besieged Madinah.

q: What is the capital of Balochistan?
f: Quetta is the provincial capital and largest city of Balochistan.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word compassion?
f: Compassion is a feeling of concern and pity for the suffering of others. Sympathy is the closest meaning.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word inhabitant?
f: An inhabitant is a person who lives permanently in a place. Resident has the same meaning.

q: What is the special unstitched cloth worn by pilgrims during Hajj called?
f: Ihram is the two-piece unstitched white cloth worn by male pilgrims during Hajj and Umrah. Wearing it begins the state of ihram.

q: In which month and Hijri year did the conquest of Makkah (Fatah Makkah) take place?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) entered Makkah with an army of about ten thousand in Ramadan 8 AH, traditionally dated 20 Ramadan.

q: On which date was the Battle of Badr fought?
f: The Battle of Badr took place on 17 Ramadan 2 AH, the first major battle between Muslims and the Quraish.

q: What is the term of a Senator in Pakistan?
f: Senators are elected for a six-year term, and half retire every three years.

q: What is the first month of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar?
f: The Hijri calendar begins with Muharram, and 1 Muharram is the Islamic New Year.

q: What is the height of Tirich Mir, the highest peak of the Hindu Kush range?
f: Tirich Mir in Chitral, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush, about 7,708 metres high.

q: What is the meaning of Wudu (Wuzu)?
o: Ablution, the ritual washing before prayer
f: Wudu means ablution, the washing of the face, hands, head and feet before prayer, from a root meaning cleanliness.

q: What is the period between a person's death and the Day of Judgment called in Islam?
f: Barzakh is the intermediate stage between death and resurrection, in which the soul stays until the Day of Judgment.

q: Which is the smallest country in the world by area?
f: Vatican City covers about 0.44 square km, the smallest independent state in the world. Monaco is the second smallest.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Hafsa (RA) with the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Hazrat Hafsa (RA), daughter of Hazrat Umar (RA), married the Prophet (PBUH) and is a Mother of the Believers.

q: On which occasion did Hinda (wife of Abu Sufyan) accept Islam?
f: Hinda bint Utbah, who had opposed Islam at Uhud, accepted Islam when Makkah was conquered in 8 AH.

q: On which date did the United Nations officially come into existence?
f: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, after ratification by China, France, the USSR, the UK, the USA and most other signatories. This date is celebrated as United Nations Day.

q: In which Hijri year was the Ghazwa (Battle) of Tabuk fought?
f: The Ghazwa of Tabuk took place in 9 AH (630 CE) against the Byzantine threat on the northern frontier. The Prophet (PBUH) led about 30,000 Muslims, but no fighting occurred.

q: Where is Jabal-e-Noor (the mountain containing the Cave of Hira) located?
f: Jabal al-Noor is a mountain near Makkah in Saudi Arabia and holds the Cave of Hira where the first revelation came to the Prophet (PBUH).

q: Where is the headquarters of the World Bank located?
f: The World Bank has its headquarters in Washington, D.C., USA. It was set up in 1944 at the Bretton Woods conference.

q: In which region of Pakistan does the River Soan flow?
f: The Soan rises in the Murree hills and flows through the Potohar Plateau near Rawalpindi and Islamabad before joining the Indus.

q: Which agreement was signed between Pakistan and India in January 1966 after the 1965 war?
f: The Tashkent Declaration was signed on 10 January 1966 by Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri. It ended the 1965 war and restored the earlier positions.

q: Which angels write down the good and bad deeds of every human being?
f: Kiraman Katibin are the two noble recording angels on a person's shoulders who write the deeds. One records good deeds and the other records bad deeds.

q: Which batsman scored 400 not out in a Test innings?
f: Brian Lara of the West Indies scored 400 not out against England at Antigua in 2004. It is the highest individual score in Test cricket.

q: Which of the following Sahabah was NOT among the Ashra Mubashira (the ten companions given the glad tidings of Paradise)?
f: Talha, Zubair and Abdur Rahman bin Auf are all in the list of ten promised Paradise in one hadith. Abu Hurairah, a great narrator of hadith, is not in that list.

q: Which country is shaped like a long boot on the map?
f: Italy is a peninsula that looks like a long boot kicking the island of Sicily.

q: Which is the largest airport in the world by area?
o: King Fahd International Airport (Dammam, Saudi Arabia)
f: King Fahd International Airport near Dammam covers about 776 to 780 square kilometres, far more than any other airport.

q: Which political party did Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto found?
f: Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto founded the Pakistan People's Party (PPP) in Lahore.

q: Which Sahabi is known by the title Jame ul Quran (compiler of the Quran)?
f: Hazrat Uthman (RA) had the Quran copied into one standard text and sent copies to the major cities.

q: Which province of Pakistan has the largest number of National Assembly seats?
f: Punjab has 141 of the 266 general seats of the National Assembly, far more than any other province.

q: Who is the Federal Minister for Railways of Pakistan?
f: Muhammad Hanif Abbasi of the PML-N is the Federal Minister for Railways in the current government.

q: Who is the President of France?
f: Emmanuel Macron was first elected President of France in 2017 and re-elected in 2022; he is still in office.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom?
f: Andy Burnham became UK Prime Minister on 20 July 2026 after Keir Starmer stepped down as Labour leader.

q: Who is the Pakistani who most recently won a Nobel Prize?
f: Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, which makes her the latest Pakistani Nobel laureate.

q: Who is the youngest Nobel Prize winner in history?
f: Malala Yousafzai was 17 years old when she received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, the youngest laureate ever.

q: Which Companion of the Holy Prophet (S.A.W) is known as Sahib-e-Sirr (keeper of the secrets) of the Prophet?
f: Hazrat Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman (R.A) was entrusted with the Prophet's secrets, including the names of the hypocrites.

q: Which country opposed Pakistan's admission to the United Nations in 1947?
f: Afghanistan was the only country that voted against Pakistan's membership of the UN in September 1947. It later withdrew its objection.

q: Who recited Surah Maryam before the king Najashi of Abyssinia?
f: Hazrat Jaffar bin Abi Talib spoke for the Muslim migrants and recited verses of Surah Maryam, which moved Najashi and the bishops.

q: Whom did Babur defeat in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526?
f: Babur defeated the Delhi Sultan Ibrahim Lodhi at Panipat on 21 April 1526, which began Mughal rule in India.

q: Who was the opponent of Field Marshal Ayub Khan in the 1965 presidential election of Pakistan?
f: Miss Fatima Jinnah, sister of the Quaid-e-Azam, contested as the joint candidate of the Combined Opposition Parties in January 1965. Ayub Khan won through the Basic Democrats electoral college.

q: Who was the first muezzin (caller to prayer) of Islam?
f: Hazrat Bilal bin Rabah (RA), an Abyssinian companion, gave the first adhan in Madina after the Prophet approved it. Hazrat Abdullah bin Zaid (RA) saw the words of the adhan in a dream.

q: Why was Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad launched in February 2017?
o: To eliminate the remaining terrorist threat across the country
f: It was a nationwide operation of the armed forces to eliminate the remaining terrorist threat, consolidate earlier gains and strengthen border security.

q: With the help of which country did Pakistan build the JF-17 Thunder fighter jet?
f: The JF-17 Thunder was developed jointly by Pakistan Aeronautical Complex and China's Chengdu Aircraft Corporation.

q: A boy is 3 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. When the boy is 11 years old, how old will his sister be?
f: Sister's age now = 3 x 3 = 9 years, so she is 6 years older. When the boy is 11 she will be 11 + 6 = 17 years.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is twice his age. What will be her age when Ali is 11 years old?
f: Sister's age now = 2 x 5 = 10 years. Ali gets 6 years older, so she will be 10 + 6 = 16 years.

q: Definitely is to absolutely as totally is to what?
f: Definitely and absolutely are synonyms, so the synonym of totally is entirely.

q: How many sides does a quadrilateral (quadrangle) have?
f: Quad means four, and a quadrilateral is a closed figure with four sides.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day is the 12th day of that month?
f: From the 1st to the 12th is 11 days, and 11 divided by 7 leaves remainder 4. Moving 4 day(s) forward from Monday gives Friday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day is the 12th day of that month?
f: From the 2nd to the 12th is 10 days, and 10 divided by 7 leaves remainder 3. Moving 3 day(s) forward from Monday gives Thursday.

q: What is the value of log 64 divided by log 4?
f: Write 64 as 4 cubed, so log 64 = 3 log 4. Therefore log 64 / log 4 = 3.

q: Arrange the letters of the word MANAGEMENT in alphabetical order. Which is the 3rd letter?
f: The letters in order are A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T. The third letter is E.

q: Which is the odd one out: iron, brass, tin, copper?
f: Iron, tin and copper are pure metallic elements. Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.

q: Against whom was the Battle of Uhud fought?
f: The Battle of Uhud (3 AH) was fought between the Muslims of Madinah and the Quraysh of Makkah led by Abu Sufyan.

q: The Cholistan Desert is located near which city?
f: Cholistan lies in southern Punjab and stretches from Bahawalpur towards the Indian border. It is also called Rohi.

q: In which city was Benazir Bhutto assassinated?
f: Benazir Bhutto was killed after an election rally at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi, on 27 December 2007.

q: Is a Pakistan Navy Lieutenant equal in rank to a Pakistan Army Captain?
o: No, Navy Lieutenant is equal to Army Major
No, Navy Lieutenant is equal to Army Lieutenant
No, Navy Lieutenant is equal to Army Colonel
f: A Navy Lieutenant ranks with an Army Captain and a Pakistan Air Force Flight Lieutenant.

q: On what date was Benazir Bhutto assassinated?
f: She was killed in a gun and bomb attack after an election rally at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi, on 27 December 2007.

q: Which country is the world's largest producer of cotton?
f: China is the leading producer of cotton, with most of its crop grown in Xinjiang. India is second.

q: One mile is approximately equal to how many kilometres?
f: One mile is 1.609 km, which is about 1.6 km.

q: After how many years does a leap year normally come?
f: A leap year occurs once every 4 years, when the year is divisible by 4, and adds 29 February.

q: A matrix is called a real matrix when:
o: All its entries are real numbers
Its number of rows equals its number of columns
f: A real matrix is one whose every entry is a real number.

q: In a rhombus, which of the following are all equal?
f: A rhombus is a parallelogram with all four sides equal in length.

q: Abu al-Bashar (father of mankind) is the title of which Prophet?
f: Hazrat Adam (AS) is the first human being and the first Prophet, so he is called Abu al-Bashar.

q: Abu Turab is the title of which companion of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) gave Hazrat Ali (RA) the title Abu Turab, meaning father of dust.

q: According to the 2023 census, which is the most populous district of Pakistan?
f: Lahore district had about 13 million people in the 2023 census, the highest of any district.

q: What system of government did the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan establish?
f: The 1973 Constitution set up a parliamentary system in which the Prime Minister heads the government and the President is head of state.

q: Adolf Hitler was a politician of which country?
f: Hitler led Germany as head of the Nazi Party and became Chancellor in 1933.

q: The Tashkent Declaration of January 1966 was signed after which war?
f: The Tashkent Declaration ended the September 1965 war between Pakistan and India.

q: The USSR was formed after which revolution of 1917?
f: The Bolshevik (October) Revolution of 1917 led by Lenin brought the communists to power, and the USSR was formally formed in 1922.

q: A number of the form a - ib, where a and b are real numbers and i is iota, is called:
f: Numbers written as a + ib or a - ib, with real a and b and i squared equal to -1, are complex numbers.

q: In which city was Arfa Karim, the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional, born?
f: Arfa Karim Randhawa was born on 2 February 1995 in a village near Faisalabad, Punjab.

q: Which city hosted the 2018 Asian Games?
f: The 2018 Asian Games were held in Jakarta and Palembang, Indonesia.

q: At what age did Hazrat Ali (RA) accept Islam, according to the most commonly stated account?
