f: Most sources say Hazrat Ali was a boy of about ten when he accepted Islam, making him among the first to do so.

q: At what age did the first revelation (wahi) come to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: The first revelation, the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq, came at the age of 40 in the Cave of Hira.

q: At which place did Pakistan conduct its nuclear tests in May 1998?
f: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests in the Chagai Hills of Balochistan on 28 and 30 May 1998.

q: Ateeq is the title of which companion of the Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) was given the title Ateeq, meaning one freed from the Fire.

q: Banu Nadir and Banu Qaynuqa were tribes of which religion?
f: Banu Nadir, Banu Qaynuqa and Banu Qurayzah were the Jewish tribes living around Madinah in the Prophet's time.

q: Between which two leaders was the Indus Waters Treaty signed in 1960?
f: The treaty was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960 by Pakistan's President Ayub Khan and India's Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.

q: In which river is the rare blind dolphin found?
f: The Indus river dolphin (bhulan) is blind and lives in the Indus river system.

q: Boxer Muhammad Ali belonged to which country?
f: Muhammad Ali (born Cassius Clay) was an American heavyweight boxer from Louisville, Kentucky.

q: By whom are the members of the Senate of Pakistan mainly elected?
f: Senators from each province are elected by the members of that province's assembly through single transferable vote.

q: By whom was Hazrat Muadh bin Jabal appointed governor of Yemen?
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) sent Muadh bin Jabal (RA) to Yemen as governor and judge around 10 AH.

q: Masjid Zarar (Dirar) was built by which group?
f: A group of hypocrites built it near Quba to divide the Muslims, and the Quran (Surah At-Tawbah) condemned it.

q: Campbellpur is the old name of which city of Pakistan?
f: The city of Attock in Punjab was called Campbellpur during British rule, after Sir Colin Campbell. It was renamed Attock in 1978.

q: Carbon dioxide gas in the atmosphere is mainly responsible for which problem?
f: Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas that traps heat in the atmosphere. Increasing amounts cause the Earth to warm.

q: Chess originated in which country?
f: Chess developed from an Indian game called chaturanga around the 6th century AD. It then spread to Persia and the Muslim world.

q: The COVID-19 outbreak first started in which province of China?
f: The first cases were reported in the city of Wuhan, the capital of Hubei province, in December 2019.

q: Dadu is a district of which province of Pakistan?
f: Dadu is a district in the northwest of Sindh, close to Lake Manchar.

q: Deficiency of vitamin D causes which disease?
f: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium for bones. Its lack causes soft, bent bones in children, called rickets.

q: Deficiency of which vitamin causes night blindness?
f: Vitamin A is needed to make the light-sensitive pigment in the retina. Its lack makes it hard to see in dim light.

q: Dr. Ruth Pfau is remembered for her work against which disease?
f: Dr. Ruth Pfau, a German doctor, spent her life in Pakistan treating leprosy patients and helped control the disease.

q: During which years did the Khilafat Movement take place in India?
f: The movement began in 1919 to protect the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I. It ended in 1924 when Turkey abolished the caliphate.

q: Fill in the blank: ________ comes home first will cook the food.
f: Whoever is the subject of the clause 'comes home first' and means any person who. Whom, which and whatever do not fit.

q: Fill in the blank: ____ sun rises in the east.
f: The sun is unique, so it takes the definite article the.

q: Fill in the blank: Three pictures are hanging ____ the wall.
f: The preposition on is used for things attached to a surface such as a wall.

q: Fill in the blank: He is ____ I am.
f: Older takes than in comparisons, and the pronoun I am follows because it is a subject comparison.

q: Fill in the blank: He is accused ____ murder.
f: The correct phrase is accused of.

q: Fill in the blank: He is adept ____ finding flaws in the system.
f: Adept is followed by at (or in), meaning very skilled.

q: Fill in the blank: He is deprived ____ all his money.
f: The correct phrase is deprived of.

q: Fill in the blank: He is jealous ____ him.
f: The adjective jealous takes the preposition of.

q: Fill in the blank: He lived here ____ six years.
f: For is used with a period of time such as six years, while since is used with a point in time.

q: Fill in the blank: He reminds me ____ his teacher.
f: The correct phrase is remind someone of someone.

q: Fill in the blank: He told me that Ali ____ ill.
f: In reported speech after the past tense told, the present is shifts to the past tense was.

q: Choose the correct word: I was tired, so I ____ to sleep.
f: The sentence is in the past tense (I was tired), so the past form went is needed.

q: Complete the sentence: Ali said that he ____ TV.
f: In reported speech after said, the present continuous is watching becomes the past continuous was watching.

q: Complete the sentence: I am mad ____ games.
f: Mad about means very fond of or passionate about something.

q: Fill in the blank: I ____ three books since Monday.
f: The word since Monday shows an action continuing up to now, so the present perfect tense is needed: have read.

q: Fill in the blank: I am good ____ games.
f: The correct preposition after good, when talking about skill, is at.

q: Fill in the blank with a preposition: I agreed ____ her proposal.
f: We agree to a proposal or plan, but agree with a person.

q: Fill in the preposition: The computer is ___ the table.
f: An object resting on a flat surface is described with the preposition on.

q: Fill in the preposition: The fridge is ___ the kitchen.
f: A room is an enclosed space, so we use in.

q: Fill in the preposition: Tokyo is the most populated city ___ the world.
f: After a superlative we normally use in with a place: the most populated city in the world.

q: For addition of matrices, what must both matrices have?
o: The same order (same number of rows and columns)
The same number of columns only
f: Matrices are added element by element, so they must have the same number of rows and columns.

q: For what is Ziarat famous?
f: Ziarat in Balochistan is known for the Quaid-e-Azam Residency, where Jinnah spent his last days in 1948.

q: For which religion is some area of Hassan Abdal sacred?
f: Hassan Abdal has Gurdwara Panja Sahib, which is sacred to Sikhs.

q: From where do plants mainly obtain nitrogen for growth?
f: Plants absorb nitrogen through their roots from the soil as nitrates and ammonium. Atmospheric nitrogen is made usable by bacteria and lightning.

q: Where does the Yangtze River originate?
f: The Yangtze rises on the Tibetan Plateau in Qinghai and flows east to the East China Sea.

q: From which country did Allama Iqbal obtain his PhD?
f: Iqbal received his PhD from the University of Munich in Germany in 1908. He studied at Cambridge in England but his doctorate was from Munich.

q: From which country does the TAPI gas pipeline start?
f: TAPI stands for Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, and the gas comes from Turkmenistan.

q: Hajj is which pillar of Islam?
f: The five pillars are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj, so Hajj is the fifth.

q: Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro belong to which civilization?
f: Both are major cities of the Bronze Age Indus Valley Civilization.

q: Fill in the blank: She is always cleaning her home ___ cleanliness is called half faith.
f: The second clause gives the reason for her cleaning, so the conjunction because fits.

q: Fill in the blank: The doctor ___ car makes noise is a good person.
f: Whose shows possession: the car belongs to the doctor.

q: Fill in the blank: Why are you so ____ with him?
f: After the linking verb are, we need an adjective describing the subject, so angry.

q: Hazrat Aisha (RA) was the daughter of which companion?
f: Hazrat Aisha (RA), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA), the first Caliph.

q: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) belonged to which clan (branch) of the Quraish tribe of Arabs?
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born in the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraish tribe. His grandfather was Abdul Muttalib, son of Hashim.

q: According to a hadith of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), lying is a sign of which kind of person?
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that the signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when trusted he betrays.

q: Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of which Prophet?
f: Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS), who was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).

q: Choose the correct word: He is afraid ___ dogs.
f: The adjective afraid is followed by the preposition of, so the correct sentence is He is afraid of dogs.

q: Choose the correct word: He was born ___ 20 August 2001.
f: The preposition on is used with specific dates and days, so the sentence is He was born on 20 August 2001.

q: Up to approximately what depth (in metres) does sunlight penetrate in the ocean (the sunlit or euphotic zone)?
f: Enough sunlight for photosynthesis reaches only to about 200 metres, which is called the sunlit (euphotic) zone.

q: How is the empty set denoted in set theory?
f: The empty set has no elements, so it is written as { } or with the symbol phi. The set {0} is not empty because it contains the element 0.

q: What is the commonly quoted length of the Pakistan-Afghanistan border (Durand Line)?
f: The Durand Line, agreed in 1893, is most commonly given as about 2,640 km long.

q: How many amendments have been made to the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan as of 2026?
f: The 26th Amendment was passed in October 2024 and the 27th Amendment was passed by Parliament in November 2025. A 28th amendment was still only under discussion in mid-2026.

q: According to the Quran (Surah Al-Anfal), how many angels were promised by Allah to help the Muslims in the Battle of Badr?
f: Surah Al-Anfal (8:9) says Allah would reinforce the Muslims with a thousand angels in succession.

q: According to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), how many countries are recognised as nuclear-weapon states?
f: The NPT recognises only the states that tested a nuclear device before 1 January 1967: USA, Russia, UK, France and China.

q: How many ayats (verses) are there in Surah Al-Kausar?
f: Surah Al-Kausar (Surah 108) has 3 ayats, which makes it the shortest surah of the Quran.

q: How many pieces of cloth are worn by a male pilgrim in the state of Ihram?
f: A male pilgrim wears two unstitched white sheets, one wrapped around the waist (izar) and one around the upper body (rida).

q: How many consecutive matches did the Pakistani squash legend Jahangir Khan win in his famous unbeaten run?
f: Jahangir Khan won 555 consecutive matches between 1981 and 1986, until Ross Norman beat him in the 1986 World Open.

q: How many countries have veto power in the United Nations Security Council?
f: Only the five permanent members have veto power: USA, UK, France, Russia and China.

q: How many Hafiz (memorisers) of the Quran are reported to have been martyred in the Battle of Yamama?
f: In the Battle of Yamama (12 AH) against the false prophet Musailima, about 70 Huffaz of the Quran were martyred, according to the commonly given account.

q: How many idols were placed in and around the Kaaba before the conquest of Makkah?
f: Traditional sources say 360 idols stood around the Kaaba when the Holy Prophet (PBUH) entered Makkah in 8 AH. He had them removed and the Kaaba cleansed.

q: What is the total number of members of the Senate of Pakistan?
f: The Senate has 96 members: 23 from each of the four provinces (92) plus 4 from the Islamabad Capital Territory. A November 2025 report still describes a 96-member Senate

q: How many Senate seats are allocated to each province of Pakistan?
f: Each province has 23 Senate seats: 14 general, 4 for women, 4 for technocrats and 1 for non-Muslims.

q: How many general (directly elected) seats does Punjab have in the National Assembly of Pakistan?
f: Under the 2024 delimitation Punjab has 141 general seats in the 336-seat National Assembly. With its 32 reserved seats for women, Punjab's share rises to 173.

q: Into how many paras (juz) is the Holy Quran divided?
f: The Quran is divided into 30 paras of roughly equal length so it can be read in a month. This is separate from its 114 surahs.

q: How many players are on the court for one team in a volleyball match?
f: A volleyball team has six players on the court at a time, three at the net and three at the back.

q: How many players of one team are on the court at a time in basketball?
f: Each basketball team plays with five players on the court at a time.

q: How many consecutive matches did squash legend Jahangir Khan win in his unbeaten run between 1981 and 1986?
f: Jahangir Khan won 555 consecutive matches over about five and a half years, a record recognised in the Guinness Book of Records as the longest winning streak in a professional sport.

q: How many states are there in the United States of America?
f: The USA has 50 states. Alaska and Hawaii were the last to join in 1959.

q: How many times does the full phrase Bismillah Al-Rahman Al-Raheem occur in the Holy Quran?
f: It opens 113 surahs (all except Surah At-Tawbah) and also appears inside Surah An-Naml (27:30), giving 114 in total.

q: How many times is the name Muhammad mentioned in the Holy Quran?
f: The name Muhammad occurs in Surah Aal-e-Imran (3:144), Al-Ahzab (33:40), Muhammad (47:2) and Al-Fath (48:29), so four times.

q: What is the Zakat nisab of silver in tolas?
f: The nisab of silver is 52.5 tolas, which is about 612.36 grams.

q: How many types of Hajj are there?
f: The three types are Ifrad, Qiran and Tamattu.

q: How often does the presidency of the UN Security Council change?
f: The presidency rotates every month among the 15 members in the English alphabetical order of their names.

q: Choose the correct word: I was worried because I thought I might ___ my train.
f: Miss means to fail to catch a train. Loose means not tight, and found is the past of find.

q: ICAO is a specialized agency of which organization?
f: The International Civil Aviation Organization is a specialized agency of the United Nations dealing with civil aviation standards.

q: What is the noun form of the adjective safe?
f: Safety is the noun that corresponds to the adjective safe, while safely is an adverb.

q: If k is the unit vector along the z-axis, what is the scalar product k . k?
f: The dot product of a unit vector with itself is its magnitude squared, 1 x 1 = 1.

q: In the Quaid-e-Azam's 14 Points (1929), Sindh was to be separated from which province?
f: The 14 Points demanded that Sindh be separated from the Bombay Presidency and made a separate province.

q: In the ratio a : b, what is a called?
f: The first term of a ratio is the antecedent and the second term is the consequent.

q: In the sentence 'The boy ran into serious difficulties this year', which word is the adjective?
f: Serious describes the noun difficulties, so it is the adjective.

q: In which battle were a large number of Hafiz-e-Quran Sahaba martyred?
f: Many Qurra (Hafiz) companions were martyred at Yamama against the false prophet Musaylima in 632 AD.

q: In which para (juz) of the Holy Quran is Ayat ul Kursi found?
f: Ayat ul Kursi is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah, and this verse falls in Para 3 (Tilka ar-Rusul).

q: In which city is Warsak Dam located?
f: Warsak Dam is built on the Kabul River about 30 km north-west of Peshawar, in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: In which city is the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) situated?
f: PIMS is a large public teaching hospital located in sector G-8 of Islamabad.

q: In which city of Pakistan does the Orange Line Metro Train run?
f: The Orange Line Metro Train is a rapid transit line in Lahore, built with Chinese financing under CPEC and opened in 2020.

q: In which city was the Indian National Congress founded in 1885?
f: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay in December 1885 under W. C. Bonnerjee.

q: In which city did the tribes of Bani Aus and Bani Khazraj live?
f: Aus and Khazraj were the two main Arab tribes of Yathrib, later named Madinah, and they accepted Islam after the Pledges of Aqaba.

q: In which country is the Gulf of Lion located?
f: The Gulf of Lion is a wide bay of the Mediterranean Sea off the southern coast of France.

q: In which country is the city of Wuhan located?
f: Wuhan is the capital of Hubei province in central China, on the Yangtze River.

q: In which country is the Suez Canal situated?
f: The Suez Canal is an artificial waterway running through Egypt.

q: Where was the first Olympic Games of ancient times held?
f: The ancient Olympic Games began at Olympia in Greece, traditionally dated to 776 BC.

q: In which country was the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) formed in 1969?
f: The OIC was founded at the Islamic Summit in Rabat, Morocco, in September 1969.

q: To which land did the Muslims make their first migration (Hijrat) to escape persecution by the Quraish?
f: In the fifth year of the Prophethood a group of Muslims crossed the Red Sea to Abyssinia, whose Christian king Negus gave them protection.

q: In which district is the Kharan Desert located?
f: The Kharan Desert lies in Kharan district of Balochistan.

q: In which district is the hill station Gorakh Hill located?
f: Gorakh Hill, about 2,300 metres high, lies in the Kirthar Mountains of Dadu district, Sindh.

q: In which division is Narowal district?
f: Narowal district belongs to Gujranwala Division of Punjab.

q: In which mathematical equation does the expression b squared minus 4ac appear?
f: For ax squared + bx + c = 0, the quantity b squared minus 4ac is the discriminant under the square root of the quadratic formula.

q: In which Ghazwa did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) adopt the war technique of digging a trench around Madina?
f: On the advice of Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA) a trench was dug to defend Madina against the Quraish and allied tribes.

q: In which Hijri year was the Ghazwa Ahzab (Khandaq) fought?
f: Most Pakistani textbooks place the Battle of the Trench in Shawwal 5 AH (627 CE).

q: In which Hijri year was Hazrat Hamza (RA) martyred?
f: Hazrat Hamza (RA) was martyred in the Battle of Uhud, fought in Shawwal 3 AH.

q: In which Hijri year was the Battle of Yarmouk fought?
f: The Muslims defeated the Byzantines at Yarmouk in 15 AH (636 CE), in the caliphate of Hazrat Umar (RA).

q: In which Islamic month did Pakistan gain independence on 14 August 1947?
f: Pakistan came into being on 27 Ramadan 1366 AH, which was 14 August 1947, a Friday.

q: In which Islamic month did the Battle (Ghazwa) of Uhad take place?
f: The Battle of Uhad was fought on 7 Shawwal 3 AH near Mount Uhad close to Madina.

q: In which Islamic month is Eid ul Fitr celebrated?
f: Eid ul Fitr is celebrated on 1 Shawwal after the month of fasting ends.

q: In which Islamic month is Laylat ul Qadr (the Night of Power)?
f: Laylat ul Qadr is sought in the last ten nights of Ramadan, especially the odd nights.

q: In which mountain range of Pakistan is Tirich Mir located?
f: Tirich Mir lies in Chitral district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, in the Hindu Kush range.

q: In which Nabawi year did the Year of Grief (Aam ul Huzn) occur?
f: In the 10th year of prophethood both Hazrat Abu Talib and Hazrat Khadijah (RA) passed away within a short time.

q: In which province is Chagai district situated?
f: Chagai is a district in the west of Balochistan bordering Afghanistan and Iran.

q: In which province is the Gomal Zam Dam located?
f: Gomal Zam Dam is built on the Gomal River in South Waziristan, in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: In which province is Kundol (Kundal) Lake situated?
f: Kundol Lake lies in the upper Swat valley near Kalam in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: In which part of Pakistan is Mirpur located?
f: Mirpur is a city and district in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (the question is often worded as province, though AJK is not a province).

q: In which province is Narowal district located?
f: Narowal is a district in northeastern Punjab near the Indian border.

q: In which province does the Soan River flow?
f: The Soan rises in the Murree hills and flows through the Potohar plateau of Punjab (Rawalpindi area) to join the Indus.

q: On which river are the Victoria Falls situated?
f: Victoria Falls lies on the Zambezi River on the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe.

q: In which Surah does the phrase Bismillah occur twice (once at the start and once within a verse)?
f: In Surah Al-Naml the Bismillah appears at the start and again in verse 30 in the letter of Prophet Sulaiman (AS) to the Queen of Sheba.

q: In which year did Britain annex Sindh?
f: Sir Charles Napier defeated the Talpur Mirs at the Battle of Miani in 1843 and Sindh was annexed.

q: In which year did Hazrat Hind (wife of Abu Sufyan) embrace Islam?
f: She accepted Islam at the Conquest of Makkah in 8 AH (630 CE).

q: In which year did Malala Yousafzai receive the Nobel Peace Prize?
f: Malala was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, jointly with Kailash Satyarthi.

q: In which year did Pakistan win the ICC Cricket World Cup?
f: Pakistan won the 1992 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand under Imran Khan, beating England in the final at Melbourne.

q: In which year did Pakistan last win the Hockey World Cup?
f: Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup in 1971, 1978, 1982 and 1994, the last of these in Sydney in 1994.

q: In which year was Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad launched in Pakistan?
f: The Pakistan Army launched Radd-ul-Fasaad in February 2017 as a nationwide intelligence-based operation against terrorism.

q: In which year was the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia founded (unified) under Abdulaziz Ibn Saud?
f: Abdulaziz Ibn Saud proclaimed the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on 23 September 1932, which is marked as Saudi National Day.

q: In which year did the first Muslim commander, Muhammad bin Qasim, invade India (Sindh)?
f: Muhammad bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir and conquered Sindh in 712 AD.

q: In which year did the Ottoman Empire come to an end?
f: The Ottoman Sultanate was abolished in November 1922, ending the empire, and Turkey became a republic in 1923.

q: In which year did the USA invade Afghanistan?
f: US-led forces began strikes on Afghanistan on 7 October 2001 after the 9/11 attacks.

q: In which year was Tarbela Dam completed?
f: Construction of Tarbela Dam on the Indus began in 1968 and the dam was completed in 1976.

q: In which year was the Pakistan Resolution passed?
f: The Resolution was passed at the Lahore session of the All India Muslim League on 23 March 1940.

q: In which year was the presidential system introduced in Pakistan by Ayub Khan under a new constitution?
f: Ayub Khan's constitution of 1962 introduced a presidential system with Basic Democracies.

q: In the straight line equation y = mx + c, what does m represent?
f: In y = mx + c, m is the slope (gradient) of the line, the change in y per unit change in x.

q: What is the shape of the graph of a quadratic equation?
f: The graph of y = ax^2 + bx + c with a not zero is a parabola.

q: What is the status of Iran in SAARC?
f: SAARC has eight full members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Iran is only an observer, so it is not a member.

q: Is the number pi a rational or an irrational number?
f: Pi cannot be written as a fraction of two integers and its decimal expansion never ends or repeats. Hence it is irrational.

q: Joe Biden, who took office in January 2021, was which President of the USA?
f: Barack Obama was 44th and Donald Trump 45th, so Joe Biden who followed him was the 46th President.

q: K2 lies on the border between Pakistan and which country?
f: K2 stands in the Karakoram range on the border of Gilgit-Baltistan (Pakistan) and Xinjiang (China).

q: Lapels are a part of which garment?
f: A lapel is the folded flap on the front of a coat or jacket below the collar.

q: Matrix A is of order 2 x 1 and matrix B is of order 1 x 2. What is the order of the product AB?
f: For a product the columns of A (1) equal the rows of B (1), so AB exists. Its order is rows of A by columns of B, that is 2 x 2.

q: Narendra Modi is a famous politician of which country?
f: Narendra Modi is the Prime Minister of India, leading the BJP.

q: Musailma Kazzab was killed in which battle?
f: Musailma, the false claimant of prophethood, was killed by Wahshi in the Battle of Yamama in 632-633 CE in the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).

q: Nanga Parbat is which highest peak of the world?
f: Nanga Parbat, at 8,126 m, is the ninth highest mountain in the world.

q: Nelson Mandela was the leader and later President of which country?
f: Mandela led the struggle against apartheid and became South Africa's first black President in 1994.

q: Nuku'alofa is the capital of which country?
f: Nuku'alofa, on the island of Tongatapu, is the capital of the Kingdom of Tonga in the Pacific.

q: On what date did Pakistan get its first constitution?
f: Pakistan's first constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956 and the country became an Islamic Republic.

q: The Simla Conference of 1945 was held on 25 June 1945 under which Viceroy?
f: Viceroy Lord Wavell called the conference at Simla to discuss his plan for an Executive Council with Indian members.

q: On what date was the State Bank of Pakistan established?
f: The State Bank of Pakistan began working on 1 July 1948 and was inaugurated by Quaid-e-Azam.

q: On what date did Quaid-e-Azam present his 14 Points, and in reply to which report?
o: 28 March 1929, reply to the Nehru Report
23 March 1940, reply to the Cripps Mission
28 March 1929, reply to the Simon Report
12 December 1930, reply to the Lahore Resolution
f: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah presented his 14 Points in Delhi on 28 March 1929 as an answer to the Nehru Report of 1928.

q: On which date of the Hijri month was the Last Sermon (Khutbah Hajjat-ul-Wida) of the Holy Prophet (SAW) delivered?
f: The sermon was delivered on 9 Dhul Hijjah, 10 AH, in the Uranah valley of Mount Arafat during the Farewell Hajj.

q: On which date was SAARC formed?
f: SAARC was established at the Dhaka summit on 8 December 1985 by seven South Asian countries.

q: According to the Quran, on which mountain did the ark of Prophet Noah (AS) come to rest?
f: Surah Hud (verse 44) says the ark settled on Al-Judi, a mountain in the Kurdistan region.

q: On which river is the Mirani Dam built?
f: Mirani Dam is built on the Dasht River in Kech district of Balochistan, near Turbat.

q: On which river is Sukkur Barrage built?
f: Sukkur Barrage was built across the Indus River at Sukkur in Sindh.

q: On which river is Tarbela Dam built?
f: Tarbela Dam is an earth-filled dam on the Indus River in Haripur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: On whom was the Zaboor (Psalms) revealed?
f: The Zaboor was revealed on Hazrat Dawud (AS).

q: Pakistan is a gateway to which region?
f: Pakistan lies between South Asia, Central Asia and the Arabian Sea, so its ports and routes give Central Asia access to the sea.

q: Pakistan is located in which continent?
f: Pakistan lies in South Asia, part of the continent of Asia.

q: Who started Pakistan's biggest ambulance service?
f: Abdul Sattar Edhi founded the Edhi Foundation, which runs Pakistan's largest ambulance network.

q: Petrol is a mixture of what?
f: Petrol is a mixture of many liquid hydrocarbons obtained from crude oil.

q: Ping pong is another name for which game?
f: Ping pong is the popular name for table tennis.

q: Pour le Merite is an award of which country?
f: Pour le Merite is a Prussian and German order of merit, first founded in 1740 by Frederick the Great.

q: In which constitution of Pakistan was the presidential form of government adopted?
f: The 1962 constitution given by Ayub Khan established a presidential system with a strong president.

q: Which countries does the 38th parallel divide?
f: The 38th parallel north was the dividing line between North and South Korea after 1945.

q: Rubber is obtained from which tree?
f: Natural rubber is made from latex tapped from the rubber tree, Hevea brasiliensis.

q: Ruh-ul-Qudus is the title of which angel?
f: Ruh-ul-Qudus (the Holy Spirit) is a title of the angel Hazrat Jibreel (AS), who brought revelation.

q: In which month is Shab-e-Qadr (Laylatul Qadr)?
f: Laylatul Qadr falls in Ramadan, most likely on an odd night of the last ten days.

q: Complete the sentence: She said that she ___ to know.
f: In reported speech with the past tense verb said, the verb shifts to the past, so wanted is used.

q: Sound travels in the form of what?
f: Sound is a mechanical (longitudinal) wave that needs a medium such as air to travel.

q: Stainless steel is an example of what?
f: Stainless steel is an alloy of iron with chromium and often nickel.

q: Which country mediated the Tashkent Declaration of 1966 between Pakistan and India?
f: The Soviet Union under Premier Alexei Kosygin mediated the Tashkent Declaration in January 1966.

q: The Thar desert of Sindh is rich in which mineral resource?
f: Thar has one of the world's largest lignite coal reserves, about 175 billion tonnes.

q: The Battle of Furqan is the name of which ghazwa?
f: The Quran calls the day of Badr Yawm al-Furqan, the Day of Distinction between truth and falsehood. So the Battle of Furqan is the Battle of Badr.

q: The census of Pakistan is conducted by which organization?
f: Population and housing censuses in Pakistan are carried out by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics. NADRA and the Election Commission only use the data or registers.

q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) appointed Hazrat Maaz bin Jabal (RA) as governor of which place?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Maaz bin Jabal to Yemen as governor and teacher of the people.

q: The Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 was made with the mediation of which organization?
f: The treaty between Pakistan and India was brokered by the World Bank and signed in Karachi in September 1960.

q: The nation of which prophet was destroyed by a rain of stones?
f: The Quran says the sinful people of Hazrat Loot (AS) were destroyed by a shower of baked clay stones.

q: The Panama Canal connects the Pacific Ocean with which ocean?
f: The canal cuts across Panama and joins the Pacific Ocean with the Atlantic Ocean through the Caribbean Sea.

q: Under the Constitution of Pakistan, the President is bound to act on the advice of whom?
f: Article 48 of the Constitution requires the President to act on the advice of the Prime Minister (or the Cabinet).

q: The river Amazon is ___ largest river of South America.
f: A superlative such as largest takes the definite article the.

q: Choose the correct reported speech: The teacher asked, Who is speaking English?
o: The teacher wanted to know who is speaking English.
The teacher wanted to know who was speaking English.
The teacher wanted to know who has spoken English.
The teacher wanted to know who speaks English was.
f: In reported speech a present continuous question changes to past continuous, so is speaking becomes was speaking, and the question order becomes a statement.

q: The Wakhan Corridor separates Pakistan from which country?
f: The narrow Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan lies between Pakistan on the south and Tajikistan on the north.

q: The word Everyone is what part of speech?
f: Everyone stands in place of a noun (all people), so it is an indefinite pronoun.

q: Thimphu is the capital of which country?
f: Thimphu is the capital and largest city of Bhutan.

q: Through which of these countries does the Tropic of Cancer not pass?
f: The Tropic of Cancer (23.5 degrees north) crosses India, Bangladesh and Egypt, but Pakistan lies north of it.

q: Through which of these countries does the Tropic of Capricorn not pass?
f: The Tropic of Capricorn (23.5 degrees south) lies in the southern hemisphere, and India is entirely in the northern hemisphere.

q: To where did the Muslims first migrate?
f: In 615 CE (5th year of the Prophethood) a group of Muslims migrated to Abyssinia to escape persecution in Makkah.

q: To which country does Olympic Airlines (now Olympic Air) belong?
f: Olympic Airlines was the national flag carrier of Greece, founded in 1957 by Aristotle Onassis. It was replaced by Olympic Air in 2009.

q: To which place did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) migrate in 622 AD?
f: In 622 AD the Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Madina (then called Yathrib). This migration is the Hijrat.

q: To which tribe did Hazrat Ali (RA) belong?
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) was born in Makkah into the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraysh tribe. He was the cousin of the Prophet (PBUH).

q: Umm Kalsoom (Umm Kulthum) was what of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA) was a daughter of the Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (RA).

q: Towards which place was the first Hijrat of the Muslims made?
f: In 615 AD a small group of Muslims migrated from Makkah to Habsha (Abyssinia) to escape persecution by the Quraysh. Its Christian king, the Negus, gave them protection.

q: To whom was the Nishan-e-Haider last awarded?
f: Havaldar Lalak Jan Shaheed received the award for gallantry in the 1999 Kargil conflict; no later award is recorded.

q: According to the 2023 census, Urdu is the mother tongue of about what percentage of Pakistanis?
f: The Pakistan Bureau of Statistics 2023 census puts Urdu at about 9.25 percent of the population. Candidates in 2021-22 recalled about 7 percent, which was the 2017 census figure (7.08 percent).

q: Which are the three largest oceans of the world, in order of size?
f: By area the Pacific is the largest, then the Atlantic, then the Indian Ocean. The Southern and Arctic Oceans are smaller.

q: Which day is celebrated on 12 June?
f: The International Labour Organization observes the World Day Against Child Labour on 12 June each year.

q: What did Thomas Edison invent (practically)?
f: Thomas Edison developed the first practical long-lasting incandescent electric light bulb in 1879. He also invented the phonograph.

q: What does the word Al-Fatiha mean?
f: Al-Fatiha means The Opening, because it opens the Quran and also opens the prayer.

q: What does the Arabic word Ansar mean?
f: Ansar means helpers. It refers to the people of Madina who sheltered and helped the Muslims migrating from Makkah.

q: Uhad (Uhud) is the name of what?
f: Uhud is a mountain just north of Madina, near which the Battle of Uhud was fought in 3 AH.

q: What was Hilf-ul-Fudul (Half-e-Fadool)?
o: A pre-Islamic pact in Makkah to protect the oppressed and uphold justice
A treaty signed between the Muslims and the Quraish in 6 AH
A pact made by the Ansar of Madinah at Aqabah
A trade agreement between Makkah and Syria
f: Hilf-ul-Fudul was a pledge made by several Makkan clans to help victims of injustice and to see that wrongs were set right. The Prophet (PBUH) took part in it as a young man.

q: What does the term Ijtehad mean in Islamic law?
o: Independent reasoning to derive rulings from the Quran and Sunnah
Migration for the sake of faith
f: Ijtehad means exerting one's utmost intellectual effort to find a legal ruling on a new matter from the Quran and Sunnah. A scholar who does this is called a Mujtahid.

q: What does the Arabic word Mantiq mean?
f: Mantiq is the Arabic word for logic, the science of correct reasoning. It is taught in Dars-e-Nizami madrassas.

q: What does NFC stand for in Pakistan's finance system?
f: NFC stands for National Finance Commission. It decides how federal tax revenue is shared between the federation and the provinces.

q: What does the abbreviation PSL stand for in Pakistani cricket?
f: PSL stands for Pakistan Super League, the franchise Twenty20 cricket league of Pakistan. It began in 2016.

q: What does the word seething mean?
f: To seethe is to boil or churn, and it is used for a person who is extremely angry but does not show it. So seething means very angry.

q: What does Tayammum mean?
o: Dry ablution with clean earth when water is unavailable
f: Tayammum is a substitute for wudu or ghusl performed with clean earth or dust when water is not available or cannot be used. It is taught in the Quran in Surah Al-Maidah.

q: What does the Silk Route connect?
o: China with the Mediterranean and Europe
f: The Silk Route was an ancient network of trade roads linking China through Central Asia to the Mediterranean world. Silk was a major good carried along it.

q: What does the word Akhuwat mean?
f: Akhuwat is an Arabic and Urdu word meaning brotherhood. It is the name of a Pakistani organisation that gives interest-free loans.

q: What important event took place in 622 AD?
o: The Hijrah (migration) of the Prophet (PBUH) from Makkah to Madinah
f: The Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Madinah in 622 AD. This year marks the start of the Islamic Hijri calendar.

q: What is the value of 0! (zero factorial)?
f: By definition 0! = 1, because there is exactly one way to arrange no objects. This also keeps the formula n! = n x (n-1)! true for n = 1.

q: What is a period of 100 years also called?
f: A century is a period of 100 years. A decade is 10 years and a millennium is 1000 years.

q: What is 22 March observed as worldwide?
f: The United Nations observes 22 March each year as World Water Day. It raises awareness of fresh water and its sustainable use.

q: What does the United Nations observe on 24 January?
f: The UN General Assembly proclaimed 24 January as International Day of Education in December 2018. It was first observed in 2019.

q: What is the value of (3 - 2i) - (3 + 2i)?
f: Subtract the real parts: 3 - 3 = 0. Subtract the imaginary parts: -2i - 2i = -4i, so the answer is -4i.

q: What is an angle of 90 degrees called?
f: An angle of exactly 90 degrees is called a right angle. Acute angles are smaller and obtuse angles are larger.

q: What was the relation of A. O. Hume with the Indian National Congress?
o: He was one of its founders in 1885
He was its first Muslim president
He was the Viceroy who banned it
f: Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, helped found the Indian National Congress in December 1885. He served as its first general secretary.

q: Which word is a synonym of complicated?
f: Complicated means made of many parts and hard to understand, which is the meaning of complex. Simple, easy and plain are its opposites.

q: Which word is a synonym of conceal?
f: To conceal means to keep something out of sight, which is to hide it. Reveal, show and expose are antonyms.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'dormant'?
f: Dormant means temporarily inactive or sleeping, as in a dormant volcano.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'evacuate'?
f: To evacuate is to leave or empty a place, especially because of danger.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'exquisite'?
f: Exquisite describes something extremely beautiful and finely made.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'persistent'?
f: Persistent means continuing firmly despite difficulty, which is what tenacious means.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'savage'?
f: Savage means fierce, wild and untamed.

q: What is a zero vector also called?
f: A vector with zero magnitude and no definite direction is called a null vector.

q: What is the abscissa of a point in the Cartesian plane?
f: In a point (x, y), the abscissa is the x-coordinate, the horizontal distance from the y-axis.

q: What is Atomic Day (the day of Pakistan's 1998 nuclear tests) called in Pakistan?
f: Pakistan tested nuclear devices in the Chagai hills in 1998, and the day is observed as Youm-e-Takbeer.

q: In statistics, what is the average of a set of numbers also called?
f: The average is the sum of the values divided by their count, which is the arithmetic mean.

q: What is Bait ul Muqaddas?
f: Bait ul Muqaddas means the Holy House and refers to Jerusalem and its Masjid al-Aqsa.

q: What is Barzakh in Islamic belief?
o: The period between death and the Day of Judgement
f: Barzakh is the barrier or intermediate state between a person's death and resurrection.

q: Which event is commemorated on Kashmir Day (Youm-e-Yakjehti-e-Kashmir) in Pakistan?
o: Solidarity with the people of Kashmir
f: Kashmir Day is observed to express support for the Kashmiri right to self-determination.

q: What is cot x . sec x equal to?
f: cot x = cos x / sin x and sec x = 1 / cos x, so the product = 1 / sin x = cosec x.

q: What is the number of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) among the Khulafa-e-Rashideen?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) was the first Rightly Guided Caliph after the Prophet (PBUH).

q: What was Hilful Fudul?
o: A peace pact of Makkan tribes to protect the oppressed
A treaty between Muslims and Jews of Madinah
f: Hilful Fudul was a pact formed in Makkah to defend the wronged and help the weak, and the young Prophet (PBUH) took part in it.

q: In vector algebra, what is the value of j . j (dot product of the unit vector j with itself)?
What is Pakistan Standard Time relative to UTC?
f: Pakistan Standard Time (PST) is five hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time.

q: Among Muslim-majority countries, what is Pakistan's rank by population?
f: Indonesia has the largest population among Muslim-majority countries and Pakistan is second.

q: Which is the most populous district of Punjab, Pakistan?
f: Lahore has the largest population of any district in Punjab (about 13 million in the 2023 census).

q: Stainless steel is mainly an alloy of iron with which metal?
f: Stainless steel is iron alloyed with at least about 10.5 percent chromium, which resists rust.

q: What is the 15th night of Shaban called?
f: The night of the 15th of Shaban is known as Shab-e-Barat (night of forgiveness or record).

q: Which is the 3rd surah of the Holy Quran?
f: The order is Al-Fatiha, Al-Baqarah, Ali Imran, so the third is Ali Imran.

q: In the commonly taught Pakistani order of the five pillars of Islam (Kalima, Salah, Roza, Zakat, Hajj), which is the 4th pillar?
f: In this order the pillars run Shahada, Salah, Fasting, Zakat, Hajj, so the fourth is Zakat.

q: An acute angle is how large compared with a right angle?
f: A right angle is 90 degrees and an acute angle is any angle between 0 and 90 degrees, so it is smaller.

q: On which date is American Independence Day celebrated?
f: The US Declaration of Independence was adopted on 4 July 1776, and that day is celebrated as Independence Day.

q: What is the antonym of 'ally'?
f: An ally is a supporter or friend, and its opposite is an enemy or foe.

q: What is the antonym of 'cease'?
f: To cease means to stop, so its opposite is to continue.

q: What is the antonym of 'chum'?
f: A chum is a close friend, and the opposite is an enemy.

q: What is the antonym of 'climb'?
f: To climb is to go up, and the opposite is to descend (go down).

q: What is the antonym of 'expansion'?
f: Expansion means growing larger, and its opposite is contraction (becoming smaller).

q: What is the antonym of 'proceed'?
f: To proceed is to go forward, and the opposite is to halt or stop.

q: What is the base of the natural logarithm?
f: The natural logarithm ln x is the logarithm to base e, where e is approximately 2.71828.

q: What is the value of tan(-x)?
f: Tangent is an odd function, because sin(-x) = -sin x and cos(-x) = cos x, so tan(-x) = -tan x.

q: Which is the biggest continent in the world by area?
f: Asia covers about 44.6 million square kilometres, which is the largest of all continents.

q: In Islam, which is the biggest sin?
f: The Quran and Hadith describe shirk as the greatest sin, and Allah does not forgive it unless a person repents.

q: What is the capital of Bangladesh?
f: Dhaka is the capital and largest city of Bangladesh.

q: What is the political capital of Burundi?
f: Burundi moved its political capital from Bujumbura to Gitega in 2019.

q: What is the capital of Canada?
f: Ottawa is the capital of Canada, although Toronto is the largest city.

q: What is the capital of Germany?
f: Berlin is the capital of Germany.

q: What is the capital of Peru?
f: Lima is the capital and largest city of Peru.

q: What is the capital of Australia?
f: Canberra is the capital of Australia, chosen as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

q: What is the capital of Azerbaijan?
f: Baku is the capital of Azerbaijan, on the Caspian Sea.

q: What is the capital of Uganda?
f: Kampala is the capital of Uganda.

q: Which city was the capital of the ancient Gandhara civilization in Pakistani textbooks?
f: Taxila (Takshashila) is the capital of Gandhara most often given in Pakistani textbooks.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word abundant?
f: Abundant means existing in large quantities. Plentiful is the closest synonym.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word collaboration?
f: Collaboration means working together with others toward a common goal. Cooperation has the closest meaning.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word extensive?
f: Extensive means covering a large area or having a wide range. Widespread is the closest meaning.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word juvenile?
f: Juvenile refers to a young person or something belonging to young people. Youthful is the closest meaning.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word slackness?
f: Slackness means lack of tightness, energy or care. Looseness or laziness fits best.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word consent?
f: Consent means agreement or permission to do something.

q: What is the combination of the upper house and lower house of a legislature called?
f: The legislature made up of the upper and lower houses is called Parliament. In Pakistan it is the Majlis-e-Shoora.

q: Which is the correct spelling?
f: The final consonant n is doubled when adding ing to begin, giving beginning.

q: What is the currency of Belarus?
f: Belarus uses the Belarusian ruble (code BYN).

q: What is the currency of Kenya?
f: Kenya uses the Kenyan shilling (code KES).

q: What is the currency of Libya?
f: Libya uses the Libyan dinar (code LYD).

q: What is the currency of Sri Lanka?
f: Sri Lanka uses the Sri Lankan rupee (code LKR).

q: What is the date of America's Independence Day?
f: The Declaration of Independence of the United States was adopted on 4 July 1776, which is celebrated as Independence Day.

q: On what date did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah die?
f: Quaid-e-Azam died in Karachi on 11 September 1948, a little over a year after Pakistan was created.

q: On which date did Dr. Abdul Qadeer Khan die?
f: Dr. Abdul Qadeer Khan, known as the father of Pakistan's nuclear programme, died in Islamabad on 10 October 2021.

q: What is the derivative of the exponential function e to the power x with respect to x?
o: x times e to the power (x minus 1)
f: The function e^x is its own derivative, so d/dx of e^x equals e^x.

q: What is the duty of Hazrat Mikail (AS)?
f: Hazrat Mikail (AS) is the angel in charge of rain and the provision of sustenance.

q: According to the Islamic teachings, which question is first asked from a person in the grave?
f: Munkar and Nakir first ask the deceased: Who is your Lord (Man Rabbuka)? Then they ask about his religion and his Prophet.

q: What is the full official name of Pakistan?
f: Article 1 of the 1973 Constitution names the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

q: What is the standard time offset of Pakistan from GMT (UTC)?
f: Pakistan Standard Time is five hours ahead of GMT, that is UTC+5.

q: Which surah is called the heart (Qalb) of the Quran?
f: A hadith narrated in the books of Hadith describes Surah Yaseen as the heart of the Quran.

q: What is the highest court of Pakistan?
f: The Supreme Court of Pakistan, in Islamabad, is the apex court of the country.

q: What is the highest power of the variable in a polynomial called?
f: The degree of a polynomial is the largest exponent of its variable. For example, x^3 + 2x has degree 3.

q: What is the integral part of a logarithm called?
f: A logarithm has two parts: the integer part is the characteristic and the decimal part is the mantissa.

q: Which is the largest hot desert of the world?
f: The Sahara in North Africa covers about 9 million square kilometres and is the largest hot desert.

q: Which is the largest gulf in the world?
f: The Gulf of Mexico covers about 1.6 million square kilometres, which is the largest gulf.

q: Which is the largest plateau of the world by area?
f: The Tibetan Plateau covers about 2.5 million square kilometres and is the largest as well as the highest plateau.

q: Which is the largest sea of Europe?
f: The Mediterranean Sea covers about 2.5 million square kilometres, more than any other sea touching Europe.

q: What is the upgraded version of the Pakistani missile Hatf-IV (Shaheen-I) called?
f: Hatf-IV is the Shaheen-I ballistic missile, and its longer-range upgraded variant is called Shaheen-IA.

q: What is the literal meaning of the word Furqan?
o: The criterion that separates right from wrong
f: Furqan comes from an Arabic root meaning to separate or distinguish. It therefore means the criterion that distinguishes truth from falsehood.

q: What is the literal meaning of the word Islam?
o: Submission and surrender to the will of Allah
f: Islam comes from the Arabic root s-l-m, meaning submission, surrender and also peace. It means submitting oneself to Allah.

q: What is the literal meaning of Tayammum?
o: To intend or aim at something
f: Tayammum literally means to intend or to aim at something. In Islamic law it means purifying oneself with clean earth when water is unavailable.

q: What is the meaning of the word Al-Noor?
f: Noor is an Arabic word meaning light, and Al-Noor means The Light.

q: What is the meaning of the word conscious?
f: Conscious means being awake and aware of oneself or one's surroundings.

q: What is the meaning of the word gallant?
f: Gallant means brave and heroic, and also politely attentive to women.

q: What is the meaning of Hilf-ul-Fudul?
f: Hilf-ul-Fudul was a pact made in Makkah by chiefs who promised to defend the oppressed and give justice to all. Its name means the pact of the virtuous.

q: What is the meaning of the name Israel?
f: Israel is a Hebrew name, the title of Hazrat Yaqub (AS), meaning servant of God (Abdullah).

q: What is the meaning of the word oppression?
o: Cruel or unjust treatment of people
f: Oppression means the prolonged cruel or unjust use of power over others.

q: What is the meaning of Ruku in prayer?
f: Ruku means to bow, and in salah it is the posture of bowing with hands on the knees.

q: What is the meaning of the word Tanzeel?
f: Tanzeel comes from an Arabic root meaning to send down, and it is used for the revelation of the Quran.

q: What is the meaning of the word voyage?
o: A long journey, especially by sea
f: A voyage is a long journey, especially one made by sea or in space.

q: What is the meaning of the word defer?
f: To defer means to put off something until a later time.

q: What is the most abundant organic compound on Earth?
f: Cellulose forms the cell walls of plants and is the most abundant organic compound on Earth.

q: Which currency is most used in world trade?
f: The US dollar is the main currency for invoicing trade and for global reserves.

q: What is the multiplicative inverse of an identity matrix?
f: Since I times I equals I, the inverse of an identity matrix is the identity matrix itself.

q: Who was the father of Hazrat Ismail (AS)?
f: Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Hajra.

q: What is the boundary line between Pakistan and India in Kashmir called?
f: The Line of Control (LoC) separates Pakistan-administered and Indian-administered Kashmir.

q: Which continent is known as the Dark Continent?
f: Africa was called the Dark Continent because its interior was unknown to Europeans for a long time.

q: What was the name of the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) who was married to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Hazrat Ayesha (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) and a wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

q: What was the name of Pakistan's first satellite?
f: Badr-1, launched on 16 July 1990 from China, was the first satellite of Pakistan.

q: Which strait separates Russia and the United States (Alaska)?
f: The Bering Strait lies between the Chukchi Peninsula of Russia and Alaska in the United States.

q: What is the national animal of Pakistan?
f: The Markhor, a wild mountain goat with spiral horns, is the national animal of Pakistan.

q: Which word is nearest in meaning to 'diversity'?
f: Diversity means a range of different things, which is what variety means. Uniformity and similarity are its opposites.

q: What is the new name of the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD)?
f: RCD, formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey, was renamed the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985.

q: What is the nisab (minimum threshold) of gold for zakat, in tola?
f: The nisab of gold is 7.5 tola (about 87.48 grams). The 52.5 tola figure is the nisab of silver.

q: What is the rate of ushr (zakat on agricultural produce) on land watered by rain?
f: Ushr means one tenth, so produce from rain-fed land is charged at 10 percent. Land irrigated at a cost is charged at half of that, 5 percent.

q: What is the opposite of 'savage'?
f: Savage means wild and uncivilized, so its opposite is civilized. Fierce, wild and brutal are similar in meaning to savage.

q: What is the opposite of 'tame'?
f: Tame means domesticated and not dangerous, so its opposite is wild. Gentle, docile and domestic are close to tame in meaning.

q: What was the Pirpur Report (1938)?
o: A report on the Bengal famine
A Muslim League report on the treatment of Muslims under Congress ministries
A report on the partition of Bengal
f: The Pirpur Report was prepared by a Muslim League committee headed by the Raja of Pirpur. It listed the injustices done to Muslims in Congress-ruled provinces from 1937 to 1939.

q: What is the radian measure of a half circle (a straight angle)?
f: A full circle is 2 pi radians, so half of it is pi radians, which equals 180 degrees.

q: Hazrat Ali (RA) was related to Hazrat Abu Talib as his:
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib, the uncle of the Prophet (PBUH), who raised Ali's cousin the Prophet.

q: What is the scalar (dot) product of two vectors A and B?
o: A B sin(theta) as a vector
f: The scalar product is A.B = |A||B|cos(theta), where theta is the angle between them. The result is a number, not a vector.

q: What is the other name of the Battle of Ahzab?
f: The Battle of Ahzab (the Confederates) is also called the Battle of Khandaq (the Trench) because the Muslims dug a trench around Madinah. It was fought in 5 AH.

q: What is the shaving of the head during Hajj called?
f: Halq is shaving the whole head, and Qasr is trimming the hair. One of them is done to come out of the state of Ihram.

q: What is the source of the Yellow River (Huang He)?
o: Bayan Har Mountains in Qinghai, China
f: The Yellow River rises in the Bayan Har Mountains of Qinghai Province, China. It then flows east into the Bohai Sea.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to ADHERENT?
f: An adherent is a supporter or follower of a person, party or idea.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to EXCITING?
f: Exciting means causing great enthusiasm or eagerness, which is thrilling.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to EXTREMELY?
f: Extremely means to a very high degree, which is exceedingly.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to FLOURISH?
f: To flourish is to grow and develop in a healthy, successful way, which is to thrive.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to HERITAGE?
f: Heritage is what is passed down from earlier generations, such as traditions and property, which is a legacy.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to HIERARCHY?
f: A hierarchy is a system in which people or things are arranged in order of rank or importance.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to IMPAIR?
f: To impair is to damage or weaken something so that it works less well. The candidate answer Ridicule has a different meaning.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to INDIFFERENCE?
f: Indifference is a lack of interest or concern, which is apathy.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to LAXITY?
f: Laxity means lack of strictness or care, which is slackness.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to LEISURE?
f: Leisure is time free from work or duties, which is free time.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to MALICIOUS?
f: Malicious means intending to harm others, which is spiteful.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to MEDIATE?
f: To mediate is to step in between two sides in a dispute to settle it, which is to arbitrate.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to OPPRESS?
f: To oppress is to keep people down by cruel or unjust use of power, which is to persecute.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to PRECEDING?
f: Preceding means coming before in time or order, which is previous.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to PREVENT?
f: To prevent is to stop something from happening, which is to avert.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to PROMINENT?
f: Prominent means well known or important, which is eminent.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to RESENTMENT?
f: Resentment is a feeling of bitter anger about unfair treatment, which is bitterness.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to SPLENDID?
f: Splendid means very impressive or excellent, which is magnificent.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to TIMID?
f: Timid means lacking courage or confidence, which is shy.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to TOTALLY?
f: Totally means in every way or to the full extent, which is completely or entirely.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to TYRANT?
f: A tyrant is a ruler who uses power in a cruel and unjust way, which is a despot.

q: Which is the tallest animal living on land?
f: An adult giraffe can reach about 5 to 5.5 metres in height. No other land animal is taller.

q: What is the title (laqab) of Hazrat Adam (AS)?
f: Hazrat Adam (AS) is called Abul Bashar, the father of mankind. He is also called Safiullah.

q: What is the title of Hazrat Isa (AS)?
f: Hazrat Isa (AS) is called Ruhullah (Spirit of Allah) and also Al-Masih. Khalilullah is for Ibrahim, Kaleemullah for Musa and Zabihullah for Ismail (AS).

q: What is the title of Hazrat Jibrael (AS)?
f: Hazrat Jibrael (AS) is called Ruh ul Amin (the Trustworthy Spirit) in the Quran, and also Ruh ul Quds.

q: What is the length of the Line of Control (LoC) between Pakistan and India in Kashmir in kilometres, as most commonly given?
f: The Line of Control was set after the 1971 war and the Simla Agreement of 1972. It is most commonly given as about 740 km.

q: How many bones are there in the adult human body?
f: An adult skeleton has 206 bones. A newborn has about 300 which fuse as the child grows.

q: How many landlocked countries are there in the world?
f: Counting internationally recognised sovereign states with no sea coastline gives 44 landlocked countries.

q: What is the upper house of the Parliament of Pakistan called?
f: Pakistan's Parliament has two houses, and the upper house is the Senate.

q: What is the rate of ushr on crops grown with artificial irrigation (tube wells, canals bought or built at cost)?
f: Ushr is 10 percent on rain-fed land and half of that, 5 percent, where artificial irrigation involves cost.

q: What is the rate of zakat on gold and silver (above nisab)?
f: Zakat on gold, silver and cash savings above nisab is one-fortieth, which is 2.5 percent.

q: Which is the world's most populous country today?
f: India overtook China in 2023 to become the most populous country, according to the United Nations.

q: What is the Yellow River of China also called?
f: The Yellow River is known in Chinese as the Huang He.

q: What is Uhud?
f: Uhud is a mountain just north of Madinah where the Battle of Uhud was fought in 3 AH.

q: Youm-ul-Furqan is the name given to the day of which battle?
f: The Battle of Badr, fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH, is called Youm-ul-Furqan, the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.

q: Which part of speech is the word 'ouch'?
f: 'Ouch' expresses sudden pain or emotion, which is the job of an interjection.

q: What technique of defence was used in the Ghazwa Khandaq (Ahzab)?
f: Muslims dug a trench around the open northern side of Madinah to stop the Quraish cavalry.

q: What type of article is 'the'?
f: 'The' points to a specific noun, so it is the definite article.

q: What type of star is the Sun?
f: The Sun is a G2V main-sequence star, usually called a yellow dwarf.

q: For what is Hakeem Luqman best known?
f: Luqman was a sage whose wisdom and advice to his son are praised in the Quran.

q: What was RCD, formed in 1964?
o: Regional Cooperation for Development among Pakistan, Iran and Turkey
Regional Council for Defence of Asia
Regional Cooperation for Defence among Muslim states
f: RCD stood for Regional Cooperation for Development, an economic grouping of Pakistan, Iran and Turkey.

q: For what is Sher Shah Suri best known?
o: Grand Trade Road and administrative reforms
f: Sher Shah Suri (1540-45) rebuilt the Grand Trade Road, introduced the silver rupee and reformed revenue administration.

q: What was the Bay of Pigs invasion of 1961?
o: A failed US-backed invasion of Cuba
A US naval battle with Japan
f: In April 1961 Cuban exiles trained by the CIA landed at the Bay of Pigs and were defeated by Fidel Castro's forces.

q: What was the Cripps Mission?
o: A 1942 British mission offering India post-war dominion status
A 1946 plan for a united India
f: Sir Stafford Cripps came to India in March 1942 with proposals to win Indian support in World War II; both Congress and the Muslim League rejected them.

q: Which is considered the first book of Hadith compiled?
f: Imam Malik compiled the Muwatta in Madinah in the 8th century, and it is generally taken as the first book of Hadith.

q: Which international organization was the predecessor of the United Nations (UNO)?
f: The League of Nations, founded in 1920 after World War I, failed to prevent World War II and was replaced by the UN in 1945.

q: In which period did Hazrat Umar (RA) hold the caliphate?
f: Hazrat Umar (RA) became caliph after Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) in 634 CE and was martyred in 644 CE, ruling about ten and a half years.

q: What was the Simla Conference of 1945?
o: A meeting of Wavell with Indian leaders on self-government that failed
The signing of the Pakistan-India peace agreement
The announcement of the Partition Plan
The first session of the Constituent Assembly
f: The Viceroy Lord Wavell called Indian leaders to Simla in June-July 1945 to discuss an Executive Council. It failed because Congress and the Muslim League could not agree on who nominates Muslim members.

q: What was the so-called Pig War between the United States and Britain over?
f: The Pig War of 1859 was a border dispute over San Juan Island; it began after an American farmer shot a British-owned pig. The only casualty was the pig.

q: According to the Hadith, what will a person be asked about first on the Day of Judgement regarding the rights of Allah?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) said that the first thing a servant will be called to account for on the Day of Judgement is prayer (Salah).

q: When an ant stings, which acid is injected into the body?
f: Ant venom contains formic acid, which causes the burning pain of the sting.

q: When did the COVID-19 (coronavirus) pandemic begin?
f: The first cases were reported in Wuhan, China, in December 2019.

q: In which year did East Pakistan separate from Pakistan to become Bangladesh?
f: East Pakistan broke away after the 1971 war, and the Dhaka surrender took place on 16 December 1971.

q: In which year of the Hijri calendar did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) perform Umrat-ul-Qaza?
f: After the Treaty of Hudaibiya the Muslims performed the Umrah they were stopped from in 6 AH. They did it the next year, in 7 AH.

q: In which year of prophethood did Hazrat Umar (RA) embrace Islam, according to most Pakistani textbooks?
f: Hazrat Umar (RA) accepted Islam in the 6th year of prophethood, after the Prophet's prayer that Allah strengthen Islam through one of the two Umars.

q: When did India first present the Kashmir issue to the United Nations?
f: India took the Kashmir dispute to the UN Security Council on 1 January 1948 under Article 35 of the UN Charter.

q: What was the legislature setup under the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan?
f: The 1956 Constitution created a single-house (unicameral) National Assembly with equal representation (parity) for East and West Pakistan.

q: In which year did India take the Kashmir issue to the UN Security Council?
f: India lodged its complaint under Article 35 of the UN Charter on 1 January 1948, after tribal and Pakistani forces entered Kashmir. The Security Council then set up the UN Commission for India and Pakistan (UNCIP).

q: In which year did the First World War end?
f: The armistice with Germany took effect on 11 November 1918, ending the fighting. The Treaty of Versailles followed in 1919.

q: In which year did the Second World War end?
f: Germany surrendered in May 1945 and Japan surrendered in August and September 1945. The war therefore ended in 1945.

q: In which year did the Cabinet Mission visit India?
f: The British Cabinet Mission arrived in India in March 1946 and announced its plan in May 1946. It proposed a loose federation, which the Congress and the Muslim League accepted only briefly.

q: In which year was the Non-Cooperation Movement launched in India?
f: Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920, supported by the Khilafat leaders, against British rule. Indians boycotted British courts, schools and goods.

q: Around which year did the Ottoman Sultanate begin under Osman I?
f: Osman I founded the Ottoman state in Anatolia around 1299. It lasted until the sultanate was abolished in 1922.

q: On which date is Kashmir Day (Kashmir Solidarity Day) observed in Pakistan?
f: Pakistan observes Kashmir Solidarity Day on 5 February every year to express support for the people of Indian-held Kashmir.

q: In which year did the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College, Aligarh, begin as a college?
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded a school in 1875, which was raised to college level as the MAO College in 1877. Lord Lytton laid its foundation stone in 1877.

q: In which Hijri year was Hajj made obligatory (according to the most commonly taught view)?
f: Most Pakistani textbooks teach that Hajj became obligatory in 9 AH. The Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Abu Bakr to lead the Hajj that year.

q: In which year was the state of Israel declared?
f: Israel declared independence on 14 May 1948, as the British Mandate over Palestine ended. The first Arab-Israeli war followed immediately.

q: In which year was the National Bank of Pakistan (NBP) established?
f: The National Bank of Pakistan was established in November 1949 to help finance the agricultural sector, notably the jute and cotton crops. It later acted as an agent of the State Bank.

q: In which Hijri year did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) deliver his Last (Farewell) Sermon?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) delivered the Last Sermon during the Farewell Hajj on 9 Dhul Hijjah, 10 AH (632 CE), at Arafat. He passed away in 11 AH.

q: In which year did Choudhary Rahmat Ali write the pamphlet 'Now or Never'?
f: Choudhary Rahmat Ali and his Cambridge colleagues issued the pamphlet 'Now or Never' in January 1933. It first proposed the name Pakistan for a Muslim homeland.

q: In which year was the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) established by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey?
f: The RCD was formally established in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey to promote economic cooperation. It replaced the earlier CENTO-linked arrangements in the economic field.

q: In which year was the Second Battle of Panipat fought between Akbar's army and Hemu?
f: The Second Battle of Panipat was fought in 1556, when Akbar's general Bairam Khan defeated Hemu. It secured the Mughal throne for Akbar.

q: On what date was the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan enforced?
f: The National Assembly passed the Constitution on 10 April 1973, and it was enforced on 14 August 1973. It was authenticated by President Fazal Elahi Chaudhry.

q: In which year was the World Trade Organization (WTO) established?
f: The WTO came into being on 1 January 1995, replacing the GATT arrangement.

q: At which place did Allama Iqbal deliver his famous Presidential Address of 1930 in which he presented the idea of a separate Muslim state?
f: Iqbal delivered the Presidential Address at the annual session of the All-India Muslim League held at Allahabad in December 1930.

q: In which region does the Yellow River (Huang He) of China originate?
f: The Yellow River rises in the Bayan Har Mountains in Qinghai province on the Tibetan Plateau and flows east to the Bohai Sea.

q: In which country is Angel Falls, the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, located?
f: Angel Falls (Salto Angel) is in Canaima National Park in Bolivar state, Venezuela.

q: Where is Lake Superior located?
f: Lake Superior is the northernmost of the Great Lakes and lies between the USA and Canada in North America.

q: Where is the MAO College (founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan) located?
f: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College was founded in 1875 at Aligarh by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.

q: In which city is the Margalla Hills National Park located?
f: The Margalla Hills form the northern backdrop of Islamabad, the capital of Pakistan.

q: Which Indian Ocean water body is the Bay of Bengal part of?
f: The Bay of Bengal is the northeastern part of the Indian Ocean, bordered by India, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Sri Lanka.

q: Between which two countries does the Bay of Bothnia lie?
f: The Gulf or Bay of Bothnia is the northern arm of the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Finland.

q: Between which countries does the Gulf (Bay) of Riga lie?
f: The Gulf of Riga is an inlet of the Baltic Sea bordered by Latvia and Estonia.

q: In which country is Shark Bay, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, located?
f: Shark Bay is on the coast of Western Australia.

q: In which region was the ancient Gandhara civilization centred?
f: Gandhara flourished in the Peshawar valley and Potohar region of northwest Pakistan, with Taxila and Peshawar as major centres.

q: Where is the headquarters of SAARC located?
f: The SAARC Secretariat was established in Kathmandu, Nepal in 1987.

q: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations located?
f: The UN headquarters is on the east side of Manhattan in New York City, USA.

q: Where is the headquarters of OPEC located?
f: OPEC moved from Geneva to Vienna, Austria in 1965 and has been headquartered there since.

q: In which city or area is Simly Dam located?
f: Simly Dam is on the Soan River in the Islamabad Capital Territory, about 30 km from the city.

q: Where is the shrine of Data Ganj Bakhsh (Hazrat Ali Hujwiri) located?
f: Data Ganj Bakhsh, the author of Kashf-ul-Mahjoob, is buried in Lahore near Bhati Gate. His shrine is one of the most visited in Pakistan.

q: Where is the tomb of the Punjabi poet Waris Shah located?
f: Waris Shah, author of the epic Heer Ranjha, is buried at Jandiala Sher Khan in Sheikhupura district, where he died in 1798.

q: Where is the Zhob River situated?
f: The Zhob River rises in Balochistan and flows through the Zhob district, joining the Gomal River.

q: Where is the world's largest active volcano, Mauna Loa, located?
f: Mauna Loa is on the Big Island of Hawaii and is regarded as the largest active volcano on Earth by volume. It erupted in November 2022 for the first time since 1984.

q: The Yangtze and the Yellow River are the two longest rivers of which country?
f: Both the Yangtze and the Yellow River (Huang He) flow through China and empty into the sea on its east coast. The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia.

q: Where was Benazir Bhutto assassinated in December 2007?
f: Benazir Bhutto was killed on 27 December 2007 after addressing an election rally at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi. She was attacked as she left the venue.

q: In which city was Pakistan's first Prime Minister, Liaquat Ali Khan, assassinated in 1951?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan was shot on 16 October 1951 while addressing a public meeting at Company Bagh in Rawalpindi.

q: In which city was the Tashkent Declaration of 1966 signed?
f: The Tashkent Declaration was signed in Tashkent, then in the Soviet Union and now the capital of Uzbekistan.

q: Where was the atomic test of Pakistan conducted on 28 May 1998?
f: Pakistan carried out its first nuclear tests in the Ras Koh hills of Chagai district, Balochistan on 28 May 1998.

q: Where was the Battle of Khaibar fought?
o: Near Khaibar oasis north of Madinah, Arabia
f: The Battle of Khaibar was fought in 628-629 AD (7 AH) against the Jewish fortresses at the Khaibar oasis in Arabia. Hazrat Ali (RA) is famous for conquering the fort of Qamus.

q: Where did the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) receive the first revelation?
f: The first revelation (the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq) came in the Cave of Hira on Jabal al-Noor near Makkah.

q: Which acid is found in milk?
f: Sour milk contains lactic acid, formed when bacteria ferment lactose. Fresh milk is only slightly acidic.

q: Which military alliance was formed in 1955 by the Soviet bloc in response to NATO?
f: The Warsaw Pact was signed in 1955 by the USSR and its eastern European allies as a counter to NATO.

q: Which angel will blow the trumpet (Sur) on the Day of Judgement?
f: Hazrat Israfil (AS) is the angel appointed to blow the Sur to end the world and again to raise the dead.

q: Which body regulates electronic media in Pakistan?
f: The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) regulates private television and radio channels.

q: Which city is known as the City of Saints (Madinat-ul-Auliya)?
f: Multan is called the City of Saints because of its many shrines of Sufi saints, such as Bahauddin Zakariya and Shah Rukn-e-Alam.

q: Which commission, headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe, drew the boundary line between Pakistan and India in 1947?
f: The Boundary Commission chaired by Sir Cyril Radcliffe demarcated the Punjab and Bengal borders, and the line is called the Radcliffe Line. The Radcliffe Award was announced on 17 August 1947.

q: Which companion of the Prophet (PBUH) addressed King Najashi of Abyssinia on behalf of the Muslim migrants?
f: Hazrat Jafar bin Abi Talib was the spokesman of the Muslims who migrated to Abyssinia. He recited verses of Surah Maryam before Najashi.

q: In which country is the Wakhan Corridor situated?
f: The Wakhan Corridor is a strip of land in the north-east of Afghanistan in Badakhshan province.

q: Which of the following are the Scandinavian countries?
f: The Scandinavian countries are Norway, Sweden and Denmark.

q: Which two countries share the border that mostly follows the 49th parallel north?
f: Much of the border between the contiguous United States and Canada runs along the 49th parallel north.

q: Which country was the first to recognise Pakistan after its creation in 1947, according to most Pakistani textbooks?
f: Most Pakistani textbooks state that Iran was the first country to recognise Pakistan. Iran also sent the first ambassador.

q: Which country supplied S-400 air defence missile systems to India?
f: India signed a deal in 2018 with Russia for S-400 Triumf air defence systems. Deliveries began in 2021.

q: Which country hosted the third modern Olympic Games in 1904?
f: The third modern Olympics were held in St. Louis, Missouri, USA in 1904. The first was in Athens in 1896 and the second in Paris in 1900.

q: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) formed in 1964?
f: The RCD was formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey. Afghanistan was never a member.

q: Which country is known as the Land of the Long White Cloud?
f: The Maori name Aotearoa is translated as Land of the Long White Cloud and refers to New Zealand.

q: Which country is the world's largest producer of chromite (chromium ore)?
f: According to USGS data, South Africa is by far the largest chromite producer, with about 22.9 million tonnes in 2024. Kazakhstan is second.

q: Which two countries jointly developed the JF-17 Thunder fighter jet?
f: The JF-17 Thunder was jointly developed by Pakistan Aeronautical Complex (PAC) Kamra and China's Chengdu Aircraft Corporation.

q: Which cricket league is played in Pakistan?
f: The Pakistan Super League (PSL) is the professional Twenty20 league of Pakistan. It started in 2016.

q: Which cricketer broke Shahid Afridi's record for the fastest century in One Day Internationals?
f: Afridi scored a century off 37 balls in 1996. Corey Anderson of New Zealand reached a hundred in 36 balls against West Indies in January 2014 and broke it.

q: Which international day does the United Nations observe on 24 June?
o: International Day of Women in Diplomacy
f: The UN General Assembly declared 24 June as the International Day of Women in Diplomacy in 2022. It promotes the participation of women in diplomacy.

q: Which famous musician was born in Salzburg, Austria?
f: Mozart was born in Salzburg on 27 January 1756. Beethoven was born in Bonn, Bach in Eisenach and Schubert in Vienna.

q: Which was the last Ghazwa in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) personally took part?
f: The Ghazwa of Tabuk in 9 AH was the last military expedition led personally by the Prophet (PBUH).

q: Which authority regulates the oil and gas sector in Pakistan?
f: OGRA was established in 2002 to regulate the midstream and downstream oil and gas sector. NDMA handles disasters, WAPDA water and power, PEMRA electronic media.

q: Which is the coldest desert in the world?
f: The Antarctic Desert is the coldest and largest desert on Earth, with extremely low rainfall and temperatures far below freezing.

q: Which is the correct spelling?
f: The verb profit ends in a single t, and the stress is on the first syllable, so the consonant is not doubled: profited.

q: Which is the deepest ocean in the world?
f: The Pacific Ocean has the greatest average depth and contains the Mariana Trench, the deepest known point.

q: Which was the first qiblah of the Muslims?
o: Bait ul Muqaddas (Masjid al-Aqsa) in Jerusalem
f: Muslims prayed towards Bait ul Muqaddas for about 16 to 17 months after the Hijrah. The qiblah was then changed to the Kaaba.

q: Which is the highest capital city of the world?
f: La Paz, the seat of government of Bolivia, stands at about 3,640 metres above sea level, higher than any other capital.

q: Which is the highest highway of Pakistan?
f: The Karakoram Highway reaches about 4,693 metres at the Khunjerab Pass on the China border, the highest paved international road.

q: Which is the highest polo ground in Pakistan and the world?
f: The Shandur polo ground at Shandur Pass is about 3,700 metres high and is called the highest polo ground in the world.

q: Which mountain is known as the Killer Mountain?
f: Nanga Parbat is called the Killer Mountain because many climbers died on it in early attempts.

q: Which is the largest country of Asia by population?
f: India overtook China in 2023 and is now the most populous country in both Asia and the world, with about 1.45 billion people.

q: Which country is called the largest democracy in the world?
f: India has the largest electorate and the largest population of any democracy. It is called the world's largest democracy.

q: Which is the largest ethnic group of Afghanistan?
