f: Pashtuns form the largest ethnic group of Afghanistan, roughly 40 percent of the population.

q: Which is the largest lake of East Africa?
f: Lake Victoria covers about 68,800 square kilometres and is the largest lake in Africa by area.

q: Which is the largest landlocked country in the world?
f: Kazakhstan has an area of about 2.72 million square kilometres and no coastline on an ocean. It is the largest landlocked country.

q: Which is the largest man-made lake (reservoir) of Pakistan?
f: Tarbela Reservoir on the Indus has the largest surface area of any reservoir in Pakistan, about 250 square kilometres.

q: Which is the largest salt mine of Pakistan?
f: The Khewra Salt Mine in Jhelum district is the largest salt mine in Pakistan and one of the largest in the world.

q: Which is the longest river in the world according to most textbooks?
f: Most textbooks give the Nile as the longest river, at about 6,650 kilometres.

q: Which is the national news agency of Pakistan?
f: Associated Press of Pakistan (APP) is the state-run national news agency of Pakistan.

q: Which is the wettest place in the world (the one most commonly named in textbooks)?
f: Mawsynram in Meghalaya, India, receives the highest average annual rainfall of any inhabited place, over 11,000 mm.

q: In the Islamic calendar, which is the year called Aam-ul-Huzn (Year of Grief)?
f: In the 10th year of Prophethood, both Hazrat Khadijah (RA) and Abu Talib passed away, so it is called the Year of Grief.

q: Which lines are called parallel lines?
o: Lines that intersect at a right angle
Lines in the same plane that never meet
Lines that meet at one point
f: Parallel lines lie in the same plane and stay the same distance apart, so they never meet however far they are extended.

q: Which mountain (peak) lies on the border between China and Pakistan?
f: K2 in the Karakoram lies on the China-Pakistan border, between Gilgit-Baltistan and Xinjiang.

q: Which mountain range lies between France and Italy?
f: The Alps, including Mont Blanc, mark part of the border between France and Italy.

q: Which mountain range separates Spain and France?
f: The Pyrenees run between France and Spain.

q: Which obligatory act is mentioned in the Quran most often together with Zakat?
f: The Quran repeatedly pairs the command to establish Salah with the command to pay Zakat.

q: Which ocean lies along the coast of Pakistan?
f: Pakistan's coastline of about 1,046 km is on the Arabian Sea, which is part of the Indian Ocean.

q: Which of the following does not mean big: huge, massive, scrap?
f: Huge and massive both mean very large, while scrap means a small piece or leftover.

q: Which ancient civilization flourished in Taxila?
f: Taxila was a major city of the Gandhara civilization and a famed centre of learning.

q: Which Pakistani army operation was launched nationwide in February 2017?
f: Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad was announced on 22 February 2017 after a wave of terror attacks across Pakistan.

q: Which principal organ of the United Nations is no longer active (suspended operations)?
f: The Trusteeship Council suspended operations in 1994 after Palau, the last trust territory, became independent.

q: Which organization oversees international civil aviation?
f: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), a UN agency, sets global standards for civil aviation.

q: Which Pakistani batter holds the highest individual score in Test cricket for Pakistan?
f: Hanif Mohammad scored 337 against West Indies at Bridgetown in 1958, still Pakistan's highest Test score.

q: Which Pakistani scientist won the Nobel Prize in 1979?
f: Dr Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics with Sheldon Glashow and Steven Weinberg for the unified electroweak theory.

q: Which planet is named after the Roman equivalent of the Greek god Zeus?
f: Jupiter is the Roman name of the king of the gods, whom the Greeks called Zeus.

q: Which planet comes closest to the Earth?
f: Venus approaches Earth to about 38 million km, closer than any other planet.

q: Which prophet built the ark (boat) at the command of Allah before the great flood?
f: Allah commanded Hazrat Nuh (AS) to build the ark to save the believers from the flood.

q: Which Sahabi did the Prophet (PBUH) call the door of knowledge?
f: A hadith reports the Prophet (PBUH) saying: I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its door.

q: Which preposition completes the sentence: 'He reminded me ___ my History teacher'?
f: The verb 'remind' takes 'of' when something resembles or recalls another person or thing.

q: Which preposition is used with 'laugh' when making fun of someone: 'laughed ___ someone'?
f: To laugh at someone means to mock them; 'laugh at' is the correct phrasal form.

q: Which province of Pakistan has the largest provincial assembly?
f: The Provincial Assembly of the Punjab has 371 seats, more than the other three assemblies.

q: Which surah of the Holy Quran is named after the ant?
f: Surah Al-Naml (the Ant), the 27th surah, takes its name from the story of the ant that warned its colony about Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) and his army.

q: Which two oceans does the Panama Canal connect?
f: The Panama Canal cuts across the Isthmus of Panama and joins the Atlantic Ocean (via the Caribbean Sea) with the Pacific Ocean. This saves ships the long voyage around South America.

q: Which two surahs of the Holy Quran are together called Muawwazatain?
f: Surah Al-Falaq (113) and Surah Al-Nas (114) both begin with a request to seek refuge (ta'awwuz) with Allah. That is why the pair is called Muawwazatain.

q: Which was the first Muslim country to become a nuclear power?
f: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests at Chagai on 28 May 1998 and became the first Muslim country with nuclear weapons.

q: Which defensive technique was used by the Muslims in the Battle of Khandaq (Trench) in 5 AH?
o: Building a wall of stones around Makkah
Fighting from the hills of Uhud
A night surprise attack on the enemy camp
f: On the advice of Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA), the Muslims dug a long trench across the open side of Madinah. The Quraish and their allies could not cross it and had to retreat.

q: Who are called Ahl ul Bait?
o: All the companions of the Prophet (PBUH)
The family members of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)
f: Ahl ul Bait means the people of the house, that is the family of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), including his wives, daughter Fatimah (RA), Hazrat Ali (RA) and their children.

q: Which of the following was a daughter of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: The four daughters of the Prophet (PBUH) were Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatimah (RA). Aisha, Hafsa and Khadija (RA) were his wives.

q: Who is called the Hawari (special helper) of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: On the day of Khandaq the Prophet (PBUH) said that every prophet has a Hawari and his Hawari is Zubair (RA), as recorded in Sahih Bukhari.

q: Who broke Shahid Afridi's record for the most sixes in One Day Internationals?
f: Rohit Sharma hit his 352nd ODI six on 30 November 2025 against South Africa at Ranchi, passing Afridi's 351.

q: Who compiled the hadith collection Sahih Muslim?
f: Sahih Muslim was compiled by Imam Muslim bin al-Hajjaj al-Naysaburi (died 261 AH).

q: Who conducts and governs the modern Olympic Games?
f: The International Olympic Committee, founded in 1894 by Pierre de Coubertin, organises the modern Olympic Games.

q: Who elects the members of the Senate of Pakistan from the provinces?
o: The members of the Provincial Assemblies
f: Senators from each province are elected indirectly by the members of that provincial Assembly through the single transferable vote system.

q: Who first raised the Kashmir issue in the United Nations Security Council, and when?
f: India lodged a complaint under Article 35 of the UN Charter on 1 January 1948, and the Security Council took up the matter.

q: Who founded the technology company Microsoft?
f: Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded Microsoft on 4 April 1975.

q: Who gave the first Azan in Islam?
f: Hazrat Bilal bin Rabah (RA) was appointed by the Prophet (PBUH) as the first muezzin and called the first Azan in Madinah.

q: Who introduced the fictional spy character James Bond?
f: Ian Fleming created James Bond in the novel Casino Royale, published in 1953.

q: Who is known as the father of the hydrogen bomb?
f: Edward Teller, working with Stanislaw Ulam, is credited with the design of the hydrogen bomb, first tested in 1952.

q: Who was Abu Lahab?
o: The uncle of the Prophet (PBUH) who opposed him
The leader of the Banu Quraiza
f: Abu Lahab (Abdul Uzza bin Abdul Muttalib) was an uncle of the Prophet (PBUH) who strongly opposed Islam.

q: Who was Baba Farid (Hazrat Fariduddin Ganj Shakar)?
o: A Sufi saint of the Chishti order
A poet of the Sikh court
f: Baba Farid (1179-1266) was a famous Punjabi Sufi saint and poet of the Chishti order, and a disciple of Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki.

q: Who is Pakistan's highest run scorer in One Day Internationals?
f: Inzamam-ul-Haq scored 11,701 runs in ODIs, the most for Pakistan.

q: Which angel is responsible for rain and sustenance according to Islamic belief?
f: Hazrat Mikaeel (AS) is the angel in charge of rain and provision.

q: Who wrote Humayun Nama, an account of the reign of Emperor Humayun?
f: Gulbadan Begum, a daughter of Babur and aunt of Akbar, wrote Humayun Nama.

q: Who was the half-brother of Hazrat Ismail (AS)?
f: Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was a son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) from Hazrat Sarah, while Hazrat Ismail (AS) was his son from Hazrat Hajra, so they were half-brothers.

q: Who is the Chief Minister of Balochistan (as of 2026)?
f: Mir Sarfraz Bugti took office as Chief Minister of Balochistan in March 2024 and was still serving in mid-2026.

q: Who is the Chief of the Naval Staff of the Pakistan Navy?
f: Admiral Naveed Ashraf took over as Chief of the Naval Staff in October 2023 and is the serving chief in 2026.

q: Who is the Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
f: Sardar Ayaz Sadiq of the PML-N was elected Speaker on 1 March 2024 and is the current Speaker.

q: Who is the Defence Minister of Pakistan?
f: Khawaja Muhammad Asif of the PML-N is the Federal Minister for Defence in the current government.

q: Who is the Federal Minister for Interior of Pakistan?
f: Mohsin Naqvi is the Federal Interior Minister in the current government.

q: Who is the Speaker of the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab?
f: Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan of the PML-N has been Speaker of the Punjab Assembly since February 2024.

q: Who is the son of Hazrat Hajira (A.S)?
f: Hazrat Hajira was the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S) and the mother of Hazrat Ismail (A.S).

q: Who is known as the Traveler of Islam?
f: Ibn Battuta, a Moroccan scholar, traveled across much of the Muslim world and beyond for about 30 years and is called the Traveler of Islam.

q: Who is the writer of the book The Spirit of Islam?
f: The Spirit of Islam (1891) was written by Syed Ameer Ali.

q: Who is the writer of the book Becoming?
f: Becoming (2018) is the memoir of Michelle Obama, former First Lady of the United States.

q: Who is the compiler of Tirmizi Sharif (Jami at-Tirmidhi)?
f: Jami at-Tirmidhi was compiled by Imam Muhammad bin Isa at-Tirmidhi.

q: Who served the Holy Prophet (S.A.W) for ten years in Madinah?
f: Hazrat Anas bin Malik (R.A) was given to the Prophet (S.A.W) as a boy by his mother and served him for about ten years.

q: Who founded Facebook?
f: Mark Zuckerberg launched Facebook in 2004 from Harvard University with his college roommates.

q: Who is the father of Hazrat Usman (R.A)?
f: Hazrat Usman (R.A) was the son of Affan bin Abi al-As of the Banu Umayya clan of Quraysh.

q: Who is called the father of modern chemistry?
f: Antoine Lavoisier is commonly called the father of modern chemistry for his work on oxygen and the law of conservation of mass.

q: Who is regarded as the founder of modern nursing?
f: Florence Nightingale established modern nursing practice and training after her work in the Crimean War.

q: Who mediated between Pakistan and India in the Tashkent Agreement of January 1966?
f: The Soviet Prime Minister Alexei Kosygin hosted and mediated the talks at Tashkent. The agreement ended the 1965 war.

q: Who first proposed the name Pakistan?
f: Choudhry Rahmat Ali, a Cambridge student, coined the name Pakistan in his 1933 pamphlet Now or Never.

q: Who refused to accept the Nobel Prize in Literature?
f: The French writer Jean-Paul Sartre declined the 1964 Nobel Prize in Literature, saying he refused official honours.

q: Under the Constitution of Pakistan, by whom are the senators of the provinces elected?
o: The members of the provincial assembly
f: Senators for each province are elected by the members of that provincial assembly by the single transferable vote.

q: Who signed the Simla Agreement of 1972 on behalf of Pakistan?
f: President Zulfikar Ali Bhutto signed the Simla Agreement with the Indian Prime Minister in July 1972.

q: Who started the Non-Cooperation Movement in India in 1920?
f: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920, supported by the Khilafat Movement.

q: Who acts as the President of Pakistan when the President is absent or unable to perform the functions of office?
o: The Speaker of the National Assembly
f: Under Article 49 of the Constitution, the Chairman of the Senate acts as President. If there is no Chairman, the Speaker of the National Assembly does so.

q: Who were the Banu Nadir (Banu Nuzair) in the history of Madina?
o: A branch of the Aws tribe
f: Banu Nadir was a Jewish tribe living near Madina. They were exiled in 4 AH after plotting against the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

q: Who became the Chief Martial Law Administrator of Pakistan after Yahya Khan in December 1971?
f: After the fall of Dhaka, Yahya Khan handed power to Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, who became President and the first civilian Chief Martial Law Administrator.

q: Who was the husband of Hazrat Ayesha (RA)?
f: Hazrat Ayesha, daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr, was married to the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).

q: Who was the second Prime Minister of Pakistan?
f: Liaqat Ali Khan was the first Prime Minister. After his assassination in 1951, Khawaja Nazimuddin became the second.

q: Who was the second President of Pakistan?
f: Iskander Mirza was the first President under the 1956 Constitution. Ayub Khan removed him in 1958 and became the second.

q: Who was the Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army during the 1965 war with India?
f: General Muhammad Musa Khan was Commander-in-Chief from 1958 to 1966 and led the army in the 1965 war.

q: Who was the closest friend of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) was the Prophet's closest friend and the first man outside his family circle to accept Islam. He is called Siddique and Yar-e-Ghar (companion of the cave).

q: Who was the commander of the Quraysh army in the Battle of Uhud?
f: Abu Sufyan bin Harb led the Makkan army of about 3,000 in 3 AH, because Abu Jahl had been killed at Badr. Khalid bin Walid commanded the cavalry wing.

q: Who was the first Ameer-ul-Momineen (Commander of the Faithful) in Islamic history?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was called Khalifa-tu-Rasul Allah, while Hazrat Umar (RA) was the first to be addressed as Ameer-ul-Momineen. Most Islamic history books record this.

q: Who was the first caliph of Islam?
f: After the Prophet (PBUH) passed away in 11 AH, the Muslims chose Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) as their first caliph at Saqifa Bani Saida.

q: Who was the first Pakistani to win a Nobel Prize?
f: Dr Abdus Salam won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979, shared with Glashow and Weinberg, for the electroweak theory. He was the first Pakistani and the first Muslim Nobel laureate in science.

q: Who was the first President of Pakistan?
f: Under the 1956 Constitution, Iskander Mirza became the first President of Pakistan on 23 March 1956. Before this, the head of state was the Governor General.

q: Who was the first Pakistani woman to climb K2?
f: Samina Baig reached the summit of K2 on 22 July 2022, a few hours before Naila Kiani. She was the first Pakistani woman to do so.

q: Who was the first woman to travel to space?
f: Valentina Tereshkova of the Soviet Union flew aboard Vostok 6 in June 1963. She orbited the Earth 48 times.

q: Who was the first woman officer of the Pakistan Army to be promoted to the rank of Lieutenant General (three-star)?
f: Lt Gen Nigar Johar of the Army Medical Corps was promoted in June 2020 and became the first woman in the Pakistan Army to reach three-star rank. She was also appointed the first female Surgeon General of the Pakistan Army.

q: Who was the guarantor and third party that brokered the Indus Waters Treaty between India and Pakistan?
f: The World Bank mediated the long negotiations and signed the treaty as a party for certain provisions. The treaty was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960.

q: Who was the head of state of Pakistan in 1960?
f: Ayub Khan took power in the October 1958 coup and was President of Pakistan in 1960. He remained in office until March 1969.

q: Who was the false prophet and enemy leader fought by the Muslims in the Battle of Yamama?
f: The Battle of Yamama in 12 AH was fought against the false claimant to prophethood Musaylima Kazzab and his tribe Banu Hanifa. The Muslim commander was Hazrat Khalid bin Walid (RA), and Musaylima was killed.

q: Who led the Simla Deputation of 1906 that presented Muslim demands to the Viceroy Lord Minto?
f: The Simla Deputation of 1 October 1906 was led by Sir Sultan Muhammad Shah, Agha Khan III. It asked for separate electorates for Muslims.

q: Who signed the Indus Waters Treaty on behalf of Pakistan in 1960?
f: President Ayub Khan signed the treaty for Pakistan in Karachi on 19 September 1960. Jawaharlal Nehru signed it for India.

q: Who was the second martial law administrator of Pakistan?
f: Ayub Khan imposed the first martial law in October 1958. General Yahya Khan imposed the second in March 1969 when Ayub resigned.

q: Why is Hazrat Usman (RA) called Zun-Noorain?
o: He married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (SAW)
He had two lights on his sword
He was the leader of two armies
He migrated to two countries only
f: Zun-Noorain means Possessor of Two Lights. He married Ruqayyah (RA) and later Umm Kulthum (RA), both daughters of the Prophet (SAW).

q: Who were the Banu Nadir?
f: Banu Nadir was one of the main Jewish tribes living near Madinah. They were exiled after they broke their agreement with the Muslims.

q: Which of the following was an uncle of the Holy Prophet (SAW)?
f: Hazrat Hamza (RA) was a paternal uncle of the Holy Prophet (SAW). Hazrat Ali (RA) was his cousin, while Abu Bakr and Umar were companions.

q: Who wrote Hayat-e-Javed, the biography of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan?
f: Hayat-e-Javed, a biography of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan, was written by Khawaja Altaf Hussain Hali in 1901.

q: Who wrote Kashf-ul-Mahjoob?
f: Kashf-ul-Mahjoob is the oldest Persian book on Sufism and was written by Hazrat Ali Hujwiri, known as Data Ganj Bakhsh.

q: Who compiled the hadith book Sunan Nasai?
f: Sunan Nasai was compiled by Imam Nasai, whose full name was Ahmad ibn Shuayb al-Nasai.

q: Who wrote the memoir Becoming?
f: Becoming is the 2018 memoir of Michelle Obama, former First Lady of the United States.

q: Who compiled the hadith book Sunan Abu Dawood?
f: Sunan Abu Dawood was compiled by Imam Abu Dawood Sulayman ibn al-Ashath al-Sijistani.

q: Who wrote the pamphlet Now or Never (1933)?
f: Now or Never: Are We to Live or Perish Forever? was written by Chaudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933.

q: Who compiled Jami at-Tirmidhi (Sunan Tirmidhi)?
f: Jami at-Tirmidhi was compiled by Imam Muhammad ibn Isa al-Tirmidhi.

q: Which of these countries has only a maritime border with Pakistan and no land border?
f: Pakistan has land borders with Afghanistan, China, India and Iran. Oman has no land border with Pakistan but shares a sea boundary in the Arabian Sea.

q: With which Indian prime minister did Pakistan sign the Lahore Declaration in 1999?
f: The Lahore Declaration of February 1999 was signed by Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

q: With whom is the theory of relativity associated?
f: The theory of relativity was developed by Albert Einstein.

q: With the help of which country was the KANUPP-1 nuclear power plant at Karachi constructed?
f: KANUPP-1 is a CANDU heavy water reactor supplied by Canada and started operating in 1972.

q: Yaum-ul-Furqan is the name of the day of which event?
f: The Quran calls the day of the Battle of Badr Yaum-ul-Furqan, the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.

q: Y = mx + c is the formula of what?
f: It is the slope-intercept form of the equation of a straight line, where m is the slope and c is the y-intercept.

q: 1 degree is equal to how many seconds (of arc)?
f: 1 degree = 60 minutes and 1 minute = 60 seconds, so 1 degree = 60 x 60 = 3600 seconds.

q: 15 is divisible by which prime numbers?
f: 15 = 3 x 5, and both 3 and 5 are prime numbers.

q: 8/7 is which type of fraction?
f: In 8/7 the numerator 8 is greater than the denominator 7, so it is an improper fraction.

q: A boy bought a book for Rs 500 and sold it for Rs 700. What is his profit percentage?
f: Profit = 700 - 500 = Rs 200. Profit percentage = 200 / 500 x 100 = 40%.

q: Ali is 3 years old and his sister is 4 times his age. When Ali is 8 years old, what will his sister's age be?
f: Sister's age now = 4 x 3 = 12 years, so she is 9 years older. When Ali is 8 she will be 8 + 9 = 17 years.

q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will his sister's age be when Ali is 11?
f: Sister's age now = 3 x 4 = 12 years, so she is 8 years older. When Ali is 11 she will be 11 + 8 = 19 years.

q: Ali is 4 years old and Sara is 3 times Ali's age. What will Sara's age be when Ali is 12?
f: Sara is 3 x 4 = 12 years old now, so she is 8 years older. When Ali is 12 she will be 12 + 8 = 20 years.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. When Ali is 11 years old, what is his sister's age?
f: Sister's age now = 3 x 5 = 15 years, so she is 10 years older. When Ali is 11 she will be 11 + 10 = 21 years.

q: A train travels 60 km in 20 minutes. What is its speed in km/h?
f: 20 minutes = 1/3 hour. Speed = 60 / (1/3) = 180 km/h.

q: A train's speed is 100 km/h. How far does it cover in 1 minute (to two decimal places)?
f: 1 minute = 1/60 hour. Distance = 100 / 60 = 1.67 km (about 1667 metres).

q: A helicopter covers 320 km using 40 gallons of fuel. How many gallons are needed to cover 700 km?
f: Fuel per km = 40/320 = 1/8 gallon. For 700 km: 700/8 = 87.5 gallons.

q: A helicopter covers 350 km using 80 gallons of fuel. How many gallons does it need for 700 km?
f: 700 km is twice 350 km, so the fuel needed is twice as much: 2 x 80 = 160 gallons.

q: A jet covers 320 km using 50 gallons of fuel. How many gallons will it use to cover 700 km?
f: Fuel per km = 50/320 = 0.15625 gallon. For 700 km: 700 x 0.15625 = 109.375 gallons.

q: A man walks towards north, after some time turns right and then turns left. In which direction is he moving now?
f: Facing north, a right turn makes him face east. A left turn from east makes him face north again.

q: If the letters of the word BEAUTY are arranged in alphabetical order, which letter will come last?
f: Alphabetical order of the letters is A, B, E, T, U, Y. The last letter is Y.

q: Ali and Hasan have 24 apples in total. Ali has 3 times as many apples as Hasan. How many apples does Hasan have?
f: Let Hasan have x apples, then Ali has 3x. So 4x = 24 and x = 6.

q: Ali is older than Kashif and Kashif is older than Haris. Who is the oldest and who is the youngest?
f: Ali is older than Kashif, who is older than Haris, so Ali is the oldest and Haris the youngest.

q: Ali is taller than Osama and Osama is taller than Faheem. Who is the tallest of all?
f: Ali is taller than Osama, who is taller than Faheem, so Ali is the tallest.

q: Ali is younger than Hassan and Akbar is younger than Ali. Who is the oldest and who is the youngest?
f: Hassan is older than Ali, who is older than Akbar, so Hassan is the oldest and Akbar the youngest.

q: Ali's sister is three times Ali's age. If Ali is 3 years old, how old will his sister be when Ali is 7 years old?
f: Sister is 3 x 3 = 9 years old when Ali is 3. The age gap is 6 years, so when Ali is 7 she is 7 + 6 = 13.

q: Are the numbers 1, 3, 9, 11, 13 even or odd numbers?
f: Each of these numbers leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2, so they are odd numbers.

q: Arrange these words alphabetically: beauty, leopard. Which comes first?
f: B comes before L in the alphabet, so beauty comes first and leopard second.

q: Complete the alphabet pairs series: AZ, BY, CX, ?
f: The first letter moves forward (A, B, C, D) while the second moves backward (Z, Y, X, W). The next pair is DW.

q: Complete the series: 115, 55, 170, 65, 235, ?
f: Terms at odd places: 115, 170, 235 (adding 55, then 65). Terms at even places: 55, 65, 75 (adding 10 each time).

q: Complete the series: 2, 4, 8, 16, ?
f: Each term is double the previous one, so 16 x 2 = 32.

q: Cows are twice the number of horses and there are 9 goats. If there are 6 cows, how many animals are there in total?
f: Horses = 6 / 2 = 3. Total = 6 cows + 3 horses + 9 goats = 18.
The number 3 appears four times, more than any other value (2 and 5 appear twice).

q: Find the next term in the coding series: 3Z, 4X, 5U, ?
f: Numbers rise by 1 (3, 4, 5, 6). Letter positions are Z=26, X=24, U=21, falling by 2, 3, then 4, so next is 17 = Q.

q: How do you find the midpoint of a line segment joining (x1, y1) and (x2, y2)?
o: Average the x values and the y values
f: The midpoint is ((x1 + x2) / 2, (y1 + y2) / 2), the average of each coordinate.

q: How many minutes are there in 20 degrees (angle measure)?
f: One degree = 60 minutes of arc, so 20 x 60 = 1200 minutes.

q: What is the maximum number of right angles a triangle can have?
f: Angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees, so two right angles (180) would leave nothing for the third angle. At most one right angle is possible.

q: How many vowels are in the letters: DACBIJUHOLEWPSI?
f: The vowels are A, I, U, O, E, I, which makes 6.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 28th be?
f: The 28th is 27 days after the 1st. 27 = 3 weeks + 6 days, so Monday + 6 days = Sunday.

q: If 2 log 5 = x, find x.
f: By the power rule, n log a = log (a^n), so 2 log 5 = log 5^2 = log 25.

q: If 20 pens cost Rs 2000, how much will 40 pens cost?
f: One pen costs 2000 / 20 = Rs 100, so 40 pens cost 40 x 100 = Rs 4000.

q: If 3x - 5 = 4, find x.
f: Add 5 to both sides: 3x = 9, so x = 3.

q: If 6 : m :: 9 : 12, what is m?
f: Proportion gives 6/m = 9/12, so m = 6 x 12 / 9 = 8.

q: If the 12th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 24th day of that month?
f: From the 12th to the 24th is 12 days, and 12 divided by 7 leaves remainder 5. Moving 5 day(s) forward from Monday gives Saturday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day is the 14th day of that month?
f: From the 2nd to the 14th is 12 days, and 12 divided by 7 leaves remainder 5. Moving 5 day(s) forward from Friday gives Wednesday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day is the 25th day of that month?
f: From the 2nd to the 25th is 23 days, and 23 divided by 7 leaves remainder 2. Moving 2 day(s) forward from Monday gives Wednesday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day is the 24th day of that month?
f: From the 2nd to the 24th is 22 days, and 22 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1. Moving 1 day(s) forward from Monday gives Tuesday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 13th day of that month?
f: From the 2nd to the 13th is 11 days, and 11 divided by 7 leaves remainder 4. Moving 4 day(s) forward from Sunday gives Thursday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day is the 23rd day of that month?
f: From the 2nd to the 23rd is 21 days, and 21 divided by 7 leaves remainder 0. Moving 0 day(s) forward from Friday gives Friday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day is the 23rd day of that month?
f: From the 2nd to the 23rd is 21 days, and 21 divided by 7 leaves remainder 0. Moving 0 day(s) forward from Monday gives Monday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Tuesday, what day is the 14th day of that month?
f: From the 2nd to the 14th is 12 days, and 12 divided by 7 leaves remainder 5. Moving 5 day(s) forward from Tuesday gives Sunday.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Friday, what day is the 26th day of that month?
f: From the 3rd to the 26th is 23 days, and 23 divided by 7 leaves remainder 2. Moving 2 day(s) forward from Friday gives Sunday.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Monday, what day is the 13th day of that month?
f: From the 3rd to the 13th is 10 days, and 10 divided by 7 leaves remainder 3. Moving 3 day(s) forward from Monday gives Thursday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 23rd day of that month?
f: From the 4th to the 23rd is 19 days, and 19 divided by 7 leaves remainder 5. Moving 5 day(s) forward from Monday gives Saturday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day is the 25th day of that month?
f: From the 4th to the 25th is 21 days, and 21 divided by 7 leaves remainder 0. Moving 0 day(s) forward from Friday gives Friday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day is the 21st day of that month?
f: From the 4th to the 21st is 17 days, and 17 divided by 7 leaves remainder 3. Moving 3 day(s) forward from Friday gives Monday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 24th day of that month?
f: From the 4th to the 24th is 20 days, and 20 divided by 7 leaves remainder 6. Moving 6 day(s) forward from Monday gives Sunday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 28th day of that month?
f: From the 4th to the 28th is 24 days, and 24 divided by 7 leaves remainder 3. Moving 3 day(s) forward from Monday gives Thursday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 12th day of that month?
f: From the 4th to the 12th is 8 days, and 8 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1. Moving 1 day(s) forward from Sunday gives Monday.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Friday, what day is the 14th day of that month?
f: From the 1st to the 14th is 13 days, and 13 divided by 7 leaves remainder 6. Moving 6 day(s) forward from Friday gives Thursday.

q: A car travels at 90 km per hour. How much distance does it cover in 40 minutes?
f: 40 minutes is 2/3 of an hour, so distance = 90 x 2/3 = 60 km.

q: If a helicopter needs 340 gallons of fuel to cover 500 km, how much fuel will it need to cover 700 km?
f: Fuel is proportional to distance: 340 x 700 / 500 = 476 gallons.

q: If A is a subset of B, then A union B is equal to which set?
f: Every element of A is already in B, so combining A and B gives just B.

q: If log x = y (common logarithm, base 10), what is x?
f: By definition, log x = y with base 10 means x = 10^y.

q: If U is the universal set and A is a subset of U, what is the set U - A called?
f: U - A contains all elements of the universal set that are not in A. This set is called the complement of A.

q: If (x - 1, y + 1) = (0, 0), what are the values of x and y?
f: Equal ordered pairs have equal components: x - 1 = 0 gives x = 1, and y + 1 = 0 gives y = -1.

q: If y = 2x + 2 and x = 2, what is the value of y?
In a class of 400 students, 340 are present. What is the percentage of students present?
f: Percentage present = 340 / 400 x 100 = 85%.

q: In a class of 500 students, 240 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
f: Absent students = 500 - 240 = 260. Percentage absent = 260 / 500 x 100 = 52%.

q: In a class of 500 boys, 340 are present. How many boys are absent?
Out of 1200 students, 560 are boys. What is the percentage of girls (to two decimal places)?
Into how many semicircles does a diameter divide a circle?
f: A diameter passes through the centre and cuts the circle into two equal halves, each called a semicircle.

q: Multiply the biggest and the smallest of the numbers 7, 4, 3, 6, 5, 2, then subtract the product from the sum of all the numbers. What is the result?
f: Biggest is 7 and smallest is 2, so the product is 14. The sum is 7+4+3+6+5+2 = 27, and 27 - 14 = 13.

q: Odd one out: Islamabad, Lahore, Quetta, Rawalpindi.
f: Islamabad is the federal capital, Lahore is the capital of Punjab and Quetta is the capital of Balochistan. Rawalpindi is not a capital.

q: P = mc + q is what type of equation?
f: The variable c appears only to the power one, so the equation is of the form y = mx + c, a linear equation.

q: Point out the odd one out: Angle, Rectangle, Square, Hexagon.
f: Rectangle, square and hexagon are closed plane figures (polygons), while an angle is not a shape but a measure formed by two rays.

q: Rearrange the letters IAPRS to form a word. What does the word name?
f: The letters I, A, P, R, S rearranged give PARIS, the capital of France.

q: Rearrange the letters RSPAI to get the name of a city.
f: The letters R, S, P, A, I rearrange to PARIS.

q: Sheep is to wool as cat is to what?
f: Wool is the covering that grows on a sheep, and fur is the covering that grows on a cat.

q: Speak is to hear as look is to what?
f: Speaking is matched by hearing, and looking is matched by seeing, the result received.

q: What is the approximate value of the square root of 3?
f: 1.732 x 1.732 is about 3.0, so the square root of 3 is about 1.732.

q: The cube of unity (1 cubed) is equal to what?
f: 1 x 1 x 1 = 1, so the cube of unity is 1.

q: The population of a village was 2000 in the year 2000. If it doubled every five years, what was its population in 1980?
f: From 1980 to 2000 is 20 years, which is 4 doublings. So the 1980 population is 2000 / 2 / 2 / 2 / 2 = 125.

q: In division, the remainder is always less than which number?
f: If the remainder were equal to or larger than the divisor, the divisor could be taken once more, so the remainder is always smaller than the divisor.

q: Today is Sunday. What will be the day after tomorrow?
f: Tomorrow is Monday, so the day after tomorrow is Tuesday.

q: There are 24 students and 1/4 of them are male. What is the percentage of females?
f: Males are 1/4 = 25%, so females are 100 - 25 = 75% (18 of 24).

q: Total students in a class are 1500 and 1200 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
What are the two square roots of 64?
f: 8 x 8 = 64 and (-8) x (-8) = 64, so the roots are +8 and -8.

q: What is 10% of 80?
What is the value of 1 - 2 + 2/2?
f: Division first: 2/2 = 1. Then 1 - 2 + 1 = 0.

q: What is 1/3 of 36?
What is the value of 2 + 2 x 2?
f: Multiplication comes first: 2 x 2 = 4, then 2 + 4 = 6.

q: What is the value of 2 + 3/3?
f: Division first: 3/3 = 1, then 2 + 1 = 3.

q: What is the value of 2 x 3 + 3 x 6?
What is 30% of 20?
What is the value of 3 + 3 x 3?
f: Multiplication first: 3 x 3 = 9, then 3 + 9 = 12.

q: What is 60% of 80?
What is 90% of 9?
What is a chord that passes through the centre of a circle called?
f: A chord through the centre is the longest chord of the circle and is called the diameter.

q: What is an angle greater than 90 degrees (and less than 180 degrees) called?
f: An angle between 90 and 180 degrees is obtuse.

q: What is a matrix whose entries are all zero called?
f: A matrix with every element equal to zero is called a null (zero) matrix.

q: What is the value of cos 90 degrees?
f: On the unit circle, the point at 90 degrees is (0, 1), and its x-coordinate, the cosine, is 0.

q: What is cos x multiplied by tan x equal to?
f: Since tan x = sin x / cos x, cos x times tan x = sin x.

q: What is one tenth of 30?
f: One tenth of 30 is 30 / 10 = 3.

q: What is the value of tan 0 degrees?
f: tan 0 = sin 0 / cos 0 = 0 / 1 = 0.

q: What is the 2nd letter of the English alphabet?
f: The alphabet runs A, B, C, so the second letter is B.

q: What is the conjugate of a real number?
f: The conjugate of a + bi is a - bi. For a real number b = 0, so the conjugate is the same number.

q: What is the common difference in the series 4, 7, 10, 13?
f: 7 - 4 = 3, 10 - 7 = 3 and 13 - 10 = 3, so the difference is 3.

q: What is the distance between the points (-2, 0) and (-2, -3)?
f: The x-coordinates are equal, so the distance is |0 - (-3)| = 3. By formula: sqrt(0 + 9) = 3.

q: Which is the distance formula between points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2)?
f: The distance comes from the Pythagorean theorem applied to the horizontal and vertical differences.

q: What is the HCF of 18 and 24?
f: 18 = 2 x 3 x 3 and 24 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3. The common factors are 2 and 3, so HCF = 6.

q: What is the value of 2 + 2/3?
f: Division comes first: 2/3. Then 2 + 2/3 = 6/3 + 2/3 = 8/3, which is 2 and 2/3.

q: Which word is a synonym of extension?
f: Extension means an act of making something longer or larger, which is expansion.

q: Which word is a synonym of severely?
f: Severely means in a very strict or intense manner, which is harshly.

q: Where does the line y = 3 + 5y lie?
o: Parallel to the x-axis, so it is neither axis
f: Rearranging gives -4y = 3, so y = -3/4. This is a horizontal line parallel to the x-axis, not the axis itself.

q: What comes next in the series: 1 X 2 Y Y 3 Z Z ?
f: The numbers 1, 2, 3 are followed by X once, Y twice and Z three times. So one more Z completes 3 ZZZ.

q: Which comes next in the series: A2, D5, F9, ?
f: Letters move +3, +2, +1 (A, D, F, G) and numbers add 3, 4, 5 (2, 5, 9, 14). So the next term is G14.

q: Which letter comes immediately before W in the English alphabet?
f: The alphabet runs ... U, V, W, X, so V comes just before W.

q: Which letter comes next: A B C D E F G H ?
f: The letters are in alphabetical order, and the one after H is I.

q: In the series A1, C3, D4, G?, what number follows G?
f: Each number is the alphabet position of its letter: A=1, C=3, D=4, so G=7.

q: Which comes next in the series: A5, B10, C15, ?
f: Letters move forward one step (A, B, C, D) and numbers increase by 5 (5, 10, 15, 20). So the next is D20.

q: Which of the letters A, H, I, W, M, O, T, U, Y look the same in a mirror (vertical mirror held beside the letter)?
o: Only A, H, I and O
Only H, I, O and W
Only M, T, U and Y
f: Every one of these letters is symmetric about a vertical line, so each looks the same when reflected.

q: Which number comes next: 105, 55, 160, 65, 225, 75, ?
f: The numbers at odd places (105, 160, 225) rise by 55, then 65, so the next rise is 75: 225 + 75 = 300. The other numbers (55, 65, 75) rise by 10 each time.

q: Which number comes next: 115, 55, 170, 65, ?
f: Two series are mixed: 115, 170 rise by 55, then 65 more, so 170 + 65 = 235. The other series 55, 65 would continue with 75 afterwards.

q: Which number comes next: 115, 55, 170, 65, 235, 75, ?
f: Each big number is the previous big number plus the small number after it: 115+55=170, 170+65=235, 235+75=310.

q: Which number comes next: 115, 55, 225, 65, 335, ?
f: The odd places 115, 225, 335 rise by 110 each time. The even places 55, 65 rise by 10, so the next is 75.

q: Which number comes next: 2, 4, 8, 14, ?
f: The differences are 2, 4, 6, so the next difference is 8. Hence 14 + 8 = 22.

q: Which number comes next: 66, 63, 57, 45, ?
f: The differences are 3, 6, 12, doubling each time, so the next difference is 24. Hence 45 - 24 = 21.

q: Which one is a prime number: 12, 25, 30, 37?
f: 12 and 30 are even, and 25 = 5 x 5. 37 has no divisor other than 1 and itself, so it is prime.

q: Which one is different: A12, B13, D15, E19, C14?
f: Letter position plus 11 gives the number: A(1)=12, B(2)=13, C(3)=14, D(4)=15. For E(5) it should be 16, but it is 19.

q: Which quantity has no unit?
f: A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind, so the units cancel and it is dimensionless. The others all have units.

q: Which one is different: Cricket, Football, Tennis, Baseball?
f: Cricket, tennis and baseball are played with a bat or racket, while football is played with the feet and no bat.

q: Who is the President of Russia?
f: Vladimir Putin is the President of Russia, in office since 2012 after earlier terms from 2000 to 2008.

q: What is the capital of Nepal?
f: Kathmandu is the capital and largest city of Nepal. It lies in the Kathmandu Valley in the Himalayan region.

q: Who is the President of the United States in October 2026?
f: Donald Trump won the 2024 election and was sworn in as the 47th President on 20 January 2025.

q: What is the capital of Lebanon?
f: Beirut is the capital and largest city of Lebanon.

q: In which year did the Minto-Morley Reforms (Indian Councils Act) come into effect?
f: The Indian Councils Act of 1909, known as the Minto-Morley Reforms, introduced separate electorates for Muslims. Lord Minto was Viceroy and Lord Morley was Secretary of State for India.

q: In which country did Pakistan open its first embassy?
f: Pakistan opened its first embassy in Iran, which was also among the first countries to recognise Pakistan in 1947.

q: Who is the current President of India?
f: Droupadi Murmu took oath as the 15th President of India on 25 July 2022.

f: The first period has only one shell, which can hold two electrons, so it contains just hydrogen (H) and helium (He).

q: By what other name is the Pakistan Resolution known?
f: The Pakistan Resolution of 1940 was passed at Lahore, so it is also called the Lahore Resolution. It demanded independent states for the Muslims of India.

q: What is the antonym of 'stagnant'?
f: Stagnant means not flowing or moving, as in stagnant water. Its opposite is flowing.

q: In football, what did BPL originally stand for in the English league?
f: The English top division was sponsored by Barclays from 2001 to 2016 and was called the Barclays Premier League (BPL). Today it is simply the Premier League.

q: What does the word venerate mean?
f: To venerate is to regard someone or something with deep respect and reverence. Its synonyms are revere and honour.

q: Which of the following vitamins is NOT water soluble?
f: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat soluble and do not dissolve in water. The B vitamins and vitamin C are water soluble.

q: A man walks 20 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes. How much time will he take to cover 1 km?
f: 1 hour 40 minutes = 100 minutes. Time for 1 km = 100 / 20 = 5 minutes.

q: Which party formed the government in the North-West Frontier Province (now KPK) at the time of independence in 1947?
f: The ministry of Dr Khan Sahib, which belonged to the Indian National Congress (backed by the Khudai Khidmatgars), was in power in the province in August 1947.

q: For how many days was the 1965 Pakistan-India war fought?
f: The war began in early September 1965 and the ceasefire came on 23 September 1965, a total of 17 days. It is remembered as the 17-day war.

q: In which year was the Mangla Dam completed?
f: Construction of Mangla Dam on the Jhelum River began in the early 1960s and it was completed in 1967. Sources differ slightly on the start year but agree on 1967.

q: Which battle of the Muslims, fought in 3 AH, is counted as the second major battle after Badr?
f: The major battles in order are Badr (2 AH), Uhud (3 AH) and Khandaq (5 AH), so Uhud is the second.

q: Which prophet was sent to the nation (Qaum) of Aad?
f: Allah sent Hazrat Hud (AS) to guide the people of Aad, who lived in Al-Ahqaf in southern Arabia.

q: Who abrogated the 1956 constitution of Pakistan?
f: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 constitution on 7 October 1958 and imposed martial law.

q: What was the real name of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
f: His name was Abdullah bin Abi Quhafa, and he received the title Siddiq and Atiq.

q: SUPARCO is the national organization of Pakistan for which field?
f: SUPARCO stands for Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, Pakistan's national space agency.

q: How many votes in the 336-member National Assembly are needed to pass a no-confidence motion against the Prime Minister?
f: A no-confidence resolution needs a majority of the total membership of the House. Half of 336 is 168, so 169 votes are needed.

q: What is cos(90 degrees - x) equal to?
f: By the complementary angle identity, cos(90 - x) = sin x.

q: Which document paved the way for the constitution of Pakistan?
f: The Objective Resolution of 1949 laid down the guiding principles for the constitutions of Pakistan and became their preamble.

q: In a village the population in 2000 was 4600 and it doubles every five years. What was the population in 1995?
f: Going back five years halves the population: 4600 / 2 = 2300.

q: Which province of Pakistan was the first to issue driving licences to transgender persons (in 2018)?
f: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa traffic police issued driving licences to transgender persons in March 2018, the first province to do so.

q: Who was the Prime Minister of India when the Indus Waters Treaty was signed in 1960?
f: Jawaharlal Nehru signed the treaty with Pakistan's President Ayub Khan at Karachi on 19 September 1960.

q: How many doors (gates) does Jannah (Paradise) have according to hadith?
f: Authentic hadith state that Paradise has eight gates, one of them being Ar-Rayyan for those who fast.

q: What does FATF stand for?
f: FATF is the Financial Action Task Force, an international body that sets standards against money laundering and terror financing.

q: Which woman is mentioned by name in the Quran?
f: Hazrat Maryam (AS), the mother of Prophet Isa (AS), is the only woman named in the Quran.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'forestall'?
f: To forestall means to prevent something from happening by taking action ahead of time.

q: Who sold the Kashmir valley to Gulab Singh in 1846?
f: By the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) the British East India Company sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh for 7.5 million rupees.

q: Who was the first Hafiz of the Holy Quran?
f: The Quran was revealed to the Holy Prophet (PBUH), who memorised it first, so he is called the first Hafiz.

q: Who issues an ordinance at the federal level in Pakistan?
f: Under Article 89 of the 1973 Constitution, the President can promulgate an ordinance when the National Assembly is not in session.

q: In which year was Pakistan's first postage stamp issued?
f: Pakistan issued its first set of four postage stamps on 9 July 1948.

q: How many Muslims were martyred in the Battle of Uhud?
f: About 70 Muslims were martyred at Uhud, including Hazrat Hamza (RA).

q: How many times did Jansher Khan win the World Open squash title?
f: Jansher Khan won the World Open squash championship eight times between 1987 and 1996.

q: Who was the king (Najashi) of Habsha (Abyssinia) who gave shelter to the Muslim migrants?
f: The Christian king of Abyssinia, known by the title Najashi (Negus), was Ashama ibn Abjar. He protected the early Muslims who migrated there.

q: What does KRL stand for?
f: KRL stands for Khan Research Laboratories, named after Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan. It is located at Kahuta.

q: What is the legislature of Pakistan called?
f: Pakistan's federal legislature is the Majlis-e-Shura (Parliament), made up of the President, the National Assembly and the Senate.

q: In which region of Pakistan is the Neelum Valley and the Neelum River located?
f: The Neelum Valley and the Neelum River lie in Azad Jammu and Kashmir.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 10 years old?
f: The sister is 15 years old when Ali is 5, so she is 10 years older than him. When Ali is 10, she is 10 + 10 = 20 years old.

q: In which city is Ayub National Park located?
f: Ayub National Park is a large public park on Murree Road in Rawalpindi, named after President Ayub Khan.

q: What is the meaning of the word prescribe?
o: To recommend or order as a remedy or rule
f: To prescribe means to advise or order something, such as a medicine or a rule. Its synonyms include recommend, advise and ordain.

q: Jabal-e-Rehmat (Mount of Mercy) is located near which city?
f: Jabal-e-Rehmat is a hill on the plain of Arafat, about 20 km southeast of Makkah in Saudi Arabia. Pilgrims stand at Arafat on 9 Dhul Hijjah.

q: In which year was the Rowlatt Act passed?
f: The Rowlatt Act was passed by the Imperial Legislative Council in March 1919. It allowed arrest and detention without trial.

q: What was the Rowlatt Act?
o: A law allowing arrest and detention without trial
f: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 gave the British government power to imprison suspects without trial and to limit press freedom. Indians called it the Black Act.

q: Which prophet is known for suffering patiently from a long skin disease?
f: Hazrat Ayyub (AS) bore a long illness, said to be a skin disease, with great patience and is the model of sabr (patience).

q: In which year was the valley of Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh Dogra under the Treaty of Amritsar?
f: After the First Anglo-Sikh War the British signed the Treaty of Amritsar on 16 March 1846 and sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh.

q: How many sons did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) have?
f: He had three sons, Qasim, Abdullah (also called Tayyab and Tahir) and Ibrahim, and all of them died in infancy.

q: What is the capital of Turkey?
f: Ankara is the capital of Turkey, chosen by Ataturk in 1923 when the republic was founded.

q: In which province does the Upper Indus Plain mainly lie?
f: The Upper Indus Plain, north of Mithankot, covers most of Punjab, where the five rivers join the Indus.

q: What is the original meaning of the word Urdu?
f: Urdu comes from the Turkish word ordu, meaning camp or army, as the language grew in the military camps and bazaars.

q: What is 80% of 90?
What is 1/10th of 90?
f: One tenth of 90 is 90 divided by 10, which is 9.

q: What did the British call the War of 1857 that Muslims and Hindus of the subcontinent called the War of Independence?
f: The British described the uprising of 1857 as a mutiny of their Indian soldiers (sepoys), calling it the Sepoy Mutiny or Indian Mutiny.

q: Who abrogated the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan in October 1958?
f: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 Constitution on 7 October 1958, dissolved the assemblies and imposed martial law.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 20th be?
f: From the 2nd to the 20th is 18 days. 18 days is 2 full weeks plus 4 day(s), so the day is 4 day(s) after Monday, which is Friday.

q: Who is generally listed as the first Governor-General of India (of Bengal, 1774)?
f: Warren Hastings became Governor-General of Bengal in 1774 and is commonly called the first Governor-General of India in textbooks.

q: Which is counted as the third major Ghazwa of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), after Badr and Uhud?
f: The major battles in order are Badr, Uhud and Khandaq (Ahzab), fought in 5 AH. The Muslims dug a trench on the advice of Salman Farsi.

q: Who acts as the President of Pakistan in the absence of the President?
f: Under Article 49 of the constitution, the Chairman of the Senate acts as President when the office is vacant or the President is absent.

q: Which prophet (AS) was sent to Pharaoh (Firaun)?
f: Allah sent Hazrat Musa (AS), together with his brother Hazrat Harun (AS), to invite Pharaoh to the truth and to free Bani Israel.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of ADVERSITY?
f: Adversity means hardship or misfortune, so its opposite is prosperity, meaning good fortune and success.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to ADVERSITY?
f: Adversity means a state of serious difficulty or misfortune. Hardship is the nearest synonym.

q: Ahmed Ghulam Ali Chagla is famous for composing what?
o: The tune of the national anthem of Pakistan
The words of the national anthem of Pakistan
The design of the flag of Pakistan
f: Ahmed Ghulam Ali Chagla (1902-1953) was a Pakistani musician who composed the music of the national anthem of Pakistan.

q: Which is the national airline of Pakistan?
f: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) is the national flag carrier of Pakistan, established in 1955.

q: Syed-ul-Ansar was the title of which Sahabi?
f: Hazrat Saad bin Muadh (RA), chief of the Aws tribe of Madina, was given the title Syed-ul-Ansar.

q: In which year was the national anthem of Pakistan officially approved and adopted?
f: The national anthem was officially approved by the government of Pakistan in August 1954.

q: What is the walking seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwa during Hajj called?
f: Sa'i is the ritual walk between Safa and Marwa, commemorating Hazrat Hajra's search for water for Ismail (AS).

q: Which animal was with the Ashab-e-Kahf (Companions of the Cave)?
f: The Quran in Surah Al-Kahf mentions that their dog lay at the entrance of the cave with outstretched paws.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, what is the term of the National Assembly and the Provincial Assemblies?
f: Unless dissolved earlier, the National and Provincial Assemblies serve a term of five years from their first meeting.

q: Against whom did the Muslims fight the Battle of Badr?
f: The Battle of Badr in 2 AH was fought between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.

q: What is the antonym of the word biased?
f: Biased means unfairly favouring one side, so its opposite is impartial.

q: What is the border line between Pakistan and India (drawn in 1947) called?
f: The Radcliffe Line was drawn by the Boundary Commission headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe at the partition of India in 1947.

q: In a bus of 24 people, 2/3 are male. What percentage are female?
f: Males are 2/3 of 24 = 16, so females are 24 - 16 = 8. Percentage = 8/24 x 100 = 33.33 percent.

q: How many times did Jahangir Khan win the World Open squash championship?
f: Jahangir Khan won the World Open six times, the last in 1988.

q: Which prophet was blessed with a son in his old age?
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) was granted Hazrat Ismail (AS) and later Hazrat Ishaq (AS) in his old age.

q: The circumference of a circle of radius r is equal to
f: Circumference = 2 x pi x r, which is the same as pi x diameter.

q: What are two circles called that have three points in common?
f: Three non-collinear points determine exactly one circle. If two circles share three points, they must be the same circle, so they coincide.

q: What are sets that have no common element called?
f: Sets with no element in common have an empty intersection, and such sets are called disjoint sets.

q: Who composed the music of the national anthem of Pakistan?
f: The tune of the anthem was composed by Ahmed Ghulamali Chagla, while the words were written by Hafeez Jalandhari.

q: A. R. Cornelius, a Chief Justice of Pakistan, belonged to which religion?
f: Justice Alvin Robert Cornelius was a Christian and served as Chief Justice of Pakistan from 1960 to 1968.

q: Which crop is grown on the largest area in Pakistan?
f: Wheat is the staple food and covers the largest cropped area, about 9 million hectares.

q: Who is the current Prime Minister of India?
f: Narendra Modi has been Prime Minister since 2014 and began his third consecutive term in June 2024.

q: What is a decimal called in which the digits repeat again and again?
f: A decimal in which a digit or block of digits repeats endlessly, like 0.333..., is called a recurring (repeating) decimal.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam declare in Dhaka that Urdu would be the state language of Pakistan?
f: On 21 March 1948 at Dhaka, Quaid-e-Azam declared that Urdu alone would be the state language of Pakistan.

q: A square matrix whose determinant is zero is called what?
f: A square matrix with determinant equal to zero has no inverse and is called a singular matrix.

q: On whose advice does the President of Pakistan dissolve the National Assembly under the Constitution as it stands today?
f: Under Article 58 the President dissolves the National Assembly only on the advice of the Prime Minister.

q: A train's speed is double that of a car, and the car travels 30 km in 1 hour. How far will the train travel in 30 minutes?
f: Car speed is 30 km/h, so train speed is 2 x 30 = 60 km/h. In 30 minutes the train covers 60 x 0.5 = 30 km.

q: What is the term (duration) of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
f: The National Assembly has a term of five years from its first sitting unless dissolved earlier.

q: What is the main source of electricity generation in Pakistan today?
f: Recent data for 2025 show hydel power as the largest single source, around 39 percent in some months. RLNG and nuclear follow.

q: How many articles are there in the English language?
f: The English articles are a, an and the. A and an are indefinite and the is definite.

q: A train travels twice as fast as a car. If the car covers 30 km in 60 minutes, in what time will the train cover 30 km?
f: The car's speed is 30 km per hour, so the train's speed is 60 km per hour. The train covers 30 km in 30 / 60 hour = 30 minutes.

q: Which is the fastest land (terrestrial) animal?
f: The cheetah is the fastest land animal and can run at about 100 to 110 km per hour in short bursts.

q: How many agencies were there in the Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA)?
f: FATA had seven agencies: Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Orakzai, Kurram, North Waziristan and South Waziristan.

q: In which year was the Bogra Formula presented?
f: Prime Minister Muhammad Ali Bogra presented the formula in 1953 to solve the constitutional deadlock.

q: What was the Bogra Formula?
o: A constitutional proposal for a two-house legislature with parity between East and West Pakistan
A plan to make Urdu the only national language
f: It proposed a bicameral legislature, with equal representation of the provinces in the upper house and representation by population in the lower house.

q: In which galaxy does the Earth lie?
f: Our solar system and the Earth lie in the Milky Way galaxy, a barred spiral galaxy.

q: The ancient region of Gandhara lay mainly between which two modern cities?
f: Gandhara covered the Peshawar valley and the Potohar plateau around Taxila, roughly from Peshawar to Rawalpindi in north-west Pakistan.

q: In which country do the Golan Heights lie?
f: The Golan Heights is a rocky plateau in south-western Syria. Most of it has been occupied by Israel since 1967.

q: If Hamza is three times as old as Ali, what will be the age of Hamza when Ali is 7 years old?
f: Hamza's age is 3 times Ali's age, so 3 x 7 = 21 years.

q: For how many years did the Quraish of Makkah boycott Banu Hashim?
f: The Quraish imposed a social and economic boycott on Banu Hashim for about three years in the valley of Shib Abi Talib.

q: What is the new name of the Kashmir Highway in Islamabad?
f: In August 2020 Pakistan renamed Islamabad's Kashmir Highway as Srinagar Highway in solidarity with Kashmiris.

q: Where was the ICC Men's T20 World Cup of 2021 played?
f: The 2021 T20 World Cup, officially hosted by the BCCI of India, was moved because of COVID-19 and played in the UAE and Oman in October and November 2021.

q: Which prophet was tested by Allah with a long and severe illness and was known for his patience?
f: Hazrat Ayub (AS) was tested with loss of wealth, family and a long illness and kept patience, so his name is a proverb for sabr.

q: What does the adjective intimate mean?
f: Intimate describes a very close, familiar relationship or a detailed, deep knowledge of something.

q: How many gates does Jannah (Paradise) have?
f: According to authentic hadith, Jannah has eight gates, one of which is Ar-Rayyan for those who fast.

q: Which fighter jet has Pakistan produced jointly with China?
f: The JF-17 Thunder is a light multirole fighter built by Pakistan Aeronautical Complex, Kamra, with China's Chengdu Aircraft Corporation.

q: Who wrote the famous biography 'Jinnah of Pakistan'?
f: Stanley Wolpert, an American historian, wrote 'Jinnah of Pakistan' in 1984.

q: Which one is different from the others: Karachi, Lahore, Balochistan, Rawalpindi?
f: Karachi, Lahore and Rawalpindi are cities, while Balochistan is a province.

q: What kind of number is 5/7?
f: A number that can be written as a ratio of two integers with a non-zero denominator is rational. 5/7 is such a ratio.

q: What is the capital of North Korea?
f: Pyongyang is the capital and largest city of North Korea.

q: Which language is the lingua franca (common link language) of Pakistan?
f: Urdu is understood across all provinces and links people of different mother tongues. It is also the national language.

q: Which letter comes after G in the English alphabet?
f: The order is F, G, H, I, so H follows G.

q: Which letter comes after the letter that is followed by M?
f: The letter followed by M is L, and the letter after L is M.

q: Who is Mark Zuckerberg?
f: Mark Zuckerberg co-founded Facebook in 2004 and is the CEO of its parent company Meta.

q: On which date did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) arrive in Madina after the Hijrat?
f: After staying at Quba, the Prophet (PBUH) entered Madina on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal, 1 AH (September 622 AD). He had left Makkah a few days earlier.

q: What is the median of the data 2, 2, 3, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 8?
f: The data is already in order and has 9 values, so the median is the 5th value. The 5th value is 5.

q: What is the midpoint of the points (3, 1) and (-3, 1)?
If a helicopter needs 50 gallons of fuel to move 320 km, how many gallons are needed to cover 400 km?
f: Fuel per km is 50 divided by 320. For 400 km, 400 x 50 / 320 = 62.5 gallons.

q: In which night was Namaz (the five daily prayers) made obligatory?
o: Shab-e-Mi'raj (the night of Isra and Mi'raj)
f: The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the night of Isra and Mi'raj (placed by tradition around the 10th-12th year of Prophethood).

q: In which Nabawi year did the Holy Prophet (SAW) migrate from Makkah to Madina?
f: The Hijrat took place in 622 CE, which was the 13th year of prophethood.

q: In which city is the head office (secretariat) of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) located?
f: The ECO secretariat is located in Tehran, Iran.

q: What does OGRA stand for?
f: OGRA stands for the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority, which regulates the midstream and downstream oil and gas sector of Pakistan.

q: In which year did Pakistan purchase Gwadar from Oman?
f: Pakistan bought the Gwadar enclave from the Sultan of Oman in 1958, and it was formally handed over on 8 December 1958.

q: Who originally built the Kaaba?
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), with the help of his son Hazrat Ismail (AS), raised the walls of the Kaaba by Allah's command. This is the answer given in most Pakistani textbooks.

q: Geographically, into how many main regions is Pakistan divided according to most textbooks?
f: Pakistan is usually divided into six regions: Northern Highlands, Western Highlands, Balochistan Plateau, Potohar Plateau and Salt Range, Indus Plain, and Deserts.

q: Where was the Battle of Plassey fought?
f: The battle was fought on 23 June 1757 at Plassey in Bengal, on the bank of the Bhagirathi river.

q: According to Pakistani textbooks, how many prophets were sent by Allah in total?
f: A well-known hadith, as taught in Pakistani textbooks, gives the number of prophets as 124,000.

q: Under which treaty did Gulab Singh purchase Kashmir from the British?
f: By the Treaty of Amritsar (March 1846) the British sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh of Jammu for 7.5 million rupees.

q: What is the meaning of the word refute?
f: To refute a claim is to prove it wrong. Synonyms include disprove, rebut and counter.

q: Which country does not have a regular army?
f: Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948 after a civil war. It relies on police forces for security.

q: What does SUPARCO stand for and what is it related to?
o: Pakistan's space and upper atmosphere research agency
f: SUPARCO is the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, Pakistan's national space agency. It was founded in 1961.

q: Is the square root of 7 a rational or an irrational number?
f: 7 is not a perfect square, so its square root is a non-terminating, non-repeating decimal and cannot be written as a fraction of integers. Hence it is irrational.

q: On what date was the Rowlatt Act passed in 1919?
f: The Imperial Legislative Council passed the Rowlatt Act on 18 March 1919.

q: In which part of Punjab is the Salt Range located?
f: The Salt Range lies in northern Punjab, between the Jhelum River and the Indus River south of Potohar Plateau. Khewra salt mine is in the range.

q: In which year was the Scientific Society founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan at Ghazipur?
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan established the Scientific Society in 1864 at Ghazipur to translate Western scientific works into Urdu.

q: In which year was Sir Syed Ahmad Khan born?
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was born in Delhi on 17 October 1817.

q: What is the value of tan 90 degrees?
f: tan 90 = sin 90 / cos 90 = 1 / 0, and division by zero is undefined.

q: At what age of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was the last revelation (wahi) revealed?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) received his first revelation at 40 and the last verses shortly before his death at the age of 63.

q: Ali is 4 years old and he is 4 years younger than his sister. When Ali is 8 years old, how old will his sister be?
f: Sister is 4 + 4 = 8 years old now, so she is 4 years older than Ali. When Ali is 8, she will be 8 + 4 = 12.

q: What is the value of any non-zero number raised to the power zero?
f: By the law of exponents a^0 = a^n / a^n = 1 for any non-zero number a.

q: If the 15th day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 1st of that month?
f: From the 1st to the 15th is 14 days, exactly two weeks, so both fall on the same weekday, Monday.

q: What is the value of sin 180 degrees?
f: On the unit circle, 180 degrees is the point (-1, 0), and sine is the y-coordinate, which is 0.

q: What is the value of cos 180 degrees?
f: On the unit circle, 180 degrees is the point (-1, 0), and cosine is the x-coordinate, which is -1.

q: What was the official name of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution?
f: Article 1 of the 1973 Constitution names the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

q: How many seats are reserved for non-Muslim minorities in the National Assembly of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution?
f: Article 51 of the Constitution reserves ten seats in the National Assembly for non-Muslims.

q: Which country hosted the 2022 Winter Olympics?
f: The 2022 Winter Olympics were held in Beijing, China, in February 2022. There was no Summer Olympics in 2022.

q: In a class of 500 students, 340 are male. What percentage of the students is male?
f: 340 divided by 500 times 100 gives 68 percent.

q: Who was the third Governor-General of Pakistan?
f: The Governors-General were Quaid-e-Azam, Khawaja Nazimuddin, Ghulam Muhammad (1951-55) and then Iskander Mirza.

q: If a helicopter covers 320 miles using 80 gallons of fuel, how many gallons are needed for 700 miles?
f: Fuel per mile = 80 / 320 = 0.25 gallons. For 700 miles: 700 x 0.25 = 175 gallons.

q: For which field is Abdur Rehman Chughtai famous?
f: Abdur Rehman Chughtai (1894-1975) was a famous Pakistani painter and artist known for his Mughal-influenced style.

q: What is the meaning of abhor?
f: Abhor means to regard with disgust and hatred.

q: What is a synonym of acute?
f: Acute can mean sharp or intense, as in acute pain, and severe is the closest synonym.

q: In which year did Allama Iqbal deliver his famous Presidential Address at the Allahabad session of the Muslim League?
f: Allama Iqbal gave his Allahabad Address in 1930, in which he proposed a separate Muslim state in north-west India.

q: What is the meaning of the word ADHERE?
f: To adhere means to stick or hold fast to something, such as a surface, a rule or a belief. Its synonyms include stick, cling and follow.

q: What does the Arabic word Alfeel mean?
f: Alfeel means elephant. Surah Al-Fil of the Quran tells of Abraha's army with elephants that tried to destroy the Kaaba in the Year of the Elephant.

q: When was the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) founded?
f: The Non-Aligned Movement was formally founded at the Belgrade Summit in September 1961 by leaders such as Tito, Nehru, Nasser, Nkrumah and Sukarno.

q: Which act of worship is mentioned in the Quran together with Zakat in many verses?
f: The Quran repeatedly commands to establish Salat and pay Zakat together, for example in Surah Al-Baqarah.

q: Amjad and Ahmad together kept 24 balls. Amjad kept three times as many as Ahmad. How many balls did Ahmad keep?
f: Let Ahmad keep x balls, so Amjad keeps 3x. Then x + 3x = 24, so 4x = 24 and x = 6.

q: What is the antonym of defile?
f: To defile means to make dirty or impure, so its opposite is to purify.

q: What is the antonym of dilate?
f: To dilate is to become wider or larger, so its opposite is to constrict or contract.

q: Saudi riyal is the currency of which country?
f: The riyal is the official currency of Saudi Arabia, issued by the Saudi Central Bank.

q: What is the circling (going around) of the Kaaba during Hajj and Umrah called?
f: Tawaf is the act of walking seven times around the Kaaba in an anticlockwise direction.

q: How many articles did the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan have?
f: The 1962 Constitution given by Ayub Khan had 250 articles.

q: Baltistan is also known as which of the following?
f: Baltistan, in Gilgit-Baltistan, is called Little Tibet (Tibet-e-Khurd) because of its culture and mountain landscape similar to Tibet.

q: Where did the Quraish tribe belong?
f: The Quraish were the leading tribe of Makkah and custodians of the Kaaba.

q: Which prophet (AS) was given the ability to understand the language of birds and animals?
f: The Quran says that Allah taught Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) the speech of birds, and he talked with the hoopoe and the ant.

q: On which date of the Islamic month was the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) born, according to the view most followed in Pakistan?
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born on Monday, 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal in the Year of the Elephant, which is about 570 AD in Makkah.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of the word brilliant?
f: Brilliant means very bright or very intelligent, and its opposite is dull.

q: On which river did India build the Baglihar dam?
f: The Baglihar hydroelectric dam is built by India on the Chenab river in Jammu and Kashmir. The Chenab flows on into Pakistan.

q: What was the Cabinet Mission of 1946?
o: A British mission sent to India to discuss the transfer of power
A Muslim League mission sent to London
A Congress mission sent to the Viceroy
A United Nations mission to Kashmir
f: The Cabinet Mission was a delegation of three British cabinet ministers sent to India in 1946. It proposed a plan for the transfer of power and a united India with a weak centre.

q: Who was the third caliph of Islam?
f: The order of the Rightly Guided Caliphs is Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali. So the third was Hazrat Uthman (RA).

q: If set A has 3 elements and set B has 4 elements, how many elements are in the Cartesian product A x B?
f: The number of elements in A x B is the product of the sizes: 3 x 4 = 12.

q: How many players play in a game of chess?
f: Chess is played between two players, one with white pieces and one with black.

q: Which is the coldest inhabited place of Pakistan?
f: Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan records the lowest winter temperatures among Pakistan's inhabited places; it recorded about minus 21 degrees Celsius in December 2019.

q: What is the real part of the complex number 6 + 7i?
f: In a + bi the real part is a, so for 6 + 7i the real part is 6 and the imaginary part is 7.

q: In which year AD was Makkah conquered by the Muslims?
f: Makkah was conquered in Ramadan 8 AH, which corresponds to January 630 AD.

q: How many copies of the Quran were prepared by Hazrat Usman (RA) and sent to different regions?
f: Hazrat Usman (RA) had standard copies prepared from the Abu Bakr copy and sent them to major centres; most Pakistani textbooks say five copies.

q: What is the meaning of the word crude?
f: Crude means in a natural or raw state, not yet processed, or rough and lacking refinement.

q: Against whom did Nawab Siraj ud Daula fight the Battle of Plassey in 1757?
f: The British East India Company forces under Robert Clive defeated the Nawab of Bengal at Plassey, helped by the betrayal of Mir Jafar.

q: Pakistan's friendship with which neighbouring country is described as higher than the mountains and deeper than the oceans?
f: Pakistani leaders describe the Pakistan-China friendship as higher than the Himalayas and deeper than the oceans.

q: Roughly what fraction of the Earth's land surface is covered by deserts (arid regions)?
f: Deserts and arid lands cover roughly one third of the Earth's land surface.

q: What is the antonym of the word 'ecstasy'?
f: Ecstasy means overwhelming joy, so its opposite is deep unhappiness, which is misery. Rapture, elation and delight are its synonyms.

q: Who elects the President of Pakistan?
o: An electoral college of the Senate, National Assembly and provincial assemblies
f: The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college made up of members of the Senate, the National Assembly and the four provincial assemblies.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word excuse (as a verb)?
f: To excuse someone means to forgive or pardon a fault. Blame, punish and accuse have the opposite sense.

q: According to Islam, fasting (Roza) protects a person from what?
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that fasting is a shield. It teaches self-control and keeps a person away from sins and evil deeds.

q: What happened on 27 February 2019 when the Pakistan Air Force responded to an Indian incursion?
o: Pakistan shot down two Indian aircraft and captured a pilot
f: On 27 February 2019 the PAF shot down Indian aircraft inside Pakistani airspace and the Indian pilot Wing Commander Abhinandan was captured.

q: What was the name of the foster mother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Halima Sadia of the Banu Saad tribe nursed and raised the infant Prophet (PBUH) in the desert.

q: Which is the fourth source of Islamic law (Shariah) in the usual order?
f: The four sources in order are the Holy Quran, the Sunnah (Hadith), Ijma (consensus of scholars) and Qiyas (analogy).

q: What is the capital of France?
f: Paris, on the River Seine, is the capital and largest city of France.

q: The Friendship Gate (Bab-e-Dosti) at Chaman is a border crossing between which two countries?
f: The Friendship Gate stands at Chaman in Balochistan on the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.

q: In which year of prophethood (Nabwi) was the Year of Grief (Aam-ul-Huzn)?
f: The Year of Grief was the 10th year of prophethood, when the Prophet (PBUH) lost his wife Hazrat Khadija (RA) and his uncle Abu Talib within a short time.

q: What is Hajr-e-Aswad?
o: The Black Stone fixed in the Kaaba
A gate of the Prophet's Mosque
f: Hajr-e-Aswad is the Black Stone set in the eastern corner of the Kaaba.

q: What is the HCF of 6 and 12?
f: 6 divides 12 exactly, so the largest number dividing both is 6.

q: At what age is Hazrat Isa (AS) commonly said to have been raised to the heavens?
f: The commonly stated age at which Hazrat Isa (AS) was raised to the heavens is 33 years.

q: Which is the highest mountain in the world?
f: Mount Everest, in the Himalayas on the Nepal-China border, is the highest mountain above sea level.

q: Which is an important river of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK)?
f: The Kabul River flows from Afghanistan through Peshawar and joins the Indus near Attock. Swat river is also a major river of the province.

q: What is the most important event of 10 Hijri?
o: The Farewell Hajj and Last Sermon of the Prophet (PBUH)
f: In 10 AH the Prophet (PBUH) performed his only Hajj, the Hajjatul Wida, and delivered the Last Sermon at Arafat.

q: Which Chinese fighter jets did Pakistan Air Force formally induct in March 2022?
f: The PAF commissioned its first six J-10C multirole fighters from China in March 2022.

q: What is the integral of ln x with respect to x?
f: Integrating by parts with u = ln x and dv = dx gives x ln x - integral of (x times 1/x) dx = x ln x - x + C.

q: What is the meaning of the word interim?
f: Interim describes something provided or done for the time between two events, that is, temporary.

q: Inzamam-ul-Haq, one of Pakistan's best batsmen, played which sport for the Pakistan national team?
f: Inzamam-ul-Haq played Test and One Day cricket for Pakistan from 1991 to 2007 and captained the team.

q: Who is regarded as the first martyr of Islam?
f: Hazrat Sumayyah (RA), mother of Hazrat Ammar (RA), was killed by Abu Jahl for her faith and is the first martyr of Islam.

q: How many Jewish tribes lived in Madina when the Holy Prophet (SAW) migrated there?
f: The three main Jewish tribes of Madina were Banu Qaynuqa, Banu Nadir and Banu Quraizah.

q: Which was the first princely state to accede to Pakistan?
f: Bahawalpur was the first princely state to accede to Pakistan, in October 1947.

q: Arfa Karim, the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional, belonged to which country?
f: Arfa Abdul Karim Randhawa was a Pakistani girl from Faisalabad who became a Microsoft Certified Professional at age 9.

q: Kathmandu is the capital of which country?
f: Kathmandu is the capital and largest city of Nepal.

q: On which river is the Khanpur Dam built?
f: Khanpur Dam is built on the Haro River in the Haripur district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: What is the LCM of 4 and 6?
f: Multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12 and multiples of 6 are 6, 12. The first common multiple is 12.

q: What is the process by which a liquid changes into vapour (gas) called?
f: When a liquid gains heat and its molecules escape into the air as vapour, the change is called evaporation or vaporization.

q: What is the value of log 1 (to any valid base)?
f: Any base b raised to the power 0 equals 1, so the logarithm of 1 is 0.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of the word 'loved'?
f: Loved means felt strong affection for, and its opposite is hated.

q: What was the approximate strength of the Muslim army sent against Musailma Kazzab in the Battle of Yamama?
f: Hazrat Khalid bin Walid (RA) led about 13,000 Muslims against the army of Musailma Kazzab at Yamama in 633 CE (11 AH).

q: In which city is Masjid-e-Nabawi located?
f: Masjid-e-Nabawi was built by the Holy Prophet (SAW) in Madina after the Hijrat.

q: Who was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Navy?
o: Vice Admiral H. M. S. Choudri
f: Vice Admiral James Wilfred Jefford of the Royal Navy became the first head of the Royal Pakistan Navy in 1947.

q: A person walks 7 miles towards the north, then turns left, then turns left again. In which direction is he going now?
f: Facing north, a left turn makes him face west. Turning left again from west makes him face south.

q: What is a matrix with only one row called?
f: A matrix having only one row is called a row matrix; its order is 1 x n.

q: If 5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes, how many pages will one man write in 5 minutes?
f: 5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes, so each man writes 1 page in 5 minutes.

q: Complete the sentence: The prices of clothes are too ___.
f: Prices are described as high or low, so high is the correct word.

q: What is the antonym of provoke?
f: Provoke means to make someone angry or stir them up; the opposite is to pacify or calm them.

q: What is a quarter of 12?
f: A quarter means one fourth. 12 divided by 4 equals 3.

q: Which political party launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942?
f: The Indian National Congress passed the Quit India resolution in Bombay in August 1942 under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi. The Muslim League opposed the movement.

q: Why do people read newspapers?
o: To get information and knowledge about current events
f: Newspapers report news and information about local and world events. People read them mainly to gain knowledge and stay informed.

q: What is the real part of the complex number -i(4i + 6)?
