f: -i(4i + 6) = -4i squared - 6i = 4 - 6i since i squared = -1. The real part is 4.

q: Who wrote the book Dead Reckoning: Memories of the 1971 Bangladesh War?
f: Dead Reckoning (2011) was written by Sarmila Bose and discusses the 1971 war and its casualty figures. It is often confused with works by authors with similar names.

q: What does the word refund mean?
f: Refund means to give back money that was paid, for example for a returned item. Its synonym is reimburse.

q: What is the meaning of the word reluctant?
f: Reluctant means unwilling or hesitant to do something. A reluctant person does not want to act.

q: Which two hadith books are called the Sahihain?
f: Sahihain means the two Sahih books: Sahih al-Bukhari by Imam Bukhari and Sahih Muslim by Imam Muslim.

q: My brother's son's sister is my what?
f: My brother's son is my nephew, and his sister is my brother's daughter, who is my niece.

q: The Sun is currently in which stage of a star's life?
f: The Sun fuses hydrogen into helium in its core, which is the main sequence stage. It has been in this stage for about 4.6 billion years.

q: Which is the largest railway station of Pakistan, according to most sources?
f: Lahore Junction is most commonly named as the largest railway station of Pakistan by area.

q: What is the closest meaning of 'strenuous'?
f: Strenuous means needing great effort or energy. Arduous has the same meaning.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "normally"?
f: Normally means in the usual way, which is usually.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "retrieve"?
f: To retrieve is to get something back, which is to recover.

q: With what is Tayammum performed?
f: Tayammum is done by striking the hands on clean earth or dust and wiping the face and arms.

q: What is the antonym of the word timid?
f: Timid means lacking courage, so its opposite is bold.

q: Jami at-Tirmidhi (Tirmizi Sharif) is a book of what?
f: Jami at-Tirmidhi is a collection of the sayings and actions (ahadith) of the Prophet (PBUH) compiled by Imam Tirmidhi.

q: In which language was the Holy Quran first translated in the subcontinent (India)?
f: Shah Waliullah made the well-known first full translation into Persian in 1738, which is the usual textbook answer.

q: Change into passive voice: Soldiers are digging trenches.
o: Trenches are being dug by soldiers.
Trenches have been dug by soldiers.
f: The present continuous active becomes am/is/are being plus the past participle in the passive.

q: In which year was Urdu declared the national language of Pakistan, as commonly taught?
f: Quaid-e-Azam declared Urdu the state language at Dhaka in March 1948, and this is the usual textbook answer.

q: Who was the first Viceroy of India?
f: Lord Canning became the first Viceroy in 1858 after the Government of India Act transferred power from the East India Company to the Crown.

q: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
f: Influenza is caused by influenza viruses. Tuberculosis and cholera are caused by bacteria and malaria by a protozoan parasite.

q: Which is the highest waterfall in the world?
f: Angel Falls in Venezuela has a total height of about 979 metres, with an uninterrupted drop of about 807 metres, making it the highest waterfall in the world.

q: What does WWW stand for in internet addresses?
f: WWW stands for World Wide Web, the system of linked pages accessed over the internet.

q: In which direction of Pakistan does the Chinese region of Xinjiang lie?
f: Xinjiang lies to the north (north-east) of Pakistan and meets Gilgit-Baltistan at the Khunjerab Pass.

q: What is 90 divided by 90 (90/90)?
f: Any non-zero number divided by itself equals 1, so 90/90 = 1.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will be the 13th of that month?
f: The 13th is 9 days after the 4th, and 9 = 7 + 2. Sunday + 2 days = Tuesday.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 14th of that month?
f: The 14th is 13 days after the 1st, and 13 = 7 + 6. Monday + 6 days = Sunday.

q: Which term comes next in the series: 3z, 6y, 9x, 15w, ?
f: The numbers 3, 6, 9, 15 follow the rule that each is the sum of the two before it (3+6=9, 6+9=15), so the next is 9+15=24. The letters go backwards from z, y, x, w to v.

q: What is the square root of 1600?
f: 40 x 40 = 1600, so the square root of 1600 is 40.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah receive the title of Quaid-e-Azam (Great Leader), as most Pakistani textbooks state?
f: Most Pakistani textbooks say that Maulana Mazharuddin Shaheed gave the title Quaid-e-Azam to Jinnah in 1938.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 19th be?
f: From the 2nd to the 19th is 17 days. 17 days is 2 full weeks plus 3 day(s), so the day is 3 day(s) after Friday, which is Monday.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 19th be?
f: From the 3rd to the 19th is 16 days. 16 days is 2 full weeks plus 2 day(s), so the day is 2 day(s) after Sunday, which is Tuesday.

q: If the 24th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 3rd be?
f: From the 3rd back to the 24th is 21 days. 21 days is 3 full weeks plus 0 day(s), so the day is 0 day(s) before Tuesday, which is Tuesday.

q: Which constitution was enforced in Pakistan in April 1972 after the separation of East Pakistan?
f: After 1971 a temporary Interim Constitution was adopted in April 1972, which ended martial law and ran until the permanent constitution of 1973.

q: Under whose government was the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan framed and passed?
f: The 1973 Constitution was drafted by a parliamentary committee and passed by the National Assembly during the premiership of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto. It was adopted in April 1973.

q: What is 2 x 2 divided by 2?
f: Work left to right: 2 x 2 is 4, and 4 divided by 2 is 2.

q: In a school of 500 students, 340 are male. What percentage of the students is female?
f: Females are 500 minus 340, which is 160. Then 160 divided by 500 times 100 gives 32 percent.

q: Out of 500 students, 360 are present. What percentage of students is absent?
f: Absent students are 500 minus 360, which is 140. Then 140 divided by 500 times 100 gives 28 percent.

q: What is 3x4 + 2x4 (also written 3x4 + 4x2)?
f: Multiply first: 3x4 = 12 and 2x4 = 8 (4x2 is also 8). Then add: 12 + 8 = 20.

q: How many columns does a matrix of order 5x4 have?
f: A matrix of order m x n has m rows and n columns. For 5x4 there are 5 rows and 4 columns.

q: If the 28th day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 8th day of that month?
f: From the 8th to the 28th is 20 days, and 20 = 2 weeks + 6 days. Going back 6 days from Monday gives Tuesday.

q: In which Hijri year was Aam-ul-Wafood (Year of Delegations)?
f: Delegations from many Arab tribes came to Madina to accept Islam in 9 AH, after the conquest of Makkah. This year is called Aam-ul-Wafood.

q: What is the meaning (synonym) of abolish?
f: To abolish a law or system means to formally put an end to it, which is to do away with it.

q: Who was the first among slaves to accept Islam, according to most Pakistani textbooks?
f: Textbooks list Abu Bakr among men, Khadija among women, Ali among children and Zaid bin Haritha among freed slaves as the first to accept Islam.

q: How many acute angles are there in an acute triangle?
f: In an acute triangle all three angles are less than 90 degrees, so all three are acute.

q: When was the Indian Independence Act passed?
f: The Indian Independence Act was passed by the British Parliament in July 1947 and created the two dominions of India and Pakistan from 15 August 1947.

q: Which word is the antonym (opposite) of ADHERE?
f: Adhere means to stick to something, so its opposite is detach, meaning to separate or loosen.

q: What does an adjective describe or explain?
f: An adjective modifies a noun or pronoun by telling its quality, quantity or kind, as in a tall boy.

q: What is the name of the border line between Pakistan and Afghanistan?
f: The Durand Line was fixed in 1893 by Sir Mortimer Durand and the Afghan ruler Amir Abdur Rahman Khan, and it forms the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

q: Point out the odd one out: America, Africa, Asia, Euro.
f: America, Africa and Asia are continents, while Euro is the currency of many European countries.

q: What is the (executive) capital of South Africa?
f: Pretoria is the administrative (executive) capital of South Africa. The country has three capitals: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.

q: Ahmed is 3 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. How old will his sister be when Ahmed is 9?
f: The sister is 3 x 3 = 9 years old now. Ahmed becomes 9 after 6 years, so she will be 9 + 6 = 15 years.

q: Who is the current President of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) as of October 2026?
f: PML-N's Dr Najeeb Naqi was elected and sworn in as the 25th President of AJK on 24 September 2026 for a five-year term.

q: Which letter comes next after O in the English alphabet?
f: The alphabet runs ... M, N, O, P, Q, so P comes right after O.

q: Which letter comes first in alphabetical order in the word MANAGEMENT?
f: The letters of MANAGEMENT are M, A, N, A, G, E, M, E, N, T. Arranged alphabetically they begin with A, so A comes first.

q: After arranging the letters of the word MANAGEMENT in alphabetical order, which letter is the third from the last?
f: MANAGEMENT has the letters M, A, N, A, G, E, M, E, N, T. In alphabetical order: A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T. Counting from the end: T (1st), N (2nd), N (3rd), so the third letter from the last is N.

q: What is the national mammal of the United States of America?
f: The American bison was declared the national mammal of the USA in 2016.

q: Amjad and Ahmad together kept 20 balloons. Amjad kept three times as many as Ahmad. How many balloons did Ahmad keep?
f: Let Ahmad keep x balloons, so Amjad keeps 3x. Then x + 3x = 20, so 4x = 20 and x = 5.

q: Which word is a synonym of anarchy?
f: Anarchy means a state of disorder due to the absence of authority, which is the same as lawlessness.

q: Which Sahabi was appointed by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) as governor of Yemen?
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Muadh bin Jabal (RA) to Yemen as governor, judge and teacher of the people.

q: Which of the following is another name of the Holy Quran?
f: Furqan, meaning the criterion that separates right from wrong, is one of the names of the Holy Quran.

q: What is the antonym of excrete?
f: To excrete is to get rid of waste matter from the body, so the opposite is to absorb or retain.

q: What is the antonym of prohibited?
f: Prohibited means not permitted, so its opposite is allowed.

q: Which word is a synonym of applaud?
f: To applaud is to show approval, which means the same as to praise.

q: What is the approximate total area of Pakistan?
f: Pakistan covers about 796,095 square kilometres, the 33rd largest country by area.

q: Around which body does the Earth revolve?
f: The Earth orbits the Sun, completing one revolution in about 365.25 days.

q: Which Article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan declares Islam as the State religion?
f: Article 2 states that Islam shall be the State religion of Pakistan.

q: In which part of Asia is India located?
f: India lies in South Asia, forming most of the Indian subcontinent.

q: Aslam was 28 years old in 1945. How old will he be in 1965?
f: From 1945 to 1965 is 20 years, so his age is 28 + 20 = 48.

q: What will be the third letter when the word AUGMENTED is arranged alphabetically?
f: Alphabetical order is A D E E G M N T U, so the third letter is E.

q: Sahih Bukhari is regarded as the most authentic book of hadith after which book?
f: Muslims regard the Holy Quran as the most authentic book, followed in authenticity by Sahih Bukhari among the hadith books.

q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) pass away?
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) passed away in 11 AH (632 AD) at the age of 63 years.

q: In the coordinate plane, the y-axis is the
f: The y-axis is the vertical number line of the plane, and the y-coordinate is called the ordinate.

q: In the coordinate plane, the x-axis is the
f: The x-axis is the horizontal number line of the plane, and the x-coordinate is called the abscissa.

q: Against whom was the War of Independence of 1857 (Jang-e-Azadi) fought by the people of the subcontinent?
f: The 1857 revolt was an uprising of Indian soldiers and people against British East India Company rule.

q: Who is the author of the famous book Hujjatullah-il-Baligha?
f: Hujjatullah-il-Baligha is a famous work on Islamic wisdom by Shah Waliullah Muhaddith Dehlvi.

q: Ali and Ahmed have 25 balls in all. If Ali has 4 times as many as Ahmed, how many balls does Ahmed have?
f: Let Ahmed have x. Then x + 4x = 25, so 5x = 25 and x = 5.

q: Who is the Governor of Balochistan (as of 2026)?
f: Jaffar Khan Mandokhail is serving as Governor of Balochistan in 2026.

q: Which barrage is commonly described as the biggest and the first barrage of Pakistan on the Indus?
f: Sukkur Barrage, opened in 1932, is the one Pakistani textbooks name as the first and biggest barrage on the Indus.

q: What is the area of a triangle with base 3 cm and height 6 cm?
f: Area = half x base x height = 0.5 x 3 x 6 = 9 square cm.

q: On which document is the Constitution of Pakistan based?
f: The Objectives Resolution of 1949 laid down the guiding principles and was made a preamble and later a substantive part (Article 2A) of the Constitution.

q: Pakistan's economy is predominantly based on which sector?
f: Agriculture is the backbone of Pakistan's economy, supporting a large share of employment and exports like textiles from cotton.

q: In which year was the First Battle of Panipat fought?
f: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodhi at Panipat in 1526, which started the Mughal Empire in India.

q: Where is the Bay of Riga located?
f: The Gulf (Bay) of Riga is an inlet of the Baltic Sea lying between Latvia and Estonia.

q: Where is the Bay of Siam located?
f: The Bay of Siam is an old name for the Gulf of Thailand, an arm of the South China Sea.

q: Choose the correct statement about air at higher altitude.
o: Air becomes lighter (thinner) as we go upward
Air becomes heavier as we go upward
Air density does not change with height
f: Atmospheric pressure and density decrease with height, so air becomes thinner and lighter as we go up.

q: To which religion did Rana Bhagwan Das belong?
f: Rana Bhagwandas was a Hindu who served as a judge of the Supreme Court and as acting Chief Justice of Pakistan.

q: Which type of brick was used in the buildings of the Indus Valley Civilization?
f: Cities like Mohenjo-daro and Harappa were built with uniform baked clay bricks, usually in a ratio of about 1:2:4.

q: What name did the British give to the War of Independence of 1857?
f: The British called the events of 1857 the Sepoy Mutiny (or Indian Mutiny) because it began with Indian soldiers in the Company army.

q: Change the first word into a pronoun: Sana broke her pen.
f: Sana is a female name, so the pronoun that replaces it is She.

q: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh during the rule of which dynasty?
f: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 711-712 AD during the reign of the Umayyad caliph Walid bin Abdul Malik. The Mughals came centuries later.

q: The Panama Canal separates which two continents?
f: The Panama Canal cuts through the Isthmus of Panama, dividing North America from South America. It connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.

q: What is the capital of the country Georgia?
f: Tbilisi is the capital of Georgia, a country in the Caucasus. Atlanta is the capital of the US state of Georgia.

q: What is the capital of Venezuela?
f: Caracas is the capital and largest city of Venezuela.

q: On which date was the Indian pilot Abhinandan Varthaman captured in Pakistan?
f: Wing Commander Abhinandan's aircraft was shot down on 27 February 2019, a day after the Balakot air strike. He was returned to India on 1 March 2019.

q: In which year was the Baghdad Pact (later renamed CENTO) signed?
f: The Baghdad Pact was signed in 1955 and was renamed CENTO in 1959 after Iraq withdrew.

q: Through which point does the line x = 6y pass?
f: Putting x = 0 and y = 0 gives 0 = 0, so the line satisfies the equation at the origin. The same is true for y = 5x.

q: Which device converts stored chemical energy into electrical energy?
f: A battery or electric cell uses chemical reactions to produce an electric current.

q: Who was the first Indian Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army (1949)?
f: General Kodandera Madappa Cariappa took over as Commander-in-Chief from the British officer Sir Francis Butcher on 15 January 1949.

q: The Chauri Chaura incident of 1922 took place during which movement?
f: On 4 February 1922 a mob burned a police station at Chauri Chaura and killed policemen, so Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement.

q: What is 5 o'clock in the afternoon in 24-hour time?
f: For afternoon hours add 12: 5 + 12 = 17, so 5 PM is 1700 hours.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'immense'?
f: Immense means extremely large or great.

q: What does the word 'cohesion' mean?
o: Act of sticking together as a united whole
f: Cohesion is the state of sticking together or forming a united whole, as in a cohesive group.

q: What is the transpose of a column matrix?
f: Transposing a matrix swaps its rows and columns. A column matrix of order n x 1 becomes a matrix of order 1 x n, which is a row matrix.

q: What was the Simon Commission?
o: A British commission sent to India in 1927 to review the Government of India Act 1919, with no Indian member
A commission for partition of Bengal
A Muslim League committee for Pakistan
A commission for dividing Punjab in 1947
f: The Simon Commission, led by Sir John Simon, arrived in India in 1928 to study constitutional reform. It had only British members, so Indian parties boycotted it.

q: In which city was the East India Company established?
f: The East India Company was formed in London and received its royal charter from Queen Elizabeth I.

q: In which year was the East India Company first established?
f: The English East India Company received its royal charter from Queen Elizabeth I on 31 December 1600.

q: Complete the sentence: If he had called me, I ___ come.
f: This is the third conditional (if + past perfect), which needs would have + past participle in the main clause.

q: What kind of number is a - ib (where a and b are real and b is not zero)?
f: A number written in the form a + ib with real a and b is a complex number; a - ib is its conjugate, which is also complex.

q: What is the antonym of 'composite'?
f: Composite means made up of several parts, and its opposite is simple, made of a single part.

q: Which are the two largest continents of the world by area?
f: Asia is the largest continent and Africa is the second largest by area.

q: Which organization controls and develops Pakistan's water and electric power system?
f: WAPDA (Water and Power Development Authority) develops the country's water and hydropower resources.

q: What is cos(-x) equal to?
f: Cosine is an even function, so cos(-x) = cos x.

q: What is sec x multiplied by cos x equal to?
f: Sec x = 1/cos x, so sec x . cos x = 1.

q: What is cosec x multiplied by tan x equal to?
f: Cosec x . tan x = (1/sin x)(sin x/cos x) = 1/cos x = sec x.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Court of Justice located?
f: The ICJ sits in the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands.

q: What is the opposite of the word crude?
f: Crude means raw or unrefined, so its opposite is refined, meaning processed or polished.

q: On which date is Pakistan Day celebrated?
f: Pakistan Day is celebrated on 23 March to mark the Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution of 1940.

q: Where is the deepest hole (borehole) drilled by humans in the world?
f: The Kola Superdeep Borehole in Russia reached about 12,262 metres in 1989.

q: Which is the deepest known point of the Earth's surface?
f: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench of the western Pacific is the deepest known point, at about 10,900 to 11,000 metres below sea level.

q: What does the word 'delight' mean?
f: Delight means great pleasure or joy; as a verb it means to please greatly.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the Cholistan Desert located?
f: The Cholistan Desert lies in southern Punjab, near Bahawalpur.

q: Which of the following is a desert of Pakistan?
f: Cholistan in Punjab is a desert of Pakistan, along with Thar, Thal and Kharan.

q: In a diagonal matrix, if all the non-zero diagonal elements are equal, what is the matrix called?
f: A diagonal matrix with equal diagonal entries is called a scalar matrix.

q: In which year (CE) did the mother of the Holy Prophet (SAW) pass away?
f: The Prophet (SAW) was born in 570 CE and his mother died when he was about six, around 577 CE.

q: Which district of Pakistan has the largest population according to the census?
f: Lahore district had about 11.1 million people in 2017 and about 13.0 million in the 2023 census, the highest of any district.

q: Dog is to bitch as horse is to what?
f: A bitch is the female dog; the female horse is a mare.

q: According to a hadith, how many good deeds (nekis) are earned by reciting one letter of the Holy Quran?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) said a good deed is rewarded tenfold, so one letter of the Quran earns ten good deeds.

q: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO)?
f: ECO members are Pakistan, Iran, Turkey, Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. Saudi Arabia is not among them.

q: What is the meaning (synonym) of the word 'ecstasy'?
f: Ecstasy is a state of intense happiness or delight. Rapture is a close synonym.

q: Where was Abdul Sattar Edhi born?
f: Edhi was born in 1928 in Bantva in Gujarat, British India, and migrated to Pakistan after Partition.

q: In whose government were the non-party based elections held in Pakistan in 1985?
f: General Zia-ul-Haq held non-party elections in February 1985. Muhammad Khan Junejo became Prime Minister after them.

q: What is the antonym of the word 'embellish'?
f: To embellish is to make something more attractive by adding decoration. Its opposite is to disfigure or spoil.

q: What is the synonym of 'enigmatic'?
f: Enigmatic describes something puzzling and hard to understand, which is mysterious.

q: In whose era was the Battle of Yamama fought?
f: The Battle of Yamama was fought in 11-12 AH against the false prophet Musaylima during the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).

q: The Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) belongs to the descendants of which prophet?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) descended from Hazrat Ismail (AS), son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), through the Quraysh.

q: On what date did Pakistan conduct its first nuclear tests?
f: Pakistan carried out its first nuclear tests in the Chagai hills, Balochistan, on 28 May 1998 (five tests, Chagai-I), followed by one more on 30 May 1998. This was a reply to India's tests earlier that month.

q: How many Nobel Prizes in Physics has Pakistan received so far?
f: Dr Abdus Salam received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979, shared with Glashow and Weinberg. No other Pakistani has won in Physics.

q: How many farz (obligatory acts) does Namaz have according to the Hanafi school?
f: Namaz has 13 farz: 6 outside the prayer (conditions such as cleanliness, covering the body, facing the Qibla, time and intention) and 7 inside it (such as takbeer, qiyam, qira'at, ruku, sajdah, qa'da akhira).

q: On which date of Ramadan was Makkah conquered (Fath-e-Makkah) in 8 AH?
f: Most Pakistani textbooks give 20 Ramadan 8 AH (January 630 CE) for the conquest of Makkah, when the Muslims entered the city peacefully.

q: What was the name of the father of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah?
f: The father of Quaid-e-Azam was Jinnahbhai Poonja, a merchant in Karachi. His mother was Mithibai.

q: Who is the Chairman of the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) of Pakistan, according to the latest available reports?
f: Rashid Mahmood Langrial was appointed FBR Chairman in August 2024 and the latest reports found show him still in office.

q: A man walks a few steps towards the north, then turns right and walks, and then turns right again. In which direction is he now going?
f: Facing north, a right turn makes him face east; a second right turn makes him face south.

q: If 3x - 9 = 2x + 7, find x.
f: Subtract 2x from both sides: x - 9 = 7, so x = 16.

q: Who was the founder of the USSR (Soviet Union)?
f: Vladimir Lenin led the Bolshevik Revolution of 1917 and headed the new state when the USSR was formally created in 1922.

q: What kind of fraction is 9/3?
f: In 9/3 the numerator 9 is larger than the denominator 3, so it is an improper fraction. It simplifies to the whole number 3.

q: A plane uses 160 gallons of fuel to cover 330 nautical miles. About how many gallons will it use to cover 700 nautical miles?
f: Fuel per mile is 160 divided by 330, and 700 times 160 divided by 330 is 112000 divided by 330, which is about 339.4 gallons.

q: Robert E. Lee was a famous general of which war?
f: Robert E. Lee commanded the Confederate army of Northern Virginia in the American Civil War (1861-1865). His main opponent on the Union side was Ulysses S. Grant.

q: What was the gift given to the Muslims on the night of Miraj?
f: On the night of Miraj, Allah made five daily prayers obligatory for the Muslims. The number was reduced from fifty to five.

q: A brother is 5 years old and his sister is three times his age. What will be the sister's age when the brother is 12?
f: The sister is 3 x 5 = 15 years old now. The brother becomes 12 after 7 years, so the sister will be 15 + 7 = 22.

q: Who was the first Governor of the North-West Frontier Province (now KPK) after the creation of Pakistan?
f: Sir George Cunningham was appointed Governor of NWFP in August 1947 at the creation of Pakistan.

q: Who was the first Governor of Punjab after the creation of Pakistan?
f: Sir Francis Mudie was the first Governor of West Punjab in 1947.

q: What was the name of the paternal grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: The Prophet's father was Abdullah, and Abdullah's father was Abdul Muttalib, the Prophet's paternal grandfather.

q: In which province does the Green Line Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system run?
f: The Green Line BRT runs in Karachi, which is the capital of Sindh province.

q: What is the HCF of 12 and 28?
f: 12 = 2 x 2 x 3 and 28 = 2 x 2 x 7. The common part is 2 x 2 = 4.

q: Bait ul Mamoor is located in which heaven?
f: In the narration of the Miraj, the Prophet (PBUH) saw Bait ul Mamoor in the seventh heaven.

q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
f: The word hexagon comes from the Greek hex meaning six, so it has six sides.

q: For how many years did the Prophet (PBUH) preach Islam in Makkah before the Hijrat to Madina?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) received his first revelation at 40 and migrated at 53, so he preached in Makkah for about 13 years.

q: In which month of the Hijri calendar was the Treaty of Hudaibiya signed (6 AH)?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) set out for Umrah in Dhul Qadah 6 AH and the treaty was signed with Quraysh at Hudaibiya in that month.

q: What is the multiplicative identity of a complex number, written as an ordered pair?
f: The complex number 1 + 0i is written (1, 0), and (a, b) times (1, 0) = (a, b) for every complex number.

q: Who wrote the book 'Culture and Imperialism'?
f: Culture and Imperialism (1993) was written by the Palestinian-American scholar Edward Said.

q: In which country did the first Industrial Revolution begin?
f: The Industrial Revolution began in Great Britain in the second half of the 18th century, with steam power and mechanised textile production.

q: Complete the sentence: Smoking is injurious ___ health.
f: The adjective injurious is followed by the preposition to, so the correct phrase is injurious to health.

q: According to the Holy Quran and hadith, killing one innocent person is equal to what?
f: Surah Al-Maidah (5:32) says that whoever kills one innocent soul is as if he had killed all of mankind.

q: Is the number 5/7 rational or irrational?
f: A rational number can be written as p/q with integers p and q and q not zero. 5/7 has this form, so it is rational.

q: Is 22/7 a rational or an irrational number?
o: Irrational, because it is close to pi
Rational, because it is a ratio of two integers
f: 22/7 is a fraction of two integers, so it is rational. It is only an approximation of pi, which is irrational.

q: Where is Jabal Arafat (Jabal-e-Rahmat), the hill where pilgrims stand on 9 Dhul Hijjah?
o: Near Makkah, in the plain of Arafat
f: Jabal Arafat, also called Jabal-e-Rahmat, stands in the plain of Arafat about 20 km southeast of Makkah.

q: Change into passive voice: He said, "I have done my job."
o: It was said by him that his job had been done by him.
It was said by him that he had done his job.
His job was done by him.
It is said by him that I have done my job.
f: In indirect passive form the statement becomes: It was said by him that his job had been done by him.

q: Change the narration: He says, "I did not care about my job."
o: He says that he had not cared about his job.
He said that he did not care about his job.
He says that he did not care about his job.
He says that I did not care about my job.
f: The reporting verb says is in the present tense, so the tense of the reported speech does not change; only the pronouns change.

q: Which one is different from the others: chimpanzee, ape, baboon, kangaroo, monkey?
f: Chimpanzee, ape, baboon and monkey are all primates, while the kangaroo is a marsupial.

q: The Karakoram Highway connects Pakistan with which country?
f: The Karakoram Highway runs from Hasan Abdal in Pakistan to Kashgar in China through the Khunjerab Pass.

q: Which of these is another name for the Karakoram Highway?
f: The Karakoram Highway is also called the Pakistan-China Friendship Highway and is numbered N-35.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the karez system of irrigation mainly used?
f: A karez is an underground channel that carries water from a hillside, and it is widely used in dry Balochistan.

q: Who described Kashmir as the jugular vein of Pakistan?
f: The statement is credited to Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, who stressed the strategic importance of Kashmir.

q: What is the antonym of the word justify?
f: To justify means to defend as right, and the opposite is to condemn or blame.

q: In which year AD was the Battle (Ghazwa) of Khyber fought?
f: The Battle of Khyber took place in 7 AH, which corresponds to 628 AD. It ended with the conquest of the Jewish fortresses of Khyber.

q: Foot is to knee as hand is to what?
f: The knee is the main joint of the leg above the foot, and the elbow is the main joint of the arm above the hand. So hand is to elbow.

q: Approximately how many disbelievers (Quraish) fought against the Muslims in the Battle of Uhud?
f: The Makkan army at Uhud numbered about 3000 men, while the Muslims were about 1000 at the start and about 700 after 300 hypocrites withdrew.

q: What is the capital of Sri Lanka as commonly given in textbooks?
f: Colombo is the largest city and commercial capital of Sri Lanka and the usual textbook answer.

q: Which is the hottest layer of the Earth's atmosphere?
f: In the thermosphere, absorption of solar radiation can heat the thin air to over 1,000 degrees Celsius.

q: What is the process by which water vapour is lost from the leaves of a plant?
f: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour through the stomata of leaves.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to LENIENT?
f: Lenient means merciful or not strict, so tolerant is the closest.

q: Which mountain range lies between Pakistan and China?
f: The Karakoram range along the north of Pakistan forms its border with China, crossed by the Karakoram Highway.

q: Which pillar of Islam was made obligatory on the Prophet (PBUH) during the Mairaj?
f: Five daily prayers were gifted to the Muslims on the night of Mairaj, after being reduced from fifty.

q: Which party won a majority of seats in East Pakistan in the 1970 general elections?
f: The Awami League led by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman won 160 of the 162 East Pakistan seats.

q: What is the capital of Malaysia?
f: Kuala Lumpur is the capital and largest city of Malaysia.

q: In a class of 30 students, 24 are male. What is the percentage of females?
f: Females = 30 - 24 = 6. Percentage = 6/30 x 100 = 20%.

q: What is the height of Mangla Dam (commonly quoted)?
f: Mangla Dam is about 147 metres (482 feet) high according to commonly cited figures.

q: What is the mean of -5 and -5?
What is the mean of 1, 4, 5, 6?
What is the migration of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) from Makkah to Madina called?
f: The migration from Makkah to Madina in 622 AD is called Hijrat (Hijrah). The Islamic Hijri calendar starts from this event.

q: What is the total number of seats in the National Assembly of Pakistan?
f: After the 25th Amendment merged FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the total fell to 336 seats. These are 266 general, 60 women and 10 minority seats.

q: Who is the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional from Pakistan?
f: Arfa Karim Randhawa became a Microsoft Certified Professional at the age of nine in 2004. She was the youngest in the world at that time.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, what is the minimum age to become a member of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
f: Article 62 requires a candidate for the National Assembly to be at least 25 years old. A voter must be 18.

q: Which planet has the largest moon in the Solar System?
f: Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter, is the largest moon in the Solar System. It is even bigger than the planet Mercury.

q: Who was the first man to land on the Moon?
f: Neil Armstrong of the Apollo 11 mission stepped on the Moon on 20 July 1969.

q: Which pronoun is most suitable for the word mom?
f: Mom is a female parent, so the feminine subject pronoun she is used.

q: What is the motto given by the Quaid-e-Azam to the nation?
f: The Quaid-e-Azam gave the nation the motto Unity, Faith, Discipline (Ittehad, Yaqeen-e-Muhkam, Nazm). This is the order used in his speeches and in Pakistani textbooks.

q: How many companions are called the Ashra Mubashra?
f: Ashra Mubashra are ten Companions who were given the glad tidings of Paradise in their lifetime.

q: What is the multiplicative inverse of 0.001?
f: The inverse of a number is 1 divided by it. 1 / 0.001 = 1000.

q: Who is the author of the book Indian Musalmans (1871)?
f: Indian Musalmans: Are They Bound in Conscience to Rebel Against the Queen? was written by Sir William Wilson Hunter.

q: How many prophets are mentioned by name in the Holy Quran?
f: The Holy Quran mentions the names of 25 prophets.

q: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I am sorry."
o: She said that she is sorry.
She said that she was sorry.
She said that I was sorry.
She said that she had been sorry.
f: In indirect speech after a past reporting verb the present tense changes to past, and the pronoun I changes to she, so am becomes was.

q: How many nautical miles is the territorial sea of Pakistan under the UN Law of the Sea?
f: Under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, a country's territorial sea extends 12 nautical miles from its coast, and Pakistan claims this limit.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of the Netherlands as of 2026?
f: Rob Jetten of the D66 party became Prime Minister on 23 February 2026, succeeding Dick Schoof.

q: Which letter comes next in the series: O, K, H, F, ?
f: The positions are 15, 11, 8, 6. The gaps are 4, 3, 2, so the next gap is 1 and 6 - 1 = 5, which is E.

q: How many nights did the Prophet (PBUH) spend in the Cave of Thawr during the Hijrat?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) hid in the Cave of Thawr for three nights before going on to Madina.

q: Which type of noun is Islamabad?
f: A proper noun is the name of a particular person, place or thing. Islamabad is the name of one specific city, so it is a proper noun and it is written with a capital letter.

q: An obtuse angle measures more than 90 degrees and less than how many degrees?
f: An obtuse angle is greater than 90 degrees (a right angle) but less than 180 degrees (a straight angle).

q: What was the official name of the country under the 1962 constitution of Pakistan?
f: The 1962 constitution named the country the Republic of Pakistan.

q: Ali is older than Waqas, and Usman is younger than Waqas. Who is the oldest of the three?
f: Ali is older than Waqas and Waqas is older than Usman, so the order from oldest is Ali, Waqas, Usman.

q: Which is generally considered the oldest civilization of the world?
f: The Mesopotamian (Sumerian) civilization, which arose between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers around 3500 BC, is usually regarded as the oldest.

q: What is the currency of Oman?
f: The official currency of Oman is the Omani rial.

q: What is meant by the order of a matrix?
o: Number of rows by number of columns
f: The order of a matrix is stated as rows x columns, for example a matrix with 2 rows and 3 columns is of order 2 x 3.

q: Which of the following is a principal organ of the United Nations?
f: The six principal organs of the UN are the General Assembly, Security Council, Economic and Social Council, Trusteeship Council, International Court of Justice and the Secretariat. The others listed are agencies or funds.

q: Out of 15000 students, 12000 are present. What is the percentage of students present?
Mark Zuckerberg is the founder and head of which company?
f: Mark Zuckerberg co-founded Facebook in 2004 and is the chairman and CEO of its parent company, Meta Platforms.

q: 6 is what percent of 20?
f: Percentage = 6/20 x 100 = 30%.

q: With what is Tayammum performed when water is not available?
f: Tayammum is performed by striking the hands on clean earth, dust or sand and wiping the face and the arms.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word PERPETUAL?
f: Perpetual means never ending or continuing forever, which matches everlasting.

q: What is the study of geometrical shapes in a plane called?
f: Plane geometry (Euclidean geometry) studies two-dimensional shapes such as lines, triangles and circles.

q: Between whom was the Battle of Plassey (1757) fought?
o: The British East India Company and Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula of Bengal
f: At Plassey the East India Company force under Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula, helped by the betrayal of Mir Jafar.

q: Through which point does the line y = 5x pass?
f: Putting x = 0 gives y = 5 times 0 = 0, so the line passes through (0, 0). The other points do not satisfy y = 5x.

q: Who is the co-chairperson of the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP)?
f: Asif Ali Zardari is the co-chairperson of the PPP.

q: Choose the correct preposition: My father died ___ the war.
f: We say died in a war, because the war is the event during which he died.

q: Who is the head of state of Jordan?
f: Jordan is a monarchy and King Abdullah II is its head of state, so it has no president.

q: What is the probability of a sure (certain) event?
f: A sure event is one that is certain to happen, so its probability is 1. Probability always lies between 0 and 1.

q: Is 2x^2 + 3x + 2 a quadratic expression?
f: The highest power of x is 2, with a non-zero coefficient 2, so it has the form ax^2 + bx + c of a quadratic.

q: What is a quarter of 1/3 of 90?
f: 1/3 of 90 is 30. A quarter of 30 is 30 divided by 4, which equals 7.5.

q: What is the literal meaning of the Arabic word Rabb?
f: Rabb means Lord, Sustainer and Nourisher, the One who brings up and provides for all creation. It is used in the Quran for Allah, as in Rabbul Alameen.

q: The Radcliffe Line is the boundary between which two countries?
f: The Radcliffe Line was drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe in 1947 to divide Punjab and Bengal between India and Pakistan. It is the border between Pakistan and India.

q: Which angel is appointed by Allah to bring rain?
f: Hazrat Mikael (AS) is the angel in charge of rain and sustenance. This is the commonly taught view in Islamic books.

q: What is the real part of the complex number 6 - 9i?
f: In a + bi form, the real part is the term without i. Here it is 6.

q: What was the real name of Iblis (Shaitan) before he was cursed?
f: Iblis is said in many Islamic traditions to have been called Azazil before he refused to bow to Adam (AS). He was a jinn and was cursed for his pride.

q: What is a decimal number that neither terminates nor repeats called?
f: A non-terminating, non-recurring decimal cannot be written as a fraction p over q. Such a number is called irrational.

q: A decimal in which one or more digits repeat endlessly in the same pattern is called:
f: In a recurring decimal, a digit or a block of digits repeats forever, such as 0.333... or 0.142857142857... Such numbers are rational.

q: What did the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (Government of India Act 1919) introduce in the provinces?
f: The 1919 reforms divided provincial subjects into transferred (under elected ministers) and reserved (under the Governor). This system was called dyarchy.

q: Between which two regions does the Rann of Kutch lie?
f: The Rann of Kutch is a large salt marsh in the Thar desert area on the border between Sindh in Pakistan and Gujarat in India. A border dispute there was settled by tribunal in 1968.

q: According to the Quran, which religion is accepted by Allah?
f: The Quran states that the religion with Allah is Islam (Surah Al-Imran 3:19). It also says no other religion will be accepted from anyone.

q: Nankana Sahib is a famous holy site of which religion?
f: Nankana Sahib is the birthplace of Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism. It is in Punjab, Pakistan.

q: The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared in response to whose challenge?
f: Lord Birkenhead, the Secretary of State for India, challenged Indian leaders to draft a constitution acceptable to all communities. The Nehru Report was the Congress-led answer to that challenge.

q: Which article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan declares that Pakistan shall be a Federal Republic known as the Islamic Republic of Pakistan?
f: Article 1 of the 1973 Constitution states that Pakistan shall be a Federal Republic to be known as the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

q: In which constitution of Pakistan was the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan first used?
f: The 1956 Constitution, Pakistan's first, named the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan. Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956.

q: Which country has the largest official gold reserves in the world?
f: The United States holds about 8,133 tonnes of official gold reserves, roughly double that of second-placed Germany.

q: In which city did the tribes of Aus and Khazraj reside?
f: Aus and Khazraj were the two main Arab tribes of Yathrib, later called Madina. They became the Ansar after welcoming the Prophet (PBUH).

q: On which date was the Pakistan Resolution (Lahore Resolution) presented?
f: The resolution was presented on 23 March 1940 at the Lahore session of the All India Muslim League, having been moved by A. K. Fazlul Haq and passed on 24 March.

q: According to the commonly given order of revelation, which Surah was the third to be revealed?
f: The usual order is Al-Alaq first, Al-Qalam second and Al-Muzzammil third.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word reward?
f: A reward is something given in return for good work or conduct, that is, a recompense.

q: Which word is the synonym of rich?
f: Rich means having a great deal of money, and wealthy has the same meaning.

q: Which river is the largest in the world by volume of water discharged?
f: The Amazon carries the greatest volume of water of any river in the world.

q: The name Punjab means the land of how many rivers?
f: Punjab is from the Persian words punj (five) and ab (water), meaning five rivers: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.

q: The Reshmi Romal (Silk Letter) Tehreek was started by Maulana Mahmud Hasan and which colleague?
f: The Silk Letter Movement of about 1913 to 1920 was organised by Shaikhul Hind Maulana Mahmud Hasan with Maulana Ubaidullah Sindhi.

q: What is the square root of 196?
f: 14 x 14 = 196, so the square root of 196 is 14.

q: What is the approximate value of the square root of 7?
f: 2.6 x 2.6 = 6.76 and 2.7 x 2.7 = 7.29, so the root lies between them; 2.65 x 2.65 = 7.02 so it is about 2.65.

q: How many roots does a quadratic equation have?
f: A quadratic equation has degree 2, and an equation of degree n has n roots. So it has 2 roots, which may be real or complex.

q: In which battle were about 70 Sahaba martyred?
f: About 70 Sahaba were martyred in the Battle of Uhud in 3 Hijri.

q: In which year did Dr Abdus Salam win the Nobel Prize in Physics?
f: Dr Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for the electroweak theory.

q: Which of the following countries is a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) as of 2026?
f: Iran became a full member in 2023 and Belarus in 2024, bringing the SCO to ten full members. Turkey is only a dialogue partner, while Afghanistan and Mongolia are observers.

q: Which fruit has its seeds on the outside of its body (on the surface of the skin)?
f: The tiny seed-like dots on a strawberry are actually separate fruits (achenes) on the outer surface, each containing a seed. The other fruits keep their seeds inside.

q: Who elects the President of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution?
o: An Electoral College of the Senate, National Assembly and Provincial Assemblies
f: Under Article 41 of the 1973 Constitution the President is elected by an Electoral College made up of members of the Senate, the National Assembly and the four Provincial Assemblies.

q: What is the measure of an angle inscribed in a semicircle?
f: By Thales' theorem, an angle inscribed in a semicircle subtends the diameter and is always a right angle, 90 degrees.

q: Who demanded the separation of Sindh from the Bombay Presidency in the Muslim proposals of the 1920s?
f: Jinnah included the separation of Sindh from Bombay in the Delhi Muslim Proposals of 1927 and again in his Fourteen Points of 1929.

q: For what is the Last Sermon (Khutbah Hajjat-ul-Wida) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) best known?
o: A treaty with the Jews of Madinah
f: In the Last Sermon the Holy Prophet (PBUH) declared the equality of all people, the sanctity of life, property and honour, the rights of women and the abolition of interest and old blood feuds. It is therefore regarded as the first great charter of human rights.

q: Where did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) deliver the Last Sermon?
o: In the valley of Uranah on the plain of Arafat
f: During the Farewell Hajj the Holy Prophet (PBUH) addressed more than one hundred thousand Muslims on the 9th of Dhul Hijjah in the valley of Uranah at Arafat.

q: Choose the correct preposition: She shouted ____ him.
f: The verb shout takes at when it means to speak angrily to someone, so the correct sentence is She shouted at him.

q: What is the meaning of the word 'Siraat' (as in Siraat-e-Mustaqeem)?
f: 'Siraat' is an Arabic word meaning a path or way. In Surah Al-Fatiha, Siraat-e-Mustaqeem means the straight path.

q: Adil is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will the age of his sister be when Adil is 15 years old?
f: The sister is now 3 x 5 = 15 years old. Adil needs 15 - 5 = 10 more years, so the sister will be 15 + 10 = 25.

q: Where is Gwadar situated?
o: On the Makran coast of Balochistan
On the coast of Sindh near Karachi
f: Gwadar is a port city on the Arabian Sea coast of the Makran region in Balochistan.

q: In which country did the Black Lives Matter slogan and movement first start?
f: The hashtag and movement began in the USA in 2013 after the acquittal of the man who shot Trayvon Martin.

q: Who sold the Kashmir valley and to whom?
o: The British East India Company to Gulab Singh Dogra
f: By the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) the British East India Company sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh, the Dogra ruler of Jammu.

q: What is the trivial solution of a homogeneous system of linear equations in three unknowns x, y and z?

o: A branch of the Quraish of Makkah
f: Banu Quraiza were a Jewish tribe living near Madinah. They broke their agreement with the Muslims during the Battle of the Trench (Khandaq).

q: What do the names of Surah Al-Fatiha and Surah Al-Baqarah mean in English?
f: Al-Fatiha means The Opening and Al-Baqarah means The Cow.

q: Where is the Sukkur Barrage located?
f: Sukkur Barrage is built on the River Indus at Sukkur in the province of Sindh.

q: What is the area of a triangle with base 6 cm and height 24 cm?
f: Area = half x base x height = 0.5 x 6 x 24 = 72 square cm.

q: What is the height of a triangle whose base is 6 cm and area is 24 square cm?
f: Area = half x base x height, so 24 = 0.5 x 6 x h = 3h. Therefore h = 8 cm.

q: Is the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan based on a parliamentary or a presidential system?
f: The 1973 Constitution set up a parliamentary form of government with the Prime Minister as chief executive and the President as head of state.

q: On which basis was Pakistan created, according to the resolution passed in 1940?
f: The Lahore Resolution of 23 March 1940, based on the Two-Nation Theory, demanded separate Muslim states and led to Pakistan.

q: Who is known as Afzalul Bashar Ba'd al-Anbiya (best of mankind after the prophets)?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) is called Afzalul Bashar Ba'd al-Anbiya, the best of mankind after the prophets.

q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is twice his age. When Ali becomes 8 years old, how old will his sister be?
f: Sister is 2 x 4 = 8 years now. Ali needs 4 more years to be 8, so sister will be 8 + 4 = 12.

q: Change into active voice: The rooms are being decorated by the students.
o: The students were decorating the rooms.
The students are decorating the rooms.
The students have decorated the rooms.
f: The passive present continuous (are being decorated) becomes the active present continuous (are decorating).

q: Fill in the blank: Did the students ----- a lot of work in class?
f: After the auxiliary did the verb takes its base form, so have is correct.

q: To what name was Islamabad's Kashmir Highway changed in August 2020?
f: In August 2020 the government renamed Kashmir Highway in Islamabad as Srinagar Highway to show solidarity with Kashmiris.

q: Which constitution was in force in Pakistan before the 1973 Constitution?
f: The 1962 Constitution, given by Ayub Khan, remained until it was abrogated in 1969 by Yahya Khan, apart from a brief interim period.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, sovereignty belongs to whom?
f: The Preamble and Objectives Resolution state that sovereignty over the entire universe belongs to Almighty Allah alone, exercised by the people as a sacred trust.

q: In which place was Benazir Bhutto buried?
f: Benazir Bhutto was buried in the family mausoleum at Garhi Khuda Bakhsh near Larkana, Sindh, beside her father.

q: What was the name of Benazir Bhutto's mother?
f: Begum Nusrat Bhutto, of Iranian-Kurdish origin, was the wife of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and mother of Benazir.

q: Between whom was the brotherhood (Mukhawat) established after the migration to Madinah?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) created brotherhood between the Muhajirin who came from Makkah and the Ansar, the helpers of Madinah.

q: Near which town is the Diamer Bhasha Dam being built?
f: Diamer Bhasha Dam is on the Indus River about 40 km downstream of Chilas on the border of Gilgit-Baltistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: What is the meaning of biased?
o: Prejudiced in favour of one side
f: A biased person unfairly favours or opposes someone or something.

q: What is a bicameral legislature?
o: A legislature chosen by the army
f: Bicameral means two chambers; the word camera means chamber.

q: Which was the first bicameral legislature of Pakistan, consisting of a National Assembly and a Senate?
f: The 1956 and 1962 Constitutions provided a single House (unicameral legislature). The 1973 Constitution created Parliament with two Houses, the National Assembly and the Senate.

q: Where is the Black Sea located?
o: Between southeastern Europe and western Asia
f: The Black Sea lies between southeastern Europe and western Asia, bordered by Turkey, Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia and Georgia.

q: In which year did Muhammad Ali Bogra become Prime Minister of Pakistan?
f: Governor-General Ghulam Muhammad dismissed Khawaja Nazimuddin in April 1953 and appointed Muhammad Ali Bogra, then ambassador to the USA, as Prime Minister.

q: Who bowled the fastest recorded delivery in cricket history at 161.3 km per hour?
f: Shoaib Akhtar bowled a delivery of 161.3 km per hour against England in the 2003 World Cup, which is still the official record.

q: In a class the number of girls is 7 more than the number of boys and the total is 33. How many boys are there?
f: Let boys be x, so girls are x + 7 and 2x + 7 = 33, giving x = 13. Girls are therefore 20.

q: Who abrogated the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan in March 1969?
f: When Ayub Khan resigned in March 1969, General Yahya Khan imposed martial law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution.

q: Which reforms of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims in British India?
f: The Indian Councils Act 1909, known as the Minto-Morley Reforms, granted separate electorates to Muslims.

q: A train travels at 120 km/h. How much distance does it cover in 30 minutes?
f: 30 minutes is half an hour, so distance = 120 x 1/2 = 60 km.

q: In a bus of 24 people, 3/4 are male. What percentage are female?
f: Males are 3/4 of 24 = 18, so females are 24 - 18 = 6. Percentage = 6/24 x 100 = 25 percent.

q: Fill in the blank: We have business classes ______ night.
f: The preposition 'at' is used with night in the phrase 'at night'.

q: From which country did Pakistan acquire the J-10C fighter aircraft?
f: The J-10C is a Chinese fighter built by Chengdu Aircraft Corporation. Pakistan Air Force inducted it from China.

q: How many days are there in a common (non-leap) calendar year?
f: A common year has 12 months totalling 365 days. A leap year has 366 days.

q: What is the complex number 4 - 2i called?
f: A number of the form a + bi with i the square root of minus 1 is a complex number. Here a = 4 and b = -2.

q: Approximately how many prophets came to the world in total, according to popular Islamic tradition?
f: A popular narration says that about 124,000 prophets were sent. The number is not given in the Quran.

q: Who was the ruler of Sindh when Muhammad bin Qasim invaded it in 711 AD?
f: Raja Dahir of the Brahman dynasty ruled Sindh from Aror. Muhammad bin Qasim defeated him in 712 AD.

q: Zakat becomes obligatory on a minimum of how many camels?
f: The nisab for camels is five. One goat is due on 5 to 9 camels.

q: Which canal separates Asia from Africa?
f: The Suez Canal in Egypt separates Africa from the Sinai Peninsula in Asia. It links the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea.

q: What is the capital of Argentina?
f: Buenos Aires is the capital and largest city of Argentina.

q: What is the capital of Bahrain?
f: Manama is the capital of Bahrain, an island country in the Persian Gulf.

q: What is the capital of Cuba?
f: Havana is the capital and largest city of Cuba.

q: What is the capital of Denmark?
f: Copenhagen is the capital and largest city of Denmark.

q: What is the capital of India?
f: New Delhi is the capital of India.

q: What is the capital of Thailand?
f: Bangkok is the capital and largest city of Thailand.

q: On which date is International Women's Day celebrated?
f: International Women's Day is observed every year on 8 March.

q: How many centimetres are there in one metre?
f: The prefix centi means one hundredth, so 1 metre equals 100 centimetres.

q: Who is the Chairman of the Senate of Pakistan as of October 2026?
f: Syed Yousaf Raza Gilani of the PPP was elected Chairman of the Senate and sworn in on 9 April 2024.

q: Who is the Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) as of October 2026?
f: Mauritania's Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed was elected OIC Secretary General on 27 August 2026 in Jeddah, succeeding Hissein Brahim Taha of Chad.

q: In mathematics, a quantity whose value can change is called a
f: A variable is a symbol that can take different values, unlike a constant whose value is fixed.

q: Who was the first Pakistani Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army?
f: Ayub Khan became the first Pakistani C-in-C in January 1951, after British generals Messervy and Gracey.

q: According to Islamic teaching, what is recited in the ear of a newborn baby?
f: It is Sunnah to recite the Azan in the baby's right ear soon after birth.

q: Which of the following is a Chinese COVID-19 vaccine?
f: Sinopharm is made in China; the other three were developed in the USA, Germany and the UK.

q: Choose the correct word: Who did you take this book ____?
f: The sentence means from whom the book was taken, so the preposition from is correct.

q: In which US state is the Grand Canyon located?
f: The Grand Canyon, carved by the Colorado River, is in northern Arizona.

q: In which period did the American Civil War take place?
f: The American Civil War between the Union and the Confederacy was fought from 1861 to 1865.

q: Who led the Union side in the American Civil War?
f: Abraham Lincoln was President of the Union (the Northern states) during the war.

q: Mohenjo-daro, a famous site of the Indus Valley Civilization, is located in which province of Pakistan?
f: Mohenjo-daro lies in Larkana district of Sindh on the bank of the Indus.

q: Who were the first people to reach the summit of Mount Everest in 1953?
f: Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and Sherpa Tenzing Norgay reached the summit on 29 May 1953.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'precious'?
f: Precious means of great value or highly prized.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'breach'?
f: To breach something is to break or violate it, such as a rule or a contract.

q: Which line is the de facto boundary between India and China?
f: The India-China frontier is known as the Line of Actual Control (LAC).

q: What is the antonym of 'coercive'?
f: Coercive means forcing someone to act by pressure or threat, so its opposite is voluntary, done by free choice.

q: Which word is a synonym of 'coercive'?
f: Coercive means using force or pressure to make someone obey, which is close in meaning to compulsory.

q: In a matrix of order 5 x 4, how many elements are there in each column?
f: The order 5 x 4 means 5 rows and 4 columns. Each column runs down through all the rows, so it has 5 elements.

q: Which letter and number come next in the series: Z1, X3, V5, T7, ?
f: The letters move back by 2 each time (Z, X, V, T, R) and the numbers increase by 2 (1, 3, 5, 7, 9). So the next term is R9.

q: What is the synonym of 'command'?
f: To command means to give an authoritative instruction, which is the same as to order.

q: The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared in response to which commission?
f: The Simon Commission of 1927 had no Indian member, and Lord Birkenhead challenged Indians to frame a constitution. The Nehru Report was the Indian reply.

q: What is common in the series 4, 8, 12, 16?
f: 4 = 4 x 1, 8 = 4 x 2, 12 = 4 x 3 and 16 = 4 x 4, so every term is a multiple of 4 with a common difference of 4.

q: The Partition of Bengal in 1905 gave benefits to which community?
f: It created the Muslim-majority province of Eastern Bengal and Assam, giving Muslims better chances in education, jobs and politics.

q: 900 employees work in a company and 480 of them are men. What is the percentage of women?
In which year did the East India Company annex the Punjab?
f: After the Second Anglo-Sikh War, the Punjab was annexed to the Company's territories in 1849.

q: Who compiled the hadith collection Musnad Ahmad?
f: Musnad Ahmad was compiled by Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, founder of the Hanbali school of fiqh.

q: What is the largest composite number from 1 to 99?
f: 97 is prime, 98 = 2 x 49 and 99 = 9 x 11 has factors other than 1 and itself. So 99 is the largest composite number.

q: On what date was the Indian National Congress established?
f: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay on 28 December 1885.

q: Which caliph received the surrender of Jerusalem (Bait-ul-Muqaddas) in 637 AD?
f: Jerusalem was besieged by Muslim armies under Abu Ubaidah and Amr bin al-As and its people surrendered to Caliph Umar (RA) in person.

q: How many members did the first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan originally have?
f: The first Constituent Assembly formed in 1947 had 69 members.

q: In which year did the construction of Tarbela Dam begin?
f: The contract was awarded in May 1968 and main construction ran from 1968 to 1976.

q: In which year was Rawal Dam built (completed)?
f: Rawal Dam on the Korang River in Islamabad is listed as completed in 1962.

q: Who performs the duties of the President of Pakistan when the President is absent or unable to act?
f: Article 49 of the Constitution says the Chairman of the Senate acts as President when the office is vacant or the President is absent.

q: Convert 60 degrees into radians.
f: Radians = degrees x pi/180 = 60 x pi/180 = pi/3.

q: Convert to passive voice: He told me about the accident.
o: I was told about the accident by him.
I am told about the accident by him.
The accident was told by him to me about.
I had told about the accident by him.
f: The past simple active becomes was/were plus past participle in passive, with the object I becoming the subject.

q: Which device converts mechanical energy into electrical energy?
f: A generator (dynamo) turns a coil in a magnetic field and produces electric current from mechanical motion.

q: What does SUPARCO stand for?
o: Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission
Satellite and Upper Atmosphere Research Corporation
Space Utilization and Planetary Research Commission
Science and Upper Atmosphere Research Council
f: SUPARCO is Pakistan's national space agency, called the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission.

q: The Wakhan Corridor connects Pakistan to which province of Afghanistan?
f: The Wakhan Corridor is a narrow strip in Badakhshan province of north-eastern Afghanistan.

q: Between which two countries is the longest international border in the world?
f: The Canada-USA border is about 8,900 km long including the Alaska border, the longest in the world.

q: A train covers 120 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. How much distance will it cover in 15 minutes?
f: 1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes, so the speed is 120 / 100 = 1.2 km per minute. In 15 minutes the train covers 1.2 x 15 = 18 km.

q: A train covers 120 km in one hour. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes?
f: 12 minutes is 1/5 of an hour. So the distance is 120 / 5 = 24 km.

q: A train covers 90 km in 1 hour. How much time will it take to cover 120 km?
f: Time = distance / speed = 120 / 90 = 4/3 hours. 4/3 hours is 1 hour 20 minutes.

q: If a car covers 20 km in an hour, what distance does it cover in 30 minutes?
f: 30 minutes is half an hour. So the distance is 20 / 2 = 10 km.

q: If a car covers 90 km in one hour and 40 minutes, in how many minutes will it cover 1 km?
f: 1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes for 90 km. So 1 km takes 100 / 90 = 10/9 minutes.

q: Which of the following British reforms introduced separate electorates for the Muslims of the subcontinent?
f: The Indian Councils Act of 1909, known as the Minto-Morley Reforms, granted Muslims separate electorates, which was a key demand of the Simla Deputation of 1906.

q: Which is the major rabi (winter) crop of Pakistan?
f: Wheat is sown in October to December and harvested in April to May, which makes it the main rabi crop.

q: On which date is World Red Cross and Red Crescent Day celebrated?
f: It is observed on 8 May, the birthday of Henry Dunant, the founder of the Red Cross.

q: After the 2026 tournament, which country or countries will host the next FIFA World Cup in 2030?
f: FIFA awarded the 2030 World Cup to Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with opening matches in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay to mark the centenary.

q: What is the currency of Belgium (Brussels) and Finland?
f: Both Belgium and Finland are members of the Eurozone and use the euro.

q: What is the currency of Uganda?
f: Uganda's national currency is the Ugandan shilling.

q: What is the name of China's currency?
f: China's official currency is the renminbi, whose main unit is the yuan.

q: Who is the current Director General of the Intelligence Bureau (IB) of Pakistan?
f: Fuad Asadullah Khan has led the IB since 2022 and in May 2026 the Prime Minister approved a four-year extension for him.

q: Who is the current Chancellor of Germany?
f: Friedrich Merz of the CDU became Chancellor in May 2025 and was still in office in October 2026.

q: If a circle is divided into 360 equal parts, what is each part called?
f: A full circle measures 360 degrees, so each of 360 equal parts is one degree.

q: Which country announced the cutting of funding to the World Health Organization in 2020 and later withdrew from it?
f: In 2020 President Trump halted US funding to the WHO, and in 2025 the United States started its withdrawal.

q: In which country is the Khanpur (Kahnpur) Dam located?
f: Khanpur Dam is on the Haro River near Haripur in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

q: Hazrat Asma (R.A), known as Dhat un-Nitaqayn, was the daughter of which Sahabi?
f: Asma bint Abu Bakr was the elder sister of Hazrat Aisha (R.A) and helped the Prophet (PBUH) during the Hijrah.

q: Hazrat Umm Kulthum (R.A), who was married to Hazrat Uthman (R.A), was the daughter of whom?
f: Umm Kulthum was a daughter of the Prophet (PBUH) and married Hazrat Uthman after the death of her sister Ruqayyah.

q: Which of the following was a daughter of Hazrat Ali (R.A) and Hazrat Fatima (R.A)?
f: Hazrat Zainab bint Ali was a daughter of Hazrat Ali and Hazrat Fatima and sister of Hasan and Husain.

q: How many days are there in a leap year?
f: A leap year has an extra day, 29 February, so it has 365 + 1 = 366 days.

q: What is the definition of a noun?
o: A word that describes an action
A word that names a person, place, thing or idea
A word that describes a noun
A word that joins two sentences
f: A noun is a naming word: it names a person, place, animal, thing or idea.

q: What is a square matrix?
o: A matrix with equal number of rows and columns
A matrix with only one row
A matrix with all elements zero
A matrix with only one column
f: A square matrix has the same number of rows as columns, for example 3 by 3.

q: Which word is a synonym of 'demise'?
f: Demise means death or the end of something.

q: In which body were the Basic Democrats of Ayub Khan's system mainly represented?
o: Electoral college for President and assemblies
f: Basic Democrats, elected from union councils, formed the electoral college that elected the President and members of the assemblies.

q: How many Basic Democrats were there in Ayub Khan's system (40,000 in each wing)?
f: Ayub Khan's Basic Democracies had 80,000 members, 40,000 in East Pakistan and 40,000 in West Pakistan.

q: What is the derivative of tan x with respect to x?
f: d/dx (tan x) = d/dx (sin x / cos x) = (cos^2 x + sin^2 x) / cos^2 x = sec^2 x.

q: Which lake is known as the world's largest permanent desert lake?
f: Lake Turkana in northern Kenya lies in a desert region and is the largest permanent desert lake, nicknamed the Jade Sea.

q: What is the determinant of a diagonal matrix?
f: For a diagonal matrix all off-diagonal entries are zero, so the determinant is the product of the diagonal elements.

q: What is a diagonal matrix?
o: A square matrix whose off-diagonal elements are all zero
A matrix with all elements equal
A matrix with one row only
A matrix whose determinant is always 1
f: A diagonal matrix is a square matrix in which every element outside the main diagonal is zero.

q: If the side of a square is a, what is the length of its diagonal?
f: By Pythagoras, diagonal = square root of (a^2 + a^2) = a times root 2.

q: What is the diameter of a circle whose radius is 28?
f: Diameter = 2 x radius = 2 x 28 = 56.

q: What is the radius of a circle with diameter 52 cm?
f: Radius = diameter / 2 = 52 / 2 = 26 cm.

q: Which word comes first in the dictionary?
f: Compare the third letter: Addidas has d, which comes before i in Adiabatic, Adjust (j) and Adit (i).

q: On which date did the singer Lata Mangeshkar die?
f: Lata Mangeshkar, the Indian playback singer, died in Mumbai on 6 February 2022.

q: Where was democracy first practised in the world?
f: Democracy began in the ancient Greek city-state of Athens around the 5th century BC.

q: The voice of which animal is described in the Holy Quran as the worst of voices?
f: Surah Luqman says the harshest of voices is surely the voice of the donkey.

q: What is the opposite of the word diversity?
f: Diversity means variety; its opposite is uniformity, meaning sameness.

q: If one dozen pencils cost Rs 60, what is the cost of 5 pencils?
f: One pencil costs 60 / 12 = Rs 5, so 5 pencils cost 5 x 5 = Rs 25.

q: If one dozen pencils cost Rs 27, what is the price of 4 pencils?
f: Four pencils are one third of a dozen, so the cost is 27 / 3 = Rs 9.

q: What is the national dress of Pakistan?
f: Shalwar Kameez is worn across all provinces and is recognised as the national dress of Pakistan.

q: What is the cutting of hair by a pilgrim at the end of Hajj called?
f: Halq means shaving the head, and qasr means trimming the hair; one of them is done to leave the state of Ihram.

q: What is the measure in degrees of each angle (corner) of a square?
f: A square has four equal angles and they sum to 360 degrees, so each is 360 / 4 = 90 degrees.

q: What does ECO stand for?
f: ECO stands for Economic Cooperation Organization, a regional group of Asian countries.

q: Abdul Sattar Edhi, the famous humanitarian known as the Angel of Mercy, belonged to which country?
f: Edhi spent his life in Pakistan and founded the Edhi Foundation in Karachi. He is regarded as one of the greatest humanitarians of Pakistan.

q: If one egg takes 2 minutes to boil, how many minutes will 5 eggs take when boiled together in the same pot?
f: Eggs boil at the same time in the same pot, so the time does not depend on the number of eggs. All 5 eggs take 2 minutes.

q: Akbar is older than Ahmad and Umair is older than Akbar. Who is the eldest?
f: Umair is older than Akbar, and Akbar is older than Ahmad. So the order is Umair, Akbar, Ahmad and Umair is the eldest.

q: If Akbar is elder than Ahmad and Adnan is elder than Akbar, then who is the eldest?
f: Adnan is elder than Akbar, and Akbar is elder than Ahmad. So Adnan is the eldest.

q: In which pact were separate electorates for Muslims granted?
f: Under the Lucknow Pact of 1916 the Congress accepted the Muslim League's demand for separate electorates for Muslims.

q: What is a set that has no element called?
f: A set with no element is called the null set or empty set and is written as a circle with a slash or as curly brackets with nothing inside.

q: What is a set with exactly one element called?
f: A set containing only one element, such as the set containing 5 alone, is called a singleton set.

q: If every element of set A is also an element of set B, then A is called what of B?
f: When all elements of A belong to B, A is a subset of B, written A is contained in B.

q: Which one is different from the rest: cow, snake, elephant, monkey?
f: Cow, elephant and monkey are mammals, while a snake is a reptile.

q: What is the meaning of the word 'embellish'?
o: To make more attractive by adding decoration
f: Embellish means to decorate or beautify something, or to add extra details to a story.

q: When was the partition of Bengal enforced by Lord Curzon?
f: Lord Curzon divided Bengal into East Bengal and Assam and West Bengal, and the partition took effect on 16 October 1905.

q: Which of the following are the vowels of the English alphabet?
f: The five vowel letters of English are A, E, I, O and U.

q: If RAT is coded as TAR (letters reversed), then what is FAT equal to?
f: RAT becomes TAR by reversing the order of letters. Reversing FAT gives TAF.

q: In trigonometry, what is tan x equal to?
o: cos x divided by sin x
sin x divided by cos x
f: Tangent is the ratio of sine to cosine, so tan x equals sin x divided by cos x.

q: What is cosecant x equal to?
o: sin x divided by cos x
f: Cosecant is the reciprocal of sine, so cosec x = 1 / sin x.

q: What type of equation is 6x - 5x - 7 = 0?
f: Simplifying gives x - 7 = 0, which has highest power 1 of x, so it is linear and gives x = 7.

q: Who headed the committee for the collection of the Holy Quran in the era of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) appointed Zaid bin Thabit, the Prophet's scribe of revelation, to collect the Quran into one volume.

q: How many end points does a ray have?
f: A ray starts at one fixed point and extends endlessly in one direction, so it has one end point.

q: Which uncle of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was among his bitter enemies?
f: Abu Lahab (Abdul Uzza) strongly opposed the Prophet (PBUH) and a Surah of the Quran is named after him. Abu Jahal was not his uncle.

q: Which event did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) take part in after the Harb-e-Fijar?
f: After the Harb-e-Fijar, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) took part in Hilf-ul-Fudul, a pact formed in Makkah to help the oppressed and protect travellers and the weak. He was a young man at the time.

q: What is the measure of each external angle of a regular hexagon?
f: The sum of the external angles of any polygon is 360 degrees. A hexagon has 6 sides, so each external angle is 360 divided by 6 = 60 degrees.

q: What is the measure of each external angle of a regular octagon?
f: The sum of the external angles of any polygon is 360 degrees. An octagon has 8 sides, so each external angle is 360 divided by 8 = 45 degrees.

q: What is meant by Laissez-faire in economics?
o: Minimum government interference in the economy
f: Laissez-faire is a French term meaning let do. It is the policy that the government should interfere as little as possible in economic affairs and leave markets free.

q: Which word comes first in the dictionary: False, Fallow, Faithful, Fallable, Falcon?
f: All words begin with Fa. The third letters are i (Faithful), l (the rest), so Faithful comes first. Then Falcon, Fallable, Fallow and False follow.

q: Hazrat Ali (RA) belonged to which family (clan) of Quraish?
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib, who was a son of Abdul Muttalib of Banu Hashim. He was thus a cousin of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

q: For what industry is Gaddani in Balochistan famous?
f: Gaddani, on the coast of Balochistan near Karachi, has one of the largest ship breaking yards in the world, where old ships are dismantled.

q: For which product is Sialkot famous?
f: Sialkot is world famous for sports goods, such as footballs, and also for surgical instruments and leather goods.

q: For what is Ziyarat in Balochistan famous?
f: Ziyarat is a hill town famous for the Quaid-e-Azam Residency, where Quaid-e-Azam spent his last days in 1948, and for one of the largest juniper forests in the world.

q: A car travels at 120 km/h and another car travels twice as fast. How far will the second car travel in 30 minutes?
f: The second car's speed is 2 x 120 = 240 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it travels 240 x 1/2 = 120 km.

q: Son is to father as nephew is to what?
f: A son is the child of his father, and a nephew is the child of the brother or sister of an uncle or aunt, so the relation is nephew to uncle.

q: What was the name of the father of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: The father of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was Hazrat Abdullah bin Abdul Muttalib, who died before the Prophet was born.

q: Surah Al-Fatiha is also called by which name?
f: Surah Al-Fatiha is also called Umm-ul-Kitab (Mother of the Book) and Umm-ul-Quran because it sums up the message of the Quran.

q: For which crime was Fatimah bint Aswad (a woman of Banu Makhzum) punished in the time of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Fatimah bint Aswad of Banu Makhzum was found guilty of theft, and the Holy Prophet (PBUH) ordered the punishment for theft. He refused to let rank or family influence the decision.

q: Which day is observed in Pakistan on 5th February every year?
f: Pakistan observes 5 February as Kashmir Solidarity Day to express support for the people of Indian-administered Kashmir.

q: Who was the first Field Marshal of Pakistan?
f: Muhammad Ayub Khan promoted himself to the rank of Field Marshal in 1959.

q: Find x if 3x - 9 = x + 7.
f: Subtract x from both sides: 2x - 9 = 7, so 2x = 16 and x = 8.

q: If 2x/28 = 2/7, find x.
What is the mean of 1, 3, 5 and 6?
f: Sum = 1 + 3 + 5 + 6 = 15; divided by 4 numbers gives 3.75.

q: Which letter comes after M in the English alphabet?
f: The alphabet runs L, M, N, so N follows M.

q: Arrange the letters 'IYTC' to form a meaningful word.
f: Rearranging I, Y, T, C gives the word CITY.

q: Which is the largest fort of Pakistan?
f: Ranikot Fort in Sindh has walls about 26 km long and is often called the largest fort in the world.

q: Between whom was the Ghazwa (Battle) of Badr fought?
o: The Muslims of Madinah and the Quraish of Makkah
The Muslims and the Jews of Khyber
The Muslims and the Byzantine army
The Muslims and the tribe of Thaqif at Taif
f: Badr was fought in 2 AH between the small Muslim army led by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and the much larger army of the Quraish of Makkah.

q: Near which city is the mountain where the Battle of Uhud was fought?
f: The Battle of Uhud was fought at the foot of Mount Uhud, a few kilometres north of Madinah.

q: Which fraction comes next in the series: 3/5, 5/8, 8/12, 12/17, ?
f: Numerators are 3, 5, 8, 12, 17 with differences 2, 3, 4, 5, so the next is 17. Each denominator equals the next numerator, and the denominators 5, 8, 12, 17 continue with 17+6 = 23.

q: What is the currency of France?
f: France uses the euro, which replaced the French franc in 2002.

q: If the first day of a month is Friday, which day will the 17th be?
f: The 15th is 14 days (two full weeks) after the 1st, so it is also a Friday. The 17th is two days later, a Sunday.

q: Change the narration (direct speech) of: He bade farewell to his friends.
o: He said to his friends that good-bye.
He told his friends, "Farewell to you."
f: To bid farewell means to say good-bye, so in direct speech it becomes: He said to his friends, "Good-bye."

q: What is the full form of PIA?
f: PIA stands for Pakistan International Airlines, the national flag carrier of Pakistan.

q: In which city were the Olympic Games named Tokyo 2020 held?
f: The 2020 Summer Olympics were awarded to Tokyo, Japan. Because of COVID-19 they were postponed and held in Tokyo from July to August 2021.

q: How many doors (gates) does the Holy Kaaba have?
f: The Kaaba has a single door, on its north-east wall, about two metres above ground level.

q: Who served as both Governor General and Prime Minister of Pakistan?
f: Khawaja Nazimuddin was Governor General from 1948 to 1951 and then Prime Minister from 1951 to 1953.

q: Who is the President of Germany?
f: Frank-Walter Steinmeier has been the Federal President of Germany since March 2017 and was re-elected in 2022. His second term ends in March 2027.

q: In which Ghazwa was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) wounded?
f: In the Battle of Uhad (3 AH) the Prophet (PBUH) was wounded in the face and his blessed tooth was broken.

q: What is jute commonly known as?
f: Jute is called the golden fibre because of its shiny golden-brown colour and its high value as a cash crop.
