f: Tallinn is the capital and largest city of Estonia, on the Gulf of Finland.

q: What do the five rings of the Olympic flag represent?
o: Five inhabited continents of the world
f: The five interlocked rings stand for the five inhabited continents joined by Olympism: Africa, the Americas, Asia, Europe and Oceania.

q: The Karakoram mountain range lies between Pakistan and which country?
f: The Karakoram range runs along the northern border of Pakistan and separates Gilgit-Baltistan from the Xinjiang region of China.

q: According to the commonly given number in Pakistani textbooks, how many Companions served as Katib-e-Wahi (scribes of revelation) for the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Many Pakistani books state that about 40 Companions wrote down the revelation, including Hazrat Ali, Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Zaid bin Thabit (RA).

q: In which country did noodles originate?
f: The oldest known noodles, about 4000 years old, were found at the Lajia site in China, and China is generally credited with their origin.

q: The Olympic Games take their name from Olympia and Mount Olympus. In which country did the Olympic Games originate?
f: The ancient Olympic Games were held at Olympia in Greece, and Mount Olympus is also in Greece. The modern Olympics are named after these ancient games.

q: The word 'terrorism' was first used in connection with which historical event?
f: The term came into use in the 1790s for the Reign of Terror of the Jacobins in revolutionary France.

q: Who wrote the poems Shikwa and Jawab-e-Shikwa?
f: Allama Muhammad Iqbal wrote Shikwa in 1909 and Jawab-e-Shikwa in 1913.

q: What is the antonym of friendly?
f: Friendly means kind and welcoming; the opposite is hostile, meaning unfriendly or aggressive.

q: To which country did Winston Churchill, the famous leader of World War II, belong?
f: Winston Churchill was British and served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1940 to 1945 and again from 1951 to 1955.

q: The determinant of the transpose of a square matrix A is equal to what?
o: Negative of the determinant of A
The inverse of the determinant of A
f: Interchanging rows and columns does not change the determinant, so det(A transpose) = det(A).

q: The speed of a train is double that of a car. If the car's speed is 60 km/h, what is the speed of the train?
f: Double of 60 km/h is 2 x 60 = 120 km/h.

q: In which year did the Muslims of the subcontinent get the right of separate electorates?
f: Separate electorates were granted to the Muslims by the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.

q: What is the average gestation period of a cow?
f: A cow carries her calf for about 283 days, which is roughly nine months. This is close to the human pregnancy length.

q: Kalimullah (the one who spoke with Allah) is the title of which prophet?
f: Hazrat Musa (AS) spoke directly with Allah on Mount Tur, so he is called Kalimullah.

q: Who has scored the most Test runs for Pakistan?
f: Younis Khan scored 10,099 runs in Tests and is Pakistan's leading Test run scorer. He was the first Pakistani to pass 10,000 Test runs.

q: What does the name Moen jo Daro (Mohenjo-daro) mean?
f: Mohenjo-daro is a Sindhi name meaning Mound of the Dead. It was a major city of the Indus Valley Civilization.

q: Which Islamic Summit of the OIC was held in Pakistan (Lahore) in 1974?
f: The Second Islamic Summit Conference of the OIC was hosted in Lahore in February 1974. The first summit was held in Rabat in 1969.

q: What is the antonym of the word plentiful?
f: Plentiful means more than enough, and its opposite is scarce, meaning in short supply.

q: On which date was the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) established?
f: The SCO was formally established in Shanghai on 15 June 2001 by China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan.

q: What does SCO stand for?
f: SCO stands for Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, a Eurasian political, economic and security grouping.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, how many seats does Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK) have in the Senate of Pakistan?
f: After the 2018 merger of FATA and the 2024 changes, KPK has 23 Senate seats: 14 general, 4 women, 4 technocrat and 1 non-Muslim.

q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word 'utility'?
f: Utility means the quality of being useful or serving a practical purpose. Usefulness is therefore its closest synonym.

q: According to the 2017 census, what was the population of Pakistan?
f: The 6th Population and Housing Census of 2017 counted 207,684,626 people in Pakistan.

q: Who made the first solo non-stop flight across the Atlantic Ocean in 1927?
f: Charles Lindbergh flew the Spirit of St. Louis alone from New York to Paris in May 1927.

q: What is the antonym of the word advance?
f: To advance means to move forward, and its opposite is to retreat or move backward.

q: Who described Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah as the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity?
f: Sarojini Naidu gave Jinnah this title, praising his work for unity at the time of the 1916 Lucknow Pact. Her 1918 book on him is titled Mohomed Ali Jinnah: An Ambassador of Unity.

q: What is the antonym of fertile?
f: Fertile land or a fertile mind produces plenty; the opposite is barren, which produces nothing.

q: What is the antonym of protect?
f: To protect is to keep safe from harm; the opposite is to endanger, to put in harm's way.

q: What is the baby (young one) of a frog called?
f: A young frog hatches from an egg as a tadpole, which lives in water and breathes with gills. It later grows legs and lungs and becomes an adult frog.

q: Bani Israel (Children of Israel) are the descendants of which prophet, whose title was Israel?
f: Israel was the title of Hazrat Yaqub (AS), and his twelve sons formed the twelve tribes of Bani Israel. Hence the people are called Bani Israel.

q: Maputo is the capital of which country?
f: Maputo, formerly Lourenco Marques, is the capital of Mozambique.

q: There are 24 members in a committee and 5 are men. What is the percentage of women?
f: Women = 24 - 5 = 19. Percentage = 19 / 24 x 100 = 79.17 percent.

q: How many nations and territories belong to the Commonwealth Games Federation, which takes part in the Commonwealth Games?
f: The Commonwealth Games Federation has 74 members (nations and territories), including dependent territories that compete under their own flags.

q: Who introduced the system of Basic Democracies in Pakistan?
f: Ayub Khan introduced Basic Democracies through the Basic Democracies Order of 1959. Ordinary citizens elected Basic Democrats from local union councils, who then acted as the electoral college.

q: Diamond is an allotrope of which element?
f: Diamond is made of carbon atoms joined in a rigid tetrahedral crystal structure.

q: What is the antonym of "embrace" in the sense of accepting an idea?
f: To embrace an idea is to accept it eagerly, so its opposite is to reject it.

q: For what is Sadequain famous?
f: Sadequain (1930-1987) was a famous Pakistani painter and calligrapher, known for his Quranic calligraphy and murals.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Fatima (RA) to Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: Hazrat Fatima (RA) was the youngest daughter of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (RA).

q: The Flemish people are found mainly in which country?
f: The Flemish are the Dutch-speaking people of Flanders, the northern region of Belgium.

q: What is the width (length between the posts) of a standard football goal?
f: The two posts of a standard football goal are 24 feet (7.32 m) apart.

q: What is the capital of Iceland?
f: Reykjavik is the capital and largest city of Iceland. It is the northernmost capital of a sovereign state.

q: In which city is the National Library of Pakistan located?
f: The National Library of Pakistan is located in Islamabad on Constitution Avenue in the same complex as other national institutions.

q: In which year was the construction of Pakistan Steel Mills at Karachi started (established)?
f: The foundation of Pakistan Steel Mills was laid in 1973 by Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto with Soviet help.

q: What is the length of the Panama Canal in nautical miles, approximately?
f: The Panama Canal is about 82 km (51 miles) long. Since 1 nautical mile is 1.852 km, this is about 44 nautical miles.

q: Which is generally regarded as the oldest sea port of Pakistan?
f: Karachi Port is the oldest and busiest port of Pakistan; modern port development there began in the 19th century.

q: How many provinces does Pakistan have?
f: Pakistan has four provinces: Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.

q: Which angel is in charge of rain and provision according to Islamic belief?
f: Hazrat Mikail (AS) is the angel entrusted with rain, vegetation and sustenance. Jibrail brings revelation, Israfil blows the Trumpet and Izrail takes souls.

q: Who first suggested the name Pakistan?
f: Chaudhry Rehmat Ali, a Cambridge student, proposed the name Pakistan in his 1933 pamphlet Now or Never.

q: How many main blood groups are there in the ABO system?
f: The main blood groups are A, B, AB and O, which makes four.

q: Who presented the famous Poor Man's (labourer's) Budget in the interim government of British India just before independence?
f: Liaqat Ali Khan, as Finance Member of the interim government, presented a budget that taxed big business and industrialists to relieve the poor. It was called the Poor Man's Budget.

q: To which city did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) migrate in 622 AD?
f: In 622 AD the Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Madinah, which was then called Yathrib.

q: Ahmed is 3 years old and his sister is 4 times his age. What will be the age of his sister after 12 years?
f: Sister's age now is 3 x 4 = 12 years. After 12 years she will be 12 + 12 = 24 years old.

q: What is the antonym of appropriate?
f: Appropriate means suitable for the situation; the opposite is inappropriate or unsuitable.

q: In which region of Pakistan is Attabad Lake located?
f: Attabad Lake lies in the Hunza valley of Gilgit-Baltistan near Karimabad. It was formed by a landslide that blocked the Hunza River.

q: The line y = 7 is parallel to which axis?
o: It is parallel to neither axis
f: The line y = 7 is horizontal, because every point on it has y equal to 7. A horizontal line is parallel to the x-axis.

q: What is the antonym of the word breach?
f: To breach means to break a rule or agreement. Its opposite is compliance or observance, meaning keeping the rule.

q: What is the capital of Zimbabwe?
f: Harare is the capital and largest city of Zimbabwe.

q: In a circle, what is the distance from the center to any point on the circle called?
f: The distance from the center to a point on the circle is the radius.

q: What is the antonym of the word 'comic'?
f: Comic means funny or amusing, while tragic means sad and causing sorrow, so tragic is the opposite.

q: In which year was the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) institution founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan at Aligarh?
f: Sir Syed founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental School at Aligarh on 24 May 1875, which later became MAO College.

q: How many member countries does the Commonwealth of Nations have?
f: The Commonwealth of Nations has 56 member states, the latest being Gabon and Togo who joined in June 2022.

q: In which year was the Communal Award announced by the British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald?
f: The Communal Award was announced on 16 August 1932 and gave separate electorates to Muslims and other minorities.

q: In which city and country is the headquarters of the Asian Development Bank located?
f: The Asian Development Bank was founded in 1966 and has its headquarters in Mandaluyong City, Metro Manila, in the Philippines.

q: In which direction is China located with respect to Pakistan?
f: China lies to the north-east of Pakistan and borders Gilgit-Baltistan through the Khunjerab Pass.

q: Change into indirect speech: Ali said, "I was doing work."
o: Ali said that he was doing work.
Ali said that he had been doing work.
Ali said that I had been doing work.
Ali said that he has been doing work.
f: The reporting verb is in the past, so past continuous 'was doing' changes to past perfect continuous 'had been doing', and 'I' becomes 'he'.

q: A car moves at 60 km/h and a train is twice as fast. How far will the train travel in 30 minutes?
f: Train speed = 2 x 60 = 120 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it covers 120 x 0.5 = 60 km.

q: How many vowels are there in the string EAVNJEGFDUI?
f: The letters are E, A, V, N, J, E, G, F, D, U, I. The vowels are E, A, E, U and I, which makes 5.

q: What does Radd-ul-Fasaad, the name of the Pakistan Army operation launched in 2017, mean?
f: Radd-ul-Fasaad is Arabic and means rejecting or eliminating discord and mischief. The operation was launched in February 2017 to remove the remaining terrorism and strengthen border security.

q: Which of the following is a prime number: 7, 9, 18, 21?
f: 7 has only two factors, 1 and 7. 9 = 3 x 3, 18 = 2 x 9 and 21 = 3 x 7 are composite.

q: Electric current is due to the flow of what?
f: In a metallic conductor, the free electrons drift under a potential difference, and this flow of charge is the electric current.

q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of genuine?
f: Genuine means real and not imitation. Authentic has the same meaning.

q: The Kirthar Hills (Kirthar Range) lie along the border of which two provinces of Pakistan?
f: The Kirthar Range runs north to south and forms the boundary between Sindh and Balochistan. It is the southern part of the Sulaiman-Kirthar system.

q: Who was the mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS)?
f: Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and his wife Hazrat Sarah. He was born when Sarah was very old.

q: On which date is Labour Day (International Workers' Day) observed?
f: Labour Day is observed every year on 1 May, including in Pakistan, where it is a public holiday.

q: What is the antonym of the word lethal?
f: Lethal means able to cause death, so its opposite is harmless. Deadly, fatal and poisonous are synonyms or close in meaning.

q: Which letter comes next in the series: Z, X, U, Q, ?
f: The positions are 26, 24, 21, 17 and the differences are 2, 3, 4, so the next difference is 5. 17 minus 5 is 12, which is L.

q: The Kirthar Range is regarded as the southern extension of which mountain range?
f: The Kirthar Range runs north to south along the border of Sindh and Balochistan and is usually described as the southern extension of the Sulaiman Range.

q: What is the approximate length of the River Nile?
f: The Nile is about 6,650 km (4,130 miles) long. It is traditionally given as the longest river in the world.

q: What is the antonym of the word obsolete?
f: Obsolete means no longer in use or out of date, so its opposite is current or modern.

q: Porto-Novo is the capital of which country?
f: Porto-Novo is the official capital of Benin in West Africa.

q: By which process do green plants prepare their food?
f: Plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide and water to make glucose in photosynthesis.

q: Who founded the political party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)?
f: PTI was founded by Imran Khan in April 1996 in Lahore. He has remained its founder and leader since.

q: Who said that the character of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was the Quran, that is, he was the embodiment of the Quran?
f: When asked about the character of the Prophet (PBUH), Hazrat Aisha (RA) replied that his character was the Quran.

q: Which is the oldest seaport of Pakistan, as given in Pakistani textbooks?
f: Karachi Port is generally given as the oldest and main seaport of Pakistan, with the modern port working from the 19th century. Gwadar and Port Qasim are much newer.

q: Which tennis Grand Slam tournament is still played on grass courts?
f: Wimbledon in London is the only Grand Slam still played on grass.

q: What is the synonym of afraid?
f: Afraid means feeling fear, which is the same as frightened.

q: What is the SI unit of temperature?
f: The kelvin (K) is the base SI unit of temperature. Celsius and Fahrenheit are not SI units.

q: Which type of engine is used in jet aircraft?
f: Jet aircraft are powered by gas turbine engines such as the turbojet and turbofan. They produce thrust by expelling a fast stream of hot gas backwards.

q: Which major event took place in the 10th year of Hijrah (10 AH)?
o: Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjat-ul-Wida) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
f: In 10 AH the Holy Prophet (PBUH) performed his only and last Hajj and delivered the Last Sermon at Arafat. The other events took place in earlier years (Badr 2 AH, Hudaibiya 6 AH, Makkah conquest 8 AH).

q: Which is the second highest mountain in the world?
f: K2, at about 8,611 m, is the second highest mountain in the world after Mount Everest.

q: Out of 500 students, 380 are present. What is the percentage of present students?
f: Percentage present = 380 / 500 x 100 = 76%.

q: Find the next number in the series: 55, 579, 65, 580, ?
f: The series is two interleaved series. The 1st, 3rd and 5th terms go 55, 65, 75 (add 10) and the 2nd and 4th terms go 579, 580, 581 (add 1). The 5th term is 75.

q: In which surah of the Holy Quran is Ruh-ul-Amin (the Trustworthy Spirit, Hazrat Jibreel AS) mentioned?
f: Surah Ash-Shu'ara (26:193) says that the Trustworthy Spirit brought down the Quran upon the heart of the Prophet (PBUH). The Trustworthy Spirit is Hazrat Jibreel (AS).

q: In what amount was the valley of Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh under the Treaty of Amritsar (1846)?
f: By the Treaty of Amritsar the British sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh Dogra for 75 lakh Nanakshahi rupees. This began Dogra rule in Kashmir.

q: What is the antonym of the word amalgamate?
f: To amalgamate means to merge or combine into one. The opposite is to separate.

q: What is the antonym of competent?
f: Competent means having the ability to do something well; the opposite is incompetent, meaning lacking ability.

q: What is the antonym of foremost?
f: Foremost means first in position or importance; the opposite is last (hindmost).

q: What is the antonym of glory?
f: Glory means high honour and fame; the opposite is disgrace or shame.

q: What is the antonym of modern?
f: Modern means belonging to the present or recent time; the opposite is ancient, meaning belonging to the distant past.

q: In which year was the first Asia Cup cricket tournament held?
f: The first Asia Cup was played in Sharjah, UAE, in 1984. India won it.

q: Who was the father of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA)?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was the son of Uthman, who was known as Abu Quhafa. He accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah.

q: What is the base of the common logarithm?
f: The common logarithm uses base 10, so log 100 = 2 because 10 squared is 100.

q: In which part of the world do the Bushmen (San people) live?
f: The Bushmen or San are indigenous hunter-gatherers of southern Africa, living mainly in the Kalahari Desert in Botswana, Namibia and South Africa.

q: Accra is the capital of which country?
f: Accra is the capital and largest city of Ghana, on the Gulf of Guinea.

q: Saint John's is the capital of which country?
f: Saint John's is the capital of Antigua and Barbuda, on the island of Antigua.

q: What is the capital of Greenland?
f: Nuuk is the capital and largest city of Greenland.

q: What is the capital of Norway?
f: Oslo is the capital and largest city of Norway.

q: In which years were the Olympic Games cancelled because of World War II?
f: The 1940 Games (Tokyo/Helsinki) and the 1944 Games (London) were cancelled due to the war.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'clumsy'?
f: A clumsy person moves or handles things in an awkward way and often drops or breaks them.

q: Change the voice: Were clothes dried by the mother?
o: Did the mother dry the clothes?
Was the mother drying the clothes?
Had the mother dried the clothes?
Does the mother dry the clothes?
f: The sentence is passive in the past simple tense, so the active form is 'Did the mother dry the clothes?' with the agent as the subject and the verb in base form after did.

q: Which of the following is the synonym of 'contain'?
f: To contain something means to have it inside or to hold it. 'Hold' is the closest in meaning.

q: Which country owes the largest amount of unpaid dues (arrears) to the United Nations?
f: The United States is the biggest contributor to the UN budget and also has the largest unpaid arrears, over 2 billion US dollars on the regular budget in 2026 plus peacekeeping dues.

q: In which year and at which city was the Lahore Declaration signed between Pakistan and India?
f: The Lahore Declaration was signed on 21 February 1999 in Lahore by Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

q: What is the antonym of the word development?
f: Development means growth or advancement, while retrogression means moving backward or declining.

q: What is the antonym of 'difference'?
f: Difference means the quality of being unlike. Its opposite is similarity, meaning likeness.

q: What is the antonym of 'divided'?
f: Divided means split apart. Its opposite is united.

q: What is the closest meaning of 'disgust'?
f: Disgust is a strong feeling of dislike and sickness at something. Revulsion has the same meaning.

q: What large sea wave is usually caused by an earthquake under the ocean floor?
f: A strong undersea earthquake suddenly moves the sea floor and displaces a huge volume of water, which travels as a tsunami.

q: Who was the first woman elected to the United States Congress?
f: Jeannette Rankin of Montana was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1916 and took her seat in 1917.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to "essential"?
f: Essential means absolutely needed, which is the meaning of necessary.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of the word 'excuse' used as a verb meaning to forgive?
f: To excuse means to forgive or let go without blame. Its opposite is to accuse or blame someone.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of the word 'exhibit'?
f: To exhibit means to show openly. Its opposite is to conceal or hide.

q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word 'exhibit'?
f: To exhibit means to show something publicly. 'Display' has the same meaning.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'exponent'?
f: An exponent is a person who explains or promotes an idea or cause, so an advocate is the closest meaning. An opponent is the opposite.

q: What is the antonym of futility?
f: Futility means uselessness or having no result. Fruitfulness, meaning being productive and useful, is the opposite.

q: Ali is going in the direction of west. He turns left and then turns right. In which direction is Ali going now?
f: Facing west, a left turn points him south. Then a right turn from south points him west again.

q: One hectare is equal to how many square metres?
f: One hectare is a square of 100 m by 100 m, which is 10,000 square metres.

q: What is the approximate length of the Himalaya mountain range?
f: The Himalayas stretch for roughly 2,400 km (about 1,500 miles) from the Indus gorge in the west to the Brahmaputra gorge in the east.

q: Which country was the world's largest arms importer in the latest SIPRI data (2021-25)?
f: SIPRI's March 2026 data for 2021-25 ranks Ukraine first, with about 9.7 percent of global arms imports, followed by India. The USA is a major exporter, not the top importer.

q: At how many points can two distinct lines in a plane intersect each other?
f: Two distinct lines meet in at most one point. If they are parallel they do not meet at all.

q: The followers of Hazrat Isa (AS) are called what?
f: The followers of Hazrat Isa (Jesus) are called Christians. Christianity is the largest religion in the world by followers.

q: Which animal did the people of Thamud kill, despite the warning of Prophet Salih (AS)?
f: The nation of Thamud killed the she-camel sent by Allah as a miracle for Prophet Salih (AS), and was then destroyed.

q: What is the meaning of the word 'kith' (as in 'kith and kin')?
f: Kith means one's friends, neighbours and acquaintances, while kin means blood relatives.

q: What is the antonym of 'kith'?
f: Kith means friends and acquaintances, so its opposite is a stranger.

q: The word 'Pakistan' means the land of what?
f: Pakistan means 'Land of the Pure' (Pak means pure and stan means land).

q: Complete the sentence: The standard of living ____ since his son joined service.
f: The subject standard is singular and since needs the present perfect tense, so has risen is correct.

q: Change into passive voice: How did you manage it?
o: How was it managed by you?
How it was managed by you?
How did it managed by you?
How is it managed by you?
f: A simple past question becomes was or were plus the past participle, so the passive is How was it managed by you?

q: On which date was the first martial law imposed in Pakistan?
f: President Iskander Mirza imposed martial law on 7 October 1958 and General Ayub Khan became the Chief Martial Law Administrator. Ayub Khan then removed Mirza on 27 October 1958.

q: Near which city is Mina, the valley where pilgrims stay during Hajj, located?
f: Mina is a valley about 5 km east of Makkah in Saudi Arabia. Pilgrims stay there and perform the stoning of the Jamarat.

q: Mogadishu is the capital of which country?
f: Mogadishu is the capital and largest city of Somalia, on the Indian Ocean coast.

q: Monrovia is the capital city of which country?
f: Monrovia is the capital and largest city of Liberia in West Africa.

q: Choose the correct word: When morning ___, the murderer was caught.
f: The natural phrase is 'when morning came', meaning when daylight arrived.

q: What is the height of Nanga Parbat, the ninth highest mountain in the world?
f: Nanga Parbat rises to 8,126 metres (26,660 feet) above sea level. It is the ninth highest mountain in the world.

q: What is the antonym of the word obscure?
f: Obscure means unclear or not well known, so its opposite is clear (or evident).

q: What was the old name of Thailand?
f: Thailand was officially known as Siam until 1939, and again briefly from 1945 to 1949. The name was changed to Thailand, meaning land of the free.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to optional?
f: Optional means left to choice and not required. Voluntary has the same sense, while the other options mean required.

q: From which region does the Indus River originate?
f: The Indus rises in the Tibetan plateau near Mount Kailash and Lake Mansarovar. It then flows through Ladakh and Pakistan into the Arabian Sea.

q: The girls are 33 and the boys outnumber the girls by 7. How many boys are there?
f: Boys = girls + 7 = 33 + 7 = 40.

q: 6 is what percentage of 20?
f: Percentage = 6 / 20 x 100 = 30 percent.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, what is the term of office of the President of Pakistan?
f: Article 44 gives the President a term of five years from the day he enters office.

q: What is the synonym of the word plentiful?
f: Plentiful means existing in large quantities, which is the same as abundant.

q: In which province of Pakistan is Gwadar Port located?
f: Gwadar is a coastal city on the Arabian Sea in southwestern Balochistan, and its deep-sea port is there.

q: Who invented the movable-type printing press in Europe around 1440?
f: Johannes Gutenberg of Germany developed the movable-type printing press in the mid-1400s.

q: Rearrange the letters RAPIS to form the name of a famous capital city. Which city is it, and of which country is it the capital?
f: The letters R, A, P, I, S rearrange to make PARIS. Paris is the capital of France.

q: What does RCD stand for in the context of Pakistan, Iran and Turkey?
f: RCD stands for Regional Cooperation for Development, a 1964 economic cooperation body of Pakistan, Iran and Turkey.

q: Which country joined the United Nations in 2002 after its people approved membership in a referendum?
f: Swiss voters approved UN membership in a referendum in March 2002, and Switzerland became the 190th member in September 2002.

q: Which Muslim League leader responded to the Nehru Report (1928) with his famous Fourteen Points in 1929?
f: The Nehru Report rejected separate electorates and Muslim demands, so Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points in March 1929 as the Muslim reply.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to seize?
f: To seize means to take hold of something suddenly and by force, which is to grab.

q: Who founded the Scientific Society in the subcontinent in 1864?
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Scientific Society at Ghazipur in 1864 to translate Western scientific works into Urdu. It later moved to Aligarh.

q: For how many years did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) live in Madina after the Hijrat?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) migrated to Madina in 622 CE and stayed there until his death in 632 CE, about ten years. He migrated at age 53 and passed away at 63.

q: Approximately how many princely states existed in British India at the time of the partition in 1947?
f: At partition about 562 princely states were ruled by local rulers under British paramountcy, and each was to join India or Pakistan.

q: The Holy Quran as revealed by Allah consists of which of the following?
f: The Quran itself is the Arabic text revealed by Allah. Translations and tafseer are human explanations and are not part of the Quran.

q: Choose the correct direct speech of: The teacher said that he could not meet all of his students.
o: The teacher said, "I cannot meet all of my students."
The teacher said, "He could not meet all of his students."
The teacher said, "I could not meet all of your students."
The teacher said, "I did not meet all of my students."
f: In direct speech the past form could changes back to can and he and his change to I and my.

q: The Dragon's Mouth (Bocas del Dragon) strait lies between Trinidad and which country?
f: The Dragon's Mouth is a strait between the north-west tip of Trinidad and the Paria Peninsula of Venezuela. It links the Gulf of Paria with the Atlantic Ocean.

q: Which of the following are the three types of blood cells?
o: Red cells, white cells and platelets
Red cells, white cells and haemoglobin
f: Blood contains red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets. Plasma is the liquid part, not a cell.

q: Which of the following is a fard (obligatory) act of wudu according to the Hanafi school?
o: Washing the hands up to the wrists
f: The four faraiz of wudu are washing the face, washing both arms up to the elbows, wiping a quarter of the head, and washing both feet up to the ankles. Gargling and rinsing the nose are sunnah.

q: Who is the author of the book 'Jinnah of Pakistan'?
f: Stanley Wolpert, an American historian, wrote 'Jinnah of Pakistan' (1984).

q: What is 2 + 2?
f: Adding 2 and 2 gives 4.

q: Out of 1500 students, 1200 are present. How many students are absent?
f: Absent students = 1500 - 1200 = 300.

q: Who was the first President under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan, taking office in August 1973?
f: Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto became Prime Minister when the 1973 Constitution came into force on 14 August 1973. Fazal Ilahi Chaudhry became the President at that time.

q: Which country became independent in 1994, ending the last United Nations trusteeship?
f: Palau gained independence on 1 October 1994 and became the last UN Trust Territory to end its trusteeship.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 24th be?
f: From the 2nd to the 24th is 22 days. 22 = 3 weeks and 1 extra days, so count 1 days forward from Friday to reach Saturday.

q: Which country hosted the largest number of refugees in 2017?
f: UNHCR reported that Turkey hosted about 3.5 million refugees at the end of 2017, the largest number worldwide.

q: Who was the 7th President of the United States?
f: Andrew Jackson served as the 7th US President from 1829 to 1837, after John Quincy Adams.

q: Which is the 6th most populous country in the world?
f: The ranking is India, China, USA, Indonesia, Pakistan and then Nigeria in sixth place.

q: If a helicopter uses 50 litres of fuel to travel 200 km, how many litres will it use to travel 350 km?
f: Fuel per km = 50 / 200 = 0.25 litre. For 350 km: 350 x 0.25 = 87.5 litres.

q: Out of 400 students, 360 are present. What is the percentage of present students?
f: Percentage present = 360 / 400 x 100 = 90%. The absent students are 40, which is 10%.

q: A helicopter uses 80 gallons of fuel to fly 320 km. How many gallons will it need to fly 800 km?
f: Fuel per km is 80 / 320 = 0.25 gallon. For 800 km the helicopter needs 800 x 0.25 = 200 gallons.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 1350 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
f: Absent students = 1500 - 1350 = 150. Percentage absent = 150 / 1500 x 100 = 10 percent.

q: In a class of 500 students, 150 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
f: Absent students = 500 - 150 = 350. Percentage absent = 350 / 500 x 100 = 70 percent.

q: On which date is Pakistan Air Force Day celebrated?
f: PAF Day is celebrated on 7 September to honour the PAF's performance in the 1965 war. On that day in 1965 PAF pilots, including M. M. Alam, shot down several Indian aircraft.

q: In which year did the United States declare its independence?
f: The Declaration of Independence was adopted on 4 July 1776. That is why 4 July is celebrated as American Independence Day.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word annihilate?
f: To annihilate is to destroy something utterly so that nothing remains. Its closest meaning is to destroy completely.

q: What is the antonym of the word sumptuous?
f: Sumptuous means grand and expensive-looking, so its opposite is meagre or poor. Lavish, splendid and rich are synonyms.

q: What is the antonym of the word Almighty?
f: Almighty means having unlimited power. Its opposite is powerless or weak.

q: What is the antonym of coma?
f: A coma is a state of deep unconsciousness, so its opposite is consciousness (being awake and aware).

q: What is the antonym of contiguous?
f: Contiguous means sharing a common border or touching; the opposite is separate or detached.

q: What is the antonym of divide?
f: Divide means to split into parts; the opposite is unite, to join together.

q: What is the antonym of inaccuracy?
f: Inaccuracy means lack of correctness; the opposite is precision or accuracy.

q: What is the antonym of isolation?
f: Isolation means being alone and apart from others; the opposite is companionship or togetherness.

q: What is the antonym of mild?
f: Mild means gentle or not severe; the opposite is harsh, meaning severe or rough.

q: What is the antonym of normally?
f: Normally means in the usual way; the opposite is abnormally, meaning in an unusual way.

q: What is the antonym of prosperous?
f: Prosperous means rich and successful; the opposite is impoverished, meaning poor.

q: What is the antonym of retrieve?
f: To retrieve is to get something back; the opposite is to lose it.

q: What is the antonym of timely?
f: Timely means happening at the right moment; the opposite is untimely, happening at the wrong moment.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of apposite?
f: Apposite means very appropriate or relevant to the matter; the opposite is irrelevant or inapt.

q: What is the synonym (closest meaning) of appropriate?
f: Appropriate means right for a particular situation, which is the meaning of suitable.

q: Which Surah of the Holy Quran was revealed immediately after Surah An-Naml (the Ant) in the commonly given order of revelation?
f: In the commonly used (Egyptian) order of revelation, Surah An-Naml is the 48th Surah revealed and Surah Al-Qasas follows it.

q: Who is the custodian of the House in the National Assembly of Pakistan?
f: The Speaker presides over the sessions of the National Assembly and is regarded as the custodian of the House. He maintains order and decides points of procedure.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)?
f: The IAEA has its headquarters in Vienna, Austria. It promotes peaceful use of nuclear energy.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah pass the matriculation examination of Bombay University?
f: Most sources state that Jinnah passed the Bombay University matriculation examination at the age of 16 in 1892. He then left for England in early 1893.

q: On which date did the Pakistan Army launch Operation Zarb-e-Azb in North Waziristan?
f: Operation Zarb-e-Azb against militants in North Waziristan began on 15 June 2014. It followed the attack on Karachi airport and the failure of peace talks.

q: How many Muslims were martyred in the Battle of Badr?
f: Fourteen Muslims were martyred at Badr, six from the Muhajirun and eight from the Ansar. About 70 of the Quraish were killed.

q: Bait-ul-Maqdas (Bait-ul-Muqaddas), the first qibla of the Muslims, is also known by which name?
f: Bait-ul-Maqdas in Jerusalem is the site of Masjid-e-Aqsa (Al-Aqsa Mosque). The city itself is also called Al-Quds.

q: A barometer is used to measure what?
f: A barometer measures the pressure of the atmosphere. A falling reading usually warns of bad weather.

q: Basic Democracies of Ayub Khan were given constitutional status by which constitution?
f: The 1962 Constitution made the 80,000 Basic Democrats the electoral college that elected the President and the assemblies.

q: In which year was the Berlin Wall built?
f: East Germany began building the Berlin Wall on 13 August 1961 to stop people leaving for West Berlin.

q: How many surahs of the Quran begin with Bismillah-ir-Rahman-ir-Rahim?
f: There are 114 surahs and only Surah At-Tawbah does not begin with Bismillah, so 113 do.

q: Why do we boil water before drinking it?
f: Boiling kills harmful bacteria and other germs that cause waterborne diseases.

q: In which of Quaid-e-Azam's Fourteen Points was the separation of Sindh from the Bombay Presidency demanded?
f: Point 9 of the Quaid's Fourteen Points (1929) demanded that Sindh be separated from the Bombay Presidency.

q: Change the voice of the sentence: I bought a book.
o: A book was bought by me.
A book is bought by me.
A book has been bought by me.
A book had been bought by me.
f: The sentence is in the simple past tense, so the passive uses was plus the past participle: A book was bought by me. The object becomes the subject.

q: By whom, and for how much money, was Kashmir bought under the Treaty of Amritsar in 1846?
o: Maharaja Gulab Singh for 75 lakh Nanak Shahi rupees
Maharaja Ranjit Singh for 50 lakh rupees
Maharaja Hari Singh for 75 lakh rupees
Maharaja Gulab Singh for 25 lakh rupees
f: After the First Anglo-Sikh War the British sold the valley of Kashmir to Gulab Singh Dogra for 75 lakh Nanak Shahi rupees under the Treaty of Amritsar.

q: Who was the Prime Minister of Britain at the time of the partition of India in 1947?
f: Clement Attlee of the Labour Party was British Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951 and passed the Indian Independence Act 1947.

q: What does BRT stand for?
f: BRT stands for Bus Rapid Transit, a bus system running on dedicated lanes. Peshawar's BRT is called Zu Peshawar.

q: Gautama Buddha, the founder of Buddhism, belonged to which country?
f: Gautama Buddha was born at Lumbini, which lies in present-day Nepal. He later attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya in India.

q: What is the approximate gestation period of a buffalo?
f: A buffalo carries its calf for about 10 months, which is roughly 305 to 320 days.

q: In which city does the Green Line bus (BRT) service run?
f: The Green Line is a Bus Rapid Transit service in Karachi that runs from Surjani Town toward Numaish.

q: San Jose is the capital of which country?
f: San Jose is the capital and largest city of Costa Rica in Central America.

q: What is the capital of Algeria?
f: Algiers is the capital and largest city of Algeria.

q: What is the capital of Ethiopia?
f: Addis Ababa is the capital of Ethiopia.

q: What is the capital of Fiji?
f: Suva is the capital and largest city of Fiji, on Viti Levu island.

q: What is the capital of Finland?
f: Helsinki is the capital and largest city of Finland.

q: What is the capital of Kenya?
f: Nairobi is the capital and largest city of Kenya.

q: What are the members of a Cartesian plane called?
f: Every point of a Cartesian plane is written as an ordered pair (x, y) of coordinates.

q: Change into passive voice: Dogs always chase the cats.
o: The cats are always chased by dogs.
The cats were always chased by dogs.
The cats are always being chased by dogs.
The cats always chase the dogs.
f: The sentence is present simple, so the passive is 'am/is/are + past participle': the cats are always chased by dogs.

q: What causes earthquakes, including those under the ocean?
f: Earthquakes occur when tectonic plates slip or collide and release energy along faults, on land or the sea floor.

q: What is the center of a circle called?
o: Point from which all boundary points are equidistant
f: The center is the fixed point inside a circle that is at the same distance from every point on the circle.

q: What is the centre of a circle?
o: A fixed point equidistant from every point on the circle
The longest chord of the circle
f: The centre is the single fixed point inside a circle that is at the same distance from all points on the circumference. A circle has exactly one centre.

q: What was the Chauri Chaura incident of 1922?
o: A mob burned a police station and killed policemen, after which Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement
A massacre of unarmed people at a garden in Amritsar
A mutiny of Indian soldiers in Meerut
A salt march to the sea
f: On 4 February 1922 at Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh a crowd set fire to a police station, killing about 22 policemen. Gandhi then called off the Non-Cooperation Movement.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'stagnancy'?
f: Stagnancy is the state of not moving, flowing or developing, so it means inactivity.

q: What is a composite number?
o: A number with exactly two factors
A positive integer greater than 1 with more than two factors
A number that is not divisible by 2
A number with only one factor
f: A composite number has at least one factor other than 1 and itself, so it has more than two factors. Examples are 4, 6, 8 and 9.

q: What is the meaning of 'contentment'?
o: Satisfaction and happiness with what one has
f: Contentment is a state of being happy and satisfied with what one has.

q: In which year AD was Khyber conquered by the Muslims?
f: The Battle of Khyber took place in Muharram 7 AH, which corresponds to about 628 AD.

q: Sahih Muslim is regarded as the most authentic book of hadith after which book?
f: Scholars rank Sahih Bukhari first and Sahih Muslim second in authenticity among the hadith collections.

q: What is the official currency of Iran?
f: The official currency of Iran is the Iranian rial. Ordinary people often quote prices in toman, which equals 10 rials.

q: Which river is the deepest river in the world?
f: The Congo River in Africa has been measured at depths of more than 220 metres, making it the deepest known river.

q: Who delivered the famous Allahabad Address of 1930 in which a separate Muslim state in the north-west of India was envisioned?
f: Allama Iqbal delivered this address as President of the All India Muslim League session at Allahabad in December 1930.

q: Which of the following is closest in meaning to the word development?
f: Development means gradual growth or advancement, so improvement is the closest meaning.

q: What is a synonym of 'difficult'?
f: Difficult means needing much effort. Hard has the same meaning.

q: Which of the following is a division of Punjab?
f: Sahiwal is one of the divisions of Punjab. Hyderabad is in Sindh, Quetta in Balochistan and Peshawar in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: How many minutes are there in 10 degrees in the DMS (degrees, minutes, seconds) system?
f: One degree is 60 minutes, so 10 degrees = 10 x 60 = 600 minutes.

q: Pakistan's economy has traditionally been described as predominantly what kind of economy?
f: Pakistani textbooks describe the country as agricultural because agriculture supports most of the rural population and provides raw material to industry.

q: By whom is the Prime Minister of Pakistan elected under the 1973 Constitution?
f: The Prime Minister is elected by the members of the National Assembly, usually the leader who has a majority there.

q: The algebraic expression 4a - 5b - 6 is what kind of expression?
f: Each variable has power 1, so the degree of the expression is 1 and it is a linear expression.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'eventually'?
f: 'Eventually' means at last, after a long time or a series of events. 'Ultimately' carries the same sense.

q: What are all the factors of 10?
f: The factors of a number are the numbers that divide it exactly. 10 divided by 1, 2, 5 and 10 leaves no remainder.

q: A train's speed is twice that of a car. If the car covers 60 km in 60 minutes, how far does the train cover in the same time?
f: The car's speed is 60 km in 1 hour = 60 km/h. The train moves at twice this speed, 120 km/h, so it covers 120 km in 60 minutes.

q: A train's speed is twice that of a car, and the train covers 120 km in 1 hour. How far does the car travel in 15 minutes?
f: The train's speed is 120 km/h, so the car's speed is 120 / 2 = 60 km/h. In 15 minutes (a quarter of an hour) the car covers 60 / 4 = 15 km.

q: Which is the fastest animal on earth?
f: The peregrine falcon reaches over 320 km/h in its hunting dive, which is faster than any other animal. The cheetah is the fastest land animal at about 110 km/h.

q: Hazrat Fatima (RA) was the wife of whom?
f: Hazrat Fatima (RA) married Hazrat Ali (RA) in 2 AH.

q: Who made the first successful powered aeroplane flight in 1903?
f: Orville and Wilbur Wright flew the first powered, controlled aeroplane at Kitty Hawk, USA, on 17 December 1903.

q: What is the formula of the discriminant of the quadratic equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0?
f: The discriminant is D = b^2 - 4ac, the expression under the square root in the quadratic formula. It decides the nature of the roots.

q: What is the meaning of futility?
f: Futility is the quality of having no useful result, so it means pointlessness or uselessness.

q: Which general imposed the NRO (National Reconciliation Ordinance) in Pakistan in 2007?
f: The National Reconciliation Ordinance was issued by President General Pervez Musharraf in October 2007. It gave amnesty in many corruption cases.

q: A class has 1500 students and 1200 of them are boys. What is the percentage of girls?
f: Girls = 1500 - 1200 = 300. Percentage = 300 / 1500 x 100 = 20 percent.

q: What is the height of a standard football goal (inside the posts, from ground to crossbar)?
f: The crossbar of a standard football goal is 8 feet (2.44 m) above the ground.

q: Who is the current Governor of Sindh (as of October 2026)?
f: Nehal Hashmi of the PML-N took oath as Governor of Sindh on 13 March 2026.

q: Who said that the life of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is the best example?
f: Allah says in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:21) that the Messenger of Allah is an excellent example for those who hope in Allah.

q: Which is the greatest number among 5, 4, 6, 9, 7 and 3?
f: Comparing all the numbers, 9 is larger than 5, 4, 6, 7 and 3.

q: After the death of which caliph was the compiled copy of the Quran passed to Hazrat Hafsa (RA) for safekeeping?
f: The copy compiled under Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) passed to Hazrat Umar (RA), and after his death it was kept with his daughter Hazrat Hafsa (RA).

q: What is the HCF of 16 and 40?
f: 16 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 and 40 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 5, so the common part is 2 x 2 x 2 = 8.

q: Fill in the blank: Ali ____ himself against a horde of ruffians.
f: The idiom is to pit oneself against someone, meaning to compete or struggle against them. The past tense is pitted.

q: Who wrote the book Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind (Causes of the Indian Revolt)?
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote it in 1859 to explain the causes of the War of Independence of 1857 and defend Muslims against blame.

q: Who was Hinda (Hind bint Utba) who accepted Islam?
f: Hinda was the wife of Abu Sufyan and the mother of Hazrat Muawiyah (RA). She accepted Islam after the Conquest of Makkah.

q: Which is the higher mountain range, the Hindu Kush or the Himalaya?
f: The Himalaya is higher: Mount Everest is 8,849 m while the Hindu Kush peak Tirich Mir is 7,708 m.

q: Which country hosted the first Asian Games in 1951?
f: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, in 1951.

q: Which city hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 2012?
f: The 2012 Summer Olympics were held in London, United Kingdom.

q: Which country hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896?
f: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.

q: What are the real and imaginary parts of the complex number 4 + 9i?
f: In a + bi, a is the real part and b is the imaginary part. So the real part is 4 and the imaginary part is 9.

q: Who is generally credited as a co-founder of Twitter (now X) and its first chief executive?
f: Twitter was founded in 2006 by Jack Dorsey, Noah Glass, Biz Stone and Evan Williams. Jack Dorsey is the best known and was its first CEO.

q: What is the capital of Ireland?
f: Dublin is the capital and largest city of the Republic of Ireland. It lies on the east coast.

q: In which year did the USSR veto a UN Security Council resolution on Kashmir, supporting India?
f: On 22 June 1962 the Soviet Union vetoed a Security Council resolution on Kashmir backed by Pakistan. This was one of several Soviet vetoes on the issue.

q: Where is Jabal Tariq (Mount of Tariq) located?
f: Jabal Tariq is the Arabic name from which the word Gibraltar comes. It is named after Tariq bin Ziyad, who landed there in 711 AD.

q: Which Muslim community of Kerala (Malabar coast), India, is well known?
f: The Moplah (Mappila) are the Muslim community of the Malabar coast of Kerala, descended from Arab traders and local converts.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the Khewra salt mine located?
f: The Khewra salt mine lies in the Salt Range near Khewra in Jhelum district, in northern Punjab.

q: Amir Khusro is regarded as the first poet of which language (in its early form)?
f: Amir Khusro (1253-1325) composed verse in Hindavi, the early form of Urdu, and is called its first poet.

q: In which valley is Ansoo Lake located?
f: Ansoo (Lake Ansoo) is a tear-shaped high-altitude lake in the Kaghan Valley of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite launched into space, was launched in which year?
f: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 on 4 October 1957, which started the space age.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to lethal?
f: Lethal means capable of causing death, which is the same as deadly.

q: Which is the last heavenly (divine) book?
f: The Holy Quran was revealed to the last Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and is the final divine book. No book will come after it.

q: In which unit is latitude measured?
f: Latitude is the angular distance north or south of the Equator, so it is measured in degrees.

q: How does the word MTVWVTM look when reflected in a mirror placed beside it (lateral reflection)?
f: The letters M, T, V and W are each symmetrical about a vertical line, and the word reads the same from both ends. So its mirror image is identical.

q: Who discovered X-rays and developed the X-ray machine?
f: Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen discovered X-rays in 1895 in Germany.

q: Fill in the blank: He lives ___ United States.
f: The preposition in is used with the name of a country or large place where someone lives.

q: In which region of Pakistan is the Mangla Dam located?
f: Mangla Dam is on the Jhelum River near Mirpur in Azad Jammu and Kashmir.

q: Which word is the antonym (opposite) of marginal in the sense of minor or slight?
f: Marginal means small or of little importance. The opposite is significant, meaning large or important.

q: What is a Field Marshal?
o: The highest rank in an army
A rank in the navy only
A police officer in charge of a district
f: Field Marshal is the highest (five-star) rank in the army of many countries. It is often given as an honour and is rarely awarded.

q: What is the median of 36 and 18?
f: For two values the median is their average: (18 + 36) / 2 = 54 / 2 = 27.

q: Which prophet (AS) was granted the ability by Allah to mould (soften) iron?
f: The Quran says that Allah made iron soft for Hazrat Dawud (AS) so he could make armour (Surah Saba).

q: According to Greek mythology, who flew too close to the sun with wings of wax and fell into the sea?
f: Icarus ignored his father's warning, flew too close to the sun, the wax melted and he fell.

q: Which number comes next: 12, 55, 14, 65, 16, 75, ?
f: There are two interleaved series: 12, 14, 16 (add 2) and 55, 65, 75 (add 10). The term after 75 belongs to the first series, so it is 16 + 2 = 18.

q: Which number comes next: 55, 65, 75, ?
f: Each number increases by 10, so 75 + 10 = 85.

q: On whom is Hajj obligatory (farz)?
o: Every sane, adult Muslim who has the means to travel and afford it
f: Hajj is farz once in a lifetime on a sane, adult (baligh) Muslim who is physically and financially able (istita'at) to make the journey.

q: Which of the following is a farz (obligatory act) of Hajj?
f: The faraiz of Hajj in the Hanafi school are Ihram, Wuquf-e-Arafah and Tawaf-e-Ziyarah. Stoning and shaving are wajib, not farz.

q: Which word is a synonym of pacify?
f: To pacify means to bring peace or to calm someone down. Calm has the same meaning.

q: In which year was the second constitution of Pakistan enforced?
f: Pakistan's first constitution came in 1956 and was abrogated in 1958. The second constitution, given by Ayub Khan, was enforced in 1962.

q: What is a quarter of 10 percent of 12?
f: 10 percent of 12 = 1.2. A quarter of 1.2 = 0.3.

q: Which of the following lists the five pillars of Islam correctly?
f: The five pillars are the declaration of faith (Kalima/Shahada), prayer (Salah), fasting (Sawm), charity (Zakat) and pilgrimage (Hajj).

q: Convert to passive voice: The pilot landed the plane safely.
o: The plane is landed safely by the pilot.
The plane was landed safely by the pilot.
The plane had landed safely by the pilot.
The plane was landing safely by the pilot.
f: The sentence is in the simple past tense, so the passive uses was or were plus the past participle. The object plane becomes the subject: The plane was landed safely by the pilot.

q: Where were the first Asian Games held in 1951?
f: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, in 1951.

q: Sadequain, a famous name in Pakistani art, is known as a
f: Sadequain (1930-1987) was a renowned Pakistani painter and calligrapher, known especially for his calligraphy of Quranic verses and verses of Allama Iqbal and Ghalib.

q: What is the approximate population of the Philippines in 2026?
f: Current estimates put the population of the Philippines at about 118 million in 2026, which ranks it around 14th in the world.

q: How many Nobel Prizes has Pakistan won?
f: Pakistan has two Nobel laureates: Dr Abdus Salam (Physics, 1979) and Malala Yousafzai (Peace, 2014).

q: In which year was the One Unit scheme established in West Pakistan?
f: The provinces of West Pakistan were merged into one unit in 1955.

q: Past is to present as preceding is to:
f: Past and present are opposites, and the opposite of preceding is following.

q: Who is the chairman of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) as of 2026?
f: Barrister Gohar Ali Khan was elected PTI chairman unopposed in December 2023 as a temporary arrangement. He is still reported as chairman in 2026.

q: What is a quarter of 1/20?
Overexposure to ultraviolet rays from the sun is most harmful to which part of the human body?
f: Ultraviolet rays damage skin cells and the eyes, causing sunburn, skin cancer and cataracts.

q: Which city or territory of Pakistan has the highest literacy rate according to the 2023 census?
f: The 2023 census showed Islamabad Capital Territory with the highest literacy rate, about 84 percent, ahead of all provinces.

q: Which is the largest religion in the world by number of followers?
f: Christianity has about 2.4 billion followers, more than any other religion.

q: What was the Lahore Resolution of 23 March 1940?
o: A demand for separate independent states for the Muslims of India
A demand for a united India
A plan to boycott the elections of 1946
f: At the Lahore session of the All-India Muslim League, the resolution demanded that Muslim-majority areas in the north-west and east be grouped into independent states.

q: What is the cube root of 8?
f: 2 x 2 x 2 = 8, so the cube root of 8 is 2.

q: What is the cube root of 92, approximately?
f: 4 cubed is 64 and 5 cubed is 125, so the cube root of 92 lies between 4 and 5. Since 4.5 cubed is 91.1, the value is about 4.5.

q: For how many years did Hazrat Usman (RA) rule as Caliph?
f: Hazrat Usman (RA) was Caliph from 23 AH to 35 AH, which is about 12 years.

q: What is the presiding officer who runs the sessions of the National Assembly of Pakistan called?
f: The National Assembly is presided over and run by its Speaker, who is elected by its members. In his absence the Deputy Speaker presides.

q: Famous footballer Mohamed Salah belongs to which country?
f: Mohamed Salah was born in Nagrig, Egypt, and captains the Egyptian national team.

q: Which is the busiest seaport in the world (by container traffic)?
f: Shanghai has been the world's busiest container port for 16 years in a row, handling about 55 million TEU in 2025. Singapore is second.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word security?
f: Security means the state of being protected from danger, which is safety.

q: For how many terms can the Secretary-General of the United Nations normally serve?
o: Two terms of five years each
Three terms of four years each
f: The UN Charter sets no limit, but by established practice the Secretary-General serves a five-year term that can be renewed once, so two terms.

q: Who started the Pan-Islamism movement in the Muslim world?
f: Syed Jamaluddin Afghani called for the unity of all Muslims against European domination and is regarded as the founder of the Pan-Islamic movement.

q: In which year was the Simla Conference between the British, the Congress and the Muslim League held?
f: The Simla Conference was convened by Viceroy Lord Wavell in 1945 to discuss the Wavell Plan for an interim government.

q: On which date was the Simla Conference of 1945 held (it began on this date)?
f: Lord Wavell opened the Simla Conference on 25 June 1945 and it ended on 14 July 1945 without agreement.

q: On which date was the Simla (Shimla) Agreement between Pakistan and India signed?
f: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi signed the Simla Agreement on 2 July 1972 after the 1971 war.

q: If one side of a square is 6 cm, what is its perimeter?
f: Perimeter of a square = 4 x side = 4 x 6 = 24 cm.

q: What is the value of sin 190 degrees?
f: 190 degrees lies in the third quadrant where sine is negative, so sin 190 = -sin 10 = -0.174.

q: Who is the Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan as of 2026?
f: Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir has been Chief of Army Staff since November 2022 and was also named Chief of Defence Forces in December 2025.

q: What does WHO stand for?
f: WHO is the World Health Organization, a United Nations agency for international public health.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word sublime?
f: Sublime means of very high excellence or grandeur, so majestic is closest.

q: Which vitamin do we get from sunlight?
f: Sunlight on the skin helps the body make vitamin D.

q: What is the synonym of stagnant?
f: Stagnant describes water or conditions that are still and not moving or developing.

q: What is the synonym of might?
f: As a noun, might means great strength or power.

q: What is the synonym of synopsis?
f: A synopsis is a brief summary of a book, film or plot.

q: In which Hijri month and year did the Ghazwa of Tabuk take place?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) marched towards Tabuk in Rajab of 9 AH, which is about October 630 CE.

q: Who is the current T20I captain of the Pakistan cricket team (October 2026)?
f: Pakistan named Sahibzada Farhan T20I captain in October 2026, ahead of the home series against Sri Lanka.

q: Which bowler of the Pakistan women's team became the first Pakistani player to take 100 wickets in T20 internationals?
f: Nida Dar became the first Pakistan player, male or female, to reach 100 T20I wickets in July 2021.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the Thar desert mainly located?
f: The Pakistani part of the Thar desert lies in the south-east of Sindh, mainly in Tharparkar district.

q: What is the order of the transpose of a matrix of order m x n?
f: The transpose is obtained by interchanging rows and columns, so an m x n matrix becomes n x m.

q: Who conquered Sindh during the Umayyad period?
f: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 711-712 AD under the Umayyad governor Hajjaj bin Yusuf and Caliph Walid I.

q: In set theory, the universal set is what of every set under consideration?
f: The universal set contains all the elements of the sets under discussion, so every set is a subset of it and it is a superset of each.

q: What is the complement of the universal set?
f: The complement of U contains the elements not in U, and there are none, so it is the empty set.

q: What is the approximate value of pi?
f: Pi is the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter, approximately 3.14159. It is commonly written as 3.14 or 22/7.

q: Vehicle is to road as ship is to ___ ?
f: A vehicle travels on a road, and a ship travels on the sea. The analogy links a vehicle or vessel with the surface it moves on.

q: Which animal uses sound waves (echolocation) to find its way, like eyes?
f: Bats emit high-frequency ultrasonic sounds and use the returning echoes to locate objects and prey in the dark. This is called echolocation.

q: What does the white band in the flag of Pakistan represent?
f: The white stripe of the flag stands for the religious minorities of Pakistan, while the green stands for the Muslim majority.

q: How many wives did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) have at the time of his death, according to the commonly taught account?
f: At the time of his death the Holy Prophet (PBUH) had 9 wives living. In total he married 11 wives; Hazrat Khadija (RA) and Hazrat Zainab bint Khuzaima (RA) had died before him.

q: In the sentence 'Wow! This is my book', what part of speech is 'Wow'?
f: 'Wow' expresses a sudden feeling of surprise, and a word that does this is an interjection.

q: What is the capital of New Zealand?
f: Wellington is the capital of New Zealand, although Auckland is its largest city.

What is 1/3 of 20?
f: One third of 20 is 20 divided by 3, which is 20/3 or about 6.67.

q: What is 2 + 1/3?
What is 1/10 of 1/5 of 120?
What is one third of 25% of 120?
f: 25% of 120 = 30. One third of 30 = 10.

If the 13th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 27th day of that month be?
f: From the 13th to the 27th is 14 days, which is exactly two weeks. So the day is the same, Sunday.

q: If the 23rd of a month falls on Friday, what day will the 14th of that month be?
f: From the 14th to the 23rd is 9 days. 9 = 7 + 2, so the 14th is 2 days before Friday, which is Wednesday.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 14th be?
f: From the 3rd to the 14th is 11 days. 11 = 7 + 4, so move 4 days ahead of Friday: Saturday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday. The 14th is Tuesday.

q: If the 29th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 15th be?
f: From the 15th to the 29th is 14 days, exactly two weeks, so both are Monday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 15th be?
f: From the 2nd to the 15th is 13 days. 13 = 7 + 6, so move 6 days ahead of Friday, which gives Thursday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 17th be?
f: From the 4th to the 17th is 13 days. 13 = 7 + 6, so the 17th is 6 days after Monday, which is Sunday.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day is the 17th of the month?
f: From the 1st to the 17th is 16 days. 16 = 14 + 2, so the 17th is 2 days after Monday, which is Wednesday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 17th be?
f: From the 4th to the 17th is 13 days. 13 = 7 + 6, so the 17th is 6 days after Sunday, which is Saturday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 18th of the month be?
f: From the 2nd to the 18th is 16 days. 16 = 14 + 2, so the 18th is 2 days after Friday, which is Sunday.

q: What is one tenth of 10% of 140?
f: 10% of 140 = 14. One tenth of 14 = 1.4.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 1340 are present. What is the percentage of absent students (to two decimal places)?
f: Absent students = 1500 - 1340 = 160. Percentage = 160 / 1500 x 100 = 10.67%.

q: Out of 2000 students, 1600 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
The population of a city was 1600 in 1960 and it doubles every year. What will the population be in 1967?
f: From 1960 to 1967 is 7 years, so the population doubles 7 times: 1600 x 2^7 = 1600 x 128 = 204800.

q: A car runs at a speed of 180 km/h. How much distance does it travel in 20 minutes?
f: 20 minutes = 1/3 hour. Distance = 180 x 1/3 = 60 km.

q: According to the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan, what was the minimum age to be elected President?
f: The 1962 Constitution required the President to be a Muslim and at least 35 years old.

q: Ali was born in 1974 and Azhar was born in 1970. Bilal is 2 years younger than Azhar. In which year was Bilal born?
f: Younger by 2 years means born 2 years later, so Bilal was born in 1970 + 2 = 1972.

q: What position did Pakistan achieve in the 1999 Cricket World Cup?
f: Pakistan reached the final of the 1999 World Cup in England but lost to Australia at Lord's.

q: Akbar was born in 1970 and Ammar in 1977. Bilal is older than Ammar. Who is the youngest of the three?
f: Bilal is older than Ammar, so Ammar is younger than Bilal. Ammar (1977) is also younger than Akbar (1970), so Ammar is the youngest.

q: What is 2% of 200?
If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 21st be?
f: From the 2nd to the 21st is 19 days. 19 = 2 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Sunday to reach Friday.

q: If the 8th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 21st be?
f: From the 8th to the 21st is 13 days. 13 = 1 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Tuesday to reach Monday.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Friday, what day will the 21st be?
f: From the 1st to the 21st is 20 days. 20 = 2 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Friday to reach Thursday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 23rd be?
f: From the 4th to the 23rd is 19 days. 19 = 2 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Sunday to reach Friday.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 23rd be?
f: From the 3rd to the 23rd is 20 days. 20 = 2 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Monday to reach Sunday.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 24th be?
f: From the 1st to the 24th is 23 days. 23 = 3 weeks and 2 extra days, so count 2 days forward from Monday to reach Wednesday.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 24th be?
f: From the 3rd to the 24th is 21 days. 21 = 3 weeks and 0 extra days, so count 0 days forward from Monday to reach Monday.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 24th be?
f: From the 1st to the 24th is 23 days. 23 = 3 weeks and 2 extra days, so count 2 days forward from Sunday to reach Tuesday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 25th be?
f: From the 4th to the 25th is 21 days. 21 = 3 weeks and 0 extra days, so count 0 days forward from Monday to reach Monday.

q: If the 5th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 25th be?
f: From the 5th to the 25th is 20 days. 20 = 2 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Friday to reach Thursday.

q: If the 5th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 25th be?
f: From the 5th to the 25th is 20 days. 20 = 2 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Sunday to reach Saturday.

q: If the 7th day of a month is Saturday, what day will the 26th be?
f: From the 7th to the 26th is 19 days. 19 = 2 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Saturday to reach Thursday.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 27th be?
f: From the 1st to the 27th is 26 days. 26 = 3 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Monday to reach Saturday.

q: If the 7th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 25th be?
f: From the 7th to the 25th is 18 days. 18 = 2 weeks and 4 extra days, so count 4 days forward from Sunday to reach Thursday.

q: If the 7th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 12th be?
f: From the 7th to the 12th is 5 days. 5 = 0 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Monday to reach Saturday.

q: The 24th of a month is Friday. What day is the 2nd of the same month?
f: The 2nd is 22 days before the 24th. 22 = 3 weeks and 1 extra day, so it is one day before Friday, which is Thursday.

q: Which country hosted the largest number of refugees in 2016?
f: According to UNHCR figures for 2016, Turkey hosted about 2.9 million refugees, mostly Syrians, which was the largest number in the world.

q: Which country hosted the 2018 Asian Games?
f: The 2018 Asian Games were held in Indonesia, in the cities of Jakarta and Palembang.

q: On which date did the 2018 Asian Games begin?
f: The 18th Asian Games opened in Jakarta on 18 August 2018 and ended on 2 September 2018.

q: Where were the 2018 Winter Olympic Games held?
f: The 2018 Winter Olympics took place in Pyeongchang, South Korea, in February 2018.

q: Which country hosted the 2018 Asia Cup cricket tournament?
f: The 2018 Asia Cup was played in the United Arab Emirates, in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, in September 2018.

q: What is the value of the percentage of absent students if 300 out of 500 students are present?
f: Absent students = 500 - 300 = 200. Percentage absent = 200 / 500 x 100 = 40%.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 300 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
There are 1500 students in a class, 1200 are boys and 300 are girls. What is the percentage of girls?
f: Percentage of girls = 300 / 1500 x 100 = 20%.

q: Out of 1200 students, 340 are present. What is the percentage of absent students, to two decimal places?
A helicopter flies at 340 km/h. About how much time does it take to cover 700 km?
f: Time = distance / speed = 700 / 340 = 2.06 hours, which is about 2 hours 4 minutes.

q: In a class of 500 students, 360 are present. How many students are absent?
f: Absent students = 500 - 360 = 140.

q: A plane uses 80 gallons of fuel to cover 320 miles. How many gallons will 800 miles need?
f: Fuel per mile = 80 / 320 = 0.25 gallon. For 800 miles: 800 x 0.25 = 200 gallons.

q: A car travels at 78 km/h. How far will it travel in 12 minutes?
f: 12 minutes = 12 / 60 = 0.2 hour. Distance = 78 x 0.2 = 15.6 km.

q: How many elements are there in each row of a matrix of order 4x3?
f: A matrix of order 4x3 has 4 rows and 3 columns, so each row has 3 elements.

q: A matrix is of order 4x3. How many rows does it have?
f: The order of a matrix is written as rows x columns, so a 4x3 matrix has 4 rows.

q: In which year was the first martial law in Pakistan lifted?
f: General Ayub Khan imposed martial law in October 1958 and it was lifted on 8 June 1962 when the new constitution came into force.

q: Which word is the antonym of abrogate?
f: To abrogate means to repeal or do away with a law. Its opposite is to enact or establish a law.

q: Which word is a synonym of abrogate?
f: To abrogate means to formally cancel or repeal a law or agreement, so repeal has the same meaning.

q: On which date was the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan abrogated?
f: General Yahya Khan imposed martial law on 25 March 1969 after Ayub Khan resigned, and the 1962 Constitution was abrogated.

q: On which date was the first Constitution of Pakistan (1956) adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
f: The Constituent Assembly adopted the 1956 Constitution on 29 February 1956.

q: What is the title of Imam Abu Hanifa's well-known book on beliefs?
f: Al-Fiqh al-Akbar is the creed work traditionally attributed to Imam Abu Hanifa.

q: What is the commutative property of addition?
o: a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c
f: The commutative property says that changing the order of the numbers being added does not change the sum, so a + b = b + a.

q: Who was the first black President of South Africa?
f: Nelson Mandela became South Africa's first black President in May 1994 after the first fully democratic elections.

q: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya (1870) in reply to which book?
o: A Life of Mahomet by William Muir
f: Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya was written to answer the objections raised against the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in William Muir's book A Life of Mahomet. Sir Syed wrote it after visiting England in 1869.

q: Who wrote the book Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya?
f: Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya is a work in defence of Islam written by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan. It was published in 1870.

q: Ahmed is 6 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. When Ahmed is 14 years old, what will be his sister's age?
f: Sister's age now is 6 x 3 = 18 years, so she is 12 years older than Ahmed. When Ahmed is 14, she is 14 + 12 = 26.

q: On which date did Allama Muhammad Iqbal die?
f: Allama Iqbal died in Lahore on 21 April 1938. He is buried near the Badshahi Mosque.

q: Complete the analogy: Sailor is to Navy as Airman is to ____.
f: A sailor serves in the Navy, in the same way an airman serves in the Air Force.

q: How many sons did Hazrat Aisha (RA) have?
f: Hazrat Aisha (RA), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), had no children. She is called Ummul Momineen.

q: On which date was the Jammu and Kashmir State Subject Rule issued?
f: The State Subject Rule defining who was a permanent resident of Jammu and Kashmir was issued by Maharaja Hari Singh on 20 April 1927. It limited land ownership and state jobs to state subjects.

q: If Ahmad is older than Akbar and Akbar is older than Ali, then Ali is ____.
f: The order of age is Ahmad, then Akbar, then Ali, so Ali is the youngest. Therefore Ali is younger than Ahmad (and Akbar).

q: Is 5x - 4y + 6 = 0 an algebraic expression or an equation?
f: It has an equals sign with an expression on each side (the right side is 0), so it is an equation. It is a linear equation in two variables.

q: The product of two algebraic expressions is ____ the product of their LCM and HCF.
f: For any two expressions (or numbers) f and g, f x g = LCM x HCF. So the product is equal to the product of LCM and HCF.

q: What comes next in the series: X3, Y2, Z?
f: The letters move forward X, Y, Z while the numbers go down 3, 2, 1. So the next term is Z1.

q: If the letters of the word ARGUMENT are arranged in alphabetical order, which letter is third?
f: The letters of ARGUMENT in alphabetical order are A, E, G, M, N, R, T, U. The third letter is G.

q: By what other name is Pakistan Day, observed on 23 March, also known?
f: Pakistan Day commemorates the Lahore Resolution (Pakistan Resolution) passed on 23 March 1940, so it is also called Resolution Day. It also marks the adoption of the first constitution in 1956.

q: Who is the angel of death (Malak-ul-Maut) in Islamic belief?
f: Hazrat Izrail (AS) is the angel entrusted with taking souls at death. The Quran refers to him as the angel of death in Surah As-Sajdah.

q: Two adjacent angles which together form a right angle are called what?
f: Two angles whose sum is 90 degrees are complementary. Together they make one right angle.

q: What is the antonym of the word abolish?
f: To abolish is to put an end to something officially. Its opposite is to establish, meaning to set up.

q: What is the antonym of the word accumulated?
f: Accumulated means gathered together over time. The opposite is dispersed, meaning scattered.

q: Find the missing number in the analogy 2 : X :: 4 : 16.
f: Since 4 : 16 shows that 16 is the square of 4 (4 x 4 = 16), the same rule applies to 2, so X = 2 x 2 = 4.

q: Anemia is mainly caused by the deficiency of which element?
f: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin in red blood cells. Without enough iron the blood cannot carry enough oxygen, which causes anemia.

q: Area of a parallelogram = base x ______.
f: The area of a parallelogram is its base multiplied by its perpendicular height, also called its altitude.

q: What is the antonym of despite?
f: Despite means in spite of something; the opposite idea is because of, which gives a cause.

q: What is the antonym of eliminated?
f: Eliminated means removed or left out; the opposite is included or retained.

q: What is the antonym of evidently?
f: Evidently means in a clear and obvious way; the opposite is obscurely, meaning in an unclear way.

q: What is the antonym of foe?
f: A foe is an enemy; the opposite is a friend.

q: What is the antonym of improvement?
f: Improvement means becoming better; the opposite is deterioration, meaning becoming worse.

q: What is the antonym of impudent?
f: Impudent means rude and disrespectful; the opposite is respectful or polite.

q: What is the antonym of multitude?
f: A multitude is a very large number of people or things; the opposite is a handful, a very small number.

q: What is the antonym of nourishment?
f: Nourishment is the food needed for life and growth; the opposite is starvation, the lack of food.

q: What is the antonym of pragmatic?
f: Pragmatic means dealing with things in a practical way; the opposite is idealistic, based on ideals rather than reality.

q: What is the antonym of purification?
f: Purification means making something clean; the opposite is contamination, making it impure.

q: What is the antonym of recalcitrant?
f: Recalcitrant means stubbornly resisting authority; the opposite is obedient or compliant.

q: What is the antonym of refuse?
f: To refuse is to say no to something offered; the opposite is to accept.

q: What is the antonym of shameful?
f: Shameful means causing shame; the opposite is honourable, deserving respect.

q: What is the antonym of strict?
f: Strict means demanding obedience to rules; the opposite is lenient, meaning easy-going or merciful.

q: What is the antonym of underhand?
f: Underhand means done in a secret or dishonest way; the opposite is honest or open.

q: What is the antonym of virtue?
f: Virtue means moral goodness; the opposite is vice, meaning immoral behaviour.

q: What is the supreme law (apex law) of Pakistan?
f: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, adopted in 1973, is the supreme law of the country and all other laws must conform to it.

q: What is the arithmetic mean of 24 and 26?
What is the arithmetic mean of 24 and 36?
What is the arithmetic mean of 8 and 36?
Who were the Ashra-e-Mubashara?
o: Ten Companions of the Prophet (PBUH) given the glad tidings of Paradise in one lifetime
The ten wives of the Prophet (PBUH)
Ten Muslim commanders of the Battle of Badr
f: The Ashra-e-Mubashara are ten Companions whom the Prophet (PBUH) named as people of Paradise while they were alive. They include the four Rightly Guided Caliphs.

q: When did the USA drop atom bombs on Japan?
f: The USA dropped the atom bomb on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945 and on Nagasaki on 9 August 1945.

q: What is the national game of Australia, as commonly stated?
f: Cricket is commonly given as the national game of Australia. It is the most popular summer sport there.

q: After the Quran, what is the most authentic source of Islamic teachings?
