f: The Suez Canal opened to ships on 17 November 1869.

q: About how long is the Suez Canal in nautical miles?
f: The canal is about 193 km long, and 193 divided by 1.852 is about 104 nautical miles.

q: In a triangle, the sum of any two sides is what compared with the third side?
f: By the triangle inequality, the sum of any two sides is always greater than the third side.

q: What is the sum of the series 2, 4, 6, 8?
If the 5th day of a month is Sunday, which day is the 28th of that month?
f: From the 5th to the 28th is 23 days. 23 divided by 7 leaves 2, so the day is Sunday + 2 = Tuesday.

q: What is a synonym of fertilizer?
f: A fertilizer is a substance added to soil to make it more fertile, and manure is a similar substance.

q: What is the synonym of advanced?
f: Advanced means ahead in development, so progressive is closest in meaning.

q: What is the synonym of annihilation?
f: Annihilation means complete destruction.

q: What is the synonym of blame?
f: To blame is to hold someone responsible for a fault, which is close to censure.

q: What is the synonym of brutal?
f: Brutal means savagely harsh, which matches cruel.

q: What is the synonym of contentious?
f: Contentious means causing or likely to cause arguments, which is the sense of controversial.

q: What is the synonym of diligent?
f: Diligent means showing careful and persistent effort, so hardworking is closest.

q: What is the synonym of exhausted?
f: Exhausted means completely used up of energy, which is the sense of drained.

q: What is the synonym of extravagant?
f: Extravagant means spending or giving far more than is necessary, which matches lavish.

q: What is the synonym of germinate?
f: To germinate is to begin to grow from a seed, which is to sprout.

q: What is the synonym of identification?
f: Identification means the act of recognizing who or what something is.

q: What is the synonym of liberal?
f: Liberal can mean giving freely or in large amounts, which is generous.

q: What is the synonym of pious?
f: Pious means deeply religious, which is the meaning of devout.

q: What is the synonym of strictly?
f: Strictly means in a way that follows rules exactly, which is rigidly.

q: What is the synonym of tired?
f: Tired means in need of rest, which matches weary.

q: What is the synonym of truth?
f: Truth means the quality of being true, and veracity is the formal word for it.

q: Which team won the most recent T20-format Asia Cup, held in 2025?
f: India beat Pakistan by 5 wickets in the 2025 final in Dubai.

q: With whose help was the Al-Khalid main battle tank developed in Pakistan?
f: Al-Khalid (MBT-2000) was co-developed by Heavy Industries Taxila and China's Norinco, based on the Chinese Type 90-II.

q: What is the approximate length of the main Tarbela Dam?
f: The main embankment dam of Tarbela is about 2,743 m long and 143 m high.

q: In which district of Pakistan is the ancient city of Taxila located?
f: Taxila is a tehsil of Rawalpindi District in Punjab.

q: Choose the correct indirect speech of: The teacher said, "I will meet you next day." (spoken to the students)
o: The teacher said that he will meet you next day.
The teacher said that I would meet them the next day.
The teacher said that he would meet you the next day.
The teacher said that he would meet them the next day.
f: In reported speech will changes to would, I changes to he, you changes to them and next day changes to the next day.

q: In which year was the Hubble Space Telescope launched?
f: NASA launched Hubble aboard the Space Shuttle Discovery in April 1990.

q: Which letter appears three times in the word 'temperature' but only once in the word 'cylinder'?
f: In 'temperature' the letter E appears 3 times (t-E-mp-E-ratur-E) while T and R appear twice. In 'cylinder' E appears once.

q: If (x, 1) = (1, y), what is the ordered pair (x, y)?
f: Two ordered pairs are equal when their corresponding elements are equal, so x = 1 and y = 1. Hence (x, y) = (1, 1).

q: If today is Friday, what day of the week will it be after 30 days?
f: 30 divided by 7 leaves remainder 2. Two days after Friday is Sunday.

q: If today is Monday, what day will it be after 15 days?
f: 15 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1. One day after Monday is Tuesday.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what will be the day after tomorrow (counting today as the 1st)?
f: Tomorrow is Tuesday (2nd), and the day after tomorrow is Wednesday (3rd).

q: Which major battle in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) participated took place in 7 AH?
f: The Battle of Khyber against the Jews of Khyber was fought in 7 AH (628 AD).

q: Who is Pakistan's highest run scorer in Test cricket?
f: Younis Khan scored 10,099 Test runs and is the leading Pakistani Test run scorer.

q: What is the main subject (topic) of Sahih Bukhari?
o: Hadith (sayings and actions of the Prophet)
f: Sahih Bukhari, compiled by Imam Bukhari, is a collection of authentic hadith of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

q: What are two circles that touch each other at exactly one point called?
f: Circles that meet at exactly one point are called tangent (touching) circles. They can touch externally or internally.

q: Which of these countries does not share a border with Pakistan?
f: Pakistan borders India, China, Afghanistan and Iran. Bangladesh is separated from Pakistan by India.

q: What is a synonym of the word 'transparent'?
f: Transparent means allowing light to pass through so things can be seen clearly. Clear is the closest synonym.

q: Ali is 3 years old and his sister is twice his age. What will his sister's age be when Ali is 12 years old?
f: The sister is 2 x 3 = 6 when Ali is 3, so she is 3 years older. When Ali is 12, she is 12 + 3 = 15.

q: Omar is 4 years old and his sister is twice his age. What will his sister's age be when Omar is 11 years old?
f: The sister is 2 x 4 = 8 when Omar is 4, so she is 4 years older. When Omar is 11, she is 11 + 4 = 15.

q: A train travels 60 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes at the same speed?
f: 1 hour 40 minutes = 100 minutes, so speed = 60/100 = 0.6 km per minute. In 12 minutes it covers 0.6 x 12 = 7.2 km.

q: If a bus travels 20 miles in an hour, how many miles does it cover in 40 minutes?
f: 40 minutes = 2/3 of an hour, so distance = 20 x 2/3 = 13 1/3 miles (about 13.3).

q: If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 25th of that month be?
f: From the 4th to the 25th is 21 days, which is exactly 3 weeks. So the 25th falls on the same day, Tuesday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 25th of that month be?
f: From the 2nd to the 25th is 23 days = 3 weeks + 2 days. Tuesday plus 2 days is Thursday.

q: How many equal sides does an isosceles triangle have?
f: An isosceles triangle has exactly two sides of equal length, and the angles opposite them are also equal.

q: To which tribe did Hazrat Khadija (RA) belong?
f: Hazrat Khadija bint Khuwaylid belonged to the Banu Asad clan of the Quraish tribe of Makkah.

q: Which was fought first, the Battle of Badr or the Battle of Uhud?
f: Badr was fought in 2 AH and Uhud in 3 AH, so Badr came first.

q: What is the approximate value of the square root of 72?
f: 72 = 36 x 2, so its square root is 6 x root 2 = 6 x 1.414 = about 8.49.

q: What is the SI unit of electric current?
f: Electric current is measured in amperes (amps), the flow of charge per second.

q: What is the capital of the USA?
f: Washington, D.C. is the federal capital of the United States and the seat of the White House and Congress. It lies on the Potomac River.

q: Who is the Vice President of the USA (as of October 2026)?
f: J. D. Vance took office as Vice President on 20 January 2025 under President Donald Trump. He is still the Vice President in October 2026.

q: Valletta is the capital of which country?
f: Valletta is the capital city of Malta, an island country in the Mediterranean Sea. It is one of the smallest national capitals in Europe.

q: If 2x + 3x + y is simplified, what is the result?
f: Like terms 2x and 3x add up to 5x. The term y is unlike, so it stays separate, giving 5x + y.

q: What is the main difference between a scalar and a vector quantity?
o: A scalar has magnitude only, while a vector has magnitude and direction
A scalar has direction only, while a vector has magnitude only
A scalar is always negative, while a vector is always positive
f: A scalar is fully described by its magnitude, such as mass or speed. A vector needs both magnitude and direction, such as velocity or force.

q: What is the magnitude of a unit vector?
f: A unit vector is defined as a vector of length one, so its magnitude is 1. It is used to indicate direction only.

q: Two non-zero vectors are parallel if their vector (cross) product is what?
f: The magnitude of A cross B is AB sin(theta). For parallel vectors theta is 0 or 180 degrees, so sin(theta) = 0 and the cross product is the zero vector.

q: What is the third form (past participle) of the verb 'flash'?
f: 'Flash' is a regular verb, so its three forms are flash, flashed, flashed. The third form is therefore flashed.

q: Which Indian tribe was forced to walk the Trail of Tears?
f: The Trail of Tears was the forced removal of the Cherokee from the south-eastern USA to Indian Territory in 1838-39 after the Indian Removal Act of 1830. Thousands died on the way.

q: A person walks 20 km north, then turns right, then left, then right again. In which direction is he now facing?
f: Facing north, a right turn gives east. A left turn then gives north, and a right turn again gives east.

q: What is the product of the frequency and the time period of a wave?
f: The time period T is the reciprocal of frequency f, that is T = 1/f. Therefore f times T = 1.

q: In Islamic history, what does Aam-ul-Wafood mean?
f: Aam-ul-Wafood is the Year of Delegations, 9 AH, when many Arab tribes sent delegations to Madinah to accept Islam.

q: Which area of Pakistan is famous for its illegal (unlicensed) arms manufacturing market?
f: Darra Adam Khel, south of Peshawar in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, is well known for its cottage-industry gunsmiths and arms bazaar.

q: In the sentence 'He is clever as well as hardworking', what part of speech is the phrase 'as well as'?
f: 'As well as' joins two words or phrases of equal rank, so it works as a (compound) conjunction.

q: Which language has the largest number of speakers (native plus second-language) in the world?
f: English is spoken by about 1.5 billion people counting second-language speakers, which is more than any other language.

q: Length multiplied by width of a rectangle gives its what?
f: The area of a rectangle is length x width, measured in square units.

q: What is the width of a standard football (soccer) goal?
f: A standard football goal is 8 yards (24 feet or 7.32 metres) wide and 8 feet (2.44 metres) high.

q: Which famous writer refused to accept the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1964?
f: The French philosopher and writer Jean-Paul Sartre declined the 1964 Nobel Prize in Literature.

q: If two thirds of a group are men, what percentage of the group are women?
f: Women are 1 - 2/3 = 1/3 of the group. 1/3 x 100 = 33.33%.

q: Change the narration: I said to him, 'Why are you working so hard?'
o: I asked him why was he working so hard.
I told him why he was working so hard.
I asked him why he was working so hard.
I asked him that why he is working so hard.
f: A question in direct speech becomes 'asked' in indirect speech. The word order becomes statement order and the tense moves back to the past continuous: he was working.

q: What is the name of the set of all positive numbers, negative numbers and zero (without fractions)?
f: Integers include the positive whole numbers, the negative whole numbers and zero.

q: What is -i(2i + 3)?
f: -i(2i + 3) = -2i squared - 3i = 2 - 3i, since i squared is -1.

q: What is -i(6 - 4i)?
What is 1/3 of 90% of 90?
f: 90% of 90 is 81, and one third of 81 is 27.
The denominators are equal, so add the numerators: 3/8.

q: What is 3 x 4?
f: Three groups of four make 12.

q: What is 4 x 3 + 3 x 4?
f: Multiply first: 4 x 3 = 12 and 3 x 4 = 12. Then add: 12 + 12 = 24.

q: What is 60% of 9?
What is 7% of 80?
What is 80% of 20?
What is 90% of 81?
What is a + ib, where a and b are real numbers and i is the square root of -1, called?
f: An expression of the form a + ib is called a complex number, with real part a and imaginary part b.

q: What is the value of Y = (1 - 2)(1 - 3)?
Muhammad Ali Bogra held which office in Pakistan?
f: Muhammad Ali Bogra served as the third Prime Minister of Pakistan from 1953 to 1955, after Khawaja Nazimuddin was dismissed.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to fragment?
f: A fragment is a small broken part or piece of something larger.

q: In which year was the first Round Table Conference held in London?
f: The first Round Table Conference was held in London from November 1930 to January 1931.

q: Freedom of speech and expression is guaranteed under which Article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan?
f: Article 19 gives every citizen the right to freedom of speech and expression, subject to reasonable restrictions.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to zest?
f: Zest means great energy and enjoyment, which is enthusiasm.

q: Which word is a synonym of 'disruption'?
f: Disruption means a break or interruption in the normal course of something. Disturbance has the same meaning.

q: In which year did Queen Elizabeth II first visit Pakistan?
f: The Queen first visited Pakistan in February 1961 during a Commonwealth tour.

q: Who discovered penicillin?
f: Alexander Fleming, a Scottish scientist, discovered penicillin in 1928 from the mould Penicillium.

q: Who is the current ODI captain of Pakistan (as of October 2026)?
f: Shaheen Shah Afridi was appointed Pakistan's ODI captain and was still leading the side in 2026.

q: Gwadar Port is linked through CPEC with which country?
f: Gwadar Port is the centrepiece of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, which links it with China's Xinjiang region.

q: Which country lies to the west of Pakistan?
f: Iran borders Pakistan on the west, mainly along Balochistan.

q: Which is considered the largest desert of Pakistan?
f: Most Pakistani textbooks name the Thar Desert in Sindh as the largest desert of Pakistan. It is shared with India.

q: In which city is the headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO) located?
f: The WHO is a specialised agency of the United Nations and has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland.

q: Why do parents give education to their children?
f: Parents educate children to groom them, that is, to prepare and train them for a successful life.

q: In which year did Balochistan become a province of Pakistan?
f: When the One Unit scheme of West Pakistan was dissolved on 1 July 1970, Balochistan became a full province.

q: Choose the correct word: The aeroplane flew ___ my head.
f: The preposition over is used when something passes above a person or object. The other options do not suit the meaning.

q: What is the approximate area of Sindh province?
f: Sindh covers about 140,914 square kilometres, which is about 17.7 percent of Pakistan.

q: How many ayat (verses) does Surah Al-Ikhlas have?
f: Surah Al-Ikhlas (112) has 4 ayat. It describes the oneness of Allah.

q: How many letters does the Pashto alphabet have according to the most commonly cited reference count?
f: The Pashto alphabet is written in an extended Arabic script and is most commonly cited as having 45 letters.

q: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: He will not approve ___ your plan.
f: The verb approve takes the preposition of when it means to think well of something.

q: In which years was the First World War fought?
f: The First World War began in July 1914 and ended with the armistice of November 1918.

q: In which year did the Second World War start?
f: The Second World War began on 1 September 1939 when Germany invaded Poland, and ended in 1945.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to obligation?
f: An obligation is something you must do, which means a duty.

q: Which country won the 2022 FIFA World Cup?
f: Argentina beat France on penalties after a 3-3 draw in the final held in Qatar on 18 December 2022.

q: In which years was the Second World War fought?
f: The Second World War began in 1939 when Germany invaded Poland and ended in 1945 with the defeat of Germany and Japan.

q: How many Pakistanis have won a Nobel Prize so far?
f: Two Pakistanis have won it: Dr Abdus Salam (Physics, 1979) and Malala Yousafzai (Peace, 2014).

q: What does Makruh mean in Islamic law?
o: A permitted act with no reward
A disliked act that is better avoided
An act that is strictly forbidden
f: A Makruh act is disliked and discouraged in Islam, but doing it is a lesser matter than a forbidden (Haram) act.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to peril?
f: Peril means serious danger or risk.

q: On which side of Punjab is the Cholistan Desert located?
f: The Cholistan Desert lies in the south of Punjab near Bahawalpur, along the border with India.

q: On which date was the Legal Framework Order (LFO) issued by President Yahya Khan?
f: President General Yahya Khan issued the Legal Framework Order on 30 March 1970 to arrange the first general elections on the basis of one man one vote. It also ended the One Unit.

q: In which month and year was the Lucknow Pact signed between the Muslim League and the Indian National Congress?
f: The Lucknow Pact was agreed at the joint sessions of the Congress and the Muslim League in Lucknow in December 1916.

q: Convert 90 degrees into radians.
f: 1 degree = pi/180 radian. So 90 degrees = 90 x pi/180 = pi/2 radians.

q: A train's speed is double that of a car. If the car travels 60 km in 1 hour, how much distance will the train cover in 30 minutes?
f: The car speed is 60 km per hour, so the train speed is 120 km per hour. In 30 minutes (half an hour) the train covers 120 x 1/2 = 60 km.

q: What is 0.01 x 100?
f: Multiplying by 100 moves the decimal point two places to the right: 0.01 becomes 1.

q: Who is the current President of Bangladesh (as of October 2026)?
f: Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned in July 2026. Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was elected by Parliament on 20 August 2026 and sworn in as the 23rd President.

q: A rectangular arrangement of numbers in rows and columns, written inside square brackets, is called what?
f: A rectangular array of numbers in rows and columns enclosed in brackets is called a matrix.

q: How many countries are there in Central Asia?
f: Central Asia has five countries: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.

q: Who was the father of Hazrat Yusuf (AS)?
f: Hazrat Yusuf (AS) was the son of Hazrat Yaqoob (AS), who was also a prophet.

q: Who was the leader of Germany in World War II?
f: Adolf Hitler led Germany as Chancellor and Fuhrer from 1933 until his death in 1945.

q: What was Hazrat Umme Kulsum (RA) to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: Hazrat Umme Kulsum (RA) was a daughter of the Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (RA).

q: Ahmed got 15 marks out of 60. What is his percentage?
f: Percentage = 15/60 x 100 = 25%.

q: Which is the oldest English newspaper of Pakistan still in publication?
f: Dawn was founded by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah in 1941 in Delhi and is the oldest widely cited English daily of Pakistan.

q: In which country is the headquarters of the Olympics (International Olympic Committee) located?
f: The International Olympic Committee has its headquarters in Lausanne, Switzerland.

q: What is the meaning of the word ominous?
o: Threatening, suggesting that something bad will happen
f: Ominous describes something that gives a sign of coming trouble or danger. For example, ominous dark clouds suggest a storm.

q: Which is the smallest of the five rivers of Punjab (Pakistan) in length?
f: The Ravi is about 720 km long, the shortest of the five rivers, and is commonly called the smallest river of Pakistan in textbooks.

q: Which country was the third largest host of refugees in 2016 according to the Amnesty International report?
f: Amnesty International's October 2016 report ranked Jordan first, Turkey second, Pakistan third (about 1.6 million) and Lebanon fourth.

q: Which country won the most medals at the Olympic Games held at Tokyo in 2020 (held in 2021)?
f: The USA topped the medal table with 113 medals, including 39 gold.

q: On which date was the 1956 constitution of Pakistan abrogated?
f: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 constitution on 7 October 1958 and imposed martial law.

q: In which valley is Attabad Lake located?
f: Attabad Lake is in the Gojal area of the upper Hunza Valley in Gilgit-Baltistan.

q: Which article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan provides the right to free and compulsory education to children aged 5 to 16?
f: Article 25A was added by the 18th Amendment in 2010. It obliges the State to give free and compulsory education to children from 5 to 16 years.

q: Between which two countries does the Durand Line lie?
f: The Durand Line is the border drawn in 1893 between British India and Afghanistan. Today it is the international border between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

q: Which article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan gives the right to education?
f: Article 25A, added by the 18th Amendment in 2010, makes education a right of children.

q: What is the value of sec 0 (secant of zero degrees)?
f: Secant is the reciprocal of cosine, and cos 0 = 1, so sec 0 = 1/1 = 1.

q: On which date did Fatima Jinnah die?
f: Fatima Jinnah, the sister of Quaid-e-Azam, died in Karachi on 9 July 1967.

q: What is the tense used to write about the future called?
f: Future tense describes actions that will happen later, usually with will or shall, as in: I will go.

q: Geographically, Greenland belongs to which continent?
f: Greenland lies on the North American continental shelf, although politically it is part of the Kingdom of Denmark.

q: Which of the following is a greenhouse gas?
f: Methane traps heat in the atmosphere, while oxygen, nitrogen and argon do not.

q: In which city is the headquarters of the European Union (EU) located?
f: The main institutions of the European Union, such as the European Commission and the Council, are based in Brussels, Belgium.

q: Who was the first Pakistani cricketer to score a triple century in Test cricket?
f: Hanif Mohammad scored 337 against the West Indies at Bridgetown in 1958. It was the first Test triple century by a Pakistani.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word lately?
f: Lately means in the recent past, which is the same as recently.

q: In which year did the British occupy Punjab?
f: The British defeated the Sikhs in the Second Anglo-Sikh War and annexed Punjab in 1849.

q: Which Quetta-area peak, also called Loe Sar Nekan, is generally given as the highest peak of Balochistan?
f: Zarghun Ghar, near Quetta, at about 3,578 metres is generally given as the highest peak in Balochistan.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'restricted'.
f: Restricted means kept within limits or not allowed freely, so the closest word is limited.

q: In which mountain range are Pakistan's famous salt mines, such as Khewra, located?
f: The Salt Range in Punjab holds huge rock salt deposits, including the Khewra salt mine.

q: Between which two countries was the Shimla Agreement of 1972 signed?
f: The Shimla Agreement was signed by Pakistan and India in July 1972 after the 1971 war.

q: How many straight lines can pass through a single given point?
f: Through one point we can draw a line in every possible direction, so there are infinitely many lines.

q: What is the sum of two supplementary angles?
f: Two angles are supplementary when they add up to 180 degrees, for example 110 and 70.

q: Who has taken the most Test wickets for Pakistan?
f: Wasim Akram took 414 Test wickets, the highest by any Pakistani bowler, and the record still stands in 2026.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to thy?
f: Thy is an old English word meaning your (belonging to you).

q: What is the meaning of the word undaunted?
f: Undaunted means not discouraged or frightened by difficulty or danger, so it means fearless.

q: In which year did Zakat become compulsory (enforced by law) in Pakistan?
f: The Zakat and Ushr Ordinance was promulgated in 1980 under General Zia-ul-Haq, and Zakat deduction from bank accounts started that year.

q: If the 14th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 19th be?
f: From the 14th to the 19th is 5 days. Sunday + 5 days = Friday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 30th be?
f: From the 4th to the 30th is 26 days. 26 divided by 7 leaves remainder 5, and Monday plus 5 days is Saturday.

q: How many degrees are there in the angle around a full circle?
f: A complete turn around the centre of a circle is 360 degrees.

q: How many daughters of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) passed away during his lifetime?
f: Hazrat Zainab, Hazrat Ruqayyah and Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA) passed away in his lifetime. Hazrat Fatima (RA) passed away about six months after him.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word chaos?
f: Chaos means complete disorder and confusion. Its opposite is order.

q: What is the antonym of the word cherish?
f: To cherish means to hold dear and care for. Its opposite is to neglect or despise.

q: In which year was the name Pakistan coined by Choudhry Rahmat Ali?
f: Choudhry Rahmat Ali put forward the name Pakistan in 1933 in his pamphlet Now or Never.

q: What do the five rings of the Olympic flag represent?
f: The five interlocked rings stand for the five inhabited continents joined together by the Olympic movement.

q: What is the common difference in the series 4, 8, 12, 16?
f: 8 - 4 = 4, 12 - 8 = 4 and 16 - 12 = 4. So the difference is 4.

q: In which year was the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan abrogated?
f: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 Constitution on 7 October 1958 and imposed martial law.

q: Pakistani people are equal because of which common bond?
f: Pakistan was created in the name of Islam, and the Islamic teaching of equality unites its people despite different languages and cultures.

q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word eradication?
f: Eradication means completely getting rid of or destroying something, which is elimination.

q: Which of the following events took place in the 8th year of Hijri (Fateh Makkah, the conquest of Makkah)?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) entered Makkah peacefully with a large army in Ramadan 8 AH. Badr was in 2 AH, Uhud in 3 AH and Khandaq in 5 AH.

q: What is the full form of SCO?
f: SCO stands for Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, a political, economic and security group of Eurasian countries.

q: What is half of the diameter of a circle called?
f: The diameter is twice the radius, so half of the diameter is the radius.

q: Which is the largest (longest) surah of the Holy Quran?
f: Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest surah of the Quran and has 286 ayat.

q: Who led the Muslim army in the Battle (Ghazwa) of Badr?
f: The Battle of Badr was fought in 2 AH and the Muslim army was commanded by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) himself. The Muslims were about 313 men.

q: Manchar Lake, the largest freshwater lake of Pakistan, is located in which district of Sindh?
f: Manchar Lake lies in Dadu district of Sindh, west of the Indus River near Sehwan.

q: What is a matrix in mathematics?
o: A rectangular arrangement of numbers in rows and columns
A single number with a sign
A curve drawn on a graph
f: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers (or symbols) arranged in horizontal rows and vertical columns.

q: What does the word Tanzil mean?
f: Tanzil is an Arabic word meaning sending down, and it is used for the revelation of the Quran.

q: What is an obligatory act called in Islam?
f: An act that must be done and whose neglect is a sin is called Farz.

q: What is the antonym of the word panic?
f: Panic is wild fear. Calm (a peaceful, steady state) is its opposite.

q: At which annual session of the All India Muslim League was the Pakistan Resolution passed in March 1940?
f: The Pakistan (Lahore) Resolution was passed at the 27th annual session of the All India Muslim League in Lahore.

q: How many princely states were there in British India at the time of partition in 1947?
f: About 562 princely states existed in British India in 1947. Each had to join India or Pakistan or stay independent.

q: What is the product of 3/2 and 2/3?
f: Multiply: (3 x 2) / (2 x 3) = 6/6 = 1. The two fractions are reciprocals of each other.

q: According to the Hadith in Sahih Muslim, which prophet was a carpenter by profession?
f: Sahih Muslim reports that Hazrat Zakariya (AS) was a carpenter.

q: Which game is played with a racket and a shuttlecock?
f: Badminton players hit a shuttlecock over a net using rackets.

q: What is the meaning of the word rash?
f: As an adjective, rash means acting without thinking about the results, so hasty and reckless.

q: What type of number is 7/9?
f: 7/9 is a ratio of two integers, so it is a rational number.

q: Which river is called the lifeline of Pakistan?
f: The Indus is the longest river of Pakistan and its water supports most of the farming of the country, so it is called the lifeline of Pakistan.

q: According to the 2023 census, about what percentage of Pakistan's population lives in rural areas?
f: The 2023 census recorded about 61.2 percent rural and 38.8 percent urban population.

q: Where is the Thal desert located in Pakistan?
o: Between the Indus and Jhelum rivers in Punjab
In the Chagai district of Balochistan
In the Cholistan region near Bahawalpur
f: The Thal desert lies in the Punjab province in the area between the Indus and Jhelum rivers, covering districts such as Bhakkar, Layyah, Khushab and Mianwali.

q: What is the synonym of "troubled"?
f: "Troubled" means disturbed or anxious, which is close to worried or distressed.

q: Under which Article of the Constitution of Pakistan is free and compulsory education a fundamental right?
f: Article 25A, added by the 18th Amendment in 2010, makes free and compulsory education a right for children aged 5 to 16.

q: How many rivers were allotted to Pakistan under the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960?
f: The treaty gave the three western rivers, Indus, Jhelum and Chenab, to Pakistan.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 14th be?
f: From the 1st to the 14th is 13 days. 13 divided by 7 leaves 6, so Sunday + 6 = Saturday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 17th be?
f: From the 2nd to the 17th is 15 days. 15 divided by 7 leaves 1, so Monday + 1 = Tuesday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 26th be?
f: From the 4th to the 26th is 22 days. 22 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1, so the day is Monday.

q: Which day is celebrated on 4th January every year?
f: World Braille Day is observed on 4 January, the birthday of Louis Braille, inventor of the Braille system.

q: On which side of Pakistan is Afghanistan situated?
f: Afghanistan lies along the western and north-western border of Pakistan. India is to the east and China to the north-east.

q: Who is known as the founder of the technology company Apple?
f: Steve Jobs co-founded Apple in 1976 with Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne and led it for many years.

q: What is the antonym of callous?
f: Callous means cold and unfeeling, so the opposite is compassionate.

q: According to the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan, who appointed the Prime Minister?
o: The Speaker of the National Assembly
f: Under the 1956 Constitution the President appointed as Prime Minister the member of the National Assembly who had the confidence of the majority of its members.

q: Which word is made by arranging the letters POEARLD?
f: The letters P, O, E, A, R, L, D can be rearranged to spell LEOPARD, using all seven letters.

q: In which year did Pakistan become a nuclear (atomic) power?
f: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests in the Chagai hills on 28 May 1998 and so became a declared nuclear power.

q: Who is known as Baba-e-Urdu (Father of Urdu)?
f: Maulvi Abdul Haq worked all his life for the promotion and development of the Urdu language and its dictionaries, so he is given the title Baba-e-Urdu.

q: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: Put the pen ___ the basket.
f: Into shows movement from outside to the inside of something, which is what putting a pen in a basket means.

q: In which type of brackets is a solution set written?
f: A solution set is a set, and sets are written inside curly brackets, for example {2, 3}.

q: What is the fraction 11/7 called?
f: In 11/7 the numerator 11 is larger than the denominator 7, so it is an improper fraction. It equals 1 and 4/7.

q: How many times were the modern Olympic Games cancelled because of world wars?
f: The Games were cancelled in 1916 (World War I), and in 1940 and 1944 (World War II). That makes three times.

q: Which country suffered the most deaths in World War II?
f: The Soviet Union lost an estimated 24 to 27 million people, mostly on the Eastern Front against Germany.

q: What is the total angle at the centre of a circle?
f: A full turn around the centre of a circle makes 360 degrees.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to denounce?
f: To denounce means to publicly criticise or condemn something as wrong.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to debate?
f: A debate is a formal discussion in which opposing views are put forward.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to rectify?
f: To rectify means to put something right or correct a mistake.

q: Fill in the blank: Children died ___ fever.
f: We use the preposition of with a cause of death, such as died of fever.

q: Which of these is the best conductor of electricity?
f: Silver has the highest electrical conductivity of all metals, higher than copper and gold.

q: What is the conjugate of the imaginary unit iota (i)?
f: The conjugate of 0 + 1i is 0 - 1i, which is -i.

q: What does the idiom 'a dark horse' mean?
o: A little-known person who unexpectedly wins or succeeds
A person who is always late
f: A dark horse is a person or competitor about whom little is known but who may surprise everyone by winning. The idiom comes from horse racing.

q: Which is the largest desert in the world by area?
f: A desert is an area with very little precipitation, and Antarctica, at about 14 million square km, is the largest. The Sahara is the largest hot desert.

q: In which district of Punjab is Harappa located?
f: The ruins of Harappa lie near the Ravi River in Sahiwal district, Punjab.

q: In which year did Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, die?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan was assassinated on 16 October 1951 at Company Bagh in Rawalpindi.

q: Who discovered micro-organisms (microscopic life)?
f: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek first observed bacteria and other tiny organisms with his own microscopes in the 1670s.

q: Where was the first All Pakistan Educational Conference held in 1947?
f: The first educational conference was held in Karachi in November and December 1947, soon after independence.

q: In which year did Queen Elizabeth II visit Pakistan for the second time?
f: The Queen first visited Pakistan in 1961 and returned in October 1997, during the 50th anniversary of independence.

q: What is the power set of the empty set?
o: The set containing 0 and the empty set
The set containing the empty set
f: The empty set has one subset, itself, so its power set has 2 to the power 0 = 1 element, namely the set containing the empty set.

q: Fill in the blank: All people ___ the world are learning English.
f: The correct phrase is 'around the world', which means everywhere in the world.

q: Which game is known as the Gentleman's Game?
f: Cricket is called the gentleman's game because of its tradition of fair play and sportsmanship.

q: Ali got 15 marks out of 60. What is his percentage?
f: Percentage = 15 divided by 60, times 100 = 0.25 times 100 = 25 percent.

q: Who was the first recipient of the Nishan-e-Haider?
f: Captain Raja Muhammad Sarwar was martyred in Kashmir in 1948 and received the first Nishan-e-Haider.

q: What does the idiom snake in the grass mean?
o: A treacherous person who pretends to be a friend
f: The idiom describes a person who appears friendly but secretly plans to harm you, like a snake hidden in grass.

q: What is the Indus River called in Hindi and Sanskrit?
f: The river is called Sindhu in Sanskrit and Hindi, and the name Sindhu gave rise to the words Sind, Hind and India.

q: What is the antonym of "impoverished"?
f: Impoverished means made poor, so its opposite is wealthy or rich.

q: How many member countries does the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) have?
f: The OIC has 57 member states spread over four continents.

q: Where is the headquarters of INTERPOL located?
f: The General Secretariat of INTERPOL is in Lyon, France.

q: Which is the current professional cricket league of Pakistan?
f: The Pakistan Super League (PSL) is the franchise T20 league of Pakistan, played every year since 2016.

q: What is the value of the limit of sin x divided by x as x approaches 0?
f: This is a standard limit: as x approaches 0 (x in radians), sin x becomes almost equal to x, so the ratio tends to 1.

q: Who first introduced the photostat (photocopying) machine?
f: Chester Carlson, an American inventor, invented the dry photocopying process called xerography in 1938.

q: Who has taken the most wickets in Test cricket?
f: Muttiah Muralitharan of Sri Lanka took 800 Test wickets, the highest ever.

q: To where did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) migrate from Makkah?
f: In 622 AD the Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Yathrib, which was later named Madinat-un-Nabi, or Madina.

q: In which year did Pakistan win its first Olympic gold medal?
f: Pakistan beat India 1-0 in the hockey final at the Rome Olympics of 1960 to win its first gold.

q: Who is called Shaheed-e-Millat in Pakistan?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, was assassinated in Rawalpindi in 1951. He is therefore called Shaheed-e-Millat, the martyr of the nation.

q: In which city is Bait-ul-Muqaddas (Al-Aqsa Mosque) located?
f: Bait-ul-Muqaddas is in Jerusalem, in Palestine. It was the first qibla of the Muslims.

q: What was the name of the brother of Hazrat Musa (AS)?
f: Hazrat Haroon (AS) was the elder brother of Hazrat Musa (AS). He was also a prophet and helped Musa (AS) before Pharaoh.

q: Which term comes next in the series: A88, C76, F52, ?
f: Letters move forward by 2, 3, 4, so after F comes J. Numbers drop by 12, 24, 36: 88, 76, 52, 16. So the next term is J16.

q: Who discovered the nucleus of the atom?
f: Ernest Rutherford discovered the atomic nucleus in 1911 through his gold foil experiment.

q: Yathrib is the old name of which city?
f: The city of Yathrib was renamed Madinah-tun-Nabi after the Hijrat of the Prophet (PBUH).

q: What is photosynthesis?
o: Making food by green plants using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide
f: In photosynthesis, plants use chlorophyll in chloroplasts and sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen.

q: Who won the Battle of Plassey (1757)?
f: The East India Company under Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula of Bengal, helped by the betrayal of Mir Jafar.

q: With which surah does the Quran begin in its written order?
f: The first surah in the Mushaf (written order) is Surah Al-Fatiha, followed by Surah Al-Baqarah.

q: If the diameter of a circle is 56, what is its radius?
f: Radius is half of the diameter. 56 / 2 = 28.

q: What is the meaning of the word reasonable?
f: Reasonable means having good sense and being fair. Its synonym is sensible.

q: What was the character of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) according to Hazrat Aisha (RA)?
f: When asked about his character, Hazrat Aisha (RA) replied that his character was the Quran.

q: In a room there are 18 girls and 6 boys. What percentage of the people in the room are boys?
f: Total people = 18 + 6 = 24. Percentage of boys = 6/24 x 100 = 25 percent.

q: Fill in the blank: ____ you were sleeping, the telephone rang.
f: 'While' joins two actions that happen at the same time, and here it links a clause with a subject and verb.

q: Fill in the blank: Throw the pen ___ the dustbin.
f: The preposition 'into' shows movement towards the inside of something, so the pen goes into the dustbin.

q: Change into indirect speech: She told, "It is a very cold day."
o: She told that it is a very cold day.
She told that it was a very cold day.
She told that it had been a very cold day.
She told that it will be a very cold day.
f: The reporting verb is in the past tense, so the present tense "is" changes to the past tense "was". The quotation marks are removed and "that" is added.

q: What is the antonym of "trivial"?
f: "Trivial" means of little importance, so its opposite is "important" or significant.

q: On which date was the One Unit scheme enforced in West Pakistan?
f: The West Pakistan One Unit scheme was enforced on 14 October 1955, merging the western provinces and states into one unit.

q: Which Prime Minister of Pakistan was the first to visit China?
f: Huseyn Shaheed Suhrawardy visited China in October 1956 and was the first Pakistani Prime Minister to do so.

q: In a group of 24 people, 18 are women. What percentage of the group are men?
Choose the correct word: She said to me that she ___ TV.
f: The reporting verb said is in the past, so the present continuous is watching changes to was watching.

q: If the 19th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 26th be?
f: From the 19th to the 26th is 7 days, exactly one week, so the weekday is the same: Sunday.

q: Which session of the All India Muslim League passed the Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution on 23 March 1940?
f: The Lahore Resolution was passed at the 27th annual session of the All India Muslim League held at Minto Park, Lahore, in March 1940.

q: In which year was the present Constitution of Pakistan made?
f: The present Constitution was passed by the National Assembly in April 1973 and enforced on 14 August 1973.

q: Who was the first president of the Indian National Congress in 1885?
f: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay in December 1885 under the presidency of W. C. Bonnerjee.

q: What is the antonym of the word abhorrent?
f: Abhorrent means disgusting or hateful, so its opposite is admirable.

q: What is the synonym of the word abhorrent?
f: Abhorrent means causing strong disgust, which matches detestable.

q: What is the closest meaning of 'accomplished' when used for a person?
f: As an adjective, accomplished describes a person who is highly skilled or talented, such as an accomplished pianist.

q: What is the meaning of 'admonished'?
f: To admonish someone is to warn or scold them firmly. Reprimand and rebuke are its synonyms.

q: Which part of speech describes or modifies a verb?
f: An adverb tells us how, when, where or how much an action happens. So it describes a verb.

q: An aeroplane flies in the air mainly because of which force?
f: The curved wings make air move faster over the top, creating lower pressure above and an upward force called lift. Lift must be greater than or equal to weight to fly.

q: Which companion narrated the largest number of ahadith?
f: Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA) is reported to have narrated about 5374 ahadith, the most of any companion.

q: At which session of the All India Muslim League was the Lahore Resolution passed?
f: The Lahore Resolution was passed at the 27th annual session of the All India Muslim League, held at Lahore from 22 to 24 March 1940.

q: Which word comes first alphabetically in a dictionary: Adidas or Addida?
f: Both words start with AD. The third letter of Addida is D and of Adidas is I, and D comes before I, so Addida comes first.

q: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: I always have a problem ____ my laptop.
f: The correct phrase in English is 'have a problem with' something.

q: What is the antonym of obnoxious?
f: Obnoxious means very unpleasant or offensive, so its opposite is pleasant.

q: What is the antonym of disingenuous?
f: Disingenuous means not sincere or pretending to know less, so the opposite is candid, meaning frank and honest.

q: What is the antonym of spirited?
f: Spirited means full of energy and courage, so the opposite is lifeless or dull.

q: What is the meaning of the word astonished?
f: Astonished means greatly surprised or amazed.

q: In which year did the United States attack Afghanistan after the 9/11 events?
f: The US-led attack on Afghanistan began on 7 October 2001, after the attacks of 11 September 2001.

q: What is the average of the first five natural numbers?
f: The first five natural numbers are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Their sum is 15 and 15 / 5 = 3.

q: In aviation, in which unit is altitude commonly measured internationally?
f: International civil aviation standards use feet for altitude and flight levels.

q: In which year did Benazir Bhutto become Prime Minister of Pakistan for the second time?
f: Her first term was from 1988 to 1990 and her second term started in October 1993 after the 1993 elections.

q: Rana Bhagwandas, who served as acting Chief Justice of Pakistan, belonged to which religious community?
f: Rana Bhagwandas was a Hindu from Sindh and became the first non-Muslim to serve as Chief Justice of Pakistan, in an acting capacity in 2007.

q: What is the approximate length of the Pakistan-China border according to most Pakistani textbooks?
f: Most Pakistani textbooks give the length of the border with China as about 523 km, running along the Karakoram range in Gilgit-Baltistan.

q: Which angel brought the message (revelation) of Allah to the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.)?
f: Hazrat Jibrail (A.S.) carried the revelation from Allah to the Prophet (S.A.W.). He is the angel of revelation.

q: If there are 2 cows and the number of camels is twice the number of cows, how many camels are there?
f: Camels = 2 x 2 = 4.

q: For how many years did Hazrat Abdul Muttalib take care of the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.) after his mother passed away?
f: The Prophet (S.A.W.) was 6 when his mother died and 8 when his grandfather died, so Abdul Muttalib cared for him for about 2 years.

q: What does the idiom 'to bell the cat' mean?
o: To take a dangerous task for the benefit of the group
f: The idiom comes from a fable in which mice wanted someone to tie a bell on the cat. It means to take on a risky task on behalf of others.

q: What is the antonym of the word charming?
f: Charming means pleasing and attractive. The opposite is unattractive or ugly.

q: Who was the Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan before General Asim Munir?
f: General Qamar Javed Bajwa served as Chief of Army Staff from November 2016 to November 2022. General Asim Munir then took over from him.

q: What is the common difference in the series 2, 6, 10, 14?
f: Each term is 4 more than the one before: 6 - 2 = 4, 10 - 6 = 4, 14 - 10 = 4.

q: What is the conjugate of the complex number 8 - 3i?
f: The conjugate of a + bi is a - bi, so the sign of the imaginary part changes: 8 + 3i.

q: What is the idiom to throw cold water on something?
f: To throw cold water on a plan or idea means to discourage it or show doubt about it.

q: In a field there is 1 cow, the donkeys are twice the number of cows, and there are 7 horses. How many animals are in the field?
f: Donkeys are 2 times 1, which is 2. Total animals are 1 cow plus 2 donkeys plus 7 horses, which is 10.

q: What is the derivative of 2x sin x with respect to x?
f: Use the product rule: d/dx (u v) = u'v + u v' with u = 2x and v = sin x. This gives 2 sin x + 2x cos x.

q: What is the derivative of ln x with respect to x?
f: The natural logarithm ln x has derivative 1/x for x greater than zero. This is a standard result of calculus.

q: Where is the Kot Diji fort located, in terms of district?
f: Kot Diji is a town in Khairpur district of Sindh. Its fort was built by the Talpur rulers.

q: Which of the following is a three-dimensional shape?
f: A cube has length, width and height, so it is three-dimensional. Square, triangle and circle are flat two-dimensional shapes.

q: Which of these antonyms is opposite in meaning to 'disgusting'?
f: Disgusting means very unpleasant. Delightful is the opposite, meaning very pleasant.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'disgusting'?
f: Disgusting means causing strong dislike or sickness. Revolting has nearly the same meaning.

q: Which group of vitamins does not dissolve in water?
f: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble. They dissolve in fat and not in water.

q: In which division of Balochistan is Gwadar located?
f: Gwadar district is part of Makran Division in southwestern Balochistan.

q: How many districts does Punjab (Pakistan) have at present?
f: Punjab has 41 districts grouped into 10 divisions. A claim of 45 districts was officially rejected.

q: Which document served as the basis for the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan?
f: The Objective Resolution of 1949 became the preamble and guiding basis of the constitutions of Pakistan, including 1973.

q: Article 25-A of the Constitution of Pakistan deals with which right?
f: Article 25-A, added by the 18th Amendment in 2010, gives free and compulsory education to children aged 5 to 16.

q: For about how long did the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan remain in force?
f: It was enforced on 23 March 1956 and abrogated in October 1958. This is about two and a half years.

q: Which of the following lists the elementary row operations of a matrix?
f: A row can be swapped with another, multiplied by a non-zero constant, or have a multiple of another row added to it.

q: What is the meaning of the idiom 'to end in smoke'?
f: The idiom means that a plan or effort fails and produces no result.

q: Mount Everest is part of which mountain range?
f: Mount Everest lies in the Mahalangur sub-range of the Himalayas on the Nepal and China (Tibet) border.

q: Which of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still exists today?
f: The Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt is the only one of the original seven wonders that still stands.

q: Ali is 2 years old and Faraz is twice Ali's age. How old is Faraz?
f: Faraz's age = 2 x 2 = 4 years.

q: Which prophet was thrown into fire by Namrood (Nimrod)?
f: Namrood threw Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) into a big fire, but Allah made it cool and safe for him.

q: What is the synonym of the word fondness?
f: Fondness means a feeling of liking or love, which is the same as affection.

q: What is the antonym of the word fondness?
f: Fondness means liking, so its opposite is dislike.

q: From which ruler did Muhammad bin Qasim conquer Sindh in 712 AD?
f: Muhammad bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir, the Brahman ruler of Sindh, in 712 AD.

q: Which city of Pakistan is known as the City of Gardens?
f: Lahore is called the City of Gardens because of its many Mughal and public gardens such as Shalimar and Jinnah Garden.

q: Greenland is an autonomous territory of which country?
f: Greenland is a self-governing territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.

q: Who was Hazrat Sarah (AS)?
o: Wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS)
f: Hazrat Sarah was the first wife of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) and the mother of Prophet Ishaq (AS).

q: What does the Arabic word Hijrat mean?
f: Hijrat means to leave one's homeland and migrate to another place, especially for the sake of faith.

q: What does the idiom "to pick holes" mean?
f: To pick holes in something means to look for its weak points and criticise it.

q: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: We are pinning all our hopes ___ the new manager.
f: The correct phrase is "pin hopes on someone", meaning to depend on that person for success.

q: What is an identity matrix?
o: A square matrix with all elements zero
A square matrix with 1 on the main diagonal and 0 elsewhere
A matrix with only one row
A matrix with all elements equal to 1
f: An identity matrix is a square matrix whose main diagonal elements are all 1 and all other elements are 0.

q: Which famous event took place in 8 Hijri?
f: The Muslims conquered Makkah peacefully in Ramadan 8 AH.

q: What is the main use of insulin in medicine?
f: Insulin is a hormone that controls blood sugar, so it is given to diabetic patients who cannot make enough of it.

q: Who was Iskander Ali Mirza?
o: The first Governor General of Pakistan
The first Prime Minister of Pakistan
The first Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan
f: Iskander Ali Mirza became Governor General in 1955 and then the first President of Pakistan under the 1956 Constitution.

q: What is the synonym of the word 'indigenous'?
f: Indigenous means originating in or belonging naturally to a place, which is the meaning of native.

q: On what date did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations?
f: Pakistan was admitted to the United Nations on 30 September 1947, a few weeks after independence.

q: Pakistan is mainly what kind of country in terms of its economy and land use?
f: Agriculture is the backbone of Pakistan's economy and a large part of its population depends on it.

q: Who is the Federal Minister for Law and Justice of Pakistan?
f: Azam Nazeer Tarar is the Federal Minister for Law and Justice in the present government, as reported in 2026.

q: Which letter comes next in the series: Z, Y, X, ?
f: The letters go backward in the alphabet one place at a time: Z, Y, X, then W.

q: How many daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) died during his lifetime?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) had four daughters. Zainab, Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum (RA) died in his lifetime, and only Fatimah (RA) died after him, about six months later.

q: Who liberated Jerusalem (Bait-ul-Muqaddas) from the Crusaders in 1187 AD?
f: Salahuddin Ayyubi defeated the Crusaders in the Battle of Hattin in 1187 and then took back Jerusalem. He was the founder of the Ayyubid dynasty.

q: Which is the longest river of Pakistan, also called the Sindh river?
f: The Indus River is about 2,900 km long and is the longest river of Pakistan. It is also called Sindh or Abaseen.

q: Which wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was known as Umm-ul-Masakin (Mother of the Poor)?
f: Hazrat Zainab bint Khuzaimah (RA) was famous for feeding and helping the poor, so she was called Umm-ul-Masakin.

q: What does the word burgle mean?
o: To enter a building illegally in order to steal
f: To burgle means to break into a house or building to steal things, and the person who does it is a burglar.

q: What is the meaning of the word compact?
o: Closely packed and small in size
f: Compact means closely and neatly packed together, and taking little space.

q: In which year did Pakistan become a member of the World Bank?
f: Pakistan joined the World Bank and the IMF on 11 July 1950.

q: In which game has Pakistan won Olympic gold medals?
f: Pakistan won Olympic gold three times in hockey, in 1960, 1968 and 1984.

q: What is the commonly quoted range of Pakistan's Babur (Hatf-VII) cruise missile?
f: The Babur ground-launched cruise missile, first tested in 2005, is commonly given a range of about 700 km. Newer versions are reported with different ranges.

q: What is the antonym of modesty?
f: Modesty means not showing off or thinking too highly of oneself. The opposite is arrogance, which is excessive pride.

q: Which mountain range lies along the Sindh side of Pakistan, on the border with Balochistan?
f: The Kirthar Range runs north to south along the Sindh and Balochistan border. Its highest point is Zardak Peak.

q: Which holy book was revealed on Hazrat Musa (AS)?
f: The Torah (Taurat) was revealed to Hazrat Musa (AS) on Mount Tur.

q: What comes next in the series: Z3, W5, T7, ?
f: The letters go back by 3 each time: Z, W, T, Q. The numbers go up by 2: 3, 5, 7, 9. So the next term is Q9.

q: Where is the headquarters of NASA located?
f: NASA, the United States space agency, has its headquarters in Washington, D.C.

q: What does NATO stand for?
f: NATO stands for North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance formed in 1949.

q: Who was Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar?
o: A leader of the Pakistan Movement and Governor of Punjab
The first Prime Minister of Pakistan
f: Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar was a senior Muslim League leader and a close associate of Quaid-e-Azam. He later served as Governor of Punjab.

q: What is the synonym of the word notorious?
f: Notorious means widely known for something bad, which is the same as infamous.

q: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence: He ___ Lahore by now.
f: The phrase by now needs the present perfect tense, which is has reached.

q: What does NWFP stand for?
f: NWFP stands for North-West Frontier Province, the old name of today's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word obnoxious?
f: Obnoxious means extremely unpleasant or offensive.

q: Into how many parts (quadrants) do the x-axis and the y-axis divide the coordinate plane?
f: The x-axis and y-axis cross at the origin and divide the plane into four parts called quadrants.

q: What is the ordered triple (three ordered numbers) written as?
f: A pair has two components, written (a, b). A triple has three ordered components, written (a, b, c).

q: What is the meaning of the word overt?
f: Overt means done or shown openly, not hidden.

q: What is the antonym of the word pacifist?
f: A pacifist is a person who opposes war and violence. An aggressive or warlike person is the opposite.

q: Choose the correct verb: The captain and his team ___ participating.
f: The captain and his team is a compound (plural) subject, so a plural verb such as were is needed. The singular forms is and is being do not agree.

q: There are 30 passengers in a bus and one third of them are men, the rest are women. What is the percentage of women?
f: Women = 2/3 of the passengers. 2/3 x 100 = 66.67 percent.

q: What is 30 percent of 30?
Which tense is used in the sentence 'Girls are playing in the garden'?
f: The verb phrase 'are playing' is is/am/are plus verb-ing, which shows an action happening now. This is the present continuous tense.

q: Who was the Prime Minister of Pakistan when Gwadar was handed over to Pakistan by Oman in 1958?
f: Gwadar was bought from Oman and formally became part of Pakistan on 8 September 1958. Feroz Khan Noon was Prime Minister at that time.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of the word 'preceding'?
f: Preceding means coming before. Its opposite is following, which means coming after.

q: What is a prime number?
o: A number with exactly two factors, 1 and itself
f: A prime number is greater than 1 and has only two factors, 1 and itself. For example 7 has only the factors 1 and 7.

q: What is the dot product of the unit vectors i and j?
f: The unit vectors i and j are perpendicular, so i . j = cos 90 degrees = 0.

q: Which organ of the human body pumps blood throughout the body?
f: The heart is a muscular organ that contracts regularly and pushes blood through the blood vessels.

q: What is the meaning of the idiom 'smell a rat'?
o: To suspect that something is wrong
f: The idiom means to sense that something is dishonest or wrong.

q: What type of number is 11/7?
f: 11/7 is a ratio of two integers with a non-zero denominator, so it is rational (and also real).

q: What was the immediate cause of the Second World War in 1939?
f: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939, and Britain and France then declared war on Germany.

q: Which angel is responsible for rain and provision according to Islamic belief?
f: In Islamic tradition Hazrat Mikael (Michael) is the angel in charge of rain and provision.

q: The square root of a prime number is always what kind of number?
f: A prime number is not a perfect square, so its square root cannot be written as a fraction of two integers. Hence it is irrational.

q: Which of the following Pakistani batters has scored a Test triple century?
f: Younis Khan scored 313 against Sri Lanka at Karachi in 2009.

q: What is the capital city of Saudi Arabia?
f: Riyadh is the capital and largest city of Saudi Arabia.

q: In which year was SEATO (South East Asia Treaty Organization) established?
f: SEATO was formed in September 1954 under the Manila Pact.

q: How many seats did the National Assembly have under the original 1973 Constitution (general plus reserved women seats)?
f: The 1973 Constitution provided 200 general seats and 10 seats reserved for women, so 210 in all.

q: If A and B are two sets, what is the set A union B?
o: The set of elements common to both A and B
The set of all elements in A or in B or in both
The set of elements in A but not in B
f: The union of A and B (written A U B) contains every element that belongs to A, to B, or to both.

q: Shahzia Sikander, who is well known internationally, is a Pakistani-born what?
f: Shahzia Sikander, born in Lahore in 1969, is a contemporary visual artist famous for reinventing Indo-Persian miniature painting.

q: Which prophet is famous for building the ship (ark) that saved the believers from the great flood?
f: Allah ordered Hazrat Nuh (Noah) AS to build a ship, and he saved the believers and pairs of animals in it from the flood.

q: Your age is 3 years and your sister is twice your age. What will be your sister's age when you are 23 years old?
f: Your sister is 3 x 2 = 6 now, so she is 3 years older. When you are 23 she will be 23 + 3 = 26.

q: What is the antonym of 'sloppy'?
f: Sloppy means careless or untidy, so its opposite is neat or careful.

q: What is a synonym of 'sloppy'?
f: Sloppy means done without care or attention, which is the same as careless.

q: In which year of the Hijri calendar does the Islamic calendar start?
f: The Hijri calendar starts from the migration of the Prophet (PBUH) from Makkah to Madinah. That year is counted as 1 AH.

q: What is the process of changing water into steam called?
f: When water is heated it changes from liquid to vapour (steam). This change is called evaporation or vaporization.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to barbarous?
f: Barbarous means cruel and uncivilised, which is close to savage.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to viciousness?
f: Viciousness means fierce, brutal behaviour, which is cruelty.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to abandon?
f: To abandon is to leave completely, which is to desert.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to achieve?
f: To achieve something is to succeed in doing it, that is to accomplish it.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to eminent?
f: Eminent means famous and respected, which is prominent.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to fragrant?
f: Fragrant means having a sweet smell, which is aromatic.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to frustration?
f: Frustration is the feeling of being upset when things do not work out, close to disappointment.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to refrain?
f: To refrain is to hold oneself back from doing something, which is to abstain.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to stingy?
f: Stingy means unwilling to spend money, which is miserly.

q: Ali is 12 years old and he is three times as old as his sister. When Ali is 15 years old, how old will his sister be?
f: Sister's age now = 12 / 3 = 4 years. Ali will be 15 after 3 years, so the sister will be 4 + 3 = 7 years.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will the sister be when Ali is 15 years old?
f: Sister's age now = 5 x 3 = 15. Ali needs 10 more years to reach 15, so the sister will be 15 + 10 = 25 years.

q: Sara is three times as old as Ali. If Ali is 4 years old, how old will Sara be when Ali is 8 years old?
f: Sara's age now = 4 x 3 = 12. Ali becomes 8 after 4 years, so Sara will be 12 + 4 = 16 years.

q: The Battle of the Trench (Khandaq) is connected with which Surah of the Holy Quran?
f: The events of the Battle of the Trench (also called Ahzab, the Confederates) are described in Surah Al-Ahzab.

q: What is a right angled triangle?
o: A triangle with all angles less than 90 degrees
A triangle with one angle of 90 degrees
A triangle with one angle more than 90 degrees
A triangle with all sides equal
f: A right angled triangle has exactly one angle equal to 90 degrees.

q: In an upper triangular matrix, what are the entries below the main diagonal?
o: All equal to the diagonal entries
f: A matrix is upper triangular when every entry below the main diagonal is zero, and the nonzero entries lie on or above the diagonal.

q: What is the synonym (closest meaning) of "trivial"?
f: "Trivial" means of very little value or importance, which is the same as insignificant.

q: What type of number is 7?
f: 7 can be written as 7/1, a ratio of two integers, so it is a rational number.

q: What does the name Uhud mean?
f: Uhud means standing alone, as the mountain stands separate from the other hills near Madina.

q: Bani Israel (the Ummah of Israel) belonged to which prophet?
f: Bani Israel were the people to whom Hazrat Musa (AS) was sent, and he led them out of Egypt.

q: What is the antonym of the word undaunted?
f: Undaunted means fearless, so its opposite is fearful, meaning easily frightened.

q: What is the meaning of the word vague?
f: Vague describes something that is unclear or lacks precise detail. Its synonyms are unclear and indefinite.

q: What is the meaning of veto power?
o: The right to reject or block a decision
The right to call a meeting
The right to join the UN
f: Veto is Latin for I forbid. It is the power to stop a resolution or decision even if others support it.

q: What is the pH value of pure water at room temperature?
f: Pure water is neutral, so its pH is 7.

q: Which Pakistani leader was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan to visit China, in 1956?
f: Huseyn Shaheed Suhrawardy visited China in October 1956 while he was Prime Minister.

q: Who wrote the Urdu poetry book Bang-e-Dara?
f: Bang-e-Dara is the first Urdu poetry collection of Allama Muhammad Iqbal.

q: What is the result when a real number is divided by zero?
f: Division by zero has no meaning in mathematics, so the result is undefined.

q: What is 90 / 60 in its simplest form as a decimal?
f: Divide both by 30 to get 3/2, which equals 1.5.

q: A train covers 100 km in 1 hour. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes at the same speed?
f: 12 minutes is 12/60 = 1/5 of an hour. Distance = 100 x 1/5 = 20 km.

q: How many inches are equal to 100 meters (to the nearest whole number)?
f: 1 meter is about 39.37 inches. So 100 meters = 100 x 39.37 = 3937 inches.

q: What is 0.001 x 100?
f: Multiplying by 100 moves the decimal point two places to the right: 0.001 becomes 0.1.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 11th be?
f: From the 1st to the 11th is 10 days. 10 divided by 7 leaves 3, so Monday + 3 = Thursday.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Friday, what day will the 11th be?
f: From the 1st to the 11th is 10 days. 10 divided by 7 leaves 3, so Friday + 3 = Monday.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 11th be?
f: From the 1st to the 11th is 10 days. 10 divided by 7 leaves 3, so Sunday + 3 = Wednesday.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 1300 are present. How many students are absent?
f: Absent students = 1500 - 1300 = 200.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what days will the 12th and the 15th be?
f: 12th: 11 days after Monday, 11 mod 7 = 4, so Friday. 15th: 14 days after Monday is exactly two weeks, so Monday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 17th be?
f: From the 2nd to the 17th is 15 days. 15 divided by 7 leaves 1, so Friday + 1 = Saturday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Thursday, what day will the 18th be?
f: From the 4th to the 18th is 14 days, exactly two weeks, so the weekday is the same: Thursday.

q: Whom did the British hold mainly responsible for the War of Independence of 1857?
f: The British blamed the Muslims for the 1857 uprising, since the Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar was its symbolic leader.

q: Which English letters are the 23rd, 18th, 22nd and 12th letters of the alphabet, in that order?
f: Counting A=1: 23 is W, 18 is R, 22 is V and 12 is L.

q: Which political party was in power in the areas that became Pakistan at the time of independence in 1947 and led the movement for Pakistan?
f: The All India Muslim League led by Quaid-e-Azam formed the first government of Pakistan in 1947.

q: On what date was the Objectives Resolution passed by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?
f: The Objectives Resolution was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan and passed on 12 March 1949.

q: What is the border agreement signed between China and Pakistan in 1963 known as?
f: On 2 March 1963 Pakistan and China signed the Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement fixing the border in the north.

q: On what date was the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan enforced?
f: The 1962 Constitution was announced on 1 March 1962 and came into force on 8 June 1962.

q: In which year did the First World War start?
f: The First World War began in 1914 after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand.

q: What is 100% of 200?
f: 100% means the whole amount, so 100% of 200 is 200.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 23rd be?
f: From the 1st to the 23rd is 22 days. 22 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1, so the day is one after Sunday, which is Monday.

q: What is the value of cos 240 degrees?
f: cos 240 = cos(180 + 60) = -cos 60. Since cos 60 is 1/2, the answer is -1/2.

q: A train travels 15 km on 1 litre of fuel. How many litres are needed to travel 300 km?
f: Litres needed = 300 divided by 15 = 20.

q: What is 44% of 350?
f: 44% of 350 = 44 times 350 divided by 100 = 154.

q: What is 497 divided by 497?
f: Any non-zero number divided by itself is 1.

q: What is 20 percent of 500?
f: 20% of 500 = 20 times 500 divided by 100 = 100.

q: What is 5% of 700?
f: 5% of 700 = 5 times 700 divided by 100 = 35.

q: If the price of 20 bottles is 800, what is the price of 5 bottles?
f: One bottle costs 800 divided by 20 = 40. Five bottles cost 5 times 40 = 200.

q: In which valley is Abbottabad located?
f: Abbottabad lies in the Orash Valley in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, between the Sarban and Shimla hills.

q: What is the full form of the abbreviation HCF?
f: HCF stands for Highest Common Factor, the largest number that divides two or more numbers exactly.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 1360 are present. What is the percentage of absent students, to two decimal places?
f: Absent students = 1500 - 1360 = 140. Percentage = 140 divided by 1500 times 100 = 9.33%.

q: In Surah Al-Muzzammil, by what word is the Prophet (PBUH) addressed?
f: The surah opens with Ya ayyuhal-Muzzammil, meaning O you who are wrapped up in garments. This is how Allah addresses the Prophet (PBUH) there.

q: What is the meaning of the word 'accomplish'?
f: To accomplish something means to complete it or achieve it successfully. Its synonyms are achieve and fulfil.

q: Who is the Supreme Commander of the Pakistan Air Force, as of October 2026?
o: The Chief of the Air Staff
f: Under Article 243 of the Constitution, the supreme command of the armed forces is vested in the President. As of 2026 the President is Asif Ali Zardari.

q: An aircraft uses 80 gallons of fuel to travel 540 km. About how much fuel is needed for 700 km?
f: Fuel per km is 80 divided by 540. For 700 km: 80 x 700 / 540 = 56000 / 540 = about 103.7 gallons.

q: Who was Ali Bogra in Pakistan's history?
f: Muhammad Ali Bogra served as the third Prime Minister of Pakistan from 1953 to 1955. He earlier served as ambassador to the USA.

q: What is the meaning of the idiom 'once for all'?
f: Once for all (also once and for all) means finally and permanently, so it need not be done again.

q: What is the meaning of the phrase 'all and sundry'?
f: All and sundry means everyone, whoever they may be.

q: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, how many rivers is Pakistan allowed to use as its main share?
f: The three western rivers, Indus, Jhelum and Chenab, were given to Pakistan. The three eastern rivers, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, went to India.

q: Find the next term in the series: a1, b3, c5, ?
f: The letters go a, b, c, d in order. The numbers go 1, 3, 5, 7, increasing by 2, so the next term is d7.

q: Arrange the letters of the word SAID in alphabetical order.
f: The letters are S, A, I, D. In alphabetical order they are A, D, I, S, so the word is ADIS.

q: How many letters are there in the English alphabet?
f: The English alphabet runs from A to Z, which makes 26 letters.

q: Which triangle has two equal sides and two equal angles?
f: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides, and the angles opposite those sides are also equal.

q: Rearrange the letters of LEAPORD to make the name of an animal.
f: The letters L, E, A, P, O, R, D can be arranged to spell LEOPARD, which is a big cat.

q: What is another name for the Lahore Resolution of 1940?
f: The Lahore Resolution, passed on 23 March 1940, demanded separate Muslim states and is also called the Pakistan Resolution.

q: Who founded Microsoft and Apple respectively?
f: Microsoft was founded by Bill Gates (with Paul Allen) in 1975, and Apple was founded by Steve Jobs (with Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne) in 1976.

q: In which year was the national anthem of Pakistan first played publicly?
f: The anthem tune was first played publicly on 13 August 1950 during the visit of the Shah of Iran.

q: What is the antonym of debatable?
f: Debatable means open to argument, so the opposite is indisputable, meaning beyond argument.

q: What is the antonym of abundance?
f: Abundance means a very large quantity, and its opposite is scarcity, meaning shortage.

q: What is the antonym of acquiesce?
f: To acquiesce is to accept something without protest, so the opposite is to resist.

q: What is the antonym of acquittal?
f: Acquittal means a court declaring a person not guilty, so the opposite is conviction.

q: What is the antonym of ductile?
f: A ductile material can be drawn into wire, while a brittle material breaks easily, so brittle is the opposite.

q: What is the antonym of endow?
f: To endow is to provide with a quality or gift, so the opposite is to deprive.

q: What is the antonym of exception?
f: An exception is something that is left out of the general pattern, so the opposite is the rule.

q: What is the antonym of malicious?
f: Malicious means intending to harm, so the opposite is benevolent, meaning kind and well meaning.

q: What is the antonym of seize?
f: To seize is to take hold of by force, so the opposite is to release.

q: What is the antonym of soft?
f: Soft means easy to press or not firm, and the opposite is hard.

q: What is the antonym of vitalise?
f: To vitalise is to give life or energy to, so the opposite is to weaken.

q: Anwar is older than Ali, and Aslam is younger than Ali. Who is the oldest of the three?
f: Anwar is older than Ali and Ali is older than Aslam, so the order from oldest is Anwar, Ali, Aslam.

q: Aslam's age is three times Ali's age. After three years Ali's age will be 7 years. What is Aslam's present age?
f: Ali's present age is 7 - 3 = 4 years. Aslam is three times that, so 3 x 4 = 12 years.

q: Choose the correct word: I felt astonished ___ the sad news.
f: The adjective astonished is normally followed by the preposition at (or by) when it is used with news, so at fits the sentence.

q: What are the authentic (reliable) Ahadees called?
f: A hadith with a continuous chain of trustworthy narrators and no defect is called Sahih, meaning authentic.

q: What is the total area of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) as given in official Pakistani sources?
f: Official AJK government publications give the total area of Azad Jammu and Kashmir as 13,297 square kilometres (about 5,134 square miles).

q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Azad Jammu and Kashmir?
f: Under the 1974 interim constitution the post of Prime Minister was created, and Abdul Hamid Khan was elected the first Prime Minister of AJK in 1975.

q: Which word comes first in the dictionary: back, racket, biscuit?
f: Words are arranged by their first letter: b comes before r. Between back and biscuit, the second letters a and i decide it, and a comes first, so the order is back, biscuit, racket.

q: What is the main theme of Surah Al-Furqan, whose name means the criterion?
o: The stories of the earlier nations only
The difference between right and wrong (truth and falsehood)
f: Furqan means that which separates truth from falsehood. The surah opens by saying Allah sent down the Furqan (the Quran) to distinguish right from wrong.

q: Near which place was the Battle of Badr fought?
o: Near the well of Badr, southwest of Madinah
f: The first major battle of Islam was fought in 2 AH at the wells of Badr, a valley about 150 km southwest of Madinah.

q: Which Mughal emperor built the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore?
f: The Badshahi Mosque was built by Emperor Aurangzeb Alamgir and completed in 1673.

q: In which year did Pakistan officially recognise Bangladesh as an independent country?
f: Pakistan recognised Bangladesh in February 1974, before the OIC Islamic Summit held in Lahore.

q: In which year was the Chashma Barrage on the Indus River completed?
f: The construction work on Chashma Barrage began after the contract of 1967 and was completed in March 1971.

q: Which number does not belong in the series: 1, 3, 6, 7, 9?
f: 1, 3, 7 and 9 are all odd numbers, while 6 is the only even number.

q: What was the date of birth of Major Rashid Minhas Shaheed (Nishan-e-Haider)?
f: Rashid Minhas was born on 17 February 1951; his family belonged to Kulyana in Jhelum district.

q: What is the normal pH of human blood?
f: Human blood is slightly alkaline, with a normal pH range of 7.35 to 7.45.

q: In which year was Shah Wali Ullah of Delhi born?
f: Shah Wali Ullah Muhaddith Dehlvi was born in Delhi in 1703 (1114 AH).

q: Fill in the blank: I bought it ____ 10 shillings.
f: The preposition for is used to show the price paid for something.

q: Who bought the valley of Kashmir from the British East India Company in 1846?
f: Under the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) Gulab Singh Dogra paid 7.5 million rupees to the British and received Kashmir.

q: Where is the famous Golden Gate Bridge located?
f: The Golden Gate Bridge spans the Golden Gate strait and connects San Francisco with Marin County in California.

q: What is the brother of your mother called in relation to you?
f: The brother of one's mother is called the maternal uncle, known as Mama in Urdu.

q: Which is larger, 1/2 or 6/12?
f: 6/12 divided by 6 on top and bottom gives 1/2, so both fractions have the same value.

q: Which is the largest peninsula in the world?
f: The Arabian Peninsula, with an area of about 3.2 million square kilometres, is the largest peninsula in the world.

q: Who is the author of the book Zulfi Bhutto of Pakistan: His Life and Times?
f: Stanley Wolpert, an American historian, wrote Zulfi Bhutto of Pakistan: His Life and Times, published in 1993.

q: Which woman of the Makhzum tribe, caught for theft, was brought before the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.) for judgement?
f: A noble woman of Banu Makhzum named Fatima bint Aswad was caught stealing and brought to the Prophet (S.A.W.). He said the law applies equally to all and that even if Fatima, daughter of Muhammad, stole, her hand would be cut.

q: Which of the following is the tallest completed building in Karachi?
f: Bahria Icon Tower in Karachi has 62 floors and is the tallest completed building in the city. Older towers such as Habib Bank Plaza are shorter.

q: A is the father of B, but B is not the son of A. What is B to A?
f: B is a child of A, but not a son, so B must be a daughter.
