q: Who were the first and second Caliphs of Islam?
o: Hazrat Abu Bakr and Hazrat Umar (R.A.)
Hazrat Abu Bakr and Hazrat Ali (R.A.)
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (R.A.) was the first Caliph and Hazrat Umar Farooq (R.A.) was the second.

q: What is the capital of Portugal?
f: Lisbon is the capital and largest city of Portugal.

q: What is the capital of Sudan?
f: Khartoum is the capital of Sudan, at the meeting of the Blue Nile and White Nile.

q: Which option correctly lists the capitals of Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan in that order?
f: The provincial capitals are Lahore (Punjab), Karachi (Sindh), Peshawar (KPK) and Quetta (Balochistan).

q: Who was the caretaker Chief Minister of Punjab in 2023 to 2024?
f: Mohsin Naqvi served as caretaker Chief Minister of Punjab from January 2023 until February 2024.

q: Who was the caretaker Prime Minister of Pakistan in 2023 to 2024?
f: Anwaar-ul-Haq Kakar led the caretaker government from August 2023 to March 2024.

q: What is the main natural source of ultraviolet (UV) rays?
f: The Sun is the main natural source of UV rays. Most of the harmful UV is absorbed by the ozone layer.

q: Infections are caused by which of the following?
o: Harmful microorganisms such as bacteria and viruses
f: Infections are caused by pathogens, which are harmful microorganisms like bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites.

q: Who was the companion of the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.) in the Cave of Thawr during the Hijrat?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (R.A.) accompanied the Prophet (S.A.W.) and hid with him in the Cave of Thawr during the migration to Madinah.

q: In which year was the second census of Pakistan held?
f: Pakistan's censuses were held in 1951, 1961, 1972, 1981, 1998, 2017 and 2023, so the second was in 1961.

q: What is the synonym of the word charming?
f: Charming means pleasing and delightful, which is close to attractive.

q: What is the synonym of the word cherish?
f: To cherish means to hold something dear, which is the same as to treasure it.

q: What is the total number of squares on a chess board?
f: A chess board has 8 rows and 8 columns, so 8 x 8 = 64 squares.

q: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) was established in which year?
f: ICAO was established in 1947 after the Chicago Convention on International Civil Aviation was signed in 1944.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to idiom?
f: An idiom is a fixed expression whose meaning is different from the meanings of its separate words.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to audacity?
f: Audacity means a willingness to take bold risks, so boldness is the closest.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to coil?
f: To coil means to wind into a series of loops or rings, like a spiral.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to deeper?
f: Deeper means going further down or more profound.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to edge?
f: The edge of something is its outer limit, which means its border or rim.

q: What is a javelin?
f: A javelin is a light spear that is thrown, and it is used in athletics.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to rear?
f: Rear means the back part of something. As a verb it also means to raise a child.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to specific?
f: Specific means clearly defined and exact, which is precise.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to sustain?
f: To sustain means to keep something going or support it over time.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to conspiracy?
f: A conspiracy is a secret plan by a group to do something harmful or illegal, which is a plot.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to instructions?
f: Instructions are details telling someone what to do, which means directions.

q: A translucent object is one that
o: lets no light pass at all
lets light pass but we cannot see clearly through it
lets light pass so we see perfectly clearly
f: A translucent object lets some light pass but scatters it, so we cannot see clearly through it. Frosted glass is an example.

q: What is the chemical (Latin) name from which the symbol Au of gold comes?
f: Gold has the symbol Au, which comes from its Latin name Aurum.

q: Where is the head office of the International Energy Agency (IEA)?
f: The IEA has its headquarters in Paris, France.

q: In a committee of 24 members, 6 are men. What percentage of the committee is women?
f: Women = 24 - 6 = 18. Percentage = 18 / 24 x 100 = 75%.

q: Who is credited in most Pakistani textbooks with first presenting the Two Nation Theory?
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan first spoke clearly of Hindus and Muslims as two separate nations in the late 1860s and 1870s.

q: How many nuclear tests did Pakistan conduct at Chagai on 28 May 1998?
f: Pakistan conducted five nuclear tests at the Chagai hills on 28 May 1998.

q: In which year was the 2nd OIC (Islamic Summit) conference held in Lahore?
f: The second Islamic Summit Conference was held in Lahore in February 1974.

q: Which Muslim commander conquered Egypt in the time of Hazrat Umar (RA)?
f: Hazrat Amr bin Al-As conquered Egypt around 640 AD during the caliphate of Hazrat Umar (RA).

q: In which Ghazwa (battle) with the Prophet (PBUH) were the most companions martyred?
f: About 70 companions were martyred in the Battle of Uhud, the highest number among the battles fought with the Prophet (PBUH) present.

q: With which tribe did the Muslims fight in the Battle of Badr?
f: The Battle of Badr in 2 AH was fought between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.

q: What is a collection of well defined distinct objects called?
f: In mathematics a well defined collection of distinct objects is called a set.

q: In which year was Warsak Dam, on the Kabul River near Peshawar, completed?
f: Warsak Dam was built in the 1950s and early 1960s under the Colombo Plan with Canadian help. Its first phase, including the dam and four 40 MW units, was completed in 1960.

q: On which river is Rawal Dam, which supplies water to Rawalpindi and Islamabad, constructed?
f: Rawal Dam is an earth-fill dam built on the Korang River in Islamabad. It stores water for the twin cities.

q: Iceland lies in which continent?
f: Iceland is an island nation in the North Atlantic Ocean. It is counted as part of Europe.

q: If 7 pairs of shoes cost Rs. 3500, what is the cost of one pair?
f: Cost of one pair equals 3500 divided by 7, which is 500.

q: A train covers 120 km in 1 hour. How many km will it cover in 12 minutes?
f: Speed is 120 km/h, which is 2 km per minute. In 12 minutes it covers 2 times 12, which is 24 km.

q: A train moves at twice the speed of a car. If the car covers 120 km in 60 minutes, in how many minutes will the train cover 120 km?
f: Car speed is 120 km/h, so train speed is 240 km/h. Time for 120 km is 120 divided by 240, which is half an hour, or 30 minutes.

q: You have five cows and 3 times as many goats. How many animals do you have in total?
f: Goats are 3 times 5, which is 15. Total is 5 plus 15, which is 20.

q: Approximately how long is the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) route from Kashgar to Gwadar?
f: CPEC links Kashgar in western China with Gwadar Port in Balochistan. The most commonly quoted length is about 3000 km.

q: What is the cube root of 196, correct to two decimal places?
f: 5.81 cubed is about 196.1, and 5.8 cubed is about 195.1, so the cube root of 196 is about 5.81. It is not a perfect cube.

q: What is the cube root of 1?
f: 1 times 1 times 1 equals 1, so the cube root of 1 is 1.

q: What is the currency of Afghanistan?
f: The official currency of Afghanistan is the Afghani (AFN). It is divided into 100 puls.

q: Which currency has the highest value per unit in the world?
f: The Kuwaiti Dinar (KWD) is worth more than any other currency unit, over 3 US dollars each. Its strength comes from Kuwait's oil wealth and tight currency policy.

q: In which direction from Karachi is Mohenjo-daro located?
f: Mohenjo-daro is near Larkana in northern Sindh, which lies north-east of Karachi. It is on the right bank of the Indus river.

q: On which date was Liaquat Ali Khan assassinated?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, was shot at a public meeting in Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951. The assassin Said Akbar was killed on the spot.

q: Which law or principle states that a body immersed in a fluid experiences an upward force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces?
f: This is the statement of Archimedes' principle. The upward force is called buoyant force and explains why ships float.

q: In which year was the Babri Mosque in Ayodhya demolished?
f: The Babri Mosque was demolished by Hindu extremist mobs on 6 December 1992. The event led to widespread riots in India.

q: Evaporation of water does NOT depend upon which of the following?
f: Evaporation happens at the surface, so it depends on temperature, surface area, humidity and wind. The depth of the water does not change the rate.

q: In which part of the world is the Gobi Desert located?
f: The Gobi is a large cold desert in East Asia. It covers parts of southern Mongolia and northern China.

q: Which nation, associated with the city of Iram in the Quran, was destroyed after rejecting Hazrat Hud (AS)?
f: The people of Aad, who lived in Iram of the pillars, rejected Hazrat Hud (AS). They were destroyed by a violent windstorm.

q: What is the determinant of a non-square matrix?
o: Equal to its number of rows
f: A determinant can be found only for a square matrix, with equal rows and columns. For a non-square matrix it does not exist.

q: In which year did Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk die?
f: Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk (Mushtaq Hussain) died in January 1917.

q: What is the common difference in the numbers of the series A4, B8, C12?
f: The numbers are 4, 8, 12 and the letters go A, B, C. The number difference is 8 - 4 = 4 and 12 - 8 = 4.

q: Which term is different in this series: A3, C5, E7, G9, I12?
f: Letters move by 2 (A, C, E, G, I) and numbers also move by 2 (3, 5, 7, 9, 11). The last term should be I11, so I12 is wrong.

q: Sidra is 5 years old and her brother is twice her age. How old is her brother?
f: Twice her age is 2 x 5 = 10 years. So the brother is 10 years old.

q: What is the antonym of 'dishonest'?
f: Dishonest means not truthful. Honest is its opposite.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'dishonest'?
f: Dishonest means untruthful or cheating. Deceitful has the same sense.

q: What is the distance between the points (4, 0) and (3, 0)?
f: Both points are on the x-axis, so the distance is the difference of x values: 4 - 3 = 1.

q: In which district of Balochistan is the Gwadar port located?
f: The port lies in Gwadar district, whose headquarters is Gwadar city.

q: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: The doctor gives him medicine ___ his cough.
f: We use 'for' to show the purpose or the illness being treated. So it is 'medicine for his cough'.

q: Horse is to mare as dog is to what?
f: A mare is a female horse. The female dog is called a bitch.

q: What is the domain of the function tan x?
o: All real numbers except odd multiples of pi/2
All real numbers except multiples of pi
f: tan x = sin x / cos x, which is undefined where cos x = 0. That happens at odd multiples of pi/2.

q: Under Article 25A of the 1973 Constitution, education is free and compulsory for children of which age group?
f: Article 25A says the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children from five to sixteen years.

q: The photoelectric effect is explained on the basis of which nature of light?
f: Einstein explained that light comes in packets of energy called photons, and one photon ejects one electron.

q: In which year was Allama Iqbal elected President of the All India Muslim League?
f: Iqbal presided over the Allahabad session of the Muslim League in 1930.

q: Who discovered the electron?
f: J.J. Thomson discovered the electron in 1897 using cathode ray experiments.

q: How many types of elementary row operations are there for a matrix?
f: The three types are interchanging two rows, multiplying a row by a non-zero number, and adding a multiple of one row to another row.

q: Seven boxes of powder weigh 49 kg in total, and one empty box weighs 1 kg. What is the weight of the powder in one box?
f: Each filled box weighs 49 / 7 = 7 kg. Taking out the 1 kg empty box leaves 6 kg of powder.

q: Which sentence is correct?
o: Making friends is more rewarding than to make enemies.
Making friend is more rewarding than making enemies.
Making friends is more rewarding than making enemies.
Make friends is more rewarding than making enemies.
f: Both parts of the comparison should have the same form, so both use the gerund: making friends and making enemies. Friends must also be plural.

q: Pakistan is to Asia as England is to what?
f: Pakistan is a country in the continent Asia, and England is a country in the continent Europe.

q: What is the currency of England?
f: England uses the pound sterling, the currency of the United Kingdom.

q: Which event made the USA enter World War 2?
f: Japan attacked the US naval base at Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941, and the USA declared war the next day.

q: Through which province of present-day Pakistan did Islam enter the subcontinent?
f: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 711 AD, so Islam spread into the subcontinent from Sindh.

q: What is drift velocity?
o: The speed of light in a conductor
The average velocity of free electrons in a conductor under an electric field
The speed of a charged particle in vacuum
The random speed of electrons without a field
f: Free electrons move randomly, but an electric field gives them a small net average velocity along the conductor. This is called drift velocity.

q: What does the idiom 'to drive home' mean?
o: To travel back to one's house
To emphasise a point so that it is clearly understood
f: To drive home a point means to make it very clear by stressing it strongly.

q: In a point (x, y) on the Cartesian plane, if y is called the ordinate, what is x called?
f: In coordinate geometry the x-coordinate is called the abscissa and the y-coordinate is called the ordinate.

q: In mathematics, ln x stands for which logarithm?
o: Logarithm of x to the base e (natural logarithm)
Logarithm of x to the base 10
Logarithm of x to the base 2
Logarithm of x to the base 1
f: The symbol ln means the natural logarithm, which is the logarithm to the base e.

q: Which term does the standard equation of a circle (x^2 + y^2 = r^2) NOT involve?
f: The equation of a circle with centre at the origin has only x^2, y^2 and r^2. There is no product term xy.

q: The equation y = 2x is called what type of equation?
f: Both x and y have power 1, so y = 2x is a linear equation, and its graph is a straight line.

q: In which year was the European Union formally established by the Maastricht Treaty?
f: The Maastricht Treaty came into force on 1 November 1993 and created the European Union.

q: Evaporation of water mainly takes place because of which of the following?
f: Heat gives water molecules enough energy to escape from the liquid surface as vapour.

q: What is the exact words of a speaker, quoted inside inverted commas, called in grammar?
f: Direct speech repeats the speaker's exact words in quotation marks.

q: What is the value of 6! (factorial of 6)?
The product of two numbers is 91 and one of them is 13. What is the other number?
Who was the first man to accept Islam (embrace faith) among adult men?
f: Most Pakistani textbooks say Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) was the first adult free man to accept Islam.

q: A train moves twice as fast as a car. If the car moves at 90 km/h, how far will the train go in 30 minutes?
f: Speed of the train = 2 x 90 = 180 km/h. Distance in 30 minutes (half an hour) = 180 x 1/2 = 90 km.

q: Ali and Farooq are brothers. Ali is three times as old as Farooq, and Farooq is now 4 years old. How old will Farooq be when Ali is 13 years old?
f: Ali's age now = 3 x 4 = 12. Ali will be 13 after 1 year, when Farooq will be 4 + 1 = 5.

q: Farooq is 10 years old and his sister is 4 times his age. How old will his sister be when Farooq is 20?
f: Sister's age now = 4 x 10 = 40. Farooq needs 10 more years to reach 20, so she will be 40 + 10 = 50.

q: Out of 1500 people, 1200 are male. What is the percentage of females?
Which is the biggest natural gas field of Pakistan?
f: The Sui gas field in Balochistan is the largest natural gas field in Pakistan.

q: In which city is the headquarters of FIFA located?
f: FIFA, the world football governing body, has its headquarters in Zurich, Switzerland.

q: Between which two groups of countries was World War 1 (1914-1918) mainly fought?
f: World War 1 was fought between the Allied Powers (Britain, France, Russia and later the USA) and the Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire and Bulgaria).

q: Naha, the capital of Okinawa Prefecture, is in which country?
f: Naha is the capital city of Okinawa Prefecture, which is part of Japan.

q: Choose the correct preposition: Stand ____ your friend in a critical situation.
f: To stand by someone means to support them, especially in difficulty.

q: Which type of energy is stored in fruits?
f: Fruits store energy in food molecules such as sugars, which is chemical energy released during digestion.

q: What was Hilf-ul-Fudul, in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) took part before prophethood?
o: A peace pact to help the oppressed and the weak
A treaty with the Jews of Madina
f: Hilf-ul-Fudul was a pact made by several Makkan tribes to protect the rights of the oppressed and the travellers.

q: Who gets the benefit of the NFC Award?
o: The federal government and the provinces
f: The National Finance Commission Award decides how the divisible tax revenue is shared between the federal government and the provinces.

q: For what are the people of ancient Gandhara famous?
f: Gandhara is famous for Gandhara art, a style of Buddhist sculpture that mixed Greek and Indian influences.

q: Mahatma Gandhi is famous for what?
o: Leading the Indian freedom movement through non-violence
f: Gandhi led the Indian independence struggle against British rule with non-violent civil disobedience.

q: Which of the following are greenhouse gases?
f: Carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and water vapour trap heat in the atmosphere and cause the greenhouse effect.

q: Which type of spectrum do monoatomic gases give?
f: Excited atoms emit light only at fixed wavelengths, so monoatomic gases give line (atomic) spectra.

q: How many general seats does the Provincial Assembly of Sindh have?
f: The Sindh Assembly has 168 seats in total: 130 general seats, 29 reserved for women and 9 for non-Muslims.

q: Fill in the blank: Ali gets angry very soon. He takes ____ his father.
f: To take after someone means to resemble them in character or looks.

q: Who is the current Governor of Gilgit-Baltistan (as of October 2026)?
f: Syed Mehdi Shah has been Governor of Gilgit-Baltistan since August 2022 and swore in the new Chief Minister in July 2026.

q: Who is the current Governor of Punjab (as of October 2026)?
f: Sardar Saleem Haider Khan of the PPP took oath as Governor of Punjab on 10 May 2024 and still holds the post.

q: Girl is to boy as woman is to what?
f: A girl is a young female and a boy is a young male. In the same way a woman is an adult female and a man is an adult male.

q: Which one is the odd one out: mango, guava, apple, potato?
f: Mango, guava and apple are fruits that grow on trees, while potato is a vegetable (an underground tuber).

q: What is the approximate total length of the Great Wall of China, according to the 2012 Chinese survey?
f: A Chinese state survey in 2012 measured all its wall sections at 21,196 km.

q: What is the name of the hadith book of Imam Bukhari (RA)?
f: Imam Bukhari compiled the collection called Al-Jami al-Sahih, known as Sahih al-Bukhari.

q: What is another name of the Khutba Hajjatul Wada?
f: Hajjatul Wada means the Farewell Pilgrimage, so the khutba is called the Last or Farewell Sermon.

q: For about how many years did General Zia ul Haq rule Pakistan?
f: Zia ul Haq took power on 5 July 1977 and remained in power until his death in a plane crash on 17 August 1988, which is about 11 years.

q: Who, as Viceroy of India, introduced separate electorates for Muslims through the reforms of 1909?
f: Lord Minto was Viceroy in 1909 and, with Secretary of State Lord Morley, brought the Morley-Minto Reforms that gave Muslims separate electorates. The demand had been made by the Simla Deputation of 1906.

q: What is the meaning of the idiom "to hit the nail on the head"?
o: To say or do exactly the right thing
f: The idiom means to describe a problem or give an answer that is exactly right. The usual form is "hit the nail on the head".

q: Fill in the blank: As I was hot, I ___ my coat.
f: Being hot, a person would remove the coat, and the phrasal verb for removing clothes is "took off". The past tense is needed because of "was".

q: Which place in Pakistan is famous for its natural hot springs?
f: Tatta Pani in Kotli district of Azad Kashmir is well known for its hot water springs. Its name means hot water in Urdu.

q: Which is the hottest desert in the world?
f: The Sahara in Africa is the largest hot desert and is generally called the hottest desert of the world.

q: According to the Holy Quran, for what purpose did Allah divide mankind into nations and tribes?
o: So that they may fight each other
So that they may know one another
So that some may rule others
f: Surah Al-Hujurat (49:13) says Allah made people into nations and tribes so that they may know one another.

q: Which gas in the air is essential for human breathing?
f: Humans need oxygen for respiration, which releases energy from food in the body cells.

q: Which country hosted the first ICC Cricket World Cup in 1975?
f: The first Cricket World Cup was played in England in June 1975 with 60-over matches.

q: Which team won the first ICC Cricket World Cup in 1975?
f: West Indies beat Australia in the 1975 final at Lord's, led by Clive Lloyd.

q: Identify the tense of the sentence: They are playing cricket.
f: The sentence uses "are" with the verb ending in -ing, which is the form of the present continuous tense.

q: What is the determinant of an identity matrix?
f: The determinant of a diagonal matrix is the product of its diagonal elements. For an identity matrix this is 1 x 1 x ... x 1 = 1.

q: What does the idiom "out and out" mean?
f: "Out and out" means complete or total, as in "an out and out liar".

q: What does the idiom "to cry wolf" mean?
f: To cry wolf is to give a false warning so that people do not believe you when real danger comes.

q: Which river is regarded as the most important river of Pakistan?
f: The Indus is the longest river of Pakistan and the main source of water for its agriculture and for the country's irrigation system.

q: What is the main purpose of zakat in Islam?
o: To increase the wealth of the rich
To reduce poverty and help the needy
f: Zakat is a compulsory share of wealth given to the poor and needy, which reduces the gap between rich and poor.

q: What is the synonym of "impoverished"?
f: Impoverished means very poor, and destitute has the same meaning.

q: In which province of Pakistan was the Sui gas field discovered and developed?
f: Sui is in the Dera Bugti district of Balochistan, and its gas field began supplying the country in the 1950s.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) located?
f: ICAO, a specialised agency of the United Nations, has its headquarters in Montreal, Canada.

q: Who invented the first practical photocopy (xerography) process?
f: Chester Carlson, an American inventor, made the first photocopy by the dry process called xerography in 1938.

q: Who is credited with inventing the radio (wireless telegraphy)?
f: Guglielmo Marconi developed practical wireless radio communication in the 1890s and is commonly credited as its inventor.

q: What is the multiplicative inverse of 3?
f: The multiplicative inverse of a number is the number that gives product 1 with it. Since 3 times 1/3 equals 1, the inverse is 1/3.

q: What is x^i times x^i, where i is iota (the square root of minus one)?
f: When the bases are the same, the powers are added: i + i = 2i, so the result is x^(2i).

q: Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the ___ of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
f: Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS), who was himself the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).

q: In which direction is Karachi located from Islamabad?
f: Islamabad is in the north (about 33.7 N, 73 E) and Karachi is far to the south and west (about 24.9 N, 67 E), so Karachi lies south-west of Islamabad.

q: Pakistan is to Islamabad as Japan is to ...?
f: Islamabad is the capital of Pakistan, and in the same way Tokyo is the capital of Japan.

q: What is the meaning of the idiom 'burning issue'?
o: A very urgent and widely discussed problem
f: A burning issue is an important and urgent problem that people are talking about and that needs a solution now.

q: What is the antonym of the word 'indigenous'?
f: Indigenous means native to a place, so its opposite is foreign or alien to that place.

q: On which date is the National Day (founding anniversary) of the People's Republic of China celebrated?
f: The People's Republic of China was proclaimed by Mao Zedong on 1 October 1949, and this day is its National Day.

q: What is a square matrix called when its transpose is equal to the matrix itself?
f: A square matrix A is symmetric when A transpose equals A, that is, a(i,j) = a(j,i) for all entries.

q: For how many million Nanakshahi rupees was Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh by the British under the Treaty of Amritsar (1846)?
f: By the Treaty of Amritsar in 1846 the British sold Jammu and Kashmir to Gulab Singh for 75 lakh (7.5 million) Nanakshahi rupees.

q: Justice Rana Bhagwandas, who served as a judge and acting Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Pakistan, belonged to which religion?
f: Rana Bhagwandas was a Hindu and was the first Hindu to serve as acting Chief Justice of Pakistan.

q: Who was the non-Muslim Chief Justice of Pakistan?
f: A. R. Cornelius, a Christian, was Chief Justice of Pakistan from 1960 to 1968.

q: In which year did Mustafa Kemal Ataturk abolish the Caliphate (Khilafat) in Turkey?
f: The Turkish Grand National Assembly abolished the Caliphate on 3 March 1924 under Mustafa Kemal.

q: Near which place in Pakistan does the Kabul River join the Indus River?
f: The Kabul River meets the Indus near Attock at Khairabad, where the clear Kabul water and the muddy Indus water can be seen side by side.

q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) marry Hazrat Khadija (RA)?
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was 25 years old when he married Hazrat Khadija (RA), who was about 40.

q: Which thermodynamic cycle is used in a jet (gas turbine) engine?
f: A jet engine works on the Brayton cycle: air is compressed, heated by burning fuel at constant pressure, and expanded through a turbine.

q: In which province is Dera Ismail Khan (DI Khan) located?
f: Dera Ismail Khan is a city and district in the south of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, on the west bank of the Indus River.

q: In which district is the tomb of Captain Karnal Sher Khan Shaheed (Nishan-e-Haider) located?
f: Karnal Sher Khan is buried in his home village in Swabi district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where a mausoleum marks his grave.

q: How many disbelievers (Quraish) marched to fight the Muslims in the Battle of Badr?
f: The Quraish army at Badr was about 1000 strong, while the Muslims were only about 313.

q: Which Mughal emperor built the Taj Mahal?
f: Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal at Agra as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

q: Who is known as the Gateway (Door) of Knowledge in Islamic tradition?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) is reported to have said that he is the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate, so Hazrat Ali (RA) is called Bab-ul-Ilm.

q: Which Prophet is known by the title Khalilullah (Friend of Allah)?
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalilullah because of his deep love and devotion to Allah.

q: When was the first railway line in the Indian subcontinent opened, between Bombay and Thane?
f: The first passenger train in India ran from Bombay (Bori Bunder) to Thane on 16 April 1853.

q: The name Adam is a word of which language?
f: Adam is a Hebrew word that is linked with the meaning man or earth.

q: Choose the correct word to fill the blank: It is ___ late.
f: The word too means more than is wanted, and it fits before the adjective late in this sentence.

q: Shariah (Islamic law) is mainly based on which two sources?
f: The two primary sources of Shariah are the Holy Quran and the Sunnah (sayings and actions) of the Prophet (PBUH).

q: Musaylima Kazzab, the false prophet, was the enemy leader in which battle?
f: Musaylima Kazzab claimed prophethood and led the Banu Hanifa against the Muslims. He was killed in the Battle of Yamamah in 632 AD during the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).

q: What is the meaning of the idiom 'at arm's length'?
o: At a safe distance, not too close
f: To keep someone at arm's length means to avoid becoming too close or familiar with them.

q: What is the literal meaning of the word Muhajireen?
f: Muhajireen is the plural of Muhajir, which means one who migrates. It is used for the Muslims who migrated from Makkah to Madina.

q: In which Surah is the command 'Stand up (to pray) at night, except a little'?
f: Surah Al-Muzzammil (73), verse 2, tells the Prophet (PBUH) to stand in prayer at night except for a small part.

q: In whose room did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) spend his last days and pass away?
f: During his last illness the Prophet (PBUH) took permission from his wives and stayed in the room of Hazrat Aisha (RA) in Madina, where he passed away in 11 AH.

q: In which year did the Black Lives Matter movement begin?
f: The phrase Black Lives Matter started as a hashtag in 2013 in the USA after the acquittal of the man who shot Trayvon Martin.

q: What is the characteristic of the common logarithm of 2179?
f: The number 2179 has 4 digits in its whole part, so the characteristic is 4 - 1 = 3.

q: What is the approximate value of log 0.9 (base 10)?
f: Since 0.9 is less than 1, its common logarithm is negative. Log 0.9 = log 9 - log 10 = 0.9542 - 1 = -0.0458.

q: Which country has the longest border with China?
f: China shares about 4,700 km of border with Mongolia, which is the longest, slightly more than its border with Russia.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: We look forward to win the match.
We look forward to winning the match.
We look forward to won the match.
We look forward for win the match.
f: The phrase look forward to is followed by a gerund (verb plus ing), because to is a preposition here. So winning is correct.

q: What is the meaning of the idiom 'to lose heart'?
f: To lose heart means to lose hope or courage and become discouraged.

q: What was the last major ghazwa of the Muslims against the Quraish of Makkah?
f: The Muslims conquered Makkah in 8 AH (630 CE), which ended the war with the Quraish.

q: In a class of 30 students, 2/3 are male. What is the percentage of males?
f: Percentage = 2/3 x 100 = 66.67%.

q: According to the Holy Quran, killing one innocent person is like killing whom?
f: Surah Al-Maidah (5:32) says that whoever kills one innocent soul, it is as if he killed all of mankind.

q: What is the meaning of the idiom "man of straw"?
o: A person of no substance or strength
f: A man of straw is a weak person or an imaginary opponent with no real substance.

q: Where is Masjid Qiblatain (Masjid-e-Zulqiblatain) located?
f: It is in Madinah, where the Prophet (PBUH) was leading prayer when the command came to turn towards the Kaaba.

q: What is the SI unit of mass?
f: The SI base unit of mass is the kilogram (kg).

q: What is the correct relation between the arithmetic mean (A.M), geometric mean (G.M) and harmonic mean (H.M) of positive numbers?
o: A.M is greater than or equal to G.M, which is greater than or equal to H.M
H.M is greater than or equal to G.M, which is greater than or equal to A.M
G.M is greater than or equal to A.M, which is greater than or equal to H.M
All three are always different and unrelated
f: For positive numbers, A.M is at least G.M, which is at least H.M, with equality only when all numbers are equal.

q: What are the signs for greater than and less than called in mathematics?
f: Signs like greater than and less than show that two quantities are not equal, so they are inequality symbols.

q: Which word fills the blank: You have not seen me ___ we met last time?
f: The present perfect tense (have not seen) is used with since to show a starting point in the past, so since is correct.

q: What does the word Hidayah mean?
f: Hidayah is an Arabic word meaning guidance, especially guidance to the right path.

q: What does the word Hukm mean?
f: Hukm is an Arabic word meaning command, order or ruling (judgement).

q: What does Fiqh mean?
f: Fiqh literally means deep understanding and is the science of deriving Islamic rules from the Quran and Sunnah.

q: Who are the Muhajirs in Islamic history?
o: Those Muslims who migrated from Makkah to Madina
f: Muhajir means one who migrates, and the term is used for the Companions who left Makkah and migrated to Madina.

q: What does the word Blind mean?
f: A blind person has no ability to see.

q: What does the word Climb mean?
f: To climb means to go up something such as a hill, tree or ladder.

q: What is the meaning of the word aqua?
f: Aqua comes from Latin and means water.

q: What is the meaning of the word coarsest?
f: Coarse means rough and not smooth, so coarsest means the most rough.

q: What is the meaning of the word decompose?
o: To rot or break down into simpler parts
f: To decompose means to break down into smaller parts, as dead plants and animals rot.

q: What is the meaning of the word expansive?
o: Wide-ranging or covering a large area
f: Expansive means covering a wide area or range, or friendly and open in manner.

q: What is the meaning of the word opaque?
o: Not allowing light to pass through
f: An opaque material blocks light, so one cannot see through it.

q: What is the meaning of the word polite?
f: A polite person is courteous and shows good manners to others.

q: What is the meaning of the word spongy?
o: Soft and full of small holes like a sponge
f: Spongy means soft, springy and porous like a sponge.

q: What is the meaning of the word stupid?
f: Stupid describes someone who shows poor judgement or lacks intelligence.

q: What is the meaning of the word suspicious?
o: Feeling or causing doubt and distrust
f: A suspicious person doubts others, and a suspicious thing causes doubt.

q: How many delegates attended the first session of the Indian National Congress in Bombay in 1885?
f: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay in December 1885 with 72 delegates.

q: In which game did Pakistan win its first Olympic medal?
f: Pakistan won its first Olympic medal, a silver in hockey, at Melbourne in 1956.

q: In which continent is Moscow, the capital of Russia, located?
f: Moscow lies on the Moskva River in the western part of Russia, which is in the European part of the country. So it is counted as a European city.

q: The Minto-Morley Reforms of 1909 were related to which country?
f: These reforms were the Indian Councils Act 1909, passed by the British government for British India. They gave Muslims separate electorates.

q: What is the minimum number of ayat (verses) in a surah of the Quran?
f: The shortest surahs, Al-Asr, Al-Kawthar and An-Nasr, each have 3 ayat. No surah has fewer.

q: Who is the current Foreign Minister of Pakistan (2026)?
f: Mohammad Ishaq Dar serves as Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Pakistan. He was still in office in August 2026 according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

q: Who was the first Finance Minister of Pakistan?
f: Malik Ghulam Muhammad was Finance Minister in the first cabinet of Liaquat Ali Khan in 1947. He later became the third Governor General.

q: In which year did Pakistan launch its first rocket into space, the Rehbar-1?
f: Rehbar-1 was launched from Sonmiani in Balochistan on 7 June 1962 by SUPARCO. It made Pakistan the third country in Asia and the tenth in the world to launch a rocket into space.

q: Find the missing number in the series: 66, 63, 56, 45, ?
f: The differences are minus 3, minus 7, minus 11, so the next difference is minus 15. Then 45 minus 15 equals 30.

q: What is the synonym of modesty?
f: Modesty means a humble and unassuming attitude. Humility has the same meaning.

q: Who are called Ummul-Momineen (Mothers of the Believers)?
o: Female companions who fought in battles
f: The Quran calls the wives of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) the mothers of the believers. This is a title of respect.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, which day will the 16th be?
f: From the 1st to the 16th is 15 days. 15 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1, so the day is one day after Monday, which is Tuesday.

q: Which two cities does the M-2 motorway connect?
f: The M-2 is the Lahore-Islamabad Motorway, about 367 km long. It opened in 1997.

q: A train is moving at 45 km per hour. How far will it travel in 5 minutes?
f: 5 minutes is 5/60 = 1/12 hour. Distance = 45 x 1/12 = 3.75 km.

q: Find the odd one out: Delhi, Ahmedabad, Mumbai, Sibbi.
f: Delhi, Ahmedabad and Mumbai are cities of India. Sibbi (Sibi) is a city of Balochistan, Pakistan.

q: Which term comes next in the series: B5, D7, F9, H11, ?
f: Letters skip one letter each time: B, D, F, H, J. Numbers go up by 2: 5, 7, 9, 11, 13. So the next term is J13.

q: Which number comes next: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, ?
f: The series is made of odd numbers, each 2 more than the one before. 9 + 2 = 11.

q: Which number comes next: 15, 11, 8, 6, ?
f: The differences are -4, -3, -2, so the next difference is -1. 6 - 1 = 5.

q: Which number is missing: 19, 38, 57, ?, 95
f: The numbers are multiples of 19: 19 x 1, 19 x 2, 19 x 3, 19 x 4 = 76, 19 x 5 = 95.

q: Which number comes next: 2, 5, 9, 14, ?
f: The differences are 3, 4, 5, so the next difference is 6. 14 + 6 = 20.

q: Which number comes next: 22, 17, 13, ?
f: The differences are -5, -4, so the next difference is -3. 13 - 3 = 10.

q: Which number comes next: 3, 9, 27, ?
f: Each term is multiplied by 3: 3 x 3 = 9, 9 x 3 = 27, 27 x 3 = 81.

q: Which number comes next: 63, 57, 45, ?
f: The differences are -6, -12, so the next is -24 (doubling each time). 45 - 24 = 21.

q: What is the mean of 6 and -9?
In the commonly taught order of the five pillars of Islam, at which number does Namaz (Salah) come?
f: The usual order taught in Pakistan is Kalima (Shahada), Salah, Roza (Sawm), Zakat and Hajj. So Salah is the second pillar.

q: In which continent is the River Nile located?
f: The Nile flows through northeastern Africa, mainly Uganda, Sudan and Egypt, and ends in the Mediterranean Sea.

q: What is the sum of 2^2 + 4^2 + 6^2 + ... + (2n)^2?
f: The sum is 4(1^2+2^2+...+n^2) = 4 x n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 = 2n(n+1)(2n+1)/3. Since 2n+2 = 2(n+1), option (a) gives 2n(2n+1) x 2(n+1)/6, which is the same.

q: What is the antonym of the word notorious?
f: Notorious means known for bad deeds, so its opposite is reputable, meaning having a good name.

q: Asad is 3 times as old as Amna when Amna is 6 years old. Now Amna is 10 years old. What is Asad's age now?
f: When Amna was 6, Asad was 3 x 6 = 18, so Asad is 12 years older. Now Amna is 10, so Asad is 10 + 12 = 22 years.

q: Ali is 3 years older than his brother. What will be Ali's age when his brother is 11 years old?
f: The age gap stays 3 years. When the brother is 11, Ali is 11 + 3 = 14 years.

q: If you can see through an object but the view is blurry, what is the object called?
f: A translucent object lets some light pass but scatters it, so things look blurry. A transparent object shows a clear view.

q: In which year was the Objective Resolution passed by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?
f: The Objective Resolution was passed on 12 March 1949 during the time of Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan.

q: In which month was Namaz made obligatory during the Mairaj?
f: The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the night of Mairaj, which is traditionally dated 27 Rajab.

q: In which year did the United States attack and occupy Afghanistan?
f: The US led an invasion of Afghanistan in October 2001 after the 9/11 attacks.

q: Which is the odd one out: India, Pakistan, China, Spain?
f: India, Pakistan and China are Asian countries, while Spain is in Europe.

q: Which is the official language of Pakistan, used in government alongside the national language Urdu?
f: The 1973 Constitution makes Urdu the national language and keeps English as the official language for government use.

q: What is the official name of the legislature of Pakistan?
f: The Parliament of Pakistan is officially called Majlis-e-Shoora and has the National Assembly and the Senate.

q: What was the old name of Beijing?
f: Beijing was long known in English as Peking.

q: Which word is the closest opposite of resentment?
f: Resentment is bitter anger over unfair treatment. Gratitude (thankfulness and goodwill) is its opposite feeling.

q: What is the opposite of the word clean?
f: Clean means free from dirt. The word with the opposite meaning is dirty.

q: What is the opposite of the word expensive?
f: Expensive means high in price. Cheap means low in price, so it is the opposite.

q: What is the opposite of the word retain?
f: Retain means to keep or continue to have something. Release (let go) is the opposite.

q: Which statement about the number 39 is correct?
o: It is an odd composite number
f: 39 is not divisible by 2, so it is odd. 39 = 3 x 13, so it has factors other than 1 and itself and is composite, not prime.

q: Which number cancels out 15 when the two are added together (the additive inverse of 15)?
f: 15 + (-15) = 0, so -15 cancels out 15 in addition.

q: What is the antonym of the word overt?
f: Overt means open and visible, while covert means hidden or secret.

q: What is a synonym of the word pacifist?
f: A pacifist believes in peace and rejects war, so peace lover (peacemaker) is a synonym.

q: In which city was the Pakistan-China boundary agreement of 1963 signed?
f: The agreement was signed in Beijing (then written Peking) on 2 March 1963 by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Chinese Foreign Minister Chen Yi.

q: On what basis is the Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chosen?
o: Elected by the members of the Provincial Assembly, as the leader of the majority
Elected directly by the people of the province
f: Under Article 130 of the Constitution, the Provincial Assembly elects the Chief Minister, who must command the confidence of the majority of members.

q: Who first suggested the name Pakistan?
f: Chaudhary Rahmat Ali, a Cambridge student, proposed the name Pakistan in his 1933 pamphlet Now or Never.

q: What is the meaning of the word panic?
f: Panic is a sudden strong fear that makes people act without thinking.

q: Which book is generally regarded as the first book written in the Pashto language?
f: Khair-ul-Bayan, written by Bayazid Ansari (Pir Roshan) in the 16th century, is generally regarded as the first Pashto book.

q: A bus has 30 passengers and two thirds of them are boys, the rest are girls. How many girls are there?
Change the narration into indirect speech: She said to me, "Can you give me your pen?"
o: She asked me if I could give her my pen.
She told me that can I give her my pen.
She said me whether I can give her pen.
She asked me that I can give me my pen.
f: A question in direct speech becomes a reporting verb asked plus if, and the tense and pronouns change: can becomes could, you becomes I, me becomes her.

q: A car travels at 60 km per hour. How much distance will it cover in 20 minutes?
f: 20 minutes is 20/60 = 1/3 of an hour. Distance = 60 x 1/3 = 20 km.

q: Approximately what percentage of Pakistan's population is non-Muslim according to the 2023 census?
f: The 2023 census gave Muslims 96.35 percent, which leaves about 3.65 percent non-Muslim.

q: What is 5/7 as a percentage (to two decimal places)?
f: 5 divided by 7 = 0.714285. Multiplying by 100 gives 71.43 percent.

q: One side of a right-angled triangle is 8 and the perpendicular is 6. What is the length of the third side (hypotenuse)?
f: By Pythagoras, hypotenuse squared = 8 squared + 6 squared = 64 + 36 = 100, so the hypotenuse is 10.

q: In a right-angled triangle, sine of an angle is the perpendicular divided by what?
f: Sin of an angle = perpendicular / hypotenuse.

q: What is the correct thing to do with the engine of your vehicle at a petrol pump?
f: Petrol vapour can catch fire from sparks, so the engine must be switched off while refuelling.

q: In which year was the Pirpur Report on the grievances of Muslims in Congress provinces published?
f: The Pirpur Report, prepared by a committee of the Muslim League headed by Raja Syed Muhammad Mehdi of Pirpur, came out in 1938.

q: Change into passive voice: Let us play a game.
o: A game was played by us.
f: For a sentence beginning with Let, the passive form is Let + object + be + past participle.

q: What are the two parts of a common logarithm called?
f: A common logarithm has an integral part called the characteristic and a decimal part called the mantissa.

q: Which is the deepest known point of the Earth's oceans?
o: Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench
f: Challenger Deep lies in the Mariana Trench in the western Pacific Ocean. It is about 10,900 metres deep.

q: According to the 2023 census, about what percentage of Pakistan's population lives in Balochistan?
f: Balochistan has about 14.9 million people out of about 241.5 million in Pakistan. That is roughly 6 percent.

q: What is the population of Balochistan according to the 2023 census of Pakistan?
f: The 2023 digital census recorded about 14.89 million people in Balochistan.

q: What is the population of Sindh according to the 2023 census of Pakistan?
f: The 2023 digital census recorded about 55.7 million people in Sindh.

q: Is Greece a nuclear-weapon state?
o: Yes, it has tested a bomb
No, it is not a nuclear power
f: Greece has no nuclear weapons. It is a NATO member but does not own an atomic arsenal.

q: Fill in the preposition: Do you agree ___ me?
f: We agree with a person and agree to a plan or proposal. Here the object is a person, so the correct word is with.

q: Fill in the blank: I always face difficulty ___ prepositions.
f: The common phrase is difficulty with something. So the correct preposition is with.

q: In which year was Pakistan's first constitution enforced, and who became the first President under it?
f: The first constitution of Pakistan was enforced on 23 March 1956. Iskander Mirza became the first President under it.

q: Is 19 a prime number?
o: Yes, it is a prime number
f: 19 is not divisible by 2, 3, 5, 7 or 11, and has no divisor other than 1 and itself. So it is prime.

q: Who was the Prime Minister of Pakistan in 1973 when the new Constitution was adopted?
f: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto became Prime Minister in August 1973 and the 1973 Constitution came into force under him.

q: What is the order of the product of a 3 x 2 matrix and a 2 x 3 matrix?
f: For a product AB, the inner orders (2 and 2) must match, and the result has the outer orders. So a 3 x 2 matrix times a 2 x 3 matrix gives a 3 x 3 matrix.

q: Which property of multiplication is shown by 9 x 7 = 7 x 9?
f: Changing the order of the numbers does not change the product, which is the commutative property.

q: Which type of tissue in the human body pumps blood regularly?
f: The walls of the heart are made of cardiac muscle, which contracts rhythmically without tiring.

q: Which companion headed the committee that prepared copies of the Quran during the caliphate of Hazrat Usman (RA)?
f: Hazrat Usman (RA) appointed Hazrat Zaid bin Thabit (RA) to lead the committee that wrote standard copies of the Quran and sent them to major cities.

q: To which caste (community) did Raja Dahir, the ruler of Sindh at the time of Muhammad bin Qasim's invasion, belong?
f: Raja Dahir belonged to the Brahmin dynasty that ruled Sindh after the Rai dynasty.

q: Is mass a scalar quantity or a vector quantity?
f: Mass has only magnitude and no direction, so it is a scalar quantity.

q: What is one quarter of one third of 36?
f: One third of 36 is 36/3 = 12. One quarter of 12 is 12/4 = 3.

q: Which one is different from the rest: Rawalpindi, Lahore, Sindh, Peshawar, Quetta?
f: Rawalpindi, Lahore, Peshawar and Quetta are cities, while Sindh is a province.

q: In which city did the Quraish tribe mainly reside?
f: The Quraish were the leading tribe of Makkah and looked after the Kaaba.

q: What is the diameter of a circle whose radius is 56?
f: Diameter is twice the radius. 2 x 56 = 112.

q: Ramiz Raja was a famous player of which game?
f: Ramiz Raja played for Pakistan in Tests and ODIs from 1984 to 1997.

q: In which province are the Ras Koh Hills located?
f: The Ras Koh Hills lie in Chagai district of Balochistan.

q: What is a rational number?
o: A number that cannot be written as a fraction
A number that can be written as p/q where p and q are integers and q is not zero
A number with a non-repeating infinite decimal
A number that is only positive
f: A rational number is any number that can be expressed as the ratio p/q of two integers with q not equal to 0.

q: How many rational numbers lie between 0 and 1?
f: Between any two rational numbers there is another one, for example their average, so the set between 0 and 1 is infinite.

q: Rearrange the letters of CHIKARA to make the name of a city. Which city is it?
f: The letters C H I K A R A can be arranged to spell KARACHI.

q: Muammar Gaddafi was the long-time ruler of which country?
f: Muammar Gaddafi ruled Libya from 1969 until he was overthrown in 2011.

q: How many countries are strictly counted as Scandinavian countries?
f: Scandinavia strictly means Denmark, Norway and Sweden.

q: Which symbol is commonly used to represent the common difference of an arithmetic sequence?
f: In an arithmetic sequence each term is found by adding a fixed number to the previous term. That fixed number is called the common difference and is written d.

q: Which number is different from the rest: 5, 7, 9, 12?
f: 5, 7 and 9 are odd numbers, while 12 is an even number.

q: Which one is different from the rest: A4, B5, C5, D7?
f: A, B, C, D are the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th letters. The number is the letter position plus 3 in A4, B5 and D7 (1+3, 2+3, 4+3), but C5 breaks it because 3+3 is 6.

q: Which one is different from the rest: 3, 5, 9, 11?
f: 3, 5 and 11 are prime numbers, while 9 = 3 x 3 is not prime, so 9 is different.

q: How many rings are there in the Olympic symbol?
f: The Olympic symbol has five interlocking rings coloured blue, yellow, black, green and red.

q: The Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 divided how many rivers between India and Pakistan?
f: The treaty covered six rivers: the three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) went to India and the three western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) went to Pakistan.

q: Gwadar Port is situated on the coast of which sea?
f: Gwadar is a deep sea port in Balochistan and lies on the Arabian Sea coast.

q: Which event is commonly called the First War of Independence against British rule in the subcontinent?
f: The uprising of 1857 against the East India Company is called the War of Independence by Muslims and Hindus of the subcontinent.

q: A train runs at a speed of 99 km/hr. What distance does it cover in 12 minutes?
f: 12 minutes = 12/60 = 1/5 hour. Distance = 99 x 1/5 = 19.8 km.

q: What is the highest individual score by a Pakistani batter in Test cricket?
f: Hanif Mohammad scored 337 against the West Indies at Bridgetown in 1958.

q: Which saint is buried in the city of Kasur?
f: The famous Punjabi Sufi poet Bulleh Shah is buried in Kasur.

q: On which date was Pakistan's first satellite, Badr-1, launched?
f: Badr-1 was launched on 16 July 1990 from China.

q: Where is the Yellow Sea located?
o: Between China and the Korean Peninsula
f: The Yellow Sea is an arm of the Pacific Ocean lying between mainland China and the Korean Peninsula.

q: What does SEATO stand for?
o: Southern Europe and Asia Treaty Organization
f: SEATO stands for South East Asia Treaty Organization, a defence alliance led by the USA.

q: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence: I ___ to school.
f: With the subject I, the simple present verb is go.

q: What comes next in the series: Z4, X8, V12, ?
f: The letters move back by two (Z, X, V, T) and the numbers go up by 4 (4, 8, 12, 16). So the next term is T16.

q: What comes next in the series: Aa, Bb, Cc, Dd, ?
f: Each term has a capital letter and its small letter, moving one letter forward each time. After Dd comes Ee.

q: What comes next in the series: A2, D9, H16, M23, ?
f: The letters jump by 3, 4, 5 places (A, D, H, M) so the next jump is 6, giving S. The numbers increase by 7 each time (2, 9, 16, 23), giving 30. So the next term is S30.

q: By which symbol is the universal set usually represented in set theory?
f: The universal set, which contains all elements under consideration, is written with the capital letter U.

q: What is a singleton set?
o: A set with exactly one element
f: A singleton set has exactly one element, for example {5}.

q: What does the idiom "cold shoulder" mean?
o: To treat someone in an unfriendly way and ignore them
To feel a pain in the shoulder
f: To give someone the cold shoulder means to deliberately ignore them or treat them coldly.

q: Ali is 10 years old and he is twice as old as his sister. How old will his sister be after 20 years?
f: His sister is 10 divided by 2 = 5 years old now. After 20 years she will be 5 + 20 = 25.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is 8 years old. When Ali is 10 years old, how old will his sister be?
f: The age difference is 8 - 5 = 3 years. When Ali is 10, his sister is 10 + 3 = 13.

q: If my mother is your sister, what am I to you?
f: Your sister is my mother, so I am her child, which makes me your sister's child, that is your nephew or niece.

q: According to the Quran, whom should a person respect and obey most (after Allah)?
f: The Quran commands good treatment of parents right after the command to worship Allah alone, and tells us not even to say 'uff' to them.

q: Fill in the blank: I go to sleep ____ I am tired.
f: 'When' shows the time at which something happens, so 'I go to sleep when I am tired' is correct.

q: Which is the smallest Muslim country of the world by area?
f: The Maldives covers only about 300 square kilometres, less than Bahrain (about 780) and Brunei (about 5,770).

q: Father is to son as mother is to ____.
f: A father and his male child are father and son. In the same way a mother and her female child are mother and daughter.

q: Which of the following was a son of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: Hazrat Qasim (RA) was the first son of the Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (RA); he died as a small child.

q: On which side of Pakistan does China lie?
f: Pakistan's northern border, through Gilgit-Baltistan, meets China's Xinjiang region.

q: Choose the correct word: The Arabian Sea is ____ in the southern part of Pakistan.
f: The sentence needs the past participle 'situated' after 'is' to mean 'located'.

q: Select the correct spelling.
f: The word is spelled d-i-v-e-r-s-i-t-y, from the Latin word diversus.

q: Who started the Khilafat Movement in the subcontinent?
o: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan and Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk
Maulana Hasrat Mohani and Liaquat Ali Khan
f: The Khilafat Movement (1919-1924) was led by the Ali Brothers, Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali. It aimed to save the Ottoman Caliphate.

q: Who started the Shuddhi movement in India?
f: The Shuddhi (purification) movement to bring converts back to Hinduism was begun by the Arya Samaj of Swami Dayanand Saraswati.

q: As of 2026, has any woman been elected President of the United States?
o: No, no woman has been elected so far
f: Hillary Clinton lost in 2016 and Kamala Harris lost in 2024. No woman has yet held the office of US President.

q: Who is the author of the book The Story of the Pakistan Army?
f: The Story of the Pakistan Army was written by Major General Fazal Muqeem Khan and first published in 1963.

q: In set theory, a set that contains another set as its subset is called what?
f: If every element of A is also in B, then A is a subset of B and B is a superset of A.

q: What is the sum of the first seven multiples of 5?
What does CNG stand for?
f: CNG is natural gas, mostly methane, stored under high pressure and used as vehicle fuel.

q: What does RAW stand for in the name of the Indian intelligence agency?
f: RAW is the external intelligence agency of India, called the Research and Analysis Wing.

q: What is Youm-e-Takbeer?
o: Anniversary of Pakistan's nuclear tests of May 1998
Day of the passing of the Lahore Resolution
Anniversary of the independence of Pakistan
f: Youm-e-Takbeer is observed every year on 28 May to mark the five nuclear tests Pakistan carried out in the Chagai hills in 1998.

q: The word Olympic is taken from which ancient Greek place?
f: The word Olympic comes from Olympia, the town in ancient Greece where the original games were held.

q: What is the chemical symbol of gold in the periodic table?
f: The symbol Au comes from the Latin name aurum, meaning gold.

q: What is the chemical symbol of potassium?
f: The symbol K comes from kalium, the Latin name for potassium.

q: Against which team did Pakistan play its first Twenty20 International match?
f: Pakistan played its first T20I against England on 28 August 2006 at Bristol and won by five wickets.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to diatribe?
f: A diatribe is a bitter and angry verbal attack, the same as a tirade.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to turbulent?
f: Turbulent means stormy and wild, which is close to violent.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to acquisitive?
f: Acquisitive means eager to get more and more possessions, which is greedy.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to aggressive?
f: Aggressive means ready to attack or confront, which is close to hostile.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to anonymous?
f: Anonymous means having no name made known, that is unnamed.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to entice?
f: To entice is to attract someone by offering something pleasing, which is to lure.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to eradicate?
f: To eradicate is to remove completely, which is to eliminate.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to extraordinary?
f: Extraordinary means beyond the ordinary, which is remarkable.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to fertile?
f: Fertile land produces plenty of crops, so it is productive.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to nutritious?
f: Nutritious food gives the body what it needs to grow, so it is nourishing.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to reddish?
f: Reddish means slightly red, which is close to ruddy.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to restrain?
f: To restrain is to keep under control, which is to hold back.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to staunch?
f: Staunch means firmly faithful to a person or cause, which is loyal.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to sympathy?
f: Sympathy is feeling sorry for another person's trouble, which is compassion.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to tempted?
f: Tempted means attracted towards doing something, which is lured.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to tolerant?
f: A tolerant person accepts other views and behaviour, which is open-minded.

q: What does the idiom 'out of temper' mean?
f: To be out of temper means to be in a bad mood and easily angered.

q: What does the idiom 'to keep one's temper' mean?
o: To remain calm and not lose control of anger
To keep a hot drink warm
f: To keep one's temper means to stay calm even when provoked.

q: What is one quarter of one tenth of 12?
f: One tenth of 12 is 1.2. One quarter of 1.2 is 1.2 / 4 = 0.3.

q: What is one third of 1/80?
What is one third of 10?
f: One third of 10 = 10 / 3 = 3.33, which is 3 and 1/3.

q: Ali is 6 years older than his sister. When Ali's age was three times his sister's age, how old was the sister?
f: Let the sister be x. Then Ali is x + 6 = 3x, so 2x = 6 and x = 3. Ali was then 9.

q: In which country is the Three Gorges Dam located?
f: The Three Gorges Dam is built on the Yangtze River in Hubei province, China.

q: Khateeb ul Ambia (the orator among the prophets) is the title of which prophet?
f: Hazrat Shuaib (AS) was known for his powerful and eloquent speech, so he is called Khateeb ul Ambia.

q: Which number completes the pattern: 2x2 = 44, 2x3 = 49, 3x4 = 916, then 2x4 = ?
f: Each answer joins the squares of the two numbers: 2x2 gives 4 and 4, 2x3 gives 4 and 9, 3x4 gives 9 and 16. So 2x4 gives 4 and 16, which is 416.

q: In which province of Pakistan did the country carry out its nuclear tests in May 1998?
f: The tests were carried out in the Chagai Hills in Chagai district, Balochistan.

q: What is the meaning of the idiom "to take to one's heels"?
f: The idiom "take to one's heels" means to run away quickly, usually from danger.

q: What is a synonym of the word "total"?
f: "Total" means the whole amount after adding everything together, which is the same as "sum".

q: What is the length of a marathon race in miles?
f: A standard marathon is 42.195 km. Dividing by 1.609 gives about 26.2 miles.

q: Complete the sentence: Our team ______ their track suits.
f: "Their" is plural, so the team is treated as a group of members and the plural verb "are wearing" agrees with it.

q: If A transpose is equal to A, then the matrix A is called what?
f: A square matrix with A^T = A is called a symmetric matrix. If A^T = -A, it is skew symmetric.

q: A car travels 70 km in one hour. How much distance will it travel in 40 minutes at the same speed?
f: 40 minutes is 40/60 = 2/3 of an hour. Distance = 70 x 2/3 = 46.67 km.

q: Insulin is used for the treatment of which disease?
f: Insulin is a hormone that controls blood sugar, so it is used to treat diabetes.

q: Who was the scribe (writer) of the Treaty of Hudaibiyah?
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) wrote the text of the Treaty of Hudaibiyah as dictated by the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

q: What is the synonym of the word "trouble"?
f: "Trouble" means a problem or hardship, which is the same as difficulty.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 26th be?
f: From the 3rd to the 26th is 23 days. 23 divided by 7 leaves 2, so Tuesday + 2 = Thursday.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 21st be?
f: From the 1st to the 21st is 20 days. 20 divided by 7 leaves 6, so Tuesday + 6 = Monday.

q: Who was the leader of the Muslim army in the Battle of Uhud?
f: The Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) himself commanded the Muslim army at Uhud.

q: Umm-ul-Masakeen (Mother of the Poor) is the title of which wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Hazrat Zainab bint Khuzaymah (RA) was known as Umm-ul-Masakeen because of her great generosity to the poor.

q: Which British queen was the first to visit Pakistan?
f: Queen Elizabeth II visited Pakistan in February 1961, the first reigning British monarch to do so.

q: In which year did the Soviet Union complete its withdrawal from Afghanistan?
f: The last Soviet troops left Afghanistan on 15 February 1989, after the 1979 invasion.

q: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, what is the position of Pakistan relative to India on the rivers?
f: The rivers rise in or pass through Indian-held territory before entering Pakistan, so Pakistan is the lower riparian (downstream) state.

q: Who has taken the most wickets in One Day Internationals?
f: Muttiah Muralitharan of Sri Lanka took 534 ODI wickets, the highest ever.

q: In which country is the White Sea located?
f: The White Sea is an inlet of the Barents Sea on the north-west coast of Russia.

q: Complete the analogy: Man is to wallet as woman is to ____.
f: A man carries money in a wallet and a woman usually carries it in a purse.

q: Change into indirect speech: He told her, "I want to meet your father."
o: He told her that he wanted to meet her father.
He told her that I want to meet your father.
He told her that he wants to meet your father.
He told her that he had wanted to meet his father.
f: In indirect speech with a past reporting verb, present tense becomes past, I becomes he, and your becomes her.

q: Which country has the second largest population in the world (2026)?
f: India is first and China is second according to 2026 estimates.

q: For which book is Gulbadan Begum, daughter of Babur, famous as a writer?
f: Gulbadan Begum wrote the Humayun-nama, a history of the reign of her brother Humayun.

q: Who wrote the work The Loyal Muhammadans of India?
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote it around 1860 to show that most Muslims were loyal to the British during the events of 1857.

q: What was the name of the mother of Hazrat Yaqoob (AS)?
f: Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS) and Rifqa (Rebecca).

q: What is the relation between Hazrat Zakariya (AS) and Hazrat Yahya (AS)?
f: Hazrat Yahya (AS) was the son of Hazrat Zakariya (AS), born in his old age by Allah's will.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA) with the Holy Prophet (SAW)?
f: Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA) was a freed slave whom the Prophet (SAW) adopted as his son before Islam.

q: Is zero a natural number, according to the definition taught in Pakistani textbooks?
o: Yes, it is the first natural number
No, it is a whole number
No, it is a negative number
Yes, it is a prime number
f: Natural numbers are the counting numbers 1, 2, 3 and so on. Zero is added to them to form the whole numbers.

q: If A = 1, then what number matches M in the same pattern?
f: Letters are numbered by their place in the alphabet. A is 1st, and M is the 13th letter.

q: What is 1 + 1?
f: Adding one and one gives two.

q: What is 1.2 + 2/2?
f: Divide first: 2/2 = 1. Then 1.2 + 1 = 2.2.

q: What is 1/(1 + 2)?
f: First solve the bracket: 1 + 2 = 3. So the value is 1/3.

q: What is 2 + 4 x 4?
f: Multiply first: 4 x 4 = 16. Then 2 + 16 = 18.

q: What is 3 x 2?
f: 3 x 2 = 6, and 2 x 3 is also 6 because multiplication is commutative.

q: What is 40% of 9?
What type of number is 7 - 3i?
f: A number written as a + bi, where i is the imaginary unit, is a complex number. Here a = 7 and b = -3.

q: What is 9 + 7?
f: Adding 9 and 7 gives 16.

q: What is 90 / 9?
f: 9 times 10 is 90, so 90 divided by 9 is 10.

q: Krone is the currency of which country?
f: The Danish krone is the currency of Denmark. Norway also uses a krone.

q: What is the boundary line between India and China called?
f: The McMahon Line was drawn in 1914 and is the boundary India claims with China in the east.

q: How many peaks above 8000 metres are located in Pakistan?
f: Pakistan has five peaks above 8000 m: K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I, Gasherbrum II and Broad Peak.

q: In which province is the Lower Indus plain mostly located?
f: The Lower Indus plain lies in Sindh, from near Sukkur down to the Arabian Sea.

q: Which country hosted the G20 summit in 2023 (New Delhi)?
f: The 2023 G20 summit was held in New Delhi, India, in September 2023. India held the G20 presidency that year.

q: Kiwi, a flightless bird, is the national symbol of which country?
f: The kiwi is the national bird of New Zealand, and New Zealanders are often called Kiwis.

q: Who wrote the novel Ice Candy Man?
f: Ice Candy Man (1988) was written by the Pakistani novelist Bapsi Sidhwa. It tells the story of Partition through a Parsi girl in Lahore.

q: In which year did Pakistan play its first Test match?
f: Pakistan's first Test was played against India in Delhi in October 1952.

q: Car is to wheel as clock is to what?
f: A wheel is a part of a car, and hands are a part of a clock.

q: When did World War 2 start?
f: World War 2 began on 1 September 1939 when Germany invaded Poland.

q: Who is credited with inventing the electric motor?
f: Michael Faraday demonstrated the first electric motor in 1821, and most textbooks credit him.

q: In which year was the Durand Line, the Pakistan-Afghanistan border, agreed?
f: The Durand Line agreement was signed in 1893 between Sir Mortimer Durand and Amir Abdur Rahman Khan of Afghanistan.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of Canada today (October 2026)?
f: Mark Carney became Prime Minister of Canada on 14 March 2025 and leads the Liberal Party. Canada has no president; the Prime Minister is head of government.

q: Who wrote the Urdu poetry book Bal-e-Jibreel (Gabriel's Wing)?
f: Bal-e-Jibreel was written by Allama Muhammad Iqbal and published in 1935.

q: Which element is the most abundant in the universe?
f: Hydrogen makes up about 75 percent of the ordinary matter in the universe by mass.

q: In which year did Aligarh College (MAO College) become Aligarh Muslim University?
f: The MAO College was given university status in 1920 and became Aligarh Muslim University.

q: For what is the city of Multan famous?
f: Multan is known as the City of Saints (Madinat-ul-Auliya) because it has many famous shrines of Sufi saints.

q: Who conquered Sindh in 712 AD?
f: Muhammad bin Qasim, a young Arab general of the Umayyad caliphate, defeated Raja Dahir and conquered Sindh.

q: Which word is closest to the opposite of envious?
f: Envious means wanting what others have. A content person is satisfied with what they have, so content is the opposite.

q: Who was known as the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity in the subcontinent?
f: Muhammad Ali Jinnah worked for Hindu-Muslim unity in the early part of his career, including the 1916 Lucknow Pact. Sarojini Naidu gave him this title.

q: What was the first book of poetry of Allama Iqbal?
f: Asrar-e-Khudi, a Persian poetry book, was published in 1915 and is usually called his first poetry book.

q: What is 1/4 of 1/10 of 120?
Which is the hottest planet of the solar system?
f: Venus is the hottest planet, about 465 degrees Celsius, because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat.

q: On which date did the full-scale 1965 war between Pakistan and India begin, according to Pakistani textbooks?
f: India attacked Lahore across the international border on 6 September 1965, which started the full-scale war. A ceasefire came on 23 September 1965.

q: Which ruler is known as the Tiger of Mysore (Sher-e-Mysore)?
f: Tipu Sultan fought the British in the Anglo-Mysore wars and is called the Tiger of Mysore.

q: Into how many main physical regions is Pakistan commonly divided in Pakistan Studies textbooks?
f: Textbooks usually list six regions: Northern Mountains, Western Mountains, Potohar Plateau, Balochistan Plateau, Indus Plains and Deserts.

q: Who is regarded as the oldest (first) poet of the Pashto language?
f: Amir Kror Suri, a ruler of Ghor in the 8th century, is regarded as the earliest known Pashto poet.

q: Which is the oldest sport in the world according to most textbooks?
f: Wrestling is usually named as the oldest sport, as cave paintings and ancient records show it thousands of years ago.

q: Where were all the Round Table Conferences (1930 to 1932) held?
f: The three Round Table Conferences were held in London to discuss constitutional reforms for India. They took place in 1930, 1931 and 1932.

q: In which region of Pakistan is the Shina (Sheena) language mainly spoken?
f: Shina is the main language of the Gilgit area and nearby valleys of Gilgit-Baltistan. It belongs to the Dardic group of languages.

q: Which vegetable is regarded as the national vegetable of Pakistan?
f: Okra, known locally as bhindi or lady finger, is commonly listed as Pakistan's national vegetable.

q: The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared by a committee headed by whom?
f: The All Parties Committee that drafted the 1928 Nehru Report was chaired by Motilal Nehru.

q: Which building is shown on the back of the Pakistani 100 rupee note?
f: The reverse of the Rs 100 note shows the Quaid-e-Azam Residency in Ziarat, Balochistan.

q: Approximately what percentage of Pakistan's area does Balochistan cover?
f: Balochistan has about 347,000 square km, which Pakistani textbooks give as roughly 44% of the country.

q: Which person won two Nobel Prizes in his life, one of them the Nobel Peace Prize?
f: Linus Pauling won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1954 and the Nobel Peace Prize in 1962.

q: Who built the Red Fort of Delhi?
f: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan built the Red Fort in Delhi, completed in 1648.

q: In which Amendment to the 1973 Constitution were Ahmadis declared non-Muslim?
f: The Second Amendment, passed in 1974, declared Ahmadis non-Muslim for the purposes of the Constitution.

q: Pablo Picasso, the famous painter, belonged to which country?
f: Pablo Picasso was born in Malaga, Spain, in 1881.

q: Which is the largest dam of Pakistan?
f: Tarbela Dam on the Indus River is the largest earth filled dam in Pakistan and one of the largest in the world.

q: On which date did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan die?
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan died on 27 March 1898 at Aligarh. He was born on 17 October 1817.

q: Which mountain range lies in the north-west of Pakistan?
f: The Hindu Kush range lies in the north-west of Pakistan, along the border with Afghanistan.

q: In which city was the second Islamic Summit Conference of the OIC held in 1974?
f: The second OIC Islamic Summit took place in Lahore in February 1974 and was hosted by Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

q: Who won the ICC Men's Cricketer of the Year (Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy) award for 2022?
f: Babar Azam of Pakistan won the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy for 2022.

q: What is the full form of ISPR?
f: ISPR stands for Inter Services Public Relations, the media wing of the Pakistan Armed Forces.

q: Which dam of Pakistan is made of earth and rock fill and is the largest earth-filled dam in the world?
f: Tarbela Dam on the Indus River is mostly built of earth and rock fill and is called the largest earth-filled dam.

q: What is 3 + 3/3?
f: Division first: 3/3 = 1. Then 3 + 1 = 4.

q: Who was the Viceroy of India in 1911 when the partition of Bengal was annulled?
f: Lord Hardinge was Viceroy from 1910 to 1916. The annulment of the 1905 partition was announced at the Delhi Durbar in December 1911.

q: In a class of 500 students, 340 are boys. What percentage of the students are girls?
On which date did the USA drop the atomic bomb on Hiroshima, Japan?
f: The first atomic bomb was dropped on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945.

q: Humayun was defeated by which ruler, forcing him to leave India in 1540?
f: Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun at Chausa in 1539 and at Kannauj in 1540. Humayun then fled India.

q: On which date did Israel declare its independence?
f: David Ben-Gurion declared the State of Israel on 14 May 1948, as the British Mandate ended.

q: Which city is known as the City of Light?
f: Paris is called the City of Light because it was an early centre of education and ideas and one of the first cities with gas street lighting.

q: Who is the author of the book Pakistaniat (What is Pakistaniat?)?
f: Pakistaniat is the idea of Pakistani national identity, and Javed Jabbar wrote a book on it titled What is Pakistaniat. He lists many elements that shape the identity of the Pakistani nation.

q: Germany invaded which country first in World War II in September 1939?
f: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939. Britain and France then declared war on Germany.

q: Butterfly is a technique (stroke) of which sport?
f: Butterfly stroke is one of the four main competitive swimming strokes.

q: What does OS stand for in computing?
f: In computers, OS stands for Operating System, the main software that runs the computer.

q: The Wagah border connects Pakistan with which country?
f: Wagah, on the Grand Trunk Road between Lahore and Amritsar, is the main land crossing between Pakistan and India.

q: What type of fraction is 9/2?
f: In 9/2 the numerator 9 is greater than the denominator 2, so it is an improper fraction. It equals the mixed number 4 and 1/2.

q: Which country is Pakistan's biggest trading partner today?
f: China is Pakistan's largest trading partner, mainly because of large imports from China.

q: Who is the head of state of Pakistan according to the 1973 Constitution (currently in office, 2026)?
f: The President is the head of state, and Asif Ali Zardari has held the office since 10 March 2024.

q: What is the tenure of a member of the Senate of Pakistan?
f: A Senator is elected for six years. Half of the members retire every three years.

q: How many Prime Ministers did Pakistan have between 1947 and 1958?
f: They were Liaquat Ali Khan, Khawaja Nazimuddin, Mohammad Ali Bogra, Chaudhry Mohammad Ali, H. S. Suhrawardy, I. I. Chundrigar and Feroz Khan Noon, which makes 7.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah join the Indian National Congress?
f: Jinnah joined the Indian National Congress in 1906, when he attended its Calcutta session.

q: In which year was the C. R. (Rajagopalachari) Formula put forward?
f: C. Rajagopalachari proposed the formula in 1944 as a basis for talks between Gandhi and Jinnah.

q: Which sport is called the Game of Gentlemen?
f: Cricket is known as the Game of Gentlemen because of its tradition of fair play and sportsmanship. The phrase comes from its English origins.

q: Who founded the Khudai Khidmatgar movement?
f: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Bacha Khan) founded the Khudai Khidmatgar (Servants of God) movement around 1929 in the Pashtun areas.

q: In which city is Paradise Point located?
f: Paradise Point is a famous rocky beach spot on the Arabian Sea coast in Karachi.

q: In which city of Pakistan is Iqbal Park located?
f: Iqbal Park in Lahore is the park where Minar-e-Pakistan stands and the Pakistan Resolution was passed in 1940.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam return to India after his self-imposed exile in England?
f: Jinnah stayed in London for some years after the Round Table Conferences. He came back in 1934 at the request of Muslim leaders and was elected president of the Muslim League.

q: A train moves at a speed of 60 km/hour. How much time will it take to cover 150 km?
f: Time = distance / speed = 150 / 60 = 2.5 hours.

q: Who prepared the Pirpur Report of 1938 on the grievances of Muslims in Congress provinces?
o: Raja Syed Muhammad Mehdi of Pirpur
f: The Pirpur Report was prepared by a Muslim League committee headed by Raja Syed Muhammad Mehdi of Pirpur.

q: Which constitution of Pakistan was enforced in 1962?
o: The second constitution, with a presidential system
The first constitution, with a parliamentary system
The third constitution, with a parliamentary system
f: The 1962 constitution was the second constitution of Pakistan and gave a presidential system with strong powers to the President.

q: Akbar is older than Khalid and Ahmed is younger than Khalid. Which statement is true?
f: The order from oldest is Akbar, Khalid, Ahmed. So Akbar is older than Ahmed.

q: What does the crescent on the flag of Pakistan represent?
f: According to the usual explanation, the crescent stands for progress.

q: Who wrote the book 'Pakistan: The Heart of Asia'?
f: Pakistan: The Heart of Asia is a collection of speeches made by Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, during his 1950 visit to the USA.

q: In which year did Pakistan become a member of the International Labour Organization (ILO)?
