f: Pakistan has been an ILO member since 1947, the year of its independence.

q: Between which latitudes does Pakistan lie?
f: Pakistan extends from about 24 degrees north in the south to about 37 degrees north in the north.

q: In which district of Sindh is Ranikot Fort (Rani Fort) situated?
f: Ranikot Fort lies in the Kirthar foothills of Jamshoro district in Sindh.

q: Which two countries are known for the greatest rivalry in Test cricket?
f: England and Australia play the Ashes series, the oldest and most famous rivalry in Test cricket.

q: In which war was Captain Muhammad Sarwar Shaheed martyred?
f: Captain Muhammad Sarwar was martyred in the 1948 Kashmir war near Uri in October 1948.

q: Who is called the Traveller of Islam?
f: Ibn Battuta, the Moroccan explorer, travelled about 120,000 km across Africa, Asia and Europe in nearly 30 years.

q: In which year was the Wavell Plan announced?
f: Lord Wavell, the Viceroy, announced his plan in June 1945, and it was discussed at the Simla Conference.

q: On a farm, goats are double the cows and camels are double the goats. If there are 10 goats, how many animals are on the farm?
f: Goats are 10, so cows are 10 / 2 = 5 and camels are 10 x 2 = 20. Total is 5 + 10 + 20 = 35.

q: Where is the National College of Arts (NCA) located?
f: The National College of Arts is a famous art and design institution in Lahore. It was founded in 1875 as the Mayo School of Art.

q: Who was the Finance Minister in the interim government of British India in 1946, before independence?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan held the finance portfolio in the interim government formed in October 1946. His budget was nicknamed the poor man's budget.

q: Who wrote the book Pakistan: A Hard Country?
f: Pakistan: A Hard Country (2011) was written by the British author Anatol Lieven.

q: If 7 books cost 3500 rupees, what is the price of 1 book?
f: Price of 1 book = 3500 divided by 7 = 500 rupees.

q: In a bus, 2/3 of the passengers are men. What is the percentage of women?
f: Women are 1 minus 2/3 = 1/3 of the passengers. 1/3 of 100 = 33.33%.

q: What is the meaning of 'doomed'?
f: Doomed means certain to meet a bad end or failure.

q: Which mammal lays eggs?
f: The platypus and the echidna are monotremes, the only mammals that lay eggs.

q: Which of the following books was written by Altaf Hussain Hali?
f: Altaf Hussain Hali wrote the long poem Musaddas, also called Madd-o-Jazr-e-Islam, in 1879. Bang-e-Dra and Shikwa are by Allama Iqbal, and Aab-e-Hayat is by Muhammad Hussain Azad.

q: Jabir bin Hayyan (Geber) is known as the father of which science?
f: Jabir bin Hayyan, a Muslim scientist of the eighth century, developed early laboratory methods such as distillation and crystallisation, so he is called the father of chemistry.

q: What is the date of Bangladesh's declaration of independence?
f: Bangladesh declared independence on 26 March 1971 and celebrates it as Independence Day. The war ended on 16 December 1971.

q: What is the lowest point on the surface of the earth on land?
f: The shore of the Dead Sea, between Israel, Jordan and the West Bank, is about 430 m below sea level, the lowest land point.

q: The ancient Mehrgarh civilization site, one of the oldest farming settlements in South Asia, is located in which province of Pakistan?
f: Mehrgarh lies on the Kachhi plain near the Bolan Pass in Balochistan.

q: What was the real (original) name of Shah Waliullah of Delhi?
f: Shah Waliullah was born as Qutbuddin Ahmad and later became known as Shah Waliullah.

q: Who is Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the United Nations in New York as of October 2026?
f: Asim Iftikhar Ahmad heads the Pakistan Mission to the UN and issues its statements in 2026.

q: Which place in Punjab is famous for its salt mountain and salt mine?
f: Khewra in the Salt Range of Jhelum district is famous for the world's second largest salt mine.

q: In which city is the shrine of the Sufi poet Bulleh Shah located?
f: Bulleh Shah is buried in Kasur, in Punjab.

q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word spurn?
f: To spurn means to refuse something with scorn. Reject is the nearest meaning.

q: If the 13th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 28th of that month?
f: 28 - 13 = 15 days later. 15 = 14 + 1, so move 1 day forward from Monday, which is Tuesday.

q: If the 27th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 9th day be?
f: From the 9th to the 27th is 18 days. 18 divided by 7 leaves 4, so Monday - 4 days = Thursday.

q: Saeed Anwar, famous in Pakistan, was a player of which sport?
f: Saeed Anwar was a left-handed opening batsman of the Pakistan cricket team.

q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 3 PM?
f: At 3 o'clock the minute hand is at 12 and the hour hand is at 3. Three hour marks of 30 degrees each make 90 degrees.

q: Who is the head of the cabinet in a parliamentary system?
f: In a parliamentary system the Prime Minister leads the cabinet and the government.

q: In which present-day country did Islam originate?
f: Islam began in Makkah in the Arabian Peninsula, in what is now Saudi Arabia.

q: Is the cosine function an even or an odd function?
f: cos(-x) = cos x for every x, which is the definition of an even function.

q: In which year was Prime Minister Khawaja Nazimuddin dismissed?
f: Khawaja Nazimuddin was dismissed on 17 April 1953.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of 'doomed'?
f: Doomed means destined for misfortune, so its opposite is blessed or fortunate.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to furtive?
f: Furtive means done in a secret or sneaky way to avoid being noticed. Stealthy has the same meaning.

q: A car travels 60 km. A train with double the speed of the car travels for half the time. What distance does the train cover?
f: Distance = speed x time. Doubling the speed and halving the time gives 2 x 1/2 = 1 times the car's distance, which is 60 km.

q: On which date is the Kargil conflict between Pakistan and India commonly said to have begun in 1999?
f: The conflict is commonly dated from 3 May 1999, when intrusions were first reported in the Kargil sector.

q: In which year was Zulfikar Ali Bhutto hanged?
f: Bhutto was hanged on 4 April 1979, after being removed from power by General Zia ul Haq in July 1977.

q: Between which longitudes does Pakistan lie?
f: Pakistan lies approximately between 61 degrees east and 75 degrees east longitude.

q: Where is the Noor Mahal located?
f: Noor Mahal is a palace built by the Nawab of Bahawalpur in 1872 in the city of Bahawalpur.

q: What is the full name of Imam Malik, founder of the Maliki school of fiqh?
f: Imam Malik is Malik ibn Anas, who lived in Madinah. He is also called Imam of Madinah.

q: Pakistan provides a sea route to the landlocked countries of which region?
f: Pakistan's ports, Karachi, Port Qasim and Gwadar, offer the shortest sea access for Afghanistan and the Central Asian states. These states have no coastline of their own.

q: Under which constitution is Pakistan currently being run?
f: Pakistan is run under the Constitution of 1973, which came into force on 14 August 1973 and has been amended many times.

q: What is the tenure (term) of the National Assembly of Pakistan, unless it is dissolved earlier?
f: Under the 1973 Constitution the National Assembly lasts five years from its first meeting. After that it stops working automatically.

q: Who was the Governor General of India during the War of Independence of 1857 and became the first Viceroy in 1858?
f: Lord Canning was Governor General from 1856 to 1858. After the Government of India Act 1858 he became the first Viceroy.

q: Who was the President of Pakistan during the 1971 war with India?
f: General Yahya Khan was President from March 1969 until 20 December 1971, so he was President during the December 1971 war.

q: Which country won the 1974 FIFA World Cup?
f: West Germany beat the Netherlands 2-1 in the final in Munich to win the 1974 FIFA World Cup.

q: In the point (3, 4), what is the number 3 called?
f: In an ordered pair (x, y) the first number x is the abscissa. The second number y is the ordinate.

q: Which province of the subcontinent did the British occupy first?
f: The British won the Battle of Plassey in 1757 and took control of Bengal first.

q: In which year was the Advisory Council of Islamic Ideology (Islamic Council) established in Pakistan?
f: The Advisory Council of Islamic Ideology was set up under the 1962 Constitution, on 1 August 1962.

q: What is the synonym of 'disastrous'?
f: Disastrous means causing great harm or damage, which is the same as catastrophic.

q: What is the synonym of 'doomed'?
f: Doomed means destined to a bad outcome, which is the same as fated.

q: Which country is the largest exporter of tea in the world by volume?
f: Kenya exports more tea by volume than any other country. India is second, and Sri Lanka and China follow.

q: In which country was FIFA founded in 1904?
f: FIFA was founded in Paris, France, on 21 May 1904 by seven European associations.

q: Which is the largest glacier of Pakistan according to most Pakistani textbooks?
f: Pakistani textbooks name the Siachen Glacier, about 76 km long, as the largest in the Karakoram and in the region.

q: The Gobi Desert lies in southern Mongolia and in which other country?
f: The Gobi Desert stretches across southern Mongolia and northern China.

q: What is the currency of Hungary?
f: Hungary uses its own currency, the forint (HUF). It has not adopted the euro.

q: The United States entered World War II after which event?
o: The Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor
f: Japan attacked the US naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, on 7 December 1941. The US declared war on Japan the next day.

q: Which group of gases is mainly responsible for damaging the ozone layer?
f: CFCs release chlorine atoms in the stratosphere, and these break down ozone molecules.

q: What is the antonym of the word liberty?
f: Liberty means freedom, so its opposite is slavery or bondage.

q: In a bus of 30 passengers, 2/3 are male. How many are female?
f: Males = 2/3 of 30 = 20. Females = 30 - 20 = 10.

q: What is the name of the force that opposes the motion between two bodies in contact?
f: Friction acts between touching surfaces and opposes their relative motion.

q: Under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan, a Federal Minister must be a member of which body?
f: Article 92 says Federal Ministers are appointed from the members of Majlis-e-Shoora, which means the National Assembly or the Senate.

q: Where is the Pakistan Navy War College located?
f: The Pakistan Navy War College is in Lahore.

q: What is a synonym of oppression?
f: Oppression means cruel and unjust use of power, which is the same as tyranny.

q: In which constitutional amendment were Qadianis declared non-Muslim in Pakistan?
f: The Second Amendment to the 1973 Constitution, passed in 1974, declared Qadianis (Ahmadis) non-Muslims. It was passed under Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

q: The product of two real numbers is always which kind of number?
f: Real numbers are closed under multiplication, so multiplying two real numbers always gives a real number.

q: Quaid-e-Azam's Fourteen Points of 1929 were presented in reply to which report?
f: The Nehru Report of 1928 rejected separate electorates and other Muslim demands. Quaid-e-Azam answered it with his Fourteen Points in March 1929.

q: Shahbaz Ahmed Senior is a renowned Pakistani player of which game?
f: Shahbaz Ahmed Senior was a famous Pakistani hockey midfielder and captain. He was part of the team that won Olympic gold in 1984.

q: In a class of 33 students, the boys outnumber the girls by 7. How many girls are there?
f: Let girls = g, then boys = g + 7. So g + g + 7 = 33, 2g = 26 and g = 13.

q: Who was the father of the Mughal emperor Humayun?
f: Humayun was the second Mughal emperor and the son of Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire.

q: Which word is pronounced differently from the rest: white, wait, wrong?
f: In wrong the w is silent and the word begins with the r sound. In white and wait the w is pronounced.

q: Which Muslim leader was given the title of knighthood (Sir) by the British in 1888?
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was awarded the title KCSI (Knight Commander of the Star of India) in 1888.

q: Who was the Speaker (President) of the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan from 1948, after Quaid-e-Azam?
f: Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan became President (Speaker) of the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan in 1948 and held the post until 1954.

q: Who was the President of Pakistan under the 1962 constitution in 1962?
f: Field Marshal Ayub Khan was President of Pakistan from 1958 to 1969, and he introduced the 1962 constitution.

q: What is shown on the back of the Pakistani 5000 rupee note?
f: The State Bank of Pakistan describes the back of the Rs 5000 note as showing the Faisal Mosque, Islamabad.

q: What is the antonym of the word sympathetic?
f: Sympathetic means feeling pity and care for others, so its opposite is callous or unfeeling.

q: What was the date of birth of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan?
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was born on 17 October 1817 in Delhi.

q: Which of these countries has a coastline on the Black Sea?
f: The Black Sea is bordered by Turkey, Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia and Georgia. Ukraine is the only one among the options.

q: In which language did Baba Bulleh Shah write his poetry?
f: Bulleh Shah, the Sufi poet of Kasur, wrote mainly in Punjabi (kafis).

q: Which region of China borders Pakistan in the north?
f: The Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region of China touches Gilgit-Baltistan in the north of Pakistan.

q: In which city is Clifton Beach located?
f: Clifton Beach, also called Sea View, is on the Arabian Sea coast in Karachi.

q: What is the process called in which a gas changes directly into a liquid?
f: Condensation is the change of a gas or vapour into a liquid, for example water vapour forming water drops.

q: What is the currency of Bhutan?
f: Bhutan's currency is the ngultrum, which is pegged to the Indian rupee.

q: Which word is a synonym of efficiency?
f: Efficiency means doing a job well with little waste, which is the same as competence.

q: In which year was the draft constitution of the European Union presented?
f: The European Convention presented the draft Treaty establishing a Constitution for Europe in 2003.

q: Change the voice: By whom is the child being fed?
o: Who is being fed by the child?
f: The sentence is in the present continuous passive. The active form is "Who is feeding the child?", with the same tense.

q: Which river do Hindus in India regard as sacred?
f: Hindus consider the Ganges (Ganga) the holiest river and bathe in it at places like Varanasi and Haridwar. It is worshipped as the goddess Ganga.

q: Who is the current President of Iraq (as of October 2026)?
f: Iraq's parliament elected Nizar Amidi (Amedi) as President on 11 April 2026.

q: In which country are the Olympic Mountains located?
f: The Olympic Mountains are in the state of Washington in the north-west United States.

q: Who was the Governor-General of India at the time of the War of Independence of 1857?
f: Lord Canning was Governor-General from 1856 and became the first Viceroy of India in 1858.

q: Gypsum is the main source of which two elements?
f: Gypsum is hydrated calcium sulfate (CaSO4.2H2O), so it supplies calcium and sulfur.

q: Which is the correct spelling?
f: The correct spelling is malevolence, from Latin male (ill) and volens (wishing).

q: A train moves at twice the speed of a car, and the car moves at 60 km/h. How far will the train go in 12 minutes?
f: Train speed is 2 x 60 = 120 km/h. In 12 minutes (12/60 = 0.2 hour) it covers 120 x 0.2 = 24 km.

q: What was the Tashkent Pact (Declaration) of 1966?
o: A peace agreement between Pakistan and India after the 1965 war
A trade treaty between Pakistan and China
A defence pact between Pakistan and the USA
A water treaty on the Indus rivers
f: It was a peace agreement signed on 10 January 1966 in which both sides agreed to withdraw to pre-war positions.

q: Who signed the Tashkent Declaration on behalf of India?
f: Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri signed it and died in Tashkent the next day.

q: If 5 men type 5 pages in 5 minutes, how long will 1 man take to type 1 page?
f: 5 men type 5 pages in 5 minutes, so each man types 1 page in 5 minutes.

q: Peshawar has traditionally been known as the city of what?
f: Peshawar was traditionally called the City of Flowers because of its many gardens.

q: In which constitution of Pakistan were Islamic provisions first included?
f: The 1956 Constitution was the first constitution of Pakistan and made the country an Islamic Republic. It included Islamic provisions.

q: Which team won the PSL trophy two times in a row?
f: Lahore Qalandars won PSL 7 in 2022 and PSL 8 in 2023, back to back. No other team has won consecutive titles.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam go into self-imposed exile in London?
f: After the Round Table Conferences, Jinnah was disappointed with Indian politics and settled in London around 1930. He returned in 1934.

q: In which game is a free throw used?
f: A free throw is an unopposed shot at the basket given to a player after a foul in basketball. It is worth one point.

q: What is the height of the Eiffel Tower in Paris, including antennas, in metres?
f: The Eiffel Tower is about 330 metres tall including its antenna, which is about 1,083 feet.

q: Who is generally regarded as the first poet of the Urdu language?
f: Amir Khusrow (1253-1325) is commonly taught as the first poet who used early Urdu (Hindavi) in verse.

q: On what date was the Wavell Plan announced?
f: Lord Wavell broadcast his plan on 14 June 1945. The Simla Conference to discuss it started on 25 June 1945.

q: In which city is the shrine of Hazrat Bahauddin Zakariya located?
f: The shrine of the Sufi saint Hazrat Bahauddin Zakariya is in Multan.

q: What is 65% of 100?
Which battle was fought in 1757 between Nawab Siraj ud Daula and the British East India Company?
f: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 in Bengal, where Robert Clive defeated Siraj ud Daula.

q: Who was the Prime Minister of Pakistan during the December 1971 war?
f: Nurul Amin was appointed Prime Minister on 7 December 1971 and held office during the war, which ended on 16 December.

q: Who was the fifth Mughal emperor of India?
f: The order was Babur, Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, then Shah Jahan. So Shah Jahan was fifth.

q: What is the square root of 900?
f: 30 x 30 = 900, so the square root of 900 is 30.

q: What is the absolute value of a number?
o: Its distance from zero, always non-negative
f: The absolute value is the distance of a number from zero on the number line, so it ignores the sign. For example |-5| = 5 and |5| = 5.

q: What is the value of absolute zero on the Celsius scale?
f: Absolute zero is 0 Kelvin, which equals -273.15 degrees Celsius. It is the lowest possible temperature.

q: Who founded Aligarh College (MAO College)?
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh.

q: Which organization runs the world's largest volunteer ambulance service, founded by Abdul Sattar Edhi?
f: The Edhi Foundation, founded by Abdul Sattar Edhi in Pakistan, is recognised by Guinness World Records as having the largest volunteer ambulance service.

q: What is the antonym of the word mighty?
f: Mighty means very strong, so its opposite is weak.

q: What is the antonym of the word opaque?
f: Opaque means that light cannot pass through, so its opposite is transparent.

q: Choose the correct word: We are going to the beach ___ car.
f: With a means of transport used without an article, the correct preposition is by: by car.

q: Was the Constitution of Pakistan of 1956 bicameral or unicameral?
o: Bicameral with a National Assembly and a Senate
Unicameral with a single National Assembly
f: The 1956 Constitution created a single house, the National Assembly. The 1962 Constitution was also unicameral.

q: What is the binding force (unifying factor) of the people of Pakistan?
f: Pakistan was created on the basis of the Two-Nation Theory, and the common religion Islam binds its diverse peoples together.

q: What are the approximate length and breadth of Pakistan?
f: Pakistan stretches about 1,600 km from north to south and about 885 km from east to west at its widest.

q: Ali buys a book for 40 rupees and sells it for 50 rupees. What is his profit percentage?
f: Profit = 50 minus 40 = 10 rupees. Profit percent = 10/40 x 100 = 25%.

q: In which years were the modern Olympic Games cancelled because of the world wars?
f: The 1916 Games were cancelled due to World War 1, and the 1940 and 1944 Games due to World War 2.

q: Hazara is the name of an ethnic group mainly found in which country?
f: The Hazara are a Persian-speaking ethnic group living mostly in central Afghanistan (Hazarajat).

q: In which district of Punjab is the main part of the Kala Chitta Range located?
f: The Kala Chitta Range is a low mountain range in northern Punjab, mainly in Attock district and partly in Rawalpindi district.

q: On which two Japanese cities did the USA drop atomic bombs in August 1945?
f: The USA dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945 and another on Nagasaki on 9 August 1945.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word tenure?
f: Tenure means the period or term during which a person holds an office or position.

q: Which letter completes the series: L, _, N, O?
f: The letters are in alphabetical order, and M comes between L and N.

q: What does the Parliament of Pakistan consist of?
f: Under Article 50 of the 1973 Constitution, Parliament consists of the President, the National Assembly and the Senate.

q: What is the value of sin 0 degrees multiplied by cos 90 degrees?
f: sin 0 = 0 and cos 90 = 0, so the product is 0 x 0 = 0.

q: Which constitution is currently in force in Pakistan?
f: The Constitution of 1973 is the current constitution of Pakistan.

q: Who is the current Director General of ISI (Pakistan)?
f: Lt Gen Muhammad Asim Malik has been DG ISI since September 2024.

q: Who is the current Prime Minister of Pakistan?
f: Shehbaz Sharif has been Prime Minister since March 2024.

q: Which is the lowest point on land in Asia, about 430 metres below sea level?
f: The shore of the Dead Sea is the lowest land elevation on Earth, about 430 metres below sea level. It lies between Jordan and Israel or the West Bank.

q: What type of democracy does Pakistan have under the 1973 Constitution?
f: The 1973 Constitution set up a federal parliamentary system. The Prime Minister heads the government and the President is the head of state.

q: What is the derivative of 9 with respect to x?
f: 9 is a constant and the derivative of any constant is zero.

q: What is the Tour de France?
f: The Tour de France is an annual multi-stage men's bicycle race held mainly in France. It usually lasts about three weeks in July.

q: In which continent is the Cape of Good Hope located?
f: The Cape of Good Hope is a rocky headland on the Atlantic coast of South Africa.

q: Choose the correct word: He was good ___ math.
f: The correct preposition after the adjective good, when talking about a skill or subject, is at.

q: Who proposed the heliocentric (sun-centred) model of the solar system?
f: Nicolaus Copernicus proposed in 1543 that the Sun is at the centre and the planets move around it. Ptolemy and Aristotle supported an Earth-centred model.

q: What is the approximate range of Pakistan's short-range ballistic missile Hatf-I?
f: Hatf-I is Pakistan's first short-range, solid-fuel missile with a range of about 70 km, later improved to about 100 km in the Hatf-IA version.

q: Justice Musarrat Hilali took oath in 2023 as the first woman Chief Justice of which high court?
f: Justice Musarrat Hilali took oath as the first woman Chief Justice of the Peshawar High Court on 1 April 2023, in an acting capacity as per some reports. She later became a Supreme Court judge.

q: What is iota (i) in mathematics?
f: Iota is the imaginary unit and is defined as i = square root of -1, so i squared = -1.

q: Choose the correct word: There is ____ water in a jar.
f: Water is uncountable, so it takes 'a lot of'. 'Many', 'several' and 'few' are used only with countable nouns.

q: In which city was Zulfikar Ali Bhutto hanged?
f: Bhutto was hanged in Rawalpindi Central Jail, and he was buried at Garhi Khuda Bakhsh near Larkana.

q: What is the LCM of 3 and 8?
f: 3 and 8 have no common factor, so LCM = 3 x 8 = 24.

q: Which is the largest lake of North America by area?
f: Lake Superior is the largest of the Great Lakes and the largest freshwater lake in North America by surface area.

q: If the sentence is completed in reported speech, which word fills the blank? Ali said that he ___ to London last year.
f: The event happened last year, so the simple past form went is correct.

q: What is the smallest unit of life?
f: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living things.

q: Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan served as President (Speaker) of Pakistan's Constituent Assembly from 1948 until which year?
f: He held the office from 1948 until the Assembly was dissolved by Governor General Ghulam Muhammad in 1954.

q: What is the meaning of the word 'Hadith'?
o: A saying or tradition of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
f: Hadith means a report, saying or tradition. In Islam it is the record of the sayings, actions and approvals of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

q: What is the meaning of the word obscure?
f: Obscure means hard to understand or see, or not well known.

q: Which number is different from the others: 3, 5, 7, 11, 12, 13, 17, 19?
f: All the numbers except 12 are prime numbers. 12 is divisible by 2, 3, 4 and 6.

q: Which scientist won Nobel Prizes in two different sciences, Physics and Chemistry?
f: Marie Curie won the Physics prize in 1903 (shared) and the Chemistry prize in 1911. She is the only person to win in two different sciences besides Linus Pauling, who won Chemistry and Peace.

q: Who wrote the folk romance Sassi Punnu in verse?
f: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai told the tale of Sassui Punhun in his Shah Jo Risalo.

q: In which city is Shalimar Bagh (Shalimar Gardens) located?
f: The Shalimar Gardens are in Lahore, Pakistan. They were built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan around 1641.

q: What is sin(270 degrees minus theta) equal to?
f: Sine of 270 minus theta lies in the third quadrant where sine is negative, and the function changes to cosine at 270. So the result is minus cos theta.

q: What is the currency of Spain?
f: Spain uses the Euro, which replaced the peseta in 2002.

q: Who was the Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan at the time of the 1956 Constitution?
f: Abdul Wahab Khan was the Speaker from 1955 and was in office when the 1956 Constitution came into force.

q: Which city of Pakistan is world famous for sports goods?
f: Sialkot is the centre of Pakistan's sports goods industry, especially footballs.

q: When did World War 1 start?
f: World War 1 began in July 1914 after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand.

q: Which part of Asia is called the subcontinent?
f: The subcontinent means South Asia, the region of Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and nearby countries.

q: Which symbol denotes the union of two sets?
f: The symbol ∪ means union, the set of all elements that are in A or in B or in both.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'console'?
f: To console means to give comfort to someone who is sad.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'consumer'?
f: A consumer is a person who buys and uses goods or services, like a customer.

q: When did the Gandhi-Jinnah talks take place in Bombay?
f: Gandhi met Quaid-e-Azam Jinnah at his house in Bombay from 9 to 27 September 1944. The talks failed because they did not agree on the Pakistan demand.

q: What is Pakistan's top export product group?
f: Textiles and clothing make up more than half of Pakistan's total exports.

q: Ernest Hemingway was a writer of which country?
f: Ernest Hemingway was an American novelist who wrote The Old Man and the Sea.

q: Which word is the opposite of zeal?
f: Zeal means strong enthusiasm, while apathy means lack of interest.

q: What is 12 + 2/2?
f: Division first: 2/2 = 1. Then 12 + 1 = 13.

q: What is 2/3 + 3?
What is 4 + 4/4?
f: Division first: 4/4 = 1. Then 4 + 1 = 5.

q: The speed of a train is twice that of a car. If the car travels 100 km in one hour, how far does the train travel in 30 minutes?
f: Train speed is 2 x 100 = 200 km/h. In half an hour it covers 200 / 2 = 100 km.

q: Which number is different: 104, 106, 108, 110, 103?
f: 104, 106, 108 and 110 are all even numbers, while 103 is odd.

q: If the 2nd of a month is Monday, what day is the 16th of that month?
f: 16 - 2 = 14 days, which is exactly two weeks, so the day is the same: Monday.

q: If a car covers 200 km in one hour, how many km will it cover in one minute?
f: One hour has 60 minutes, so distance in one minute is 200 divided by 60 = 3.33 km (10/3 km).

q: Who was the Chief Justice of Pakistan in 2018?
f: Mian Saqib Nisar was Chief Justice of Pakistan from December 2016 until January 2019, which covers all of 2018.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 19th of that month be?
f: From the 4th to the 19th is 15 days later. 15 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1, so move 1 day(s) forward from Sunday to reach Monday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 22nd of that month be?
f: From the 4th to the 22nd is 18 days later. 18 divided by 7 leaves remainder 4, so move 4 day(s) forward from Monday to reach Friday.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Thursday, what day will the 25th of that month be?
f: From the 3rd to the 25th is 22 days later. 22 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1, so move 1 day(s) forward from Thursday to reach Friday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 27th of that month be?
f: From the 2nd to the 27th is 25 days later. 25 divided by 7 leaves remainder 4, so move 4 day(s) forward from Friday to reach Tuesday.

q: In a class of 1000 students, 850 are present. What is the percentage of absentees?
What is the cube of 900?
In which year were the Geneva Accords on Afghanistan signed, leading to the Soviet troop withdrawal?
f: The Geneva Accords were signed on 14 April 1988 by Pakistan, Afghanistan, the USA and the USSR.

q: Which word is a synonym of accuse?
f: To accuse is to charge someone with a fault or crime, which means to blame.

q: Aliza is 12 years older than Asad. When Asad was 6, Aliza was 3 times his age. How old will Aliza be when Asad is 14?
f: When Asad was 6, Aliza was 3 x 6 = 18, so the gap is 18 - 6 = 12 years, which never changes. When Asad is 14, Aliza is 14 + 12 = 26.

q: Which word is a synonym of 'ally'?
f: An ally is a friend or partner who supports you, so 'partner' is the closest meaning.

q: In which year were Ahmadis declared non-Muslim in Pakistan?
f: The Second Amendment of 1974 declared Ahmadis non-Muslim.

q: In which constitution of Pakistan were Ahmadis declared non-Muslim?
f: The change came through the Second Amendment of 1974 to the 1973 Constitution.

q: What is the antonym of the word broadly?
f: Broadly means in a wide way, so its opposite is narrowly.

q: What is the antonym of the word industrious?
f: Industrious means hardworking, so its opposite is lazy.

q: What is the antonym of the word relinquish?
f: Relinquish means to give up, so its opposite is retain or keep.

q: At what age did Arfa Karim become the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional in the world?
f: Arfa Karim Randhawa passed the Microsoft Certified Professional exam in 2004 at the age of 9. This made her the youngest MCP in the world at that time.

q: What is the currency of Argentina?
f: Argentina uses the Argentine peso as its official currency. The real belongs to Brazil and the bolivar to Venezuela.

q: Who is known as Baba-e-Sahafat (Father of Journalism) in Pakistan?
f: Maulana Zafar Ali Khan, editor of the daily Zamindar, is most commonly given this title in Pakistani textbooks.

q: Data Ganj Bakhsh (Hazrat Ali Hujwiri) wrote his famous book Kashf-ul-Mahjoob in which language?
f: Kashf-ul-Mahjoob, a classic work on Sufism, was written in Persian.

q: What is the meaning of the idiom 'beat about the bush'?
o: To avoid coming to the main point
f: The idiom means talking around a subject without addressing it directly.

q: What is the last letter of the word BEAUTY?
f: B-E-A-U-T-Y ends with the letter Y.

q: Which event caused the United States to enter the Second World War, and which country attacked it?
o: Japan attacked Pearl Harbor in December 1941
f: On 7 December 1941 Japan launched a surprise air attack on the US naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii. The next day the United States declared war on Japan.

q: Ali is 3 years old and his sister is 4 times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali becomes 10?
f: Sister's age now is 3 x 4 = 12 years. Ali gains 7 years (10 - 3), so the sister also gains 7 years: 12 + 7 = 19.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali becomes 8?
f: Sister's age now is 5 x 3 = 15. Ali gains 3 years (8 - 5), so she is 15 + 3 = 18.

q: Fill in the blank: I ___ to Lahore in August.
f: The sentence refers to a finished past time (August), so the simple past tense went is correct.

q: Fill in the blank: She was afraid ___ dogs.
f: The adjective afraid is followed by the preposition of.

q: How many times has Brazil won the FIFA World Cup?
f: Brazil won the World Cup in 1958, 1962, 1970, 1994 and 2002, which makes 5 titles. It did not win in 2026.

q: What is the capital of Kuwait?
f: Kuwait City is the capital.

q: What is the characteristic of the common logarithm of 99?
f: 99 lies between 10 and 100, so log 99 is between 1 and 2 (about 1.9956). The whole number part, the characteristic, is 1.

q: Grass is to ground as chimney is to what?
f: Grass grows on the ground, in the same way a chimney stands on top of the roof of a house.

q: Florida is a what?
f: Florida is a state in the south-eastern United States.

q: Where is the headquarters of the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission (PAEC)?
f: The PAEC, Pakistan's main nuclear agency, has its headquarters in Islamabad.

q: Complete the series: 1, 3, 7, 13, ?
f: The differences are 2, 4, 6, so the next difference is 8. Then 13 + 8 = 21.

q: The Torkham border crossing connects Pakistan with which country?
f: Torkham is at the western end of the Khyber Pass and joins Pakistan's Khyber district with Nangarhar in Afghanistan.

q: A book is bought for 30 and sold for 40. What is the percentage profit?
f: Profit = 40 - 30 = 10. Profit percent = 10 / 30 x 100 = 33.33 percent.

q: Balochistan covers roughly what percentage of the total area of Pakistan?
f: Balochistan has about 347,190 square km out of about 796,095 square km, which is about 44 percent.

q: What is the most frequently occurring value in a set of data called?
f: The mode is the value that is repeated the most times in the data.

q: Which team won two consecutive Pakistan Super League titles?
f: Lahore Qalandars won the PSL in 2022 and again in 2023.

q: What is the national currency of Pakistan?
f: Pakistan's currency is the Pakistani rupee, issued by the State Bank of Pakistan.

q: What is the sum of the number of days in March and December?
f: March has 31 days and December has 31 days. So 31 + 31 = 62.

q: In which year was the Simla (Shimla) Deputation held?
f: A Muslim delegation led by Sir Aga Khan met Viceroy Lord Minto at Simla on 1 October 1906. This led to the founding of the Muslim League in December 1906.

q: After how many years of Pakistan's creation did East Pakistan separate to become Bangladesh?
f: Pakistan came into being in 1947 and East Pakistan separated in December 1971, which is 24 years later.

q: Which element in haemoglobin is necessary for carrying oxygen in the blood?
f: Haemoglobin contains iron, and the iron binds oxygen in the red blood cells. Lack of iron causes anaemia.

q: Which Egyptian footballer is famous as Mo Salah?
f: Mohamed Salah is the well known Egyptian forward who plays for Liverpool and is nicknamed the Egyptian King.

q: Which word is a synonym of envious?
f: Envious means feeling resentment about another person's success or belongings, which is the same as jealous.

q: At which port city did the British first set up a trading base in India?
f: The British East India Company set up its first factory at Surat in Gujarat in 1613.

q: How many faces does a hexagonal prism have?
f: A hexagonal prism has 6 rectangular side faces and 2 hexagonal faces (top and bottom), so 6 + 2 = 8.

q: For what is Al-Razi (Rhazes) famous?
f: Al-Razi was a great Muslim physician and chemist, who described measles and smallpox in his medical works.

q: Which team was the runner-up in the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar?
f: Argentina beat France on penalties after a 3-3 draw in the 2022 final, so France was the runner-up.

q: Against which power did Tipu Sultan of Mysore fight his main wars?
f: Tipu Sultan fought the Anglo-Mysore wars against the British East India Company and was martyred defending Seringapatam in 1799.

q: A jet uses 80 gallons of fuel to fly at 320 km per hour (80 gallons per 320 km). How many gallons are needed to cover 700 km?
f: Fuel per km = 80 / 320 = 0.25 gallons. For 700 km: 700 x 0.25 = 175 gallons.

q: Which form of government was provided by the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan?
f: The 1956 Constitution made Pakistan an Islamic Republic with a federal, parliamentary system and a single-house legislature.

q: Where was the United Nations founded in 1945?
f: The UN Charter was signed in San Francisco on 26 June 1945 at the conference that created the organization.

q: The Strait of Gibraltar connects the Mediterranean Sea with which water body?
f: The Strait of Gibraltar is a narrow channel between Spain and Morocco that joins the Mediterranean Sea to the Atlantic Ocean.

q: A person walks 6 km towards the north, then turns right and walks some distance, then turns right again. Which direction is he now heading?
f: Facing north, a right turn makes him face east. Another right turn from east makes him face south.

q: Who is the Federal Minister for National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination of Pakistan (health minister) as of 2026?
f: Syed Mustafa Kamal of the MQM-P holds the federal health portfolio in the government formed after the February 2024 elections.

q: Ahmed is 5 years old and his sister is four times his age. When Ahmed is 12 years old, what is his sister's age?
f: Sister is 4 x 5 = 20 years now, so the gap is 15 years. When Ahmed is 12, sister is 12 + 15 = 27 years.

q: What is the highest peak of the Himalayas?
f: Mount Everest, on the Nepal-China border, is the highest peak of the Himalayas and of the world. Its official height is about 8849 m.

q: In which battle were the most Huffaz (memorisers) of the Quran martyred?
f: Many Huffaz were martyred at Yamama (12 AH) against the false prophet Musailma. This led Hazrat Umar (RA) to urge Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) to compile the Quran in one book.

q: What is the capital of Hungary?
f: Budapest is the capital and largest city of Hungary. It lies on the River Danube.

q: Who were the four Rightly Guided Caliphs (Khulafa-e-Rashideen) of Islam, in order?
f: After the Holy Prophet (PBUH), the caliphs were Hazrat Abu Bakr, Hazrat Umar, Hazrat Uthman and Hazrat Ali (RA) in that order.

q: In which year did the USA and its allies invade Iraq?
f: The US-led invasion of Iraq began in 2003 to remove the government of Saddam Hussein.

q: Where is the historic Jamrud Fort located?
o: Peshawar, at the entrance of the Khyber Pass
f: Jamrud Fort stands near Peshawar at the eastern mouth of the Khyber Pass in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It was built in 1836 by the Sikh general Hari Singh Nalwa.

q: What is the capital of Japan?
f: Tokyo is the capital and largest city of Japan.

q: Who wrote the book Asrar-e-Khudi (Secrets of the Self)?
f: Allama Muhammad Iqbal wrote Asrar-e-Khudi in Persian, and it was published in 1915.

q: Approximately how many people died in World War II (soldiers and civilians together)?
f: Most estimates put the total deaths of World War II, including civilians, at roughly 70 to 85 million.

q: The Kohat Tunnel connects Kohat with which city?
f: The Kohat Tunnel links Kohat with Peshawar through the Kohat Pass road, which makes the journey shorter.

q: Which landlocked country can use Pakistan's seaports (Karachi, Port Qasim and Gwadar) for its sea trade?
f: Afghanistan has no coastline, so it uses Pakistan's ports under the Afghan Transit Trade arrangement. Central Asian states are also linked to these ports by road routes.

q: Which language is mainly spoken in Chitral?
f: Khowar (also called Chitrali) is the main local language of Chitral district.

q: At which Inn of Court in London did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah study law and qualify as a barrister?
f: Jinnah joined Lincoln's Inn in 1893 and was called to the bar in 1896, at the age of 19.

q: What type of legislature did the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan provide?
f: The 1956 Constitution created a single-house (unicameral) National Assembly of 300 members.

q: What is the date of birth of Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan was born on 1 October 1895 in Karnal, in present-day Haryana, India.

q: What is a synonym of the word liberty?
f: Liberty means the state of being free, so its synonym is freedom.

q: Where is the Mahmud Ghaznavi Mosque, one of the oldest mosques in Pakistan, located?
f: The Mahmud Ghaznavi Mosque stands at Odigram (Udegram) in Swat District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It dates from the Ghaznavid period, around 1048-49 AD.

q: In which year was the Nishan-e-Haider awarded to Major Aziz Bhatti?
f: Major Aziz Bhatti was martyred in the 1965 war near the BRB canal at Lahore and was honoured with the Nishan-e-Haider for it that year.

q: Who was the first Chief Martial Law Administrator of Pakistan in 1958?
f: Martial law was imposed on 7 October 1958 by President Iskander Mirza, who made General Ayub Khan the Chief Martial Law Administrator.

q: What is the geometric mean of 4 and 16?
f: GM = square root of (4 x 16) = square root of 64 = 8.

q: How many member countries does SAARC have?
f: SAARC has eight members: Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives and Afghanistan.

q: What is the mode of the numbers 3, 3, 4, 5, 6?
f: The mode is the value that appears most often. The number 3 appears twice and all others appear once.

q: To which age do the people of the Indus Valley Civilization belong?
f: The Indus Valley people used copper and bronze tools, so the civilization belongs to the Bronze Age.

q: For what were the people of Mohenjo-daro and Harappa famous?
o: Well-planned cities with a drainage system
f: Their cities had straight streets, brick houses and covered drains. This shows advanced town planning.

q: If the first day of a month is Monday, what day will the 21st day be?
f: The 21st is 20 days after the 1st. 20 divided by 7 leaves remainder 6, and Monday plus 6 days is Sunday.

q: Suo motu notice by the Supreme Court of Pakistan is taken under which article of the Constitution?
f: Article 184(3) gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction on matters of public importance involving fundamental rights.

q: On which date was NATO founded?
f: The North Atlantic Treaty was signed in Washington on 4 April 1949.

q: In 1999 General Pervez Musharraf replaced Nawaz Sharif and became what?
f: After the coup of 12 October 1999 Musharraf took the title Chief Executive.

q: Which was the first battle of the Muslims against a non-Arab power?
f: The Battle of Muta in 8 AH (629 CE) was fought against the Byzantine (Roman) army, a non-Arab power.

q: Which word is a synonym of obvious?
f: Obvious means easy to see or understand, which is the same as evident.

q: In which year did the Third Battle of Panipat take place?
f: The Third Battle of Panipat was fought in 1761 between the Marathas and the Afghan ruler Ahmad Shah Abdali.

q: About what percent of the total area of Pakistan is covered by Balochistan?
f: Balochistan has about 347,190 square km out of about 796,095 square km, which is about 43.6 percent.

In which type of cricket match is the pink ball used?
o: Only one-day matches played in the morning
f: The pink ball is easier to see under floodlights, so it is used in day-night Test matches.

q: On which date was the first cricket World Cup played (started)?
f: The first Cricket World Cup, the Prudential Cup, began on 7 June 1975 in England.

q: What is the capital of Poland?
f: Warsaw is the capital and largest city of Poland. It lies on the Vistula river.

q: Which building is shown on the back of the Pakistani 5000 rupee note?
f: The State Bank of Pakistan states that the reverse of the Rs 5000 note carries a picture of Faisal Mosque, Islamabad.

q: Under which article of the 1973 Constitution is the definition of a Muslim and non-Muslim given, as added by the Second Amendment?
f: The Second Amendment added clause 3 to Article 260 and defined who is a Muslim. Qadianis were thus declared non-Muslim.

q: In which year was the Radcliffe Award announced?
f: The Radcliffe Boundary Commission award was announced on 17 August 1947, after independence. It fixed the Punjab and Bengal boundaries.

q: Who received the first Nobel Prize in Physics, awarded in 1901?
f: The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in 1901, and the Physics prize went to Wilhelm Rontgen for discovering X-rays.

q: In which province is the Rekodiq mining project (copper and gold) located?
f: Rekodiq is a copper-gold deposit in Chagai district of Balochistan.

q: For what work did Dr Abdus Salam win the Nobel Prize?
o: Unifying the weak and electromagnetic forces
f: Dr Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for the electroweak unification theory.

q: Which phrase does the Quran use for the Holy Prophet (PBUH) as a mercy for all?
f: Surah Al-Anbiya says the Prophet was sent as Rahmatul lil Alamin, a mercy for all the worlds.

q: What is the gap in years between the first (1956) and second (1962) constitution of Pakistan?
f: The first constitution came into force in March 1956 and the second in June 1962. 1962 minus 1956 is 6 years.

q: Which letter is used to denote the set of rational numbers?
f: Rational numbers are written as quotients (fractions) of integers, so the set is denoted by Q.

q: What is the domain of the function sin x?
f: Sine is defined for every real value of x. Its range, not its domain, is from minus 1 to 1.

q: What is the determinant of a singular matrix?
f: A square matrix is called singular exactly when its determinant is zero. Such a matrix has no inverse.

q: If the sum of two angles of a triangle is 90 degrees, what is the third angle?
f: The three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees. So the third angle is 180 - 90 = 90 degrees.

q: Ship is to captain as car is to what?
f: A captain is the person who controls a ship. In the same way a driver controls a car.

q: How many countries are there in South Asia (the SAARC region)?
f: South Asia has eight countries: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

q: Spain is located in which continent?
f: Spain lies in the south-west of Europe on the Iberian Peninsula.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'strength'?
f: Strength means the quality of being strong, which is the same as power or force.

q: What is the sum of 2 and 8?
Which word is closest in meaning to 'momentary'?
f: Momentary means lasting only a very short time, which is the same as brief.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'fragile'?
f: Fragile means easily broken, which is the same as delicate.

q: In which district and province is the Tanda Dam located?
f: Tanda Dam is a small dam built near Kohat in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It supplies drinking and irrigation water.

q: In which district of Punjab is Tandlianwala located?
f: Tandlianwala is a city and tehsil in Faisalabad district of Punjab.

q: Tarbela Dam construction began in 1968 during whose rule?
f: Work on Tarbela Dam started in 1968 when Field Marshal Ayub Khan was President. It followed the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960.

q: Fill in the blank: He is too weak ___ walk.
f: The pattern is too + adjective + to + verb, so the correct word is to.

q: Which PSL team won the title in two consecutive seasons, 2022 and 2023?
f: Lahore Qalandars won the PSL final in 2022 and again in 2023, the only back-to-back titles in PSL history.

q: Which tribe of Pashtuns did Sher Shah Suri belong to?
f: Sher Shah Suri belonged to the Sur tribe of the Pashtuns, which is why he is called Suri.

q: Sher Shah Suri belonged to which ethnic group?
f: Sher Shah Suri was a Pashtun (Afghan) from the Sur tribe.

q: Who was the leader of the hypocrites (Munafiqeen) in the Battle of Uhud?
f: Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul withdrew with about 300 men before the battle began.

q: What does the expression Bird's Eye View mean?
o: A view from a high point looking down
f: A bird's eye view means a wide view from high above, as a bird would see it.

q: Which famous book was written by the Punjabi poet Waris Shah?
f: Waris Shah wrote the Punjabi romantic epic Heer (Heer Ranjha) around 1766.

q: On what date did Pakistan win the Cricket World Cup final in 1992?
f: Pakistan beat England in the final at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on 25 March 1992 under Imran Khan.

q: Fill in the blank: He writes ____ blue ink.
f: We say write in ink, writing in blue ink, when the colour of the writing is meant. With is also used for the pen, but in is the standard choice here.

q: Who wrote the book Pakistan: The Formative Phase?
f: Pakistan: The Formative Phase was written by the political scientist Khalid B. Sayeed.

q: What is 2/2?
f: A number divided by itself equals 1.

q: What is 9/2?
f: 9 divided by 2 is 4.5.

q: A train covers 20 km in 100 minutes. How long will it take to cover 1 km?
f: 100 minutes divided by 20 km gives 5 minutes for each km.

q: Which number is different: 103, 104, 105, 116, 106?
f: 103, 104, 105 and 106 are consecutive numbers, but 116 does not fit in the sequence.

q: Today is Monday and it is the 12th day of the month. What day will the 10th of the same month be?
f: The 10th is 2 days before the 12th. Two days before Monday is Saturday.

q: Which number comes next: 65, 115, 75, 175, ?
f: Alternate terms form two series. The 1st, 3rd and 5th terms go 65, 75, so the next is 75 + 10 = 85. The even-place terms go 115, 175.

q: Total students are 1500 and 1300 are absent. What is the percentage of present students (approximately)?
f: Present students = 1500 - 1300 = 200. Percentage = 200/1500 x 100 = 13.33%.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 12th of that month?
f: 12 - 3 = 9 days later. 9 = 7 + 2, so move 2 days forward from Sunday, which is Tuesday.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 13th of that month?
f: 13 - 1 = 12 days later. 12 = 7 + 5, so move 5 days forward from Sunday, which is Friday.

q: If the 24th date of a month is Friday, what day is the 14th of that month?
f: 24 - 14 = 10 days earlier. 10 = 7 + 3, so go back 3 days from Friday: Thursday, Wednesday, Tuesday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day is the 14th of that month?
f: 14 - 4 = 10 days later. 10 = 7 + 3, so move 3 days forward from Friday: Saturday, Sunday, Monday.

q: Find the odd one out: 150, 261, 372, 594, 695
f: The series goes up by 111: 150, 261, 372, 483, 594, then 705. The term 695 does not fit (it should be 705).

q: Which reforms were introduced in British India in 1919?
f: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms were enacted as the Government of India Act 1919 and introduced dyarchy in the provinces.

q: Who launched the Quit Kashmir Movement in 1946 against the Dogra Maharaja?
f: Sheikh Abdullah and his National Conference launched the Quit Kashmir Movement in May 1946 against Maharaja Hari Singh.

q: Which constitution of Pakistan was made in 1956?
f: The Constituent Assembly passed the first constitution of Pakistan in 1956, which made the country an Islamic Republic.

q: What was the first amendment to the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan about?
o: Recognition of Bangladesh by changing the definition of the territories of Pakistan
Allowing the President to dissolve the Assembly
Changing the name of the country
f: The First Amendment of 1974 changed Article 1 so that the territories of Pakistan no longer included East Pakistan, after Bangladesh was recognized.

q: Who was the Prime Minister of Pakistan during the 1999 Kargil conflict?
f: Nawaz Sharif was Prime Minister from 1997 until October 1999, so he was in office during the Kargil conflict.

q: On which date was the first Cricket World Cup final played in 1975?
f: The first Cricket World Cup was played in England in June 1975 and its final was held at Lord's on 21 June 1975.

q: A plane uses 60 gallons of fuel to cover 90 km. How many gallons are needed to cover 200 km?
f: Fuel per km is 60/90 = 2/3 gallon. For 200 km: 200 x 2/3 = 133.33 gallons.

q: Who won the 2014 ICC World Twenty20 (T20 World Cup)?
f: Sri Lanka beat India by six wickets in the final at Dhaka in April 2014.

q: Who won the 2023 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup?
f: Australia beat hosts India by six wickets in the final at Ahmedabad on 19 November 2023.

q: What is the value of 2 + 2 x 3?
f: By BODMAS, multiplication comes first: 2 x 3 = 6. Then 2 + 6 = 8.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 19th of that month be?
f: From the 2nd to the 19th is 17 days later. 17 divided by 7 leaves remainder 3, so move 3 day(s) forward from Monday to reach Thursday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 20th of that month be?
f: From the 4th to the 20th is 16 days later. 16 divided by 7 leaves remainder 2, so move 2 day(s) forward from Monday to reach Wednesday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 20th of that month be?
f: From the 2nd to the 20th is 18 days later. 18 divided by 7 leaves remainder 4, so move 4 day(s) forward from Friday to reach Tuesday.

q: If the 31st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 25th of that month be?
f: From the 31st to the 25th is 6 days earlier. 6 divided by 7 leaves remainder 6, so move 6 day(s) backward from Monday to reach Tuesday.

q: If the 12th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 29th of that month be?
f: From the 12th to the 29th is 17 days later. 17 divided by 7 leaves remainder 3, so move 3 day(s) forward from Monday to reach Thursday.

q: If the 31st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 20th of that month be?
f: From the 31st to the 20th is 11 days earlier. 11 divided by 7 leaves remainder 4, so move 4 day(s) backward from Monday to reach Thursday.

q: If the 31st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 2nd of that month be?
f: From the 31st to the 2nd is 29 days earlier. 29 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1, so move 1 day(s) backward from Monday to reach Sunday.

The 3rd June Plan, which announced the partition of British India, was announced in which year?
f: Lord Mountbatten announced the plan on 3 June 1947. It decided the partition of India into India and Pakistan.

q: Who was the third wife of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), in order of marriage?
f: In order of marriage the wives were Khadija, Sawda, then Aisha (RA). So Aisha (RA) was the third.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 14th day be?
f: From the 4th to the 14th is 10 days. 10 divided by 7 leaves 3, so Monday + 3 days = Thursday.

q: If the 15th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 4th of that month?
f: From the 4th to the 15th is 11 days. 11 divided by 7 leaves 4, so Monday - 4 days = Thursday.

q: If the 5th day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 18th of the month?
f: From the 5th to the 18th is 13 days. 13 divided by 7 leaves 6, so Sunday + 6 days = Saturday.

q: If the 9th of a month is Sunday, what day is the 26th of the month?
f: From the 9th to the 26th is 17 days. 17 divided by 7 leaves 3, so Sunday + 3 days = Wednesday.

q: What is the abscissa of a point also called?
f: The abscissa is the horizontal distance of a point, which is its x-coordinate.

q: Where did Maulana Syed Abul Ala Maududi die?
f: Maududi died in Buffalo, New York, USA, on 22 September 1979 while seeking medical treatment.

q: If the force on an object is doubled while its mass stays the same, what happens to its acceleration?
f: By Newton's second law, F = ma, so a = F / m. Acceleration is directly proportional to force when mass is fixed.

q: What is acceleration?
f: Acceleration is how fast the velocity of an object changes with time, a = change in velocity / time.

q: What is the additive identity of 5?
f: The additive identity is the number which leaves a number unchanged when added. 5 + 0 = 5.

q: What is the additive inverse of 65?
f: The additive inverse is the number which gives zero when added. 65 + (-65) = 0.

q: On which date was the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan adopted by the National Assembly?
f: The National Assembly adopted the Constitution on 10 April 1973. It was enforced later, on 14 August 1973.

q: In the sentence 'He fought bravely', what part of speech is the word 'bravely'?
f: 'Bravely' tells how he fought, so it modifies a verb. Words that modify verbs and end in -ly like this are adverbs.

q: What type of adverb is the word 'often'?
f: 'Often' tells how many times something happens. Adverbs that answer 'how often' are adverbs of frequency.

q: The age of Ahmad is three times the age of his sister, and his sister is 4 years old. What will Ahmad's age be after 10 years?
f: Ahmad is 3 x 4 = 12 years old now. After 10 years he will be 12 + 10 = 22 years old.

q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is double his age. What is his sister's age?
f: Double of 4 is 2 x 4 = 8, so the sister is 8 years old.

q: Akbar is older than Ahmed and Bilal is younger than Akbar. Who is the oldest of the three?
f: Akbar is older than both Ahmed and Bilal, so he is the oldest.

q: Which airline belongs to Italy and is its national flag carrier since 2021?
f: ITA Airways is the national airline of Italy. It took over from Alitalia in October 2021.

q: Which is the intelligence agency of Israel?
f: Mossad is the national intelligence agency of Israel, responsible for foreign intelligence.

q: Abul Ala Maududi, the founder of Jamaat-e-Islami, was born in which city?
f: Maududi was born in 1903 in Aurangabad in the Deccan, British India.

q: In which year did Abul Ala Maududi die?
f: Maududi died in 1979 in Buffalo, USA, and was buried in Lahore.

q: In which country is the city of Allahabad (now Prayagraj) located?
f: Allahabad is in the state of Uttar Pradesh in India. Its name was changed to Prayagraj in 2018.

q: Allama Iqbal did his graduation (BA) from which college?
f: Iqbal passed his BA in 1897 from Government College Lahore, and later his MA there in 1899.

q: Complete the series: 4Z, 5Y, ?
f: The numbers go up by 1 (4, 5, 6) and the letters go backwards (Z, Y, X). So the next term is 6X.

q: Altaf Hussain Hali was a famous poet of which language?
f: Altaf Hussain Hali (1837-1914) was a well-known Urdu poet and critic.

q: Ali is older than Hammad but younger than Amir. Hammad is younger than Amir. Who is the youngest of the three?
f: Amir is older than Ali, and Ali is older than Hammad. So the order from oldest is Amir, Ali, Hammad, and Hammad is the youngest.

q: Muhammad Amir is a famous fast bowler of which country?
f: Muhammad Amir is a left-arm fast bowler who plays cricket for Pakistan.

q: Which country annexed Sindh in 1843?
f: The British East India Company, under General Charles Napier, defeated the Talpur Mirs at Miani in 1843 and annexed Sindh.

q: From which ruling family did the British annex Sindh in 1843?
f: The Talpur Mirs ruled Sindh when Charles Napier defeated them in the Battle of Miani in 1843.

q: What is the antonym of the word intricate?
f: Intricate means very complicated, so its opposite is simple.

q: What is the antonym of the word solitude?
f: Solitude means being alone, so its opposite is company.

q: What is the antonym of the word elegant?
f: Elegant means graceful and stylish, so its opposite is clumsy or awkward.

q: What is the antonym of the word generous?
f: Generous means ready to give freely, so its opposite is stingy.

q: What is the antonym of the word pleasant?
f: Pleasant means enjoyable, so its opposite is unpleasant.

q: What is the antonym of the word terrible?
f: Terrible means very bad, so its opposite is wonderful or excellent.

q: What is the antonym of the word vicious?
f: Vicious means cruel and violent, so its opposite is gentle.

q: What is the antonym of the word wide?
f: Wide means large from side to side, so its opposite is narrow.

q: What is another name of Tipu Sultan, the ruler of Mysore?
f: Tipu Sultan was known as the Tiger of Mysore because of his bravery against the British.

q: What was the old name of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia before 1932?
f: Abdulaziz Ibn Saud ruled the Kingdom of Hejaz and Najd, which was renamed Saudi Arabia in September 1932.

q: Argentina is located in which continent?
f: Argentina lies in the southern part of South America. It shares borders with Chile, Bolivia, Paraguay, Brazil and Uruguay.

q: Which country is ranked as the strongest military in the world by the Global Firepower index?
f: The Global Firepower index ranks the USA first because of its budget, technology, air power and navy. Russia and China follow.

q: What percentage of Pakistan's total area does Balochistan, the largest province, cover?
f: Balochistan covers about 347,190 square km out of about 796,095 square km (the area commonly used for the provinces). 347,190 divided by 796,095 is about 0.44, so about 44 percent

q: Whose expedition completed the first voyage around the world (1519 to 1522)?
f: The Spanish expedition that Ferdinand Magellan led was the first to sail around the Earth. Magellan was killed in the Philippines in 1521 and Juan Sebastian Elcano completed the voyage.

q: What was the name of the dog that stayed with the Companions of the Cave (Ashab-e-Kahf)?
f: Muslim tradition names the dog of the Ashab-e-Kahf as Qitmir (Kitmir). The dog is mentioned in Surah Al-Kahf of the Quran, though its name is given in commentaries.

q: Akbar is older than Ahmad and Aslam. Ahmad is younger than Aslam. Which statement is true?
o: Aslam is older than Ahmad and younger than Akbar
f: Akbar is older than both. Ahmad is younger than Aslam, so the order from oldest is Akbar, Aslam, Ahmad.

q: In which continent is Australia located?
f: Australia is both a country and a continent, and it is part of the Oceania region in the southern hemisphere.

q: What is the average of 18 and 54?
f: Add the numbers: 18 + 54 = 72. Divide by 2: 72 / 2 = 36.

q: What is the average of 30 and 42?
f: Add the numbers: 30 + 42 = 72. Divide by 2: 72 / 2 = 36.

q: What is the average of 8 and 12?
f: Add the numbers: 8 + 12 = 20. Divide by 2: 20 / 2 = 10.

q: Who has the highest batting average in Test cricket (minimum 20 innings)?
f: Sir Donald Bradman of Australia scored 6,996 runs at an average of 99.94 in Tests. No other player is close to this average.

q: Who was the first Pakistani to win a Nobel Prize, and in which field?
f: Dr Abdus Salam won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979, shared with Glashow and Weinberg. He was the first Pakistani and the first Muslim to win a science Nobel.

q: Choose the correct word: Ayesha repaired the glasses because her brother ___ them before.
f: The repair happened after an earlier action, so the earlier action takes the past perfect tense: had broken.

q: How many divisions does Azad Jammu and Kashmir have?
f: AJK is divided into three divisions: Muzaffarabad, Poonch and Mirpur.

q: On which date was Major Aziz Bhatti martyred in the 1965 war?
f: Major Raja Aziz Bhatti was martyred on 10 September 1965 defending the BRB Canal sector near Lahore.

q: Who was the son of the Mughal emperor Babur?
f: Babur's eldest son and successor was Humayun.

q: Kala Bagh Dam is proposed on which river, in which district of Punjab?
f: Kalabagh is in Mianwali district where the Indus leaves the salt range. The dam has been proposed there but not built.

q: A bag has 5 red balls and 3 green balls. What is the probability of drawing a blue ball?
f: There is no blue ball in the bag, so favourable outcomes are 0 and the probability is 0/8 = 0.

q: Jinnah Barrage is built on which river?
f: Jinnah Barrage is on the Indus River at Kalabagh in Mianwali district.

q: By what other name is the Ghulam Muhammad Barrage known?
f: The Ghulam Muhammad Barrage is the Kotri Barrage on the Indus near Hyderabad, Sindh.

q: Who was the President of India when the Indus Waters Treaty was signed in 1960?
f: Rajendra Prasad was India's President from 1950 to 1962, which includes 1960.

q: Which word is a synonym of 'beauty'?
f: Loveliness has the same meaning as beauty.

q: Which is the smallest bird in the world?
f: The bee hummingbird of Cuba is only about 5 to 6 cm long, the smallest bird.

q: When a bill is passed by both the National Assembly and the Senate of Pakistan, whose assent does it need to become law?
f: A bill passed by both houses is sent to the President for assent. After assent it becomes an Act of Parliament.

q: On which date did Pakistan come into being?
f: Pakistan became an independent state on 14 August 1947, which was 27 Ramadan 1366 AH.

q: Christopher Columbus, the explorer who reached the Americas in 1492, was from which country?
f: Columbus was born in Genoa, in present-day Italy, though he sailed for the Spanish crown.

q: How many bones does a young child (infant) have approximately?
f: A newborn baby has about 300 bones. Many of them fuse together as the child grows, leaving 206 in an adult.

q: Who wrote the book Al-Bidaya wan-Nihaya?
f: Al-Bidaya wan-Nihaya (The Beginning and the End) is a large history book by Hafiz Ibn Kathir.

q: Where was Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah born?
f: Quaid-e-Azam was born on 25 December 1876 in Karachi (Wazir Mansion).

q: Where was Sir Syed Ahmad Khan born?
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was born in Delhi in 1817.

q: On what date did Oman hand over Gwadar to Pakistan after it was purchased?
f: Pakistan bought Gwadar from Oman and took formal control on 8 September 1958.

q: What is the international boundary between Pakistan and India called?
f: The Radcliffe Line was drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe in 1947 and is the Pakistan-India boundary.

q: What is the capital of Brazil?
f: Brasilia is the capital of Brazil. It replaced Rio de Janeiro in 1960.

q: Which is the longest river in Brazil?
f: The Amazon is the longest river in Brazil and the largest river in the world by volume.

q: Ali's age is 10 and his sister Aisha is double his age. When Ali is 15, how old will Aisha be?
f: Aisha is 20 now. Ali will be 15 after 5 years, so Aisha will be 20 plus 5 = 25.

q: Where was Liaquat Ali Khan buried?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan was assassinated in 1951 and buried in Karachi next to the Mazar-e-Quaid.

q: Who was the Prime Minister of Canada during World War 2?
f: William Lyon Mackenzie King led Canada from 1935 to 1948, which covers the whole of World War 2.

q: Kiev (Kyiv) is the capital of which country?
f: Ukraine is the capital.

q: Kuala Lumpur is the capital of which country?
f: Malaysia is the capital.

q: What is the capital of Albania?
f: Tirana is the capital.

q: What is the capital of Antigua and Barbuda?
f: Saint John's is the capital.

q: Asturias is a region of which country, and what is its capital city?
f: Oviedo, Spain is the capital.

q: What is the capital of Colombia?
f: Bogota is the capital.

q: What is the capital of Kyrgyzstan?
f: Bishkek is the capital.

q: Manama is the capital of which country?
f: Bahrain is the capital.

q: What is the capital of Syria?
f: Damascus is the capital.

q: What is the capital of Yemen?
f: Sanaa is the capital.

q: The Centaurus Mall is located in which city?
f: The Centaurus is a shopping mall and tower complex in Sector F-8 of Islamabad, on Jinnah Avenue.

q: What is the term of the Chairman of the Senate of Pakistan?
f: The Chairman of the Senate is elected by the Senate members for a term of three years.

q: Surprise Day is observed in Pakistan on which date, marking the 2019 downing of Indian aircraft?
f: On 27 February 2019 the Pakistan Air Force shot down two Indian aircraft after an Indian incursion, and the day is remembered as Surprise Day.

q: Which city is regarded as the spiritual centre of Islam?
f: Makkah in Saudi Arabia is home to the Kaaba, the direction of prayer for all Muslims.

q: Which is the odd one out: panda, chimpanzee, bamboo?
f: Panda and chimpanzee are animals, while bamboo is a plant.

q: Who led the Civil Disobedience Movement of 1930 in India?
f: Mahatma Gandhi started the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930 with the Salt March.

q: Into how many main periods is the Indus Valley Civilization commonly divided?
f: It is commonly divided into three periods: Early Harappan, Mature Harappan and Late Harappan.

q: By what name are the people of the Harappa civilization known?
f: The people who lived in Harappa and other cities of this civilization are called Harappans.

q: Where was the Harappa civilization mainly located?
f: The Harappa civilization, also called the Indus Valley Civilization, grew along the Indus River and its tributaries in Pakistan and north-west India.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word spirited?
f: Spirited means full of energy, courage and enthusiasm, which is closest to lively.

q: Which elements make up gypsum (hydrated calcium sulphate, CaSO4.2H2O)?
f: Gypsum has the formula CaSO4.2H2O, so it contains calcium, sulphur, oxygen and hydrogen.

q: What is the value of 5C0 (5 combination 0)?
f: nC0 = n! / (0! x n!) = 1, because there is exactly one way to choose nothing.

q: Which term comes next in the series: A3, D5, G7, ?
f: The letters move 3 steps forward (A, D, G, J) and the numbers increase by 2 (3, 5, 7, 9), so the next term is J9.

q: Which letter comes after f in the English alphabet?
f: The alphabet runs a, b, c, d, e, f, g, so g comes right after f.

q: Which letter comes after L in the English alphabet?
f: The alphabet runs J, K, L, M, so M comes right after L.

q: In which city is the Command and Staff College of the Pakistan Army located?
f: The Command and Staff College of the Pakistan Army is in Quetta, Balochistan.

q: The Statute of Westminster, which formally established the Commonwealth as a group of self-governing members, was passed in which year?
f: The Statute of Westminster was passed on 11 December 1931 and gave the British dominions legislative independence.

q: What percentage of the total area of Pakistan does Balochistan cover, as given in most textbooks?
f: Balochistan has about 347,190 sq km out of Pakistan's 796,096 sq km, which is about 44%.

q: What is the antonym of the word compassionate?
f: Compassionate means showing pity and care for others, so its opposite is cruel or ruthless.

q: What is the synonym of the word compassionate?
f: Compassionate means feeling concern for the suffering of others, which is the same as sympathetic.

q: Choose the correct word: I have to go ___ school.
f: The verb go takes the preposition to when it shows movement towards a place.

q: Complete the sentence: If I knew the answers, I ___ you.
f: This is a second conditional sentence. It uses the past simple in the if part and would plus a verb in the main part.

q: Complete the series: b, 3, d, 5, f, 7, ?
f: Letters at odd places go b, d, f, skipping one letter each time, so the next is h. The numbers go 3, 5, 7.

q: Complete the series: F, H, K, O, T, ?
f: The jumps are +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next jump is +6. T is the 20th letter and 20 + 6 = 26, which is Z.

q: What is the main role of an operating system in a computer?
o: To manage hardware and software resources
To connect to the internet only
f: The operating system controls the hardware, runs programs and gives users a way to work with the computer.

q: The Red Cross movement was inspired by which battle?
f: Henry Dunant saw the suffering of wounded soldiers at the Battle of Solferino in 1859 and this led to the founding of the Red Cross.

q: How many items are there in one dozen?
f: One dozen is a group of 12 items.

q: What is the value of cot 0 degrees?
f: cot x = cos x divided by sin x. At 0 degrees this is 1 divided by 0, which is undefined.

q: A car covers 30 km in 60 minutes. How far will it cover in 30 minutes at the same speed?
f: Speed is 30 km per hour. In half an hour it covers 30 / 2 = 15 km.

q: A car travels at 60 km per hour. How much distance will it cover in 40 minutes?
f: 40 minutes = 2/3 hour. Distance = 60 x 2/3 = 40 km.

q: A man covers 3 km in 1 hour. How much distance will he cover in 20 minutes at the same speed?
f: 20 minutes = 1/3 hour. Distance = 3 x 1/3 = 1 km.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to the word crude?
f: Crude means rough, raw or unrefined, so coarse is closest in meaning.

q: Which country won the most recent Thomas Cup (men's world team badminton championship) in 2026?
f: China won the 2026 Thomas Cup, beating France in the final in Horsens, Denmark.

q: What is the currency of Nepal?
f: Nepal's national currency is the Nepalese rupee.

q: What is the currency of the United Arab Emirates?
f: The UAE uses the dirham (AED), not the riyal.

q: Who is the current Chief Justice of Pakistan (Supreme Court)?
f: Justice Yahya Afridi became the 30th Chief Justice of Pakistan in October 2024.

q: Who was the youngest daughter of the Holy Prophet (SAW)?
f: Hazrat Fatima (RA) is regarded as the youngest daughter of the Holy Prophet (SAW).

q: What is the Arabic word for 'day'?
f: In Arabic a day is called Youm (Yawm). Layl is night, Shahr is month and Sana is year.

q: Who demanded the separation of Sindh from the Bombay Presidency in his Fourteen Points?
f: Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points in 1929 and one of them demanded that Sindh be separated from Bombay and made a separate province.

q: In which province of Pakistan is Dera Ghazi Khan located?
f: Dera Ghazi Khan is a city and division in southern Punjab, on the west bank of the Indus river.

q: How many degrees is a right angle?
f: A right angle is one quarter of a full turn of 360 degrees, which is 90 degrees.

q: In which year did Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan, the father of Pakistan's nuclear programme, die?
f: Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan died in Islamabad on 10 October 2021 at the age of 85.

q: In which year did Hazrat Khadija (RA), the first wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), die?
f: Hazrat Khadija (RA) died in 619 CE, in the 10th year of prophethood, a few days after the death of Abu Talib.

q: Which word is a synonym of 'difference'?
f: Disparity means a noticeable difference between things.

q: Which two numbers have a sum of 28 and a difference of 4?
Which one is different: 7D, 9G, 4A, 6C?
f: Letter positions are D=4, G=7, A=1, C=3. Number minus letter position gives 3, 2, 3, 3, so 9G breaks the pattern.

q: Which digit is neither positive nor negative?
f: Zero is neither positive nor negative.

q: What is the hundreds digit in the number 970?
f: In 970 the digits from left are hundreds (9), tens (7) and ones (0).

q: What is the antonym of 'disastrous'?
f: Disastrous means very harmful or unlucky, so its opposite is fortunate or successful.

q: Syed Ahmad Shaheed (Barelvi) was a disciple of which scholar?
f: Syed Ahmad Shaheed studied under and was a disciple of Shah Abdul Aziz Dehlvi, son of Shah Waliullah.

q: Who dismissed Prime Minister Khawaja Nazimuddin in 1953?
f: Governor General Ghulam Muhammad dismissed Nazimuddin even though he still had the support of the Assembly.

q: The United Nations resolved the dispute between India and Pakistan over which territory?
f: The UN Security Council passed resolutions in 1948 and 1949 calling for a plebiscite in Jammu and Kashmir.

q: What is the antonym of 'distraction'?
f: Distraction means something that takes attention away, so its opposite is concentration or focus.

q: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I was doing my work honestly."
o: He said that he was doing his work honestly.
He said that he had been doing his work honestly.
He said that I had been doing my work honestly.
He said that he did his work honestly.
f: With a past reporting verb, the past continuous 'was doing' changes to past perfect continuous 'had been doing', and 'I' and 'my' change to 'he' and 'his'.

q: What was the code name of the atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima?
f: The uranium bomb dropped on Hiroshima was called Little Boy.

q: What was the name of the nuclear bomb dropped on Nagasaki?
f: The plutonium bomb dropped on Nagasaki on 9 August 1945 was called Fat Man.

q: On which date was the Durand Line agreement signed?
f: The agreement between Sir Mortimer Durand and Amir Abdur Rahman Khan was signed on 12 November 1893 in Kabul.

q: Who negotiated the Durand Line for British India?
f: Sir Mortimer Durand, the Foreign Secretary of British India, negotiated the line with Amir Abdur Rahman Khan in 1893. The line is named after him.

q: In which year did the Pakistan-India war of 1965 end?
f: The 1965 war began in August and ended with a ceasefire on 23 September 1965, so it ended in the same year.

q: Where is the embassy of the USA in Pakistan located?
f: The US Embassy in Pakistan is in the Diplomatic Enclave of Islamabad, the capital.

q: Which word is the antonym (opposite) of eminent?
f: Eminent means famous and respected. Obscure means unknown, so it is the opposite.

q: What is the plural of editor-in-chief?
f: In a compound noun the main noun takes the plural. Here the main noun is editor, so it becomes editors-in-chief.

q: What is the name of the most recently named element of the periodic table (atomic number 118)?
f: Oganesson has atomic number 118 and is the heaviest and newest named element. It was officially named in 2016.

q: Which part of the Earth receives the most heat from the Sun?
f: Near the equator the Sun's rays fall almost straight down, so the same energy heats a smaller area.

q: Which country has the largest economy in the world by nominal GDP (2026)?
f: IMF data for 2026 puts the United States first with over 31 trillion dollars, and China second.

q: Who is the Minister for Education in the Sindh government (2026)?
f: Syed Sardar Ali Shah is the Sindh Minister for School Education and Literacy in 2026.

q: Where was the Simla (Shimla) Agreement between Pakistan and India signed after the 1971 war?
f: The agreement was signed in Shimla, India, in July 1972 by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi.

q: If a week starts on Friday and ends on Thursday, how many days are in that week?
f: Counting Friday, Saturday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday gives 7 days.

q: In what form do plants store food energy?
f: Plants make glucose in photosynthesis and store the extra as starch.

q: In which year was the Government of India Act, which gave provinces autonomy, passed?
f: The Government of India Act was passed by the British Parliament in 1935 and proposed a federation and provincial autonomy.

q: If a matrix A is symmetric, its transpose is equal to what?
f: A matrix is symmetric when it does not change on transposing, so A transpose equals A.

q: According to Ohm's law, voltage (V) is equal to what?
f: Ohm's law states V = I x R, where I is the current and R is the resistance.

q: What is the equation of the x-axis?
