f: Hirohito was the Emperor of Japan from 1926 to 1989, including the whole period of World War II.

q: Which country was the top source of workers' remittances to Pakistan in 2024 and also in FY2026?
f: State Bank of Pakistan data show Saudi Arabia as the largest source, with about 9.78 billion US dollars in FY2026, ahead of the UAE at about 8.81 billion.

q: Who won the men's Ballon d'Or in 2023?
f: Lionel Messi won the 2023 Ballon d'Or, his eighth, after Argentina won the 2022 World Cup.

q: Is the area of a figure always positive or negative?
f: Area measures the size of a surface, so it is always a positive quantity.

q: Monkey, ape and chimpanzee all belong to which group of animals?
f: Monkeys, apes and chimpanzees are all members of the order Primates.

q: Which is the biggest country in the world by population?
f: India overtook China as the most populous country in 2023, with more than 1.4 billion people.

q: Fill in the blank with a preposition: He is kind ___ slaves.
f: The adjective kind takes the preposition to, so the correct phrase is kind to.

q: Fill in the blank: They said that Adil ___ ill.
f: The reporting verb said is in the past tense, so the reported clause also moves to the past: was.

q: In which year did Pakistan conduct its nuclear tests at Chagai?
f: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests in the Chagai Hills on 28 May 1998, after India tested in May 1998.

q: Who wrote the book The Republic?
f: The Republic is a famous philosophical work written by the Greek philosopher Plato.

q: What are the capital and currency of Mexico?
f: The capital of Mexico is Mexico City and its currency is the Mexican peso (MXN).

q: Who was the captain of the Pakistan ODI cricket team at the 2023 World Cup?
f: Babar Azam captained Pakistan in ODIs at the 2023 ODI World Cup in India, and resigned as captain after it.

q: The speed of a train is twice the speed of a car, and the car covers 60 km in 30 minutes. How many km does the train cover in 30 minutes?
f: Car speed = 60 km in half an hour = 120 km/h. Train speed = 2 x 120 = 240 km/h, so in 30 minutes it covers 120 km.

q: A car runs at 90 km/h and the train runs at double the car speed. How much distance does the train cover in 30 minutes?
f: Train speed = 2 x 90 = 180 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it covers 180 / 2 = 90 km.

q: Change into passive voice: Parents send their children to school.
o: Children were sent to school by their parents.
Children are sent to school by their parents.
Children is sent to school by parents.
Children have been sent to school by their parents.
f: The sentence is in the simple present tense, so the passive uses are plus the past participle: are sent.

q: Change into passive voice: They constructed a wall.
o: A wall is constructed by them.
A wall has been constructed by them.
A wall was constructed by them.
A wall were constructed by them.
f: The sentence is in the simple past tense, so the passive uses was plus the past participle: was constructed.

q: Change into passive voice: We boil the milk.
o: The milk was boiled by us.
The milk is boiled by us.
The milk is being boiled by us.
f: The sentence is in the simple present tense, so the passive is: The milk is boiled by us.

q: Which ray is negatively charged?
f: Beta rays are streams of electrons, so they carry a negative charge.

q: Hen is to chicken as cow is to what?
f: A chicken is the young one of a hen, and a calf is the young one of a cow.

q: What is the name of the border between India and China?
f: The effective border between India and China is called the Line of Actual Control (LAC).

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Ali runs more faster than Akram.
Ali runs most faster than Akram.
f: Faster is already a comparative, so more must not be added before it.

q: What is the correct indirect speech of: He said, "We won the match."?
o: He said that they won the match.
He said that they had won the match.
He said that we had won the match.
He said that they have won the match.
f: We changes to they, and the simple past won changes to the past perfect had won.

q: What is the least count of a standard screw gauge?
f: A standard screw gauge has a pitch of 1 mm and 100 circular divisions, so least count = 1 / 100 = 0.01 mm.

q: Which country won the Cricket World Cup in 1992?
f: Pakistan beat England in the final at Melbourne on 25 March 1992 under Imran Khan.

q: How many days are there in a week?
f: A week has seven days, Monday to Sunday.

q: What is a poem written on the death of a beloved person or friend called?
f: A poem of mourning written for someone who has died is called an elegy.

q: What is the definition of a radian?
o: The angle at the centre of a circle made by an arc equal in length to the radius
The angle made by an arc equal to the diameter
The angle of a full circle
f: One radian is the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc whose length equals the radius.

q: Torque depends on which two quantities?
o: Force and distance from the axis
f: Torque is force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation.

q: Which one is different from the rest: Mango, Carrot, Apple, Banana?
f: Mango, apple and banana are fruits, while carrot is a vegetable.

q: Who discovered hydrogen?
f: Henry Cavendish identified hydrogen as a distinct substance in 1766.

q: What is the unit of acceleration due to gravity?
f: Acceleration is change in velocity per unit time, so its unit is metre per second squared.

q: What is the biggest source of fresh water on Earth?
f: About two thirds of the world's fresh water is locked in glaciers and ice caps.

q: On which sector does the economy of Pakistan mainly depend?
f: Agriculture is the largest employer and the backbone of Pakistan's economy, with cotton, wheat and rice as major crops.

q: What is the degree (highest power) of a quadratic equation?
f: A quadratic equation has the form ax squared plus bx plus c equals 0, so its highest power is 2.

q: Which country issued the world's first adhesive postage stamp, the Penny Black, in 1840?
f: The Penny Black was issued in Great Britain in May 1840.

q: In which year was the Palestinian group Hamas founded?
f: Hamas was founded in 1987 during the first Palestinian intifada.

q: In which year was the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) founded?
f: The PLO was founded in 1964 at a meeting of the Arab League in Jerusalem.

q: Where was the G20 summit of 2023 held, and where was the one of 2025 held?
o: Rio de Janeiro, then New Delhi
f: The 2023 summit was in New Delhi, India, and the 2025 summit was in Johannesburg, South Africa.

q: Which country hosted the G20 summit in 2024?
f: The 2024 G20 summit was held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

q: In which sport is the word love used for a zero score?
f: In tennis, a score of zero is called love.

q: How many general seats are there in the National Assembly of Pakistan?
f: After the merger of FATA with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the National Assembly has 266 general seats, plus 60 women and 10 minority seats.

q: Who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2023?
f: The 2023 Nobel Peace Prize went to Narges Mohammadi of Iran for her fight against the oppression of women.

q: Who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2023?
f: The 2023 Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded to the Norwegian writer Jon Fosse.

q: Which country hosted the Hajj in 2024?
f: Hajj is performed in Makkah and nearby places in Saudi Arabia, which hosts it every year.

q: What is the highest temperature officially recorded in Pakistan, at Turbat in 2017?
f: Turbat in Balochistan recorded 53.7 C on 28 May 2017, accepted as Pakistan's highest reliable temperature.

q: Which country hosted the COP28 climate summit in 2023?
f: COP28 was held in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, from November to December 2023.

q: Which country brought a genocide case against Israel before the International Court of Justice in December 2023?
f: South Africa filed the case at the ICJ in December 2023, under the Genocide Convention.

q: Which international organization's 1947 partition plan (Resolution 181) paved the way for the creation of Israel?
f: The UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 181 in November 1947, proposing separate Arab and Jewish states.

q: Which of these countries became a full member of BRICS in January 2024?
f: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE joined BRICS as full members on 1 January 2024.

q: What does KPK stand for?
f: KPK is the short form of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, a province of Pakistan.

q: What is the approximate area of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
f: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa covers about 101,741 square kilometres.

q: Which is the largest city of Israel by population?
f: Jerusalem has the largest population of any Israeli city, about one million people.

q: What does Newton's second law of motion state?
o: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
A body stays at rest unless a force acts on it
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed
f: Newton's second law says F = ma: the force on a body equals its mass multiplied by its acceleration.

q: Which letter is missing in the sequence A, E, I, __, U?
f: The sequence lists the English vowels in order: A, E, I, O, U.

q: Which is the lightest metal?
f: Lithium has the lowest density of all metals, about 0.53 g per cubic centimetre.

q: What is the value of log 100 to base 10?
f: Since 10 raised to the power 2 equals 100, log 100 = 2.

q: What is the value of log of 60 to the base 4, to two decimal places?
f: log4(60) = ln 60 divided by ln 4 = 4.0943 divided by 1.3863, which is about 2.95. It lies between 2 (log4 16) and 3 (log4 64).

q: About how long does sunlight take to reach the Earth?
f: The Sun is about 150 million km away and light travels at about 300,000 km per second. This gives about 500 seconds, or 8 minutes 20 seconds.

q: What is the property of a skew-symmetric matrix A?
o: A transpose equals the inverse of A
f: A matrix is skew-symmetric when its transpose is the negative of itself, A^T = -A. Because of this all its diagonal elements are zero.

q: What does the word 'optimistic' mean?
f: An optimistic person has a positive outlook and expects good outcomes.

q: If Ali's sister is your mother, then what is Ali to you?
f: Your mother's brother is your maternal uncle (mama). Ali is the brother of your mother, so he is your maternal uncle.

q: In which country does the Kanchenjunga mountain lie?
o: On the border of India and Nepal
f: Kanchenjunga lies on the border between Nepal and Sikkim (India) in the Himalayas.

q: Who painted 'The Starry Night'?
f: Vincent van Gogh painted The Starry Night in 1889.

q: Which is the largest country in North America by area?
f: Canada is about 9.98 million square km, slightly larger than the United States, and the largest country in North America.

q: Why has Pakistan not recognised Israel?
o: It supports Palestinian rights and wants a Palestinian state first
Because Israel is too far away
Because of a border war with Israel
f: Pakistan says it will not recognise Israel until a fair solution gives Palestinians an independent state based on the 1967 borders with Al-Quds as capital.

q: Is zero included in the natural numbers? Choose the textbook answer.
f: Natural numbers are counting numbers 1, 2, 3 and so on. Adding zero gives the whole numbers.

q: What is the difference between rational and irrational numbers?
o: A rational number can be written as p over q, an irrational number cannot
A rational number has no decimals
An irrational number is always negative
Rational numbers are always whole numbers
f: Rational numbers can be written as a fraction p over q with q not zero. Irrational numbers like root 2 and pi cannot, and their decimals never end or repeat.

q: Ali is six years older than his sister. When Ali's sister is 12 years old, how old is Ali?
f: Ali's age is the sister's age plus 6, so 12 + 6 = 18 years.

q: How many medals did Pakistan win at the 2024 Paris Olympics?
f: Pakistan won one medal, the gold medal of Arshad Nadeem in javelin throw.

q: Out of 1500 students, 1340 are male. What is the percentage of females?
What was the name of Pakistan's military operation against India in May 2025, in reply to India's Operation Sindoor?
f: Pakistan named its response Operation Bunyan-um-Marsoos, meaning a wall of lead.

q: The Simla Agreement of 1972 between Pakistan and India took place after which war?
f: The Simla Agreement was signed after the 1971 war that led to the creation of Bangladesh.

q: Who is generally called the pioneer of Artificial Intelligence, having coined the term in 1956?
f: John McCarthy coined the term Artificial Intelligence at the 1956 Dartmouth conference.

q: Where is the deepest point of the Pacific Ocean?
f: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is about 10,900 m deep, the deepest known point of the oceans.

q: What is the present status of Palestine at the United Nations?
f: Since 2012 Palestine has been a non-member observer state at the UN. Full membership is blocked in the Security Council by a US veto.

q: Which Palestinian organisation is resisting Israel and controls the Gaza Strip?
f: Hamas is a Palestinian group that has governed the Gaza Strip since 2007.

q: Which country gives the most military aid to Israel?
f: The United States is the largest provider of military aid to Israel, about 3.8 billion dollars each year under a 2016 agreement.

q: Which border did Pakistan support for a Palestinian state at the UN?
o: The 1967 borders with Al-Quds as capital
f: Pakistan supports a two-state solution with an independent Palestine on pre-1967 borders and Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital.

q: What did Pakistan demand at the UN for Palestine and Gaza?
f: Pakistan has repeatedly demanded an immediate and lasting ceasefire in Gaza and humanitarian aid.

q: Which letter and number come next in the series: B3, D5, F7, ?
f: Letters move by two (B, D, F, H, J) and numbers go up by two (3, 5, 7, 9, 11). So the next term is H9, followed by J11.

q: Z=3, X=5, V=7, T=9. What comes next?
f: Letters go back by two (Z, X, V, T, R) and numbers go up by two (3, 5, 7, 9, 11). So next is R=11.

q: Who is the President of the State of Palestine (Palestinian Authority) as of October 2026?
f: Mahmoud Abbas has been President of the Palestinian Authority since 2005 and was re-elected Fatah leader in May 2026. Presidential elections have been announced for 2027 but may be delayed.

q: What is the system called in which one person holds absolute power over a country?
f: In an autocracy, one person has unlimited power and is not bound by elections or a legislature. A monarchy can be an autocracy only if the monarch rules absolutely.

q: If 15 pencils cost Rs 175, what is the price of 12 pencils?
f: Price of 12 pencils = 175 x 12 / 15 = 2100 / 15 = Rs 140.

q: A man buys a pen for Rs 30 and sells it at a 40 percent profit. What is the selling price?
f: Profit = 40 percent of 30 = 12 rupees. Selling price = 30 + 12 = Rs 42.

q: Which two regions does the Khunjerab Pass connect?
f: The Khunjerab Pass lies on the Karakoram Highway and links Gilgit-Baltistan in Pakistan with Xinjiang in China.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the Warsak Dam situated?
f: Warsak Dam is built on the Kabul River near Peshawar, which is in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: How many vowel letters are in the series: A b d A U C M A u E?
f: The vowels are A, A, U, A, u and E, which makes 6.

q: Who was the first woman Governor of Sindh?
f: Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan became Governor of Sindh in 1973, the first woman to hold the post in Pakistan.

q: Solve for x: 4x + 5 = 6.
On which date did the current Gaza war begin?
f: The war began on 7 October 2023 after Hamas attacked southern Israel and Israel launched a military campaign in Gaza.

q: What are the capital and currency of the United States?
f: The capital of the United States is Washington D.C. and its currency is the US Dollar (USD).

q: What are the capital and currency of the United Kingdom?
f: The capital of the United Kingdom is London and its currency is the Pound Sterling (GBP).

q: What is the Sun?
f: The Sun is a star, a huge glowing ball of hot gas that produces energy by nuclear fusion.

q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 12 years old?
f: The sister is 12 when Ali is 4, so she is 8 years older. When Ali is 12 she will be 12 + 8 = 20.

q: Which billionaire bought Twitter, which was later renamed X?
f: Elon Musk bought Twitter in October 2022 for about 44 billion US dollars and renamed it X in 2023.

q: What is the SI unit of the modulus of elasticity (Young's modulus)?
f: Young's modulus is stress divided by strain. Strain has no unit, so the unit is that of stress, N/m squared, called the pascal.

q: Which isotope is used to treat goiter and thyroid disorders?
f: The thyroid gland absorbs iodine, so radioactive iodine-131 is used to shrink an overactive thyroid or goiter.

q: A man walks 20 km in 40 minutes. How long does he take to walk 1 km?
f: Time per km = 40 / 20 = 2 minutes.

q: Whom did the British blame most for the War of 1857?
f: After 1857 the British held the Muslims mainly responsible, as the last Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar had led the revolt.

q: If 5 men complete a piece of work in 11 days, how many days will 1 man take to do it?
f: Total work = 5 x 11 = 55 man-days. One man needs 55 days.

q: Who wrote the science fiction novel Dune?
f: Dune was written by the American author Frank Herbert and published in 1965.

q: The 2023 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences was awarded to Claudia Goldin for her work on what?
f: Claudia Goldin was honoured for improving our understanding of women's earnings and labour market participation over the centuries.

q: Which country won the FIFA Women's World Cup in 2023?
f: Spain beat England 1-0 in the 2023 final held in Sydney, Australia.

q: Rearrange the letters BUYAET to form a word. What is the last letter of the word?
f: The letters BUYAET form the word BEAUTY, which ends with the letter Y.

q: For what work was the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine awarded?
o: Nucleoside base modifications that enabled mRNA vaccines against COVID-19
f: Katalin Kariko and Drew Weissman won it for discoveries about nucleoside base modifications that made effective mRNA vaccines against COVID-19 possible.

q: A rectangle has a width of 8 and a length of 4. What is its area?
f: Area of a rectangle = length x width = 4 x 8 = 32.

q: Into which river does the Ravi River fall?
f: The Ravi joins the Chenab near Ahmad Pur Sial in Punjab, Pakistan.

q: Boat is to water as aeroplane is to what?
f: A boat moves through water, and an aeroplane moves through air, the medium it travels in.

q: In which year did the Chauri Chaura incident take place in India?
f: The Chauri Chaura incident took place on 4 February 1922 in Gorakhpur district. A mob burned a police station, after which Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement.

q: If AX = B, where A is an invertible matrix, what is X?
f: Multiply both sides on the left by the inverse of A. This gives (A inverse)(A)X = (A inverse)B, so X = A inverse times B.

q: What is the value of (x^2 times x^2) divided by x^2?
f: x^2 times x^2 = x^4 by adding powers. Then x^4 divided by x^2 = x^2 by subtracting powers.

q: What is the value of 2 square root 8 plus 3 square root 8?
f: Both terms have the same radical, so add the coefficients: 2 + 3 = 5. The result is 5 square root 8, which equals 10 square root 2.

q: What is 70% of 70?
The Constitution of 1956 was adopted by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan on which date?
f: The Constituent Assembly adopted the first Constitution on 29 February 1956 (1956 was a leap year).

q: Which Prime Minister played the leading role in framing the Constitution of 1956?
f: Chaudhry Muhammad Ali was Prime Minister when the Constituent Assembly passed the 1956 Constitution.

q: On which date did the Constitution of 1956 come into force?
f: The 1956 Constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956 and Pakistan became an Islamic Republic.

q: The Constitution of 1956 was framed by the Constituent Assembly in the name of whom?
f: The Constitution was adopted in the name of the people of Pakistan, as the preamble says.

q: The Constitution of 1956 received its assent from which office holder?
f: The Governor General (Iskander Mirza) gave assent to the Constitution passed by the Constituent Assembly. He became the first President on 23 March 1956.

q: What name did the Constitution of 1956 give to the country?
f: The 1956 Constitution declared Pakistan an Islamic Republic, the first in the world.

q: Which part of the Constitution of 1956 dealt with Fundamental Rights?
f: Fundamental Rights were placed in Part II of the 1956 Constitution.

q: Which form of government was provided by the Constitution of 1956?
f: The 1956 Constitution set up a parliamentary system with a Prime Minister and cabinet responsible to the National Assembly.

q: According to the Constitution of 1956, who was the Head of State?
f: The President replaced the Governor General as constitutional Head of State.

q: What was the minimum age to become President under the Constitution of 1956?
f: The 1956 Constitution required the President to be at least 40 years old and a Muslim.

q: What type of legislature did the Constitution of 1956 provide?
f: It provided a single-house National Assembly of 300 members, equally divided between East and West Pakistan.

q: Which was the highest court of the country under the Constitution of 1956?
f: The 1956 Constitution created the Supreme Court of Pakistan, replacing the Federal Court that existed since 1948. The source marked Federal Court, which is wrong.

q: Which languages were made national languages by the Constitution of 1956?
f: Urdu and Bengali were declared the state languages in the 1956 Constitution, with English used officially for 20 years.

q: Which type of federal structure did the Constitution of 1956 provide?
f: It provided a federation of two wings, East and West Pakistan, with federal, provincial and concurrent lists.

q: How many Articles and Parts did the Constitution of 1956 contain?
f: The 1956 Constitution had 234 Articles, 13 Parts and 6 Schedules.

q: For about how long did the Constitution of 1956 remain in force?
f: It was enforced on 23 March 1956 and abrogated on 7 October 1958, about two and a half years.

q: On which date was the Constitution of 1956 abrogated?
f: President Iskander Mirza abrogated it on 7 October 1958 and imposed martial law.

q: Which body enacted the Constitution of 1956?
f: The second Constituent Assembly passed it, as the first one had been dissolved in 1954.

q: What was the total strength of the National Assembly under the Constitution of 1956?
f: It had 300 members, 150 from each wing, plus 10 seats reserved for women, so 310. The Constitution also kept parity between the wings.

q: How were members of the National Assembly elected under the Constitution of 1956?
f: The Constitution provided direct elections to the National Assembly, though no general election was held before it was abrogated.

q: What type of citizenship did the Constitution of 1956 provide?
f: Pakistan had a single citizenship for all citizens, as in a federation like India but unlike the USA.

q: Under the Constitution of 1956, how were powers divided in the federation?
f: Powers were shared through a Federal List, a Provincial List and a Concurrent List.

q: Under the Constitution of 1956, to whom was the Cabinet collectively responsible?
f: In the parliamentary system the Cabinet led by the Prime Minister was answerable to the National Assembly.

q: On which date was the Constitution of 1962 enforced?
f: President Ayub Khan promulgated it on 1 March 1962 and it came into force on 8 June 1962. Note the source gave 28 February, which is not the correct date.

q: In how many Parts was the Constitution of 1962 divided (it had 250 Articles)?
f: The 1962 Constitution had 250 Articles, 12 Parts and 3 Schedules.

q: Which form of government did the Constitution of 1962 provide?
f: It created a strong presidential system with the President as Chief Executive.

q: How was the President elected under the Constitution of 1962?
f: The President was elected indirectly by an electoral college of Basic Democrats.

q: The electoral college under the Constitution of 1962 was originally formed of how many Basic Democrats?
f: Originally 80,000 Basic Democrats (40,000 per wing) formed the electoral college.

q: What was the voting age under the Constitution of 1962?
f: The 1962 Constitution set the minimum voting age at 21 years.

q: What was the minimum age for a person to be elected President under the Constitution of 1962?
f: The 1962 Constitution required the President to be at least 35 years of age and a Muslim.

q: Under the Constitution of 1962, who had the power to dissolve the National Assembly?
f: The President held the power to dissolve the Assembly, one of his wide powers. The source asked the Article number, which could not be verified.

q: Under the Constitution of 1962, who could be impeached by the National Assembly?
f: The Constitution provided a process for impeaching the President, though it was very difficult to use.

q: The Constitution of 1962 provided a federation of the centre and how many provinces?
f: The federation consisted of two provinces, East Pakistan and West Pakistan.

q: What was the original name of the country under the Constitution of 1962?
f: The 1962 Constitution dropped the word Islamic and called the country the Republic of Pakistan.

q: In which month of 1963 did the National Assembly pass the amendment restoring the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan?
f: The first Amendment Act was passed in December 1963 and restored the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

q: Who was the Chief Executive of the country under the Constitution of 1962?
f: The President was both head of state and chief executive.

q: What was the term of office of the President under the Constitution of 1962?
f: The President held office for five years.

q: Which was the highest court of the country under the Constitution of 1962?
f: The Supreme Court remained the apex court of the country.

q: What type of legislature did the Constitution of 1962 provide?
f: It provided a single-house National Assembly.

q: Up to which age could a Supreme Court judge serve under the Constitution of 1962?
f: The 1962 Constitution set retirement of Supreme Court judges at 65 years.

q: Which languages were national languages under the Constitution of 1962?
f: Urdu and Bengali were national languages, while English remained in official use.

q: Which system of local government did Ayub Khan make the base of the Constitution of 1962?
f: The Basic Democracies system of 1959 created union councils whose members formed the electoral college.

q: Which city was named as the capital of Pakistan in the Constitution of 1962?
f: The 1962 Constitution named the newly built city of Islamabad as the capital, with Rawalpindi serving as the interim capital while it was being built.

q: Under which Article of the 1962 Constitution could the President promulgate Ordinances when the National Assembly was not in session?
f: Article 29 of the 1962 Constitution allowed the President to make an Ordinance with the same force as an Act when the Assembly was dissolved or not in session and immediate legislation was needed.

q: Under Article 226 of the 1962 Constitution, who was treated as the first President of Pakistan under that Constitution?
f: Article 226 (transitional provisions) provided that, following the referendum of February 1960, Field Marshal Muhammad Ayub Khan was to be the first President under the 1962 Constitution.

q: Which Order, issued by General Yahya Khan on 30 March 1970, set the framework for the first general elections and for making a new constitution?
f: The Legal Framework Order of 30 March 1970 laid down the basis for the December 1970 elections and required the elected Assembly to frame a constitution within 120 days.

q: In which month and year was the Constitution of 1962 abrogated?
f: General Yahya Khan imposed martial law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution on 25 March 1969.

q: For approximately how many years did the Constitution of 1962 remain in force?
f: It was in force from 8 June 1962 until 25 March 1969, which is about seven years (nearly six years and nine months).

q: Which system of government was introduced by the Constitution of 1962?
f: The 1962 Constitution concentrated executive power in the President, who was both head of state and head of government, so critics called it a one-man show.

q: Who abrogated the Constitution of 1962?
f: General Agha Muhammad Yahya Khan took over from Ayub Khan and abrogated the 1962 Constitution on 25 March 1969.

q: On which date was the Constitution of 1973 authenticated by the President of Pakistan?
f: The National Assembly passed the Constitution on 10 April 1973 and President Fazal Elahi Chaudhry authenticated it on 12 April 1973.

q: On which date did the Constitution of 1973 come into force?
f: The Constitution was enforced on 14 August 1973, the Independence Day, after being authenticated on 12 April 1973.

q: How many Articles does the Constitution of 1973 contain?
f: The Constitution of 1973 has 280 Articles divided into 12 Parts.

q: According to the Objectives Resolution, sovereignty over the entire Universe belongs to whom?
f: The Objectives Resolution states that sovereignty over the entire Universe belongs to Almighty Allah alone.

q: According to the Objectives Resolution, the authority exercised by the people of Pakistan within limits set by Allah is a what?
f: The Resolution says the authority to be exercised by the people within the limits prescribed by Allah is a sacred trust.

q: According to the Objectives Resolution, through whom shall the State exercise its powers and authority?
o: The chosen representatives of the people
f: The Objectives Resolution says the State shall exercise its powers and authority through the chosen representatives of the people.

q: According to the Objectives Resolution, how shall Muslims be enabled to order their lives?
o: In accordance with the teachings and requirements of Islam
f: The Resolution says Muslims shall be enabled to order their lives in the individual and collective spheres in accordance with the teachings and requirements of Islam as set out in the Quran and Sunnah.

q: According to the Objectives Resolution, what freedom shall be given to minorities?
o: To profess and practise their religions and develop their cultures freely
To follow only the teachings of Islam
To live as decided by government policy
f: The Resolution says adequate provision shall be made for minorities freely to profess and practise their religions and develop their cultures.

q: According to the Objectives Resolution, the independence of the judiciary shall be what?
f: The Resolution states that the independence of the judiciary shall be fully secured.

q: According to the Objectives Resolution, Pakistan will make its full contribution towards what?
o: International peace and progress and the happiness of humanity
f: The Resolution says the people of Pakistan should attain their rightful place among nations and make their full contribution towards international peace and progress and the happiness of humanity.

q: In what form was the Objectives Resolution placed in the Constitution of 1973 as originally enacted?
f: In the original 1973 Constitution the Objectives Resolution was the Preamble. It became a substantive part later through Article 2A.

q: What name does Article 1 of the Constitution of 1973 give to Pakistan?
f: Article 1(1) says Pakistan shall be a Federal Republic to be known as the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

q: After the 25th Amendment of 2018, what do the territories of Pakistan under Article 1 comprise?
o: Four provinces, FATA and the Federal Capital
The provinces of Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab and Sindh, and the Islamabad Capital Territory (plus such other territories as may be included)
Four provinces, Azad Kashmir and Islamabad only
f: The 25th Amendment (2018) merged FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and removed it from Article 1, so Article 1(2) now lists four provinces and the Islamabad Capital Territory. The older answer with FATA is outdated.

q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is Islam declared the State religion of Pakistan?
f: Article 2 states that Islam shall be the State religion of Pakistan.

q: Which Article of the 1973 Constitution makes the Objectives Resolution a substantive part of the Constitution?
f: Article 2A states that the principles and provisions of the Objectives Resolution (Annex) are made substantive part of the Constitution and have effect accordingly.

q: Under Article 5(1) of the Constitution of 1973, loyalty to whom is the basic duty of every citizen?
f: Article 5(1) says loyalty to the State is the basic duty of every citizen.

q: Article 5(2) of the Constitution of 1973 describes obedience to the Constitution and law as the what of every citizen?
f: Article 5(2) says obedience to the Constitution and law is the inviolable obligation of every citizen wherever he may be and of every other person within Pakistan.

q: A person who abrogates, subverts, suspends or holds in abeyance the Constitution by force or unconstitutional means is guilty of what under Article 6?
f: Article 6(1) says any person who abrogates or subverts the Constitution by use of force or show of force or other unconstitutional means is guilty of high treason.

q: Under Article 6(3) of the Constitution, who is empowered to provide the punishment for persons found guilty of high treason?
f: Article 6(3) says the Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) shall by law provide for the punishment of persons found guilty of high treason.

q: In which Article of the 1973 Constitution is the State defined for the purposes of Fundamental Rights?
f: Article 7 defines the State as the Federal Government, Parliament, a Provincial Government, a Provincial Assembly and local authorities.

q: Which Articles of the 1973 Constitution contain the Principles of Policy?
f: Chapter 2 of Part II, Articles 29 to 40, sets out the Principles of Policy.

q: Under Article 8 of the 1973 Constitution, a law that is inconsistent with the Fundamental Rights is what?
o: Void to the extent of the inconsistency
f: Article 8 says any law inconsistent with or in derogation of the Fundamental Rights shall, to the extent of such inconsistency, be void.

q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is no person to be deprived of life or liberty save in accordance with law?
f: Article 9 (security of person) says no person shall be deprived of life or liberty save in accordance with law.

q: Which Articles of the 1973 Constitution deal with the Fundamental Rights?
f: Chapter 1 of Part II, Articles 8 to 28, contains the Fundamental Rights.

q: What is Chapter 1 of Part II of the 1973 Constitution (Articles 8 to 28) called?
f: Chapter 1 of Part II is titled Fundamental Rights, the rights guaranteed by the Constitution and enforceable in court.

q: Safeguards as to arrest and detention are provided in which Article of the 1973 Constitution?
f: Article 10 gives safeguards on arrest and detention, including the right to be told the grounds and to appear before a magistrate within 24 hours.

q: Article 10A of the 1973 Constitution deals with which right?
o: Right to fair trial and due process
f: Article 10A guarantees the right to fair trial and due process in the determination of civil rights and criminal charges.

q: Through which amendment was the right to fair trial (Article 10A) added to the Fundamental Rights?
f: Article 10A was inserted by the 18th Amendment of 2010.

q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution are slavery and forced labour prohibited?
f: Article 11 prohibits slavery, forced labour and the employment of children below fourteen in factories, mines or hazardous work.

q: Article 12 of the 1973 Constitution gives protection against what?
f: Article 12 gives protection against retrospective punishment, meaning no one can be punished for an act that was not an offence when it was done.

q: Article 13 of the 1973 Constitution gives protection against what?
f: Article 13 says no person shall be punished more than once for the same offence nor be compelled to be a witness against himself.

q: Under which provision of the 1973 Constitution is no person to be subjected to torture for extracting evidence?
f: Article 14(2) says no person shall be subjected to torture for the purpose of extracting evidence.

q: Which freedom is guaranteed by Article 15 of the 1973 Constitution?
f: Article 15 guarantees every citizen the right to remain in, enter and move freely throughout Pakistan and settle in any part of it, subject to law.

q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is freedom of assembly guaranteed?
f: Article 16 gives every citizen the right to assemble peacefully and without arms, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the interest of public order.

q: Which freedom is provided in Article 17 of the 1973 Constitution?
f: Article 17 gives every citizen the right to form associations or unions and to form or be a member of a political party, subject to restrictions in the interest of sovereignty and integrity of Pakistan.

q: Which freedom is guaranteed by Article 18 of the 1973 Constitution?
o: Freedom of trade, business or profession
f: Article 18 gives every citizen the right to enter upon any lawful profession or occupation and to conduct any lawful trade or business.

q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution does every citizen have the right of access to information in matters of public importance?
f: Article 19A, inserted by the 18th Amendment in 2010, gives every citizen the right of access to information in all matters of public importance, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law.

q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is there safeguard against taxation for the purposes of any particular religion?
f: Article 21 says no person shall be compelled to pay any special tax the proceeds of which are to be spent on the propagation or maintenance of any religion other than his own.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 19th day be?
f: The gap is 19 - 4 = 15 days; 15 divided by 7 leaves 1, so Friday + 1 = Saturday.

q: What is one third of 10% of 90?
f: 10% of 90 = 9, and one third of 9 = 3.

q: How many months of a year have 31 days?
f: January, March, May, July, August, October and December have 31 days, so there are seven.

q: What is the value of 2 + 2/2?
f: Division comes first: 2/2 = 1, then 2 + 1 = 3.

q: What is a quarter of one tenth of 120?
f: One tenth of 120 = 12, and a quarter of 12 = 3.

q: There are 30 passengers in a bus and 2/3 of them are men. What is the percentage of women?
Ali bought a pen for Rs 30 and sold it for Rs 40. What is the profit percentage?
Which one is different from the others: Monkey, Ape, Chimpanzee, Panda, Baboon?
f: Monkey, ape, chimpanzee and baboon are primates; the panda is a bear.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 26th day be?
f: The gap is 26 - 4 = 22 days; 22 divided by 7 leaves 1, so Tuesday + 1 = Wednesday.

q: There are 30 passengers in a bus and 2/3 of them are men. How many women are there?
A man walked towards the north, then turned left. After some time he turned right. What is his present direction?
f: North, then left gives West, then right from West gives North.

q: Complete the series: 66, 63, 57, 45, ?
f: The differences are 3, 6, 12 (doubling), so the next difference is 24 and 45 - 24 = 21.

q: Complete the series: 2, 6, 14, 30, 62, ?
f: Each term is double the previous plus 2: 62 x 2 + 2 = 126.

q: Complete the series: B, E, J, Q, ?
f: Letter positions are 2, 5, 10, 17 with gaps 3, 5, 7, so the next gap is 9 and 17 + 9 = 26 = Z.

q: Complete the series: A, C, F, J, O, ?
f: Positions are 1, 3, 6, 10, 15 (gaps 2, 3, 4, 5), so the next gap is 6 and 15 + 6 = 21 = U.

q: Complete the series: L, M, N, ?
f: The letters are consecutive in the alphabet, so after N comes O.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 19th day be?
f: The gap is 15 days; 15 divided by 7 leaves 1, so Sunday + 1 = Monday.

q: If the 14th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 4th day be?
f: The gap is 10 days backwards; 10 divided by 7 leaves 3, so Sunday - 3 = Thursday.

q: Why do we boil milk?
f: Boiling kills harmful germs (bacteria), making the milk safe to drink.

q: A train's speed is twice that of a car. If the car covers 60 km in one hour, how much distance will the train cover in 30 minutes?
f: Train speed = 2 x 60 = 120 km/h; in 30 minutes (half an hour) it covers 60 km.

q: What is the sound made by an eagle called?
f: The call of an eagle is described as a scream.

q: What is half of 9/90?
f: 9/90 = 0.1, and half of 0.1 = 0.05 = 1/20 (so the source statement of 1/5 or 0.2 is wrong).

q: In a class of 1500 students, 1200 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
My brother's sister is your mother. Taking me as a male, what am I to you?
f: My brother's sister is my own sister, and she is your mother, so I am your mother's brother, that is, your maternal uncle.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 12th day be?
f: The gap is 11 days; 11 divided by 7 leaves 4, so Monday + 4 = Friday (the source statement of Saturday is wrong).

q: If 5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes, how long will 1 man take to write 1 page?
f: Each man writes 1 page in 5 minutes (5 men write 5 pages in the same 5 minutes).

q: A train's speed is double that of a car, and the car travels 30 km in 1 hour. How much distance will the train cover in 30 minutes?
f: Train speed = 2 x 30 = 60 km/h; in half an hour it covers 30 km.

q: If a man travels 90 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes, in how many minutes will he cover 1 km?
f: Time is 100 minutes for 90 km, so 1 km takes 100 / 90 = 1.11 minutes (the source value 0.9 is wrong).

q: In a classroom, out of 1500 students 1200 are present. What is the percentage of present students?
If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 12th day be?
f: The gap is 10 days; 10 divided by 7 leaves 3, so Monday + 3 = Thursday (the source statement of Friday is wrong).

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 23rd day be?
f: The gap is 21 days, which is exactly 3 weeks, so the day stays Sunday.

q: What is the value of (2 + 2)?
f: Adding the numbers in the bracket gives 2 + 2 = 4 (the source statement of 8 is wrong).

q: Ali moves towards the north, after some time he turns left, then turns left again. What is his present direction?
f: North, then left gives West, then left again gives South.

q: A train is moving at a speed of 90 km/h. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes?
f: 12 minutes = 1/5 hour; 90 / 5 = 18 km.

q: A man covers 20 km in one hour and 40 minutes. In how many minutes will he cover 1 km?
f: Total time is 100 minutes for 20 km, so 1 km takes 100 / 20 = 5 minutes (the source value 0.2 is wrong).

q: If the 15th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 4th day be?
f: The gap is 11 days backwards; 11 divided by 7 leaves 4, so Monday - 4 = Thursday.

q: In a class of 24 students, 1/4 are male. What is the percentage of females?
A man walks towards the north, then turns left, then turns right. What is his present direction?
f: North, left gives West, then right from West gives North again.

q: Vehicle is to wheels as clock is to what?
f: Wheels are a part of a vehicle, and hands are a part of a clock.

q: After how many years does a leap year normally come?
f: A leap year (366 days) comes every 4 years, for example 2024 and 2028.

q: A train covers 120 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes. How much distance will it cover in 15 minutes (at the same speed)?
f: 1 hour 40 minutes = 100 minutes, so speed = 120/100 = 1.2 km per minute; in 15 minutes: 1.2 x 15 = 18 km. The printed answer 30 km in the source is wrong.

q: If yesterday was Friday, what day will tomorrow be?
f: Yesterday Friday means today is Saturday, so tomorrow is Sunday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 14th day be?
f: The gap is 10 days and 10 mod 7 = 3, so the day moves 3 step(s) ahead of Sunday, which gives Wednesday. The source statement (14th is Monday) is wrong.

q: A car is moving at 120 km/h. How much distance does it cover in 10 minutes?
f: 10 minutes = 1/6 hour, and 120 x 1/6 = 20 km.

q: What is 120 x 7?
If the 28th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 8th day be?
f: The 2nd date is 20 days earlier; 20 mod 7 = 6, so go back 6 day(s) from Monday (same as 1 ahead), which gives Tuesday.

q: Ahmad walks towards the north and then turns left. In which direction is he facing now?
f: Facing north, the left hand side is west.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 23rd day be?
f: The gap is 21 days and 21 mod 7 = 0, so the day moves 0 step(s) ahead of Friday, which gives Friday.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister Sidra is twice his age. How old will Sidra be when Ali is 11 years old?
f: Sidra is 10 now, so she is 5 years older than Ali. When Ali is 11, Sidra is 11 + 5 = 16.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 13th day be?
f: The gap is 12 days and 12 mod 7 = 5, so the day moves 5 step(s) ahead of Monday, which gives Saturday.

q: In a class of 500 students, 340 are boys. What percentage are boys?
If 1 dozen pencils cost Rs 60, what is the cost of 5 pencils?
f: 1 dozen = 12 pencils, so one pencil costs 60/12 = Rs 5; 5 pencils cost Rs 25.

q: After arranging the letters of SIRAP, it becomes the name of a country, city, ocean or state. Which one is it?
f: The letters of SIRAP rearrange to PARIS, the capital city of France. So it is a city.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 18th day be?
f: The gap is 14 days and 14 mod 7 = 0, so the day moves 0 step(s) ahead of Monday, which gives Monday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 14th day be?
f: The gap is 12 days and 12 mod 7 = 5, so the day moves 5 step(s) ahead of Friday, which gives Wednesday.

q: What will be the last letter of UTYEAB after arranging its letters alphabetically?
f: Alphabetical order is A, B, E, T, U, Y, so the last letter is Y.

q: What will be the 3rd letter of the word Managment when its letters are arranged alphabetically?
f: Letters of Managment: A, A, E, G, M, M, N, N, T in alphabetical order, so the 3rd letter is E. The source answer G is wrong (G is 4th). The same answer E applies to the correctly spelled MANAGEMENT.

q: A person purchased a book for Rs 500 and sold it for Rs 700. What is the profit percentage?
If yesterday was Monday, what day will be the day after tomorrow?
f: Yesterday Monday means today is Tuesday; tomorrow is Wednesday and the day after tomorrow is Thursday.

q: If a helicopter needs 50 gallons of fuel to move 320 km, how many gallons will it need to move 400 km?
f: Fuel per km = 50/320; for 400 km: 50 x 400/320 = 62.5 gallons.

q: Amjad and Ahmad kept 24 balls together. Amjad kept 3 times as many as Ahmad. How many balls did Ahmad keep?
f: Let Ahmad have x; Amjad has 3x, so 4x = 24 and x = 6.

q: A boy is 3 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. How old will his sister be when the boy is 11 years old?
f: The sister is 9 now, so she is 6 years older. When the boy is 11, she is 17.

q: What is the sister of my brother's son to me?
f: My brother's son's sister is my brother's daughter, who is my niece.

q: My age is 10 years and my brother is 2 times my age. What will be the ratio of my age to my brother's age after 10 years?
f: Brother is 20 now. After 10 years I am 20 and he is 30, so the ratio is 20:30 = 2:3 (the reverse order gives 3:2).

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 23rd day be?
f: The gap is 20 days and 20 mod 7 = 6, so the day moves 6 step(s) ahead of Friday, which gives Thursday.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will be the age of his sister when Ali is 10 years old?
f: The sister is 15 now, so she is 10 years older than Ali. When Ali is 10, she is 20.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 12th day be?
f: The gap is 8 days and 8 mod 7 = 1, so the day moves 1 step(s) ahead of Tuesday, which gives Wednesday.

q: Saleem has an average of 60 in 4 subjects. His average drops to 58 after the next test. How many marks did he score in that test?
f: Total of 4 = 240. Total of 5 = 58 x 5 = 290. Next test = 290 - 240 = 50. (The source asks to find the grade; the marks are the only value that can be worked out.)

q: 10 men dig a well in 5 days. How many days will 5 men take to dig it?
f: Work = 10 x 5 = 50 man-days; with 5 men: 50/5 = 10 days. The source answer 20 is wrong.

q: Salman is 4 years old and Ali's age is twice Salman's age. What will be Ali's age when Salman is 12 years old?
f: Ali is 8 now, 4 years older than Salman. When Salman is 12, Ali is 16.

q: Akbar is older than Ahmad. Umair is older than Akbar. Who is the eldest?
f: Order from eldest: Umair, Akbar, Ahmad.

q: Adil is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will be the age of his sister when Adil is 15 years old?
f: Sister is 15 now, 10 years older than Adil. When Adil is 15, she is 25.

q: The sister of my brother is your mother. What is your relation to me?
f: My brother's sister is my sister (taking me as male), and she is your mother, so I am your mother's brother and you are my nephew or niece.

q: Adnan walks 10 meters towards the north, then towards the south. After this he turns back and then turns left. In which direction is he facing now?
f: After walking south he faces south; turning back he faces north; turning left from north he faces west.

q: A train covers 20 km in one hour. How much distance does it cover in 1 minute?
f: 20 km / 60 minutes = 1/3 km = 0.333 km. The printed answer 0.3 km is only a rounded value.

q: What is 80% of 10?
What is one-third of 10% of 120?
f: 10% of 120 = 12, and one-third of 12 = 4.

q: What is one-third of 10% of 90?
f: 10% of 90 = 9, and one-third of 9 = 3.

q: What is one-fourth of 120?
f: 120 divided by 4 = 30.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what will be the 24th day of that month?
f: From the 4th to the 24th is 20 days; 20 mod 7 = 6, and Monday plus 6 days = Sunday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what will be the 23rd day of that month?
f: From the 2nd to the 23rd is 21 days = exactly 3 weeks, so the day is again Sunday.

q: A boy is 3 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will be the age of the sister when the boy is 11 years old?
f: Sister is 9 when the boy is 3, so she is 6 years older. When the boy is 11, she is 11 + 6 = 17.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 1200 are present. What is the percentage of present and absent students?
f: 1200/1500 x 100 = 80% present, so absent = 300 students = 20%.

q: Amjad and Ahmad kept 25 balls. Amjad kept 4 times as many as Ahmad. How many balls did Ahmad keep?
f: Let Ahmad have x; then x + 4x = 25, so x = 5 (Amjad has 20).

q: Ali bought a pen for Rs. 30 and sold it for Rs. 40. What is his profit percentage?
If a man travels 90 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes, how much time will he take to cover 1 km?
f: Time is 100 minutes for 90 km, so 1 km takes 100/90 = 10/9 minutes, about 1.11 minutes.

q: If 5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes, in how many minutes will 1 man write 1 page?
f: Each man writes 1 page in 5 minutes (5 men x 5 minutes gives 5 pages, one page per man).

q: There are 30 passengers in a bus and 2/3 of them are men. What is the number of women?
Akbar is older than Ahmad, and Umair is older than Akbar. Who is the oldest?
f: Umair is older than Akbar, who is older than Ahmad, so Umair is the oldest.

q: Akbar is older than Ahmad, and Umair is older than Akbar. Who is the youngest?
f: Umair is older than Akbar, who is older than Ahmad, so Ahmad is the youngest.

q: Ali moves towards the north, after some time he turns left, then again turns left. What is his present direction?
f: Facing north, a left turn gives west, and another left turn gives south.

q: A man walked towards the north, then he turned left. After some time he turned right. What is his present direction?
f: North, left turn gives west, right turn from west gives north again.

q: What will be the 3rd letter of the word MANAGEMENT when its letters are arranged alphabetically?
f: Sorted letters: A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T. The 3rd letter is E.

q: What will be the 3rd letter when the word AUGMENTED is arranged alphabetically?
f: Sorted letters: A, D, E, E, G, M, N, T, U. The 3rd letter is E.

q: The jumbled word UTYEAB is rearranged to form a word. What will be the last letter of that word when its letters are arranged alphabetically?
f: UTYEAB forms BEAUTY. Alphabetical order is A, B, E, T, U, Y, so the last letter is Y.

q: Arrange the jumbled word OPERALD to form a word and identify its category.
f: OPERALD rearranges to LEOPARD, a big wild cat.

q: According to the dictionary order, which word comes first: MOUNTAIN, MARGALLA, MACHINE?
f: All start with M; the second letters A, A, O put Mountain last. Between MACHINE and MARGALLA, C comes before R, so Machine is first.

q: What comes next in the series: B, E, J, Q, ?
f: Letter positions are 2, 5, 10, 17 with gaps 3, 5, 7, so the next gap is 9: 17 + 9 = 26 = Z.

q: Find the odd one out: Wheat, Hay, Rice, Maize.
f: Wheat, rice and maize are food grains for humans, while hay is dried grass used as animal fodder.

q: Find the odd one out: Monkey, Ape, Chimpanzee, Panda.
f: Monkey, ape and chimpanzee are primates; the panda is a bear.

q: If my brother's sister is your mother, who am I to you (taking me as a male)?
f: My brother's sister is also my sister, and she is your mother, so I am your mother's brother, your maternal uncle.

q: The sister of my brother's son is my what?
f: My brother's son is my nephew; his sister is my brother's daughter, i.e. my niece.

q: Vehicle is to wheels as Sound is to ?
f: A vehicle moves by means of wheels, and sound travels by means of waves.

q: Water is to flow as Air is to ?
f: Water flows and air blows.

q: A bat cannot see well and a snake cannot ?
f: The analogy is a sense that the animal lacks; snakes have no outer ears and are largely deaf to airborne sound.

q: What is the value of 3P2 (3 permutation 2)?
What is the area of a rectangle whose width is 3 and height is 8?
f: Area = width x height = 3 x 8 = 24.

q: What is the eccentricity of a parabola?
f: A parabola is the conic section with eccentricity exactly 1.

q: The probability of an event always lies between which values?
f: Probability is 0 for an impossible event and 1 for a certain event; all others lie in between.

q: Which city is known as the heart of Pakistan?
f: Lahore is commonly called the heart of Pakistan (and the cultural capital).

q: What was the earlier capital of Pakistan before Islamabad?
f: Karachi was the first capital from 1947; Rawalpindi was temporary capital and Islamabad became capital in the 1960s.

q: Who is the President of China?
f: Xi Jinping has been President of China since 2013.

q: Who was the leader of Germany in World War 2?
f: Adolf Hitler led Nazi Germany as Fuhrer from 1934 to 1945.

q: What is the most important resource of the Arabian countries?
f: Oil (petroleum) is the main economic resource of the Arab Gulf countries.

q: Which is the smallest continent in the world?
f: Australia (Oceania) is the smallest continent by land area.

q: Which is the 2nd largest continent in the world?
f: Asia is the largest, and Africa is second with about 30.3 million sq km.

q: What is the main source of freshwater in the world?
f: About 68-69% of the world's freshwater is locked in glaciers and ice caps.

q: Which country is the biggest coffee producer in the world?
f: Brazil is the largest coffee producer, supplying roughly a third of the world's coffee.

q: Which is the longest river in the world (by the traditional measurement)?
f: The Nile is traditionally ranked longest at about 6,650 km; the Amazon is the largest by water volume.

q: Which is the fastest bird in the world?
f: The peregrine falcon reaches over 320 km/h in its hunting dive.

q: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations (UNO)?
f: The UN headquarters is in New York City, USA.

q: Where is the headquarters of the Asian Development Bank?
f: The Asian Development Bank is headquartered in Mandaluyong, Metro Manila, Philippines.

q: At the end of 2016, which country was the third-largest refugee-hosting country in the world according to UNHCR?
f: UNHCR Global Trends 2016: Turkey (2.9 million) was first, Pakistan (1.4 million) second and Lebanon (1.0 million) third.

q: Why did America take part in World War 2?
o: Because of the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor
Because of the sinking of the Titanic
Because of the Cuban Missile Crisis
f: The USA entered the war after Japan attacked Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941.

q: The 2015 nuclear agreement between Iran and world powers (including the USA) is known as?
f: The JCPOA was agreed in July 2015 with Iran by the P5+1; the USA withdrew from it in 2018.

q: In which year did India conduct its first nuclear test?
f: India's first test (Smiling Buddha) was on 18 May 1974 at Pokhran.

q: What is the antonym of Wild?
f: Tamed (domesticated) is the opposite of wild.

q: What is a synonym of Gorgeous?
f: Gorgeous means very beautiful or stunning.

q: Who is the author of Shikwa and Jawab-e-Shikwa?
f: Allama Muhammad Iqbal wrote Shikwa (1909) and Jawab-e-Shikwa (1913).

q: Who wrote the book Friends Not Masters?
f: Field Marshal Ayub Khan wrote his autobiography Friends Not Masters in 1967.

q: Who wrote the book Jinnah of Pakistan?
f: Stanley Wolpert, an American historian, wrote Jinnah of Pakistan (1984).

q: What is the national bird of Pakistan?
f: The Chukar partridge is the national bird of Pakistan.

q: Who designed the flag of Pakistan?
f: The national flag of Pakistan was designed by Syed Amir-ud-Din Kidwai, based on the Muslim League flag.

q: In which region of Asia is Pakistan located?
f: Pakistan is a country of South Asia.

q: Which is the largest river of Pakistan?
f: The Indus is the longest and largest river of Pakistan, about 3,180 km long.

q: Which is the largest district of Pakistan by area?
f: Chagai in Balochistan is the largest district of Pakistan, with about 44,748 square km.

q: What is the height of Tirich Mir, the highest peak of the Hindu Kush in Pakistan?
f: Tirich Mir in Chitral is 7708 m high.

q: Which line is the boundary between China and India in the eastern sector?
f: The McMahon Line was drawn in 1914 and marks the China-India border in the eastern sector; China does not accept it.

q: The Wakhan border of Pakistan is shared with which country?
f: The Wakhan strip is part of Afghanistan and touches northern Chitral in Pakistan.

q: How was Attabad Lake in Gilgit-Baltistan formed?
f: A massive landslide in January 2010 blocked the Hunza River and formed the lake.

q: In which province is Mohenjo-Daro located?
f: Mohenjo-Daro is in Larkana district, Sindh.

q: Why do people visit Ziarat in Balochistan?
o: The tomb of Allama Iqbal is there
f: The Quaid-e-Azam Residency, where Jinnah spent his last days, is in Ziarat.

q: Why do parents send children to school?
o: To groom them and give them education
To keep them away from home
f: Parents send children to school for education and character building.

q: PEMRA is the regulatory body for which media?
f: The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority regulates TV and radio.

q: Which city started television broadcasting first in Pakistan?
f: Pakistan Television started in Lahore on 26 November 1964.

q: When did Pakistan join the United Nations?
f: Pakistan became the 56th member of the UN on 30 September 1947.

q: When did Quaid-e-Azam present his 14 Points?
f: Jinnah presented the 14 Points in March 1929 in reply to the Nehru Report.

q: In which year did Allama Iqbal deliver the Allahabad Address?
f: Iqbal gave his presidential address at the Muslim League session in Allahabad in December 1930.

q: When did Muslims get the right of separate electorates?
f: Separate electorates for Muslims were granted by the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.

q: When did Quaid-e-Azam join the All India Muslim League?
f: Jinnah joined the Muslim League in 1913.

q: What was the date of the Lahore Resolution?
f: The Lahore Resolution was passed on 23 March 1940, moved by A. K. Fazlul Haq.

q: What was the official reason given for the Partition of Bengal in 1905?
f: Lord Curzon said Bengal was too big to govern, so it was divided for administrative reasons.

q: Who became the Prime Minister of Pakistan after Liaquat Ali Khan?
f: Khawaja Nazimuddin was Governor-General and then became Prime Minister in 1951 after Liaquat Ali Khan was killed.

q: Who was the third Governor-General of Pakistan?
f: The order was Jinnah, Nazimuddin, then Malik Ghulam Muhammad (1951-55).

q: Which Act was used as the basis of Pakistan's first (interim) constitution?
f: Pakistan adopted the Government of India Act 1935 with changes as its interim constitution.

q: The 1956 Constitution was framed under the Prime Ministership of which leader?
f: Chaudhry Muhammad Ali was Prime Minister when the first constitution was adopted on 23 March 1956.

q: The 1962 Constitution of Pakistan was abrogated by whom?
f: General Yahya Khan imposed martial law and abrogated it in March 1969.

q: When were the first general elections held after the 1962 Constitution was abrogated?
f: General elections were held in December 1970 under Yahya Khan.

q: How many general seats did the Awami League win in the 1970 elections?
f: The Awami League of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman won 160 general seats, all in East Pakistan.

q: The Shimla Agreement of 1972 was signed between which two leaders?
o: Liaquat Ali Khan and Jawaharlal Nehru
Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi
Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri
f: Bhutto and Indira Gandhi signed it in Shimla on 2 July 1972.

q: How many days did the 1965 Pakistan-India war last?
f: The war ran from 6 September to 23 September 1965, which is 17 days.

q: What is the date of Pakistan's first nuclear test?
f: Pakistan conducted its first nuclear tests on 28 May 1998 (Chagai-I).

q: How many nuclear blasts did Pakistan conduct in 1998?
f: Five blasts on 28 May and one on 30 May 1998, a total of six.

q: Who was the first female Prime Minister of Pakistan (and of the Muslim world)?
f: Benazir Bhutto became Prime Minister in December 1988, the first woman to lead a Muslim-majority country.

q: Who is the current Chief Minister of Punjab (Pakistan)?
f: Maryam Nawaz has been Chief Minister of Punjab since February 2024, the first woman in this post.

q: Who is the current Chief Minister of Balochistan?
f: Mir Sarfraz Bugti was elected Chief Minister of Balochistan in March 2024 and still holds the office.

q: Pakistan created the post of Chief of Defence Forces through which constitutional amendment?
f: The 27th Amendment (November 2025) changed Article 243 and created the Chief of Defence Forces.

q: Which Chinese-made fighter jet was inducted by the Pakistan Air Force in 2022 and used in the May 2025 conflict?
f: The PAF inducted the Chinese J-10CE in 2022 and used it in May 2025.

q: What is the Uraan Pakistan plan?
o: A plan to build a new airport
A military exercise of the Air Force
A national economic transformation plan launched in December 2024
f: Uraan Pakistan is the government's economic transformation plan led by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, with five pillars including exports and digital economy.

q: Who was the first Pakistani to win a Nobel Prize?
f: Dr. Abdus Salam won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979.

q: Ahsan Ramzan is a famous player of which sport?
f: Ahsan Ramzan is a Pakistani snooker player who won the IBSF World Snooker Championship in 2012.

q: Jahangir Khan is famous for which sport?
f: Jahangir Khan won the British Open ten times and was unbeaten for about five years.

q: Abdul Hafeez Kardar was a player of which sport?
f: Kardar was the first captain of Pakistan's Test cricket team.

q: Which game is played with a racket and a shuttle?
f: Badminton uses rackets and a shuttlecock.

q: Which ICC tournament did Pakistan host in 2025?
f: Pakistan hosted the ICC Champions Trophy in February-March 2025, its first ICC event in about 29 years.

q: Who said that the life of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is the practical interpretation of the Holy Quran?
f: When asked about his character, Hazrat Ayesha R.A said his character was the Quran.

q: Over what period was the Holy Quran revealed?
f: Revelation began in 610 CE and ended about 23 years later, around 632 CE.

q: How many Ayats are in Surah Al-Baqarah?
f: Surah Al-Baqarah has 286 Ayats.

q: What is the meaning of Khatam-ul-Nabiyyin?
f: Khatam-ul-Nabiyyin (Surah Al-Ahzab 33:40) means the Seal or Last of the Prophets.

q: Who was the first martyr of Islam?
f: Hazrat Sumayyah R.A was killed by Abu Jahl for her faith and is known as the first martyr of Islam.

q: Who was the first woman to accept Islam?
f: Hazrat Khadija R.A was the first person to accept Islam after the Prophet (PBUH).

q: Who narrated the largest number of Ahadith?
f: Hazrat Abu Hurairah R.A narrated about 5,374 Ahadith.

q: Which of the following lists names all four daughters of Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: The four daughters were Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatima R.A.

q: Hazrat Ayesha R.A was the daughter of which Sahabi?
f: Hazrat Ayesha R.A was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr R.A and wife of the Prophet (PBUH).

q: Which of the following was a daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr R.A?
f: Hazrat Ayesha R.A (and also Hazrat Asma R.A) were daughters of Hazrat Abu Bakr R.A.

q: Hazrat Ali R.A belonged to which clan?
f: Hazrat Ali R.A was from Banu Hashim, the clan of the Prophet (PBUH).

q: Which was the first major battle of Islam, fought between Muslims and the Quraysh?
f: Badr in 2 AH was the first major battle; earlier expeditions such as Widdan had no fighting.

q: Youm-e-Furqan is the title of which battle?
f: The Quran calls the day of Badr Youm-ul-Furqan, the day that separated truth from falsehood.

q: In which year of Hijrah did the Battle of Badr take place?
f: The Battle of Badr took place in Ramadan 2 AH (624 CE).

q: How did Abu Jahl die?
o: Killed in the Battle of Uhud
Killed in the Battle of Badr, struck by two young boys Mu'adh and Mu'awwidh
f: Two young Ansari brothers, Mu'adh and Mu'awwidh, struck him down at Badr and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud finished him.

q: What does the word Ahzab mean?
f: Ahzab means groups or confederates; the tribes allied against Madinah in 5 AH.

q: Which companion suggested digging a trench in the Battle of Ahzab (Khandaq)?
f: Hazrat Salman Farsi R.A suggested the Persian idea of a trench to defend Madinah.

q: When was the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah signed?
f: The treaty was signed in Dhul Qa'dah 6 AH (628 CE).

q: Which special prayer is performed in the middle of the night?
f: Tahajjud is the voluntary night prayer offered after sleeping, in the last part of the night.

q: Where is Mina located?
f: Mina is a valley about 5 km from Makkah where pilgrims stay during Hajj and stone the Jamarat.

q: Where is Mina located?
o: Near Makkah (about 5 km east of it)
f: Mina is a valley a few kilometres east of Makkah where pilgrims stay and stone the Jamarat during Hajj.

q: How many gates does Jannah (Paradise) have?
f: Authentic Ahadith state that Jannah has eight gates, one of which is Ar-Rayyan for those who fast.

q: Who will blow the Trumpet (Soor) on the Day of Judgment?
f: Angel Israfil A.S has been entrusted to blow the Soor to announce Qiyamat and again for resurrection.

q: According to Pakistani textbooks, in which year A.D. was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) born (in Rabi-ul-Awwal, commonly given as 22nd April)?
f: The year of the Elephant is taken as 571 A.D in Pakistani textbooks, with the date given as 22nd April (12 Rabi-ul-Awwal). Some historians give 570 A.D.

q: What was the name of the father of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: The father of the Prophet (PBUH) was Abdullah bin Abdul Muttalib, who died before the Prophet was born.

q: What was the name of the mother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: The mother of the Prophet (PBUH) was Amina bint Wahb of Banu Zuhra.

q: What was the name of the maternal grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Amina was the daughter of Wahb bin Abd Manaf, chief of Banu Zuhra, so he was the maternal grandfather.

q: What was the name of the maternal grandmother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), as given in the list?
f: Amina's mother was Barrah bint Abd al-Uzza, which the list spells as Batarah.

q: What was the real name of Abdul Muttalib, grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Abdul Muttalib's real name was Shaybah; he was called Abdul Muttalib because he was brought up by his uncle Muttalib.

q: What was the name of the paternal grandmother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), the mother of Abdullah?
f: Abdullah's mother was Fatima bint Amr of Banu Makhzum, so she was the Prophet's paternal grandmother.

q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) travel to Syria with his uncle Abu Talib?
f: At age 12 he went with Abu Talib on a trade caravan, where the monk Bahira recognised signs of prophethood.

q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) marry Hazrat Khadija R.A?
f: He married Khadija R.A at age 25, while she was about 40.

q: Among adult free men, who was the first to accept Islam?
f: Abu Bakr Siddiq R.A was the first adult free man to accept Islam.

q: Who was the first among children to accept Islam?
f: Ali R.A, then about ten years old and living in the Prophet's house, was the first child to accept Islam.

q: After the first revelation, which relative of Hazrat Khadija R.A confirmed that the Prophet (PBUH) was the awaited Prophet?
f: Khadija R.A took the Prophet (PBUH) to her cousin Waraqa bin Naufal, a Christian scholar, who confirmed his prophethood.

q: How many children did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) have, according to the common Seerah account?
f: The common account gives 3 sons (Qasim, Abdullah, Ibrahim) and 4 daughters (Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, Fatima).

q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) receive the first revelation (Wahy)?
f: The first revelation came in the cave of Hira when he was 40 years old.

q: Who was the second wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: After Khadija R.A passed away, the Prophet (PBUH) married Sawda R.A, so she is his second wife. The name Zubaida in the list is not correct.

q: In which year A.D. did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) migrate to Madina?
f: The Hijrah took place in 622 A.D, which is the start of the Islamic calendar.

q: Which pair were among the foster mothers (wet nurses) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Thuwaybah (the freed slave of Abu Lahab) and Halima Sa'diyah both nursed the Prophet (PBUH). The list's Sobia is Thuwaybah.

q: Besides Hazrat Halima, whom did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) call his mother?
o: Hazrat Asma bint Abu Bakr R.A
f: The Prophet (PBUH) called Umm Ayman, who raised him after Amina's death, 'my mother after my mother'.

q: How many years after the birth of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) did his mother Hazrat Amina die?
f: Amina died at Abwa while returning from Madina when the Prophet was about six years old.

q: What was the name of the foster sister of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Shaima (Hudhafa bint Harith), daughter of Halima, used to carry and care for the Prophet (PBUH) as a child.

q: Which of these was a foster brother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), a son of Hazrat Halima?
f: Abdullah bin Harith, son of Halima and Harith, was nursed with the Prophet (PBUH) and is known as his foster brother.

q: For how long, according to the common account, did Hazrat Halima look after the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: The common Seerah account says the Prophet stayed with Halima in the desert for around four years (some say five).

q: How old was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) at the time of the Hajr-e-Aswad (Black Stone) incident?
f: When the Kaaba was rebuilt, the Prophet (PBUH), then 35, settled the dispute by placing the stone on a sheet carried by all tribal leaders.

q: Who used to spread thorns in the way of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
o: Umm Jamil, wife of Abu Lahab
f: Umm Jamil bint Harb, wife of Abu Lahab, used to put thorns on the Prophet's path; Surah Al-Lahab mentions her as the carrier of firewood.

q: Whose house was used as the centre of secret preaching by the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
o: Hazrat Arqam bin Abi Arqam R.A
f: The house of Arqam on Mount Safa was Dar-e-Arqam, the first centre of Islamic teaching in Makkah.

q: In which year of Prophethood did the boycott of Banu Hashim begin?
f: Quraish boycotted Banu Hashim and Banu Muttalib from the 7th year of prophethood and they stayed in Shib Abi Talib for about three years.

q: Which Prophet did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the first heaven during Miraj?
f: Authentic Ahadith of Bukhari and Muslim say he met Adam A.S in the first heaven.

q: Which Prophets did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the second heaven during Miraj?
o: Hazrat Musa A.S and Hazrat Haroon A.S
Hazrat Isa A.S and Hazrat Yahya A.S
f: In the second heaven he met the cousins Isa A.S and Yahya A.S.

q: Which Prophet did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the third heaven during Miraj?
f: Authentic Hadith says he met Yusuf A.S in the third heaven. The list's answer Yaqub is not correct.

q: Which Prophet did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the fourth heaven during Miraj?
f: He met Idris A.S in the fourth heaven.

q: Which Prophet did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the fifth heaven during Miraj?
f: He met Haroon A.S in the fifth heaven.

q: Which Prophet did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the sixth heaven during Miraj?
f: He met Musa A.S in the sixth heaven; Musa advised him to ask Allah to reduce the number of prayers.

q: Which Prophet did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the seventh heaven during Miraj?
f: He met Ibrahim A.S in the seventh heaven, leaning against Bait-ul-Mamoor.

q: What was the name of the camel on which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) traveled during the Hijrah?
f: The Prophet's well-known she-camel was Al-Qaswa, and he rode her to Madina.

q: From whom did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) purchase the land for the mosque in Madina (Masjid-e-Nabawi)?
f: The land of Masjid-e-Nabawi belonged to two orphans, Sahl and Suhail, and the Prophet (PBUH) bought it from them.

q: In which Hijri year was the Charter of Madina (Meesaq-e-Madina) issued?
f: The Charter of Madina was made soon after the Hijrah, in 1 A.H, between Muslims, Jews and others of Madina.

q: In which Hijri year was the change of Qibla (from Baitul Maqdis to Kaaba) ordered?
f: The order to turn towards the Kaaba came in the 2nd year after Hijrah, during prayer at Masjid-e-Qiblatain.

q: According to the common Seerah count, how many Ghazwat (expeditions led by the Prophet PBUH himself) are there?
f: Seerah books commonly count 27 Ghazwat, in which the Prophet (PBUH) took part himself; he actually fought in about nine of them.

q: Which was the first Ghazwa of Islam?
f: The first Ghazwa led by the Prophet (PBUH) was Abwa, also called Waddan, in 2 A.H, and no fighting took place.

q: Who was the first to compile Ahadith (Hadith) officially, on the order of Hazrat Umar bin Abdul Aziz?
f: Imam Ibn Shihab Zuhri is widely regarded as the first to compile Ahadith formally, at the order of Umar bin Abdul Aziz.

q: How many Ahadith are reported from Hazrat Abu Hurairah R.A?
f: Hazrat Abu Hurairah R.A is credited with 5374 narrations, the highest among the Sahaba, according to Baqi bin Makhlad.

q: Which Prophet is known as Shaikh-ul-Anbiya?
f: Hazrat Nuh A.S is called Shaikh-ul-Anbiya (Elder of the Prophets) because of his very long life of preaching.

q: Who was given the title Ameen-ul-Ummat?
o: Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah R.A
Hazrat Saad bin Abi Waqqas R.A
f: The Prophet (PBUH) gave Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah R.A the title Ameen-ul-Ummat (Trustworthy of the Ummah).

q: What is the dome over the sacred grave of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) known as?
f: The dome over the Prophet's tomb in Masjid-e-Nabawi is known as the Green Dome (Gumbad-e-Khizra).

q: Where is Bait-ul-Mamoor located?
f: Bait-ul-Mamoor is a house of worship of the angels in the seventh heaven, directly above the Kaaba.

q: Which mosque was demolished on the order of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: The hypocrites built Masjid-e-Dirar to harm Muslims, and the Prophet (PBUH) had it destroyed after Surah At-Tawbah revealed its purpose.

q: Who conquered the fort of Qamus during the Battle of Khyber?
f: Hazrat Ali R.A, given the flag by the Prophet (PBUH), conquered the fort of Qamus and killed its champion Marhab.

q: Which woman tried to poison the Holy Prophet (PBUH) at Khyber?
f: A Jewish woman, Zainab bint Harith, served poisoned roasted goat meat to the Prophet (PBUH) after the conquest of Khyber.

q: Which Surah did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) recite at the conquest of Makkah?
