q: Antonym of "optimistic" is:
f: 'Optimistic' means hopeful about the future, so the antonym is 'pessimistic' (expecting bad things). A) 'hopeful' is a synonym. B) 'positive' is a synonym. D) 'cheerful' is close in meaning, not opposite.

q: By 10 p.m., they ___ the exercise.
f: "By 10 p.m." means the action will be complete before that future time, so we use the future perfect: will have + past participle ("will have finished"). A) "finish" is simple present and does not show completion before a future time. C) "finished tomorrow" mixes past tense with a future word. D) "a

q: Antonym of "expand" is:
f: 'Expand' means to become bigger, so the antonym is 'contract' (to become smaller). A) 'increase' is a synonym. B) 'enlarge' is a synonym. D) 'extend' is also a synonym.

q: "We will meet ___ Monday."
f: Use 'on' for days of the week: on Monday. A) 'in' is wrong: 'in' is for months and years. C) 'at' is wrong: 'at' is for clock time. D) 'from' is wrong: it shows a starting point and needs 'to/till'.

q: The candidate was tired, ___ he completed the run.
f: A is right: being tired but still completing the run is a contrast, so 'yet' (but) fits. B) 'because' is wrong: tiredness is not a reason for completing the run. C) 'so that' is wrong: it shows purpose. D) 'unless' is wrong: it means 'if not'.

q: Choose the antonym of RECOVER.
f: Recover means to get back something lost; its opposite is Lose. A) Regain, B) Retrieve and D) Restore are wrong: they all mean getting something back, like recover.

q: Choose the synonym of NEED.
f: Need means lack of something necessary; its synonym is Want. B) Surplus, C) Luxury and D) Plenty are wrong: they mean having more than enough, the opposite.

q: Choose the synonym of QUIT.

He said that he was tired.
He says that he was tired.

q: Choose the synonym of SHY.
f: Shy means nervous with other people; its synonym is Bashful. A) Confident, C) Outgoing and D) Bold are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.

q: ___ Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean.
f: Names of oceans, seas and rivers always take "the", so "The Pacific Ocean". A) and B) "A" and "An" are for one of many unspecified things, but there is only one Pacific Ocean. D) "No article" is wrong because ocean names need "the".

q: Antonym of "transparent" is:
f: "Transparent" means see-through, so its antonym is "opaque", meaning light cannot pass through it. A) "clear", C) "visible" and D) "plain" all have meanings close to transparent, so they are not opposites.

q: "He has lived here ___ four years."
f: Use 'for' with a period of time: for four years. A) 'since' is wrong: 'since' needs a starting point like 2022. C) 'at' is wrong: it is for clock time. D) 'by' is wrong: it means 'not later than'.

q: Passive of "You must obey the rules" is:

q: Choose the synonym of HUMBLE.
f: Humble means modest, not proud; its synonym is Meek (quiet and gentle). A) Proud, B) Vain and C) Arrogant are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.

q: Antonym of "lenient" is:

q: The word "whose" in "The candidate whose file was missing returned" is a:

q: "She ___ in Rawalpindi for five years." (She still lives there.)

q: Passive of "Someone has stolen my bag" is:

q: "The decision depends ___ the weather."

q: In "The candidates waited outside," "outside" functions as a:
f: 'Outside' tells WHERE they waited, so it modifies the verb 'waited' and is an adverb of place. B) article is wrong: the only articles are a, an, the. C) pronoun is wrong: it does not replace a noun. D) conjunction is wrong: it joins nothing.

q: In "Running improves stamina," "Running" is a:
f: 'Running' is the -ing form used as the subject of the sentence, so it is a gerund working as a noun. B) finite verb is wrong: the finite verb is 'improves'. C) adjective is wrong: it does not describe a noun here. D) preposition is wrong: it shows no relation.

q: He is not only punctual ___ also reliable.
f: A is right: the fixed pair is 'not only ... but also'. B) 'and only' does not form this pair. C) 'nor' pairs with 'neither' (neither ... nor). D) 'or' pairs with 'either' (either ... or).

q: Which word is an interjection?

f: The sun rising in the east is a universal truth, so simple present 'rises' is used. A) 'rose' is wrong: facts that are always true are not put in the past. q: "Assert" means:

q: Choose the synonym of EFFICIENCY.
f: Efficiency means power to do work well; Potency (power, effectiveness) is the closest synonym. B) Weakness, C) Waste and D) Laziness are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.

q: Choose the synonym of EFFICIENCY.
f: Efficiency means ability to do work well; its synonym is Capability. B) Inability, C) Idleness and D) Weakness are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.

q: Active of "The message was sent by Ali" is:
o: Ali sends the message now necessarily.
Ali was sent the message by it.
f: 'Was sent' is simple past passive, so the active is simple past with Ali as subject: Ali sent the message. B) 'sends' is present tense and adds extra words. C) reverses the meaning: the message sent Ali. D) is still passive and adds a new meaning.

q: Which sentence is in present perfect tense?
f: 'I have finished the work' uses have + past participle, which is present perfect. A) is wrong: 'finish' is simple present. B) is wrong: 'finished' is simple past. D) is wrong: 'had finished' is past perfect.

q: He was exhausted, ___ he continued working.
f: A is right: 'yet' shows contrast here: he was tired, but still he continued working. B) 'because' shows reason; tiredness is not the reason for continuing. C) 'unless' means 'if not' and gives no sense. D) 'therefore because' joins two connectors together, which is wrong.

q: Choose the antonym of RAMBLING.
f: Rambling means talking or writing in a long, wandering, unorganized way; its opposite is Methodical (orderly, organized). A) Disorganized, C) Lengthy and D) Wandering are wrong: they all describe rambling.

q: Which pair consists entirely of prepositions?
f: 'In' and 'on' both show relation of place or time, so both are prepositions. B) 'and, but' are wrong: they are conjunctions. C) 'very, quite' are wrong: they are adverbs (intensifiers). D) 'he, they' are wrong: they are pronouns.

q: Choose the synonym of DILIGENT.
f: Diligent means hard-working and careful; its synonym is Industrious. B) Idle, C) Lazy and D) Careless are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.

q: Choose the synonym of TENDENCY.
f: Tendency means a natural leaning toward something; its synonym is Leaning. A) Dislike, C) Reluctance and D) Aversion are wrong: they mean not wanting, the opposite.

q: The instructions were so clear ___ everyone understood them.
f: B is right: the pattern is 'so + adjective + that' to show a result. A) 'than' is wrong: it is used for comparison. C) 'as' is wrong: it is used in 'as ... as' comparisons. D) 'which' is wrong: it is a relative pronoun, not a result linker.

q: Which reporting verb is most suitable for a question?
f: Questions are reported with 'asked' (also inquired, wanted to know). B) 'ordered' is for commands. C) 'exclaimed' is for exclamations like Alas or Hurrah. D) 'promised' is for promises, and 'always' makes no sense here.

q: "Endeavour" means:
f: A is right: an endeavour is a serious attempt or effort; as a verb it means to try hard. B) 'victory' is wrong: that is the result, not the attempt. C) 'order' is wrong: that is a command. D) 'rest' is wrong: that is the opposite of effort.

q: Passive of "She has completed the task" is:
o: The task has been completed by her.
The task was completed by her.
The task is completing by her.
f: Present perfect active (has completed) becomes 'has/have been + past participle': The task has been completed by her. A) misses 'been', so it sounds like the task did the completing. C) 'was completed' is simple past, wrong tense. D) 'is completing' is active continuous, not passive.

q: "Reluctant" means:
f: B is right: reluctant means unwilling or hesitant to do something. A) 'eager' is wrong: it is the opposite (keen, willing). C) 'certain' is wrong: that means sure. D) 'powerful' is wrong: that means strong.

q: Choose the simple past sentence.
f: 'He trained yesterday' uses the past form 'trained' with the finished time 'yesterday', so it is simple past. A) is wrong: 'trains daily' is simple present. C) is wrong: 'has trained' is present perfect. D) is wrong: 'will train' is simple future.

q: Choose the antonym of COMPULSORY.
f: Compulsory means something you must do; its opposite is Optional (you may choose). B) Mandatory, C) Necessary and D) Obligatory are wrong: they all mean must-do, like compulsory.

q: "Prudent" means:

q: "He sat ___ me during the lecture."
f: 'Beside' means next to or by the side of: He sat beside me. A) 'besides' is wrong: it means 'in addition to' (Besides English, he knows Arabic). C) 'among' is wrong: it is for more than two people, and 'me' is one person. D) 'across' is wrong: it means on the other side or from side to side.

f: Curb means to control or hold back; its synonym is Restrain. A) Release, B) Encourage and D) Free are wrong: they mean let go or push forward, the opposite.

q: "She speaks ___ Urdu fluently."
f: Names of languages take no article: 'speaks Urdu'. A) 'a', B) 'an' and C) 'the' are wrong: we do not put an article before a language name.

q: Choose the synonym of BLAME.
f: Blame means to say someone is responsible for a wrong; its synonym is Censure (criticize strongly). A) Approve, B) Pardon and C) Praise are wrong: they are opposite in meaning to blame.

q: Choose the synonym of NEGLECT.
f: Neglect means not giving proper care; its synonym is Negligence. A) Care, B) Attention and D) Diligence are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.

q: In "The wounded soldier recovered," "wounded" is functioning as a:
f: 'Wounded' describes the noun 'soldier' (which soldier?), so here this past participle works as an adjective. A) noun is wrong: the noun is 'soldier'. C) adverb is wrong: it does not modify the verb 'recovered'. D) conjunction is wrong: it joins nothing.

q: Which is grammatically correct?
f: 'Know' is a stative verb (a state of mind), so it is used in simple form: 'I know him'. A) is wrong: stative verbs are not normally used in continuous form. C) is wrong: 'have knowing' is not a correct verb form. D) is wrong: 'was know' mixes 'was' with a base verb.

q: Choose the synonym of DECIDE.
f: Decide means to make up one's mind; its synonym is Determine. A) Hesitate, B) Waver and C) Doubt are wrong: they all mean being unable to decide.

q: Read the passage: Efficient reading is not the same as reading every line at maximum speed. Skilled readers vary their pace according to purpose. They may scan a page to locate a date, skim an article to grasp its main argument, or read slowly when a paragraph contains dense reasoning. They also monitor comprehension. If a key sentence is unclear, they pause, reread, and connect it with surrounding ideas. This flexible approach is especially useful in timed tests, where spending too long on one difficult sentence can reduce the time available for easier questions.  QUESTION: Skimming is mainly used to:
o: grasp the main argument or general idea
f: B is right: the passage says readers 'skim an article to grasp its main argument'. A) 'find a single word only' is wrong: that is scanning. C) 'translate every sentence' is wrong: not mentioned. D) 'check spelling' is wrong: that is proofreading.

q: "His father went to ___ school to meet the principal."
f: His father did not go to study; he went to the building to meet the principal, so 'the school' is used. A) 'a' and B) 'an' are wrong: a specific school (his son's) is meant. D) is wrong: no article is used only when we go for the main purpose (to study).

q: Passive of "The manager is reviewing the application" is:
o: The application is being reviewed by the manager.
The manager is being reviewed by the application.
f: A is right: present continuous passive is is/are + being + past participle: 'is being reviewed', and the object 'the application' becomes the subject. B) 'is reviewed yesterday' has the wrong tense and a past time word. C) 'has review' is not a passive and the verb form is wrong. D) it swaps the rol

q: Read the passage: Pressure narrows attention. This can be useful when a task demands immediate focus, but it can also make a person overlook information that would normally be considered. Good decision makers therefore use simple structures under stress: they identify the objective, separate facts from assumptions, compare the most realistic options, and consider the likely consequences of each. They also know when time is too limited for perfect information. In such cases, the goal is not certainty but a reasonable decision based on the best available evidence. Afterward, reviewing the outcome helps improve future judgment.  QUESTION: Good decision makers separate:
f: A is right: the passage says good decision makers 'separate facts from assumptions'. B) 'speed from strength' is wrong: not mentioned. C) 'leaders from teams' is wrong: not mentioned. D) 'rules from laws only' is wrong: not mentioned.

q: "Pakistan is in ___ Asia."
f: Names of continents take no article, so 'in Asia'. A) 'a', B) 'an' and C) 'the' are wrong: continent names like Asia, Africa, Europe are used without any article.

q: Choose the synonym of MOB.
f: A mob is a large, often disorderly, group of people; its synonym is Crowd. B) Loner, C) Few and D) Individual are wrong: they mean one or a small number of people.

q: The task was ___ difficult that many candidates ran out of time.
f: A is right: the pattern is 'so + adjective + that'; 'difficult' is an adjective. B) 'such a' needs a noun: 'such a difficult task that'. C) 'too much' does not go before an adjective with 'that'. D) 'very a' is not correct English.

q: Which is a correct passive sentence?
f: A passive needs 'be' + past participle; 'is being repaired' is correct present continuous passive. A) 'is repairing' is active, meaning the road repairs something. C) has wrong word order. D) 'has repairing' is not a correct verb form; it should be 'has been repaired'.

q: Choose: "___ United Kingdom".
f: C is right: names of countries with words like Kingdom, States or Republic take 'the': the United Kingdom. A) 'A' and B) 'An' are for one thing among many, not a unique country name. D) 'no article' is used with most single-word country names like Pakistan, not with this one.

q: Which word is a pronoun in "They completed the obstacle course"?
f: 'They' is used in place of the names of people, so it is a pronoun. B) 'completed' is wrong: it is the verb (action). C) 'obstacle' is wrong: here it describes 'course' like an adjective (noun used as modifier). D) 'course' is wrong: it is a noun.

q: Choose the synonym of EQUAL.
f: Equal means the same in amount or level; Uniform (the same throughout) is the synonym. B) Different, C) Unequal and D) Uneven are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.

q: Read the passage: A team is not effective merely because its members are individually talented. Performance depends on coordination: members must understand the objective, know their responsibilities, share relevant information, and adjust when another member encounters difficulty. Trust reduces the time spent checking whether others will perform basic duties, but trust does not mean the absence of accountability. Strong teams make standards clear and address problems early. They also avoid confusing agreement with unity. Members may disagree about methods while still remaining committed to the same mission.  QUESTION: The passage says individual talent alone is:
o: not sufficient for effective team performance
f: B is right: the passage says a team 'is not effective merely because its members are individually talented'; coordination is also needed. A) 'sufficient' is wrong: it is the opposite of 'not merely'. C) 'harmful' is wrong: talent is not called bad. D) 'unrelated to performance' is wrong: talent help

q: "The bus ___ before we reached the stop."
f: The bus left before another past action (we reached), so the earlier action takes past perfect 'had left'. A) 'left' is wrong: it does not show which action happened first as clearly. B) 'has left' is wrong: present perfect does not match the past 'reached'. D) 'leaves' is wrong: it is present tense

q: Choose the antonym of MERRY.
f: Merry means happy and cheerful; its opposite is Sad. B) Cheerful, C) Jolly and D) Lively are wrong: they all mean happy or full of fun, so they are synonyms.

q: "Impartial" means:
f: B is right: impartial means neutral and fair, not favouring any side. A) 'biased' is wrong: it is the opposite (partial, prejudiced). C) 'hostile' is wrong: that means unfriendly. D) 'uncertain' is wrong: that means not sure.

q: The officer asked the men ___ remain calm.
f: B is right: the pattern is 'ask + person + to + verb': asked the men to remain calm. A) 'for' is wrong: 'ask for' is used before a thing, e.g. ask for help. C) 'that they to' is wrong: 'that' needs a full clause, and 'they to' is not one. D) 'of' is wrong: 'ask of' means request something from someo

q: You will not improve ___ you practise regularly.
f: B is right: 'unless' means 'if not': you will not improve if you do not practise. A) 'if' is wrong: it gives the opposite meaning (you will not improve if you practise). C) 'because' is wrong: practice is not a reason for not improving. D) 'and' is wrong: it does not make a conditional link.

q: Read the passage: Pressure narrows attention. This can be useful when a task demands immediate focus, but it can also make a person overlook information that would normally be considered. Good decision makers therefore use simple structures under stress: they identify the objective, separate facts from assumptions, compare the most realistic options, and consider the likely consequences of each. They also know when time is too limited for perfect information. In such cases, the goal is not certainty but a reasonable decision based on the best available evidence. Afterward, reviewing the outcome helps improve future judgment.  QUESTION: When perfect information is impossible, the goal should be:
f: B is right: the passage says 'the goal is not certainty but a reasonable decision based on the best available evidence'. A) 'total certainty' is wrong: the passage rejects it directly. C) 'no decision at all' is wrong: a decision is still needed. D) 'a random choice' is wrong: the decision must be b

q: Choose the synonym of AGREEABLE.
f: Agreeable means willing to agree or go along; Conformable (fitting in, in agreement) is the synonym. A) Opposed, B) Hostile and D) Contrary are wrong: they mean against, the opposite.

q: "Scrutinize" means:
f: A is right: scrutinize means to examine something very closely and carefully. B) 'avoid looking at' is wrong: it is the opposite. C) 'destroy' is wrong: that means to ruin. D) 'summarize quickly' is wrong: scrutinizing is slow and detailed.

q: In passive voice, the main verb is normally in the:
f: Every passive uses a form of 'be' + the past participle (third form): written, done, built. A) the base form (write) is not used after 'be' in passive. C) the present participle (-ing) is used for active continuous, not passive. D) 'infinitive without be' is not a passive form at all.

q: Read the passage: A team is not effective merely because its members are individually talented. Performance depends on coordination: members must understand the objective, know their responsibilities, share relevant information, and adjust when another member encounters difficulty. Trust reduces the time spent checking whether others will perform basic duties, but trust does not mean the absence of accountability. Strong teams make standards clear and address problems early. They also avoid confusing agreement with unity. Members may disagree about methods while still remaining committed to the same mission.  QUESTION: Trust in a team does NOT mean:
f: B is right: the passage says 'trust does not mean the absence of accountability'. A) 'reduced unnecessary checking' is wrong: trust does reduce checking. C) 'confidence in basic duties' is wrong: trust does mean this. D) 'reliable performance' is wrong: trust is linked to members doing their duties.

q: Synonym of "accurate" is:
f: 'Accurate' means exactly correct with no mistakes, so 'precise' is the synonym. B) 'careless' means without care, often causing mistakes. C) 'vague' means not clear. D) 'rough' here means not exact (a rough guess).

q: "Credible" means:
f: A is right: credible means believable and worthy of trust. B) 'unrelated' is wrong: that is irrelevant. C) 'illegal' is wrong: that means against the law. D) 'weak' is wrong: that means feeble.

q: Synonym of "vital" is:
f: 'Vital' means very important or necessary, so 'essential' is the synonym. B) 'minor' means small and unimportant, the opposite. C) 'optional' means not required, also the opposite idea. D) 'weak' means lacking strength.

q: The teacher said, "The earth revolves around the sun."
o: The teacher said that the earth revolved around the sun only.
The teacher said that the earth revolves around the sun.
The teacher told that the earth has revolved.
f: A universal truth (a fact that is always true) does not change its tense: The teacher said that the earth revolves around the sun. A) changes to 'revolved' and adds 'only'. C) 'told that' needs an object and 'has revolved' changes the meaning. D) 'earth revolving' is not a complete clause.

q: "By the time you arrive, I ___ the report."
f: The report will be finished before a future moment (you arrive), so future perfect 'will have finished' is correct. A) 'finish' is wrong: it does not show completion before a point. B) 'finished' is wrong: it is past. D) 'am finishing yesterday' is wrong: present continuous cannot go with 'yesterday

q: Read the passage: Efficient reading is not the same as reading every line at maximum speed. Skilled readers vary their pace according to purpose. They may scan a page to locate a date, skim an article to grasp its main argument, or read slowly when a paragraph contains dense reasoning. They also monitor comprehension. If a key sentence is unclear, they pause, reread, and connect it with surrounding ideas. This flexible approach is especially useful in timed tests, where spending too long on one difficult sentence can reduce the time available for easier questions.  QUESTION: If a key sentence is unclear, skilled readers should:
o: pause, reread, and connect it with context
f: B is right: the passage says they 'pause, reread, and connect it with surrounding ideas'. A) 'guess and move on always' is wrong: they pause and reread. C) 'stop the test' is wrong: not mentioned. D) 'ignore the paragraph entirely' is wrong: they work to understand it.

q: Choose the antonym of HUMBLE.
f: Humble means modest, not proud; its opposite is Vain (proud of oneself). B) Modest, C) Simple and D) Meek are wrong: they are all close in meaning to humble.

q: Which word is a coordinating conjunction?
f: C is right: 'but' is a coordinating conjunction; these are FANBOYS: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so. A) 'although', B) 'because' and D) 'while' are subordinating conjunctions; they start a dependent clause.

q: Choose the synonym of "abandon".
f: 'Abandon' means to leave something or someone completely and not come back, so 'leave' is the synonym. B) 'collect' means to gather, which is the opposite idea. C) 'repair' means to fix. D) 'praise' means to say good things about someone.

q: I will call you ___ I arrive.
f: A is right: 'when' tells the time: I will call you at the time I arrive. B) 'unless' means 'if not', so the meaning becomes wrong. C) 'despite' must be followed by a noun or -ing, not a clause like 'I arrive'. D) 'during' is followed by a noun (during the trip), not a clause.

q: Choose the antonym of ACTIVITY.
f: Activity means being busy or moving and doing things; its opposite is Inactivity (doing nothing). A) Energy, C) Movement and D) Action are wrong: they are all close in meaning to activity, not opposite.

q: Passive of "They make cars here" is:
f: Simple present active (make) becomes 'am/is/are + past participle': Cars are made here. 'They' is a general subject so it is dropped. B) 'were made yesterday' is past tense and adds new time. C) 'Cars make here' is active and has no 'be'. D) 'are making' is active continuous, meaning cars are making

q: He succeeded ___ working consistently.
f: A is right: 'by + -ing' shows the method or means of doing something: succeeded by working consistently. B) 'with' is wrong: 'with' is used with a tool or noun, not with -ing for method. C) 'at' is wrong: 'at' is for skill (good at). D) 'to' is wrong: it does not show method.

q: "Here" commonly changes to:
f: In reported speech, 'here' (this place) usually changes to 'there' (that place). B) 'then' is the change for 'now', a time word. C) 'that' is the change for 'this'. D) 'before' is the change for 'ago'.

q: Which word is a determiner/article in "An officer entered the room"?
f: 'An' is the indefinite article placed before 'officer', which starts with a vowel sound. A) 'officer' is wrong: it is a noun. B) 'entered' is wrong: it is a verb. D) 'room' is wrong: it is a noun; 'the' before it is also an article, but it is not an option.

q: Choose the correct form: "He ___ to the academy every morning."
f: A daily habit (every morning) uses simple present, and the singular subject 'He' takes -es: 'goes'. A) 'go' is wrong: it is for I/we/you/they. C) 'went' is wrong: 'every morning' shows a present habit, not past. D) 'going' is wrong: an -ing form needs 'is' before it.

q: Choose the synonym of COLLAPSE.
f: Collapse means to fall down suddenly or fail; its synonym is Break down. A) Build up, B) Recover and D) Rise are wrong: they mean getting stronger or higher, the opposite.

q: Read the passage: Pressure narrows attention. This can be useful when a task demands immediate focus, but it can also make a person overlook information that would normally be considered. Good decision makers therefore use simple structures under stress: they identify the objective, separate facts from assumptions, compare the most realistic options, and consider the likely consequences of each. They also know when time is too limited for perfect information. In such cases, the goal is not certainty but a reasonable decision based on the best available evidence. Afterward, reviewing the outcome helps improve future judgment.  QUESTION: Why review the outcome afterward?
o: To make the original decision perfect
f: B is right: the passage says 'reviewing the outcome helps improve future judgment'. A) 'To assign blame' is wrong: blame is not mentioned. C) 'To avoid evidence' is wrong: the passage values evidence. D) 'To make the original decision perfect' is wrong: a past decision cannot be changed.

q: Choose the antonym of IMAGINARY.
f: Imaginary means existing only in the mind; its opposite is Real. B) Fanciful, C) Fictional and D) Unreal are wrong: they all mean not real, the same as imaginary.

q: Synonym of "rapid" is:
f: 'Rapid' means very fast, so 'swift' is the synonym. A) 'slow' is the opposite. C) 'late' means after the right time, not speed. D) 'weak' means lacking strength.

q: "He waited for ___ hour."
f: The h in 'hour' is silent, so it begins with a vowel sound and takes 'an'. A) 'a' is wrong: 'a' is for consonant sounds. C) 'the' is wrong: no specific hour is meant. D) is wrong: 'hour' is a singular countable noun and needs an article.

q: Choose the synonym of WICKED.
f: Wicked means very bad; its synonym is Evil. A) Virtuous, C) Kind and D) Noble are wrong: they mean good, the opposite.

q: "I ___ this book since Monday."
f: 'Since Monday' shows an action that started in the past and is still going on, so present perfect continuous 'have been reading' is correct. A) 'read' is wrong: simple tense does not show continuation till now. B) 'am reading' is wrong: present continuous cannot be used with 'since'. D) 'had read' i

q: "___ Quran is the holy book of Islam."
f: Names of well-known holy books take 'the', so 'The Quran'. A) 'A' and B) 'An' are wrong: there is only one Quran, not any one of many. D) is wrong: the name is used with 'the' by convention.

q: Complete: "He left early ___ avoid the traffic."
f: A is right: 'in order to' + base verb shows purpose: he left early to avoid traffic. B) 'because' needs a full clause (because he wanted to avoid). C) 'although' shows contrast and needs a clause. D) 'despite' shows contrast and needs a noun or -ing, not 'avoid'.

q: Choose the antonym of EQUAL.
f: Equal means the same in size, amount or level; its opposite is Uneven (not the same). A) Same, B) Uniform and D) Identical are wrong: they all mean alike, like equal.

q: He said, "May you succeed!"
o: He prayed that I might succeed.
He said that I may succeeded.
f: A wish or prayer (May you...) is reported with 'prayed/wished that' + 'might': He prayed that I might succeed. B) keeps 'may' and uses 'succeeded'; after a modal use the base form. C) 'asked me to succeeding' is wrong form and wrong verb. D) 'ordered success' changes the meaning; a prayer is not an

q: Antonym of "frequent" is:
f: "Frequent" means happening often, so its antonym is "rare" (happening seldom). A) "common", B) "regular" and D) "repeated" all have meanings close to frequent, so they are synonyms, not opposites.

q: "Listen! Someone ___ at the door."
f: 'Listen!' shows the knocking is happening right now, so present continuous 'is knocking' is correct. A) 'knocks' is wrong: simple present is for habits. B) 'knocked' is wrong: it is past. D) 'has knocked' is wrong: it shows a completed action, not one in progress.

q: "She is ___ best candidate in the group."
f: Superlative adjectives (best, tallest, most famous) take 'the', so 'the best candidate'. A) 'a' and B) 'an' are wrong: a superlative points to one specific person, not any one. D) is wrong: a superlative normally needs 'the'.

q: "Sustain" most nearly means:
f: A is right: 'sustain' means to keep something going or to maintain it. B) 'destroy' is the opposite. C) 'forget' is unrelated. D) 'interrupt' means to stop for a while, which is nearly the opposite.

q: "He arrived ___ the airport on time."
f: We use 'arrive at' for a specific place or building like an airport, station or school. A) 'arrive in' is used for a city or country (arrive in Lahore). C) 'arrive on' is not used for places; 'on' is for days (arrive on Monday). D) 'arrive by' shows the means or a deadline (arrive by train, by 5 pm)

q: "Adaptable" means:
f: A is right: 'adaptable' means able to adjust or change to fit new conditions. B) 'unable to change' is the opposite meaning. C) 'careless' means not paying attention, a different idea. D) 'slow only' has no link to the word.

q: Choose the synonym of REASON.
f: As a verb, reason means to think and discuss logically, to argue a point; so Argue is the synonym. B) Ignore is wrong: it means to pay no attention. C) Accede is wrong: it means to agree to a demand. D) Obey is wrong: it means to follow orders.

q: Choose the antonym of MAJORITY.
f: Majority means the larger part or number; its opposite is Minority (the smaller part). A) Plurality, C) Bulk and D) Mass are wrong: they all refer to the larger part or a big amount.

q: Choose the antonym of ABILITY.
f: Ability means power or skill to do something; its opposite is Incapability (not being able). A) Capability, B) Skill and C) Talent are wrong: they all mean ability.

q: In the same sentence, "omission" most nearly means:
f: A is right: an omission is something left out or forgotten. B) a reward is a prize, not related. C) an explanation is giving reasons. D) a prediction is a guess about the future.

q: Which of the following is a conjunction?
f: 'Because' joins two clauses and gives a reason, so it is a (subordinating) conjunction. A) 'under' is wrong: it is a preposition of place. C) 'quickly' is wrong: it is an adverb of manner. D) 'brave' is wrong: it is an adjective.

q: "We crossed ___ Indus River."
f: Names of rivers take 'the', so it is 'the Indus River'. A) 'a' and B) 'an' are wrong: a particular named river is not 'any one'. D) is wrong: river names are not used without 'the'.

q: "He ___ for two hours before the rain stopped."
f: 'For two hours before the rain stopped' stresses how long an action continued before another past event, so past perfect continuous 'had been running' is correct. A) 'ran' is wrong: it does not show duration before another past event. C) 'has been running' is wrong: it links to the present, not the

q: Indirect: He said, "What a beautiful view!"
o: He exclaimed that it was a very beautiful view.
He asked whether the view was beautiful.
He said what was a view?
f: An exclamation is reported with "exclaimed that" and changed into a statement: "He exclaimed that it was a very beautiful view." The word "What" becomes "very". B) "asked whether" turns it into a question, which is wrong. C) "ordered" is for commands. D) "said what was a view?" keeps a question form

q: "The train passed ___ the tunnel."
f: 'Through' is used for moving inside something from one end to the other, like a tunnel, pipe or forest. The train went in one end and came out the other. B) 'across' is for moving from one side of a flat surface to the other, like a road or river. C) 'over' means above, but a train goes inside a tun

q: Passive of "They are building a bridge" is:
o: A bridge is being built by them.
A bridge was built by them.
A bridge has been built by them.
f: Present continuous active (are building) becomes 'is/are being + past participle' in passive: A bridge is being built by them. B) 'was built' is simple past, wrong tense. C) 'has been built' is present perfect, wrong tense. D) 'is built them' misses 'being' and the word 'by', and is the wrong tense.

q: "Concise" means:
f: A is right: concise means brief but complete, saying a lot in few words. B) 'very confusing' is wrong: that is muddled or obscure. C) 'lengthy' is wrong: it is the opposite (verbose, wordy). D) 'careless' is wrong: that is negligent, not about length.

q: Passive of "You should follow the instructions" is:
f: With a modal verb, the passive is modal + be + past participle: "The instructions should be followed." B) "should followed" is missing "be". C) "are should follow" puts two verbs wrongly together; a modal never follows "are". D) "The instructions followed you" changes the meaning and is not passive.

q: Choose the synonym of RESCIND.
f: Rescind means to cancel a law, order or agreement; its synonym is Cancel. B) Enact, C) Approve and D) Confirm are wrong: they mean make or keep valid, the opposite.

q: Neither Ali ___ Hamza was late.
f: C is right: 'neither' is always paired with 'nor': neither ... nor. A) 'and' is wrong: it pairs with 'both'. B) 'or' is wrong: it pairs with 'either'. D) 'but' is wrong: it is not a partner of 'neither'.

q: A writer says, "The plan is costly; nevertheless, it may be necessary." "Nevertheless" signals:
f: A is right: 'nevertheless' means 'in spite of that', so it shows contrast between 'costly' and 'necessary'. B) cause words are because or since. C) time words are then, later, after. D) addition words are also, moreover, furthermore.

q: Choose the antonym of "scarce".
f: 'Scarce' means not enough or hard to find, so the antonym is 'abundant' (more than enough). A) 'rare' is a synonym, not an antonym. B) 'limited' also means not much, a synonym. D) 'small' is about size and is close in meaning, not opposite.

q: He is responsible ___ the equipment.
f: The fixed phrase is "responsible for" something or someone. A) "of" is wrong with responsible. B) "to" is used for the person you report to: "responsible to the manager", not for the equipment. D) "at" is not used with responsible.

q: "At 8 p.m. yesterday, we ___ for the test."
f: An action that was going on at a fixed past time (8 p.m. yesterday) uses past continuous 'were studying'. A) 'studied' is wrong: it shows a completed action, not one in progress at that moment. C) 'have studied' is wrong: present perfect cannot be used with 'yesterday'. D) 'study' is wrong: it is pr

q: Synonym of "brave" is:
f: 'Brave' means not afraid of danger, so 'courageous' is the synonym. A) 'cowardly' is the opposite (antonym). C) 'weak' means lacking strength, not the same. D) 'silent' means quiet and has no link to bravery.

q: "Pakistan became independent ___ 1947."
f: Use 'in' for years: in 1947. B) 'on' is wrong: 'on' is for days and dates. C) 'at' is wrong: 'at' is for clock time. D) 'since' is wrong: it goes with perfect tenses (has been independent since 1947).

q: In reported questions, the word order is generally:
f: In reported questions we use statement order (subject + verb), not question order: He asked where she lived, not where did she live. A) question order is used only in direct speech. C) 'inverted twice' is not a grammar rule. D) 'verb only' is wrong; the clause needs a subject too.

q: "The plane flew ___ the clouds."
f: 'Above' means at a higher level, so the plane flew above the clouds. B) 'between only' is wrong: 'between' needs two things and 'only' makes it ungrammatical. C) 'beside' is wrong: it means next to, at the side. D) 'since' is wrong: it is for time, not place.

q: The team consists ___ ten members.
f: The fixed phrase is "consist of", meaning to be made up of. A) "consist in" is a different, formal phrase meaning "to have as the main part" and does not fit here. C) "on" and D) "at" are not used with consist.

q: Read the passage: Efficient reading is not the same as reading every line at maximum speed. Skilled readers vary their pace according to purpose. They may scan a page to locate a date, skim an article to grasp its main argument, or read slowly when a paragraph contains dense reasoning. They also monitor comprehension. If a key sentence is unclear, they pause, reread, and connect it with surrounding ideas. This flexible approach is especially useful in timed tests, where spending too long on one difficult sentence can reduce the time available for easier questions.  QUESTION: Efficient readers vary their pace according to:
f: B is right: the passage says 'Skilled readers vary their pace according to purpose.' A) 'page color' is wrong: not mentioned. C) 'handwriting' is wrong: not mentioned. D) 'mood only' is wrong: not mentioned.

q: Synonym of "robust" is:
f: "Robust" means strong and healthy, so its synonym is "strong". B) "fragile" means easily broken, which is the opposite. C) "silent" means quiet, not related. D) "rare" means not common, not related.

q: Choose the synonym of DETERMINATION.

She asked that he sat down.
f: A polite request with "please" is reported with "requested" + object + to-infinitive, and "please" is dropped: "She requested him to sit down." B) "said him" is wrong ("said" takes "to": said to him) and it keeps "please". C) "asked that he sat down" is not the right pattern for a command. D) "order

q: "She ___ already ___ the form."
f: Present perfect is has/have + past participle, and 'already' comes between them: 'has already submitted'. B) 'had submit' is wrong: 'submit' is not a past participle. C) 'is submitted' is wrong: it is passive and does not fit 'She ... the form'. D) 'was submit' is wrong: 'was' with a base verb is no

q: Passive of "They have postponed the match" is:
f: The active is present perfect, so the passive is has/have been + past participle: "The match has been postponed." B) "had postpone" uses the wrong tense and the base form. C) "is postponing" is active present continuous. D) "was postponing" is active past continuous, not passive.

q: Choose the antonym of WILD.
f: Wild means not tamed, savage; its opposite is Civilized. A) Fierce, B) Untamed and C) Savage are wrong: they all mean the same as wild.

q: Passive of "Open the door" is best expressed as:
o: Let open the door by you.
f: Imperative sentences (orders) become passive with 'Let + object + be + past participle': Let the door be opened. B) 'The door open' has no 'be' and no passive form. C) 'Door is opened you' is broken grammar with no 'by'. D) 'Let open the door by you' has wrong word order and no 'be'.

q: I ___ him yesterday at the library.
f: "Yesterday" is a finished past time, so we use the simple past "met". A) "meet" is present tense and does not fit a past time. B) "have met" is present perfect, which is not used with a definite past time like yesterday. D) "am meeting" is present continuous and shows now or the future, not yesterda

q: Choose the synonym of WILD.
f: Wild means untamed and fierce; its synonym is Savage. B) Gentle, C) Civilized and D) Tame are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.

q: Take an umbrella ___ it rains.
f: A is right: 'in case' shows a precaution against something that may happen. B) 'although' is wrong: it shows contrast. C) 'because of' is wrong: it must be followed by a noun, not a clause. D) 'despite' is wrong: it shows contrast and also needs a noun.

q: Choose the antonym of JUSTICE.
f: Justice means fairness; its opposite is Inequity (unfairness). A) Honesty, C) Equity and D) Fairness are wrong: they are close in meaning to justice.

q: The word "resilient" most nearly means:
f: A is right: resilient means able to recover quickly from difficulty or shock. B) 'easily broken' is wrong: that is fragile, the opposite. C) 'unwilling to learn' is wrong: that is stubborn or obstinate. D) 'extremely noisy' is wrong: that is boisterous or deafening.

q: Read the passage: Errors are unavoidable in serious learning. Their value, however, depends on what happens after they are noticed. Repeating an error without analysis produces little improvement. Effective learners identify the cause, correct the method, and test the correction under similar conditions. They also distinguish between a careless mistake and a conceptual misunderstanding. The first may require better attention; the second may require rebuilding knowledge from the foundation. This process can feel slower than simply doing more questions, but it usually produces more durable progress because it changes the mechanism that caused the failure.  QUESTION: The passage argues that errors become useful when learners:
f: B is right: the passage says effective learners 'identify the cause, correct the method, and test the correction'. A) 'ignore them' is wrong: the passage says to analyse errors. C) 'repeat more questions immediately' is wrong: 'Repeating an error without analysis produces little improvement.' D) 'av

q: Synonym of "allocate" is:
f: A is right: 'allocate' means to give or assign something for a purpose, e.g. allocate funds for schools. B) 'remove' is almost the opposite. C) 'hide' is unrelated. D) 'oppose' means to be against.

q: "She bought ___ umbrella and ___ raincoat."
f: 'Umbrella' starts with a vowel sound, so 'an umbrella'; 'raincoat' starts with a consonant sound, so 'a raincoat'. A) 'a / a' is wrong: 'a umbrella' is incorrect. C) 'the / an' is wrong: 'an raincoat' is incorrect and no specific umbrella is meant. D) 'an / an' is wrong for the same reason.

q: Choose the synonym of DISCLOSE.
f: Disclose means to make known a secret; its synonym is Reveal. B) Hide, C) Cover and D) Conceal are wrong: they mean keep secret, the opposite.

q: "Coherent" means:
f: A is right: coherent means logical and well connected, easy to follow. B) 'broken physically' is wrong: coherent is about ideas, not physical damage. C) 'secret' is wrong: that is covert or confidential. D) 'angry' is wrong: that is irate.

q: She said, "Where are you going?"
o: She asked where was I going.
She asked where I was going.
She said where I am going.
She asked that where I went.
f: A wh-question keeps the wh-word but uses statement order (subject before verb): She asked where I was going. A) keeps question order 'was I'. C) uses 'said' and present 'am', with no tense change. D) 'asked that where' is wrong; do not add 'that', and 'went' changes the tense wrongly.

q: Choose the synonym of TROTH.
f: Troth is an old word meaning faith, loyalty or a promise; so Faith is the synonym. A) Doubt, B) Betrayal and D) Treachery are wrong: they mean distrust or disloyalty, the opposite.

q: Choose the antonym of ACCUSATION.
f: An accusation is a charge that someone did wrong; its opposite is Defence (speaking to protect oneself against the charge). B) Allegation, C) Charge and D) Blame are wrong: they all mean the same as accusation.

q: Active of "English is spoken in many countries" is:
o: People speak English in many countries.
People spoke English in many countries only.
Many countries are speaking English people.
f: 'Is spoken' is simple present passive with no agent, so the active uses a general subject in simple present: People speak English in many countries. B) 'spoke' is past tense and 'only' adds a new meaning. C) 'English speaks people' reverses the meaning. D) is wrong tense (continuous) and broken word

q: She ___ for the interview when I called.
f: When one past action was in progress and another past action happened in the middle of it, the longer action takes the past continuous: "was preparing". A) "prepared" is simple past and shows a completed action, not one in progress. C) "has prepared" is present perfect and does not match the past cl

q: In "He is extremely careful," "extremely" modifies:
f: 'Extremely' is an intensifier that tells how careful he is, so it modifies the adjective 'careful'. A) 'He' is wrong: adverbs do not modify pronouns. B) 'is' is wrong: it does not tell how he 'is'; it grades the quality. D) is wrong: it modifies one word, not the whole sentence.

q: Choose the antonym of SIN.
f: Sin means a wrong or evil act; its opposite is Virtue (goodness). A) Crime, C) Evil and D) Wrongdoing are wrong: they all mean the same as sin.

q: Choose the antonym of FLEXIBLE.
f: Flexible means easy to bend or change; its opposite is Rigid (stiff, cannot bend). A) Pliable, B) Supple and D) Elastic are wrong: they all mean bendable, so they are synonyms.

q: Choose the antonym of QUESTIONABLE.
f: Questionable means doubtful, not certain; its opposite is Unquestionable (certain, beyond doubt). A) Doubtful, C) Dubious and D) Uncertain are wrong: they all mean the same as questionable.

q: "Meticulous" means:
f: B is right: meticulous means very careful about every small detail. A) 'careless' is wrong: it is the opposite. C) 'lazy' is wrong: that is idle or indolent. D) 'fearful' is wrong: that means afraid.

q: "Contingency" most nearly means:
o: a possible future event or emergency
f: A is right: a contingency is a possible future event or emergency that you prepare for. B) 'a fixed certainty' is wrong: contingency means something that may or may not happen. C) 'a celebration' is wrong: that is a festivity. D) 'a routine fact only' is wrong: a contingency is unplanned, not routin

q: He studied hard; ___, he passed the test.
f: B is right: passing the test is the result of studying hard, so 'therefore' fits. A) 'however' is wrong: it shows contrast. C) 'otherwise' is wrong: it means 'if not', giving a bad result. D) 'nevertheless' is wrong: it shows contrast, but here there is cause and effect.

q: Which is an adverb of manner?
f: A is right: an adverb of manner tells HOW something is done, and 'carefully' tells how. B) 'yesterday' is an adverb of time (when). C) 'often' is an adverb of frequency (how often). D) 'outside' is an adverb of place (where).

q: Antonym of "ancient" is:
f: 'Ancient' means very old, from long ago, so the antonym is 'modern' (new, of present times). A) 'old' is a synonym. B) 'historic' is about the past, close in meaning. D) 'former' means earlier, also close in meaning, not opposite.

q: "She wants to become ___ engineer."
f: 'Engineer' begins with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an'. A) 'a' is wrong: 'a' comes before consonant sounds. C) 'the' is wrong: she wants to be any one engineer, not a specific one. D) is wrong: a singular countable noun of profession needs an article.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: He is capable to do it.
He is capable of doing it.
He is capable for do it.
f: The correct pattern is "capable of" + verb-ing: "He is capable of doing it." A) "capable to do" is a common mistake; capable does not take a to-infinitive. C) "capable for do" uses the wrong preposition and the base verb. D) "He capable of do it" has no verb "is" and uses "do" instead of "doing".

q: Choose the correct sentence.
f: "Police" is a plural noun even without "s", so it takes the plural verb: "The police are investigating." A) "is" is singular, so it is wrong. C) "are investigates" is wrong grammar: after "are" we use the -ing form. D) "A police" is wrong: we cannot use "a" with police; we say "a police officer".

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: I look forward to meet you.
I look forward to meeting you.
I look forward for meet you.
I am look forward to meeting you.
f: In "look forward to", the word "to" is a preposition, not part of an infinitive, so it is followed by verb-ing: "I look forward to meeting you." A) "to meet" wrongly treats "to" as an infinitive. C) "for meet" uses the wrong preposition and the base verb. D) "am look" is wrong grammar; it should be

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: She has less books than me.
She has fewer books than I do.
She has lesser books than I.
f: B is right: 'books' can be counted, so we use 'fewer', and 'than I do' is correct (I have books). A) 'less' is for uncountable nouns like water or sugar, not books. C) 'lesser' means lower in importance, not smaller in number. D) 'She have' is wrong: with 'she' we use 'has'.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: He denied to take the money.
f: B is right: the verb 'deny' is followed by a gerund (verb + ing), so 'denied taking'. A) 'deny to take' is wrong: 'deny' does not take 'to' + verb. C) 'denied take' is wrong: a bare verb cannot follow 'deny'. D) 'denied that taking' is wrong: 'that' needs a full clause like 'that he took'.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: She is one of the best player.
She is one of the best players.
She is one of best players is.
She one of the best player.
f: B is right: 'one of the' + superlative is followed by a plural noun: 'one of the best players'. A) 'player' is singular, which is wrong after 'one of the'. C) extra 'is' at the end and missing 'the' make it wrong. D) it has no verb ('is') and uses a singular noun.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
f: B is right: 'candidates' is a plural countable noun, so we use 'are fewer'. A) 'less' is for uncountable nouns, not candidates. C) 'is' does not agree with plural 'candidates'. D) 'lesser' is wrong here and 'candidate' should be plural.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
f: With 'does not', the main verb stays in the base form: He does not know me. A) 'He do not' is wrong; 'he' takes 'does', not 'do'. B) 'does not knows' is wrong; after 'does' do not add -s. D) 'not does know' has wrong word order.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: She is more senior than me always.
f: Latin comparatives like senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior take 'to', not 'than': She is senior to me. A) 'senior than' is a common mistake. C) 'senior from' is wrong. D) 'more senior than' is wrong here, and 'always' adds extra meaning.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Neither of the boys are absent.
Neither of the boys is absent.
f: 'Neither of' + plural noun takes a singular verb: Neither of the boys is absent. A) 'are' is the plural verb, wrong here. C) 'Neither boys' is wrong; without 'of', neither takes a singular noun (neither boy). D) misses 'the' and uses plural 'are'.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Each of the players have a kit.
Each of the players has a kit.
Each of players have a kit.
f: 'Each of' + plural noun takes a singular verb: Each of the players has a kit. A) 'have' is plural, wrong here. C) 'Each players' is wrong; without 'of', 'each' takes a singular noun, and 'a' is missing. D) misses 'the' and uses plural 'have'.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: He has been living here since five years.
He has been living here for five years.
He is living here for five years ago.
He lived here since five years.
f: Use 'for' with a period of time (five years) and 'since' with a point of time (2020): He has been living here for five years. A) 'since five years' is a common mistake. C) mixes present 'is living' with 'ago'. D) simple past 'lived' does not go with 'since'.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: I prefer tea over than coffee.
f: 'Prefer' takes 'to', not 'than': I prefer tea to coffee. A) 'prefer than' is a common mistake. C) 'over than' mixes two forms and is wrong. D) 'prefer from' is wrong.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: One of my friend is here.
One of my friends is here.
One of my friends are here.
f: 'One of' is followed by a plural noun, and the verb is singular because the subject is 'one': One of my friends is here. A) 'friend' must be plural after 'one of'. C) 'are' is wrong; the subject 'one' is singular. D) misses 'of'.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
f: 'News' looks plural but is uncountable and takes a singular verb: The news is good. A) 'are' is plural, wrong. C) 'were' is plural, and 'always' adds extra meaning. D) 'are a good' is broken grammar.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
f: The fixed phrase is 'good at' a subject or skill: He is good at English. A) 'good in' is a common mistake in Pakistani English. C) 'good on' is wrong. D) 'good for' means helpful to (Milk is good for health), a different meaning.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
f: 'Discuss' is a transitive verb and takes a direct object with no preposition: She discussed the issue. A) 'discussed about' is a common mistake. C) 'discussed on' is also wrong. D) 'was discussed' is passive and makes no sense with 'the issue' after it.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
f: B is right: 'return' already means 'go back', so 'returned home' is enough. A) 'returned back' is wrong: 'back' repeats the meaning (redundant). C) 'back returned' is wrong word order and still redundant. D) 'returned to back home' is wrong: 'to back' makes no sense and is redundant.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: I am used to wake early.
I am used to waking early.
I used to waking early now.
I am use to wake early.
f: B is right: 'be used to' means 'be in the habit of', and here 'to' is a preposition, so it takes the -ing form: 'am used to waking'. A) 'used to wake' is wrong: after 'be used to' we need -ing, not the base verb. C) 'I used to waking' is wrong: 'am' is missing, and 'used to' alone (past habit) takes

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: If I was you, I would apply.
If I were you, I would apply.
If I am you, I would apply.
If I were you, I will applied.
f: B is right: for an imaginary or unreal condition we use 'were' for all subjects, then 'would + base verb': 'If I were you, I would apply.' A) 'If I was you' is wrong in formal and exam English: the subjunctive 'were' is needed. C) 'If I am you' is wrong: present tense cannot express an impossible si

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: He is married with a doctor.
He is married to a doctor.
He is married by a doctor.
He married to with a doctor.
f: B is right: the correct preposition is 'married to' someone. A) 'married with' is wrong: 'with' is not used for the spouse (it can be used for children: married with two kids). C) 'married by' is wrong: 'by' shows the person who performs the ceremony, not the spouse. D) 'married to with' is wrong: t

q: Choose the correct sentence.
f: B is right: after 'did not' (did/does/do) we use the base form of the verb: 'did not go'. A) 'did not went' is wrong: the past is already shown by 'did', so 'went' is double past. C) 'not did go' is wrong word order: 'not' comes after 'did'. D) 'did not gone' is wrong: 'gone' is a past participle, u

q: Choose the correct sentence.
f: B is right: 'furniture' is an uncountable noun, so it takes a singular verb: 'The furniture is expensive.' A) 'furniture are' is wrong: uncountable nouns take singular verbs. C) 'furnitures' is wrong: 'furniture' has no plural form. D) 'Furniture are an expensive' is wrong: plural verb, and 'an' can

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: He asked that where I lived.
He asked where did I live.
He asked where I did lived.
f: B is right: in reported (indirect) questions we use statement word order and no 'that': 'He asked where I lived.' A) 'asked that where' is wrong: 'that' is not used before a question word. C) 'where did I live' is wrong: this is direct question order, not reported speech. D) 'where I did lived' is w

q: Choose the correct sentence.
f: B is right: 'reasons' is plural, so we use 'There are' and 'many'. A) 'There is' is wrong: 'is' is singular but 'reasons' is plural. C) 'There have' is wrong: we use 'there is/are' to show existence, not 'there have'. D) 'much reasons' is wrong: 'much' is for uncountable nouns; 'reasons' is countabl

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: My brother is elder than me.
My brother is older than I am.
My brother is more elder than me.
f: B is right: to compare age with 'than' we use 'older': 'older than I am'. A) 'elder than' is wrong: 'elder' is not used with 'than'. C) 'more elder' is wrong: double comparative, and 'elder' still cannot take 'than'. D) 'older to me' is wrong: the verb 'is' is missing and comparatives take 'than', n

q: Choose the correct sentence.
f: B is right: 'hardly' is already negative, so we pair it with 'ever': 'hardly ever complains' (almost never). A) 'hardly never' is wrong: it is a double negative. C) 'ever hardly never' is wrong: wrong order and double negative. D) 'hardly complains never' is wrong: double negative and 'never' is in

q: "Feasible" means:
f: A is right: feasible means possible and practical to do. B) 'illegal' is wrong: that means against the law. C) 'dangerous only' is wrong: that means risky, not about possibility. D) 'impossible' is wrong: it is the opposite.

q: Choose the antonym of TROUBLE.
f: Here trouble is a verb meaning to disturb or worry someone; its opposite is Appease (calm or soothe). A) Disturb, B) Annoy and C) Worry are wrong: they all mean the same as trouble.

q: Choose the antonym of EXCESS.
f: Excess means more than needed; its opposite is Scarcity (too little). A) Surplus, B) Abundance and D) Plenty are wrong: they all mean a large amount, like excess.

q: Choose the correct article: "He is ___ honest man."
f: The h in 'honest' is silent, so the word begins with a vowel sound (on-est) and takes 'an'. A) 'a' is wrong: 'a' is for consonant sounds. C) 'the' is wrong: the man is not a specific one already known. D) is wrong: a singular countable noun needs an article.

q: Which sentence is correct?
f: Games and sports used in general take no article, so 'He plays cricket' is correct. A) is wrong: 'the cricket' is not used for the game. C) is wrong: 'a cricket' means an insect. D) is wrong: 'an' is used only before vowel sounds, and no article is needed anyway.

q: "___ Himalayas lie north of Pakistan."
f: Names of mountain ranges (plural) take 'the', so 'The Himalayas'. A) 'A' and B) 'An' are wrong: these are for one non-specific thing. D) is wrong: plural names of ranges are not used without 'the'.

q: Active form of "The gate was opened by the guard" is:
o: The guard was opening by the gate.
f: In the passive, 'was opened' is simple past, so the active is simple past: The guard opened the gate. B) 'opens' is present tense, wrong tense. C) swaps doer and object, so the gate opens the guard, which is nonsense. D) is wrong: 'was opening by' is not a correct active form and the meaning is reve

q: Mother said, "Do not waste time."
o: Mother advised me not to waste time.
Mother said me do not waste time.
Mother told that not waste time.
f: Advice or a negative imperative is reported with 'advised' + object + 'not to' + verb: Mother advised me not to waste time. B) 'said me' is wrong and keeps 'do not'. C) 'told that' needs an object and 'that' is wrong for imperatives. D) 'advised not wasting me' has wrong word order and form.

q: Synonym of "obstacle" is:
f: 'Obstacle' means something that blocks your way, so 'hindrance' is the synonym. B) 'benefit' means an advantage, the opposite idea. C) 'reward' is something given for good work. D) 'solution' is the answer to a problem.

q: "When I was a child, I ___ cricket every evening."
f: 'When I was a child' places the habit in the finished past, so simple past 'played' is correct. A) 'play' is wrong: it is present. C) 'have played' is wrong: present perfect does not go with a finished past time. D) 'am playing' is wrong: it shows action happening now.

q: The correct collocation is:
f: B is right: the verb 'depend' is always followed by 'on'. A) 'depend of' is a common mistake. C) 'depend at' is wrong. D) 'depend to' is wrong.

q: Choose the antonym of NERVOUS.
f: Nervous means worried and afraid; its opposite is Bold (brave, confident). A) Anxious and B) Restless are wrong: they mean worried or uneasy, like nervous. C) Timid is wrong: it means shy and fearful, also close to nervous.

q: Complete: "___ he was inexperienced, he learned quickly."
f: A is right: 'although' joins two clauses that show contrast: he was inexperienced, but he learned quickly. B) 'because of' needs a noun (because of his inexperience) and shows reason, not contrast. C) 'unless' means 'if not' and gives no sense. D) 'therefore' shows result and cannot start the first

q: Read the passage: Pressure narrows attention. This can be useful when a task demands immediate focus, but it can also make a person overlook information that would normally be considered. Good decision makers therefore use simple structures under stress: they identify the objective, separate facts from assumptions, compare the most realistic options, and consider the likely consequences of each. They also know when time is too limited for perfect information. In such cases, the goal is not certainty but a reasonable decision based on the best available evidence. Afterward, reviewing the outcome helps improve future judgment.  QUESTION: The tone of the passage is primarily:
f: A is right: the passage calmly explains steps for making decisions, so its tone is instructional and analytical. B) 'comic' is wrong: there is no humour. C) 'angry' is wrong: there is no strong emotion. D) 'nostalgic' is wrong: it does not long for the past.

q: Choose the antonym of TENDENCY.
f: Tendency means a natural leaning to do something; its opposite is Disinclination (unwillingness). B) Habit, C) Leaning and D) Inclination are wrong: they are all close in meaning to tendency.

q: "She ___ the report before the meeting began."
f: A is right: the reading finished before the meeting began (both in the past), so we use the past perfect 'had read'. B) 'has read tomorrow' mixes present perfect with a future word. C) 'reads yesterday' mixes present tense with a past word. D) 'is read' is a present passive and gives the wrong meani

q: The cadet trained daily ___ he wanted to improve his endurance.
f: A is right: the second part gives the reason for training, so 'because' fits. B) 'although' is wrong: it shows contrast, but there is no contrast here. C) 'unless' is wrong: it means 'if not', which makes no sense. D) 'whereas' is wrong: it compares two opposite facts.

q: No sooner had the bell rung ___ the candidates entered.
f: B is right: 'No sooner' is always followed by 'than': No sooner had ... than. A) 'when' is wrong: 'when' goes with 'hardly' or 'scarcely'. C) 'then' is wrong: it is about time, not this fixed pair. D) 'that' is wrong: it is not part of this pattern.

q: "If he studies hard, he ___ the test."
f: This is a first conditional (a real, possible future): if + simple present, then will + base verb, so 'will pass'. A) 'passes' is wrong: the result clause needs 'will'. B) 'passed' is wrong: past does not fit a present-tense condition. D) 'would pass' is wrong: it is used in the second conditional (

q: Choose the antonym of PUNCTUAL.
f: Punctual means arriving on time; its opposite is Unpunctual (late, not on time). A) Regular and D) Careful are wrong: they are not opposites of punctual. B) Prompt is wrong: it is a synonym (on time).

q: Choose the antonym of ACHIEVEMENT.
f: Achievement means success in doing something; its opposite is Failure. A) Accomplishment, B) Attainment and C) Success are wrong: they all mean achievement.

q: "This is ___ same book that I borrowed."
f: 'Same' is always used with 'the': 'the same book'. A) 'a' and B) 'an' are wrong: 'a same' or 'an same' is incorrect English. D) is wrong: 'same' cannot be used without 'the' before it.

q: Choose the synonym of URGE.
f: Urge means to push or strongly encourage; its synonym is Incite (stir up, provoke to action). A) Discourage, B) Deter and C) Restrain are wrong: they mean to stop or hold back, the opposite.

q: In "Ali and Hamza trained together," "and" is a:
f: 'And' joins two words of equal rank (Ali and Hamza), so it is a coordinating conjunction. B) preposition is wrong: it does not show relation of place or time. C) adjective is wrong: it describes nothing. D) adverb is wrong: it does not modify a verb.

q: Choose the antonym of ATTRACTION.
f: Attraction means a pull towards something; its opposite is Repulsion (pushing away, strong dislike). B) Appeal, C) Allure and D) Charm are wrong: they all mean attraction.

q: Choose the antonym of EFFICIENCY.
f: Efficiency means doing work well without waste; its opposite is Inefficiency. A) Skill, B) Competence and C) Capability are wrong: they are close in meaning to efficiency.

q: Choose the synonym of NERVOUS.
f: Nervous means fearful and worried; its synonym is Timorous (full of fear). A) Bold, B) Calm and D) Brave are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.

q: If I had known, I ___ you.
f: B is right: third conditional: If + had + past participle, would have + past participle: 'would have told'. A) 'would tell' is wrong: that is second conditional, for present unreal. C) 'will tell' is wrong: that is first conditional, for real future. D) 'told' is wrong: the result part needs 'would

q: "Vigilant" means:
f: A is right: vigilant means alert and watchful, especially for danger. B) 'sleepy' is wrong: it is almost the opposite (drowsy). C) 'careless' is wrong: it is the opposite of watchful. D) 'weak' is wrong: that means feeble.

q: Choose the synonym of SCOLD.
f: Scold means to speak angrily to someone for doing wrong; its synonym is Reprove. A) Praise, B) Commend and D) Flatter are wrong: they all mean saying good things, the opposite.

q: Antonym of "hostile" is:
f: 'Hostile' means unfriendly and showing enmity, so the antonym is 'friendly'. A) 'unfriendly' is a synonym. B) 'aggressive' is close to hostile, not opposite. D) 'angry' is also close, not opposite.

q: Choose the synonym of GODLY.
f: Godly means religious and devoted to God; its synonym is Pious. B) Wicked, C) Irreligious and D) Sinful are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.

q: She said, "I can swim."
o: She said that she could swim.
She said that she can swam.
She told that I could swim.
f: 'Can' changes to 'could', and 'I' changes to 'she': She said that she could swim. B) keeps 'can' and uses 'swam'; after a modal use the base form 'swim'. C) 'told that' needs an object and keeps 'I'. D) 'could swam' is wrong; after 'could' use 'swim'.

q: "He was accused ___ theft."
f: The fixed phrase is 'accused of' a crime. A) 'for' is wrong: 'accused for' is a common mistake. C) 'with' is wrong: we say 'charged with' theft, not 'accused with'. D) 'by' is wrong: 'by' shows who accused him (accused by the police).

q: "He ___ to Lahore last week."
f: 'Last week' is a finished past time, so simple past 'went' is correct. A) 'has gone' is wrong: present perfect cannot be used with a definite past time. B) 'goes' is wrong: it is present. D) 'had go' is wrong: the past participle is 'gone', and past perfect is not needed.

q: Passive of "They had finished the work" is:
f: Past perfect active (had finished) becomes 'had been + past participle': The work had been finished. B) 'has been finished' is present perfect, wrong tense. C) 'was finishing' is past continuous active. D) 'had finished them' is active and reverses the meaning.

q: Choose the antonym of PROGRESS.
f: Progress means moving forward; its opposite is Retrogress (go backward). A) Develop, C) Proceed and D) Advance are wrong: they all mean moving forward, like progress.

q: In "She worked despite the rain," "despite" is a:
f: "Despite" comes before the noun phrase "the rain" and shows its relation to the verb "worked", so it is a preposition. B) It is not a pronoun: it does not stand in place of a noun. C) It is not an interjection: it shows no sudden emotion. D) It is not an adverb of manner: it does not tell how she wo

q: Indirect: "Do not touch the switch," he said to us.
o: He warned us not to touch the switch.
He said us do not touch.
He asked that we not touched.
f: A is right: a negative command in reported speech uses 'not to' + verb, and 'warned' suits a caution: He warned us not to touch the switch. B) 'said us' is wrong ('said to us') and the command form is not changed. C) 'asked that we not touched' is wrong grammar. D) 'told not touch us' has wrong word

q: Choose the synonym of EMPTY.
f: Empty means containing nothing; its synonym is Vacant. A) Crowded, B) Full and C) Occupied are wrong: they mean filled, the opposite.

q: In "He can swim well," "can" is a:
f: 'Can' helps the main verb 'swim' and shows ability, so it is a modal auxiliary. A) main verb is wrong: the main verb is 'swim'. C) noun is wrong: here 'can' is not a tin container. D) preposition is wrong: it shows no relation of place or time.

q: In which Surah does Bismillah occur twice?
f: A) is right: In Surah An-Naml, Bismillah comes at the start and also inside, in the letter of Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) to Queen Bilqees. B) Al-Baqarah has Bismillah only at the start. C) Surah At-Tauba has no Bismillah at its start. D) Al-Fatiha has Bismillah only once.

q: In which year of Hijri did the Holy Prophet PBUH send letters to kings inviting them to Islam?
f: D) 7 AH is right. The letters to kings were sent at the end of 6 AH and in 7 AH. A) 2 AH is wrong: that is the year of Badr. B) 4 AH is wrong: that is the year of Rajih. C) 10 AH is wrong: that is the year of Hajjat-ul-Wida.

q: What was the religion of Najashi, the king of Habsha, before Islam?
f: D) Christianity is right. Najashi was a Christian king who gave shelter to the Muslims. A) Judaism is wrong: he was not a Jew. B) Fire worship (Majoosi) is wrong: that was the religion of Persia. C) Idol worship is wrong: that was the religion of the Quraish.

q: Which companion of the Holy Prophet PBUH is mentioned by name in the Holy Quran?
f: D) is right: Hazrat Zaid (RA) is the only companion named in the Quran (Surah Al-Ahzab). A) Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) is referred to (companion in the cave) but not by name. B) Hazrat Umar (RA) is not named in the Quran. C) Hazrat Ali (RA) is not named in the Quran.

q: Hazrat Saleh (AS) was sent to which nation?
f: D) Samood is right. Hazrat Saleh (AS) was sent to the nation of Samood. A) Aad is wrong: Hazrat Hood (AS) was sent to Aad. B) Bani Israel is wrong: Hazrat Moosa (AS) was sent to Bani Israel. C) Ahl-e-Madyan is wrong: Hazrat Shoaib (AS) was sent to Madyan.

q: The first revelation came to the Holy Prophet PBUH in which cave?
f: A) is right: The first revelation came in Cave Hira on Jabal-e-Noor. B) There is no such revelation cave; Uhud is a mountain of a battle. C) Cave Saur is where the Holy Prophet PBUH hid during Hijrat. D) That is the cave of the sleepers in Surah Al-Kahf.

q: Hajj was made compulsory in which year?
f: B) is right: Hajj was made Farz in 9 AH. A) 2 AH is the year of fasting and Zakat. C) 10 AH is the year of Hajjat-ul-Wida (Last Hajj). D) 8 AH is the year of Conquest of Makkah.

q: Ghazwa Hunain was fought in which year of Hijri?
f: D) 8 AH is right. Ghazwa Hunain was fought in 8 AH, soon after the Conquest of Makkah. A) 3 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Uhud. B) 5 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Khandaq. C) 9 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Tabuk.

q: Which prophet is called Abu-al-Arab (father of the Arabs)?
f: B) Hazrat Ismail (AS) is right. Hazrat Ismail (AS) is called Abu-al-Arab. A) Hazrat Ishaq (AS) is wrong: he is the ancestor of Bani Israel. C) Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is wrong: he is called Abu-al-Anbiya (father of prophets). D) Hazrat Hood (AS) is wrong: he was sent to Aad.

q: Masjid Zarrar was demolished in which year of Hijri?
f: A) 9 AH is right. Masjid Zarrar, built by the hypocrites, was demolished in 9 AH after Tabuk. B) 3 AH is wrong: that is the year of Uhud. C) 6 AH is wrong: that is the year of Hudaibiya. D) 11 AH is wrong: the Holy Prophet PBUH passed away in this year.

q: Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accepted Islam in which year of Hijri?
f: C) 8 AH is right. Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accepted Islam in 8 AH, before the Conquest of Makkah. A) 6 AH is wrong: that is the year of Sulah Hudaibiya. B) 5 AH is wrong: that is the year of Ghazwa Khandaq. D) 3 AH is wrong: in 3 AH he fought against the Muslims at Uhud.

q: The Nikah of Hazrat Fatima (RA) with Hazrat Ali (RA) took place in which year of Hijri?
f: D) 2 AH is right. The Nikah of Hazrat Fatima (RA) and Hazrat Ali (RA) took place in 2 AH. A) 5 AH is wrong: that is the year of the Nikah of Hazrat Zainab bint Jahsh (RA). B) 7 AH is wrong: that is the year of Khaibar. C) 9 AH is wrong: that is the year of Tabuk.

q: The second migration to Habsha (Abyssinia) took place in:
f: C) 616 AD is right. The second migration to Habsha took place in 616 AD. A) 615 AD is wrong: this is the year of the first migration. B) 610 AD is wrong: this is the year of the first revelation. D) 622 AD is wrong: this is the year of Hijrat to Madina.

q: Masjid Qiblatain (mosque of two Qiblas) is located in:
f: C) Madina is right. Masjid Qiblatain is in Madina, where the order to change the Qibla came. A) Makkah is wrong: it is not in Makkah. B) Taif is wrong: it is not in Taif. D) Bait-ul-Muqaddas is wrong: that was the first Qibla, not this mosque.

q: Ghazwa Tabuk was against which power?
f: B) The Romans (Byzantine Empire) is right. Ghazwa Tabuk (9 AH) was against the Romans (Byzantine Empire). A) The Egyptians is wrong: Egypt was not the enemy at Tabuk. C) The Persians is wrong: the Persians were not the enemy at Tabuk. D) The Quraish of Makkah is wrong: Makkah had already been conque

q: How many Ayats (verses) are there in the Holy Quran?
f: C) is right: The commonly accepted count of Ayats in the Holy Quran is 6236. A) 6348 is wrong; it is not the accepted count. B) 6666 is a popular but wrong number. D) 6000 is wrong; it is only a round figure.

q: When does the pilgrim stop reciting Talbiyah?
o: At the first Rami (10th Zil Hajj)
f: B) is right: Talbiyah stops when the pilgrim starts the first Rami of Jamrat-ul-Aqabah on 10th Zil Hajj. A) Talbiyah continues during Arafat. C) Talbiyah starts on entering Ihram; it does not stop then. D) Talbiyah has already stopped long before Tawaf-e-Wida.

q: What was the real name of Iblees?
f: D) Azazeel is right. The real name of Iblees was Azazeel. A) Haroot is wrong: Haroot and Maroot were two angels in Babylon. B) Qabeel is wrong: he was a son of Adam (AS). C) Samri is wrong: he made the calf in the time of Moosa (AS).

q: Ghazwa Uhud was fought in which year of Hijri?
f: A) 3 AH is right. Ghazwa Uhud was fought in 3 AH, in Shawwal. B) 2 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Badr. C) 5 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Khandaq. D) 7 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Khaibar.

q: Which of the following Surahs is NOT named after a Prophet?
f: A) is right: Hazrat Maryam was a pious lady, not a Prophet, so Surah Maryam is not named after a Prophet. B) Surah Younis is named after Hazrat Younis (AS), a Prophet. C) Surah Hood is named after Hazrat Hood (AS), a Prophet. D) Surah Ibrahim is named after Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), a Prophet.

q: The tragedy of Karbala took place in which year of Hijri?
f: C) 61 AH is right. The tragedy of Karbala took place in 61 AH. A) 11 AH is wrong: that is the year the Holy Prophet PBUH passed away. B) 40 AH is wrong: that is the year Hazrat Ali (RA) was martyred. D) 35 AH is wrong: that is the year Hazrat Usman (RA) was martyred.

q: The event of Mubahila with the Christians of Najran took place in which year of Hijri?
f: D) 10 AH is right. The Mubahila with the Christians of Najran is placed in 10 AH. A) 3 AH is wrong: that is the year of Uhud. B) 5 AH is wrong: that is the year of Khandaq. C) 7 AH is wrong: that is the year of Khaibar.

q: Which angel is in charge of rain and sustenance (Rizq)?
f: B) is right: Hazrat Mikail (AS) is in charge of rain and sustenance. A) Izrail (AS) takes the souls. C) Israfeel (AS) blows the trumpet. D) Jibrail (AS) brought revelation.

q: In which year of Hijri was Ghazwa Waddan (Abwa), the first Ghazwa, fought?
f: C) 2 AH is right. Ghazwa Waddan (Abwa) was fought in Safar 2 AH. A) 3 AH is wrong: that is the year of Ghazwa Uhud. B) 4 AH is wrong: that is the year of the Rajih incident. D) 5 AH is wrong: that is the year of Ghazwa Khandaq.

q: The siege of Taif took place in which year of Hijri?
f: C) 8 AH is right. The siege of Taif came right after Ghazwa Hunain in 8 AH. A) 2 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Badr. B) 4 AH is wrong: that is the Rajih incident. D) 6 AH is wrong: that is Sulah Hudaibiya.

q: On which date was Ghazwa Badr fought?
f: B) 17th Ramadan is right. Ghazwa Badr was fought on 17th Ramadan, 2 AH. A) 7th Shawwal is wrong: this is the date of Ghazwa Uhud (3 AH). C) 10th Muharram is wrong: this is the day of Ashura and Karbala. D) 9th Zil Hajj is wrong: this is the day of Arafat in Hajj.

q: Ghazwa Khandaq is also known as:
f: B) Ghazwa Ahzab is right. Ghazwa Khandaq is also called Ghazwa Ahzab (the Battle of the Confederates). A) Ghazwa Hunain is wrong: Hunain was a separate battle in 8 AH. C) Ghazwa Tabuk is wrong: Tabuk was a separate expedition in 9 AH. D) Ghazwa Mutah is wrong: Mutah was a separate battle in 8 AH.

q: Which was the first revelation (Wahi) of the Holy Quran?
f: B) is right: The first revelation was the first five Ayats of Surah Al-Alaq (Iqra). A) Al-Fatiha is the first Surah in order of the Mushaf, not the first revealed. C) Al-Baqarah is a Madani Surah revealed much later. D) Al-Muddassir came after the gap in revelation, not first.

q: Which event is called Fath-e-Mubeen (a clear victory) in the Quran?
f: B) Sulah Hudaibiya is right. Sulah Hudaibiya (6 AH) is called Fath-e-Mubeen in Surah Al-Fath. A) Ghazwa Badr is wrong: Badr is called Yaum-ul-Furqan. C) Ghazwa Khaibar is wrong: Khaibar is not given this title. D) Ghazwa Hunain is wrong: Hunain is not given this title.

q: Fasting in Ramadan was made Farz in which year of Hijri?
f: D) 2 AH is right. Fasting in Ramadan became Farz in 2 AH. A) 1 AH is wrong: that is the year of the first Azan. B) 3 AH is wrong: that is the year of Uhud. C) 5 AH is wrong: that is the year of Khandaq.

q: King Namrood was killed by:
f: C) A mosquito is right. A mosquito entered the nose of Namrood and caused his death. A) Drowning in the sea is wrong: that was the end of Firaun. B) Birds with stones is wrong: that was the end of Abraha's army. D) A windstorm is wrong: that was the end of the nation of Aad.

q: Hajjat-ul-Wida (the Farewell Hajj) was performed in which year of Hijri?
f: C) 10 AH is right. The Holy Prophet PBUH performed Hajjat-ul-Wida in 10 AH. A) 8 AH is wrong: that is the Conquest of Makkah. B) 9 AH is wrong: in 9 AH Hazrat Abu Bakar (RA) led the Hajj. D) 11 AH is wrong: the Holy Prophet PBUH passed away in this year.

q: Banu Quraiza were punished for their treachery in which year of Hijri?
