f: A) 5 AH is right. Banu Quraiza were dealt with in 5 AH, right after Ghazwa Khandaq. B) 2 AH is wrong: that is the year of Badr. C) 7 AH is wrong: that is the year of Khaibar. D) 9 AH is wrong: that is the year of Tabuk.

q: In Hajj, stoning the devil (Shaitan) is called:
f: B) Rami is right. Stoning the devil is called Rami. A) Istilam is wrong: it is touching the Black Stone. C) Saee is wrong: it is walking between Safa and Marwa. D) Tawaf is wrong: it is going around the Kaaba.

q: Which was the first Ghazwa of the Holy Prophet PBUH?
f: A) Ghazwa Waddan (Abwa) is right. Ghazwa Waddan (also called Abwa) was the first Ghazwa, in Safar 2 AH. B) Ghazwa Badr is wrong: it came later, in Ramadan 2 AH, and was the first big battle. C) Ghazwa Uhud is wrong: it was fought in 3 AH. D) Ghazwa Khandaq is wrong: it was fought in 5 AH.

q: Which of the following is one of the 3 Farz of Hajj?
f: C) is right: The 3 Farz of Hajj are Ihram, Wuquf-e-Arafat and Tawaf-e-Ziarat. A) Rami is Wajib, not Farz. B) Saee is Wajib, not Farz. D) Tawaf-e-Wida (farewell) is Wajib, not Farz.

q: What was the title of Hazrat Yaqoob (AS)?
f: B) Israel is right. Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) is called Israel, so his children are Bani Israel. A) Kaleemullah is wrong: it is the title of Moosa (AS). C) Ruhullah is wrong: it is the title of Essa (AS). D) Khaleelullah is wrong: it is the title of Ibrahim (AS).

q: How many rounds of Saee are made between Safa and Marwa?
f: A) 7 is right. Saee has 7 rounds between Safa and Marwa. B) 5 is wrong: this is not the number. C) 3 is wrong: this is not the number. D) 9 is wrong: this is not the number.

q: What is the Rukn-e-Azam (greatest pillar) of Hajj?
f: C) is right: Wuquf-e-Arafat on 9th Zil Hajj is the greatest pillar; without it Hajj is not valid. A) Rami is Wajib, not the greatest pillar. B) Saee is Wajib. D) Stay at Muzdalifa is Wajib.

q: In Hajj, what is Istilam?
o: Touching or kissing the Black Stone
f: C) Touching or kissing the Black Stone is right. Istilam means touching or kissing the Hajr-e-Aswad (Black Stone). A) Stoning the devil is wrong: this is called Rami. B) Walking between Safa and Marwa is wrong: this is called Saee. D) Staying at Arafat is wrong: this is called Wuquf.

q: Who killed Marhab the Jew in Ghazwa Khaibar?
f: B) Hazrat Ali (RA) is right. Hazrat Ali (RA) killed Marhab in Khaibar (7 AH). A) Hazrat Hamza (RA) is wrong: he was martyred at Uhud in 3 AH. C) Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) is wrong: he was not yet a Muslim in 7 AH. D) Hazrat Umar (RA) is wrong: he did not kill Marhab.

q: The Conquest of Makkah (Fath Makkah) took place in which year of Hijri?
f: C) 8 AH is right. Makkah was conquered in Ramadan 8 AH. A) 6 AH is wrong: that is Sulah Hudaibiya. B) 7 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Khaibar. D) 10 AH is wrong: that is Hajjat-ul-Wida.

q: How many Surahs of the Holy Quran are named after Prophets?
f: B) is right: Six Surahs are named after Prophets: Yousaf, Hood, Younis, Ibrahim, Nooh and Muhammad. A) 8 is wrong; only six Surahs carry a Prophet's name. C) 25 is the number of Prophets mentioned by name in the Quran. D) 4 is wrong; there are six such Surahs.

q: How many Muslims took part in Ghazwa Badr?
f: A) 313 is right. 313 Muslims fought against about 1000 men of the Quraish at Badr. B) 1000 is wrong: this was the size of the Quraish army. C) 700 is wrong: this is close to the Muslim number at Uhud. D) 1400 is wrong: this is the number of companions at Hudaibiya.

q: Who killed Abu Jahl in Ghazwa Badr?
f: A) Hazrat Muaz (RA) and Hazrat Muawwaz (RA) is right. Two young brothers, Hazrat Muaz (RA) and Hazrat Muawwaz (RA), killed Abu Jahl at Badr. B) Hazrat Ali (RA) is wrong: he killed Marhab at Khaibar. C) Hazrat Hamza (RA) is wrong: he was a hero of Badr but did not kill Abu Jahl. D) Hazrat Khalid bin

q: The orders of Wudu, Ghusl and Tayammum are given in which Surah?
f: C) is right: Surah Al-Maida (Ayat 6) gives the orders of Wudu, Ghusl and Tayammum. A) Al-Baqarah has orders of fasting, not the Wudu Ayat. B) Surah Yaseen is the heart of the Quran; no Wudu orders. D) Al-Imran has the order of Hajj.

q: How many Madani Surahs are there in the Holy Quran?
f: A) is right: There are 28 Madani Surahs (revealed after Hijrat). B) 86 is the number of Makki Surahs. C) 14 is the number of Sajdas. D) 30 is the number of Paras.

q: To which prophet were 30 Sahifas given?
f: A) Hazrat Idrees (AS) is right. Hazrat Idrees (AS) was given 30 Sahifas. B) Hazrat Sheeth (AS) is wrong: he was given 50 Sahifas. C) Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is wrong: he was given 10 Sahifas. D) Hazrat Adam (AS) is wrong: he was given 10 Sahifas.

q: The third Ashra (last ten days) of Ramadan is the Ashra of:
f: A) Nijat (freedom from Hell) is right. The third Ashra of Ramadan is Nijat (freedom from Hell). B) Rehmat (mercy) is wrong: it is the first Ashra. C) Maghfirat (forgiveness) is wrong: it is the second Ashra. D) Sabr (patience) is wrong: it is not the name of an Ashra.

q: Which angel will blow the trumpet (Soor) on the Day of Judgement?
f: C) is right: Hazrat Israfeel (AS) will blow the trumpet. A) Izrail (AS) takes the souls. B) Mikail (AS) brings rain and sustenance. D) Jibrail (AS) brought revelation.

q: Salat-ul-Khauf (the prayer of fear) was introduced in which year of Hijri?
f: C) 4 AH is right. Salat-ul-Khauf was introduced in 4 AH. A) 1 AH is wrong: that is the year of the first Azan. B) 6 AH is wrong: that is the year of Hudaibiya. D) 8 AH is wrong: that is the year of Fath Makkah.

q: Sulah Hudaibiya and Bait-e-Rizwan took place in which year of Hijri?
f: B) 6 AH is right. Both Sulah Hudaibiya and Bait-e-Rizwan took place in 6 AH. A) 5 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Khandaq. C) 7 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Khaibar. D) 8 AH is wrong: that is the Conquest of Makkah.

q: The nation of Hazrat Hood (AS) was destroyed by:
f: A) A violent windstorm is right. The nation of Hazrat Hood (AS), Aad, was destroyed by a violent windstorm for 7 nights and 8 days. B) A rain of stones is wrong: that was the punishment of the nation of Lut (AS). C) A great flood is wrong: that was the punishment of the nation of Nooh (AS). D) A mig

q: The order of Hajj is given in which Surah?
f: D) is right: Surah Al-Imran (Ayat 97) makes Hajj Farz on those who can afford it. A) Surah Yaseen is the heart of the Quran. B) At-Tauba mentions Masjid-e-Quba. C) Al-Maida gives orders of Wudu, Ghusl and Tayammum.

q: Who was made Ameer-e-Hajj in 9 AH?
f: A) Hazrat Abu Bakar (RA) is right. Hazrat Abu Bakar (RA) led the Hajj as Ameer-e-Hajj in 9 AH. B) Hazrat Umar (RA) is wrong: he was not the Ameer-e-Hajj in 9 AH. C) Hazrat Usman (RA) is wrong: he was not the Ameer-e-Hajj in 9 AH. D) Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) is wrong: he was a general, not the A

q: Zakat was made Farz in which year of Hijri?
f: C) 2 AH is right. Zakat was made Farz in 2 AH. A) 4 AH is wrong: that is the year of Rajih. B) 6 AH is wrong: that is the year of Hudaibiya. D) 8 AH is wrong: that is the year of Fath Makkah.

q: Hazrat Moosa (AS) and Hazrat Haroon (AS) were:
f: C) Brothers is right. Hazrat Moosa (AS) and Hazrat Haroon (AS) were brothers. A) Father and son is wrong: they were brothers, not father and son. B) Uncle and nephew is wrong: they were brothers. D) Cousins is wrong: they were real brothers.

q: How many doors does Jannat (Heaven) have?
f: A) 8 is right. Jannat has 8 doors, while Jahannam (Hell) has 7 doors. B) 7 is wrong: this is the number of doors of Hell. C) 6 is wrong: this is not the number. D) 10 is wrong: this is not the number.

q: How many Paras (Juz) are there in the Holy Quran?
f: C) is right: The Holy Quran is divided into 30 Paras so it can be read in a month. A) 114 is the number of Surahs, not Paras. B) 40 is wrong; there are 30 Paras. D) 28 is the number of Madani Surahs, not Paras.

q: How many major heavenly books were revealed?
f: D) 4 is right. Four major books were revealed: Taurat, Zaboor, Injeel and the Quran. A) 3 is wrong: one book would be missing. B) 5 is wrong: there are only four. C) 100 is wrong: this is the number of Sahifas.

q: Which angel brought the revelation (Wahi) to the Prophets?
f: C) is right: Hazrat Jibrail (AS) brought revelation to the Prophets. A) Izrail (AS) takes the souls. B) Mikail (AS) brings rain and sustenance. D) Israfeel (AS) blows the trumpet.

q: Which companion was born inside the Khana Kaaba?
f: A) Hazrat Ali (RA) is right. Hazrat Ali (RA) was born inside the Khana Kaaba. B) Hazrat Abu Bakar (RA) is wrong: he was not born in the Kaaba. C) Hazrat Umar (RA) is wrong: he was not born in the Kaaba. D) Hazrat Usman (RA) is wrong: he was not born in the Kaaba.

q: In how much time was the Holy Quran completely revealed?
f: A) is right: The revelation was completed in about 22 years, 5 months and 14 days (about 23 years). B) 40 years was the age of the Holy Prophet PBUH at the first revelation. C) 13 years is the Makki period only. D) 10 years is the Madani period only.

q: The first Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid-ul-Adha were celebrated in which year of Hijri?
f: D) 2 AH is right. The first Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid-ul-Adha were celebrated in 2 AH. A) 1 AH is wrong: that is the year of the first Azan. B) 3 AH is wrong: that is the year of Uhud. C) 7 AH is wrong: that is the year of Khaibar.

q: Masjid-e-Quba is mentioned in which Surah?
f: C) is right: Surah At-Tauba (Ayat 108) refers to Masjid-e-Quba, the mosque founded on Taqwa. A) Al-Fatiha mentions no mosque. B) Al-Kausar is about the fountain of Kausar. D) An-Naml is about Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) and the ant.

q: Which land is known as the Land of Prophets?
f: B) Palestine is right. Palestine (Sham region) is called the Land of Prophets. A) Egypt is wrong: it is not given this title. C) Iraq is wrong: it is not given this title. D) Yemen is wrong: it is not given this title.

q: Which Surah is called the "Heart of the Quran"?
f: D) is right: Hadith calls Surah Yaseen the heart of the Quran. A) Al-Ikhlas is equal to one-third of the Quran. B) Al-Fatiha is called Umm-ul-Kitab (Mother of the Book). C) Surah Rahman is called the bride (Uroos) of the Quran.

q: The Holy Prophet PBUH passed away in which year of Hijri?
f: C) 11 AH is right. The Holy Prophet PBUH passed away in 11 AH. A) 9 AH is wrong: that is the year of Tabuk. B) 10 AH is wrong: that is the year of Hajjat-ul-Wida. D) 13 AH is wrong: that is the year Hazrat Abu Bakar (RA) passed away.

q: What was the profession of Hazrat Abu Bakar (RA) before the Khilafat?
f: A) Cloth merchant is right. Hazrat Abu Bakar (RA) was a cloth merchant. B) Farmer is wrong: he was a trader, not a farmer. C) Blacksmith is wrong: he did not work as a blacksmith. D) Shepherd is wrong: he was a merchant, not a shepherd.

q: Which is the longest Surah of the Holy Quran?
f: C) is right: Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest Surah with 286 Ayats. A) Surah Al-Imran is the third Surah and shorter (200 Ayats). B) Surah Yaseen is called the heart of the Quran, not the longest. D) Surah An-Nisa is long (176 Ayats) but not the longest.

q: Which is the first compiled book of Hadith?
f: A) Muwatta Imam Malik is right. Muwatta Imam Malik is the first compiled book of Hadith. B) Sahih Bukhari is wrong: it was compiled later by Imam Bukhari. C) Sahih Muslim is wrong: it was compiled later by Imam Muslim. D) Sunan Abu Dawood is wrong: it was compiled later.

q: Salat-ul-Kusuf is offered at the time of:
f: A) is right: Kusuf means solar eclipse; Salat-ul-Kusuf is offered then. B) Lunar eclipse is Khusuf; its prayer is Salat-ul-Khusuf. C) For drought, Salat-ul-Istisqa is offered. D) Earthquake is wrong: Kusuf means solar eclipse, not earthquake.

q: The first Ashra (ten days) of Ramadan is the Ashra of:
f: D) Rehmat (mercy) is right. The first Ashra of Ramadan is Rehmat (mercy). A) Maghfirat (forgiveness) is wrong: it is the second Ashra. B) Nijat (freedom from Hell) is wrong: it is the third Ashra. C) Barakat (blessing) is wrong: it is not the name of an Ashra.

q: How many Sajdas (prostrations of recitation) are there in the Holy Quran?
f: D) is right: There are 14 Sajdas of recitation in the Holy Quran (Hanafi view). A) 15 is the count of some other schools, not the common (Hanafi) count used in Pakistan. B) 12 is wrong; there are 14 Sajdas. C) 30 is the number of Paras, not Sajdas.

q: How many years did the Holy Prophet PBUH live in Madina after the Hijrat?
f: C) 10 years is right. The Holy Prophet PBUH lived 10 years in Madina (1 AH to 11 AH). A) 13 years is wrong: this is the time spent preaching in Makkah. B) 8 years is wrong: this is too short. D) 23 years is wrong: this is the whole period of Prophethood.

q: Which prophet is called Kaleemullah (one who spoke with Allah)?
f: C) Hazrat Moosa (AS) is right. Hazrat Moosa (AS) is called Kaleemullah. A) Hazrat Essa (AS) is wrong: he is called Ruhullah. B) Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is wrong: he is called Khaleelullah. D) Hazrat Adam (AS) is wrong: he is called Safiullah.

q: What is the rate of Ushr on land watered by rain?
f: B) is right: Ushr on rain-watered land is 1/10 of the produce. A) 1/20 is for land watered by irrigation (wells/tubewells). C) 1/40 (2.5 percent) is the rate of Zakat on wealth. D) 1/5 is Khums.

q: Which prophet was the first to write with a pen and to sew clothes?
f: C) Hazrat Idrees (AS) is right. Hazrat Idrees (AS) was the first to write with a pen and to sew clothes. A) Hazrat Adam (AS) is wrong: he was the first man, not the first writer. B) Hazrat Nooh (AS) is wrong: he is known for the Ark. D) Hazrat Dawood (AS) is wrong: he is known for making armour from

q: According to Sahih Bukhari, what was the height of Hazrat Adam (AS)?
f: B) 60 cubits (about 90 feet) is right. Sahih Bukhari says Hazrat Adam (AS) was 60 cubits tall, which is about 90 feet. A) 40 cubits (about 60 feet) is wrong: this is not the number in the Hadith. C) 30 cubits (about 45 feet) is wrong: this is not the number in the Hadith. D) 100 cubits (about 150 fe

q: Cave Hira is located in which mountain?
f: A) Jabal-e-Noor is right. Cave Hira is in Jabal-e-Noor near Makkah. B) Jabal-e-Soor is wrong: it has Cave Soor. C) Mount Uhud is wrong: it is near Madina. D) Mount Judi is wrong: the Ark of Nooh (AS) rested there.

q: Masjid-e-Nabvi was built in which year of Hijri?
f: B) 1 AH is right. Masjid-e-Nabvi was built in 1 AH, soon after the Hijrat to Madina. A) 2 AH is wrong: that is the year the Qibla changed. C) 4 AH is wrong: that is the year of Rajih. D) 6 AH is wrong: that is the year of Hudaibiya.

q: Ghazwa Khandaq (Ahzab) was fought in which year of Hijri?
f: D) 5 AH is right. Ghazwa Khandaq, also called Ghazwa Ahzab, was fought in 5 AH. A) 3 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Uhud. B) 6 AH is wrong: that is Sulah Hudaibiya. C) 9 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Tabuk.

q: Wuquf-e-Arafat takes place on which date?
f: A) is right: Wuquf-e-Arafat is on 9th Zil Hajj. B) On 8th Zil Hajj pilgrims go to Mina. C) 12th Zil Hajj is a day of Rami at Mina. D) 10th Zil Hajj is Eid-ul-Adha (Rami, sacrifice, Tawaf-e-Ziarat).

q: Ghazwa Tabuk took place in which year of Hijri?
f: C) 9 AH is right. Ghazwa Tabuk took place in 9 AH and was the last Ghazwa of the Holy Prophet PBUH. A) 7 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Khaibar. B) 8 AH is wrong: that is the Conquest of Makkah. D) 11 AH is wrong: the Holy Prophet PBUH passed away in this year.

q: The first Juma prayer and Khutba was delivered by the Holy Prophet PBUH in:
f: C) 1 AH is right. The first Juma Khutba was delivered in 1 AH, at the time of Hijrat. A) 3 AH is wrong: that is the year of Uhud. B) 6 AH is wrong: that is the year of Hudaibiya. D) 8 AH is wrong: that is the year of Fath Makkah.

q: Tawaf-e-Ziarat is normally performed on which date?
f: B) is right: Tawaf-e-Ziarat is performed on 10th Zil Hajj (can be done till 12th). A) 8th is the day of going to Mina. C) 1st Zil Hajj is the start of the month, no Hajj rite. D) 9th is the day of Wuquf-e-Arafat.

q: The Holy Prophet PBUH married Hazrat Zainab bint Jahsh (RA) in which year of Hijri?
f: A) 5 AH is right. The Nikah with Hazrat Zainab bint Jahsh (RA) took place in 5 AH. B) 2 AH is wrong: that is the year of the Nikah of Hazrat Fatima (RA). C) 8 AH is wrong: that is the year of Fath Makkah. D) 10 AH is wrong: that is the year of Hajjat-ul-Wida.

q: Rami of Jamarat (stoning) is done at which place?
f: D) is right: Rami of Jamarat is done at Mina. A) Pebbles are collected at Muzdalifa, but Rami is at Mina. B) Safa Marwah is for Saee. C) Arafat is for Wuquf on 9th Zil Hajj.

q: How many basic pillars (foundations) of Islam are there?
f: A) is right: Islam has 5 pillars: Kalma, Namaz, Fasting, Zakat and Hajj. B) 4 is wrong; there are 5. C) 6 is the number of articles of faith (Iman-e-Mufassal). D) 3 is the number of Farz of Hajj.

q: Hazrat Yousaf (AS) was the son of:
f: B) Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) is right. Hazrat Yousaf (AS) was the son of Hazrat Yaqoob (AS). A) Hazrat Ishaq (AS) is wrong: he was the grandfather of Yousaf (AS). C) Hazrat Ismail (AS) is wrong: he was the brother of Ishaq (AS). D) Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is wrong: he was the great-grandfather of Yousaf (AS).

q: What is the minimum number of camels on which Zakat becomes due?
f: D) is right: Zakat on camels starts at 5 camels. A) 10 is wrong. B) 40 is the Nisab for goats. C) 30 is the Nisab for cows/buffaloes.

q: During the Hijrat, how many days did the Holy Prophet PBUH stay in Cave Soor?
f: D) 3 days is right. The Holy Prophet PBUH and Hazrat Abu Bakar (RA) stayed 3 days in Cave Soor. A) 7 days is wrong: this is not the correct period. B) 10 days is wrong: this is not the correct period. C) 1 day is wrong: they stayed longer than one day.

q: How was the nation of Hazrat Saleh (AS) (Samood) punished?
f: A) A mighty blast and earthquake is right. Samood was destroyed by a mighty blast (sayha) and an earthquake. B) A rain of stones is wrong: that was for the nation of Lut (AS). C) A great flood is wrong: that was for the nation of Nooh (AS). D) A windstorm of 7 nights is wrong: that was for Aad, the

q: Hazrat Abbas (RA) was the Holy Prophet's PBUH:
f: A) Uncle is right. Hazrat Abbas (RA) was the uncle of the Holy Prophet PBUH. B) Cousin is wrong: Hazrat Ali (RA) was a cousin. C) Grandfather is wrong: Abdul Muttalib was the grandfather. D) Son-in-law is wrong: Ali (RA) and Usman (RA) were sons-in-law.

q: What is the rate of Khums?
f: A) is right: Khums means one-fifth (1/5). B) 1/40 is Zakat on wealth. C) 1/20 is Ushr on irrigated land. D) 1/10 is Ushr on rain-watered land.

q: Ghazwa Bani Lihyan took place in which year of Hijri?
f: B) 6 AH is right. Ghazwa Bani Lihyan took place in 6 AH. A) 2 AH is wrong: that is the year of Badr. C) 3 AH is wrong: that is the year of Uhud. D) 9 AH is wrong: that is the year of Tabuk.

q: How many doors does Jahannam (Hell) have according to the Quran?
f: D) 7 is right. Jahannam has 7 doors (Surah Al-Hijr). A) 8 is wrong: this is the number of doors of Jannat. B) 5 is wrong: this is not the number. C) 9 is wrong: this is not the number.

q: Ghazwa Khaibar was fought in which year of Hijri?
f: A) 7 AH is right. Ghazwa Khaibar was fought in 7 AH. B) 5 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Khandaq. C) 6 AH is wrong: that is Sulah Hudaibiya. D) 9 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Tabuk.

q: Which angel takes the souls (Malak-ul-Maut)?
f: C) is right: Hazrat Izrail (AS), the angel of death, takes the souls. A) Israfeel (AS) blows the trumpet. B) Mikail (AS) brings rain and sustenance. D) Jibrail (AS) brought revelation.

q: On which mountain did the Ark of Hazrat Nooh (AS) come to rest?
f: C) Mount Judi is right. The Ark of Hazrat Nooh (AS) rested on Mount Judi (near the Turkey-Iraq border). A) Jabal-e-Noor is wrong: it has the Cave Hira. B) Mount Toor (Sinai) is wrong: it is linked with Hazrat Moosa (AS). D) Jabal-e-Soor is wrong: it has the Cave Soor of Hijrat.

q: Umrat-ul-Qaza was performed in which year of Hijri?
f: D) 7 AH is right. Umrat-ul-Qaza was performed in 7 AH, one year after Sulah Hudaibiya. A) 5 AH is wrong: that is the year of Khandaq. B) 9 AH is wrong: that is the year of Tabuk. C) 10 AH is wrong: that is the year of Hajjat-ul-Wida.

q: How many Sahifas were revealed in total?
f: D) 100 is right. In total 100 Sahifas were revealed: Sheeth 50, Idrees 30, Ibrahim 10, Adam 10. A) 30 is wrong: this is the number given to Idrees (AS). B) 50 is wrong: this is the number given to Sheeth (AS). C) 4 is wrong: this is the number of big heavenly books.

q: The incident of Rajih took place in which year of Hijri?
f: D) 4 AH is right. The incident of Rajih, when companions were martyred by treachery, was in 4 AH. A) 2 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Badr. B) 6 AH is wrong: that is Sulah Hudaibiya. C) 8 AH is wrong: that is the Conquest of Makkah.

q: Who were the wives of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS)?
f: C) Hazrat Sarah and Hazrat Hajra is right. Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) had two wives: Hazrat Sarah and Hazrat Hajra. A) Hazrat Asia and Hazrat Maryam is wrong: Asia was the wife of Firaun and Maryam was mother of Essa (AS). B) Hazrat Hawwa and Hazrat Sarah is wrong: Hawwa was the wife of Adam (AS). D) Hazra

q: What is the minimum number of cows/buffaloes on which Zakat becomes due?
f: C) is right: Zakat on cows and buffaloes starts at 30. A) 5 is the Nisab for camels. B) 10 is wrong. D) 40 is the Nisab for goats.

q: Iblees, before he disobeyed Allah, was known as the:
f: B) Teacher of the angels is right. Iblees (Azazeel) was known as the teacher of the angels. A) King of the jinn is wrong: he was not given this title. C) Guard of Jannat is wrong: the guard of Jannat is Rizwan. D) Guard of Jahannam is wrong: the guard of Jahannam is Malik.

q: Which was the first mosque (house of worship) in the world?
f: B) Khana Kaaba is right. Khana Kaaba was the first house of worship in the world. A) Masjid-e-Nabvi is wrong: it was built in 1 AH in Madina. C) Masjid-e-Aqsa is wrong: it was built after the Kaaba. D) Masjid-e-Quba is wrong: it was the first mosque built by the Holy Prophet PBUH.

q: What is the Nisab of Zakat for silver?
f: C) is right: The Nisab for silver is 52.5 tola. A) 40 tola is wrong. B) 7.5 tola is the Nisab for gold. D) 62.5 tola is wrong.

q: Which day is called Yaum-ul-Furqan (the Day of Distinction) in the Quran?
o: The day of the Conquest of Makkah
f: B) The day of Ghazwa Badr is right. The day of Ghazwa Badr is called Yaum-ul-Furqan because it separated truth from falsehood. A) The day of Ghazwa Uhud is wrong: Uhud is not given this title. C) The day of the Conquest of Makkah is wrong: it is known as Fath Makkah, not Yaum-ul-Furqan. D) The day o

q: The Battle of Mutah was fought in which year of Hijri?
f: D) 8 AH is right. The Battle of Mutah against the Romans was fought in 8 AH. A) 5 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Khandaq. B) 9 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Tabuk. C) 10 AH is wrong: that is Hajjat-ul-Wida.

q: Which prophet is called Ruhullah?
f: D) Hazrat Essa (AS) is right. Hazrat Essa (AS) is called Ruhullah. A) Hazrat Moosa (AS) is wrong: he is called Kaleemullah. B) Hazrat Nooh (AS) is wrong: he is called Najiullah. C) Hazrat Ismail (AS) is wrong: he is called Zabeehullah.

q: What is the rate of Ushr on land watered by irrigation (wells/tubewells)?
f: A) is right: On irrigated land Ushr is half, i.e. 1/20 of the produce. B) 1/40 is the rate of Zakat on wealth. C) 1/10 is for rain-watered land. D) 1/5 is Khums.

q: The Qibla was changed from Bait-ul-Muqaddas to Khana Kaaba in which year of Hijri?
f: A) 2 AH is right. The Qibla was changed in 2 AH. B) 1 AH is wrong: that is the year Masjid-e-Nabvi was built. C) 4 AH is wrong: that is the year of Rajih. D) 6 AH is wrong: that is the year of Hudaibiya.

q: How many Makki Surahs are there in the Holy Quran?
f: D) is right: There are 86 Makki Surahs (revealed before Hijrat). A) 28 is the number of Madani Surahs. B) 114 is the total number of Surahs. C) 90 is wrong; the count is 86.

q: Hazrat Sheeth (AS) was the son of:
f: B) Hazrat Adam (AS) is right. Hazrat Sheeth (AS) was a son of Hazrat Adam (AS). A) Hazrat Nooh (AS) is wrong: his sons were Saam, Haam and Yafis. C) Hazrat Idrees (AS) is wrong: Idrees (AS) came after Sheeth (AS). D) Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is wrong: his sons were Ismail (AS) and Ishaq (AS).

q: What is the minimum number of goats on which Zakat becomes due?
f: B) is right: Zakat on goats starts at 40 goats. A) 20 is wrong. C) 30 is the Nisab for cows/buffaloes. D) 5 is the Nisab for camels.

q: Uhud, after which the Ghazwa is named, is the name of a:
f: C) Mountain is right. Uhud is a mountain near Madina; the battle was fought at its foot. A) River is wrong: Uhud is not a river. B) Well is wrong: Badr was the place with wells, not Uhud. D) Tribe is wrong: Uhud is a place, not a tribe.

q: What was the miracle of Hazrat Saleh (AS)?
o: A staff (asa) that became a snake
f: B) A she-camel is right. A she-camel came out of a rock as the miracle of Hazrat Saleh (AS). A) A staff (asa) that became a snake is wrong: that was the miracle of Moosa (AS). C) Cooling of the fire is wrong: that was for Ibrahim (AS). D) Giving life to the dead is wrong: that was a miracle of Essa

q: Hazrat Abu Bakar (RA) became the first Khalifa in which year of Hijri?
f: B) 11 AH is right. Hazrat Abu Bakar (RA) became Khalifa in 11 AH, after the death of the Holy Prophet PBUH. A) 8 AH is wrong: that is the year of Fath Makkah. C) 10 AH is wrong: that is the year of Hajjat-ul-Wida. D) 13 AH is wrong: that is the year Hazrat Umar (RA) became Khalifa.

q: Which companion is known as Zul-Shahadatain (whose witness equals two)?
f: B) Hazrat Khuzaima bin Sabit (RA) is right. Hazrat Khuzaima bin Sabit (RA) is called Zul-Shahadatain. A) Hazrat Usman (RA) is wrong: he is called Zun-Noorain. C) Hazrat Abu Bakar (RA) is wrong: he is called Siddiq. D) Hazrat Umar (RA) is wrong: he is called Farooq.

q: Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of:
f: D) Hazrat Ishaq (AS) is right. Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS). A) Hazrat Ismail (AS) is wrong: he was the uncle of Yaqoob (AS). B) Hazrat Yousaf (AS) is wrong: Yousaf (AS) was the son of Yaqoob (AS). C) Hazrat Haroon (AS) is wrong: he came much later, with Moosa (AS).

q: The first Azan was given in which year of Hijri?
f: D) 1 AH is right. Azan started in 1 AH in Madina. A) 3 AH is wrong: that is the year of Uhud. B) 5 AH is wrong: that is the year of Khandaq. C) 7 AH is wrong: that is the year of Khaibar.

q: Ghazwa Badr was fought in which year of Hijri?
f: D) 2 AH is right. Ghazwa Badr was fought in 2 AH. A) 3 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Uhud. B) 5 AH is wrong: that is Ghazwa Khandaq. C) 8 AH is wrong: that is the Conquest of Makkah.

q: How many times does the word "Islam" occur in the Holy Quran?
f: D) is right: The word "Islam" occurs 6 times in the Holy Quran. A) 92 is wrong; the word Islam occurs only 6 times. B) 25 is the number of Prophets named in the Quran. C) 14 is the number of Sajdas in the Quran.

q: Which Surah does not begin with Bismillah?
f: B) is right: Surah At-Tauba (Bara'at) is the only Surah that does not start with Bismillah. A) Surah Al-Anfal starts with Bismillah. C) Surah An-Naml has Bismillah twice. D) Surah Al-Kausar starts with Bismillah.

q: What is the plural of Hadith?
f: A) Ahadith is right. The plural of Hadith is Ahadith. B) Hadisaat is wrong: this is not the plural. C) Muhaddis is wrong: this means a scholar of Hadith. D) Tahdees is wrong: this is not the plural.

q: Salat-ul-Khusuf is offered at the time of:
f: B) is right: Khusuf means lunar eclipse; Salat-ul-Khusuf is offered then. A) Solar eclipse is Kusuf. C) Prayer in war is Salat-ul-Khauf. D) Prayer for rain is Salat-ul-Istisqa.

q: Which angels question the dead in the grave?
f: A) is right: Munkar and Nakeer question the dead in the grave. B) Harut and Marut were angels sent to Babylon (Surah Al-Baqarah). C) Kiraman Katibeen write our deeds. D) Israfeel blows the trumpet and Mikail brings rain.

q: What is the Nisab of Zakat for gold?
f: D) is right: The Nisab for gold is 7.5 tola. A) 10 tola is wrong. B) 52.5 tola is the Nisab for silver. C) 5 tola is wrong.

q: Which is the shortest Surah of the Holy Quran?
f: D) is right: Surah Al-Kausar is the shortest Surah with only 3 Ayats. A) Surah Al-Ikhlas is short (4 Ayats) but not the shortest. B) Surah An-Nas is the last Surah (6 Ayats), not the shortest. C) Surah Al-Fatiha has 7 Ayats; it is the opening Surah.

q: Who threw Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) into the fire?
f: B) Namrood is right. King Namrood threw Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) into the fire, and Allah made it cool. A) Firaun is wrong: he was the enemy of Moosa (AS). C) Abraha is wrong: he attacked the Kaaba with elephants. D) Abu Jahl is wrong: he was the enemy of the Holy Prophet PBUH.

q: What is the negative of iota (i)?
f: The negative of any number x is -x, so the negative of i is -i. i is the number itself, and 1 and -1 are real numbers, not the negative of i.

q: Where was Benazir Bhutto assassinated on 27 December 2007?
f: Benazir Bhutto was killed after an election rally at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi. Karsaz in Karachi was the earlier October 2007 attack on her rally, and Garhi Khuda Bakhsh is where she is buried.

q: What was the name of the father of Hazrat Khadija (RA)?
f: Hazrat Khadija (RA) was the daughter of Khuwaylid ibn Asad of the Quraysh. Abu Talib was the Prophet's uncle, Abdul Muttalib his grandfather, and Abu Quhafa the father of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).

q: Who married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Hazrat Uthman (RA) married Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA) and, after her death, Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA), so he is called Dhun-Nurayn (possessor of two lights). Hazrat Ali (RA) married only Hazrat Fatima (RA), and Abu Bakr and Umar (RA) were fathers-in-law of the Prophet.

q: What is the meaning of Al-Ahzab, the name of Surah 33?
f: Ahzab means the confederates or allied groups, the tribes who joined to attack Madinah in the Battle of the Trench. The Cave is Al-Kahf, the Spoils of War is Al-Anfal, and the Victory is Al-Fath.

q: What is the capital city of Australia?
f: Canberra is the capital of Australia. Sydney is the largest city, and Melbourne and Perth are other big cities, not the capital.

q: The Eiffel Tower in Paris was completed in which year?
f: The Eiffel Tower was built from 1887 and completed in 1889 for the World Fair in Paris. 1789 was the French Revolution, and 1901 and 1914 are too late.

q: Ayat al-Birr (the verse of righteousness) is in which Surah?
f: Ayat al-Birr is verse 177 of Surah Al-Baqarah; it says righteousness is not turning faces east or west but true faith and good deeds. The other Surahs do not contain this verse.

q: Which animal was with the Ashab-e-Kahf (People of the Cave) in the cave?
f: Surah Al-Kahf says a dog stretched its forelegs at the entrance of the cave. The Quran mentions no cat, camel or horse with them.

q: Who wrote the book My Brother?
f: My Brother is a book by Mohtarma Fatima Jinnah about her brother Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah. The Quaid did not write it about himself, and Iqbal and Begum Ra'ana Liaquat did not write it.

q: Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests in May 1998 at which site?
f: Pakistan tested its nuclear devices on 28 May 1998 in the Ras Koh Hills of Chagai, Balochistan. Kahuta is the uranium enrichment lab (KRL), Thar is famous for coal, and Kharan was used for the 30 May test only, not the main site.

q: Hazrat Hajra (AS) was the mother of which Prophet?
f: Hazrat Hajra (AS) was the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and the mother of Hazrat Ismail (AS). Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was the son of Hazrat Sarah (AS), Yaqub (AS) was son of Ishaq, and Yusuf (AS) was son of Yaqub.

q: Which female companion narrated the most Hadith?
f: Hazrat Aisha (RA), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), narrated about 2210 Hadith, the most by any woman. Umm Salama (RA) and Hafsa (RA) narrated far fewer, and Hazrat Fatima (RA) narrated very few.

q: Who was the second Khalifa of Islam?
f: Hazrat Umar Farooq (RA) became the second Khalifa in 634 AD after Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA). Abu Bakr (RA) was the first, Usman (RA) the third and Ali (RA) the fourth.

q: Who is known as Abu Hafs?
f: Abu Hafs was the kunya (title) of Hazrat Umar (RA); Hafs means lion cub, and his daughter was Hafsa (RA). Abu Turab was Hazrat Ali's title, and Saifullah was Khalid bin Waleed's title. Abu Bakr is itself a kunya.

q: Who was the second Governor-General of Pakistan?
f: Khawaja Nazimuddin became the second Governor-General in September 1948 after Quaid-e-Azam died. Ghulam Muhammad was the third and Iskander Mirza the fourth (last). Liaquat Ali Khan was the first Prime Minister.

q: The Simla (Shimla) Agreement was signed in which year and by whom?
o: 1966, Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri
1972, Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi
1999, Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee
1950, Liaquat Ali Khan and Jawaharlal Nehru
f: The Simla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi after the 1971 war. 1966 was the Tashkent Declaration, 1999 the Lahore Declaration, and 1950 the Liaquat-Nehru Pact.

q: On which date were the general elections of 2024 held in Pakistan?
f: Pakistan's 12th general elections were held on 8 February 2024. 25 July was the date of the 2018 election and 11 May of the 2013 election; 8 March 2024 was not an election day.

q: Choose the synonym of EMINENT.
f: Eminent means famous and respected, so distinguished is the synonym. Ordinary and hidden are nearly opposites. Imminent is a different word meaning about to happen.

q: Change into indirect speech: The teacher asked, "Who speaks English?"
o: The teacher asked who speaks English.
The teacher asked who spoke English.
The teacher asked that who spoke English.
The teacher asked who had spoken English?
f: In indirect speech the present tense (speaks) changes to past tense (spoke), and the question word who is kept with no that and no question mark. Option A keeps the present tense, C wrongly adds that, and D uses the wrong tense and a question mark.

q: What are the three degrees of adjectives?
f: Adjectives have three degrees: positive (tall), comparative (taller) and superlative (tallest). Simple, compound, complex are kinds of sentences, and present, past, future are tenses.

q: What are the two pieces of the male Ihram called?
f: The male Ihram is two white unstitched sheets: the Izar (wrapped round the waist) and the Rida (over the shoulders). Stitched clothes like qamees, shalwar or jubba are not allowed in Ihram for men.

q: In which year did East Pakistan separate and become Bangladesh?
f: East Pakistan separated on 16 December 1971 after the war with India and became Bangladesh. 1965 was the Pakistan-India war, 1969 was when Yahya Khan took power, and Pakistan recognised Bangladesh in 1974.

q: Tarbela Dam is built on the River Indus in which district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
f: Tarbela Dam is on the River Indus in Haripur District, KP. Swabi lies across the river and Kohat has the small Tanda Dam, while Mansehra has no big dam.

q: Mangla Dam is built on which river?
f: Mangla Dam is on the River Jhelum in Mirpur, Azad Kashmir. The Indus has Tarbela, the Chenab and Ravi have no big storage dam in Pakistan.

q: Which is the largest (longest) river of Pakistan?
f: The Indus is about 3,180 km long and flows through all of Pakistan to the Arabian Sea. Jhelum, Chenab and Kabul are its smaller tributaries.

q: Which is the longest river of Asia?
f: The Yangtze in China is about 6,300 km long, the longest in Asia and third in the world. The Ganges, Indus and Mekong are all much shorter.

q: Which river is commonly called the shortest river of the world?
f: The Roe River in Montana, USA, is only about 61 m long and is known as the shortest river. The Danube, Thames and Volga are long rivers of Europe.

q: Which is the smallest ocean of the world?
f: The Arctic Ocean around the North Pole is the smallest and shallowest ocean. The Indian, Southern and Atlantic Oceans are all bigger.

q: Which is the deepest ocean of the world?
f: The Pacific is the deepest ocean; its Mariana Trench (Challenger Deep) is about 11,000 m deep. The Atlantic, Indian and Arctic are shallower.

q: Which is the smallest country of the world?
f: Vatican City in Rome is only about 0.44 sq km, the smallest country. Monaco is second smallest, and Nauru and San Marino are bigger.

q: Which country has no official capital city?
f: Nauru, a small island country in the Pacific, has no official capital; government offices are in Yaren District. Tuvalu's capital is Funafuti, the Maldives' is Male, and Monaco is a city-state.

q: Which country has the largest number of satellites in space?
f: The United States has by far the most active satellites, mostly due to SpaceX Starlink. China is second, while Russia and India have far fewer.

q: Who is the Chief Minister of Sindh (October 2026)?
f: Syed Murad Ali Shah of PPP became CM Sindh for a third time in February 2024 and still holds the post. Qaim Ali Shah is a former CM, Sharjeel Memon is a Sindh minister and Kamran Tessori is a former Governor (until March 2026).

q: Since 11 October 2026, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has been under Governor's Rule. Who is running the province as Governor?
f: On 11 October 2026 the President imposed emergency and Governor's Rule in KP, and Governor Faisal Karim Kundi took over the provincial government. Ali Amin Gandapur resigned as CM in October 2025, Sohail Afridi was CM until 11 October 2026, and Haji Ghulam Ali is a former Governor.

q: Who is the Chief Minister of Punjab (October 2026)?
f: Maryam Nawaz Sharif of PML-N became CM Punjab in February 2024 and is the first woman CM of any province. Hamza Shehbaz and Usman Buzdar are former CMs, and Mohsin Naqvi was caretaker CM.

q: Who is the Chief Minister of Balochistan (October 2026)?
f: Mir Sarfraz Bugti of PPP was elected CM Balochistan unopposed in March 2024 and still holds the post. Bizenjo and Jam Kamal are former CMs and Ali Mardan Domki was caretaker CM in 2023-24.

q: The Rann of Kutch lies on the border of India and which province of Pakistan?
f: The Rann of Kutch is a salt marsh between Sindh (Pakistan) and Gujarat (India). Punjab, Balochistan and KP do not touch it.

q: What is the name of the border line between Pakistan and India?
f: The Radcliffe Line was drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe in 1947 to divide Punjab and Bengal. The Durand Line is the Pak-Afghan border, the McMahon Line is India-China, and the LAC is also India-China.

q: What is the name of the border line between India and China?
f: The McMahon Line was drawn in 1914 at the Simla Conference and is the India-China border in the east. The Radcliffe Line is Pak-India, the Durand Line is Pak-Afghan, and the Oder-Neisse Line is Germany-Poland.

q: Who wrote the famous book Kitab-ul-Umm?
f: Kitab-ul-Umm is the main fiqh book of Imam Muhammad bin Idris al-Shafi'i. Imam Malik wrote Al-Muwatta, Imam Ghazali wrote Ihya Ulum al-Din, and Abu Hanifa left no such book.

q: Who wrote Zabur-e-Ajam?
f: Zabur-e-Ajam (1927) is a Persian poetry book of Allama Muhammad Iqbal. Ghalib, Hali and Faiz wrote other works.

q: In which year were the first Asian Games held?
f: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi in March 1951. 1954 was the second Games in Manila, 1962 was in Jakarta, and 1948 was the London Olympics year.

q: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is in which country?
f: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is in the city of Pisa, Italy; it is the bell tower of Pisa Cathedral. France, Spain and Greece have other famous landmarks.

q: Where was Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) born?
f: The Holy Prophet (SAW) was born in Makkah in 571 CE, the Year of the Elephant. He migrated to Madinah in 622 CE, visited Taif to preach, and Jerusalem is linked to the Miraj.

q: Who looked after Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) in his childhood as his foster mother?
f: Hazrat Halima Sadia of Banu Saad nursed and raised him in the desert as a child. Hazrat Amina was his own mother, Khadija his first wife and Fatima his daughter.

q: Who was the first wife of Hazrat Muhammad (SAW)?
f: He married Hazrat Khadija (RA) at age 25 when she was 40; she was also the first person to accept Islam. Sauda, Aisha and Hafsa were married later.

q: What is the height of K2, the second highest mountain of the world?
f: K2 is 8,611 m high and is the highest peak in Pakistan. 8,848 m is Mount Everest, 8,126 m is Nanga Parbat, and 7,708 m is Tirich Mir.

q: What is the value of log 1 (logarithm of unity)?
f: Log of 1 is 0 in any base, because any base raised to power 0 equals 1. Log 10 to base 10 is 1, and log 0 is undefined.

q: In which year was the first countrywide Martial Law imposed in Pakistan?
f: On 7 October 1958 President Iskander Mirza imposed Martial Law and made General Ayub Khan Chief Martial Law Administrator. 1969 (Yahya Khan) and 1977 (Zia-ul-Haq) were later martial laws, and 1956 was the year of the first Constitution.

q: Which is the biggest bird of the world?
f: The ostrich is the largest and heaviest living bird and cannot fly. The emu is second tallest, and the albatross and condor are big flying birds.

q: Which is the smallest bird of the world?
f: The bee hummingbird of Cuba is the smallest bird, about 5 cm long. Sparrows, kiwis and swifts are all much bigger.

q: Which is the fastest bird of the world?
f: The peregrine falcon dives at over 320 km/h and is the fastest bird (and animal). The ostrich is the fastest runner but cannot fly; the golden eagle is fast but slower; the hummingbird is tiny.

q: The kiwi bird is found in which country?
f: The kiwi is a flightless bird found only in New Zealand and is its national symbol. Australia has the emu, and South Africa and Brazil have no kiwis.

q: In which year was the Deoband Movement (Darul Uloom Deoband) started?
f: Darul Uloom Deoband was founded on 30 May 1866 by Maulana Qasim Nanotvi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi. 1857 is the War of Independence, 1875 the founding of MAO School Aligarh, and 1885 of the Indian National Congress.

q: When did Gandhi launch the Quit India Movement?
f: Congress launched the Quit India Movement on 8 August 1942 in Bombay to demand an end to British rule. 23 March 1940 is the Lahore Resolution, 12 March 1930 the start of the Salt March, and 3 June 1947 the partition plan.

q: Who started the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930?
f: Gandhi started the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930 with the Salt March (Dandi March). Nehru and Bose were Congress leaders but did not launch it, and Tilak died in 1920.

q: In which year was the First Round Table Conference held?
f: The First Round Table Conference was held in London from November 1930 to January 1931; Congress boycotted it. 1931 was the Second and 1932 the Third conference, and 1928 was the Nehru Report.

q: In which year was the Second Round Table Conference held?
f: The Second Round Table Conference was held in London in 1931, and Gandhi attended it for Congress. 1930 was the First, 1932 the Third, and 1935 the Government of India Act.

q: In which year was the Third Round Table Conference held?
f: The Third Round Table Conference was held in London in November-December 1932. 1930 and 1931 were the First and Second, and in 1933 Choudhry Rahmat Ali's pamphlet 'Now or Never' came out.

q: What is the currency of Malaysia?
f: The Malaysian Ringgit (MYR) is the currency of Malaysia. The Rupiah is Indonesia's, the Baht is Thailand's, and the Peso is the Philippines'.

q: What is the height of Tirich Mir, the highest peak of the Hindu Kush range?
f: Tirich Mir in Chitral is about 7708 meters high and is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush. 8611 m is K2, 8126 m is Nanga Parbat and 7788 m is Rakaposhi.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam present his famous Fourteen Points?
f: Quaid-e-Azam presented the Fourteen Points in March 1929 (commonly given as 28 March 1929) in reply to the Nehru Report. 1928 was the Nehru Report itself, 1916 the Lucknow Pact and 1930 Allama Iqbal's Allahabad Address.

q: Under the Constitution of Pakistan, the President is the head of:
f: The President is the Head of State (Article 41) and represents the unity of the Republic. The Prime Minister is the head of government, and Parliament is led by its presiding officers. The President is Supreme Commander, but that is not the main title asked here.

q: Warsak Dam is located near which city?
f: Warsak Dam is on the Kabul River about 30 km from Peshawar, KP. Tarbela is in Haripur, Mangla is near Jhelum (Mirpur), and Kohat has Tanda Dam.

q: Green plants make their food through which process?
f: Plants make food (glucose) by photosynthesis using sunlight, carbon dioxide and water, with the help of chlorophyll. Respiration breaks food down for energy, transpiration is loss of water from leaves, and digestion happens in animals.

q: The Indus Waters Treaty between Pakistan and India was brokered by:
f: The World Bank brokered the Indus Waters Treaty, signed in Karachi in 1960 by Ayub Khan and Nehru. The UN, IMF and ADB were not the mediators.

q: Who founded the newspaper Dawn?
f: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah founded Dawn in Delhi in 1941 as the voice of the Muslim League. Sir Syed started the Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq, and Iqbal and Liaquat Ali Khan did not found Dawn.

q: When was the first Cricket World Cup held?
f: The first Cricket World Cup was held in England in 1975 and the West Indies won it. India won in 1983, Pakistan won in 1992, and 1971 was the first ODI match, not a World Cup.

q: Who gave the heliocentric (Sun-centred) model of the Solar System?
f: Nicolaus Copernicus proposed in 1543 that the Sun, not the Earth, is at the centre of the Solar System. Ptolemy gave the Earth-centred model, Galileo later supported Copernicus with his telescope, and Newton gave the laws of gravity.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)?
f: The IMF headquarters is in Washington D.C., USA. New York has the UN, Geneva has WHO, and London has Amnesty International.

q: In which year was the Lucknow Pact signed between the Congress and the Muslim League?
f: The Lucknow Pact was agreed in December 1916 at Lucknow, and Quaid-e-Azam played a key role. 1906 was the founding of the Muslim League, 1919 the Khilafat Movement, and 1920 when Quaid left Congress.

q: When did Quaid-e-Azam resign from the Indian National Congress?
f: Quaid-e-Azam left Congress in December 1920 (Nagpur session) because he disagreed with Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement. He joined the Muslim League in 1913, 1916 was the Lucknow Pact, and 1928 was the Nehru Report.

q: World Hepatitis Day is observed on:
f: World Hepatitis Day is on 28 July, the birthday of Dr Baruch Blumberg who discovered the hepatitis B virus. 7 April is World Health Day, 1 December is World AIDS Day and 24 March is World TB Day.

q: What is the approximate range of Pakistan's Nasr (Hatf-IX) missile?
f: Nasr (Hatf-IX) is a short-range tactical missile with a range of 60 km, raised to 70 km in the improved version (2017). 290 km is Ghaznavi, 750 km is Shaheen-I and 2750 km is Shaheen-III.

q: In which year was the Pakistan-China boundary agreement signed?
f: Pakistan and China signed their boundary agreement on 2 March 1963. 1951 is when diplomatic ties began, and 1978 is when the Karakoram Highway opened.

q: The 38th parallel divides which two countries?
f: The 38th parallel is the line that divides North Korea and South Korea. The McMahon Line is between India and China, the 17th parallel divided Vietnam, and the 49th parallel is the USA-Canada border.

q: Who is the President of China (October 2026)?
f: Xi Jinping has been President of China since 2013 and still holds the post. Li Qiang is the Premier, Wang Yi is the Foreign Minister, and Hu Jintao was the earlier President.

q: Muhammad bin Qasim invaded Sindh in:
f: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 712 CE and defeated Raja Dahir. 1001 CE was Mahmud of Ghazni's first attack, 1192 CE was the Second Battle of Tarain, and 632 CE was when the Prophet (PBUH) passed away.

q: In which year did Pakistan buy Gwadar from Oman?
f: Pakistan bought Gwadar from the Sultanate of Oman in 1958 (handed over on 8 September 1958) during Feroz Khan Noon's government. The other years are wrong.

q: How many seats are reserved for women in the National Assembly of Pakistan?
f: Article 51 reserves 60 seats for women in the National Assembly, and this is still the number in 2026. 10 seats are for non-Muslims, 70 is wrong, and 33 is not the women quota in the NA.

q: Which is the largest desert of Pakistan?
f: The Thar Desert (in Sindh and part of Punjab) is the largest desert in Pakistan. Thal is in Punjab, Kharan is in Balochistan, and Cholistan is a smaller desert in Punjab next to Thar.

q: What is the reported range of Pakistan's Ababeel missile?
f: Ababeel is a MIRV ballistic missile with a reported range of about 2200 km, first tested in 2017. 70 km is Nasr, 750 km is Shaheen-I and 2750 km is Shaheen-III.

q: In which year was the present Constitution of Pakistan adopted?
f: The present Constitution was passed on 10 April 1973 and came into force on 14 August 1973. 1956 and 1962 were earlier constitutions, and 1985 was the 8th Amendment.

q: Which river is generally called the longest river in the world?
f: The Nile in Africa (about 6650 km) is usually counted as the longest river. The Amazon carries the most water, the Yangtze is the longest in Asia, and the Indus is the longest in Pakistan.

q: Who wrote 'Mein Kampf'?
f: Adolf Hitler wrote 'Mein Kampf' (My Struggle) in the 1920s. Marx wrote 'Das Kapital', and Mussolini and Stalin did not write it.

q: In which year was the Lahore Declaration signed between Pakistan and India?
f: The Lahore Declaration was signed in February 1999 by Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee. 1966 was Tashkent, 1972 was the Simla Agreement, and 2004 was the Islamabad meeting.

q: About what percentage of the adult human body is water?
f: Water makes up about 50-60% of an adult body weight (about 60% in men). 20-30% and 10-15% are too low, and 80-90% is too high for a whole adult.

q: Islam originated in the:
f: Islam began in Makkah, in the Arabian Peninsula, in the 7th century. Persia, Egypt and Central Asia received Islam later through conquest and preaching.

q: Which country is called the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes'?
f: Finland is called the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes' (it really has about 188,000 lakes). Norway is the Land of the Midnight Sun, Switzerland is the Playground of Europe, and Canada is the Land of Maple Leaf.

q: The Hingol River flows in which province of Pakistan?
f: The Hingol River is in Balochistan and is the longest river of Balochistan. It flows through Hingol National Park into the Arabian Sea. It is not in Sindh, KP or Punjab.

q: In English grammar, 'the' is:
f: 'The' is the definite article because it points to a specific thing. 'A' and 'an' are indefinite articles, and 'the' is not a pronoun or preposition.

q: The Battle of Plassey was fought on:
f: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757, when Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah. 1764 was the Battle of Buxar, 1799 was Tipu Sultan's death, and 1857 was the War of Independence.

q: World War II ended on:
f: World War II formally ended on 2 September 1945, when Japan signed the surrender. 1 September 1939 is when it started, 11 November 1918 ended World War I, and the war in Europe ended on 8 May 1945, not 1944.

q: The Al-Khalid main battle tank was inducted into the Pakistan Army in which decade?
f: Al-Khalid was made by Heavy Industries Taxila with China and was inducted into the Pakistan Army in 2001, so in the 2000s. It was being developed in the 1990s but not yet inducted, and the 1970s and 1980s are too early.

q: Choose the antonym of 'Embrace':
f: 'Embrace' means to accept or hold warmly, so its opposite is 'reject'. Hug, accept and adopt are close in meaning (synonyms), not opposites.

q: Milk is boiled mainly to:
f: Boiling milk kills harmful bacteria and pathogens so it is safe to drink. Boiling does not add vitamins (it can reduce some), does not increase fat and does not make milk sweeter.

q: In which year was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) born in Makkah?
f: He was born in Makkah in 571 CE (some books say 570 CE), in the Year of the Elephant. 610 CE is the year of the first revelation and 632 CE is the year he passed away. 550 CE is too early.

q: To which clan of the Quraysh tribe did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) belong?
f: He belonged to Banu Hashim, the clan named after his great-grandfather Hashim. Banu Makhzum was the clan of Abu Jahl and Khalid bin Walid, Banu Umayyah of Abu Sufyan and Uthman (RA), and Banu Taym of Abu Bakr (RA).

q: What was the name of Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) mother?
f: His mother was Aminah bint Wahb from Banu Zuhrah. Halimah was his foster (wet) mother, Fatimah was his daughter, and Safiyyah was his aunt (and also the name of a wife).

q: Who was the father of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: His father was Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib, who died before the Prophet (PBUH) was born. Abdul Muttalib was his grandfather, and Abu Talib and Hamza were his uncles.

q: Who was the foster mother who nursed Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in the desert?
f: Halimah al-Sa'diyyah of Banu Sa'd nursed him in the desert. Umm Ayman (Barakah) was his nurse/caretaker in Makkah, Fatimah bint Asad was Abu Talib's wife, and Sobia is a wrong option.

q: Who took care of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) after his mother's death?
f: His grandfather Abdul Muttalib took care of him after his mother died. Abu Talib took care of him later, after Abdul Muttalib died. Abu Lahab was an enemy, and Hamza was a young uncle.

q: Which uncle took responsibility for Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) after his grandfather's death?
f: Abu Talib, the full brother of his father Abdullah, became his guardian. Abu Lahab opposed Islam, while Abbas and Hamza did not raise him.

q: Who accompanied Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) on the journey to Syria during his childhood?
f: He went to Syria with his uncle Abu Talib on a trade caravan when he was about 12. Abdul Muttalib had already died, and Abu Bakr and Hamza did not go on this trip.

q: Which titles were associated with Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) because of his honesty?
f: The people of Makkah called him Al-Amin (the trustworthy) and As-Sadiq (the truthful). Al-Farooq is the title of Umar (RA), As-Siddiq of Abu Bakr (RA), and Saifullah of Khalid bin Walid (RA).

q: Which pact did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) participate in to support the oppressed?
f: Hilf al-Fudul was a pact made in Makkah before prophethood to help the oppressed, and he took part in it as a young man. Hudaybiyyah (6 AH), the Pledges of Aqabah and the Charter of Madinah all came after prophethood.

q: Which Surah contains the first five verses identified as the first revelation?
f: The first revelation was the first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq, starting with Iqra (Read), in the Cave of Hira. Al-Muddaththir came after the pause in revelation, and Al-Fatihah and Al-Baqarah came later.

q: Who was the first person to accept Islam?
f: Hazrat Khadijah (RA) was the first person of all to accept Islam. Abu Bakr (RA) was the first free adult man, Ali (RA) the first child, and Zayd (RA) the first freed slave.

q: Who is commonly identified as the first adult free man to accept Islam?
f: Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (RA) was the first free adult man to accept Islam. Ali (RA) was a child then, Uthman (RA) accepted Islam through Abu Bakr (RA), and Umar (RA) accepted Islam years later.

q: Who is commonly identified as the first child to accept Islam?
f: Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) was about 10 years old when he accepted Islam, so he was the first child Muslim. Hasan, Husayn and Usama (RA) were born after that.

q: Who was the first freed slave commonly identified among the earliest Muslims?
f: Zayd ibn Harithah (RA), the freed slave and adopted son of the Prophet (PBUH), was among the first four Muslims. Bilal (RA) accepted Islam a little later, Ammar (RA) was not a freed slave of the Prophet, and Salman (RA) accepted Islam in Madinah.

q: For approximately how many years was the Islamic message initially preached privately?
f: The secret preaching lasted about 3 years. Then Allah ordered open preaching, and the Prophet (PBUH) called the Quraysh from Mount Safa. 2, 5 and 7 years are not the accepted period.

q: Which Christian scholar did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) meet through Hazrat Khadijah (RA)?
f: After the first revelation, Khadijah (RA) took him to her cousin Waraqah ibn Nawfal, who said the same angel (Namus) came to Musa (AS). Bahira was the monk met on the Syria trip, Heraclius was the Roman emperor, and Nestorius was an old church leader.

q: From which hill did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) publicly call the Quraysh to Islam?
f: He stood on Mount Safa near the Kaaba and called the Quraysh openly to Islam. Uhud is in Madinah, Arafat is outside Makkah, and Marwah is the other hill of Sa'i, not this event.

q: Which uncle opposed Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) during his public warning at Mount Safa?
f: Abu Lahab cursed him at Mount Safa, and Surah Al-Lahab (Al-Masad) was revealed about him. Abu Talib protected him, Hamza later accepted Islam, and Abbas did not oppose him there.

q: Who is traditionally recognized as the first martyr of Islam?
f: Sumayyah (RA), mother of Ammar (RA), was killed by Abu Jahl and is the first martyr of Islam. Her husband Yasir (RA) was also martyred but after her, Bilal (RA) survived, and Hamza (RA) was martyred later at Uhud.

q: Which companion endured persecution while repeatedly declaring the oneness of Allah?
f: Bilal (RA) was tortured by his master Umayyah ibn Khalaf on hot sand but kept saying Ahad, Ahad (Allah is One). Ammar, Abu Dharr and Khabbab (RA) were also persecuted, but the Ahad Ahad story is of Bilal (RA).

q: Where did the first migration of Muslims to escape persecution take place?
f: The first Hijrah was to Abyssinia (Habshah, now Ethiopia) in the 5th year of Prophethood. Hijrah to Yathrib (Madinah) was later, Taif was only a visit, and Yemen is wrong.

q: What title was used for the Christian ruler of Abyssinia who gave shelter to Muslims?
f: The king of Abyssinia was called Najashi (Negus); his name was Ashama. Heraclius was the Roman emperor, Chosroes (Kisra) the Persian king, and Muqawqis the ruler of Egypt.

q: Which uncle and protector of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) died during the Year of Sorrow?
f: Abu Talib died in the 10th year of Prophethood, called Aam al-Huzn (Year of Sorrow). Abu Lahab died after Badr, Hamza (RA) was martyred at Uhud, and Abbas (RA) lived long after.

q: Which city did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) visit seeking support after facing opposition in Makkah?
f: After the Year of Sorrow he went to Taif to seek help, but its people stoned him. Madinah was the place of Hijrah later, and Khaybar and Tabuk are places of later expeditions.

q: Which companion accompanied Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) on his journey to Taif?
f: Zayd ibn Harithah (RA) went with him to Taif and was injured while protecting him. Abu Bakr (RA) was his companion in the Hijrah, not Taif; Ali and Umar (RA) did not go.

q: What is the night journey from Masjid al-Haram to Masjid al-Aqsa called?
f: The night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem is called Isra. Mi'raj is the ascension from Al-Aqsa to the heavens, Hijrah is migration, and Ghazwah is a battle.

q: What is the ascension of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to the heavens called?
f: Mi'raj means the ascension from Masjid al-Aqsa up through the heavens. Isra is only the night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem. Ghazwah is a battle and Umrah is the lesser pilgrimage.

q: Which fundamental act of worship was prescribed during the event of Mi'raj?
f: The five daily prayers (Salah) were made obligatory on the night of Mi'raj. Fasting and Zakat came in 2 AH in Madinah, and Hajj was made obligatory later (about 9 AH).

q: From which sacred mosque did the night journey begin in Makkah?
f: The Isra began at Masjid al-Haram in Makkah, as Surah Al-Isra verse 1 says. Masjid al-Aqsa was the end point of the journey. Quba and Masjid an-Nabawi are in Madinah and were built after Hijrah.

q: What were the pledges made between Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and people from Yathrib called?
f: The people of Yathrib gave their pledges at Aqabah near Mina, so they are called the Pledges of Aqabah. Hudaybiyyah (6 AH) was a treaty with Quraysh, the Charter of Madinah came after Hijrah, and Ridwan was under a tree at Hudaybiyyah.

q: What was the earlier name of Madinah?
f: Madinah was called Yathrib before Hijrah; it became Madinat-un-Nabi, the City of the Prophet. Bakkah is an old name of Makkah, Faran is a name linked to the Makkah area, and Khaybar is a separate oasis north of Madinah.

q: Who was sent to Yathrib as an early Muslim teacher after the First Pledge of Aqabah?
f: Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) was the first teacher (envoy) of Islam sent to Yathrib. Abu Bakr and Bilal stayed in Makkah, and Mu'adh ibn Jabal was a man of Madinah, later sent to Yemen.

q: Who slept in Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) bed on the night of Hijrah?
f: Ali (RA) slept in the Prophet's bed to trick the Quraysh and later returned people's trusts (amanat). Abu Bakr travelled with the Prophet, Umar had migrated openly earlier, and Uthman had gone to Abyssinia and Madinah.

q: Who accompanied Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) during the migration to Madinah?
f: Abu Bakr (RA) was the Prophet's companion on the Hijrah and in the cave (Surah At-Tawbah 9:40). Ali stayed back in Makkah, Umar migrated before, and Zayd went with the Prophet to Taif, not on Hijrah.

q: In which cave did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and Abu Bakr (RA) take refuge during Hijrah?
f: They hid for three nights in the Cave of Thawr, south of Makkah. Cave Hira is where the first revelation came, and Uhud and Quba are places in Madinah.

q: Who was the leader of the hypocrites in Madinah commonly mentioned in Seerah?
f: Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul led the hypocrites (Munafiqun) in Madinah. Abu Jahl was an open enemy in Makkah, Musaylimah was a false prophet, and Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf was a Jewish poet.

q: Which Jewish scholar of Madinah accepted Islam and became a companion?
f: Abdullah ibn Salam (RA), a rabbi of Banu Qaynuqa, accepted Islam soon after Hijrah. Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and Huyayy ibn Akhtab stayed enemies, and Abu Jahl was a pagan of Makkah.

q: What title was given to the Muslims of Madinah who welcomed the emigrants?
f: Ansar means helpers; they were the Muslims of Madinah (Aws and Khazraj). Muhajirun were the emigrants from Makkah, Tabi'un came after the companions, and Ashab al-Suffah lived on the Suffah platform.

q: What was the platform in Masjid an-Nabawi associated with companions devoted to learning?
f: The Suffah was a shaded platform where poor companions lived and learned; it is called the first residential school of Islam. The Mihrab is the prayer niche, the Minbar is the pulpit, and the Rawdah is the area between the pulpit and the Prophet's house.

q: Which companion reported a dream containing the wording of the Adhan?
f: Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA) saw the words of the Adhan in a dream and told the Prophet, who approved them. Bilal was told to call it because of his strong voice. Uthman and Abu Bakr did not report this dream.

q: Who became the most famous early Mu'adhdhin of Islam?
f: Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) was the first and most famous Mu'adhdhin of the Prophet. Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum was a second Mu'adhdhin but less famous, while Ammar and Salman were not Mu'adhdhins.

q: In which month of 2 AH was fasting in Ramadan made obligatory?
f: The order to fast in Ramadan came in Sha'ban of 2 AH, just before the first Ramadan in Madinah. Ramadan is the month of fasting itself, not the month the order came, and Rajab and Shawwal are wrong months.

q: In which year of Hijrah was the obligation of Ramadan fasting introduced?
f: Fasting in Ramadan became obligatory in 2 AH. In 1 AH Masjid an-Nabawi was built, 5 AH was the Battle of the Trench, and 9 AH is when Hajj became obligatory (per most scholars).

q: In which direction did Muslims pray before the Qiblah was changed to the Kaaba?
f: Muslims first prayed toward Bait al-Maqdis (Masjid al-Aqsa) in Jerusalem for about 16-17 months after Hijrah. Damascus, Cairo and Mount Sinai were never the Qiblah.

q: Which mosque is associated with the change of Qiblah during prayer?
f: Masjid al-Qiblatayn means the mosque of two Qiblahs, because the Qiblah changed during a prayer there. Quba is the first mosque built in Islam, Masjid an-Nabawi is the Prophet's mosque, and al-Ghamamah is linked to Eid prayer.

q: Which daughter of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) married Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA)?
f: Fatimah (RA) married Ali (RA) in 2 AH. Zaynab married Abu al-As, and Ruqayyah and then Umm Kulthum married Uthman (RA).

q: Which expedition is regarded as the first Ghazwah led personally by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: Ghazwah al-Abwa (Waddan), in Safar 2 AH, was the first expedition the Prophet led himself. Buwat, Safwan (first Badr) and Ushayrah came after it in the same year.

q: What is a military campaign attended personally by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) called?
f: A Ghazwah is a campaign in which the Prophet himself took part. A Sariyyah is one he sent without going himself, Hijrah is migration, and Umrah is the lesser pilgrimage.

q: Which prominent Quraysh leader was killed at Badr?
f: Abu Jahl (Amr ibn Hisham) was killed at Badr by the young Mu'adh and Mu'awwidh, and finished by Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. Abu Sufyan, Ikrimah and Amr ibn al-Aas survived and later accepted Islam.

q: How many Muslims were martyred at the Battle of Badr according to accounts?
f: 14 Muslims were martyred at Badr (6 Muhajirun and 8 Ansar). 70 is the number of Quraysh killed at Badr and also of Muslims martyred at Uhud, so it is wrong here.

q: Approximately how many Quraysh fighters were killed at Badr?
f: About 70 Quraysh were killed and about 70 were taken prisoner at Badr. 14 is the number of Muslim martyrs, and 100 and 300 are not given in the accounts.

q: Which daughter of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) died around the time of the Battle of Badr?
f: Ruqayyah (RA), wife of Uthman, died in Madinah while the Muslims were at Badr; Uthman stayed back to nurse her. Zaynab died in 8 AH, Umm Kulthum in 9 AH, and Fatimah after the Prophet.

q: What educational condition was set for releasing certain literate prisoners after Badr?
o: Teach children to read and write
f: Literate prisoners who could not pay ransom were freed after each taught 10 Muslim children to read and write. Ransom was for those who could pay, no one was forced to convert, and building houses was not a condition.

q: What name does the Qur'an use for the day of the Battle of Badr?
f: Surah Al-Anfal 8:41 calls Badr Yaum al-Furqan, the Day of Criterion between truth and falsehood. Fath refers to the Conquest of Makkah, Ahzab to the Trench, and Jumu'ah is Friday.

q: According to the Qur'an, how many angels were initially promised as reinforcement at Badr?
f: Surah Al-Anfal 8:9 says Allah helped with a thousand angels one after another. 3,000 and 5,000 are mentioned in Surah Al-Imran as further promises, and 100 and 10,000 are not mentioned.

q: Who was the former master of Bilal (RA) who was killed at Badr?
f: Umayyah ibn Khalaf tortured Bilal (RA) in Makkah and was killed at Badr. Utbah and Walid were killed in the first duels at Badr but were not Bilal's masters, and Abu Lahab did not go to Badr and died in Makkah.

q: Which uncle of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was captured at Badr?
f: Abbas (RA) fought on the Quraysh side and was taken prisoner, then paid ransom. Abu Talib had died before Hijrah, Hamza fought for the Muslims, and Abu Lahab did not join the battle.

q: Which Jewish tribe was expelled from Madinah after the conflict following Badr?
f: Banu Qaynuqa broke the treaty after Badr and were expelled in 2 AH. Banu Nadir were expelled in 4 AH, Banu Qurayzah were punished after the Trench in 5 AH, and Ghatafan was an Arab tribe, not Jewish.

q: Which cousin of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) distinguished himself in the fighting at Badr?
f: Ali (RA), the Prophet's cousin, won his duel against Walid ibn Utbah and fought bravely at Badr. Abu Bakr was not a cousin and stayed with the Prophet at the command shelter, Uthman was absent, and Mu'adh ibn Jabal was not a cousin.

q: Which Surah contains the final explicit Qur'anic prohibition of intoxicants?
f: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:90-91 gave the final, complete ban on wine and gambling. Al-Baqarah 2:219 only said the harm is greater than the benefit, while Al-Fil and Al-Kawthar are short Makki surahs not about intoxicants.

q: Which expedition is commonly known as the Battle of Sawiq?
f: Ghazwah as-Sawiq (2 AH) was the chase of Abu Sufyan after his raid near Madinah; his men threw away bags of sawiq (barley flour) while fleeing. Uhud, Khandaq and Khaybar were different, bigger battles.

q: In which Islamic month and year did the Battle of Uhud take place?
f: Uhud was fought in Shawwal 3 AH (March 625 CE). Ramadan 2 AH was Badr, and the other dates do not match any of these battles.

q: How many Muslims initially set out toward Uhud before a group withdrew?
f: About 1,000 Muslims set out; Abdullah ibn Ubayy then left with about 300, leaving about 700. 313 was Badr, 3,000 was the Quraysh army, and 700 is the number left after the withdrawal.

q: Approximately how many Quraysh soldiers participated in the Battle of Uhud?
f: The Quraysh came to Uhud with about 3,000 soldiers under Abu Sufyan. 1,000 was their number at Badr, and 10,000 was the size of the allied army at the Trench (Ahzab).

q: How many archers were positioned to guard the Muslim army's rear at Uhud?
f: The Prophet placed 50 archers on the hill of Ainain (Jabal ar-Rumat) to guard the rear. About 10 stayed back when the others left, and 100 and 200 are wrong.

q: Who commanded the archers positioned at Uhud?
f: Abdullah ibn Jubayr (RA) led the 50 archers and stayed at his post until he was martyred. Mus'ab held the standard, Hamza fought in the main army, and Khalid was then on the Quraysh side.

q: Which military commander exploited the opening left by archers at Uhud?
f: Khalid ibn al-Walid led the Quraysh cavalry around the hill and attacked from behind when the archers left. Abu Sufyan was the overall leader, and Ikrimah helped Khalid but did not lead the attack; Amr ibn al-Aas did not lead it.

q: Which uncle of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), the Lion of Allah, was martyred at Uhud?
f: Hamza (RA), Asadullah, was martyred at Uhud by Wahshi's spear. Abu Talib died before Hijrah, Abbas lived long after, and Ja'far was a cousin martyred at Mu'tah.

q: Who was the Muslim standard-bearer martyred at Uhud?
f: Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) carried the flag at Uhud and was martyred holding it. Ali took the flag after him and survived, Hamza was martyred but not as flag-bearer, and Sa'd was an archer who survived.

q: How many Muslims were martyred at the Battle of Uhud according to accounts?
f: About 70 Muslims were martyred at Uhud, most of them Ansar. 14 was Badr's number of martyrs, 313 was the Muslim army at Badr, and 100 is not given.

q: What injury did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) sustain during the Battle of Uhud?
f: At Uhud a front tooth (lower right) of the Prophet was broken and two rings of his helmet went into his cheek. He did not break his arm, did not lose his sight, and was not unhurt.

q: Which companion is remembered for defending Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) at Uhud?
f: Talhah (RA) shielded the Prophet with his own body and his hand was paralysed by arrows. Abu Lahab was an enemy who died after Badr, Ibn Ubayy left before the battle, and Musaylimah was a false prophet.

q: What major lesson is drawn from Uhud regarding the Muslim archers?
o: Obedience to the Prophet (PBUH) was essential
f: The archers left their post against the Prophet's clear order, and the Muslims lost the upper hand; so the lesson is obedience. Leaving early caused the loss, cavalry was in fact used against them, and returning to Makkah makes no sense.

q: Which is the third Surah of the Holy Quran?
f: Surah Aal-e-Imran comes third, after Al-Fatihah and Al-Baqarah.

q: What is the capital city of Sindh province?
f: Karachi is the provincial capital of Sindh. Hyderabad is a big city of Sindh but not its capital.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of 'Wild'?
f: 'Wild' means not controlled by people; 'tame' means trained or domesticated.

q: What title was given to Liaquat Ali Khan?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan, Pakistan's first Prime Minister, is called Quaid-e-Millat (Leader of the Nation).

q: What is one-third of 120?
Why do we boil milk before drinking it?
o: To add more vitamins to it
To make it digest more slowly
To kill harmful bacteria and germs
f: Boiling kills the harmful microorganisms in raw milk.

q: The Injeel (Gospel) was revealed to which Prophet?
f: Allah revealed the Injeel to Hazrat Isa (A.S).

q: Which is the last (12th) month of the Islamic calendar?
f: Dhul-Hijjah is the 12th month; Hajj and Eid-ul-Adha take place in it.

q: When was the Pakistan-China Border Agreement signed?
f: The Sino-Pakistan boundary agreement was signed on 2 March 1963.

q: Hazrat Maryam (A.S) is the mother of which Prophet?
f: Hazrat Maryam (A.S) gave birth to Hazrat Isa (A.S) without a father, by Allah's command.

q: In which year of Prophethood (Nabwi) were the five daily prayers made obligatory?
f: The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the night of Isra and Mi'raj, commonly dated to the 10th year of Prophethood.

q: What is the synonym of 'Prevalent'?
f: 'Prevalent' means common or widespread.

q: Which is the longest river in Europe?
f: The Volga (about 3,530 km) flows through Russia into the Caspian Sea.

q: Which is the smallest continent in the world?
f: Australia is the smallest continent by land area.

q: Where and when was Liaquat Ali Khan assassinated?
f: He was shot at Company Bagh (now Liaquat Bagh), Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951.

q: The absolute value of any real number is always:
f: |x| is the distance from zero on the number line, so it is never negative.

q: In statistics, the 'average' is also called the:
f: The average (arithmetic mean) is the sum of values divided by their number.

q: What is the current total strength of the Senate of Pakistan?
f: After the 25th Amendment merged FATA into KP, its 8 Senate seats ended, so the Senate went from 104 to 96 members.

q: How many general seats does each province have in the Senate?
f: Each province has 23 Senate seats in total: 14 general, 4 women, 4 technocrat/ulema and 1 non-Muslim.

q: During the Khilafat Movement (Hijrat Movement of 1920), Muslims migrated to which country?
f: In 1920 many Indian Muslims, calling India Dar-ul-Harb, migrated to Afghanistan.

q: Where did Hazrat Amina, mother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), pass away?
f: She died at Abwa, between Makkah and Madinah, when the Prophet (PBUH) was about six.

q: Who was the first Muazzin of Islam?
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) chose Hazrat Bilal (R.A) to give the first Azan in Madinah.

q: Who were the first to offer Namaz (prayer) in Islam?
o: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (R.A)
Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A) and Hazrat Umar (R.A)
f: Hazrat Khadija (R.A) was the first to pray along with the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

q: Which pass connects Chitral with Upper Dir?
f: The Lowari Pass links Dir and Chitral; the Lowari Tunnel now runs under it.

q: Who was the last Governor-General of Pakistan?
f: Iskander Mirza became Governor-General in 1955 and then the first President in 1956.

q: Which day is observed internationally on 12 July?
f: The UN declared 12 July, Malala Yousafzai's birthday, as Malala Day.

q: Who was the first captain of the Indian women's cricket team?
f: Shantha Rangaswamy led India in its first women's Test in 1976.

q: How many articles were in the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan?
f: The 1956 Constitution had 234 articles in 13 parts and 6 schedules.

q: In which year were the first general elections held under the 1973 Constitution?
f: Elections were held in March 1977; protests followed and martial law came in July 1977.

q: In which country is the Great Slave Lake located?
f: Great Slave Lake is in Canada's Northwest Territories.

q: How many continents are there in the world?
f: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.

q: Ghazwa-e-Tabook was led against which empire?
f: In 9 AH the Holy Prophet (PBUH) led the army to Tabook against the Byzantine Romans.

q: When was the Tashkent Declaration between Pakistan and India signed?
f: Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri signed it after the 1965 war.

q: Which is the most abundant chemical element in the universe?
f: Hydrogen makes up about 75% of the normal matter in the universe; helium is second.

q: What was the relationship between Hazrat Asma (R.A) and Hazrat Aisha (R.A)?
f: Both were daughters of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (R.A), from different mothers.

q: When was the Basic Democracies system introduced in Pakistan?
f: Ayub Khan introduced Basic Democracies in 1959 with 80,000 elected members.

q: Mangla Dam was built during whose government?
f: Mangla Dam on the Jhelum River was completed in 1967 under the Indus Basin Project in Ayub Khan's era.

q: Which is the longest river in North America?
f: The Missouri (about 3,767 km) is slightly longer than the Mississippi, which it joins.

q: By which treaty was Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh in 1846?
f: On 16 March 1846 the British sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh for 75 lakh rupees.

q: Who founded the Mughal Empire in India?
f: Babur founded it after defeating Ibrahim Lodhi at Panipat in 1526.

q: Which country opposed Pakistan's UN membership in 1947?
f: Afghanistan cast the only vote against, over the Durand Line dispute.

q: How many member states does SAARC have?
f: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

q: Which is the smallest continent by land area?
f: Australia covers about 7.7 million sq km, the smallest of all continents.

q: Why is Sindh historically called 'Bab-ul-Islam'?
o: It was the capital of the Mughal Empire
Islam entered the subcontinent through it with Muhammad bin Qasim
It has the most mosques in Pakistan
The Pakistan Resolution was passed there
f: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 712 AD, so Islam entered South Asia through Sindh (the 'Gateway of Islam').

q: Which book of Hadith is regarded as the most authentic after the Quran?
f: Imam Bukhari's collection is considered the most authentic book after the Quran; Sahih Muslim is second.

q: When is the International Day of Education observed?
f: The UN General Assembly declared 24 January the International Day of Education.

q: Pakistan bought Gwadar from which country in 1958?
f: Gwadar was handed over by the Sultanate of Oman on 8 September 1958.

q: Which city is known as the 'City of Mosques'?
f: Dhaka, Bangladesh, is famous for its many mosques.

q: How many categories of Zakat recipients (Masarif-e-Zakat) are named in the Quran?
f: Surah At-Tawbah, verse 60, names eight categories, such as the poor (Fuqara) and the needy (Masakeen).

q: Which South American country is the longest from north to south?
f: Chile stretches over 4,300 km along the western coast of South America.

q: Who was President of the 76th UN General Assembly?
f: Abdulla Shahid of the Maldives presided over the 76th session (2021-22).

q: Which city is called the 'Manchester of Pakistan'?
f: Faisalabad is called this because of its huge textile industry.

q: What does the word 'Hikmah' mean?
f: Hikmah means wisdom or deep understanding.

q: How was Hazrat Abu Talib related to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Abu Talib was the brother of the Prophet's father, Abdullah, and protected him in Makkah.

q: Who looked after the Holy Prophet (PBUH) after the death of Hazrat Amina?
f: His grandfather Abdul Muttalib cared for him until he died when the Prophet was eight; then Abu Talib took over.
