q: What is the total length of Pakistan's railway track (route)?
f: Pakistan Railways has a route length of about 7,791 km.

q: The Makran Coastal Highway connects Karachi with which city?
f: The Makran Coastal Highway (N-10) runs along the coast from Karachi to Gwadar.

q: What is the other name of Ghazwa-e-Ahzab?
f: It is called Khandaq (trench) because Muslims dug a trench around Madinah in 5 A.H.

q: Which city is known as the 'City of Gold' (Golden City) of the world?
f: Johannesburg in South Africa grew from the 1886 gold rush and is called the City of Gold.

q: What is the maximum length of a cricket bat?
f: Under the Laws of Cricket, a bat may not be longer than 38 inches (96.5 cm).

q: How many players play a game of chess?
f: Chess is played between two players, one with white pieces and one with black.

q: Pakistan purchased Gwadar from which country?
f: Pakistan bought Gwadar from the Sultan of Oman on 8 September 1958.

q: In which year did Allama Iqbal present the idea of a separate Muslim state (Pakistan)?
f: Allama Iqbal gave this idea in his Allahabad Address in 1930.

q: What is Pakistan's highest military award?
f: Nishan-e-Haider is Pakistan's highest military award for bravery.

q: Which wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) came from a Jewish family?
f: Hazrat Safiyya (R.A.) was the daughter of Huyayy bin Akhtab, chief of the Jewish tribe Banu Nadir.

q: What is the synonym of 'perpetual'?
f: Perpetual means never ending or lasting forever, so 'eternal' has the same meaning.

q: The gold maple leaf is the emblem of which country?
f: The maple leaf is Canada's national symbol and is on its flag.

q: In which city was the OIC formed?
f: The OIC was founded at the summit in Rabat, Morocco, in 1969.

q: Which was the last complete Surah revealed?
f: Surah An-Nasr is known as the last complete Surah revealed to the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

q: How many Khulafa-e-Rashideen were there?
f: The four rightly guided caliphs were Abu Bakr, Umar, Usman and Ali (R.A.).

q: Hazrat Umar (R.A.) was which number caliph of Islam?
f: Hazrat Umar (R.A.) was the second caliph after Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A.).

q: What did the British do after the War of 1857?
o: Made the Mughal emperor the ruler again
Ended Company rule and established direct British Crown rule
f: After 1857, the Government of India Act 1858 ended East India Company rule and India came under the British Crown.

q: Which country has the largest number of active military personnel?
f: China has about 2 million active troops, the most in the world.

q: What is Nishan-e-Haider?
o: The highest military gallantry award of Pakistan
The highest civil award of Pakistan
f: Nishan-e-Haider is given for the highest bravery in war; it is Pakistan's top military award.

q: What type of government did the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan give?
o: Federal parliamentary with a Prime Minister
f: The 1962 Constitution, made under Ayub Khan, gave a presidential system with powers in the President.

q: In which area of Pakistan is the famous high-altitude polo ground located?
f: Shandur Pass (about 3,700 m), between Chitral and Gilgit, has the world's highest polo ground.

q: At which place did the mother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), Hazrat Amina, die?
f: Hazrat Amina died at Abwa, between Madinah and Makkah, when the Prophet (PBUH) was about 6 years old.

q: Who offered the first prayer (Salah) in Islam?
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was the first to offer prayer, taught by Hazrat Jibrael (A.S.).

q: The Lowari Pass connects Chitral with which district?
f: Lowari Pass links Chitral with Upper Dir; the Lowari Tunnel now keeps the route open in winter.

q: Who was the first captain of Pakistan's women's cricket team?
f: Shaiza Khan captained Pakistan in the team's first ODIs in 1997.

q: How many articles were there in the 1956 Constitution?
f: The 1956 Constitution had 234 articles divided into 13 parts.

q: Great Slave Lake is in which country?
f: Great Slave Lake is in Canada's Northwest Territories; it is the deepest lake in North America.

q: During the Khilafat Movement, Muslims migrated (Hijrat) to which country?
f: In the Hijrat Movement of 1920, thousands of Indian Muslims moved to Afghanistan.

q: In which year of Prophethood (Nabvi) was Salah made obligatory?
f: Five daily prayers became obligatory on the night of Mi'raj, which the notes place in the 10th year of Prophethood.

q: Which is the largest river of Europe?
f: The Volga (about 3,530 km) in Russia is Europe's longest and largest river.

q: In which city was Liaquat Ali Khan assassinated?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan was shot at Company Bagh, Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951.

q: The absolute value of every number is always:
f: Absolute value is the distance from zero, so it is never negative; |0| = 0, and every other number gives a positive value.

q: Average is also known as the:
f: The average (arithmetic mean) is the sum of values divided by the number of values.

q: What is the total number of seats in the Senate of Pakistan?
f: After the FATA merger (25th Amendment), the Senate has 96 seats.

q: How many Senate seats are given to each province of Pakistan?
f: Each province gets 23 seats: 14 general, 4 women, 4 technocrats/ulema and 1 non-Muslim.

q: An adjective is a word that describes a:
f: An adjective tells us more about a noun or pronoun, e.g. 'a tall man'.

q: Where is Ranikot Fort located?
f: Ranikot Fort is in Jamshoro District of Sindh.

q: Where is Tarbela Dam located?
f: Tarbela Dam is on the Indus River in Haripur District (near Swabi), Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: Which is the largest lake of the world?
f: The Caspian Sea is the largest lake by area (about 371,000 sq km).

q: Which Prophet was blessed with a son (Hazrat Ishaq) in old age?
f: Allah gave Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S.) sons Ismail and Ishaq (A.S.) in his old age.

q: Imam-ul-Haq is a player of which game?
f: Imam-ul-Haq is a Pakistani cricketer (opening batsman).

q: Fasting (Roza) protects a person from:
f: Fasting teaches Taqwa (God-consciousness) and keeps a person away from sins (Surah Al-Baqarah, 183).

q: In which year did Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (R.A.) accept Islam?
f: Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (R.A.) accepted Islam in Safar 8 A.H., before the conquest of Makkah.

q: When did Ghazwa-e-Tabuk take place?
f: Ghazwa-e-Tabuk, against the Romans, took place in 9 A.H.; no fighting happened.

q: According to the notes, how many times is Namaz (Salah) mentioned in the Quran?
f: The notes say Salah is mentioned about 700 times in the Quran.

q: Who was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A.)?
f: Hazrat Aisha (R.A.), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was Hazrat Abu Bakr's daughter.

q: How many basic pillars (Arkan) does Islam have?
f: Islam has five pillars: Kalma, Namaz, Roza, Zakat and Hajj.

q: Who wrote 'India of My Dreams'?
f: 'India of My Dreams' is a collection of Mahatma Gandhi's writings.

q: Who wrote 'India Wins Freedom'?
f: 'India Wins Freedom' is the autobiography of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.

q: Who led the non-believers (Quraish) at the Battle of Uhud?
f: Abu Sufyan commanded the Quraish army at Uhud (3 A.H.).

q: Who started the newspaper Dawn?
f: Quaid-e-Azam founded Dawn in Delhi in 1941 as a weekly; it became daily in 1942.

q: Who was Prime Minister of Pakistan when the 1956 Constitution was passed?
f: Chaudhry Muhammad Ali was PM (1955-56) and the 1956 Constitution was made during his term.

q: In which year was the state of Swat fully merged into Pakistan?
f: Swat joined Pakistan in 1947 but was fully merged as a district in 1969.

q: What does the word 'hawk' mean?
f: A hawk is a bird of prey that hunts with sharp claws and good eyesight.

q: What does 'Tanzil' mean?
f: Tanzil means sending down, used for the revelation of the Quran from Allah.

q: The process in which a liquid changes into gas is called:
f: Evaporation (vaporization) is the change of a liquid into a gas.

q: Olympic Air is the airline of which country?
f: Olympic Air is a Greek airline based in Athens.

q: Which is the national (most famous) fruit of Pakistan?
f: The mango is the national fruit of Pakistan.

q: Which department conducts the census (Mardam Shumari) in Pakistan?
f: The Pakistan Bureau of Statistics conducts the population census.

q: The Hindu Kush range links Pakistan with which country?
f: The Hindu Kush runs from northern Pakistan into Afghanistan.

q: On which date is Youm-e-Takbir celebrated?
f: Youm-e-Takbir marks Pakistan's nuclear tests at Chagai on 28 May 1998.

q: Which is the fastest land animal?
f: The cheetah can run at about 110-120 km/h, the fastest of all land animals.

q: What is the synonym of 'replenish'?
f: Replenish means to fill something again, so 'refill' has the same meaning.

q: Who is the current Prime Minister of the United Kingdom?
f: Keir Starmer of the Labour Party became UK Prime Minister in July 2024.

q: What was Hazrat Hamza (R.A.) to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Hazrat Hamza (R.A.) was a son of Abdul Muttalib, so he was the Prophet's paternal uncle (and also his foster brother).

q: In which country did Pakistan open its first embassy, according to the notes?
f: The notes give Iran; Iran was also the first country to recognize Pakistan.

q: Which is the latest fighter jet inducted by the Pakistan Air Force?
f: PAF inducted the Chinese J-10C fighter in 2022, its latest 4.5 generation jet.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of Malaysia?
f: Anwar Ibrahim became Malaysia's Prime Minister in November 2022.

q: Which is the oldest internet search engine?
f: Archie was created in 1990 by Alan Emtage at McGill University, before the World Wide Web was popular.

q: What is meant by a 'hung parliament'?
o: A parliament that has been dissolved by the president
A parliament where no single party wins an absolute majority
A parliament whose term has ended
A parliament where the opposition has no members
f: In a hung parliament no party has a majority, so a coalition or minority government must be formed.

q: Which UN organization has won the Nobel Peace Prize twice?
f: The UN refugee agency (UNHCR) won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1954 and 1981. UNICEF won it only once (1965).

q: Through which strait does a very large share of the world's oil trade pass?
f: The Strait of Hormuz links the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman; Gulf oil exports pass through it.

q: How many countries were members of the Islamic Military Counter Terrorism Coalition (IMCTC) when it was formed?
f: The Saudi-led coalition started with 34 countries in 2015 and grew to 41 when Oman joined in 2016.

q: Which country is Pakistan's largest trading partner?
f: China is Pakistan's largest overall trading partner (mostly Pakistan's imports). The USA is Pakistan's largest single export market.

q: What was the Khmer Rouge?
o: A brutal communist movement that ruled Cambodia from 1975 to 1979
A nationalist party that ruled Vietnam from 1955 to 1975
A royal dynasty that ruled Laos
A military government that ruled Thailand in the 1970s
f: The Khmer Rouge under Pol Pot ruled Cambodia (1975-79); about 1.5-2 million people died under its rule.

q: Where is the headquarters of the IMF?
f: The International Monetary Fund has its headquarters in Washington, D.C., like the World Bank.

q: Deficiency of Vitamin C causes which disease?
f: Lack of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) causes scurvy, with bleeding gums. Rickets is caused by lack of Vitamin D.

q: CPU stands for:
f: CPU means Central Processing Unit, the 'brain' of the computer.

q: In which year was OGRA (Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority) formed?
f: OGRA was set up under the OGRA Ordinance of 2002 to regulate Pakistan's oil and gas sector.

q: Under the 1956 Constitution, what was the official name of Pakistan?
f: The 1956 Constitution first named the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

q: In which year (Hijri) was the Battle of Uhud fought?
f: The Battle of Uhud was fought in Shawwal 3 A.H. (625 AD). Badr was in 2 A.H.

q: How many elements does a triangle have?
f: A triangle has 6 elements: 3 sides and 3 angles.

q: Which act of worship is mentioned most often in the Holy Quran?
f: Salah is ordered and mentioned many times in the Quran, more than the other acts of worship.

q: Which prophet stayed in the belly of a fish?
f: Hazrat Yunus (A.S.) was swallowed by a fish and prayed to Allah inside it (Surah Al-Anbiya 21:87).

q: In which year was SAARC established?
f: SAARC was founded at Dhaka on 8 December 1985.

q: The Tashkent Agreement (1966) was signed in which present-day country?
f: Tashkent is the capital of Uzbekistan (then part of the USSR). The agreement ended the 1965 Pakistan-India war.

q: Which prophet is said to have spent 40 days in the belly of a fish?
f: Hazrat Yunus (A.S.) was swallowed by a fish. The Quran does not give the number of days; some traditions say 40.

q: When was the Nehru Report published?
f: The Nehru Report was presented in August 1928 by a committee led by Motilal Nehru.

q: Which prophet is known as Kaleemullah?
f: Kaleemullah means 'the one who spoke with Allah'; Hazrat Musa (A.S.) spoke with Allah at Mount Tur.

q: Hazrat Hamza (R.A.) was martyred in which battle?
f: Hazrat Hamza (R.A.), the Prophet's uncle, was martyred at Uhud in 3 A.H.

q: Which country was the first to buy the JF-17 Thunder?
f: Myanmar was the first export customer of the JF-17 (order 2015, deliveries from 2018).

q: Which railway station of Pakistan has the longest platform?
f: Rohri Junction in Sindh has the longest railway platform in Pakistan (about 1,894 ft).

q: Which is the longest river of Europe?
f: The Volga (about 3,530 km) in Russia is Europe's longest river.

q: What is the antonym of 'autonomy'?
f: Autonomy means self-rule or independence, so the opposite is dependence.

q: Who built the Kaaba for the second time?
f: According to some traditions, after Hazrat Adam (A.S.) his son Hazrat Sheesh (A.S.) rebuilt the Kaaba.

q: 'Israel' is the title of which prophet?
f: Hazrat Yaqoob (A.S.) was called Israel; his descendants are called Bani Israel.

q: Who will blow the trumpet (Soor) on the Day of Judgement?
f: The angel Israfeel will blow the Soor to start the Day of Judgement.

q: Under the 1973 Constitution, what is Pakistan's system of government?
f: The 1973 Constitution gives Pakistan a federal parliamentary system where the Prime Minister is head of government.

q: Which country awards the Nobel Prizes?
f: Most Nobel Prizes are given in Stockholm, Sweden, following Alfred Nobel's will. Only the Peace Prize is given in Oslo, Norway.

q: When did Fatima Jinnah die?
f: Mohtarma Fatima Jinnah died in Karachi on 9 July 1967.

q: How many faces (planes) does a triangular prism have?
f: A triangular prism has 2 triangular faces and 3 rectangular faces, total 5.

q: A bus has 30 passengers and 3/5 of them are males. How many are females?
f: Males = 3/5 x 30 = 18, so females = 30 - 18 = 12.

q: What is a synonym of 'applaud'?
f: To applaud means to praise or clap in approval.

q: What is a synonym of 'retrieve'?
f: To retrieve means to get something back, i.e. recover it.

q: What is a synonym of 'refute'?
f: To refute means to prove a claim wrong, i.e. disprove it.

q: About what percentage of Pakistan's area is covered by forest?
f: Pakistan's forest cover is about 4.8-5% of its area, far below the 25% generally recommended.

q: Which city of Pakistan has the highest literacy rate?
f: Islamabad Capital Territory has the highest literacy rate in Pakistan.

q: Which companion is known as Hawari-e-Rasool (the disciple of the Prophet)?
f: The Holy Prophet said: 'Every prophet has a hawari (disciple), and my hawari is Zubair.'

q: A quadratic equation is also known as a:
f: In a quadratic equation (ax^2 + bx + c = 0) the highest power of x is 2.

q: Who is the President of Sri Lanka?
f: Anura Kumara Dissanayake won the September 2024 election and became President of Sri Lanka.

q: In which battle did Allah send angels to help the Muslims?
f: The Quran (Surah Al-Anfal and Aal-e-Imran) says Allah sent angels to help the Muslims at Badr.

q: Where did the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.) migrate in 622 AD?
f: In 622 AD the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.) migrated from Makkah to Madinah (Yathrib). This Hijrah starts the Islamic calendar.

q: When did the Khilafat Movement start?
f: The Khilafat Movement started in 1919 to protect the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I.

q: The Lucknow Pact (1916) was signed between:
o: Indian National Congress and All-India Muslim League
Muslim League and the British Government
Muslim League and the Unionist Party
f: In the Lucknow Pact of 1916 the Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims; Quaid-e-Azam played a key role.

q: Which city hosted the Olympic Games held in 2021?
f: The 2020 Tokyo Olympics were postponed to 2021 due to COVID-19.

q: In which city was the OIC established?
f: The OIC was founded at the Rabat (Morocco) summit in September 1969. Jeddah is its headquarters, not its founding city.

q: Mark Zuckerberg is the founder of:
f: Mark Zuckerberg founded Facebook in 2004 at Harvard; the company is now called Meta.

q: Where was the first railway track laid in present-day Pakistan?
f: The first railway line in Pakistan's area opened on 13 May 1861 between Karachi and Kotri.

q: What does 'Wuzu' mean?
f: Wuzu (wudu) is the ablution of washing face, hands, arms and feet before prayer.

q: Which is the largest polar desert in the world?
f: Antarctica (about 14 million sq km) is the largest desert, because it gets very little precipitation.

q: How many times has a Pakistani won the Nobel Prize in Physics?
f: Dr. Abdus Salam won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979, the only Pakistani to do so.

q: Who was the first Pakistani woman to win a Nobel Prize?
f: Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014 at age 17, the youngest Nobel laureate.

q: Tipu Sultan wrote letters seeking help to:
f: Tipu Sultan wanted French help against the British and wrote to Napoleon Bonaparte.

q: What is Pakistan's biggest source of electric power?
f: Most of Pakistan's electricity comes from thermal plants using oil, gas and coal.

q: Sofia is the capital of:
f: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria. Bucharest is the capital of Romania.

q: What is the ambassador of one Commonwealth country to another called?
f: Commonwealth countries exchange High Commissioners instead of ambassadors.

q: When did Quaid-e-Azam present his Fourteen Points?
f: Quaid-e-Azam presented his Fourteen Points in March 1929 at Delhi in reply to the Nehru Report.

q: Which bridge in Turkey connects Asia with Europe?
f: The Bosphorus Bridge (now 15 July Martyrs Bridge) crosses the Bosphorus Strait in Istanbul, linking Europe and Asia.

q: How many players does a football team have on the field?
f: Each football (soccer) team has 11 players on the field, including the goalkeeper.

q: Which of the following was a son-in-law of the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.)?
f: Hazrat Ali (R.A.) married Hazrat Fatima (R.A.); Hazrat Uthman (R.A.) also married two daughters of the Prophet. Abu Bakr and Umar were his fathers-in-law.

q: Where did the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.) deliver the Last Sermon (Khutba Hajjatul Wida)?
f: The Last Sermon was delivered on 9 Zil-Hajj 10 A.H. at Arafat (Jabal-e-Rahmat).

q: Which prophet addressed (debated) Namrood?
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S.) argued with King Namrood (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:258) and was thrown into fire, which Allah made cool.

q: The Reko Diq mining project is in which province?
f: Reko Diq, one of the world's largest copper and gold deposits, is in Chagai district, Balochistan.

q: Who demanded the separation of Sindh from Bombay in his Fourteen Points?
f: One of Quaid-e-Azam's Fourteen Points (1929) demanded that Sindh be separated from the Bombay Presidency.

q: Through which pass is Pakistan connected with China?
f: The Karakoram Highway crosses into China at the Khunjerab Pass (about 4,693 m).

q: In which country was the OIC founded?
f: The OIC was founded at Rabat, Morocco, in 1969. Its headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

q: When was the All-India Muslim League established?
f: The Muslim League was founded at Dhaka on 30 December 1906 at the All-India Muhammadan Educational Conference.

q: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed to solve which problem?
o: The 1971 war and the fall of Dhaka
The water dispute that arose after the 1947 partition
f: After partition India stopped canal water to Pakistan in April 1948; the World Bank then mediated the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty.

q: What is the Nisab of Zakat on gold?
f: Zakat is due on gold of 7.5 tolas (about 87.48 grams) or more. 52.5 tolas is the Nisab for silver.

q: In which year (Hijri) did the Battle of Uhud take place?
f: The Battle of Uhud took place in Shawwal 3 A.H. near Mount Uhud, north of Madinah.

q: When was the Liaquat-Nehru Pact signed?
f: The Liaquat-Nehru Pact (Delhi Pact) was signed on 8 April 1950 to protect minorities in both countries.

q: Who elects the President of Pakistan?
f: The President is elected by an Electoral College of the Senate, National Assembly and the four provincial assemblies.

q: In the absence of the President of Pakistan, who acts as President?
f: Under Article 49, the Chairman Senate acts as President; if he is not available, the Speaker National Assembly does.

q: What is the meaning of 'forestall'?
o: To delay a decision without reason
To prevent something by acting beforehand
To repeat an action many times
f: To forestall means to stop or prevent something by taking action before it happens.

q: Sahih Bukhari ranks at which number among the authentic books of Hadith?
f: Sahih Bukhari is considered the most authentic book after the Quran; Sahih Muslim is second.

q: According to the 2023 census, what is the total population of Pakistan?
f: The 7th census (2023), the first digital census, counted 241.49 million people.

q: The Salt Range is located in which province of Pakistan?
f: The Salt Range lies in northern Punjab, between the Jhelum and Indus rivers.

q: Rehman Baba was a poet of which language?
f: Abdul Rehman Baba (17th century) is a famous Sufi poet of Pashto.

q: In the first quadrant, what is the sign of sin x?
f: In the first quadrant all trigonometric ratios (sin, cos, tan) are positive.

q: In which month and year was the Nehru Report presented?
f: The All Parties Conference committee under Motilal Nehru issued its report in August 1928.

q: What does 'Hadith' literally mean?
f: Hadith literally means saying, talk or speech; in Islam it means the sayings of the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.).

q: In which year (Hijri) was fasting (Roza) made obligatory?
f: Fasting in Ramadan was made obligatory in 2 A.H. (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:183).

q: On which date does India celebrate its Independence Day?
f: India celebrates Independence Day on 15 August, one day after Pakistan (14 August).

q: Where is the headquarters of ECO (Economic Cooperation Organization)?
f: ECO's secretariat is in Tehran, Iran.

q: Who abrogated the 1956 Constitution?
f: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 Constitution and imposed martial law on 7 October 1958.

q: Which bridge in Turkey connects Asia and Europe over the Bosphorus?
f: The Bosphorus Bridge in Istanbul, opened in 1973, was the first bridge linking Europe and Asia.

q: About what percentage of Pakistan's area is covered by mountains?
f: Mountains and plateaus cover roughly 58-60% of Pakistan's land.

q: On which occasion did Hind bint Utbah accept Islam?
f: Hind, wife of Abu Sufyan, accepted Islam at the Conquest of Makkah in 8 A.H.

q: Who is the President of Uzbekistan?
f: Shavkat Mirziyoyev has been President of Uzbekistan since 2016. Tokayev is President of Kazakhstan.

q: Which is the largest airport of Pakistan?
f: Islamabad International Airport, opened in 2018, is Pakistan's largest airport by area.

q: Where did the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.) deliver his Last Sermon?
f: The Last Sermon was delivered at Arafat (Jabal-e-Rahmat) during the Farewell Hajj, 10 A.H.

q: Justice Alvin Robert Cornelius was:
f: Justice A.R. Cornelius was Chief Justice of Pakistan from 1960 to 1968, the 4th to hold the post.

q: Pakistan, Iran and Turkey formed which organization in 1964?
f: RCD was formed in July 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey.

q: Which country has no regular army?
f: Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948. Switzerland has an army based on conscription.

q: Which country delivered the S-400 missile system to India?
f: India bought the S-400 Triumf air-defence system from Russia in a 2018 deal.

q: In which year did Pakistan join the ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF)?
f: Pakistan joined the ASEAN Regional Forum in July 2004. Pakistan has been an ASEAN sectoral dialogue partner since 1993.

q: When was the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan enforced?
f: The 1973 Constitution was passed by the National Assembly on 10 April 1973, signed on 12 April and enforced on 14 August 1973.

q: Over how many years was the Holy Quran revealed?
f: The Quran was revealed gradually over about 23 years: 13 years in Makkah and 10 years in Madinah.

q: Who was the first Governor-General of India (British India)?
f: Under the Charter Act 1833, Lord William Bentinck became the first Governor-General of India. Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal (1773).

q: Which caliph is called Jami-ul-Quran (compiler of the Quran)?
f: Hazrat Uthman (R.A.) made standard copies of the Quran in one dialect and sent them to all provinces.

q: In which year did the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.) migrate to Madinah?
f: The Hijrah to Madinah took place in 622 AD and marks the start of the Islamic calendar.

q: The Cholistan Desert is mainly located in which district of Punjab?
f: Most of the Cholistan Desert lies in Bahawalpur district; it also extends into Bahawalnagar and Rahim Yar Khan.

q: What is a quarter of one-tenth of 120?
f: One-tenth of 120 = 12, and a quarter of 12 = 3.

q: How many daughters did the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.) have?
f: The Prophet's daughters were Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatima (R.A.).

q: What title is given to the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.) in the Quran (Surah Al-Anbiya 21:107)?
f: The Quran says: 'We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds' (21:107).

q: How many sugar mills did Pakistan have in 1947?
f: At independence Pakistan had only 2 sugar mills; most industry was in India.

q: What is the rate of Zakat on silver?
f: Zakat on gold, silver and cash is 2.5% (one-fortieth) of the wealth held for one year.

q: In which city is PIMS hospital located?
f: PIMS (Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences) is in Islamabad.

q: 'Islamabad' is which type of noun?
f: Islamabad is the name of a particular place, so it is a proper noun.

q: In which direction of Pakistan is China situated?
f: China lies to the north (north-east) of Pakistan, bordering Gilgit-Baltistan.

q: In which year was Mangla Dam completed?
f: Mangla Dam on the Jhelum River was completed in 1967. Tarbela was completed in 1976.

q: The Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with:
f: The Khunjerab Pass on the Karakoram Highway is the border crossing between Pakistan and China.

q: Who is the head of state of Japan?
f: Japan has no president; it is a constitutional monarchy where the Emperor is head of state and the Prime Minister heads the government.

q: The Khyber Pass connects Pakistan with:
f: The Khyber Pass links Peshawar (Pakistan) with Afghanistan via Torkham.

q: What is the antonym of 'wild'?
f: Wild means not controlled by humans; the opposite is tame (domesticated).

q: Which is the largest international airport in the world by area?
f: King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia, covers about 776 sq km, the largest by area.

q: When was the SCO (Shanghai Cooperation Organisation) established?
f: The SCO was formed in Shanghai on 15 June 2001.

q: Which line marks the border between Pakistani Punjab and Indian Punjab?
f: Sir Cyril Radcliffe drew the boundary between Pakistan and India in 1947.

q: In which year was the NATO treaty signed?
f: The North Atlantic Treaty was signed on 4 April 1949 in Washington, D.C.

q: Which planet is called the 'sister' or 'twin' of Earth?
f: Venus is called Earth's sister because it is very close to Earth in size, mass and distance from the Sun.

q: In which year was the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) born?
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born in Makkah in 571 AD (the Year of the Elephant). 610 AD is the year of the first revelation.

q: When is World Hepatitis Day observed?
f: World Hepatitis Day is marked every year on 28 July, the birthday of Nobel winner Baruch Blumberg, who discovered the hepatitis B virus.

q: In which year was the first Test cricket match played?
f: The first Test match was played between Australia and England at Melbourne in March 1877.

q: In which year did the First Round Table Conference begin in London?
f: The First Round Table Conference opened in London in November 1930; the Second was in 1931 and the Third in 1932.

q: Who wrote the book 'Pakistan: A Hard Country'?
f: 'Pakistan: A Hard Country' (2011) was written by British journalist and scholar Anatol Lieven.

q: Which organization mediated the Indus Waters Treaty between Pakistan and India?
f: The World Bank brokered the Indus Waters Treaty, signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960.

q: Who is the Head of State according to the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan?
f: Under the 1973 Constitution the President is the Head of State, while the Prime Minister is the head of government.

q: Which ruler of Mysore did the British defeat and kill at Seringapatam in 1799?
f: Tipu Sultan was killed fighting the British in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War at Seringapatam in 1799.

q: Who is the author of 'Pakistaniaat'?
f: The notes give Javed Jabbar as the author of 'Pakistaniaat'.

q: Who wrote 'Kitab al-Umm'?
f: 'Kitab al-Umm' is the main book of fiqh written by Imam Muhammad bin Idris al-Shafi'i.

q: The Tochi Pass connects which two places?
f: The Tochi Pass in North Waziristan links Bannu in Pakistan with Ghazni in Afghanistan.

q: Where is the headquarters of Amnesty International?
f: Amnesty International, the human rights organization founded in 1961, has its headquarters in London.

q: In which year was the first nationwide martial law imposed in Pakistan?
f: Martial law was imposed across Pakistan on 7 October 1958. (In 1953 only a limited martial law was imposed in Lahore.)

q: In which year did construction of Tarbela Dam start?
f: Work on Tarbela Dam on the Indus River began in 1968; it was completed in 1976.

q: Where is the International Court of Justice located?
f: The ICJ, the main judicial body of the UN, sits in the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands.

q: The passes of the Hindu Kush connect Pakistan with which country?
f: The Hindu Kush range lies along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border and its passes link the two countries.

q: In which year did the Hindi-Urdu controversy start?
f: In 1867 Hindus of Benares demanded that Hindi replace Urdu in courts, which started the controversy.

q: What is the antonym of 'Embarrass'?
f: To embarrass is to make someone feel awkward or ashamed, so the opposite is to put them at ease. The other options mean nearly the same as 'embarrass'.

q: In which year were the first Asian Games held in New Delhi?
f: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, in March 1951.

q: What is the height of Tirich Mir, the highest peak of the Hindu Kush?
f: Tirich Mir in Chitral is 7,708 m high, the highest peak of the Hindu Kush. 8,611 m is K2 and 8,126 m is Nanga Parbat.

q: Which was the only (first) Muslim country to oppose Pakistan's membership of the UN in 1947?
f: Afghanistan voted against Pakistan's admission to the UN in September 1947, mainly over the Durand Line issue.

q: In which province is the archaeological site of Kot Diji located?
f: Kot Diji is in Khairpur district of Sindh; it is an early Indus civilization site.

q: Wudu (ablution) and Tayammum are described in which Surah?
f: Verse 6 of Surah Al-Ma'idah describes the method of wudu and allows tayammum when water is not available.

q: What is the synonym of 'Persistent'?
f: 'Persistent' means continuing firmly despite difficulty, which is the same as 'determined'.

q: Which country did Liaquat Ali Khan visit on his first official foreign tour as Prime Minister?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan made his famous visit to the USA in May 1950, instead of going to the USSR.

q: What was the old name of Attock?
f: Attock was called Campbellpur after Sir Colin Campbell; it was renamed Attock in 1978.

q: In which year was Jinnah given the title 'Quaid-e-Azam'?
f: Jinnah was given the title Quaid-e-Azam in 1938 by Maulana Mazharuddin.

q: When did Pakistan's first Education Conference begin in Karachi?
f: The first Pakistan Educational Conference was held in Karachi from 27 November to 1 December 1947; Quaid-e-Azam sent a message to it.

q: On which date was the Objectives Resolution passed?
f: The Constituent Assembly passed the Objectives Resolution, moved by Liaquat Ali Khan, on 12 March 1949.

q: The Victoria Cross is the highest military award of which country?
f: The Victoria Cross is the highest gallantry award of the British (and Commonwealth) armed forces, started in 1856.

q: When was the Quit India Movement started?
f: The Congress launched the Quit India Movement on 8 August 1942 in Bombay.

q: With the help of which country was KANUPP (Karachi Nuclear Power Plant) built?
f: KANUPP, Pakistan's first nuclear power plant (1972), was built with Canadian help.

q: In which year did Dr. Abdus Salam win the Nobel Prize in Physics?
f: Dr. Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on the electroweak theory.

q: In which country was the OIC established?
f: The OIC was set up at the Rabat summit in Morocco in September 1969. Its headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

q: What is the antonym of 'Sympathetic'?
f: 'Sympathetic' means showing care for others' feelings, so 'unfeeling' is the opposite. The other options are synonyms.

q: What does 'Irksome' mean?
f: 'Irksome' means irritating or annoying.

q: What is the synonym of 'Spontaneous'?
f: 'Spontaneous' means happening naturally without planning, so 'unforced' is closest. The others are opposites.

q: Where is the Gobi Desert located?
f: The Gobi Desert covers southern Mongolia and northern China.

q: Who is the author of the book on 'Happiness' named in the notes?
f: The notes name Neil Pasricha, a Canadian author known for books on happiness such as 'The Happiness Equation'.

q: How many years did Pakistan take to make its first Constitution?
f: Pakistan became independent in 1947 and its first Constitution came into force on 23 March 1956, about 9 years later.

q: In which year did Benazir Bhutto first become Prime Minister?
f: Benazir Bhutto became PM on 2 December 1988, the first woman to lead a Muslim country. Her second term began in 1993.

q: Who was made Chief Martial Law Administrator when Pakistan's first martial law was imposed in 1958?
f: President Iskander Mirza proclaimed martial law on 7 October 1958 and named General Ayub Khan as Chief Martial Law Administrator; Ayub took full power soon after.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam resign from the Indian National Congress?
f: Jinnah left the Congress in 1920 (Nagpur session) because he opposed Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement.

q: Who started the Non-Cooperation Movement?
f: Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920; he called it off in 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident.

q: Who wrote the travel book 'Rihla'?
f: 'Al-Rihla' is the travel account of Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta, who visited India in the 14th century.

q: Which mountain range lies in the northwest of Pakistan?
f: The Hindu Kush runs through northwestern Pakistan (Chitral) into Afghanistan.

q: When was the Pakistan-Iran gas pipeline agreement signed?
f: Pakistan and Iran signed the gas pipeline agreement on 16 March 2010; the groundbreaking took place in March 2013.

q: The Panama Canal connects which two oceans?
f: The Panama Canal cuts across Panama to link the Atlantic Ocean (Caribbean Sea) with the Pacific Ocean.

q: In which country did the game of chess originate?
f: Chess began in India around the 6th century as 'chaturanga' and then spread to Persia.

q: On which date did the State of Kalat (Balochistan) join Pakistan?
f: The Khan of Kalat signed the accession to Pakistan on 27 March 1948.

q: Who wrote the novel 'The Book of Happiness'?
f: 'The Book of Happiness' is a novel by Russian-born writer Nina Berberova.

q: Where do the Indus and Kabul rivers meet?
f: The Kabul River joins the Indus near Attock.

q: Which place in Pakistan is famous for making small arms?
f: Darra Adam Khel in Kohat district is known for its hand-made small arms market.

q: Which is the oldest library in Pakistan?
f: The Punjab Public Library in Lahore was founded in 1884, making it the oldest library listed here.

q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Azad Jammu and Kashmir?
f: The post of AJK Prime Minister was created in 1975 and Khan Abdul Hamid Khan was the first to hold it.

q: Who was the first person to climb Mount Everest (with Tenzing Norgay)?
f: New Zealander Edmund Hillary and Sherpa Tenzing Norgay reached the summit on 29 May 1953.

q: How many member countries does the United Nations have?
f: The UN has 193 member states; South Sudan became the 193rd in 2011.

q: Which is the largest (freshwater) lake of Pakistan?
f: Manchar Lake in Jamshoro district, Sindh, is Pakistan's largest freshwater lake.

q: When was NATO formed?
f: NATO was set up by the North Atlantic Treaty, signed in Washington on 4 April 1949.

q: Which rivers were given to India under the Indus Waters Treaty?
f: India got the three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej); Pakistan got the three western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab).

q: In which year did the State of Swat accede to Pakistan?
f: The Wali of Swat signed the accession to Pakistan in November 1947. The state was fully merged into Pakistan in 1969.

q: Which country is shaped like a boot?
f: Italy is famous for its boot-like shape on the map.

q: Who is the current Chancellor of Germany (as of 2026)?
f: Friedrich Merz (CDU) became Chancellor of Germany on 6 May 2025, replacing Olaf Scholz. Steinmeier is the President.

q: In which year was SUPARCO established?
f: SUPARCO started as a committee on 16 September 1961 under Dr. Abdus Salam.

q: How many amendments have been made to the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan?
f: The 26th Amendment was passed in October 2024 and the 27th Amendment in November 2025.

q: How many full member countries does BRICS have?
f: BRICS: Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, plus Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE (2024) and Indonesia (January 2025) = 10.

q: Lake Superior is in which continent?
f: Lake Superior lies on the USA-Canada border and is one of the Great Lakes of North America.

q: According to the notes, what is the average width of the Amazon River?
f: The notes give 2,300 feet; the Amazon's width actually varies a lot with season, from about 1.6 km to many km in the wet season.

q: Islamabad lies at the foot of which hills?
f: Islamabad is built at the foot of the Margalla Hills, which form its northern edge.

q: What is the other name of the Battle of Badr given in the Quran?
f: The Quran calls the day of Badr 'Yaum-ul-Furqan' (the Day of Criterion) because it separated truth from falsehood (Surah Al-Anfal, 8:41).

q: How many times is the name 'Muhammad' (PBUH) mentioned in the Quran?
f: The name 'Muhammad' appears four times in the Quran (3:144, 33:40, 47:2, 48:29).

q: Who was the foster sister of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Hazrat Shaima was the daughter of Hazrat Halima Sadia, the Prophet's foster mother.

q: 'Israel' is the title of which Prophet?
f: 'Israel' was the title of Hazrat Yaqub (AS); his descendants are called Bani Israel.

q: In which year of Hijrah did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) perform Hajjat-ul-Wida (the Farewell Hajj)?
f: The Farewell Hajj was performed in 10 AH (632 AD), when the Prophet gave the famous Farewell Sermon.

q: Who was the mother of Hazrat Ismail (AS)?
f: Hazrat Hajra was the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and mother of Hazrat Ismail (AS). Hazrat Sarah was the mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).

q: What is the synonym of 'Retreat' (as a verb)?
f: To retreat means to move back or withdraw. 'Drawback' means a disadvantage.

q: What is a common cause of Vitamin D deficiency?
o: Too little vitamin C in the diet
f: The skin makes Vitamin D when exposed to sunlight, so lack of sunlight causes deficiency.

q: How many times has the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan been amended?
f: The 27th Amendment was passed in November 2025, after the 26th Amendment of October 2024.

q: Which of today's Pakistani provinces did the British occupy first?
f: The British conquered Sindh in 1843 (Charles Napier). Punjab, including today's KP, was annexed in 1849.

q: Which is the brightest planet seen in the night sky?
f: Venus is the brightest planet in our sky. It is not a star; the only star in the solar system is the Sun.

q: The Asian Games started in which country?
f: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, in 1951.

q: Who was the first Governor-General of independent India?
f: Lord Mountbatten stayed on as independent India's first Governor-General (1947-48). C. Rajagopalachari was the last (and only Indian) one.

q: In which year did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) migrate to Madinah?
f: The Hijrah took place in 622 AD; the Islamic calendar starts from this event.

q: How many peaks above 8,000 metres are in Pakistan?
f: Pakistan has five 8,000 m peaks: K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I, Broad Peak and Gasherbrum II. The world has 14.

q: In which city was the Indian National Congress founded?
f: The Congress was founded in Bombay in December 1885 by A.O. Hume.

q: The zero factor property (if ab = 0 then a = 0 or b = 0) is also called the:
f: If a product equals zero, at least one factor must be zero; this is the zero product property, used to solve quadratic equations.

q: When did Dr. Abdul Qadeer Khan die?
f: Dr. A.Q. Khan, father of Pakistan's nuclear programme, died in Islamabad on 10 October 2021.

q: In which city is OPEC headquartered?
f: OPEC moved its headquarters from Geneva to Vienna in 1965.

q: When did Islamabad formally become the capital of Pakistan in place of Karachi?
f: Islamabad was formally declared the federal capital on 14 August 1967; Rawalpindi served as interim capital before that.

q: What is China's highest military award?
f: The 'August 1st Medal' (Bayi Medal), created in 2017, is the highest honour of China's armed forces.

q: In which year was the Nehru Report published?
f: The Nehru Report was presented in 1928; Jinnah replied with his Fourteen Points in 1929.

q: In which year was the Pirpur Report published?
f: The Pirpur Report (1938) of the Muslim League described the mistreatment of Muslims under Congress ministries (1937-39).

q: What is the synonym of 'Console'?
f: To console someone means to comfort them in sadness.

q: When did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan die?
f: Sir Syed died on 27 March 1898 in Aligarh. He was born on 17 October 1817.

q: Which region is called 'Bab-ul-Islam' (Gateway of Islam)?
f: Sindh is called Bab-ul-Islam because Islam entered the subcontinent through it with Muhammad bin Qasim in 712 AD.

q: In which year was the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental school (later Aligarh University) founded?
f: Sir Syed founded the MAO school at Aligarh in 1875; it became a college in 1877 and Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

q: When was Major Aziz Bhatti martyred?
f: Major Raja Aziz Bhatti was martyred on 12 September 1965 on the BRB Canal near Lahore and received the Nishan-e-Haider.

q: What form of government did the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan provide?
f: The 1956 Constitution gave Pakistan a parliamentary system with the Prime Minister as head of government.

q: What is the synonym of 'Indifference'?
f: 'Indifference' means not caring or having no interest.

q: When did Pakistan become a full member of the SCO?
f: Pakistan and India became full SCO members at the Astana summit on 9 June 2017.

q: The 1956 Constitution of Pakistan set up which system of government?
f: The 1956 Constitution was parliamentary; the presidential system came with the 1962 Constitution.

q: What is the range of the Hatf-1 missile?
f: Hatf-1 is a short-range battlefield missile with a range of about 70 km.

q: How many articles are in the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan?
f: The 1973 Constitution has 280 articles. The 1956 Constitution had 234 and the 1962 one had 250.

q: Which article of the 1973 Constitution gives the right to education?
f: Article 25A, added by the 18th Amendment (2010), makes free and compulsory education for children aged 5-16 a right.

q: What is the synonym of 'Zeal'?
f: 'Zeal' means great energy or enthusiasm, the same as passion.

q: Khanpur Dam is built on which river?
f: Khanpur Dam near Haripur is on the Haro River and supplies water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi.

q: Which is described in the notes as Pakistan's second highest civil award?
f: The notes give Hilal-i-Imtiaz, which comes after the Nishan-i-Imtiaz for services to the country.

q: Where is the headquarters of the IMF?
f: The International Monetary Fund is based in Washington D.C., USA.

q: Who wrote 'Humayun Nama'?
f: 'Humayun Nama' was written by Gulbadan Begum, Humayun's sister and Babur's daughter.

q: Who wrote the Punjabi folk tale 'Sohni Mahiwal'?
f: The famous Punjabi qissa 'Sohni Mahiwal' was written by Fazal Shah. Waris Shah wrote 'Heer Ranjha'.

q: When did the USA invade Iraq?
f: The US-led invasion of Iraq began on 20 March 2003.

q: Who wrote the novel 'Ice Candy Man'?
f: 'Ice Candy Man' (1988), about Partition in Lahore, was written by Bapsi Sidhwa.

q: Choose the antonym of ABUNDANT.
f: Abundant means present in large amounts; scarce means in short supply.

q: Noor Mahal palace is located in which district?
f: Noor Mahal was built in 1872 by Nawab Sadiq Muhammad Khan IV in Bahawalpur.

q: Choose the synonym of MOMENTARY.
f: Momentary means lasting for a very short time, i.e. brief.

q: Captain Muhammad Sarwar Shaheed (Nishan-e-Haider) was martyred in which war?
f: Captain Sarwar was martyred on 27 July 1948 in the Uri sector during the first Kashmir War.

q: Choose the synonym of EXCUSE (verb).
f: To excuse a fault is to defend or justify it; accuse, blame and condemn are opposites.

q: Choose the synonym of DISASTER.
f: Disaster and catastrophe are both nouns meaning a sudden great misfortune.

q: What was the real name of Shah Waliullah?
f: Shah Waliullah Dehlvi (1703-1762) was born Qutbuddin Ahmad; 'Waliullah' was his title.

q: Which battle was fought in 1757 between Nawab Sirajuddaula and Robert Clive?
f: The Battle of Plassey (1757) gave the East India Company control of Bengal.

q: Jamrud Fort is located near which city?
f: Jamrud Fort stands at the entrance of the Khyber Pass, west of Peshawar (Khyber District).

q: Choose the synonym of IDLENESS.
f: Idleness means not working or being lazy.

q: Choose the antonym of INTIMATE.
f: Intimate means very close; distant is its opposite.

q: Who was known as the 'Desert Fox'?
f: German Field Marshal Erwin Rommel earned the name for his North African campaign in WWII.

q: Who first proposed that the Earth revolves around the Sun (heliocentric theory)?
f: Copernicus presented the heliocentric model in 1543; Galileo later supported it with observations.

q: Where is the headquarters of the IAEA?
f: The International Atomic Energy Agency is based in Vienna, Austria.

q: Habba Khatoon, the famous poetess, belonged to which region?
f: Habba Khatoon was a 16th-century Kashmiri poetess, wife of Yusuf Shah Chak.

q: Who is the last (most recent) recipient of the Nishan-e-Haider?
f: Havaldar Lalak Jan was martyred on 7 July 1999 in the Kargil conflict, after Karnal Sher Khan (5 July 1999).

q: When did the Simon Commission arrive in India?
f: The Commission was appointed in November 1927 and landed in Bombay on 3 February 1928.

q: Which city is called the 'City of Saints'?
f: Multan has many shrines of Sufi saints such as Bahauddin Zakariya and Shah Rukn-e-Alam.

q: Which scientist won two unshared Nobel Prizes (Chemistry 1954 and Peace 1962)?
f: Linus Pauling is the only person to win two unshared Nobel Prizes.

q: The Soan River flows through which region?
f: The Soan rises near Murree and drains the Potohar Plateau before joining the Indus.

q: Who was the Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army during the 1965 war?
f: General Muhammad Musa Khan led the Army in 1965, while Ayub Khan was President.

q: The abscissa of a point is its:
f: The abscissa is the horizontal (x) coordinate.

q: Choose the synonym of INSURGENTS.
f: Insurgents are people who rise in revolt against authority, i.e. rebels.

q: Choose the antonym of MARGINAL.
f: Marginal means small or minor; substantial means large or important.

q: Choose the antonym of CRUDE.
f: Crude means raw or unrefined, so its opposite is refined.

q: In which year was the Treaty establishing a Constitution for Europe (EU Constitution) signed?
f: It was signed in Rome in 2004 but was rejected by French and Dutch voters in 2005, so it never came into force.

q: On which date did World War II formally end?
f: Japan signed the surrender on 2 September 1945, ending WWII.

q: Choose the meaning of DISRUPT.
f: To disrupt is to disturb or throw into disorder.

q: What is the range of Pakistan's Nasr (Hatf-IX) missile?
f: Nasr is a short-range tactical missile with a range of about 60-70 km.

q: The 38th Parallel is the boundary between:
f: The 38th parallel was the line that divided Korea after WWII.

q: One inch is equal to:
f: By definition, 1 inch = 2.54 cm (25.4 mm).

q: Which is the largest (longest) river of Balochistan?
f: The Hingol (about 560 km) is the longest river in Balochistan.

q: Who wrote 'Friends Not Masters'?
f: Field Marshal Ayub Khan wrote his autobiography 'Friends Not Masters' in 1967.

q: How many member countries does the OIC have?
f: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation has 57 member states.

q: What was the profession of Fatima Jinnah?
f: Fatima Jinnah qualified as a dentist and opened a clinic in Bombay in 1923.

q: Who invented the electric motor?
f: Faraday demonstrated electromagnetic rotation, the first electric motor, in 1821.

q: When did India conduct its first nuclear test?
f: India's first test, 'Smiling Buddha', was held at Pokhran on 18 May 1974.

q: Which US President improved US-China relations by visiting China in 1972?
f: Nixon's 1972 visit to Beijing opened US-China relations.

q: How many Farz (obligatory acts) are there in Hajj?
f: The three Farz of Hajj are Ihram, Wuquf-e-Arafat and Tawaf-e-Ziyarat.

q: What is the old name of Makkah mentioned in the Quran?
f: Surah Aal-e-Imran (3:96) calls Makkah 'Bakkah'.

q: Which famous pamphlet was written by Chaudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933?
f: 'Now or Never' (1933) first used the word 'Pakistan'.

q: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations?
f: The UN headquarters is in New York, USA.

q: Which is the largest river of Pakistan?
f: The Indus is Pakistan's longest and largest river.

q: How many bones are there in an adult human body?
f: An adult human skeleton has 206 bones.

q: Which country is the largest producer of coffee?
f: Brazil produces about a third of the world's coffee.

q: Which country is the largest producer of tea?
f: China is the world's largest tea producer, followed by India.

q: When was Israel created?
f: Israel declared independence on 14 May 1948.

q: Manchar Lake is located in which district?
f: Manchar, Pakistan's largest freshwater lake, lies in Jamshoro District (formerly part of Dadu).

q: Which Surah contains Bismillah twice?
f: Surah An-Naml has Bismillah at its start and again in verse 30 (Sulaiman's letter).

q: What is the name of the boundary line between India and China (eastern sector)?
f: The McMahon Line was drawn at the Simla Convention of 1914.

q: What is the length of Pakistan's coastline?
f: Pakistan's coastline is about 1046 km (Balochistan about 770 km, Sindh about 270 km).

q: Who drew the first map of the proposed Pakistan?
f: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali, who coined the name 'Pakistan', also published the first map of the proposed state.

q: Mohabbat Khan Mosque is located in which city?
f: The Mughal-era Mohabbat Khan Mosque (1630s) is in Peshawar.

q: What is the term of the National and Provincial Assemblies of Pakistan?
f: Under the 1973 Constitution, assemblies serve five years unless dissolved earlier.

q: The Shina language is mainly spoken in:
f: Shina is the main language of Gilgit and nearby valleys.

q: When was the Soviet Union formed?
f: The USSR was established on 30 December 1922.

q: The TAPI gas pipeline starts from which country?
f: TAPI begins at the Galkynysh gas field in Turkmenistan and goes through Afghanistan and Pakistan to India.

q: Where is the headquarters of NASA?
f: NASA's headquarters is in Washington D.C.

q: Choose the synonym of SPURN.
f: To spurn is to reject with contempt.

q: Choose the antonym of WILD.
f: Wild animals live naturally; tame ones are domesticated.

q: Which is the longest river in Asia?
f: The Yangtze (about 6300 km) in China is the longest river in Asia.

q: The shrine of Bahauddin Zakariya is located in which city?
f: Bahauddin Zakariya (Suhrawardi saint) is buried in Multan.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Zubair ibn al-Awwam (RA) with Hazrat Aisha (RA)?
f: Zubair was married to Asma bint Abu Bakr, Aisha's elder sister, so he was her brother-in-law.

q: Who was the first female Prime Minister of a Muslim country?
f: Benazir Bhutto became PM of Pakistan in December 1988.

q: When is the Independence Day of Bangladesh?
f: Bangladesh's independence was declared on 26 March 1971.

q: Which force opposes motion between two surfaces in contact?
f: Friction acts at the contact surface and opposes relative motion.

q: Which is the last month of the Islamic calendar?
f: Dhul-Hijjah, the month of Hajj, is the 12th and last Islamic month.

q: What was the population of Pakistan according to the 2023 census?
f: The 2023 digital census counted about 241.5 million people.

q: What is the real name of Imam Bukhari?
f: Imam Bukhari's name was Muhammad bin Ismail; his kunya was Abu Abdullah.

q: Pakistan's first constitution was made how many years after independence?
f: The first constitution came into force on 23 March 1956, about 9 years after 1947.

q: Which is the longest bridge in the world?
f: The Danyang-Kunshan railway viaduct in China is about 164 km long.

q: When and where were the first modern Olympic Games held?
f: The first modern Olympics were held in Athens in 1896.

q: Footballer Mohamed Salah belongs to which country?
f: Mohamed Salah is an Egyptian forward who plays for Liverpool.

q: Who discovered X-rays?
f: Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-rays in 1895 and won the first Nobel Prize in Physics (1901).

q: The Kala Chitta Range is located in which district?
f: The Kala Chitta Range lies mainly in Attock District, Punjab.

q: The Battle of Plassey, won by Robert Clive, was fought on:
f: Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 in Bengal.

q: When did the Kargil conflict begin?
f: The conflict began in early May 1999 (intrusions first reported on 3 May).

q: On which date did the 1965 Pakistan-India war begin (with Operation Gibraltar)?
f: The war is dated from 5 August 1965, when Operation Gibraltar began in Kashmir; India attacked Lahore on 6 September.

q: In which year was the 2nd OIC Summit held in Lahore?
f: The Second Islamic Summit was held in Lahore on 22-24 February 1974.

q: When was the Montagu-Chelmsford Report published?
f: The Montagu-Chelmsford report on reforms was published on 8 July 1918 and led to the Government of India Act 1919.

q: How many Farz are there in Ghusl?
f: The three Farz of Ghusl are rinsing the mouth, rinsing the nose and washing the whole body.

q: In which year did Hazrat Khalid bin Walid (RA) accept Islam?
f: Khalid bin Walid accepted Islam in Safar 8 AH, a few months before the Conquest of Makkah.

q: Warsak Dam was built with the help of which country?
f: Canada funded and built Warsak Dam under the Colombo Plan; it was completed in 1960.

q: According to the notes, how long did the Flood of Prophet Nuh (AS) last?
f: Traditional accounts say the Ark stayed afloat for about six months before resting on Mount Judi.

q: At which place did the British (East India Company) first set up a factory in India?
f: The East India Company set up its first factory at Surat in 1613 with Jahangir's permission.

q: Who represented India at the Tashkent Agreement?
f: Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri signed it with President Ayub Khan.

q: Ranikot Fort is located in which district?
f: Ranikot Fort, called the 'Great Wall of Sindh', is in Jamshoro District.

q: Which is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush range?
f: Tirich Mir (7708 m) in Chitral is the highest Hindu Kush peak.

q: What is the other name of K2?
f: K2 is also called Mount Godwin-Austen after the British surveyor.

q: What is the range of Pakistan's Ababeel missile?
f: Ababeel is a MIRV-capable missile with a range of about 2200 km.

q: Which is the smallest dam in Pakistan?
f: Among Pakistan's major dams, Warsak (Kabul River) is the smallest.

q: What was Allama Iqbal's first book?
f: Iqbal's first book was 'Ilm-ul-Iqtisad' (on economics, 1903).

q: The proposed Kalabagh Dam site is in which province?
f: The Kalabagh site is on the Indus in Mianwali District, Punjab.

q: Who gave the idea of SAARC?
f: Bangladesh's President Ziaur Rahman proposed SAARC in 1980.

q: Which country hosted the G20 summit in 2023?
f: India hosted the G20 summit in New Delhi in September 2023.

q: Gomal Zam Dam is located in:
f: Gomal Zam Dam is on the Gomal River in South Waziristan, KP.

q: Which Caliph was given the title 'Dhun-Nurayn' (Possessor of Two Lights)?
f: Hazrat Uthman married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum.

q: When was the Tashkent Agreement signed?
f: Ayub Khan and Shastri signed the Tashkent Declaration on 10 January 1966.

q: The Kharan River (Kharan basin) is in which province?
f: Kharan is a desert district of Balochistan with inland drainage.

q: In Islamic sources, what is the meaning of the name 'Israel' (title of Prophet Yaqub AS)?
f: In Hebrew 'Isra' means servant and 'El' means God, so Israel means Abdullah (servant of Allah).

q: Joe Biden was which number President of the USA?
f: Joe Biden served as the 46th President (2021-2025).

q: Two lines that intersect at a right angle are called:
f: Perpendicular lines meet at 90 degrees.

q: What is the real name of Imam Malik?
f: Imam Malik's full name was Malik ibn Anas; he compiled 'Al-Muwatta'.

q: According to the notes, which is the shortest river in South Africa?
f: The notes name the Klein River, a short coastal river in the Western Cape.

f: According to the notes, Israeli strikes on Iranian (nuclear and military) facilities turned the conflict into a direct war.

f: Iran relies mainly on its large missile and drone forces to hit back.

It is the main route for Chinese silk exports
It controls a large share of global oil flow
It is the world's largest fishing ground

A rise in global food surplus
